[^03-4]: Krishna's left side is Radha's place. Instead of "the Lord taking into His embrace", PK manuscripts ka, kha, gha, cha,
KGC and GPT read simply "taking into His embrace", BR — "clasping Gadadhara to His breast". The humble "does not fathom" in
the signature is Narahari's usual formula.

## 2. Narahari (Sarakara) — "mo mena manu gorācāndere dekhiyā…" (PK 103)
*Lila: Navadvipa — Gaura walks along the road to the Ganga; a young townswoman tells how she saw Him. In PK — a
gaura-chandrika to purvaraga (love dawning at first sight). According to Majumdar — Narahari Sarakara's pada about a real
mood, though it contains expressions of nagari-bhava. Raga dhanashi.*[^03-5]

**2.1.** Seeing Gorachand, I all but died:[^03-6]
wondrous is His form — it outshines pure gold.

**2.2.** Now He walks swiftly, slapping His shoulders like a wrestler,
now, grown calm, He steps slowly along the road to the Suradhuni.[^03-7]

**2.3.** With His reddish eyes He gazes again and again, unblinking —
and has driven the arrows of His glances into the very heart.

**2.4.** His arms, reaching to the knees, sway on either side;
young women, in love, long to give Him their youth.[^03-8]

**2.5.** Now He smiles softly, now He shouts for joy;
not fathoming it, Narahari is lost in rapture.

[^03-5]: The signature is "Narahari". In PK the pada is the second gaura-chandrika to the section "Purvaraga — the age of
transition" (after a pada by Radhamohana); in GPT1 — p. 170, no. 41 (raga dhanashi). Majumdar discusses it among the nine
Navadvipa padas of Narahari Sarakara in PK and cites the line "With His reddish eyes He gazes again and again".
[^03-6]: The opening is obscure: "mo mena manu" (PK; ms. ka and GPT1 — "mo mene manu"). We translate tentatively: "mo" — "I",
"manu" — an old form for "I died" (cf. "malum̐"); "I think I perished" is also possible. The sense is the shock of seeing Gaura.
[^03-7]: "Slapping one's shoulders" (mālasāṭa mārā) is the gesture of a wrestler challenging to a bout; in another pada of GPT the
Lord does the same in kirtana ("now He slaps His shoulders, now calls 'Krishna!', now 'Radha!'"). The Suradhuni is the Ganga.
[^03-8]: The words about young women belong to the language of nagari-bhava (Gaura as the nagara, the beloved of the
townswomen); we translate them faithfully to the author. Vrindavana Dasa stresses that in this incarnation the Lord never
looked at another man's wife; the Gaudiya tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta) does not
accept the worship of Gaura in the spirit of "gaura-nagari". In PK the pada is a gaura-chandrika: it sets the tone for
Radha's purvaraga, and the attraction here is an image of prema for Krishna, not of a worldly feeling.

## 3. Narahari (Sarakara) — "ki lāgiyā mora gaura-sundara…" (PK 307)
*Lila: Navadvipa — the Lord in the mood of Radha as vasakasajja (the heroine who adorns herself and the bower while
awaiting her beloved) dresses Himself and waits for Krishna. In PK — a gaura-chandrika to "vasakasajja in spring".
According to Majumdar — a description of a real mood; the Lord's dress and ornaments in the Navadvipa padas are not
invented. Raga dhanashi.*[^03-9]

**3.1.** Why does my beautiful Gaura
sit in the house
and, preparing clothes, a seat and jewelled ornaments,
adorn His body with them?

**3.2.** Seeing the shadow of His own body,
He starts in His heart:
"Why has the Lord not come even now?
Why does He delay so long?"[^03-10]

**3.3.** Narahari says: my Gaurahari,
thinking of Rai's condition,
looks at the road with tear-filled eyes
and speaks in a faltering voice.

[^03-9]: The signature is "Narahari". In GPT1 (p. 306, no. 22) with minor variants (section "vasakasajja"). Majumdar adduces
the pada as an example that Narahari's gaura-chandrikas are not conventional preludes but descriptions of moods he saw;
that the Lord wore ornaments in Navadvipa is attested by the sannyasa pada PK 2241 (chapter 2, no. 5): "golden
armlets… — all that enchanting attire He gave up."
[^03-10]: A shadow mistaken for the beloved's step is a usual trait of the vasakasajja in rasa-shastra: Radha starts at every
rustle, thinking Krishna has come. The Lord experiences Her waiting; this is a manifestation of prema, not of worldly
longing.

## 4. Narahari (Sarakara) — "hema darapaṇi gaurāṅga-lāvaṇi…" (PK 316)
*Lila: Navadvipa — the Lord in the mood of Radha as vipralabdha (the deceived heroine whose beloved did not come to the
tryst) rolls in the dust, calls "Lord of My life!" and weeps before His companions. In PK — a gaura-chandrika to
"vipralabdha in spring". According to Majumdar — a pada of vipralambha (separation). Raga bhairavi.*[^03-11]

**4.1.** Gauranga's beauty is like a golden mirror,
yet its lustre is grey with dust;
leaving His seat and clothes, He weeps
like a beauty of Vraja.

**4.2.** Crying "Hari, Hari!", calling Him Lord of His life,
He rises, leaning on the ground:
"Where shall I go? Whom shall I tell?
My heart is breaking!"

**4.3.** Weeping, He speaks to His companions,
raising His face:
"What is happening to My heart —
to whom can I tell this pain?"

**4.4.** Narahari Dasa says in a faltering voice:
my Gauranga
wanders under another pretext, delivering all —
yet He Himself is ever drunk with Radha's love.[^03-12]

[^03-11]: The signature is "Narahari Dasa". S. Ray notes that the pada is found in only one PK manuscript (kha) and placed it in
the text because the other sections of this pallava open with gaura-chandrikas. In GPT1 (p. 307, no. 27) with minor
variants. B. B. Majumdar (1961) gives the pada from a Baranagar manuscript with the reading "aśana vasana" ("food and clothes")
instead of "āsana vasana" ("seat and clothes").
[^03-12]: Cf. CC Adi 4: the external reason for the Lord's appearance is to give the world the holy name and prema, the internal
one — to taste Radha's love. Narahari expresses the same thought: delivering the world is the "pretext", while the Lord's
heart is ever in Radha's prema.

## 5. Narahari (Sarakara) — "āre mora āre mora gaurāṅga rāya…" (PK 408)
*Lila: Navadvipa — the Lord in the mood of Radha as khandita (the heroine whose beloved comes at dawn bearing the marks of a
tryst with another) angrily reproaches Krishna. In PK — a gaura-chandrika to the section "Khandita — the impatient
(adhira) madhya". According to Majumdar — Narahari Sarakara's pada of the khandita. Raga suhai.*[^03-13]

**5.1.** Ah, my, ah, my Gauranga Raya!
Full of His former love, He walks with slow steps.

**5.2.** His eyes have reddened, His face has darkened;
in anger, His heart trembling, the Lord speaks haltingly:

**5.3.** "I know You, I know Your false love!
Go and bow to her with whom You spent the night."[^03-14]

**5.4.** Having said this, Gauranga is wholly overcome by bhava:
in the waves of bhava He is as if after a sleepless night.

**5.5.** Narahari says: in Radha's mood He has become
like one who was given a promise and deceived.

[^03-13]: The signature is "Narahari". In GPT1 (p. 309, no. 4) with minor variants (section "khandita, mana"). Majumdar cites
the line "I know You, I know Your false love". The khandita is one of the eight heroines of rasa-shastra
(*Ujjvala-nilamani*).
[^03-14]: The words of Radha as khandita to Krishna, who has come in the morning from Her rival. Radha's jealousy and pique
(mana) are a manifestation of the highest prema, not a worldly feeling; the Lord experiences them in Her mood.

## 6. Narahari (Sarakara) — "gorā pahum̐ virale vasiyā…" (PK 421)
*Lila: Navadvipa — the Lord in the mood of Radha as khandita sits alone after a sleepless night and weeps: "Having given Me
hope, You deceived Me all night." In PK — a gaura-chandrika to "khandita — the composed-impatient (dhira-adhira) madhya".
According to Majumdar — Narahari Sarakara's pada of the khandita. Raga gandhara.*[^03-15]

**6.1.** Lord Gora, sitting alone,
has lowered His face.

**6.2.** In bhava His eyes are heavy with sleep —
the sleepless night is witness to it.

**6.3.** With a faded face He says:
"Having given Me hope, You deceived Me all night."

**6.4.** Weeping, Gora Raya says:
"I cannot bear this pain."

**6.5.** He laments, full of grief;
Narahari begs for grace.[^03-16]

[^03-15]: The signature is "Narahari". In GPT1 (p. 309, no. 5) with minor variants, immediately after the preceding pada
(PK 408). Majumdar cites the lines "Having given Me hope, You deceived Me all night, — weeping, says Gora Raya".
[^03-16]: "Begs for grace" — in the original "begs for prasada" (parasāda): the Lord's mercy.

## 7. Ananta Dasa — "āpāda-mastaka prema-dhārā varikhata…" (PK 2208)
*Praise of Gauranga: from head to foot He pours streams of prema; at His qualities wood and stone melt, beasts and birds
weep; the poet asks only one thing — to sing of Gauranga, wandering from land to land. In PK — the section "Sri Gaurachandra —
in another way". Majumdar names the pada among Ananta's padas on Gauranga's mood. Raga mangala.*[^03-17]

**7.1.** From head to foot He pours down streams of prema,
His rays flash in every direction;
His gait is lovelier than a lordly elephant's,
moons rise at His feet.[^03-18]

**7.2.** What kind of Creator, having fashioned Gaurangachand's body,
remained firm himself?
What kind of heart is his — of wood and stone —
that it did not melt at once?[^03-19]

**7.3.** At my Gauranga's qualities wood and stone —
what of wood and stone! — melt and flow down to the earth;
the beasts and birds of the forest weep and weep:
there is no living being that does not weep.

**7.4.** In whatever family I may be born,
whatever body I may receive, —
Ananta Dasa's one wish is to sing of Thakura Gauranga's qualities,
wandering from land to land.

[^03-17]: The signature is "Ananta Dasa". According to Majumdar, Ananta Dasa was a poet of Advaita's branch and a contemporary
of the Lord; PK has 32 padas with his signature. In GPT1 (p. 39, no. 41) and GPT2 with variants.
[^03-18]: The moons at His feet are the Lord's toenails, shining like moons.
[^03-19]: PK: "…fashioned Gaurangachand's body, remaining firm himself" (daṛhiyā); the P-R-Sa manuscript and GPT2 read "dhariyā",
and GPT "Gaurangachand" (cām̐dere ye): "…fashioned Gaurangachand, taking on his own body". The image of the Creator (vidhi) who "sculpted" beauty is a
poetic convention (poets speak so of Radha and Krishna too); the Lord's body is not created — it is eternal, full of being,
knowledge and bliss ("ishvarah paramah krishnah sac-cid-ananda-vigrahah", *Brahma-samhita* 5.1).

## 8. Ananta Dasa — "dekha dekha aparūpa gaurāṅga nitāi…" (PK 2336)
*Praise of Gaura and Nitai — the two brothers who purify the fallen: They give prema to all without distinction and weep on
seeing the fallen. In PK — the section "The form and qualities of Sri Chaitanya and Nityananda". According to Majumdar it
"sounds like the word of a contemporary". Raga kamoda.*[^03-20]

**8.1.** *(Refrain)* Look, look: the wondrous Gauranga and Nitai!
By the good fortune of all living beings there wander the earth
the two brothers who purify the fallen.

**8.2.** Whomever They see, They give prema to him, entreating him,
making no distinction between high and low;
the people of the three worlds, drinking the nectar of prema,
know neither old age, nor death, nor sorrow.

**8.3.** The wish-fulfilling tree and the ocean will not give a drop unasked —
shame even to compare them with Them!
Seeing the fallen, Both weep, unable to restrain Themselves,
and, entreating, give priceless bhakti and prema.[^03-21]

**8.4.** If someone does not serve such merciful Lords —
what hope is there in his wretched life?
Even if he be a sannyasi or a brahmana, he is counted among the asuras:
such is the word of Ananta Dasa.[^03-22]

[^03-20]: The signature is "Ananta Dasa". In GPT1 (p. 39, no. 42, raga shri or kamoda) and GPT2 with minor variants; there the
pada immediately follows the preceding one (PK 2208).
[^03-21]: "Entreating" (yāciyā): the Lord and Nityananda Themselves beg people to accept the name and prema (cf. CB Madhya
13: Nitai and Haridasa go from house to house begging, "Sing Krishna's name"; CC Adi 7). Instead of "Both" (dom̐he)
manuscript ka reads "body" (deha): "Their body knows no rest".
[^03-22]: Cf. *Bhagavad-gita* 7.15: the deluded do not surrender to the Lord, "having taken shelter of the nature of the asuras".

## 9. Ananta Acharya — "jaya śacīnandana jaga-jīvana sāra…" (PK 2285)
*Lila: from the appearance to Nilachala — the Lord of Goloka descends in Navadvipa, teaches the dharma of the age —
sankirtana, accepts sannyasa from Keshava Bharati, shows the six-armed form in Utkala and settles in Nilachala. In PK —
the section "The sannyasa of Sri Gauranga, etc." According to Majumdar — probably a pada by Ananta Acharya, who lived in
Navadvipa; an important detail: the Lord Himself "gave the mantra" to Bharati. Raga shri (as for the preceding PK pada).*[^03-23]

**9.1.** *(Refrain)* Glory to the Son of Shachi, the essence of the world's life!
In life and in death Gora is my Lord.

**9.2.** Coming with His associates, the Lord of Goloka
descended in Navadvipa;
establishing the dharma of the age — His own sankirtana —
He explained it by dancing and singing.

**9.3.** He of golden form put on the kaupina and the cord,
an upper cloth the colour of the morning rays;
Gaurangachandra took the kamandalu and staff in His hands,
casting aside Vishnupriya's hopes.[^03-24]

**9.4.** Hari, the guru of the whole world, made Bharati His guru:
having given him the mantra, He received it from him.[^03-25]
The scoffers and unbelievers, who had once reviled Him much,
began to worship Him as Narayana.[^03-26]

**9.5.** Going to the land of Utkala, He taught the holy name,
manifesting the six-armed form.
Ananta Acharya says: with all the great souls
He made His dwelling in Nilachala.[^03-27]

[^03-23]: The signature is "Ananta Acharya"; in S. Ray's index of poets it is the only pada of Ananta Acharya in PK. Majumdar
considers it probably a pada of Ananta Acharya of Advaita's branch, who lived in Navadvipa (CC Adi 12). In GPT1
(pp. 19–20, no. 53) and GPT2 with minor variants; the refrain there (and in PK manuscripts ka, kha, cha) begins "The Son of
Shachi…" without "Glory".
[^03-24]: The kaupina is the sannyasi's loincloth; the kamandalu, a water-pot; the staff (danda), the sign of sannyasa.
"Vishnupriya's hopes" — in the original "vishnupriya-abhilasha": the Lord left His wife, who hoped to keep Him at home
(CC Adi 17; Lochana, Madhya-khanda).
[^03-25]: According to CB (Madhya 28), the Lord spoke into Keshava Bharati's ear a mantra He said He had heard in a dream, and
then received it from him as from a guru; thus He, the guru of the world, showed the example of a disciple's humility. Cf.
Murari 3.2.
[^03-26]: Cf. CC Adi 17: the Lord accepted sannyasa so that those who had reviled Him in Navadvipa, by bowing to a sannyasi,
would be freed from their offences; a sannyasi is honoured as Narayana.
[^03-27]: Utkala is Orissa. The six-armed form the Lord showed to Sarvabhauma (CB Antya 3; see the next pada). Instead of
"with" (laiyā) the P-R-Sa manuscript reads "in lila" (līlā).

## 10. Gauridasa Pandita — "pahu mora nityānanda rāya…" (PK 2313)
*Praise of Nityananda — the "market of the holy name" (hat-pattan): Nityananda is king of the market on the Ganga's bank,
Ramai carries out His orders, Haridasa is the kotwal, Krishnadasa the weighman, Srivasa the scribe; Vishvambhara and
Gadadhara trade in the Acharya's courtyard; Gauridasa, sitting near the king, hears of the market's glory. In PK — the
section "The qualities of Sri Nityananda". According to Majumdar — the first pada of the hat-pattan genre, written after
the sannyasa (the Lord is called "Chaitanya"). Raga shri.*[^03-28]

**10.1.** *(Refrain)* My Lord is Nityananda Raya!
Having churned all the tantras, the great mantra — the name of Hari —
He explains to living beings, holding them by the hand.

**10.2.** His name is "Chaitanya's elder brother", He has no equal in the three worlds;
on the bank of the Suradhuni He set up a post;
arranging a market in due form, Nityananda became its king,
with the hero's banner that crushes the unbelievers.[^03-29]

**10.3.** Ramai, a worthy servant, carries out the royal orders,
Haridasa became the kotwal;
Krishnadasa became the weighman — no one can slip past by cheating;
the writing and reading is Srinivasa's.[^03-30]

**10.4.** The traders are Vishvambhara and the beloved Gadadhara:
in the Acharya's courtyard there is buying and selling.
Gauridasa, smiling, sits near the king
and hears a little of the market's glory.[^03-31]

[^03-28]: The signature is "Gauridasa". Gauridasa Pandita of Ambika (Kalna) was a companion of the Lord and of Nityananda;
Jayananda praises his poetry; PK has only two padas with his signature (161 and 2313). In GPT1 (p. 420, no. 20) with
minor variants. "Hat-pattan" ("opening a market") is a genre of padas where the preaching of the holy name is pictured
as a market at which prema is given away; later poems also belong to it. Majumdar regards Gauridasa's pada as the first
example of the genre and dates it after the sannyasa: Nityananda is called "Chaitanya's elder brother". Cf. CC Madhya 15
and Murari 4.21–4.22: the Lord sends Nityananda from Puri to preach in Gauda.
[^03-29]: Tantras here means the scriptures in general. A post (thānā) — a guard station. "The hero's banner that crushes the
unbelievers": Nityananda is Balarama, and His preaching is a victory over the pashandas.
[^03-30]: Ramai is probably Ramai Pandita (Sri Rama Pandita), Srivasa's younger brother, or Abhirama (Ramadasa), Nityananda's
companion; a kotwal is the chief of the town watch; Haridasa is Haridasa Thakura. "Weighman" — in the original "dāṛyā"
(mss. "ḍāṛyā", "ḍeṛyā"): the meaning is unclear — the one who holds the scales (dām̐ṛi) or a gatekeeper; "by cheating"
(bhām̐ṛyā) — manuscript cha reads "bhem̐ṛyā", P-R-Sa "chāṛyā" ("let off"). Krishnadasa is probably Gauridasa's younger
brother, the author of PK 2358 (chapter 1, no. 24). Srinivasa is Srivasa Pandita (Srinivasa is his full name).
[^03-31]: The Acharya is Advaita Acharya. Vishvambhara is the Lord Himself (His name before sannyasa). The humble "hears a
little" in the signature: the poet is merely present at this play.

## 11. Vasu Ghosha — "acaitanya śrīcaitanya sārvvabhauma-ghare…" (GPT1, p. 402)
*Lila: Puri, 1510 — the Lord lies unconscious in Sarvabhauma's house; Sarvabhauma sees Him in the forms of the avataras, and
when the Lord stands up in the six-armed form, he falls at His feet. Only in GPT (section "Antya-lila"). Raga suhai.*[^03-32]

**11.1.** Sri Chaitanya lies unconscious in Sarvabhauma's house;
Gopinatha, sitting beside Him, massages His feet.[^03-33]

**11.2.** Sarvabhauma gazes unblinking at the Lord's face
and cannot make out Who He is.

**11.3.** Now he sees the Lord in the form of Nrisimha,
now again in the form of the boy Vamana;

**11.4.** now he sees the forms of Matsya, Kurma, Varaha,
now Bhrigurama with a fearsome axe in His hand;

**11.5.** at times he sees a form dark as a blade of durva grass,
at times the Holder of the flute, the colour of a rain-cloud.[^03-34]

**11.6.** Seeing all this, he gave up his doubts;
the Lord rose and stood in the six-armed form.[^03-35]

**11.7.** Shachi's darling is that very Butter-thief:
within — the dark Kanu, without — Gaura.[^03-36]

**11.8.** Falling to the ground, Sarvabhauma prostrates himself.
Vasu Ghosha says: why any more vain delusion?

[^03-32]: The signature is "Vasu Ghosha". The pada is neither in PK nor in BR — only in GPT1 (p. 402, no. 2 of the section
"Antya-lila") and GPT2; by Majumdar's criterion Vasu Ghosha's padas known only from GPT are unreliable, and the attribution
remains doubtful. In GPT the pada stands between Madhavi's two padas on the Lord's arrival in Puri (PK 2239, 2240; chapter
02, nos. 1–2). Cf. CC Madhya 6, CB Antya 3, Murari 3.11–3.12.
[^03-33]: Gopinatha Acharya, Sarvabhauma's brother-in-law, had known the Lord already in Navadvipa. According to CC (Madhya 6),
the Lord fell unconscious on seeing Jagannatha, and Sarvabhauma had Him carried to his house.
[^03-34]: The forms of the avataras: Nrisimha, Vamana (the boy brahmana), Matsya, Kurma, Varaha, Parashurama (Bhrigurama);
"dark as durva grass" — Ramachandra; the Holder of the flute — Krishna.
[^03-35]: The six-armed form (with Rama's bow, Krishna's flute, and the sannyasi's staff and water-pot) the Lord showed to
Sarvabhauma according to CB (Antya 3); according to CC (Madhya 6) — first a four-armed form, then Krishna's two-armed form
with the flute.
[^03-36]: The Butter-thief is Krishna. Cf. *Tattva-sandarbha* (2): "antah krishnam bahir gauram" — "Krishna within, Gaura
without"; CC Adi 1, 4.

## 12. Narahari (Sarakara) — "āova gaura punahi nadiyāpura…" (PK 1970)
*Lila: Navadvipa in the years when the Lord lives in Puri: the devotees dream of His return — to see His face and His
kirtana again. In PK — a gaura-chandrika to the section "Bhavollasa" (Radha's joy at the news of Krishna's return), headed
"The words of the devotees, the residents of Navadvipa". Raga dhanashi.*[^03-37]

**12.1.** Gaura will come again to the town of Nadia —
and the heart will be filled with joy.
Shall we really see again that fountain of bliss,
His play in kirtana?

**12.2.** *(Refrain)* Hari, Hari! When shall I see that moon-like face?
When shall I swim across the ocean of separation,
and the heart's bewilderment be dispelled?

**12.3.** When shall I see a lustre like the purest gold
and the gleaming sacred thread?
Raising both arms, He will cry "Hari, Hari!",
dancing amid the devotees.[^03-38]

**12.4.** Having said this, all fell still with closed eyes,
drunk with love for Gaura.
Narahari Dasa: when will the hope be fulfilled —
to see the youthful Gaura?

[^03-37]: The signature is "Narahari Dasa". Majumdar does not discuss this pada; its attribution to Narahari Sarakara is likely
(simple language) but not proven. In GPT1 (p. 411, no. 27) with variants, in the section on the years in Puri; there
instead of "will come" (āova) it reads "is coming" (āota). In PK the pada follows a gaura-chandrika by Radhamohana to the
same section.
[^03-38]: The Lord wore the sacred thread (upavita) before sannyasa; on accepting sannyasa He gave it up. The Navadvipa
devotees remember His former form — as they saw Him in the kirtanas of 1509.

## 13. Narahari (Sarakara) — "locane jharajhara ānanda-lora…" (PK 1707)
*Lila: Navadvipa in the years of separation: the poet sees in a dream how Gaura, after a long separation, has come to
Navadvipa and strolls among the devotees; on waking he weeps. In PK — a gaura-chandrika to the section "Telling of a dream"
(svapna-rasodgara), headed "Here — Sri Mahaprabhu". Raga suhai.*[^03-39]

**13.1.** Tears of joy stream from my eyes:
in a dream I saw the youthful Gaura.

**13.2.** After so many days He came to Navadvipa
and joyfully strolls in the circle of devotees.

**13.3.** What shall I tell you, friend, of the bliss of that night!
After so many days I saw Gora's moon-like face.

**13.4.** All the people of Nadia, tormented by separation,
saw Gora's face — and all their sorrow went far away.

**13.5.** And now, not seeing Him, the heart is breaking:
Narahari Dasa weeps, rolling in the dust.[^03-40]

[^03-39]: The signature is "Narahari Dasa". Majumdar does not discuss the pada. In GPT1 (p. 410, no. 25) with minor variants,
in the section on the years in Puri, next to padas on the Lord's meeting with the Navadvipa devotees. In PK the section
"telling of a dream" consists of Radha's words relating to a friend Her dream of meeting Krishna; the gaura-chandrika
transfers them to Gaura. Cf. Shachi's dream of Nimai's coming (Vasu Ghosha, chapter 1, no. 22) and the Lord's visit to
Navadvipa in 1514 (CC Madhya 16).
[^03-40]: Waking after a dream of meeting is a usual motif of separation: the joy of the dream makes separation still keener.

## 14. Vasu Ghosha — "svarūpera kare dhari gorārāya…" (GPT1, p. 310)
*Lila: Puri — the Lord in Radha's mood, holding Svarupa's hand, reviles "Shyama, the friend": He ruined Her honour and went
to another. Only in GPT (section "Khandita, mana"). Raga suhai.*[^03-41]

**14.1.** Holding Svarupa's hand, Gora Raya
heaps abuse on Shyama, the friend:

**14.2.** "That cheat, that rake, that thief of love —
how many woes He has brought on Me!

**14.3.** He ruined My family and My honour,
He set fire to My husband's house;

**14.4.** and in the end, the Dark One left Me
and sports with another.[^03-42]

**14.5.** Have I become a stranger to Him?" —
saying this, Gaurahari sobs in despair.

**14.6.** Vasu says: what can I understand?
The One You weep for, Lord, is You Yourself.[^03-43]

[^03-41]: The signature is "Vasu". The pada is neither in PK nor in BR — only in GPT1 (p. 310, no. 8) and GPT2 (sec. 4.6, no.
8); Majumdar considers Vasu Ghosha's padas known only from GPT unreliable, and two padas signed Vasu in which Svarupa
accompanies the Lord in Navadvipa or on the Yamuna outright spurious (Svarupa came to the Lord only in Puri). Here, to judge
by Svarupa's presence, the scene is Puri, but the attribution remains doubtful. In GPT the pada follows the pada of
Narahari (?) "prema kari kulavatī sane" (chapter 2, no. 8). Svarupa Damodara in the Lord's mood is Radha's friend Lalita
(CC Antya 14–19; *Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika*).
[^03-42]: "Another" — Radha's rival (Chandravali). Radha's abuse in mana is the language of the highest prema, not of worldly
jealousy; the Lord experiences it in Radha's mood.
[^03-43]: Cf. CC Adi 4: Krishna accepted Radha's mood and lustre to taste His own sweetness and Radha's love for Him. The poet
says: the Krishna You seek is You Yourself.

## 15. Narahari (Sarakara) — "kanaka-campaka gorācānde…" (PK 849)
*Lila: the Lord in Radha's mood reproaches the Creator (vidhi): "Who has driven Me mad? Why did he make such a union?" In PK
— a gaura-chandrika to the section "reproaches to the Creator" (akshepanuraga). Raga suhai.*[^03-44]

**15.1.** Gorachand, the colour of the golden champaka —
why does He weep, fallen on the ground?

**15.2.** Now He rises and cries, "Hari, Hari!
Who has driven Me mad?"

**15.3.** Raising His arms that reach to the knees,
He keeps reviling the Creator:

**15.4.** "Shame on the Creator's decrees!
Why did he make such a union?"[^03-45]

**15.5.** With what feeling does Gora Raya say this? —
Narahari goes about asking everyone.

[^03-44]: The signature is "Narahari". Majumdar does not discuss this pada separately, but he calls Narahari Sarakara's
gaura-chandrikas in the PK sections on akshepanuraga (853, 799, 820, 832, 840) descriptions of the Lord's real moods. In GPT1
(p. 300, no. 27) and GPT2 the pada comes immediately after PK 840 ("Ah, my youthful Gaura!", chapter 2, no. 7), among the
Puri padas. The pada itself does not name the place.
[^03-45]: "Union" (yoṭanā; ms. ka "yoṭana", kha "yoṭinā"; GPT "joṭana"): Radha reproaches the Creator because Her love for Krishna
has been joined with the bonds of family and duty and brings only suffering. The madness (vāuri) here is the madness of
prema. Instead of "Shame…" PK reads "vahe dhik" — apparently a misprint for "kahe dhik" ("says: shame…"), as in GPT.

## 16. Narahari (Sarakara) — "āre mora gaura kiśora. nāhi jāne divāniśi…" (PK 1746)
*Lila: the mood of separation — the Lord does not distinguish day from night, laughs without cause, sings aloud asking,
"Where is the Lord of My life?", trembles, leaps, dances, speaks incoherently, weeps with closed eyes. In PK — a
gaura-chandrika to the section "Separation in the winter season" (hemanta and shishira). According to Majumdar — Narahari
Sarakara's pada of viraha ("laughter without cause"). Raga pahida.*[^03-46]

**16.1.** *(Refrain)* Ah, my youthful Gaura!
Not knowing day from night, He laughs without cause —
the Lord is lost in the bewilderment of His heart.

**16.2.** Now He sings aloud — of whom, of what does the Lord ask? —
"Where is the Lord of My life?"
Now His whole body trembles as with cold, now He leaps:
"Where shall I find Him? Where shall I go? With whom?"[^03-47]

**16.3.** Now, raising His arms, He dances, whirling and whirling,
now again and again He speaks incoherently;
now He closes His eyes and weeps, "O Natha!",
now again and again He is in torment.

**16.4.** Narahari Dasa says: ah, my Gaurahari
has become like this from Radha's love.
He resolved in His heart to deliver the age of Kali —
why then am I left out?[^03-48]

[^03-46]: The signature is "Narahari Dasa". Majumdar cites the line "Now He sings aloud — of whom, of what does the Lord ask?"
among Narahari Sarakara's viraha padas. In GPT1 (p. 315, no. 8) and GPT2 (sec. 4.7, no. 8) the pada stands immediately after
PK 1662 and 1663 (no. 17 of this chapter), among the padas on the divine madness of prema; there instead of "speaks
incoherently" (pralāpa) it reads "laments" (vilāpa), with a note of the reading "pralāpa". In PK the pada is preceded by the
heading "Separation befitting winter. Here — Sri Gaurachandra".
[^03-47]: Radha's words in separation: She seeks Krishna and does not know where to go. Trembling is a sattvika-bhava; in PK
the pada opens the section on winter separation, and trembling "as with cold" matches the season. This is the madness of
prema (divya-unmada) described in CC Antya 14–20, not worldly longing.
[^03-48]: Cf. CC Adi 4. The formula "why then am I left out" is Narahari's usual signature (cf. PK 2241, chapter 2, no. 5).

## 17. Unsigned (Vasu Ghosha? Govinda Dasa?) — "cetana pāiyā gorā rāya…" (PK 1663)
*Lila: a continuation of PK 1662 (Vasu Ghosha, chapter 2, no. 15): the Lord, coming to Himself after running to the sea,
sees Svarupa and Ramaraya before Him and laments: "Where is My Krishna with the flute at His lips? I saw Him just now!" In PK
— the section "Divya-unmada". Raga shri.*[^03-49]

**17.1.** Coming to His senses, Gora Raya,
lying on the ground, looks this way and that.

**17.2.** Before Him are Svarupa and Ramaraya;
seeing them, the Lord cries, "Alas, alas!

**17.3.** Where is My Krishna with the flute at His lips?
I saw Him just now!

**17.4.** O Lord, supremely merciful,
be gracious, show Yourself!"[^03-50]

**17.5.** So laments Gorachand;
seeing this, the devotees weep.

[^03-49]: In PK the pada is unsigned; in the P-R-Sa manuscript "Govinda Dasa" stands instead of "the devotees" ("seeing this,
Govinda Dasa weeps"), so that the pada is signed by Govinda Dasa; in GPT1 (p. 315, no. 7) and GPT2 (sec. 4.7, no. 7) a sixth
couplet is added with Vasu Ghosha's signature: "Vasu Ghosha says: my Gora is drunk with love for Krishna". The attribution
is disputed: it may be a continuation of Vasu Ghosha's PK 1662, but the witnesses disagree. Ramaraya is Ramananda Raya. Cf.
CC Antya 14: coming to Himself after running to Chataka-parvata, the Lord says to Svarupa, "Why have you brought Me here? I
just saw Krishna…"; Antya 17–18.
[^03-50]: "Krishna with the flute at His lips" — in the original "murali-vadana", "He whose face bears the flute". The Lord
speaks in the mood of Radha, who has just seen Krishna and lost Him again.

## 18. Narahari — "gaurāṅga ke jāne mahimā tomāra…" (PK 2293)
*Praise of Gauranga, the avatara who purifies the fallen in the age of Kali: from the ocean of Shyama, as if by churning,
the sweet Gauranga appeared, and a downpour of prema flooded the three worlds. In PK — the last pada of the section "The
sannyasa of Sri Gauranga, etc." Raga varadi ("the same" as for the preceding PK pada), dhanashri (GPT).*[^03-51]

**18.1.** *(Refrain)* Gauranga, who knows Your greatness?
To deliver the age of Kali You appeared — the avatara who purifies the fallen.

**18.2.** How long the Creator
churned the ocean of Shyama!
How much nectar he made from it —
and the sweet Gauranga appeared.[^03-52]

**18.3.** In the three worlds a downpour of prema came —
the rain of Gaura's love;
the lowly and wretched are drowned in that rasa, —
so Narahari sings of His qualities.

[^03-51]: The signature is "Narahari". Majumdar does not discuss the pada; in the stage-1 catalogue another pada ("nīlācale yave
majhu nātha" — in GPT1 signed by Vaishnava Dasa) was wrongly linked to PK 2293. The language and imagery (churning, a downpour
of prema) are closer to later stutis; the pada may also belong to Narahari Chakravarti — its attribution to Sarakara is not
established. In GPT1 (p. 28, no. 6) and GPT2 with the variant "mathiyā se karatāla" instead of "mathiyā se kata kāla".
[^03-52]: The image is the churning of the Milk Ocean, from which the amrita appeared. "The Creator" (vidhi) is a poetic figure:
Gauranga is not created — He is Shyama (Krishna) Himself, who accepted Radha's lustre and mood (CC Adi 4).

---

# Chapter 4. Gaura's Form, Navadvipa, the Sannyasa and the Return

*Padas of contemporaries which Majumdar (*Sri-Chaitanya-chariter upadan*, ch. 2) regards as eyewitness testimony, in the
order of the lilas: the six-armed form and the beauty of Gorachand in Navadvipa, Radha's mood in Gadadhara's lap, the
swing festival on the bank of the Ganga, the goshtha-lila, praise of Gaura and Nityananda; then Vasu Ghosha's cycle on the
sannyasa (the last night at home, the lament of Shachi and Vishnupriya, Katwa, Keshava Bharati, the shorn curls, the
lament of Nadia), the dance of the Lord as a sannyasi, and the Lord's return to the neighbourhood of Navadvipa (1514/15).
The text follows the *Padakalpataru* (PK), the *Bhakti-ratnakara* (BR), the *Kshanada-gita-chintamani* (KGC) and the
*Gaura-pada-tarangini* (GPT1 — 1st ed., 1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934); the Bengali original, variants and word-for-word
translation are in the full version of the book.*

## 1. Ananta Dasa — "kām̐cā se soṇāra tanu…" (PK 2167)
*Lila: Navadvipa — the Lord's six-armed form (shad-bhuja): Rama's bow and arrows, Krishna's flute, the sannyasi's staff and
waterpot. In PK the pada is headed "Then the form that revealed six arms, in Navadvipa". Majumdar mentions this pada when
speaking of Ananta Dasa, a poet of Advaita's branch and a contemporary of the Lord. Raga tirotha-dhanashi.*[^04-1]

**1.1.** His body is like pure gold, all of it quivering;
on His moon-face a smile — waves of nectar.

**1.2.** A forest garland hangs down to the very earth;
drawn by its fragrance, swarms of bees surround it.

**1.3.** Of the six arms the upper ones hold sharp arrows and a bow —
at the sight of them enemies tremble.[^04-2]

**1.4.** These arms are the colour of durva grass, their nails like moons;
bracelets and armlets of jewels shine on them.

**1.5.** Below, two arms dark as a thundercloud;
in them gleams the matchless, enchanting flute.

**1.6.** The jewel-nails outshine the moon, the palms are red;
seeing the jewelled ornaments on them, Ananga himself swoons.[^04-3]

**1.7.** Lower still, hands with the waterpot and the staff,
which shatter the filth of Kali and the godless.[^04-4]

**1.8.** At the throat and on the breast jewels and pearls sway;
the Kaustubha swings, the breast is marked with the Shrivatsa.

**1.9.** The broad chest is anointed with sandal;
the navel is deep, the waist slender as a lion's.

**1.10.** The red cloth falls to His very feet;
Ananta Dasa offers himself to the nails of His feet.[^04-5]

[^04-1]: The signature is "Dasa Ananta". In PK the pada stands last in the 18th pallava ("The form of Sri Gauranga, etc.";
vol. 3, PDF p. 256, printed p. 245; MS P-R-Sa no. 2274); in GPT1 — p. 141, no. 89; in GPT2 — sect. 3.1, twice (nos. 44 and
89), with minor variants. The Lord revealed the six-armed form to Nityananda in Navadvipa (CB Madhya 5; Murari 2.8) and
to Sarvabhauma in Puri (CC Madhya 6). Majumdar regards Ananta Dasa as a contemporary; PK has 32 padas with his signature.
[^04-2]: Bow and arrows are the form of Ramachandra, and the colour of durva grass (a dark greenish hue) is the colour of His
body. PK reads "uta chaya bhuja para" ("there, of the six arms…"), GPT "ubhadvaya bhujapara" ("on the two raised arms");
the sense is the same.
[^04-3]: The middle pair of arms holding the flute, dark as a cloud, is Krishna's form. Ananga ("the bodiless") is Kamadeva,
the god of love.
[^04-4]: The lowest pair of arms holds the staff (danda) and waterpot (kamandalu) of a sannyasi: the form of Gaura Himself.
For "the godless" (pāṣaṇḍa) MSS "ka", "ca" read "filth" (kaluṣa); so also GPT: "the filth, the sin of Kali".
[^04-5]: Nichhani (nichani) is the custom of waving something round a beloved person to ward off harm from him and then giving it
away; the poet "offers himself" in such an offering to the nails of the Lord's feet. MSS "ka", "ca", P-R-Sa read "nichani".

## 2. Govinda Ghosha — "gorācām̐da kivā tomāra vadana-maṇḍala…" (PK 1029)
*Lila: Gorachand's form — a song of the Lord's beauty in Navadvipa. In PK it opens the section "Delight in the form"
(rupa-ullasa) as a gaura-chandrika. According to Majumdar, Govinda Ghosha, the eldest of the Ghosha brothers, conveys his
own impression of Gauranga's form. Raga dhanashi.*[^04-6]

**2.1.** *(Refrain)* Gorachand, how wondrous is the orb of Your face!
Is it a golden lotus, is it the full autumn moon —
it shines by night and by day.

**2.2.** The colour of Your body outshines yellow haritala
and seems to surpass a motionless lightning;
is it fresh gorochana, is it gold of the finest assay —
You enchant the mind of Manmatha himself.[^04-7]

**2.3.** Your nose is lovelier than Garuda's beak, Your speech sweet as nectar —
there is none like You in the three worlds.
Eyes reaching to the ears are arrows, brows a drawn bow:
with a sidelong glance You pierce the hearts of women.[^04-8]

**2.4.** Arms reaching to the knees are anointed with sandal,
and rings and bracelets shine on them.
The waist is slenderer than a lion's, the thighs like golden plantain stems,
on the feet are anklets.

**2.5.** The gait is lovelier than a maddened elephant's and the king of swans';
seeing such a treasury of beauty,
Govinda Ghosha speaks, with joy in his heart for Gora:
"I would give myself up for Him."[^04-9]

[^04-6]: The signature is "Govinda Ghosha". In PK (vol. 2, PDF p. 225, printed p. 212; MS P-R-Sa no. 1455) the pada comes
under the heading "Now, delight in the form. Sri Gaurachandra" and opens the songs on the beauty of Radha and Krishna. It is
not in GPT. Majumdar names PK 1029 and 2146 (no. 3) among Govinda Ghosha's padas on Gaura's form.
[^04-7]: Haritala is orpiment, a golden-yellow paint; gorochana is a yellow pigment used for tilaka; "gold of ten van"
(daśavān) is gold refined many times, of the finest assay. Manmatha is Kamadeva: the Lord's beauty enchants the god of love
himself (cf. Krishna's name Madana-mohana). MS P-R-Sa reads "tanu" ("body") for "janu" ("as if").
[^04-8]: "You pierce the hearts of women" (MSS "kha", "gha", P-R-Sa: "the heart of a woman") is a stock image of the poetics
of describing beauty; we translate faithfully. Vrindavana Dasa stresses that in this incarnation the Lord never looked at
another man's wife; worship of Gaura in the spirit of "Gaura-nagari" is not accepted by the Gaudiya tradition (Vrindavana
Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta).
[^04-9]: The words "gora mane santoṣa" also allow the reading "and Gora is pleased at heart"; our rendering is tentative.
"Give myself up" (nichani jāiye) — see note 5. For "maddened" (mayamatta) MSS "ka", "kha" read "madamatta" (same sense).

## 3. Govinda Ghosha — "kanayā kaṣila mukha-śobhā…" (PK 2146)
*Lila: Gaura's form — the causeless smile, the yellow silk, a bee flying to His feet. According to Majumdar, an
eyewitness's impression of Gauranga's form. Raga sindhura.*[^04-10]

**3.1.** The beauty of His face is like gold tried on the touchstone;
one glance, and the mind of the whole world is filled with longing.

**3.2.** Without any cause Gora's face smiles;
He is clad in yellow silk.[^04-11]

**3.3.** Drawn by the fragrance of His body,
a young bee has come flying;

**3.4.** round and round it circles at His feet,
humming sweetly.

**3.5.** In Govinda Ghosha's heart it awakens:
if I do not see Gora, everything tastes of poison.

[^04-10]: The signature is "Govinda Ghosha". PK: 18th pallava "The form of Sri Gauranga, etc." (vol. 3, PDF p. 248, printed
p. 237; MS P-R-Sa no. 2253); GPT1 — p. 116, no. 17; GPT2 — sect. 3.1, no. 17 (almost without variants). Majumdar quotes
from it the lines "without cause Gora's face smiles" and "if I do not see Gora, everything tastes of poison".
[^04-11]: "Without cause" (vini) — the smile comes not from an outward occasion but from inner joy. Yellow silk (pita-pata) is
Krishna's garment; in Navadvipa the Lord, in Krishna's mood, asked for yellow cloth (cf. PK 2122, chapter 3, no. 1). MS
P-R-Sa: "mukhe" ("on the face").

## 4. Govinda Ghosha — "śrīdāma sudāma saṅge ye rasa karilum̐ raṅge…" (PK 2128; BR, p. 919)
*Lila: Navadvipa — the Lord remembers the pastimes of Vrindavana and, crying "The flute, the flute!", falls senseless into
Gadadhara's lap; then, in Radha's mood, He repeats Her name and calls Lalita and Vishakha. Around Him are Vasu Ghosha,
Ramananda, Srivasa, Jagadananda, Narahari. According to Majumdar — an eyewitness's testimony; he cites the line about
Narahari as proof that Narahari Sarakara was with the Lord already in Navadvipa. Raga mangala (PK, GPT), dhanashi (BR).*[^04-12]

**4.1.** "The pastimes I enjoyed so gladly with Shridama and Sudama!.." —
saying this, the Lord cries out in agitation.
Crying "The flute, the flute!", Gaurahari loses consciousness,
and the Lord falls into Gadadhara's lap.[^04-13]

**4.2.** The rasa-lila, Vrindavana, the dear friends and girl-companions —
waves of prema rise.
Vasu Ghosha, Ramananda, Srivasa, Jagadananda —
with Narahari the Lord is intoxicated.[^04-14]

**4.3.** Absorbed in Radha's mood, He has become golden — Gora —
and ceaselessly repeats Radha's name.
Crying "Lalita, Vishakha!", the Lord rolls on the ground:
"Where is My hill Govardhana?

**4.4.** Where is the bank of the Yamuna? Where is My banyan Vamshivata?" —
saying this, He again loses consciousness.
Poor Govinda Ghosha received but a particle of this —
shame on such a life![^04-15]

[^04-12]: The signature is "Govinda Ghosha". PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 239–240 (printed pp. 228–229), 18th pallava, right after
Shivananda Sena's pada PK 2127; MS P-R-Sa no. 2235; after it PK notes "Such is the description of absorption in bhava".
Narahari Chakravarti quotes the pada in BR (wave 12; ed. 1913, p. 919; ed. 1960, vv. 2997–3000) among the testimonies to
the Lord's moods in Navadvipa; GPT1 — pp. 281–282, no. 15; GPT2 — sect. 4.3, no. 15. Majumdar quotes the line about Vasu
Ghosha, Ramananda, Srivasa, Jagadananda and Narahari after BR. In the stage-1 catalogue the first line of the next pada
(PK 2129) was wrongly assigned to PK 2128.
[^04-13]: Shridama and Sudama are Krishna's cowherd friends in Vraja; BR and GPT read "Shridama and Subala". The Lord in
Krishna's mood remembers His pastimes with His friends. Gadadhara Pandita, according to the *Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika*, is a
manifestation of Radha in Gaura's lila (cf. chapter 3, no. 1).
[^04-14]: "Ramananda" is probably Ramananda Vasu of Kulinagrama (the Lord met Ramananda Raya only after His sannyasa). BR and
GPT read "the Lord dances with Narahari". Majumdar sees in the line proof that Narahari Sarakara was a companion of the Lord
already in Navadvipa.
[^04-15]: "In Radha's mood… became golden" — cf. CC Adi 4: Krishna took on Radha's lustre and mood to taste Her love.
Vamshivata is the banyan in Vrindavana under which Krishna played the flute. BR and GPT1 read "nā pāyala lavaleśe" — "did
not receive even a particle"; P-R-Sa, BR and GPT — "e chāra jīvana" — "this wretched life". The signature is the usual
formula of humility.

## 5. Vasu Ghosha — "dekhata jhulata gauracandra…" (PK 1550)
*Lila: Navadvipa — the swing festival (jhulana) in the bright fortnight of Shravana: the devotees swing Gaurachandra, the
townspeople come running at the cries of "Hari, Hari!". In PK — the gaura-chandrika opening the section on the swinging
of Radha and Krishna. According to Majumdar — a pada about an event Vasu Ghosha saw himself. Raga jayajayanti.*[^04-16]

**5.1.** Behold: Gaurachandra is swinging,
the wondrous jewel among the twice-born;
the utmost of the Creator's making, a matchless form
that outshines tested gold.

**5.2.** Many devotees push the swing,
surrounding Gaurachandra;
in joy the cries of "Jaya!" sound again and again,
overflowing the town in a wave.[^04-17]

**5.3.** Eyes like lotuses, a spotless face
that outshines the autumn moon;
the townspeople come running in a throng,
hearing the cries of "Hari, Hari!".

**5.4.** Blessed is the Kali age, blessed Gora's descent,
blessed, blessed the Suradhuni!
Nothing but Gorachand is in the heart —
so says Vasu Ghosha, having understood this.[^04-18]

[^04-16]: The signature is "Vasu Ghosha". PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 456 (printed p. 441), 30th pallava of the 3rd shakha ("The
swing lila"), under the heading "Now, the swinging game in the bright fortnight of Shravana. Jhulana. Here — Sri
Gaurachandra"; MS P-R-Sa no. 2015. In GPT (GPT1, pp. 323–324, no. 8; GPT2, section on the jhulana, no. 8) the pada is
shorter — three couplets: after the first two comes "Eyes like lotuses… outshines the autumn moon; / with Gadadhara He
swings joyfully — seeing it, Shiva-Ram is blessed", i.e. the signature of the poet Shivarama. Majumdar counts PK 1550
among Vasu Ghosha's historically valuable padas describing what the poet saw himself (the jhulana); we accept the
signature of Vasu after PK.
[^04-17]: The end of the couplet is damaged in the PK scan; we read "uthale nagara bhariyā" ("overflowing the town in a
wave"); GPT: "uṭhata nāgara nadīyā" ("[the din] rises in the town of Nadia").
[^04-18]: The Suradhuni is the Ganga, on whose bank the swing was set up. "Having understood this" — having understood that
Gaura is the Lord Himself.

## 6. Narahari — "āju racita nava ratana-him̐ḍora…" (PK 1559)
*Lila: Navadvipa — the jhulana: on the bank of the Ganga, under a tall tree, a new jewelled swing has been set up; the
companions swing Gaura, sing and dance to the drums, the people of Nadia come running, the gods shower the Lord with
flowers. In PK — a gaura-chandrika in the same section on the jhulana. Raga imana-beloyara.*[^04-19]

**6.1.** *(Refrain)* Today a new jewelled swing has been set up;
there, on the bank of the Suradhuni, under a tall tree, —
the young Gaura, full of rasa.

**6.2.** The skilful companions gently push the swing
and sing melodies, intoxicated with sweet rasa;
they call out the syllables of the rhythm — "khol, khol, tak, thai-thai" —
dance sweetly and play in every manner.[^04-20]

**6.3.** In the town of Nadia no one has stayed at home:
from every side men and women come;
the joy in their hearts grows ever greater
as they behold the Lord's smiling moon-face.

**6.4.** The gods in the sky with their retinues, in bliss,
shower flowers and cry "Jaya!";
Narahari says: the world has gone mad with joy —
who can describe this wondrous, boundless play?[^04-21]

[^04-19]: The signature is "Narahari". PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 460 (printed p. 445), 30th pallava, the third pada of the section
on the jhulana after the padas of Shivarama (PK 1556–1557, the swinging of Radha and Krishna) and Uddhava Dasa (PK 1558,
Gaura swinging with Gadadhara); MS P-R-Sa no. 2103. GPT1 — p. 326, no. 16 (raga imana); GPT2 — section on the jhulana,
no. 16. S. Ray's index of poets assigns PK 1557 to Narahari, but that is Shivarama's pada on the swinging of Radha and
Krishna; the gaura-pada signed Narahari in this section is PK 1559. The attribution to Narahari Sarakara is not proven: the
signature "Narahari" is also borne by padas of Narahari Chakravarti, and the language here is Vrajabuli, which according
to Majumdar is absent from Sarakara's genuine padas.
[^04-20]: The khol is a clay drum (mridanga); "tak, thai-thai" are rhythmic syllables of the dance. For "play" (vāota) MS
P-R-Sa reads "vājāyata" (same sense).
[^04-21]: "Has gone mad" (umatāyala) — intoxicated with the joy of prema at the sight of the Lord.

## 7. Chaitanyadasa — "gaurāṅga-cāndera mane ki bhāva uṭhila…" (PK 1169)
*Lila: Navadvipa — the goshtha-lila: seeing Gauridasa, the Lord remembers His play as a cowherd boy, asks for the milking
rope and the milk pail, calls the cows Dhavali and Shangali and His friends Shridama and Sudama; Nityananda embraces Him. In
PK — the gaura-chandrika to the goshthashtami festival. According to Majumdar — the same goshtha-lila (Gauridasa, the
milking rope) as in Vasu Ghosha. Raga bhupali.*[^04-22]

**7.1.** What bhava has arisen in the heart of Gaurangachand?
It seems He has remembered His former deeds.

**7.2.** Seeing Gauridasa's face, He rejoices at heart
and calls aloud: "Bring the milking rope!

**7.3.** Today is an auspicious day — let us go to the pasture:
from today I shall begin to milk the cows.

**7.4.** Where are Dhavali and Shangali? Where are Shridama and Sudama?
Give the milk pail into My hands, Rama!"[^04-23]

**7.5.** Beside Himself with bhava is the son of Shachi;
and at once Nityananda comes and embraces Him.

**7.6.** Chaitanyadasa says: the milking rope
Gauridasa has lost — the gopis have stolen it.[^04-24]

[^04-22]: The signature is "Chaitanyadasa". PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 286, 20th pallava of the 3rd shakha, the first pada of the
section "Goshthashtami-yatra", under the heading "Sri Gaurachandra"; MS P-R-Sa no. 1700. GPT1 — p. 331, no. 32 (raga
bhupala); GPT2 — no. 32 — with minor variants. Goshthashtami (Kartika, eighth day of the bright fortnight) is the festival
of Krishna's first going out to herd the cows. Majumdar regards Chaitanyadasa (probably of Gadadhara's branch) as a
contemporary and compares the pada with the goshtha-lila in Vasu Ghosha (BR, p. 935; chapter 1, no. 11) and Vamshivadana
(PK 2564; chapter 1, no. 12).
[^04-23]: Dhavali ("the white one") and Shangali (śāṅalī, "the dark one"; GPT — Shamali, the same sense) are Krishna's cows.
"Rama" is Balarama: so the Lord addresses Nityananda, who in Krishna's lila is Balarama. Shridama and Sudama are Krishna's
cowherd friends.
[^04-24]: A playful signature: Gauridasa Pandita in Krishna's lila is the cowherd boy Subala (according to the
*Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika*), and in Vraja the gopis hide the milking rope to delay Krishna. GPT and MS P-R-Sa read "ḍuri"
for "daṛi" (same sense).

## 8. Nayanananda — "kali-ghora-timire garāsala jaga-jana…" (PK 2204)
*Praise of Gaura: when the darkness of Kali had swallowed the world and people had abandoned dharma, the Creator granted,
without any sadhana, the chintamani gem — Gora, the Lord of great mercy; learning without worship of Gauranga is useless.
Raga shri (PK), suhai (GPT).*[^04-25]

**8.1.** The dense darkness of Kali has swallowed the people of the world,
dharma and righteous deeds remain far away;
without any effort the Creator brought and bestowed the chintamani gem —
Gora, the Lord of great mercy.[^04-26]

**8.2.** *(Refrain)* Brother, brother, Gora's virtues cannot be told:
however many hundred-mouthed ones, however many four-faced ones there are —
describing them, they find no end.[^04-27]

**8.3.** One who has studied the four Vedas and six darshanas
but does not worship Gauranga —
what use is his learning? As a mirror to the blind,
so is all his knowledge to him.[^04-28]

**8.4.** One who knows neither the Vedas nor learning
but knows that Gauranga is the essence of all —
says Nayanananda — he knows everything,
all perfections lie in the palm of his hand.

[^04-25]: The signature is "Nayanananda". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 270 (printed p. 259), 20th pallava ("Sri Gaurachandra — another
manner"), raga the same as that of the preceding pada (shri); MS P-R-Sa no. 2312. GPT1 — p. 32, no. 18 (raga suhai);
GPT2 — sect. 1.3, no. 18. Nayanananda (Nayana Mishra) is the nephew and disciple of Gadadhara Pandita; Majumdar counts him
among the contemporary poets. In the stage-1 catalogue a GPT-only pada signed Narahari, "gorā vaṛa dayāra ṭhākura" (NS-009),
was wrongly linked to PK 2204: the words "Gora, the Lord of great mercy" occur here too, but PK 2204 is Nayanananda's
pada.
[^04-26]: Chintamani is the wish-fulfilling gem. "Without any effort" (asādhane) — without sadhana: Gaura bestows prema by
causeless mercy, without asking about qualification (cf. CC Adi 8).
[^04-27]: "The hundred-mouthed" — Ananta-Shesha, who ever sings of the Lord with a thousand mouths; "the four-faced" — the
Brahmas of the universes.
[^04-28]: PK: "as to the eyeless [a mirror] — what is a mirror to him?"; GPT: "what is the blind man to do with a mirror?". The
six darshanas are the six philosophical schools (nyaya, vaisheshika, sankhya, yoga, mimamsa, vedanta).

## 9. Raya Ananta — "preme matta nityānanda…" (KGC, 11th kshanada)
*Praise of Nityananda: intoxicated with prema, He walks swaying, rolls on the ground with the name of Hari and weeps looking
at the face of His brother, Gaura; Advaita, seeing Him, roars; the companions sing the names of Hari and Gaura. Raga
kamoda (KGC), mangala (GPT).*[^04-29]

**9.1.** Nityananda, intoxicated with prema, the source of natural bliss,
walks swaying, swaying;
intoxicated with His brother's mood, knowing all truths,
crying "Hari!" He rolls on the ground.[^04-30]

**9.2.** *(Refrain)* Nitai's body is moulded of love for Gora;
looking at His brother's face, He sinks down limply,
and streams of tears flow, watering the earth.[^04-31]

**9.3.** Advaita, the source of bliss, seeing Nitai's moon-face,
roars, and His body bristles with rapture;
they cry "Hari, Hari!", and again "Gaura, Gaura!" —
the dear companions sing His virtues.

**9.4.** The flood of Goloka's prema has blessed the earth —
a matchless, boundless ocean of rasa;
the world is intoxicated, filled with the names "Nitai — Chaitanya";
Raya Ananta begs but a drop.[^04-32]

[^04-29]: The signature is "Raya Ananta" (rāya ananta). The pada is known from KGC (11th kshanada — Krishna-ekadashi, no. 2,
a gaura-chandrika marked "of Sri Nityananda"; p. 83) and GPT (GPT1 — pp. 429–430, no. 52; GPT2 — sect. 6.1, no. 52); it had
not previously been found in PK (see below). B. B. Majumdar (1961) identifies the "Raya Ananta" of KGC with Ananta of Advaita's branch, a contemporary of the
Lord; the identification is not proven. The text follows KGC (checked against the scan).
Full PK check (chapter 16): the pada is also in PK — **PK 2328** (vol. 3, 22nd pallava, PDF pp. 313–314, label "॥৩৫॥২৩২৮॥", MS P-R-Sa no. 2432); PK signature "ananta nā pāila eka vindu" (MSS ka, kha: "rāya ananta māge eka vindu").
[^04-30]: "The source of natural bliss" (sahaje ānanda-kanda) — Nityananda ("eternal bliss") by His very nature. "Knowing all
truths" — Nityananda (Balarama) knows the hidden truth about Gaura.
[^04-31]: "Brother" (bhāiyā) is Gaura; for "looking at His brother's face" GPT reads "looking at Gadadhara's face".
[^04-32]: Goloka is Krishna's supreme abode; "the flood of Goloka's prema" is the prema that Gaura and Nitai brought to the
earth. GPT: "begs a single drop".

## 10. Vasu Ghosha — "śacīra mandire āsi duyārera pāśe vasi…" (PK 2221)
*Lila: the last night in Navadvipa — Vishnupriya wakes, does not find the Lord and comes to Shachi; Shachi and her
daughter-in-law search for Nimai with a lamp, the people of Nadia question passers-by; someone has seen Him on the road to
Kanchananagara (Katwa). According to Majumdar — a pada of Vasu Ghosha's cycle on the sannyasa ("Nimai-sannyasa"): a
historical picture with poetic exaggerations. Raga bibhasa-karuna.*[^04-33]

**10.1.** Coming to Shachi's rooms, sitting down by the door,
softly Vishnupriya speaks:
"He was in the bedchamber — where has He gone in the night,
bringing down a thunderbolt upon my head?

**10.2.** Gauranga is awake in my heart, there is no sleep in my eyes…" —
hearing this, Mother Shachi rose;
with dishevelled hair she runs, her cloth slipping off —
hearing her daughter-in-law's words.[^04-34]

**10.3.** Quickly lighting a lamp, she looked here and there,
but nowhere found a trace;
together with her daughter-in-law Vishnupriya, weeping and weeping on the road,
Shachi calls: "Nimai!"

**10.4.** Hearing this, the people of Nadia weep aloud in grief,
asking everyone for news:
if one man goes along the road, ten ask him:
"Have you seen where Gauranga went?"

**10.5.** He answers: "I saw Him on the road — no one was with Him,
He hastens along the road to Kanchananagara."
Vasu Ghosha says: such is Shachi's state —
"What if He shaves His head!"[^04-35]

[^04-33]: The signature is "Vasu Ghosha". PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 275–276 (printed pp. 264–265), 21st pallava ("Sri Gauranga's
sannyasa, etc."), the fourth pada of the pallava — after Lochana Dasa's padas PK 2219 (before dawn the Lord goes to the
Ganga and on to Kanchananagara) and PK 2220 (Vishnupriya wakes and does not find the Lord); MS P-R-Sa no. 2326. GPT1 —
p. 372, no. 20 (raga bibhasa or karuna), GPT2 — sect. 5.3, no. 20: one couplet longer (at the beginning: "She touched the
bed with her hand — and a thunderbolt fell on her head…") and with another signature ("Vasu says: ah, my Sri Gaurahari —
what if He shaves His head!"). The events — CB Madhya 28; CC Adi 17; Murari 3.1; Lochana, Madhya-khanda. Majumdar includes
PK 2221–2223, 2225, 2226, 2229 in Vasu Ghosha's sannyasa cycle. In the stage-1 catalogue the first line of PK 2220 (a pada
of Lochana Dasa) was wrongly assigned to PK 2221.
[^04-34]: Vishnupriya thought of the Lord all night: "Gauranga is awake in my heart". GPT: "…no sleep in the eyes — hearing
this, mother Shachi awoke".
[^04-35]: Kanchananagara (Kantaka-nagara) is Katwa, where the Lord took sannyasa from Keshava Bharati. "Shaves His head" —
takes sannyasa.

## 11. Vasu Ghosha — "sakala mahānta meli sakāle sināna kari…" (PK 2222)
*Lila: the morning after the Lord's departure — the devotees come to see Gauranga, but He is gone: Vishnupriya lies
prostrate, Shachi weeps at the gate and asks who taught her son sannyasa. Raga pahida.*[^04-36]

**11.1.** All the great souls together, having bathed in the morning,
came to see Gauranga.
Gauranga has gone, leaving home; Vishnupriya lies prostrate,
Shachi weeps at the outer gate.[^04-37]

**11.2.** Shachi says: "Listen, my Nitai, jewel of virtues:
who came and gave Him a mantra, who taught Him what tantra?
What has happened — I know nothing.[^04-38]

**11.3.** I was asleep in the house, knowing nothing —
what has He done, going away and leaving me?

**11.4.** What cruelty He has done! He has cast me adrift on a shoreless sea —
whose face shall I look to now?"

**11.5.** Vasudeva Ghosha says: such is Shachi's state —
she lies as if dead;

**11.6.** striking her head with her hand, she gestures to Ishana:
"Gora has gone, leaving Nadia."[^04-39]

[^04-36]: The signature is "Vasudeva Ghosha". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 276 (printed p. 265), 21st pallava, no. 5; MS P-R-Sa no. 2327,
P-R 40.34. GPT1 — p. 373, no. 22; GPT2 — sect. 5.3, no. 22 (OCR "21"). MS P-R gives a number of lines differently (see
bn/04.md).
[^04-37]: Great souls (mahānta) — the senior devotees. MS P-R: "all went to Gora", "[Vishnupriya] senseless on the ground".
[^04-38]: "Nitai" — so the main text of PK and MS P-R; MSS "kha", P-R-Sa and GPT read "Nimai": Shachi addresses her departed son.
"Mantra" and "tantra" mean initiation into sannyasa: Shachi does not know who gave her son the mantra (according to CB Madhya
28, the Lord Himself whispered the sannyasa mantra into Keshava Bharati's ear and then received it from him).
[^04-39]: Ishana is the old servant in the house of Shachi and Vishnupriya. "Gestures" — in her grief she cannot speak.

## 12. Vasu Ghosha — "kāñcananagare eku vṛkṣa manohara…" (PK 2223)
*Lila: Katwa (Kanchananagara) — Gauranga sits under a tree on the bank of the Ganga; the townspeople come running, struck by
His beauty and resolve; Keshava Bharati appears, the Lord bows to him and asks for the gift of devotion. Raga shri.*[^04-40]

**12.1.** In Kanchananagara there is a lovely tree;
on the bank of the Suradhuni — a cool and beautiful shade.

**12.2.** Beneath it the beautiful Gauranga sat down;
His body shines brighter than the lustre of gold.

**12.3.** The townspeople come running — young men and young women;
the wife leaves her husband, the ascetic leaves his japa.[^04-41]

**12.4.** Someone says: "In what land did this young nagara live?
How do the men and women of that land go on living now?"[^04-42]

**12.5.** Someone says: "He has come, treading on His wife's throat
and killing His mother's life."[^04-43]

**12.6.** At that time the magnanimous Keshava Bharati came;
seeing him, the Lord bowed down to him:

**12.7.** "Make Me Krishna's servant, Gosai, grant Me the gift of devotion!"
Vasu Ghosha says: a thunderbolt has fallen on the head.[^04-44]

[^04-40]: The signature is "Vasu Ghosha". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 276 (printed p. 265), 21st pallava, no. 6; MS P-R-Sa no. 2328. In
GPT1 (pp. 368–369, no. 10, raga shri) and GPT2 (sect. 5.3, no. 10) the pada is longer: women stand with pitchers on their
hips, the lame run leaning on sticks; the townspeople praise the mother who bore Him and plead: "Go back home, do not
become a sannyasi, do not shave Your hair"; the Lord answers: "Bless Me, mothers and fathers: I shall give My head to
Krishna's feet"; the signature — "May a thunderbolt fall on the head!". Kanchananagara (Kantaka-nagara) is Katwa; the
events — CB Madhya 28, CC Adi 17, Murari 3.2.
[^04-41]: A hyperbole: the Lord's beauty draws everyone away from their usual occupations; this is wonder at the sight of the
Lord, not worldly attraction.
[^04-42]: Nagara (nāgara) — an elegant young townsman; so the people of Katwa speak of the Lord. MS "gha": "enā gaura" ("this
Gaura"), P-R-Sa: "enā nāgara".
[^04-43]: That is, leaving His young wife and His mother in mortal grief. GPT: "has come having killed mother and father".
[^04-44]: Cf. CB Madhya 28: the Lord asks Keshava Bharati for sannyasa as a mercy, to attain service to Krishna. "A
thunderbolt" — the poet's grief: the sannyasa is settled.

## 13. Vasu Ghosha — "muṛāiyā cām̐cara cule snāna kari gaṅgā-jale…" (PK 2225)
*Lila: the sannyasa at Katwa — having shaved His curly locks and bathed in the Ganga, the Lord asks for red garments;
Keshava Bharati gives two pieces of red cloth and a kaupina; the Lord asks the devotees to bless Him "that the sannyasa may
not become a mockery and that in Vraja I may attain the Lord of Vraja", and runs off, heedless of direction. According to
Majumdar — an episode omitted by the biographers; the "Nimai-sannyasa" cycle is a historical picture with poetic
exaggerations. Raga pahida.*[^04-45]

**13.1.** Having shaved His curly locks and bathed in the water of the Ganga,
He says: "Give Me red garments."
Hearing Gauranga's words, the devotees
weep aloud.

**13.2.** Two pieces of red cloth Bharati brought and gave,
and also gave one kaupina;
touching them to His head, Gaurahari put them on,
regarding Himself as utterly lowly.[^04-46]

**13.3.** "You are My friends; give Me this blessing,
laying your hands upon My head:
I have taken sannyasa — let it not become a mockery,
let Me attain the Lord of Vraja in Vraja!"[^04-47]

**13.4.** Saying this, Gaura Raya runs, His face raised to the sky,
heedless of the quarters and the points between;
following the devotees, rolling and rolling on the ground beside them,
Vasu Ghosha weeps and sobs.[^04-48]

[^04-45]: The signature is "Vasu Ghosha". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 277 (printed p. 266), 21st pallava, no. 8; MS P-R-Sa no. 2330.
GPT1 — p. 370, no. 14; GPT2 — sect. 5.3, no. 14 (with minor variants); in GPT it is followed (no. 15) by another pada with
the same signature and similar lines ("You are the best of Vaishnavas, give Me this blessing… that going to Vraja I may
attain the Lord of Vraja"). Majumdar quotes the lines "You are My friends, give Me a blessing…" as an example of a detail
that the later biographers omitted for fear of diminishing the Lord's divinity. The preceding pada in PK (no. 2224, on the
shaving of the head) bears the signature of Rasikananda, a later poet, not Vasu Ghosha.
[^04-46]: The kaupina is a sannyasi's loincloth. "Touching them to His head" — respectfully receiving the sannyasi's garments
from the guru. The Lord's humility is an example for sannyasis (cf. CC Adi 17).
[^04-47]: The Lord plays the role of a devotee and asks for a blessing as befits a seeker: for Him sannyasa is a way to the
service of Krishna in Vraja, not renunciation for its own sake. Cf. CC Madhya 3: after the sannyasa the Lord, in ecstasy,
longs for Vrindavana.
[^04-48]: "Heedless of direction" — in ecstasy the Lord runs, thinking He is going to Vrindavana (CC Madhya 3; CB Antya 1).

## 14. Vasu Ghosha — "āre mora gaurāṅga nāyara…" (PK 2226)
*Lila: after the sannyasa — the Lord, His waterpot tied at His waist, runs wherever His eyes lead and does not turn at
Nitai's call; Nitai pleads: "All the sinners You have saved will count for something if You save me." Raga bhatiyari (PK),
suhai (GPT).*[^04-49]

**14.1.** *(Refrain)* Ah, my Gauranga, my beloved hero!
His golden body is drenched with the tears of prema.[^04-50]

**14.2.** His waterpot tied at His waist, He runs along the roads in every direction;
Nitai, His brother in prema, calls Him — He does not turn round.

**14.3.** Nitai says: "However many sinners You have saved —
all that will bear fruit if You save me.[^04-51]

**14.4.** Of all the incarnations that have been on earth,
to You alone the name Purifier of the Fallen is fitting."

**14.5.** Vasudeva Ghosha says: I am ill-starred —
seeing me fallen, do not withhold Your mercy from me.[^04-52]

[^04-49]: PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 277 (printed p. 266), 21st pallava, no. 9; MS P-R-Sa no. 2331, P-R 14.1. The last couplet (with
Vasudeva Ghosha's signature) is only in MS P-R-Sa; in the other MSS of PK the pada is unsigned. In GPT1 (p. 371, no. 17,
raga suhai) and GPT2 (sect. 5.3, no. 17) there are four couplets; there the signature is woven into the plea: "Vasu says:
Lord, however many sinners You have saved — it will be more if You save me." In the stage-1 catalogue this pada is entered
twice: VG-061 (after GPT) and VG-137 (PK 2226, with a wrong first line taken from PK 2224).
[^04-50]: Nayara (nāyara, from nāgara) — beloved, hero; GPT: "sundara" ("beautiful"), with the variant "nāyara".
[^04-51]: Nityananda speaks out of humility, as a devotee. According to CC (Madhya 3) and CB (Antya 1), after the sannyasa the
Lord wandered for three days in ecstasy through Radha-desha, and Nityananda followed Him and brought Him to Shantipura.
[^04-52]: "Ill-starred" (abhāgiyā) is the usual formula of humility in a signature.

## 15. Vasu Ghosha — "ki lāgiyā daṇḍa dhare aruṇa vasana pare…" (PK 2229)
*Lila: Navadvipa after the sannyasa — the devotees are bewildered and grieve: why has the Lord taken the staff and red
garments, shaved His head and, weeping "Radha, Radha", left His homeland; Srivasa sobs, Gadadhara can scarcely live,
tears stream from Mukunda's eyes. According to Majumdar — a pada of the sannyasa cycle. Raga bhatiyari.*[^04-53]

**15.1.** Why does He hold a staff, why has He put on red garments,
why has He shaved His hair?
Why, weeping "Radha, Radha!" with His moon-face,
why has He left His native land?[^04-54]

**15.2.** At Srivasa's loud weeping stones melt;
Gadadhara has no strength to live;
hot streams flow, like the Mandakini,
from both of Mukunda's eyes.[^04-55]

**15.3.** They go round the houses of all the great souls, consoling: "So the Creator ordained," —
but no one can be calm:
"A wife like a blazing flame — why did He leave her?
Why did He reject her love?"[^04-56]

**15.4.** What can I say of the grief? To speak is pain in the depths of the heart;
not seeing Him, my heart is torn apart.
Knowing neither day nor night, in the anguish of separation
Vasu Ghosha falls senseless.

[^04-53]: The signature is "Vasu Ghosha". PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 278–279 (printed pp. 267–268), 21st pallava, no. 12; MS P-R-Sa
no. 2334. GPT1 — p. 374, no. 26; GPT2 — sect. 5.3, no. 26 (almost without variants).
[^04-54]: After the sannyasa the Lord is in Radha's mood: for Him sannyasa is a way of service to Krishna (cf. note 47).
[^04-55]: The Mandakini is the heavenly Ganga. Srivasa, Gadadhara and Mukunda are the Lord's closest companions in Navadvipa.
[^04-56]: "Consoling: 'So the Creator ordained'" — our understanding of the line "sakala mahānta ghare vidhātā vujhāi phire"
(MSS "ka", "gha", "ca": "vujhāiyā", "kha": "vujhāite"). "Like a blazing flame" — radiant with beauty and purity (of
Vishnupriya); one may also understand "He left His wife — [now] burning like the fire [of separation]".

## 16. Vasu Ghosha — "hari hari ki nā haila nadīyā nagare…" (PK 2228)
*Lila: the lament of the women of Nadia after the sannyasa (nagari-bhava): Keshava Bharati has struck their hearts as with
a thunderbolt; the sannyasis have robbed them of their treasure; how will Vishnupriya survive now; Nadia, which was joy,
has become like Gokula after Krishna's departure. According to Majumdar — a pada of nagari-bhava. Raga pahida.*[^04-57]

**16.1.** *(Refrain)* Hari, Hari! What has not befallen the town of Nadia!
Keshava Bharati came and hurled a thunderbolt
upon the house of the souls of those full of rasa.[^04-58]

**16.2.** Giri, Puri, Bharati came and made Him an ascetic —
they snatched the jewel from the end of our cloth.
All that we and our dear companions longed for in joy —
all of it has become like a dream.[^04-59]

**16.3.** The youthful age, the attire, the curly locks on His head,
the smile lighting up His face…
We are others' wives, and even we cannot keep life in us —
how then will Vishnupriya survive?[^04-60]

**16.4.** The trees on the bank of the Suradhuni, lovely in the kadamba groves —
the heart weeps seeing the ketaki.
Nadia was joy — and has become like Gokula;
Vasu Ghosha is dying, weeping.[^04-61]

[^04-57]: The signature is "Vasu Ghosha". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 278 (printed p. 267), 21st pallava, no. 11; MS P-R-Sa no. 2333,
P-R 40.105. GPT1 — p. 373, no. 24; GPT2 — sect. 5.3, no. 24. Majumdar counts PK 2228 among Vasu Ghosha's padas of
nagari-bhava. The pada is put into the mouths of the women of Nadia; we translate faithfully to the author. Vrindavana Dasa
stresses that in this incarnation the Lord never looked at another man's wife; worship of Gaura in the spirit of
"Gaura-nagari" is not accepted by the Gaudiya tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta).
[^04-58]: "Those full of rasa" (rasavatī) — the women of Nadia, whose hearts are given to Gaura. MS P-R-Sa and GPT read
"kuliśa" for "vajara" (thunderbolt; same sense).
[^04-59]: Giri, Puri, Bharati are names of orders of sannyasis; Keshava Bharati belonged to the Bharati order. "The jewel from
the end of the cloth" — what one keeps tied in the end of one's sari.
[^04-60]: "Others' wives" — married women for whom Gaura is not a husband; the words convey the force of their grief. MSS
P-R-Sa, P-R and GPT: "how will Vishnupriya pass [her life]" (vañcive).
[^04-61]: Gokula after Krishna's departure for Mathura is an image of inconsolable separation. Kadamba and ketaki blossom in the
rainy season and recall Krishna. The second half of the first line is read variously: PK "kadambakhaṇḍite cāru", MSS "ka",
"kha", "ca" "…varu", P-R-Sa "kadamba khaṇḍita uru", GPT "kadambakhaṇḍete uru".

## 17. Madhava Ghosha — "nāce pahu kaladhauta-gorā…" (PK 2289)
*Lila: the dance of the Lord as a sannyasi — golden Gora in a kaupina and a red outer cloth, a garland at His throat, in
tears of prema and bristling with rapture, trembling like a plantain tree at dawn. The place is not named; in PK the pada
stands in the pallava on the sannyasa. According to Majumdar — one of Madhava Ghosha's four padas on the Lord's sannyasa.
Raga mayura.*[^04-62]

**17.1.** *(Refrain)* The Lord dances — golden Gora;
ceaselessly, like the full moon, shines the orb of His face;
ever is He intoxicated with the rasa of prema.

**17.2.** His two red eyes outshine the petals of a red lotus,
the two pupils are a pair of bumblebees;
as a heavenly river runs down a golden mountain,
so streams of prema flow down His breast.

**17.3.** His waist is slenderer than a lion's, on it a slender kaupina,
the outer cloth is red in colour;
at the throat a garland, the ornaments glow with light,
the nose is like an opening sesame flower.[^04-63]

**17.4.** The two arms are like a pair of golden lotus stalks,
the two hands — the play of lotuses;
the red lotus cannot compare with His feet —
at their touch the earth rejoices.

**17.5.** From feet to head His body bristles with rapture,
like a kadamba flower in full beauty;
like a plantain at dawn His body trembles again and again, —
captivating the heart of Madhava Ghosha.[^04-64]

[^04-62]: The signature is "Madhava Ghosha". PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 299–300 (printed pp. 288–289), 21st pallava, no. 72, under the
heading "Another manner"; MS P-R-Sa no. 2393. In GPT1 — p. 153, no. 123 (raga mayura), with the reading "nāce pahu avadhūta
gorā" ("the Lord dances — Gora the avadhuta"); in GPT2 — twice: sect. 3.1, no. 123 (likewise) and sect. 4.2, no. 38
("kaladhauta"). MSS "ka", "kha", "ca" of PK also read "avadhauta" — "avadhuta" (a wanderer above all rules). Majumdar counts
PK 2289 among Madhava Ghosha's four padas on the Lord's sannyasa. In the stage-1 catalogue this pada is entered three times
(MG-001, MG-002, MG-007).
[^04-63]: "Donā" (donāra mālā) — the meaning is unclear (perhaps a garland of dona leaves or flowers); MS P-R-Sa: "at the
throat a garland sways" (dolaye). The sesame flower is a traditional comparison for a beautiful nose.
[^04-64]: Bristling hair (pulaka) and trembling are sattvika-bhavas, signs of prema; the kadamba flower with its protruding
filaments is an image of a body bristling with rapture. The editor of PK suggests the reading "pravāte" — "in the wind"
instead of "prabhāte" — "at dawn".

## 18. Vasu Ghosha — "eta dine sadaya haila more vidhi…" (PK 1994)
*Lila: the Lord's return to the neighbourhood of Navadvipa (1514/15) — the words of a devotee who sees Gora again after a
long separation. In PK — a gaura-chandrika to "samriddhiman-sambhoga" (the fullness of the joy of Radha and Krishna's
meeting after a long separation), marked "words of the devotees". According to Majumdar — an eyewitness's pada on the
Lord's return to Navadvipa. Raga suhai.*[^04-65]

**18.1.** At last the Creator has had mercy on me:
he has brought and given me Gora, the treasury of virtues.

**18.2.** At last the cruel grief is over:
my eyes have found their purpose, seeing the moon-face.

**18.3.** Long have my eyes been fasting —
as if a thirsty chakora had found the moon.[^04-66]

**18.4.** Vasudeva Ghosha sings the song of Gora:
as if one blind from birth had gained his eyes.

[^04-65]: The signature is "Vasudeva Ghosha". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 191 (printed p. 180), the first pada of the 13th pallava of
the 4th shakha ("The outpouring of rasa of samriddhiman-sambhoga. Here — Sri Gaurachandra: words of the devotees"); MS P-R
26.1 (raga bibhasa in it). GPT1 — p. 413, no. 33 (raga suhai); GPT2 — sect. 5.5, no. 33. On the same page of GPT1 (no. 31)
stands Vasu Ghosha's pada "The people of Nadia came to see Gauranga" (chapter 1, no. 23), which Majumdar quotes from GPT,
p. 413; it is also in PK — no. 1991 (vol. 3, PDF p. 190, reading "dhāola" — "came running") — a correction to chapter 1.
Majumdar counts PK 1991, 1994 and 2273 among Vasu Ghosha's padas on the Lord's return to Navadvipa: on His way to Gauda
(1514/15) the Lord stopped at Kuliya opposite Navadvipa, and crowds flocked to Him (CC Madhya 1, 16; CB Antya 3).
[^04-66]: The chakora is a bird which, according to poetic tradition, feeds on moonlight. MS P-R: "my eyes fasted greatly".

## 19. Vasu Ghosha — "sannyāsī haiyā gelā puna yadi vāhuṛilā…" (PK 2273)
*Lila: having taken sannyasa, the Lord returned to Gauda (1514/15) but did not come to the town of Nadia; Vishnupriya's
grief: "Akrura was better — he took Krishna only to Mathura, whence news comes, but Bharati has made You a stranger in
foreign lands." According to Majumdar — a pada on the Lord's return to Navadvipa. Raga pahida.*[^04-67]

**19.1.** "Having become a sannyasi, He went away; and even when He returned,
He did not come to the town of Nadia,
to press heart to heart, making no difference between one's own and others,
and to let us see His moon-face.[^04-68]

**19.2.** *(Refrain)* Hari, Hari! Gauranga, why have You become like this?
To all You are merciful — only me, a woman, You have deprived
and cast into this ocean of grief.

**19.3.** In this early youth, having shaved Your curly locks —
I do not know what perfection You were seeking.
What worthless purana, what beast-like pandita
enjoined sannyasa on Gauranga?[^04-69]

**19.4.** Akrura was better: at the king's word he took [Krishna] away
and kept Him in the city of Mathura;
every day people come and go — from them one gets news;
but Bharati has made You a stranger in foreign lands."[^04-70]

**19.5.** Saying this, Vishnupriya, pained to the depths of her heart,
begs the earth to open.
Vasudeva Ghosha says: there is no wretch like me —
and yet my heart is breaking.[^04-71]

[^04-67]: The signature is "Vasudeva Ghosha". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 294 (printed p. 283), 21st pallava, no. 56; MS P-R-Sa no. 2377.
The same pada is printed in PK once more — no. 1801 (vol. 3, PDF p. 111), in the section on separation, before "The twelve
months of Sri Radhika's separation". GPT1 — p. 389, no. 23 (raga pahida); GPT2 — no. 23. Majumdar counts PK 2273 among the
padas on the Lord's return to Navadvipa; cf. CC Madhya 16 (the Lord at Kuliya) and chapter 1, nos. 22–23.
[^04-68]: The stanza also allows another understanding: "…[we] waited, pressing heart to heart, making no difference between
one's own and others, to see the moon-face." MSS "gha", "ca", PK 1801 and GPT: "tāra mukha" — "His face".
[^04-69]: These are Vishnupriya's words of grief, not the poet's judgement on the shastras: the sannyasa was the will of the Lord
Himself, accepted for the deliverance of living beings (CC Adi 17; CB Madhya 26). We read "ki chāra purāṇa se, paśuvat
paṇḍita ye" after PK 1801 and MSS "ka", "kha", "ca", P-R-Sa; the main text of PK 2273 has "ki chāra parāṇa ye, paśuvata
paṇḍita se" ("what worthless life…"), GPT "ki jāni parāṇa ye" ("I know not what life…").
[^04-70]: Akrura, at the order of King Kamsa, took Krishna and Balarama from Vraja to Mathura (Bhag. 10.39). "A stranger in
foreign lands" (deśāntarī) — one who has gone to distant parts.
[^04-71]: "Begs the earth to open" (dharaṇīre māgaye vidāra) — like Sita; MS P-R-Sa: "vidāya" ("begs the earth for leave to
depart"). The signature is a formula of humility.

# Chapter 5. Praise of Gaura, the Pastimes of Navadvipa, Separation, and Nityananda in Gauda

*Padas of contemporaries which Majumdar (*Sri-Chaitanya-chariter upadan*, ch. 2) assigns to the Lord's own time, in the
order of the lilas: praise of Gaura (Paramananda); a kirtana festival in Advaita's house (Parameshvara Dasa); the Lord's
pastimes with Gadadhara and His companions in Navadvipa, which Narahari Chakravarti cites in the *Bhakti-ratnakara* as the
testimony of the eyewitness Vasu Ghosha (the battle of flowers, the game of dice, the water play, the rasa, the spring
festival of colours); the Lord's ecstatic moods (Shivananda, Chaitanyadasa); the separation of Navadvipa after the
sannyasa (Paramananda, Vasu Ghosha, Chaitanyadasa, Madhava Ghosha); and Nityananda in Gauda (Kanu Thakura). The text
follows the *Padakalpataru* (PK), the *Bhakti-ratnakara* (BR), the *Kshanada-gita-chintamani* (KGC) and the
*Gaura-pada-tarangini* (GPT1 — 1st ed., 1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934); the Bengali original, variants and word-for-word
translation are in the full version of the book.*

## 1. Paramananda (Gupta) — "gorā-avatāre yāra nā haila bhakati-sāra…" (PK 2202)
