Going out into the middle of the Suradhuni, having become a young boatman,
He plays together with His companions.

**17.2.** With dear Gadadhara, in the merriment of the former play,
seated in the boat, He sports;
the boat is about to sink, a fierce wind blows —
seeing it, Gora, who wears the forest garland, laughs.[^06-56]

**17.3.** Someone makes a din, crying "Haribol" again and again,
on both banks the people of Nadia watch;
seeing the world-enchanting Boatman, enraptured,
hundreds of thousands of young wives forgot themselves.[^06-57]

**17.4.** The thief of the hearts of the world's people is my Gaurasundara:
whatever He does is before everyone's eyes.
Lowly Ramananda says: in such a fount of bliss
I alone have remained deprived.

[^06-55]: Signature: "Ramananda". PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 391 (printed p. 378), "Then the boat play on the Yamuna. Fixing the mind on
the feet of Sri Radha and Krishna, listen. First — Sri Mahaprabhu", no. 9 (mark "॥৯॥১৪১৭॥"); raga dhanashi; MS P-R-Sa
no. 1963. GPT1 — pp. 333–334, no. 43 (raga dhanashi); GPT2 — sect. 5.1 (OCR 38886). On the attribution see note 24.
[^06-56]: "The former play" (pūrava rabhasa) — Krishna's play with Radha in a boat on the Yamuna. "Who wears the forest
garland" (vanamālī) is an epithet of Krishna. MS "kha": "laughing".
[^06-57]: Cf. note 21: the image speaks of the Lord's irresistible beauty, not of worldly passion; the Gaudiya Vaishnava
tradition does not accept worship of Gaura in the mood of "gaura-nagari". MSS "ka", "gha": "having gathered" (meliyā);
"kha": "that" (tāi).

## 18. Ramananda Dasa — "suradhuni-tire āju gaura kiśora…" (PK 2615)
*Lila: jhulana on the bank of the Ganga: the companions have woven a swing of flowers, Gaura swings together with
Gadadhara; Mukunda, Madhava, Vasu and Haridasa sing of former pastimes. In PK it is a gaura-chandrika to the "swing lila" in
the section of the "eightfold eternal lila". Signature: "Ramananda Dasa". Raga saranga.*[^06-58]

**18.1.** Today on the bank of the Suradhuni is young Gaura:
the Lord is lost in the taste of the swing play.

**18.2.** Out of various flowers they have all woven a swing;
all the companions are drunk with bliss.

**18.3.** Gaura swings, and with Him Gadadhara:
how many waves of prema arise thereby!

**18.4.** Mukunda, Madhava, Vasu, Haridasa together
sing of the joyful play of former times.[^06-59]

**18.5.** How many such pastimes in the town of Nadia! —
Ramananda Dasa cherishes the hope [of seeing them].

[^06-58]: Signature: "Ramananda Dasa". PK: vol. 4, PDF p. 94 (printed pp. 84–85), 30th pallava ("The eightfold eternal lila"),
"Then the swing lila", no. 14 (mark "॥১৪॥২৬১৫॥"); raga saranga. GPT1 — p. 326, no. 18 (raga saranga); GPT2 — sect. 5.1,
no. 18. In the stage-1 catalogue (RM-009) the PK number was not given. Cf. the jhulana padas of Vasu Ghosha (PK 1550) and
Narahari (PK 1559) — chapter 4, nos. 5–6. On the attribution see note 24.
[^06-59]: Mukunda is Mukunda Datta; Madhava and Vasu are the Ghosha brothers; Haridasa is Haridasa Thakura. "The play of former
times" — the swing of Radha and Krishna in Vraja. MSS "ka", "ca" in 18.2: "lost to themselves" (vibhora); so too GPT1.

## 19. Shankara Ghosha (?) — "śrīvāsa-aṅgane vinoda vandhāne…" (KGC 30.2)
*Lila: Nityananda's dance in Srivasa's courtyard: men and gods, men and women run to see; the devotees sing, the khol and
kartals sound; in the midst, intoxicated with the mood of "Brother", Nitai dances in the guise of a wrestler, leaps and
roars, watering the earth with a rain of prema; Advaita roars, Srivasa weeps holding His feet, Mukunda sobs embracing
Gadadhara. In KGC it is a pada on Nityananda signed by Shankara Ghosha; in GPT the same pada is about Gauranga and signed by
Vrindavana Dasa. Raga mangala.*[^06-60]

**19.1.** In Srivasa's courtyard, to a wondrous rhythm,
Nityananda Raya dances;
men and gods, males and females —
all run to see.

**19.2.** The circle of devotees sings an auspicious song,
the khol and kartals sound;
in the midst, beside Himself with prema, Nitai dances,
intoxicated with the mood of "Brother".[^06-61]

**19.3.** His arms lovelier than golden pillars,
His waist slimmer than a lion's;
His face a moon, His eyes lotuses,
a form that enchants Cupid.

**19.4.** Again and again He roars, again and again He leaps,
in the guise of a wrestler He dances;
from His reddish eyes, with a rain of prema,
He waters the circle of the earth.[^06-62]

**19.5.** Upon the circle of the earth a downpour of prema
has the Avadhuta-moon poured;
the men and women of the fourteen worlds, forgetting themselves,
weep, gazing and gazing at His beauty.

**19.6.** The Lord of Shantipura roars without cease,
seeing the transformations of prema;
holding the holy feet, magnanimous
Pandita Srivasa weeps.

**19.7.** Mukunda, rejoicing, sobs and sobs,
embracing Gadadhara;
from the eyes of Thakura Abhirama prema flows,
again and again resounds "Hari, Hari!"[^06-63]

**19.8.** Knowing neither day nor night, in the taste of prema float
all the companions;
Shankara Ghosha Dasa cherishes hope
in Nitai's lotus feet.

[^06-60]: Signature: "Shankara Ghosha Dasa". KGC: 30th kshanada (purnima), no. 2 ("to Sri Nityanandachandra"), pp. 239–241;
raga mangala. GPT1 — p. 275, no. 88, and GPT2 — sect. 4.2, no. 88 (raga mangala): "In Srivasa's courtyard… Gauranga Raya
dances", without stanza 19.3, with a different ending: "Knowing neither day nor night, in the taste of prema float all the
companions; Vrindavana Dasa reveals prema at Nitai's lotus feet". B. B. Majumdar (1961) cites the pada as Shankara Ghosha's
(after KGC). The attribution is disputed (C): KGC is older than GPT, but a later substitution of the signature is possible
in the KGC recension too.
[^06-61]: "The mood of 'Brother'" (bhāiyāra bhāve) — Nityananda's love for Gauranga, His Brother (cf. chapter 5, note 53). GPT:
"the khol and kartals sound" (vājata).
[^06-62]: "In the guise of a wrestler" (mallaveśa) — Nityananda reveals the mood of Balarama. GPT in 19.5: "…all men and women,
seeing the beauty of the Lord of the world, weep".
[^06-63]: Abhirama Thakura is a companion of Nityananda (in Vraja, Shridama). GPT: "again and again resounds 'Brother,
brother!'". The Lord of Shantipura is Advaita Acharya.

## 20. Murari (?) — "premāveśe prabhure rākhiyā śāntipure…" (PK 2231)
*Lila: after the sannyasa: leaving the Lord, overwhelmed by prema, in Shantipura, Nityananda comes to Nadia; thinking of
Shachi's grief, He rolls on the ground on the way; arriving at the house, He stands before the mother, sighing heavily — His
heart breaks to tell of His Brother's sannyasa: "Gaura has taken sannyasa and come to Shantipura; He has sent Me to fetch
you." Shachi, Nitai and all Nadia weep. According to Majumdar, Murari Gupta's authorship is unproven: in one of the
manuscripts known to the compiler of GPT the same pada bears the name of Vasu Ghosha. Raga suhai.*[^06-64]

**20.1.** Leaving the Lord, overwhelmed by prema, in Shantipura,
Lord Nityananda came to the town of Nadia.

**20.2.** Thinking of Shachi's grief, Nityananda Raya
rolls on the ground in the middle of the road.

**20.3.** Barely composing Himself, Nitai came to the house;
hearing it, Shachi Thakurani came outside.

**20.4.** Standing before the mother, He sighs heavily:
His heart breaks to tell of His Brother's sannyasa.

**20.5.** "Gaura has taken sannyasa and come to Shantipura;
He has sent Me to fetch you."[^06-65]

**20.6.** Shachi weeps, Nitai weeps, the people of Nadia weep:
"Leaving everyone, Nimai has become a sannyasi!"

**20.7.** Murari says: if I do not see Gorachand,
I shall surely die — I shall enter the waters of the Ganga.[^06-66]

[^06-64]: Signature: "Murari". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 279 (printed p. 268), 21st pallava ("Sri Gauranga's sannyasa etc."), no. 14
(mark "॥১৪॥২২৩১॥"); raga suhai; MS P-R-Sa no. 2336. GPT1 — p. 378, no. 40 (raga dhanashi; in Majumdar "pp. 373–374"), GPT2 —
sect. 5.3, no. 40: longer, with three extra couplets (see note 65); in a note GPT1 gives a signature "according to some
books": "Vasu Ghosha says: do not weep, mother Shachi — for the sake of the living beings your Gaura will become the Giver of
prema". In PK the pada is followed by PK 2232 (signature "wretched Vallabha"): the women of Nadia agree to go to Advaita's
house. Cf. CC Madhya 3; CB Antya 1; Murari, *Kadacha* (book 3).
[^06-65]: In GPT after 20.4: "Seeing Nitai, Shachi fell: 'Where is my Nimai?' — 'Do not weep, mother Shachi, hear Me: Lord
Gaura, the treasure of virtues, has taken sannyasa'"; after 20.5: "Hearing of the sannyasa from Nitai's lips, Shachi fell
senseless to the ground. Nityananda raised her: 'Come to Shantipura — your Nimai is in Advaita's house'".
[^06-66]: The poet's grief, not a vow: thus padas of separation express that life without the Lord is unbearable.

## 21. Madhavi Dasa — "nīlācala haite śacīre dekhite…" (PK 1853)
*Lila: Jagadananda comes from Nilachala to see Shachi; from afar Nadia seems to him like Gokula in separation: leaves fall
out of season, the sun does not shine, birds with closed eyes do not eat and weep, repeating Gorachand's name, cows stand
silent on the road — and the Pandita falls to the ground. Continued in Chandrashekhara's pada PK 1854 (chapter 1, no. 25).
Signature: "Madhavi Dasa". Raga dhanashi (GPT).*[^06-67]

**21.1.** From Nilachala, to see Shachi,
Jagadananda comes;
stopping at a distance, he sees Nadia —
it is like Gokula.[^06-68]

**21.2.** *(Refrain)* Pandita Raya reflects:
"Shall I find Shachi or not?" —
with this thought he walks on.

**21.3.** Trees and creepers — hundreds and hundreds — he sees:
out of season their leaves are falling;
the sun's rays do not break through,
the clouds seem crimson.

**21.4.** Birds sitting on the branches, both eyes closed,
having given up fruit and water,
weep, crying aloud,
repeating the name of Gorachand.

**21.5.** Cows stand in herds on the road —
not a sound from any of them;
Thakura Pandita, [the master] of Madhavi Dasa,
crashed to the ground.[^06-69]

[^06-67]: Signature: "Madhavi Dasa". PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 129–130 (printed pp. 118–119), 10th pallava ("Separation of various
kinds"), no. 2 (mark "॥২॥১৮৫৩॥"), headed "the same raga"; MSS according to the apparatus: "ka", "gha", "ca". GPT1 — p. 407,
no. 17 (raga dhanashi); GPT2 — sect. 5.5, no. 17. It is followed in PK and GPT1 (no. 18, pp. 407–408) by Chandrashekhara's
pada PK 1854 on Jagadananda entering Shachi's house (in GPT1 with an extra couplet about the faithful servant Ishana; the
stage-1 catalogue entry ChSh-001 lacked the GPT1 reference). In the stage-1 catalogue the first line of PK 1853 was given
from its third line ("rahi katho dūre…"). Cf. CC Antya 12 (Jagadananda's journeys to Navadvipa on the Lord's commission). The
attribution to Madhavi (Madhavi Devi of Puri or another poet) is not established.
[^06-68]: "Like Gokula" (gokulapurera chanda) — Nadia after Gaura's departure resembles Gokula after Krishna's departure for
Mathura. MS "ka": "how many" (kata for katho, so too GPT).
[^06-69]: "[The master] of Madhavi Dasa" (mādhavī dāsera ṭhākura paṇḍita) — the poet calls Jagadananda his master (thakura),
i.e. he was evidently his follower. MS "gha": "sees" (dekhi), "sobbing" (ḍukuri); "ka", "ca": "of anyone" (kāra); GPT1: "fell,
crashing down" (āchāṛi).

## 22. Ramananda — "bhāla bhāli nāce gaurāṅga raṅgiyā…" (PK 2257)
*Lila: the Lord's kirtana — evidently in Nilachala: Gauranga dances, Nitai supports Him from behind; Murari, Mukunda and Vasu
sing to the kartals and mridangas; the Lord asks: "Speak, speak, Narahari!" and looks at Gadadhara; coming up to Svarupa and
Rupa, He asks for the flute and stands in the tribhanga pose; Advaita rejoices, mighty Kashishvara supports Him. The
presence of Svarupa, Rupa and Kashishvara points to Nilachala, where the Gaudiyas came for the Ratha-yatra. Signature:
"Ramananda". Raga dhanashi.*[^06-70]

**22.1.** *(Refrain)* Splendidly, splendidly joyful Gauranga dances!
Intoxicated with prema, with His roar He destroys the filth of Kali;
behind Him Nitai walks, supporting [Him].

**22.2.** Kartals and mridangas sound, all sing aloud —
with Him Murari, Mukunda, Vasu;
hearing the pada, Gora Raya [dances] —
His feet do not touch the ground —
the ocean of prema surges in waves.[^06-71]

**22.3.** Lord Gaurahari asks: "Speak, speak, Narahari!" —
and looks at Gadadhara on His left;
blessed is dear Gadadhara, whose life is Chaitanya:
"Gadai's Gauranga," people sing.[^06-72]

**22.4.** Coming up to Svarupa and Rupa, He says: "Give Me the enchanting flute!" —
now He stands bent in three places;
His speech a heap of nectar; now, softly, softly laughing,
He raises both arms and cries "Hari".[^06-73]

**22.5.** "Glory, glory to the Jewel of the twice-born!" — an auspicious cry rose up,
Advaita's bliss increased;
mighty Kashishvara supports Advaita,
and Ramananda, seeing it, rejoices.[^06-74]

[^06-70]: Signature: "Ramananda". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 289 (printed p. 278), 21st pallava, after the heading "Then a description of
Sri Gauranga's form in sankirtana", no. 40 (mark "॥৪০॥২২৫৭॥"); raga dhanashi; MS P-R-Sa no. 2362. GPT1 — p. 261, no. 42 (raga
dhanashi); GPT2 — sect. 4.2, no. 42. The next PK pada, 2258, "nāce śacīnandana bhakata-jīvana-dhana", which GPT gives with the
signature of Narahari (catalogue NS-007), is signed by Lochana Dasa in PK. On the attribution to Ramananda see note 24.
[^06-71]: "The pada" — the song the kirtaniyas sing. This tripadi line has three members.
[^06-72]: "Gadai's Gauranga" (gadāira gaurāṅga) — "Gadadhara's Gauranga", a set expression for the inseparability of the Lord and
Gadadhara Pandita.
[^06-73]: Svarupa Damodara lived with the Lord in Puri; Rupa Gosvami came to Puri in 1516–1517 (CC Antya 1). MS P-R-Sa: "Coming up
to Svarupa, He says: 'Do give Me the enchanting flute!'" (svarūpera… deha nā) — without Rupa. The request for the flute and
the tribhanga pose are the mood of Krishna (cf. note 43).
[^06-74]: "The Jewel of the twice-born" (dvijamaṇi) is Gaura. Kashishvara was the Lord's mighty servant in Puri, who cleared a
path for Him through the crowd (CC Adi 10).

## 23. Madhavi Dasa — "ānande nācata saṅge bhakata…" (PK 2290)
*Lila: the festival of colours (phagu) in Nilachala: young Gaura dances with the devotees, they shower one another with
coloured powder; the women of Puri run to see, the people of Nilachala watch the play with delight; kartals and khol sound.
Signature: "Madhavi Dasa". Raga vasanta.*[^06-75]

**23.1.** In bliss, with the devotees, dances
the young king Gaura:
scattering phagu powder, they shower one another
in the midst of the city of Nilachala.[^06-76]

**23.2.** Hearing of it, the women, full of love,
ran out to the road;
seeing Gaura, they were bewildered
and could not take their eyes off [His] face.[^06-77]

**23.3.** Raising both arms, He goes about dancing
together with the devotees;
the people of Nilachala, full of longing [to see],
watch the play with delight.

**23.4.** The kartals sound, [people] cry "Splendid, splendid!",
and the khol sounds as well;
Madhavi Dasa rejoices in his heart
and ceaselessly cries "Haribol".

[^06-75]: Signature: "Madhavi Dasa". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 300 (printed p. 289), 21st pallava, no. 73 (mark "॥৭৩॥২২৯০॥"); raga
vasanta; MS P-R-Sa no. 2394. GPT1 — p. 260, no. 39 (raga vasanta); GPT2 — sect. 4.2, no. 39. On the attribution see note 67.
[^06-76]: Phagu is the red powder (abir) with which people shower one another at the spring festival of Holi (Dola-yatra; the
Phalguna full moon is the day of the Lord's appearance). MS P-R-Sa: "city" (pura for purī).
[^06-77]: MS P-R-Sa: "having come, all look" (āsiyā sakali dekhe). On such images see note 21.

## 24. Ramananda — "hari hari aiche ki hoyava hāmāra…" (PK 3057)
*The poet's prayer: "Hari, Hari! Will I have such fortune — to see Gaura's pastimes with His companions in Nadia: dance and
kirtana on the bank of the Ganga, the Lord in His place in Srivasa's house — Nityananda on the right holding the parasol,
Gadadhara on the left; someone will take me there, and I shall see His moonlike face; and when, calling His mother, He comes
home to dine…" In PK it stands among the prayer-padas (prarthana). Signature: "Ramananda". The raga is the same as that of
the preceding pada.*[^06-78]

**24.1.** *(Refrain)* Hari, Hari! Will I have such [fortune] —
joyfully, together with the companions, Lord Gaura's
pastimes in Nadia to behold?

**24.2.** On the bank of the Suradhuni, in the taste of dancing, my Lord
will sport in kirtana —
shall I see it, filling my eyes?
My long-held desire will be fulfilled.

**24.3.** When in Srivasa's house, with His own,
He sits in His place,
Nityananda on the right holding the parasol,
Pandita Gadadhara on the left —

**24.4.** then someone will take me and lead me there,
and I shall see that moonlike face;
my whole body will be covered with thrills,
and I shall attain the bliss of prema.

**24.5.** When, calling His mother, He comes home
and sits to eat and drink —
what Ramananda will behold in bliss!
Then my two eyes will not have been in vain.[^06-79]

[^06-78]: Signature: "Ramananda". PK: vol. 4, PDF p. 253 (printed p. 244), among the prayer-padas, no. 73 (mark
"॥৭৩॥৩০৫৭॥"); "the same raga"; MS P-R-Sa no. 2554. GPT1 — pp. 491–492 (sect. 7, "Prarthana"; first line "hari hari aiche
bhāgya hoyaba hāmāra" — "will I have such good fortune"). On the attribution see note 24. A prayer in the form of a longing
to see the pastimes of Navadvipa is common among later poets (cf. the prarthanas of Narottama Dasa); but it may also be the
word of a contemporary yearning after the sannyasa for the days of Navadvipa. MSS "ka", "kha", "ca", P-R-Sa in 24.1: "to me"
(āmāra for hāmāra).
[^06-79]: "Calling His mother" (janani sambodhane) — MS "ka": "with address to the mother" (sambodhana). GPT1: "…then I shall see
[it] and make both eyes fruitful".

# Chapter 7. Praise of Nitai and Chaitanya, the Appearance of Nityananda and Gaura, Nimai's Childhood, the Abhisheka, Kirtanas, the Sannyasa, Nilachala, the Deities at Ambika, Prayers

*Padas of contemporaries known from the *Padakalpataru* (PK), in the order of the lilas: praise of Nitai and Chaitanya
and of the sankirtana (Krishnadasa); Nityananda's appearance at Ekachakra (Krishnadasa); Gaura's appearance and His
childhood play in Shachi's house (Vasu Ghosha); the Govardhana of bhakti in Navadvipa (Chaitanyadasa); the abhisheka in
Srivasa's house (Krishnadasa); the dance of the Lord hearing of Vrindavana (Ramachandra); Nityananda's dance (Vasu
Ramananda); separation in autumn (Krishnadasa); the sannyasi Lord on the seashore (Ramananda); Nilachala (Paramananda);
the Deities of Gaura and Nitai in Gauridasa's house at Ambika (Krishnadasa); and Krishnadasa's prayers. The text follows
PK, checked against the scans, with the variants of the *Bhakti-ratnakara* (BR) and the *Gaura-pada-tarangini* (GPT1 —
1st ed., 1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934); the Bengali original, variants and word-for-word translation are in the full version of the book.*

## 1. Krishnadasa — "prema-sindhu gorā rāy…" (PK 2343)
*Praise of Nitai and Chaitanya: Gaura is an ocean of prema, Nitai the wave upon it; Rupa and Sanatana, diving into this
ocean, bring up jewels and string them on the thread of bhakti; the kirtana of the lilas is a blossoming lotus forest.
In PK it stands in the 23rd pallava (the form and qualities of Chaitanya and Nityananda). Raga dhanashi.*[^07-1]

**1.1.** An ocean of prema is Gora Raya, Nitai the wave upon it,
on all four sides — the wind of compassion.
Prema surges and spills over — the world draws breath again:
everyone's heat and thirst are gone.[^07-2]

**1.2.** *(Refrain)* Behold, behold the merciful Nitai and Chaitanya!
To the swans and chakravakas — the devotees — They call: "Drink, drink!"
Having found such a thing, why stay deprived?[^07-3]

**1.3.** Diving, Rupa and Sanatana bring up many treasures, jewels,
and carefully string a garland of them.
Making the creeper of bhakti the thread — take it, souls, adorn your necks:
the scorching heat of the sun will go.[^07-4]

**1.4.** The sankirtana of the taste of the lilas is a blossoming lotus forest,
whose fragrance has filled the world.
The forest of flowers has bloomed, the bees are intoxicated —
yet Krishnadasa, having found it, has stayed deprived.[^07-5]

[^07-1]: Signature: "Krishnadasa". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 319 (printed p. 308), 23rd pallava, no. 12 (mark "॥১২॥২৩৪৩॥"); raga
dhanashi; ms. P-R-Sa no. 2447. GPT1 — pp. 32–33, no. 19 (raga dhanashi); GPT2 — sect. 1.3, no. 19. Which Krishnadasa wrote
the pada is not established: PK gathers under this signature padas of different poets (including Krishnadasa Kaviraja);
the mention of Rupa and Sanatana dates it not earlier than 1514–1516. Majumdar does not discuss it.
[^07-2]: "The world draws breath again" (jagata hāphān chāṛe) — like one exhausted by the heat breathing with relief; ms.
"ka" and GPT1 — hākāla ("the world cries out"). Ms. "kha": "sin" (pāpa) instead of "heat".
[^07-3]: Hamsa-swans and chakravakas are water birds living on the ocean of prema; the image continues the ocean metaphor.
[^07-4]: Rupa and Sanatana Gosvami are disciples of the Lord whose books opened the treasures of bhakti. Ms. "gha": "the
thread of a book" (grantha) instead of "creeper". "The heat of the sun" is worldly suffering; GPT1: "your burning will go".
[^07-5]: The humility usual with Vaishnava poets: the poet considers himself deprived of what is being given to all.

## 2. Krishnadasa — "navadvīpe śuni siṃhanāda…" (PK 2089)
*The sankirtana in Navadvipa as a battle: Gaurachandra is the great chariot-warrior, Nityananda the general, Advaita the
vanguard; the enemies are bound with a noose of the rope of prema; the Lord, mounted on the elephant of Kali, sets up
outposts on every side. In PK it stands in the 17th pallava (the dance and pastimes of Gauranga). Raga ramakeli.*[^07-6]

**2.1.** *(Refrain)* In Navadvipa a lion's roar was heard!
The Vaishnavas arrayed themselves, starting the sankirtana of Hari —
the fools took it for a calamity.[^07-7]

**2.2.** Gaurachandra is the great chariot-warrior, Nityananda the general,
Advaita at the head of the army.
With a noose of the rope of prema they bound many foes;
unceasingly thunders the name of Hari.

**2.3.** Sri Chaitanya wages the battle, mounted on the elephant of Kali,
in the array of a hero, the crusher of godlessness.
To deliver the souls of the Kali age the Lord came to the earth
and set up outposts on all four sides.[^07-8]

**2.4.** High and low — all obtained the treasure of prema
by a particle of the mercy of Nitai and Chaitanya.
But Krishnadasa, seeing Yama before him, grieves deeply:
he has not found even a trace of prema.[^07-9]

[^07-6]: Signature: "Krishnadasa". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 226 (printed p. 215), 17th pallava, no. 31 (mark "॥৩১॥২০৮৯॥"); raga
ramakeli; ms. P-R-Sa no. 2198; after the pada a PK rubric: here the pada "kali timira ghora…" is also sung. GPT1 — p. 274,
no. 85 (raga ramakeli); GPT2 — sect. 4.2. The catalogue's former first line ("kali-jīva tarāite…") is the beginning of
the third stanza. Which Krishnadasa it is has not been established.
[^07-7]: "A lion's roar" is the thundering kirtana; "the fools" (mūṛhamati) are the opponents of the kirtana in Navadvipa
(cf. CB Madhya 23).
[^07-8]: "Mounted on the elephant of Kali" (kali-gaje ārohaṇa): the Kali age, subdued, serves the Lord as His war elephant;
mss. "ka", "kha", "ca": "mounted on an elephant" (kari-gaje). GPT1: "Nityananda is the charioteer" (sārathi) instead of
"the general". The Lord crushes godlessness (pāṣaṇḍa) not with weapons but with the holy name: cf. CC Adi 17 — the
Kazi subdued by the kirtana.
[^07-9]: Yama is the lord of death. The self-abasement usual with Vaishnava poets.

## 3. Krishnadasa — "jaya jaya mahāprabhu jaya gauracandra…" (PK 2847)
*A nama-kirtana: glory to Mahaprabhu, His parents, Navadvipa, the Ganga, the Lord's consorts and His devotees. In PK
it is the gaura-chandrika to the morning lila (32nd pallava, the "eightfold lila"). Raga "kau".*[^07-10]

**3.1.** Glory, glory to Mahaprabhu, glory to Gaurachandra!
Glory to Vishvambhara, glory to the ocean of mercy!

**3.2.** Glory to the Son of Shachi, glory to Pandita Nimai!
Glory to Mishra Purandara, glory to Mother Shachi!

**3.3.** Glory, glory to Navadvipa, glory to the Suradhuni!
Glory to Lakshmi and Vishnupriya, the Lord's consorts![^07-11]

**3.4.** Glory, glory to the devotees who dwell in Navadvipa!
Glory, glory to the feet of Nityananda and Advaita!

**3.5.** Ever hoping for the two feet of Nityananda,
Krishnadasa has sung this nama-sankirtana.[^07-12]

[^07-10]: Signature: "Krishnadasa". PK: vol. 4, PDF pp. 179–180 (printed pp. 170–171), 32nd pallava, "Now the morning
lila. Sri Gaurachandra", no. 10 (mark "॥১০॥২৮৪৭॥"); raga "kau" (an abbreviation; so also GPT1). GPT1 — pp. 22–23,
no. 62 (without couplet 3.3); GPT2 — sect. 1.2, no. 62. The attribution is not established; the hope placed in Nityananda's feet
in the signature points rather to a poet of Nityananda's branch than to Krishnadasa Kaviraja.
[^07-11]: Mishra Purandara is Jagannatha Mishra, the Lord's father. Suradhuni is the Ganga. Lakshmi is Lakshmipriya, the
Lord's first consort; Vishnupriya the second.
[^07-12]: Nama-sankirtana — the singing of the Lord's names.

## 4. Krishnadasa — "rāṛhadeśe nāma ekacakrā grāma…" (PK 1116)
*Nityananda's appearance: in Radha-desha, in the village of Ekachakra, in the house of Hadai Pandita, on the bright
thirteenth of Magha, Haladhara was born; Hadai celebrates his son's birth, the earth sways with joy; Advaita in
Shantipura perceives that Rama, Krishna's elder brother, has appeared. In PK: "Then the appearance of Shri
Nityananda-chandra" (3rd shakha, 18th pallava, the "janma-lila"). Raga shri.*[^07-13]

**4.1.** In Radha-desha, in the village named Ekachakra,
in the house of Hadai Pandita,
in the auspicious month of Magha, on the bright thirteenth,
Haladhara was born.[^07-14]

**4.2.** Hadai Pandita, filled with joy,
holds a festival for his son.
The circle of the earth sways,
unable to contain the bliss.

**4.3.** The Lord of Shantipura, rejoicing,
divined something:
in His heart He knew: surely there is born
Rama, the elder brother of Krishna.[^07-15]

**4.4.** The hearts of the Vaishnavas grew serene,
they float in an ocean of bliss.
"Even this wretched sinner will be delivered,"
says the unhappy Krishnadasa.[^07-16]

[^07-13]: Signature: "Krishnadasa". PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 265 (printed p. 252), 3rd shakha, 18th pallava (the "janma-lila"),
section "tataḥ śrīnityānandacandrāvirbhāvaḥ", no. 5 (mark "॥৫॥১১১৬॥"); raga shri; ms. P-R-Sa no. 1614. GPT1 — p. 416, no. 7
(raga shri); GPT2 — sect. 6.1, no. 7. In the catalogue the pada was listed as PK 1117 (PK 1117 is the next pada, below,
no. 5). Which Krishnadasa it is has not been established.
[^07-14]: Radha-desha (Rarh) is the region west of the Ganga. Hadai Pandita (Hadai Ojha) is Nityananda's father. Haladhara
("bearer of the plough") is Balarama: Nityananda is Balarama Himself. Magha is January–February; the same date is in the
*Advaita-prakasha*. Ms. "ka" and P-R-Sa: "Radha-desh" (without the locative ending).
[^07-15]: The Lord of Shantipura is Advaita Acharya. Rama is Balarama, Krishna's elder brother.
[^07-16]: "Unhappy" (dukhī) is the poet's humble name for himself.

## 5. Krishnadasa — "bhuvana-ānanda-kanda valarāma nityānanda…" (PK 1117)
*Praise of Nityananda, descended in the Kali age: He is golden like the champaka, the nails of His fingers are a row of
moons, His face eclipses the full moon, His arms reach His knees; bee-devotees hover at His lotus feet. In PK it is the
next pada of the same section. Raga suhai.*[^07-17]

**5.1.** The root of the world's bliss, Balarama Nityananda,
has descended in the Kali age.
All sorrows are gone: seeing that moon-face,
people float on waves of bliss.[^07-18]

**5.2.** *(Refrain)* Glory, glory to Nityananda-Rama!
His lustre is that of the golden champaka, on His fingers a row of moons;
by His beauty He has conquered millions of Kamadevas.[^07-19]

**5.3.** Seeing that face, to what can the full moon compare?
Long eyes, eyebrows like bows.
Arms reaching the knees, palms like land-lotuses,
a waist slender as a lion's.[^07-20]

**5.4.** At His lotus feet the bee-devotees hover;
His half-words pour out nectar.
"Now the souls of this Kali age will be delivered,"
says the humble, unhappy Krishnadasa.[^07-21]

[^07-17]: Signature: "Krishnadasa". PK: vol. 2, PDF pp. 265–266 (printed pp. 252–253), 18th pallava, no. 6 (mark
"॥৬॥১১১৭॥"); raga suhai (P-R-Sa: shri); ms. P-R-Sa no. 1615. GPT1 — p. 416, no. 8 (raga suhai); GPT2 — sect. 6.1, no. 8.
Which Krishnadasa it is has not been established.
[^07-18]: Mss. "ka", "kha": haila (the same form, "descended"); P-R-Sa: "in an ocean of bliss" (sāgare) instead of "on waves".
[^07-19]: According to Ray's apparatus, the refrain is marked only in ms. P-R-Sa; in GPT1 too it stands after the first
stanza. Kamadeva is the god of love: the Lord's beauty surpasses that of millions of Kamadevas.
[^07-20]: "As a lion's" — literally "as the elephant's enemy's" (kari-ari); ms. "ka": airi, "ca": vairi (same meaning).
[^07-21]: Ms. "kha": "bringing nectar" (āniyā). Ms. "ka": "are delivered" (haila), P-R-Sa: haiba ("will be delivered");
GPT1: "the souls of the Kali age are all delivered".

## 6. Vasu Ghosha — "jaya jaya kalarava nadiyā nagare…" (PK 1121; BR, p. 763)
*Gaura's appearance: in Nadia cries of "Jaya!" resound; at the full moon of Phalguna, under the Phalguni nakshatra,
Gora was born to Shachi; as in the Dvapara age Krishna appeared to Yashoda, so now He has appeared in Nadia to deliver
the souls of the Kali age. Narahari Chakravarti cites the pada in the *Bhakti-ratnakara* in the account of the Lord's
appearance. According to Majumdar, Vasu Ghosha's padas on the Lord's birth and childhood are poetic invention: Vasu was
not in Navadvipa at that time. Raga tudi (BR: basanta).*[^07-22]

**6.1.** Glory, glory! — cries resound in the city of Nadia:
Gora has appeared from Shachi's womb.[^07-23]

**6.2.** At the full moon of Phalguna, under the Phalguni nakshatra,
at an auspicious moment Gora was born, the jewel of the twice-born.

**6.3.** His radiance eclipsed the full moon —
the darkness, losing hope, went far away.[^07-24]

**6.4.** In the Dvapara age Krishna appeared in Nanda's house —
the whole world knows of His birth from Yashoda.

**6.5.** Now He has been born to Shachi in Nadia
to deliver all the souls of the Kali age.

**6.6.** So says Vasudeva Ghosha, cherishing hope in his heart,
trusting in his mind in the two feet of Gaura.[^07-25]

[^07-22]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha". PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 267 (printed p. 254), 18th pallava, no. 10 (mark "॥১০॥১১২১॥");
raga tudi; ms. P-R-Sa no. 1619. BR, 12th wave: 1912/1913 eds. — p. 763 ("tathāhi gīte vasantaḥ"), 1960 ed. — vv.
895–900; in BR lines 6.3–6.5 differ (see VAR). GPT1 — p. 51, no. 2 (raga tudi or karuna); GPT2 — sect. 2.1, no. 2.
Majumdar: Vasu's padas on the birth and childhood (PK 1121, 1150, 1151, 1161 and others) are the poet's invention; we
translate them as a poetic contemplation of lilas known from the biographies (CB Adi 2–5; CC Adi 13–14).
[^07-23]: "From Shachi's womb" is the ordinary language of the biographies about the Lord's appearance: the Lord is not born
like a conditioned soul but manifests Himself, as Krishna appeared to Devaki (Bhag. 10.3; CC Adi 13). BR: "Gorachand was
born".
[^07-24]: The Lord appeared during a lunar eclipse (CC Adi 13.89–98); the poet plays on this: the moon was dimmed before His
radiance.
[^07-25]: Vasudeva Ghosha is Vasu Ghosha. Mss. "ka", "kha", P-R-Sa: bharasā (the same). BR: "sings Vasudeva Ghosha…
trusting in the two feet of Lord Gora".

## 7. Vasu Ghosha — "gorā-rūpe ki diva tulanā…" (PK 1137)
*Gaura's form: neither gold of the highest assay, nor lightning in a cloud, nor a garland of champakas, nor the golden
ketaki, nor gorochana can compare with Him; the fragrance of His body surpasses kunkuma. In PK it is the gaura-chandrika
to the festival of Sri Radha's birth; no raga is given.*[^07-26]

**7.1.** To what shall I compare the form of Gora?
Even gold of the highest assay does not compare with it.[^07-27]

**7.2.** Lightning in a cloud is no likeness of this form;
a garland of champakas does not compare with it.

**7.3.** The petal of the golden ketaki does not compare,
pure gorochana does not compare.[^07-28]

**7.4.** The fragrance of His body, surpassing kunkuma, captivates the heart.
Says Vasu: out of what did the Creator fashion Gora?[^07-29]

[^07-26]: Signature: "Vasu". PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 274 (printed p. 261), 18th pallava, "Now the festival of Sri Radhika's birth.
There — Sri Gaurachandra", no. 11 (mark "॥১১॥১১৩৭॥"); according to Ray's apparatus — ms. P-R-Sa nos. 371 and 1641 and ms.
P-R no. 21 (the pada recurs in the manuscripts). GPT1 — p. 110, no. 1 (raga shri; the beginning of the section on the
Lord's form); GPT2 — sect. 3.1, no. 1. According to Majumdar, PK 1030 = 1137 (the pada stands twice in PK); he counts it
among Vasu's padas on Gaura's form.
[^07-27]: "Gold of the highest assay" (kaṣila vāna sonā) — gold tested on the touchstone; P-R: another reading (kaṣida kāṃcā).
Mss. "ka", "kha", "ca" and GPT1: "likeness" (upamā) instead of "comparison".
[^07-28]: Ketaki is the screw-pine with golden flowers; gorochana is a bright yellow pigment. P-R-Sa and P-R, instead of
"golden": "with the form" (rūpera, rūpe).
[^07-29]: Kunkuma is saffron. P-R-Sa, P-R: "the form, so captivating" (rūpa ati) instead of "the fragrance of the body".

## 8. Vasu Ghosha — "eka mukhe ki kahava gorācāndera līlā…" (PK 1141)
*The infant Gaura crawls about the courtyard: saliva trickles down His little face, His lips are redder than a ripe
bimba, on His little arms are bracelets, on His feet anklets, on His neck a tiger's claw amulet, on His back a golden
chain with a silken tassel. In PK: "Now parental love befitting infancy. Sri Gaurachandra" (the beginning of the 19th
pallava). Raga tudi.*[^07-30]

**8.1.** With one mouth how can I tell the lilas of Gorachand?
Shachi's Child crawls on all fours, starting all kinds of games.[^07-31]

**8.2.** Saliva trickles down His little face — how lovely it is!
His lips are redder than a ripe bimba fruit.[^07-32]

**8.3.** On His lovely little arms are armlets and bracelets;
on His feet makara-headed anklets, on His neck a tiger's claw.[^07-33]

**8.4.** On His back a golden chain with a silken tassel.
Says Vasudeva Ghosha: "I give my very self for Him."[^07-34]

[^07-30]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha". PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 275 (printed p. 262), 3rd shakha, 19th pallava, "atha
vātsalyaṃ kaumārakālocitaṃ yathā. śrīgauracandraḥ", no. 1 (mark "॥১॥১১৪১॥"); raga tudi; ms. P-R-Sa no. 1648. GPT1 — p. 62,
no. 2 (raga tudi); GPT2 — sect. 2.2, no. 2. Among Vasu's childhood padas Majumdar names "PK 1140" — evidently PK 1141:
PK 1140 is a pada of Uddhava Dasa on Radha's birth. On his assessment see note 22.
[^07-31]: P-R-Sa instead of the second line: "crawling, He plays in all kinds of ways".
[^07-32]: Mss. "ka", "ca": nāle (the same, "saliva"). Mss. "ka", "kha", "gha", "ca": "lovely" (sundara) instead of "red"
(suraṅga). The bimba is a fruit with a bright red skin, a common comparison for lips.
[^07-33]: Armlets (aṅgada) and bracelets (valayā), makara-headed anklets (magarā khāṛu), the tiger's claw (vāghanakha) are
common ornaments and amulets of children in Bengal.
[^07-34]: "I give my very self" (nichani āpanā) — the nichhani rite: one waves something around a beloved one and gives it
away (here — oneself) for his welfare.

## 9. Vasu Ghosha — "kiye hāma pekhaluṃ kanaka-putaliyā…" (PK 1150; BR, p. 774)
*The boy Gaura dances in Shachi's courtyard, all covered with dust, amid naked boys, crying "Hari, Hari!"; His mother
listens to the jingling of His anklet bells. Narahari Chakravarti cites the pada in the *Bhakti-ratnakara*: Srinivasa,
in Navadvipa, is told how Vishvambhara danced in this courtyard. In PK: "Now parental love befitting childhood and
boyhood. Sri Gaurachandra". Raga mayur (BR: kamoda).*[^07-35]

**9.1.** What a golden doll I have seen!
In Shachi's courtyard He dances, all grey with dust.[^07-36]

**9.2.** On all sides naked boys surround Him,
and in their midst Gora dances, saying "Hari, Hari!"

**9.3.** On reddish lotus feet the jewel of the twice-born runs about;
His mother listens with joy to the jingling of His anklet bells.[^07-37]

**9.4.** Says Vasudeva Ghosha, who knows the taste of the childhood play:
"Blessed are the people of Nadia, blessed is Navadvipa!"[^07-38]

[^07-35]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha". PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 279 (printed p. 266), 19th pallava, no. 10 (mark
"॥১০॥১১৫০॥"); raga mayur (mss. "gha", "ca": maur). BR, 12th wave: 1913 ed. — p. 774 ("gīte rāgaḥ kāmoda"), 1960 ed. —
vv. 1035–1038. GPT1 — p. 63, no. 4 (raga beloar — dashakoshi); GPT2 — sect. 2.2, no. 4. On Majumdar's assessment see
note 22.
[^07-36]: "What… I have seen" (kiye hāma pekhaluṃ) is a Vrajabuli turn of phrase.
[^07-37]: "The jewel of the twice-born" is the young brahmana Nimai; GPT1: "the sun-jewel" (dinamaṇiyā); BR: "on radiant lotus
feet". In 9.2 mss. "gha", "ca": veṛiyā (the same, "surrounding"); ms. "gha": "Gaura". Ms. "ka": "the sweet jingle of the
bells".
[^07-38]: BR after the pada: "O Srinivasa, in this courtyard Vishvambhara danced in all kinds of ways — a wonderful sight".

## 10. Vasu Ghosha — "śacīra āṅgināya nāce viśvambhara rāy…" (PK 1151; BR, p. 774)
*Hide-and-seek: Vishvambhara dances in the courtyard and, laughing, hides from His mother, covering His face with the
end of His cloth: "I have hidden!" — Shachi plays along: "Vishvambhara, I cannot see You!"; holding the end of her sari,
He skips along with the gait of a wagtail. In BR it comes right after the previous pada. The same raga (BR: vibhasa).*[^07-39]

**10.1.** In Shachi's courtyard Vishvambhara Raya dances;
laughing, turning about, He hides from His mother.

**10.2.** Covering His face with His cloth, He says: "I have hidden!"
Shachi says: "Vishvambhara, I cannot see You!"[^07-40]

**10.3.** Holding the end of His mother's sari, on restless little feet
He goes skipping with the gait of a wagtail.[^07-41]

**10.4.** Says Vasudeva Ghosha: "A wondrous beauty!
Seeing the form of the Child, the world is filled with longing."

[^07-39]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha". PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 279 (printed p. 266), 19th pallava, no. 11 (mark "॥১১॥১১৫১॥");
"tathā rāga" (mayur); ms. P-R-Sa no. 1657. BR, 12th wave: 1913 ed. — p. 774 ("gīti vibhāṣaḥ"), 1960 ed. — vv. 1040–1043.
GPT1 — p. 63, no. 5 (beloar — dashakoshi); GPT2 — sect. 2.2, no. 5.
[^07-40]: P-R-Sa: "on the face" (vadane) — the same meaning.
[^07-41]: The wagtail (khañjana) is a bird with a lively, skipping gait; a common poetic comparison.

## 11. Vasu Ghosha — "gorā nāce śacīra dulāliyā…" (PK 1161; BR, pp. 774–775)
*Shachi's darling Gora dances, the boys around Him clap their hands: "Haribol!"; on His head a red cap, on His neck golden
beads, His mother has lovingly tied His little dhoti; the poet exclaims: "Take Him in your arms — Gora is the life of my
life!" In BR it is the third pada of the same series. In PK: "Now the rasa of parental love, another mode. Shri
Gaurachandra" (the beginning of the 20th pallava). Raga bhatiyari (BR: bhatyali).*[^07-42]

**11.1.** *(Refrain)* Gora dances, Shachi's darling;
the boys have gathered around, all clap their hands,
saying "Haribol, Haribol!"

**11.2.** On His head a red cap, on His neck golden beads;
with love His mother has tied His little dhoti tight.[^07-43]

**11.3.** Lovely curling hair, a well-formed body;
a dress that charms the world, eyebrows — Kamadeva's bow.

**11.4.** Silver and golden ornaments
adorn His body charmingly.
As He lifts His feet — red lotuses —
the anklet bells ring.

**11.5.** In Shachi's courtyard He dances and dances,
babbling half-words.
Says Vasudeva Ghosha: "Hold Him, hold Him, take Him in your arms —
Gora is the life of my life!"[^07-44]

[^07-42]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha". PK: vol. 2, PDF pp. 282–283 (printed pp. 269–270), 3rd shakha, 20th pallava, "atha
vātsalyarasaḥ prakārāntaraṃ yathā. śrīgauracandraḥ", no. 1 (mark "॥১॥১১৬১॥"); raga bhatiyari; ms. P-R-Sa no. 1680. BR,
12th wave: 1913 ed. — pp. 774–775 ("punaḥ rāga bhāṭyāli"), 1960 ed. — vv. 1044–1048. GPT1 — p. 63, no. 3 (raga
bhatiyari); GPT2 — sect. 2.2, no. 3. The catalogue's former first line ("śacīra aṅgane nācaye saghane") is the
beginning of the last stanza.
[^07-43]: "Cap" (catunā) — a child's cap; ms. "ca": catulā. "Beads" (kāṃṭhi) — a string of beads. Ms. "ka": parāñāche (the
same, "has tied").
[^07-44]: Ms. "ka": "Gora, Gora is the life of my life"; BR: "Gora is like the life of my life".

## 12. Chaitanyadasa — "dekha dekha aparūpa gaurāṅga-vilāsa…" (PK 1242)
*An allegory: in Navadvipa Gauranga again manifests the lila of lifting Govardhana. He bids the people of Kali worship
the "Govardhana" of pure bhakti: the nine kinds of bhakti are its peaks, the five rasas its fruits, pulaka, tears and
trembling its adornment. The "Indra" of the Kali age, on the "Airavata" of irreligion, sends a downpour of lust,
lightnings of anger and a hail of greed, but Gauranga lifts the mountain of bhakti; Kali, put to shame, begs forgiveness
and vows not to touch those who sing the Lord's glory. In PK it is the gaura-chandrika to the "Govardhana-yatra" (3rd
shakha, 23rd pallava). Raga gandhara (P-R-Sa: dhanashi).*[^07-45]

**12.1.** *(Refrain)* Behold, behold the wondrous play of Gauranga!
Again the lifting of the hill — in the order of the former lila —
He has manifested in Navadvipa.[^07-46]

**12.2.** "People of the world, worship the Govardhana of pure bhakti!" —
such is the law He gave in the Kali age.
The nine branches of bhakti beginning with hearing are its peaks, like wish-fulfilling trees;
the five rasas are the fruits that adorn them.[^07-47]

**12.3.** Sprouts of pulaka are its beauty, streams of tears captivate the heart,
a gentle breeze is its lovely trembling.
Serve this best of hills, offering it your own senses as gifts —
you will obtain the jewel of prema, the desired boon.[^07-48]

**12.4.** Seeing how people lived, the king of the gods of the Kali age
shook with anger.
On the Airavata of irreligion, together with Indrani — evil-mindedness —
he came with his army arrayed.[^07-49]

**12.5.** The clouds of lust poured down, the thunderbolts of anger were hurled —
a great fear seized the people.
Under the blows of the stones of greed and delusion, under the harsh winds of envy and the rest,
steadfastness and dharma are ceaselessly blown away.[^07-50]

**12.6.** Seeing the fear of the living beings, the merciful Sri Gauranga
conceived a means in His heart:
Himself accepting the essence of a devotee's bhava,
He lifted the mountain of bhakti.[^07-51]

**12.7.** Under its shelter people forgot grief and sorrow,
everyone's fear of Kali was dispelled.
Then Kali, the king of the gods, ashamed of his defeat,
offers praise to the lotus feet.

**12.8.** Having begged forgiveness for his offence, he humbly says:
"All souls are under the Lord's shelter;
whoever sings Your glory — over him I have no claim," —
this he solemnly confirmed.[^07-52]

**12.9.** The Lord showed him mercy — "Blessed Kali" became his name,
and to this day the world proclaims it.
Says Chaitanyadasa: under the guise of the Govardhana lila —
from age to age the deliverance of souls.[^07-53]

[^07-45]: Signature: "Chaitanyadasa" ("caitanyadāsete vale"). PK: vol. 2, PDF pp. 312–313 (printed pp. 299–300), 3rd shakha,
23rd pallava, "atha govarddhana-yātrā. taducita-śrīgauracandraḥ", no. 1 (mark "॥১॥১২৪২॥"); raga gandhara (P-R-Sa:
dhanashi); ms. P-R-Sa no. 1776. In the catalogue this pada was wrongly listed as PK 1243 by Krishnadasa (KR-013); PK 1243
is the next pada, on the Govardhana-puja in Vraja, signed "Krishnadasa" (Krishna-lila; not translated). The pada was not
found in GPT1. Chaitanyadasa was, according to Majumdar, a contemporary of the Lord (cf. chapters 4–6); the allegorical
form, however, suggests rather a later author.
[^07-46]: Krishna lifted Govardhana, protecting Vraja from Indra's wrath (Bhag. 10.24–25); the poet sees in Gauranga's
preaching of bhakti a "repetition" of that lila.
[^07-47]: The nine kinds of bhakti are hearing, chanting, remembering and so on (Bhag. 7.5.23–24). The five rasas are shanta,
dasya, sakhya, vatsalya, madhurya. Mss. "ka", "kha", "ca", P-R-Sa: "limbs" (aṅga) instead of "peaks" (śṛṅga).
[^07-48]: Pulaka is the bristling of the body's hair in ecstasy; tears and trembling are also sattvika-bhavas. Serving the
Lord of the senses with the senses is the definition of bhakti (Narada-pancharatra, quoted in *Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu*
1.1.12).
[^07-49]: Airavata is Indra's elephant, Indrani his consort: here "the king of the gods" is Kali himself, the personified age.
[^07-50]: Ms. "kha", P-R-Sa: mahā (the same, "great").
[^07-51]: "Accepting the essence of a devotee's bhava" — in this avatara the Lord accepts the mood of His devotee (CC Adi 4).
[^07-52]: Mss. "ka", "kha", "ca": khemāiyā (a dialect form of "having begged forgiveness").
[^07-53]: "Blessed Kali" (dhanya kali) — cf. Bhag. 11.5.36 and 12.3.52: the wise praise the Kali age, for in it the highest
goal is attained by sankirtana.

## 13. Krishnadasa — "ānande bhakatagaṇa dei jaya-rava…" (PK 1570)
*Gaura's abhisheka in Srivasa's house: the devotees cry "Jaya!", Gauranga is bathed with panchagavya, panchamrita and
the water of a hundred pots; He sits on a jewelled platform; Advaita and Nityananda float in prema, Mukunda, Murari and
others sing, Haridasa dances crying "Hari!"; the men and women of Nadia see it all with their own eyes. In PK: "Now the
abhisheka-vilasa. First, that of Sri Gaurachandra" (3rd shakha, 31st pallava). Raga suhai.*[^07-54]

**13.1.** In bliss the devotees raise the cry "Jaya!";
in the house of Srivasa Pandita there is a great festival.

**13.2.** With panchagavya, panchamrita, the water of a hundred pots
they joyfully perform the abhisheka of Gauranga.[^07-55]

**13.3.** On the jewelled platform sits Gorachand;
a wondrous beauty — a snare for the hearts of women.[^07-56]

**13.4.** The Lord of Shantipura and Nityananda Raya,
gazing at Gauranga's face, float away in prema.[^07-57]

**13.5.** Mukunda, Murari and others sing sweetly;
crying "Hari!", Haridasa dances all around.

**13.6.** Says Krishnadasa: the abhisheka of Gorachand
the men and women of Nadia see with their own eyes.[^07-58]

[^07-54]: Signature: "Krishnadasa". PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 465 (printed p. 452), 3rd shakha, 31st pallava,
"athābhiṣeka-vilāsaḥ. ādau śrīgauracandrasya", no. 2 (mark "॥২॥১৫৭০॥"); raga suhai; ms. P-R-Sa no. 2114. GPT1 — p. 239,
no. 5 (raga suhai); GPT2 — sect. 4.1, no. 5. The catalogue's former first line ("ratana-vedīra para…") is the
beginning of the third couplet. The next pada of PK (1571) is Vasu Ghosha's pada on the abhisheka (chapter 1, no. 2).
Which Krishnadasa it is has not been established. On the Lord's abhisheka in Srivasa's house see CB Madhya 9.
[^07-55]: Panchagavya — the five products of the cow; panchamrita — the five nectars (milk, curd, ghee, honey, sugar); the
Deity is bathed with them at the abhisheka.
[^07-56]: The image (as in the padas on Krishna) speaks of the Lord's irresistible beauty, not of mundane passion; worship of
Gaura in the mood of "gaura-nagari" is not accepted by the Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa
Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati): in Navadvipa, according to CB (Adi 15), the Lord did not even jest with women.
[^07-57]: The Lord of Shantipura is Advaita. Mss. "ka", "kha", P-R-Sa: "having seen" (heri); P-R-Sa: "form" (rūpa) instead
of "face".
[^07-58]: "With their own eyes" (parateka = pratyakṣa).

## 14. Ramachandra — "dekha śacīnandana jagata-jīvana-dhana…" (PK 2064)
*The Lord's dance: the Son of Shachi, the treasure of the world's life, ceaselessly gives out prema; in ecstasy He dances,
crying "Hari"; hearing of Vrindavana's glories, He rolls on the ground and laughs; Kashishvara, Abhirama, Pandita
Purushottama and Narahari Dasa sing His glory; at the sound of the khol and karatalas children and wealthy alike come
running. In PK it stands in the 17th pallava (the dance and pastimes of Gauranga). Raga "the same" (tathā rāga).*[^07-59]

**14.1.** Behold: the Son of Shachi, the treasure of the world's life,
ceaselessly offers people the treasure of prema.
Rapt in bhava, the Best One — His golden body thrilling —
crying "Hari" again and again, Lord Gora dances.[^07-60]

**14.2.** *(Refrain)* The essence of all avataras is the Gora-avatara!
His peerless body surpasses the colour of gold,
from His reddish eyes flow streams of prema.

**14.3.** Hearing Vrindavana's glories, this jewel of the twice-born rolls on the ground;
overflowing with bhava, my Lord laughs.
Kashishvara, Abhirama, Pandita Purushottama
sing His glory, and with them Narahari Dasa.[^07-61]

**14.4.** Hearing the khol and karatalas, children and wealthy alike
come running — all in hope of prema.
Whoever's heart is awakened to such qualities of Gaura —
his servant is Ramachandra Dasa.[^07-62]

[^07-59]: Signature: "Ramachandra Dasa". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 217 (printed p. 206), 4th shakha, 17th pallava, no. 6 (mark
"॥৬॥২০৬৪॥"); "tathā rāga"; ms. P-R-Sa no. 2173. GPT1 — p. 250, no. 6 (raga beloar; without stanza 14.4, i.e. without
the signature); GPT2 — sect. 4.2, no. 6. According to Majumdar, Ramachandra is probably Ramachandra Kaviraja of
Nityananda's branch (not his namesake, the friend of Narottama), a companion of the Lord: Narahari Chakravarti cites
another pada of his (PK 2186 = BR p. 919, chapter 1) as the testimony of an eyewitness.
[^07-60]: "Lord Gora" (gorā pahuṃ); ms. "kha", P-R-Sa: "crying 'Hari, Hari', the Lord dances".
[^07-61]: Kashishvara is a servant of the Lord (according to CC a disciple of Ishvara Puri, later in Puri); Abhirama Thakura
is a companion of Nityananda; Pandita Purushottama is a companion of the Lord (CC Adi 10–11 names several Purushottamas);
Narahari Dasa is Narahari Sarakara. The place (Navadvipa or Puri) cannot be determined with certainty from the list of
companions.
[^07-62]: The khol is the clay drum of kirtana, the karatalas are hand cymbals.

## 15. Vasu Ramananda — "aruṇa vasane vidita bhuvane…" (PK 2331)
*Nityananda's dance: in red garments, with a dancer's turban, He dances, looking around and crying "Hari, Hari"; His gait
is that of a mighty elephant, His anklet bells ring; in ecstasy He knows no directions and roars "Gaura!"; the devotees
roll on the ground gazing at His moon-face, and Vasu Ramananda weeps, clasping Nitai's feet. In PK it is the last pada of
the 22nd pallava (on Nityananda). The same raga (suhai).*[^07-63]

**15.1.** In red garments, renowned in the world,
with a dancer's turban on His head,
looking around on every side He cries "Hari, Hari!" —
and dances in all manner of ways.[^07-64]

**15.2.** *(Refrain)* Lovely Nitai dances!
In those reddish eyes, in that moon-face —
how much sweetness there is![^07-65]

**15.3.** Lovely is His gait — like a mighty elephant's,
His anklet bells jingle.
Overcome by bhava, knowing no directions,
He roars out: "Gaura!"[^07-66]

**15.4.** All the devotees roll on the ground
gazing at that moon-face.
And Vasu Ramananda weeps, disconsolate,
clasping the feet of Nitai.

[^07-63]: Signature: "Vasu Ramananda". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 315 (printed p. 304), 4th shakha, 22nd pallava, no. 38 (mark
"॥৩৮॥২৩৩১॥"); "tathā rāga" (after the preceding pada — suhai); ms. P-R-Sa no. 2435. Not found in GPT1 or KGC. In Ray's
index of poets it stands among the padas of Vasu Ramananda. The red garments, turban and jingling ornaments recall the
description of Nityananda in Gauda after 1515 (CB Antya 5–6), but the pada names no place.
[^07-64]: A dancer's turban (naṭapaṭi pāga) — a gay turban, as worn by Krishna-Natavara. Mss. "ka", "ca": "Hari, Hari"
instead of "looking around" (heri heri).
[^07-65]: Ms. "gha": kata nā (the same meaning).
[^07-66]: According to Ray's apparatus, the lines "Lovely is His gait… jingle" were omitted by scribal error in mss. "ka",
"kha", "ca" and P-R-Sa.

## 16. Krishnadasa — "śarata-cānda jini gorā-mukha cānda…" (PK 1743)
*Separation in autumn: Gauranga, whose face surpasses the autumn moon, gazes at the autumn moon and weeps, remembering the
happiness of the autumn season, sobbing aloud; the heart breaks at the sight of His face, even a fool loses his
composure; all the dear companions weep. In PK it is the gaura-chandrika to "separation befitting autumn": "Shri
Mahaprabhu, overcome by that bhava" (8th pallava). Raga sindhura.*[^07-67]

**16.1.** The moon-face of Gora, surpassing the autumn moon,
gazes at the autumn moon — and weeps.[^07-68]

**16.2.** Remembering again and again the happiness of autumn,
Lord Gauranga weeps, sobbing aloud.[^07-69]

**16.3.** The heart breaks at the sight of that face;
even a fool cannot keep his composure.

**16.4.** All the dear companions weep in distress.
Krishnadasa says: "I am a great sinner."

[^07-67]: Signature: "Krishnadasa". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 92 (printed p. 81), 4th shakha, 8th pallava ("separation befitting
spring and the other seasons"), "atha śaratkālocita-virahaḥ. tadbhāvākrāntaḥ śrīmahāprabhuḥ", no. 33 (mark
"॥৩৩॥১৭৪৩॥"); raga sindhura; ms. P-R-Sa no. 967. Not found in GPT1. Which Krishnadasa it is has not been established.
[^07-68]: Autumn is the time of the rasa ("the autumn nights", Bhag. 10.29.1). The Lord's weeping is separation in Radha's
mood — pure prema, not worldly longing (CC Antya 14–20).
[^07-69]: P-R-Sa: "the face of autumn" (mukha) instead of "happiness".

## 17. Ramananda — "dekha dekha jīva gaurāṅgacām̐dera līlā…" (PK 2248)
*The sannyasi Lord: He who in a moment enchanted hundreds of thousands of gopis has exchanged His yellow garments for the
kaupina and the staff; leaving the happiness of the Kalindi's bank, He stands awesome on the seashore; in the Rama-avatara
He held the bow, in Gokula He played the flute, and now, out of compassion for souls, He has taken the sannyasi's staff;
the poet says: this is no sannyasi's garb, but the armour of a hero crushing godlessness. In PK it stands in the 21st
pallava (Gauranga's sannyasa). Raga varadi.*[^07-70]

**17.1.** *(Refrain)* Behold, souls, the lila of Gaurangachand!
He who in the twinkling of an eye enchanted hundreds of thousands of gopis —
why has He become a sannyasi?[^07-71]

**17.2.** Leaving His yellow garments, putting on the string and kaupina,
the crooked He has made a straight staff.
Leaving the happiness of the Kalindi's bank,
awesome is He on the shore of the sea.[^07-72]

**17.3.** In the Rama-avatara He held the bow,
in Gokula He filled the flute with sound,
and now, out of compassion for souls,
taking the staff, He has become a sannyasi.[^07-73]

**17.4.** Taking a new staff and a water-pot,
He has settled on the shore of the sea.
Says Ramananda: this is no sannyasi's garb —
it is the armour of a hero crushing godlessness.[^07-74]

[^07-70]: Signature: "Ramananda". PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 285–286 (printed pp. 274–275), 4th shakha, 21st pallava (Gauranga's
sannyasa), no. 31 (mark "॥৩১॥২২৪৮॥"); raga varadi; ms. P-R-Sa no. 2353. GPT1 — p. 18, no. 49 (raga varadi); GPT2 — sect.
1.2, no. 49. In the catalogue (RM-001) this pada was confused with the preceding PK 2247 ("goloka chāṛiyā pahu kene vā
avanī"): that one is signed in PK "Govinda Dasa", in GPT "Nayanananda", and Ramananda is only mentioned in it ("Raya
Ramananda weeps"). The attribution of PK 2248 to Vasu Ramananda is not proven (the signature is only "Ramananda"); by its
content the pada was written after the sannyasa, about the Lord in Puri.
[^07-71]: The gopis are Krishna's friends in Vraja; their prema is pure, without a trace of the mundane — the highest love of
God.
[^07-72]: "The crooked" (vākuyā) — the reading is unclear; probably "crooked" (vām̐kuyā): Krishna, who stood "bent in three
places" (tribhanga) with the flute, now holds the straight staff of a sannyasi. The Kalindi is the Yamuna. "Awesome"
(paracaṇḍa = pracaṇḍa).
[^07-73]: Mss. "ka", "kha", "ca", P-R-Sa: "holding the bow" (dhariyā).
[^07-74]: The staff (danda) and the water-pot (karaṅga, kamandalu) are the sannyasi's belongings; mss. "ka", "kha", P-R-Sa:
"taking along" (laiyā saṅge) instead of "taking a water-pot". "The armour of a hero" (vīra-vānā — a warrior's array): the
Lord's sannyasa is a weapon against godlessness; cf. note 8.

## 18. Paramananda — "śrīnityānanda caitanya hare…" (PK 2971)
*A nama-kirtana in Vrajabuli: the Son of Shachi, descended in Nadia, first of all spread the holy name; He dances in
kirtana, Gadadhara at His left; tears of prema wash away the darkness of Kali; He embraces all without distinction;
living in Nilachala, He beholds the Lord of the Yadus (Jagannatha); He goes from house to house for the sake of the
fallen, offering prema. In PK it is unsigned, in the 34th pallava (nama-sankirtana); in GPT the last line carries
Paramananda's signature. Ragini "kau", tala madhyaman (according to ms. "gha").*[^07-75]

**18.1.** *(Refrain)* Sri Nityananda, Chaitanya, Hari!

**18.2.** The Son of Shachi, descended in Nadia,
having taken the form of Gaura of radiant hue,
first of all spread the holy name in the world —
who else so compassionately saves the fallen?[^07-76]

**18.3.** He who delights in dance in the taste of sankirtana,
all thrilled with unbroken pulaka, the benefactor of the devotees,
laughs, dances and sings, enraptured —
the people of the three worlds cry "Glory!" — so He enchants.[^07-77]

**18.4.** Overcome by bhava, He stands in the tribhanga pose;
at His left shines the joyful Gadadhara;
on all sides the companions have gathered and shine —
so glows the Son of Shachi, who delights in Vrindavana.[^07-78]

**18.5.** Unceasingly streams of prema flow from His eyes;
sprinkling, they wash away the darkness of Kali.
He embraces all without distinction —
peerless are His qualities, form and bhava, boundless![^07-79]

**18.6.** In Nilachala dwells the Son of Shachi
and beholds God, the Lord of the Yadus;
His body anointed with radiant sandal paste —
His whole form calls forth delight.[^07-80]

**18.7.** Sweetly, sweetly He utters the name of Hari,
for the fallen He goes from house to house;
the merciful Lord Himself offers prema —
the fear of the world's people He drives away.[^07-81]

[^07-75]: PK: vol. 4, PDF pp. 221–222 (printed pp. 212–213), 4th shakha, 34th pallava (nama-sankirtana), no. 14 (mark
"॥১৪॥২৯৭১॥"); "rāgiṇī kau — tāla madhyamāna" (according to Ray, this heading is only in ms. "gha"). In PK there is no
signature: the last line is "jaga-janake bhaya dūrahi bhājata" ("He drives away the fear of the world's people"). GPT1 —
p. 403, no. 5 (raga dhanashi; the section on Puri), where the same line reads "paramānandaka bhaya dūrahi bhāgata" ("He
drives away Paramananda's fear") — Paramananda's signature; the catalogue's attribution (PA-007) rests on it. The
catalogue connected Paramananda with PK 2966 and 2974: PK 2966 is a pada of Gopala Dasa on Radha and Krishna; PK 2974
("hare hare govinda hare") does bear Paramananda's signature, but it is a nama-kirtana to Krishna without gaura-lila (not
translated). Majumdar ascribes Paramananda's Vrajabuli padas to Paramananda of Vrindavana, a follower of Rupa, not to
Paramananda Gupta; authority C.
[^07-76]: The last words of the stanzas (kohe, mohe, sohe…) are Hindi exclamatory endings ("who?", "enchants", "shines"),
usual in Vrajabuli nama-kirtanas.
[^07-77]: "Glory!" (valihāri) — literally "I give myself for Him".
[^07-78]: Tribhanga is the "thrice-bent" pose of Krishna with the flute; "who delights in Vrindavana" (vṛndāvana-raṅgī) is
Krishna. Ms. "gha": another reading instead of "gathered" (ota nita).
[^07-79]: Ms. "gha": "tears of prema flow" (vahata premajala); "ka", "kha", "ca": siṃcata (the same, "sprinkling"); "ka":
mohata, "kha": mocata ("wash away"); "ka", "kha": kara (the same, "embraces").
[^07-80]: The Lord of the Yadus (yadunandana) is Jagannatha. GPT1: "beholds every day".
[^07-81]: "Himself offers prema" (premahi yācata) — He gives it without waiting to be asked. Ms. "ka": "fallen people"
(patitaloka); "ka", "kha": līye (the same, "for the sake of").

## 19. Krishnadasa — "ākula dekhiyā tāre kahe gaura dhīre dhīre…" (PK 2359)
*The continuation of PK 2358 (chapter 1, no. 24). Seeing Gauridasa distraught, the Lord softly says: "We have stayed with
you"; He comes to the Pandita with two Deities, and four stand before Gauridasa — the Lord, Nityananda and Their Deities;
the Lord bids him keep whichever two he wishes and promises, for the sake of his faith, to eat at his house, asking for
food; Gauridasa cooks, and all four partake; having thus turned his heart, the Lord left Both with him in Their Deities,
while the two brothers Themselves went to Nilachala. In PK it stands in the section on Gauridasa Pandita (24th pallava,
"the character of Gaura's devotees"). The same raga (bhatiyari).*[^07-82]

**19.1.** Seeing him distraught, Gaura says softly, softly:
"We have stayed with you.
Know it for certain: in this house of yours
We have stayed, the two brothers."[^07-83]

**19.2.** Having consoled him thus, taking two Deities,
the Lord appeared before the Pandita.
Four stood there side by side — the Pandita was amazed,
tears of bhava flow from his eyes.[^07-84]

**19.3.** Again the Lord says to him: "Whichever you wish,
those two keep in your house.
For the sake of your faith I will eat at your house, asking for food —
know it in your heart: it is true, true."

**19.4.** Hearing this, the king of panditas set about cooking —
and the four partook of the meal.
Offering flower garlands and clothes, presenting betel and the rest,
he anointed Their whole bodies with sandal paste.

**19.5.** Having strengthened his faith in every way and turned his heart,
the Lord left Both in his house.
For the Pandita's love the two brothers eat there, asking for food —
while They Themselves went to the city of Nilachala.[^07-85]

**19.6.** The Pandita serves Them: whenever They wish for whatever,
so They sport.
Such is my master Gauridasa; hoping for his feet,
says the humble, lowly Krishnadasa.[^07-86]

[^07-82]: Signature: "Krishnadasa". PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 324–325 (printed pp. 313–314), 4th shakha, 24th pallava, no. 7
(mark "॥৭॥২৩৫৯॥"); "tathā rāga" (after PK 2358 — bhatiyari); ms. P-R-Sa no. 2463. GPT1 — p. 406, no. 15 (raga kamoda;
right after PK 2358 = GPT1 no. 14); GPT2 — sect. 5.5, no. 15 (in the catalogue GD-003, wrongly ascribed to Gauridasa and
to PK 2360). The first line in the catalogue (KR-011, "nityānandacāṃda…") is the end of PK 2357. According to Majumdar,
Krishnadasa is Gauridasa's younger brother; he dates PK 2358 to the Lord's lifetime, and this pada directly continues it.
Cf. Murari 4.14.12–17.
[^07-83]: Ms. "kha": "seeing" (dekhite); "ka": "with you" (tomāra); GPT1: "We have stayed, the two brothers, as captives"
(vandī).
[^07-84]: The four are the Lord, Nityananda and Their two Deities (so also GPT1's note). Ms. "ka": "murti, murti" (mūrtti
mūrtti). The Deity is not a statue but the Lord Himself, manifesting Himself out of love for His devotee: the Lord shows
Gauridasa that He and His Deity are one.
[^07-85]: Ms. "ka", P-R-Sa: "then" (sei) instead of "whenever". "Asking for food" (khāy māgi) — the Lord Himself asks
Gauridasa for food, reciprocating his love.
[^07-86]: "Master" (prabhu) is Gauridasa, the poet's elder brother and, it seems, his teacher.

## 20. Krishnadasa — "dekha dui bhāi gaura nitāi…" (PK 1576)
*The abhisheka of Gaura and Nitai in Gauridasa's house: the two brothers sit on the altar as if the moon and the sun had
come down from the sky; Thakura Pandita with his people pours scented water over Them to the sound of conches, bells,
gongs, flutes, vinas, khols and karatalas; having bathed and dressed Them, he seats Them on a throne, performs puja,
feeds Them, offers betel and sandal, puts on garlands and performs arati. In PK the pada concludes a series of padas,
in the section on the abhisheka (31st pallava), about the festival at Gauridasa's: in the two preceding ones (signed
"Svarupa") the Lord and Nityananda promise Gauridasa in a dream to come and stay in his temple, he prepares the
festival, and They come. Raga varadi.*[^07-87]

**20.1.** Behold: the two brothers, Gaura and Nitai,
sit upon the altar,
as if the moon and the sun, leaving the sky,
had come down to the earth.[^07-88]

**20.2.** Seeing it, Thakura Pandita rejoices;
taking his people along,
filling many pots with scented water,
he pours it over the heads of Both.

**20.3.** Conches, bells, gongs, flutes, vinas, pipes,
khols and karatalas sound;
cries of "Jaya, jaya!", shouts of "Hari, Hari!" —
on all sides the devotees sing.[^07-89]

**20.4.** Having bathed and dressed Them,
he seated Them on the throne.
Lighting incense and lamps, taking a plate of arghya,
he performed the puja of Both.[^07-90]

**20.5.** Having fed Them with all kinds of offerings,
at the end — betel and sandal;
putting on flower garlands and performing arati,
Krishnadasa bowed down [before Them].

[^07-87]: Signature: "Krishnadasa". PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 467 (printed p. 454), 3rd shakha, 31st pallava, no. 8 (mark
"॥৮॥১৫৭৬॥"); raga varadi; ms. P-R-Sa no. 2146. GPT1 — p. 241, no. 12 (raga varadi); GPT2 — sect. 4.1, no. 12. The pada
belongs to the same story as PK 2358–2360 (here nos. 19, 21), but PK places it in the section on the abhisheka. Which
Krishnadasa it is, is not stated; by the theme, probably Gauridasa's younger brother.
[^07-88]: Mss. "ka", "kha", "gha", "ca": nāmilā āsiyā (the same, "came down"); "ka", "kha": "night and the sun" (niśā)
instead of "the moon".
[^07-89]: P-R-Sa: vāje (the same, "sound"), gāhe (the same, "sing").
[^07-90]: Arghya is a respectful offering of water with flowers and rice. P-R-Sa: arghyathālī (the same).

## 21. Krishnadasa — "śrīvṛndāvana nāma ratna-cintāmaṇi-dhāma…" (PK 2360)
*Praise of Gauridasa: in Vrindavana, the abode of chintamani jewels, beside Krishna and Balarama, was Subala-chandra —
now he has become Gauridasa and lives in Ambika; Nitai and Chaitanya accepted his service, and all four partook of his
food; as Subala once subdued Rama and Kanu, so now this has become manifest; knowing nothing but Nitai and Chaitanya, he
kept the two brothers Themselves in his house. In PK it is the next pada of the same section. The same raga
(bhatiyari).*[^07-91]

**21.1.** There is Sri Vrindavana, the abode of chintamani jewels;
there, beside Krishna and Balarama,
was he, named Subala-chandra — now he has become Gauridasa
and lives in the city of Ambika.[^07-92]

**21.2.** Nitai and Chaitanya accepted his service —
four murtis partook of his food.
As Subala once subdued Rama and Kanu,
so now it has become manifest.[^07-93]

**21.3.** Nothing but Nitai and Chaitanya does he know —
who can tell the greatness of his prema?
He kept in his house before his very eyes —
who else could do so? — Nitai and Chaitanya, the two brothers.

**21.4.** In prema he leaps and bounds, thrilled all over, he roars,
now he weeps, now he laughs.
Adorning his body with the dust of his lotus feet,
says the humble, lowly Krishnadasa.

[^07-91]: Signature: "Krishnadasa". PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 325 (printed p. 314), 24th pallava, no. 8 (mark "॥৮॥২৩৬০॥"); "tathā
rāga"; ms. P-R-Sa no. 2464. GPT1 — p. 458, no. 19 (raga bhatiyari; the section on the companions); GPT2 — sect. 6.3. After
the pada a section on Rupa and Sanatana begins in PK.
[^07-92]: Subala is a cowherd friend of Krishna in Vraja; according to the *Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika* (128), Gauridasa is
Subala. In P-R-Sa "named" and "abode" are interchanged. Chintamani is the wish-fulfilling jewel: according to the
scriptures, Vrindavana is made of them.
[^07-93]: The four murtis are the Lord and Nityananda and Their Deities (cf. no. 19); ms. "ka": "forms" (mūrtte). Rama
and Kanu are Balarama and Krishna.

## 22. Krishnadasa — "nitāi caitanya doṃhe vaṛa avatāra…" (PK 2991)
*A prayer of repentance: Nitai and Chaitanya are the greatest avataras, none will be more generous than They; They
delivered mlecchas, chandalas and blasphemers; yet the poet has gained nothing — he did not worship Their feet, he himself
put poison into his mouth; the whole world drowned in the prema of the gaura-kirtana, but not a drop touched him. In PK
it stands in the 36th pallava (prayers). Raga shri.*[^07-94]

**22.1.** Nitai and Chaitanya — Both are great avataras;
such merciful givers there will never be again.[^07-95]

**22.2.** Mlecchas, chandalas, blasphemers, the godless —
how many of them They delivered by Their mercy![^07-96]

**22.3.** In such an avatara nothing at all fell to my lot —
alas, cruel life, in what contentment you abide!

**22.4.** However many avataras have come into the world —
one like this, brother, never comes.

**22.5.** Not worshipping the two feet of such a Lord,
with my own hand I raised poison to my mouth and ate it.[^07-97]

**22.6.** The world drowned in the prema of the gaura-kirtana —
alas, not a drop has touched the unfortunate one.

**22.7.** Krishnadasa weeps, tearing his hair:
"Shame, shame! Why does the unfortunate one not die?"

[^07-94]: Signature: "Krishnadasa". PK: vol. 4, PDF p. 228 (printed p. 219), 36th pallava (prarthana), no. 7 (mark
"॥৭॥২৯৯১॥"); raga shri; ms. P-R-Sa no. 2500. GPT1 — p. 14, no. 34 (raga shri); GPT2 — sect. 1.2, no. 34. Which Krishnadasa
it is has not been established.
[^07-95]: Ms. "gha": dayālu (the same, "merciful").
[^07-96]: Mlecchas are foreigners and unbelievers; chandalas are untouchables. P-R-Sa: "hundreds" (śata) instead of "how
many".
[^07-97]: Ms. "ka" and GPT1: "lotus feet" (pādapadma).

## 23. Krishnadasa — "adoṣa-daraśī mora prabhu nityānanda…" (PK 2992)
*A prayer to Nityananda: Lord Nityananda sees no fault in people, yet the poet did not worship His feet; at the news of
Nitai's mercy even stone melts, but his heart does not soften; Nitai and Chaitanya do not count offences and give prema
to all alike. In PK it is the next pada. The same raga (shri).*[^07-98]

**23.1.** My Lord Nityananda sees no fault in anyone —
yet I did not worship the lotus feet of such a Lord.

**23.2.** Alas, I myself do not know what kind of demon I am:
having found so merciful a Master, I did not worship Him.[^07-99]

**23.3.** Alas, life of the unfortunate one, in what contentment do you abide?
Why do you not die crying "Nitai"?

**23.4.** At the news of Nitai's mercy stone melts —
but my cruel heart, alas, does not soften at it.

**23.5.** Nitai and Chaitanya do not count offences —
to all and sundry They give Their prema-bhakti.

**23.6.** When I utter His name, my heart does not melt.
Krishnadasa says: "I am the most unfortunate of all."[^07-100]

[^07-98]: Signature: "Krishnadasa". PK: vol. 4, PDF p. 228 (printed p. 219), 36th pallava, no. 8 (mark "॥৮॥২৯৯২॥"); "tathā
rāga" (shri); ms. P-R-Sa no. 2501. GPT1 — p. 433, no. 63 (raga shri; the section on Nityananda); GPT2 — sect. 6.1, no. 63.
[^07-99]: Mss. "ka", "kha": kemata (the same, "what kind of").
[^07-100]: Ms. "ca", P-R-Sa: "is not touched" (lāgaye) instead of "does not melt" (galaye).

## 24. Krishnadasa — "jaya jaya nityānanda rāy…" (PK 3006)
*A prayer to Nityananda: the poet confesses his sins and reminds the Lord of His name "Purifier of the fallen": if He
rejects the sinner, that name will bear a stain; He once delivered even yavanas — He will not push him away either, if He
does not despise him. In PK it stands in the 36th pallava. The same raga.*[^07-101]

**24.1.** *(Refrain)* Glory, glory to Nityananda Raya!
My offences and sins have no end —
deliver me by Your own mercy!

**24.2.** My mind is wicked, I have no attraction to Your name —
I am not even ashamed to say it.
How many births in a row have I destroyed myself —
that is why such are my deeds.[^07-102]

**24.3.** You are an ocean of mercy, the friend of sinners;
if this time You reject me,
then on Your peerless, pure name "Purifier of the fallen"
there will be a great stain.

**24.4.** I have heard with my own ears: You once delivered
yavanas and so many offenders.
Krishnadasa reckons: You will not be able to push him away,
if You do not despise him in Your heart.[^07-103]

[^07-101]: Signature: "Krishnadasa". PK: vol. 4, PDF p. 233 (printed p. 224), 36th pallava, no. 22 (mark "॥২২॥৩০০৬॥"); "tathā
rāga" (the raga of this series of padas is not named separately); ms. P-R-Sa no. 2515. GPT1 — pp. 432–433, no. 62 (raga
suhai; the section on Nityananda); GPT2 — sect. 6.1, no. 62. Which Krishnadasa it is has not been established.
[^07-102]: "Destroyed myself" (ātmaghāta) — lived forgetting the Lord, to the harm of the soul.
[^07-103]: Yavanas are foreign Muslims; cf. the Lord's mercy to the Kazi in Navadvipa (CC Adi 17).
