# Chapter 8. Vasu Ghosha: the Gaura Avatara and Gaura's Form, the Lord's Kirtana and Bhavas in Navadvipa

*Padas of Vasu (Vasudeva) Ghosha known from the *Padakalpataru* (PK), in the order of the lilas: praise of the Gaura
avatara and His qualities; Gaura's form in Nadia; the Lord's dance and kirtana with the devotees on the bank of the
Ganga; the Lord in Radha's mood — gaura-chandrikas to the sections of PK on Radha's states of love (prema-vaichittya,
vasaka-sajja, khandita, mana). Majumdar regards Vasu Ghosha as an eyewitness of the Navadvipa kirtanas and counts these
padas among his padas on the Lord's form and bhava. The text follows PK, checked against the scans, with the
manuscript variants from PK's apparatus, the *Gaura-pada-tarangini* (GPT1 — 1st ed., 1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934), the
*Bhakti-ratnakara* (BR) and the *Kshanada-gita-chintamani* (KGC); the Bengali original, variants and word-for-word
translation are in the full version of the book.*

## 1. Vasu Ghosha — "ki kahiva śata śata tuyā avatāra…" (PK 2292)
*Praise of the Gaura avatara: of hundreds of incarnations, the poet holds dear Gauranga alone; as Rama built a bridge
across the ocean, Gaura made kirtana a bridge to carry across the lame, the dull and the blind; the poet knows neither
japa, nor austerity, nor Vedic reasoning, and begs Gauranga to carry him across too. In PK it stands at the end of the
21st pallava. Raga barari.*[^08-1]

**1.1.** What shall I say of Your hundreds and hundreds of incarnations?
Gaurangachand alone is my life.

**1.2.** In the incarnation of Vishnu You are a beggar asking for prema,
taking four with You: Shiva, Shuka, Narada…[^08-2]

**1.3.** In the incarnation of Rama You built the bridge across the ocean —
but now Your fame will resound through all the world.[^08-3]

**1.4.** In the age of Kali You made kirtana the bridge:
let all the lame, the dull and the blind cross over with ease.[^08-4]

**1.5.** By what qualities do men dance, by what qualities women?
By Gora's qualities the fourteen worlds are intoxicated.[^08-5]

**1.6.** I know neither japa, nor austerity, nor this Vedic reasoning.
Says Vasu: "Gauranga, carry me across!"

[^08-1]: Signature: "Vasu." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 300 (printed p. 289), 21st pallava, no. 75 (mark "॥৭৫॥২২৯২॥"); raga
barari; MS P-R-Sa no. 2396. GPT1 — p. 46, no. 67 (raga barari); GPT2 — sect. 1.3, no. 67. The catalogue listed the pada
twice: under PK 2294 (wrongly: PK 2294 is a pada of Atmarama Dasa on Nityananda, "āre mora nitāi nāyara") and under
PK 2292. Majumdar counts PK 2292 among Vasu Ghosha's stavas and prarthanas.
[^08-2]: The sense of the line is not fully clear. Probably the poet speaks of Gaura as the Lord Himself (Vishnu) come as
a devotee — a "beggar" asking for prema — together with the greatest bhaktas: Shiva, Shuka, Narada (and presumably
Brahma; "janā cāri" — "four," or simply "a handful of people"). The Gaudiya tradition sees in Gaura's associates
incarnations of these bhaktas (Advaita — Shiva, Srivasa — Narada; GGD).
[^08-3]: Rama built the bridge (setu-vandha) to Lanka. MS P-R-Sa: "at last" (avaśeṣa) instead of "but now."
[^08-4]: The "bridge" of kirtana carries one across the ocean of worldly existence. MSS "ka," "ca" and GPT1: without "all"
(yata); "kha": "let them cross over now."
[^08-5]: The fourteen worlds — the whole universe (the seven higher and seven lower planetary systems).

## 2. Vasu Ghosha — "nā jāni ki jāni mora bhela…" (PK 2210)
*Praise of Gaura's qualities: remembering them, trees and creepers weep, the forest deities, beasts and birds weep,
stones melt, no one can stay at home; the poet loses himself. In PK it stands in the 20th pallava ("Sri Gaurachandra —
another mode"). Raga suhai.*[^08-6]

**2.1.** *(Refrain)* I do not know what has happened to me:
thinking of Gauranga's qualities, I have forgotten my body.

**2.2.** Remembering Gora's qualities, the trees and creepers weep;
remembering His qualities, the deities of the forest weep.[^08-7]

**2.3.** Remembering Gora's qualities, the stones melt;
remembering His qualities, no one stays at home.

**2.4.** Vasudeva Ghosha weeps, remembering His qualities;
at His qualities beasts and birds weep, finding no rest.

[^08-6]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 272 (printed pp. 260–261), 20th pallava, no. 27 (mark
"॥২৭॥২২১০॥"); raga suhai; MS P-R-Sa no. 2318. GPT1 — pp. 43–44, no. 57 (raga suhai); GPT2 — sect. 1.3, no. 57.
Majumdar does not discuss this pada separately.
[^08-7]: Cf. CC Madhya 17: in the forests of Jharikhanda the beasts and birds, trees and creepers came into ecstasy hearing
the Lord sing the holy name. GPT1: "no one remains in the house" (raya ghare) — the same meaning.

## 3. Vasu Ghosha — "gorā-guṇa gāo gāo śuni…" (PK 2185)
*Praise of Gaura: the poet asks that His qualities be sung; the Lord is the touchstone of prema; a single glance of His
dries up the ocean of grief of all souls; His eyes are full of tears, His words are engraved on the heart, His body is
covered with the thrill of ecstasy. In PK it stands in the 20th pallava. Raga mallar.*[^08-8]

**3.1.** *(Refrain)* Sing, sing of Gora's qualities — let me hear!
By the fruit of many pious deeds that Lord has been revealed to us —
the touchstone of the rasa of prema.[^08-9]

**3.2.** This ocean of grief of all souls
He dries up in the blink of an eye.
Without the touch of even a drop of that prema,
with what will you cool your heart?

**3.3.** His reddish eyes are the abode of Varuna
when the Merciful One gazes;
in His sweet talk every word
is as if written into the heart.[^08-10]

**3.4.** He sways in prema; the thrill of ecstasy
fills His body from head to foot.
Says Vasudeva: a thousand streams are flowing —
as if Sumeru were being bathed.[^08-11]

[^08-8]: Signature: "Vasudeva." PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 262–263 (printed pp. 251–252), 20th pallava, no. 2 (mark
"॥২॥২১৮৫॥"); raga mallar; MS P-R-Sa no. 2290. GPT1 — pp. 41–42, no. 50 (raga mallar); GPT2 — sect. 1.3, no. 50. The
catalogue listed the pada twice (by GPT and by PK). Majumdar counts PK 2185 among Vasu's padas on the Lord's bhava.
[^08-9]: The touchstone (paraśa-maṇi) turns iron into gold; so the prema the Lord bestows transforms the soul.
[^08-10]: Varuna is the lord of the waters: the Lord's eyes are full of tears, like the ocean. "Written into the heart" —
lit. "written, laid out upon the ribs" (pām̐jare pātiyā likhane). GPT1: "reddish eyes" (aruṇa-nayane), "gaze" (nirikhaṇe) — the
same meaning.
[^08-11]: Sumeru is the golden mountain; the Lord's golden body, washed by streams of tears, is like Sumeru with rivers
running down it.

## 4. Vasu Ghosha — "cīta-cora gaura mora…" (PK 341)
*Gaura's form: the stealer of hearts, intoxicated with prema, embraces the destitute and the fallen; His name is the
cause of the deliverance of the worlds; for the sake of souls He left His abode and appeared in Nadia like the autumn
moon; the Creator fashioned Him an ocean of rasa; seeing Him, all sorrow departs. In PK it is the gaura-chandrika at
the beginning of the 6th pallava (abhisarikas of the rainy season, etc.). Raga tori.*[^08-12]

**4.1.** The stealer of hearts is my Gaura,
intoxicated with prema, immersed, enraptured;
the destitute He takes in His embrace —
the friend of the fallen and the low.

**4.2.** His name is the cause of the deliverance of the worlds;
for the sake of souls He left His abode
and appeared in the town of Nadia
like the autumn moon.[^08-13]

**4.3.** Who can find the limit of His boundless glory?
He steals the very life of young women.
From what did the Creator fashion Gaura —
a vast ocean of rasa?[^08-14]

**4.4.** Looking and looking, joy arises,
all the sorrow of the heart is taken away.
Says Vasu Ghosha: what beauty is this!
Beholding it, the heart is full of bliss.

[^08-12]: Signature: "Vasu Ghosha." PK: vol. 1, PDF p. 232 (printed p. 220), 2nd shakha, 6th pallava ("Now the
abhisarika, vasaka-sajja and the rest befitting the rainy season. First of all, Sri Gaurachandra"), no. 1 (mark
"॥১॥৩৪১॥"); raga tori; PK gives no manuscript number or variants. GPT1 — pp. 131–132, no. 60 (raga tori); GPT2 — sect.
3.1, no. 60. Majumdar counts PK 341 among Vasu's padas on the Lord's form.
[^08-13]: "Left His abode" — the spiritual world, Goloka (cf. CC Adi 3: the Lord descends to give souls prema). "Appeared"
(prakaṭa hailā) — the Lord is not born like a conditioned soul but reveals Himself. GPT1: "appeared in the town of Nadia
like the autumn moon."
[^08-14]: "Steals the very life of young women" is a stock image of the poetics of describing beauty; we translate
faithfully. Vrindavana Dasa stresses that in this incarnation the Lord never looked at another man's wife; worship of
Gaura in the spirit of "Gaura-nagari" is not accepted by the Gaudiya tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja,
Bhaktisiddhanta).

## 5. Vasu Ghosha — "dekha dekha gorā naṭa-rāy…" (PK 2143)
*The form of Gaura, the king of dancers: His face is the autumn moon with a gentle smile; champaka buds in His curls;
golden earrings, lips redder than the bimba; His voice is a wave of nectar drowning the world in the rasa of Hari; His
arms are lovelier than an elephant's trunk; His chest is a golden mountain, His navel a lotus lake; He wears crimson
cloth, and ankle-bells ring on His feet. In PK it stands in the 18th pallava (the form of Gauranga). Raga
gandhara.*[^08-15]

**5.1.** Behold, behold Gora, the king of dancers!
His face is the autumn moon, and on it a gentle, gentle smile;
seeing it, chaste women swoon.[^08-16]

**5.2.** On His head, curling locks, and in them champaka buds —
and the bee-hearts of young women.
At the roots of His lotus ears golden earrings sway;
His lips surpass the ripe bimba fruit.[^08-17]

**5.3.** From His conch-like throat come soft words, a wave of nectar
that drowns the world in the rasa of Hari.
Surpassing the trunk of a mighty elephant are His two rounded arms,
and on them armlets and bracelets shine.

**5.4.** His chest a golden mountain, His navel a lotus lake;
seeing His waist, the lion runs away.
He is clad in crimson cloth, ankle-bells ring on His feet —
Vasu Ghosha sings of Gora's qualities.[^08-18]

[^08-15]: Signature: "Vasu Ghosha." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 247 (printed p. 236), 18th pallava (the form of Sri Gauranga,
etc.), no. 35 (mark "॥৩৫॥২১৪৩॥"); raga gandhara; MS P-R-Sa no. 2250. GPT1 — p. 116, no. 15 (raga gandhara; the refrain is
marked after the first stanza); GPT2 — sect. 3.1, no. 15. The catalogue listed the pada under PK 2144 (wrongly: PK 2144
is the next pada, no. 11 here), while under PK 2143 it gave a first line from PK 2139 (Govinda Dasa). Majumdar counts
PK 2143 among Vasu's padas on the Lord's form.
[^08-16]: The words about women are a stock image of the poetics of describing beauty; we translate faithfully (see note
14).
[^08-17]: Champaka is a tree with fragrant golden flowers; the bimba is a fruit with bright red skin, a usual comparison for
lips. "The bee-hearts of young women" is an image of beauty that draws every heart (see note 14).
[^08-18]: "The lion runs away" — the Lord's slender waist surpasses a lion's (a usual comparison). Crimson (saffron) cloth
is a frequent detail of Gaura's form in Vasu's padas (cf. no. 15).

## 6. Vasu Ghosha — "jāmbunadacaya rucira gañjaya…" (PK 2087)
*Gaura's form: the radiance of His body outshines a heap of the finest gold; His arms, anointed with sandal, are like
the trunk of a king of elephants; the youthful dancer, absorbed in bhava, with faltering voice, dances throughout Nadia,
knowing neither day nor night; on the bank of the Ganga, beneath a young tree, He sits revealing Himself and sprinkles
all His servants with prema. In PK it stands in the 17th pallava (the dance and play of Gauranga). Raga
dhanashi.*[^08-19]

**6.1.** Outshining a heap of jambunada gold,
the radiance of His body glitters;
His arms, anointed with sandal and adorned,
shine like the trunk of a king of elephants.[^08-20]

**6.2.** I beheld Gaura, the youthful dancer, the hero;
in seeing Him, bliss knows no end.
His body is rapt in bhava, His heart overflowing,
in His throat a faltering voice.[^08-21]

**6.3.** Filling the whole town of Nadia with endless delights,
the Knower of rasa, the Wise One, dances;
manifold artistry, the grace of play —
He knows neither day nor night.

**6.4.** On the bank of the Suradhuni, at the roots of a young tree,
He sits, revealing Himself.
Sings Vasudeva Ghosha: the gift of prema has been received —
He has sprinkled all His servants with it.[^08-22]

[^08-19]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 225 (printed p. 214), 17th pallava, no. 29 (mark
"॥২৯॥২০৮৭॥"); raga dhanashi; MS P-R-Sa no. 2196. GPT1 — p. 131, no. 58 (raga dhanashri; the second stanza "I beheld
Gaura…" serves as the refrain); GPT2 — sect. 3.1, no. 58. The catalogue's former first line ("aichana bhāva vujhai nā pāriye")
is the reading of MS P-R-Sa in the closing lines (see note 22). Majumdar counts PK 2087 among Vasu's padas on the Lord's
form.
[^08-20]: Jambunada is the finest gold (according to the Puranas, from the river Jambu). GPT1: "surpassing" (gañjana). MS
"kha": "beautifully adorned" (sumaṇḍita).
[^08-21]: "Hero" (nāyara, i.e. nāgara) — the graceful hero, a usual epithet of Gaura with Vasu Ghosha. MS P-R-Sa: "young" (nava)
instead of "dancer."
[^08-22]: The Suradhuni is the Ganga. "Revealing Himself" (nija parakāśe) — in His true form (or "in His own radiance"). MS
P-R-Sa, instead of the last two lines: "Such a bhava cannot be understood, says Vasudeva Ghosha." GPT1: "Vasudeva Ghosha
sings."

## 7. Vasu Ghosha — "avatāra bhāla gaurāṅga avatāra kailā bhāla…" (PK 665)
*Kirtana in Navadvipa: wondrous is Gauranga's incarnation — even Jagai and Madhai dance; the moon, the sun and the stars
dance, Vasuki in the underworld dances repeating "Gora, Gora"; the devotees and all the destitute dance; the Lord
delivers the dull, the blind, the infirm and the fallen — only the poet is left deprived. In PK it is a gaura-chandrika
in the 6th pallava (rasodgara). The raga is that of the preceding pada — vibhasa.*[^08-23]

**7.1.** Wondrous is the incarnation — wondrously has Gauranga descended!
Jagai and Madhai are dancing — such is His great power![^08-24]

**7.2.** The moon dances, the sun dances, and the stars dance;
in the underworld Vasuki dances, repeating: "Gora, Gora!"[^08-25]

**7.3.** The devotees dance, enraptured;
all the destitute dance, intoxicated with prema.

**7.4.** He delivers the dull, the blind, the infirm, the fallen.
Says Vasu Ghosha: "I alone have been left deprived."[^08-26]

[^08-23]: Signature: "Vasu Ghosha." PK: vol. 2, PDF pp. 57–58 (printed pp. 44–45), 3rd shakha, 6th pallava (rasodgara),
no. 2 (mark "॥২॥৬৬৫॥"); "tathā rāga" — the raga of the preceding pada PK 664 (Chaitanyadasa, part 06, no. 10) — vibhasa;
MS P-R-Sa no. 1140. GPT1 — pp. 248–249, no. 2 (raga vibhasa), right after PK 664; GPT2 — sect. 4.2, no. 2. Majumdar does
not discuss this pada separately.
[^08-24]: Jagai and Madhai are the robber brothers whom the Lord and Nityananda delivered in Navadvipa (CB Madhya 13; CC Adi
17); their dancing in the kirtana is a sign of the Lord's all-conquering mercy. "Great power" (vaṛa ṭhākurāla) — the Lord's
majesty. MS "ka": "made" (kaila).
[^08-25]: Vasuki is the king of the serpents in the lower worlds (Patala). MS "ka," GPT1: "saying" (vali); "ca": vole; "kha":
"Gora" only once.
[^08-26]: MSS "gha," "ca": atura (the same, "infirm"); P-R-Sa: "the infirm and the rest" (aturādi). The usual self-abasement
of Vaishnava poets.

## 8. Vasu Ghosha — "kām̐cā se soṇāra tanu…" (PK 2100)
*Gaura's dance: His body is pure gold, whole Gangas flow from His eyes; His companions surround Him and sing to
karatalas and mridangas; seeing this, the Suradhuni surges in waves; the poet marvels at His smile. In PK it stands in
the 17th pallava (the dance and play of Gauranga). Raga gandhara (as for PK 2098).*[^08-27]

**8.1.** His body is pure gold, every limb brimming over;
how many Suradhunis flow in waves from His eyes![^08-28]

**8.2.** *(Refrain)* Gora dances in supreme bliss;
surrounding Him on all sides, His companions sing.

**8.3.** In their hands are karatalas, the mridanga sounds;
seeing this, the Suradhuni surges in waves.

**8.4.** His limbs are powerless with bhava, His speech falters.
Says Vasu: how sweet is that smile of joy![^08-29]

[^08-27]: Signature: "Vasu." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 230 (printed p. 219), 17th pallava, no. 42 (mark "॥৪২॥২১০০॥"); "tathā rāga" —
the raga of PK 2098–2099 — gandhara; MS P-R-Sa no. 2209. GPT1 — p. 257, no. 28 (raga dhanashi); GPT2 — sect. 4.2, no. 28.
Majumdar counts PK 2100 among Vasu's padas on the Lord's form.
[^08-28]: "Pure gold" — lit. "raw (unworked) gold" (kām̐cā soṇā), i.e. native gold without alloy. The Suradhuni is the Ganga:
tears flow from the Lord's eyes like rivers.
[^08-29]: MSS "ka," "ca," P-R-Sa: "surrounding" (veṛiyā) in 8.2; "kha," "ca," P-R-Sa: "sounds" (vājaye) in 8.3. In 8.4 MSS
"kha," "ca": "body" (tanu) instead of "limbs"; P-R-Sa: hu; MS "ka" omits the word; MS "ka" and GPT1: "the smile of the lips" (mukha) instead of "the smile of joy." GPT1 reads with MSS "ka,"
"ca," "kha": veṛiyā, vājaye, tanu.

## 9. Vasu Ghosha (?) — "gorā nāce prema-vinadiyā…" (PK 2079)
*Dance in the sankirtana: the Lord of all the worlds, rapt in the play of prema, dances in Nadia without regard to
direction, crying "Hari!" with tears; distributing to souls the wealth of Goloka's prema, He dances in the sankirtana
and begs everyone He sees: "Take the sweet name!" In PK it stands in the 17th pallava. Raga tori.*[^08-30]

**9.1.** *(Refrain)* Gora dances, rapt in the play of prema:
the Lord of all the worlds sports in Nadia.

**9.2.** Dancing and dancing, Gora knows no direction;
moon-faced, He cries "Hari!", weeping and weeping.

**9.3.** Distributing to souls the wealth of Goloka's prema,
Gora dances in the sankirtana, crying: "Haribol!"

**9.4.** Whomever He sees, He begs: "Take the sweet name!"
Vasu Ghosha, not having received it, weeps without end.[^08-31]

[^08-30]: PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 222 (printed p. 211), 17th pallava, no. 21 (mark "॥২১॥২০৭৯॥"); "tathā rāga" — the raga of PK
2078 — tori; MS P-R-Sa no. 2188. GPT1 — p. 252, no. 14 (raga tori); GPT2 — sect. 4.2. The attribution is doubtful: according
to PK's apparatus, couplet 9.4 with the signature "Vasu Ghosha" is found only in MS P-R-Sa; in GPT1 the pada ends
differently, with the signature of Balarama Dasa (see note 31). Majumdar counts PK 2079 among Vasu's padas on the
Lord's bhava. The next pada, PK 2080 ("savahum̐ gāyata savahum̐ nācata"), which the catalogue assigned to Vasu, is by Govinda
Dasa.
[^08-31]: According to PK's note, couplet 9.4 is found only in MS P-R-Sa. GPT1 has instead: "His body brims with prema, a
gentle smile on His lips; Balarama Dasa alone was left deprived of this rasa." GPT1: "rapt in the play of prema" (prema
vinodiyā).

## 10. Vasu Ghosha — "śuni vṛndāvana-guṇa…" (PK 2078)
*Dance in the kirtana: hearing of the glories of Vrindavana, Gaura, maddened by rasa, raises His arms and cries "Hari!",
whirls in the dance, and streams flow from His eyes; He is beyond purusha and prakriti and enchants Manmatha Himself;
His body thrills with ecstasy and is anointed with perfume and sandal. In PK it stands in the 17th pallava (the dance
and play of Gauranga). Raga tori.*[^08-32]

**10.1.** Hearing of the glories of Vrindavana, His heart maddened by rasa,
raising both arms, He cries: "Hari!"
Whirling, Gora Raya dances — how many streams are flowing:
His two eyes are pitchers of prema.

**10.2.** A dancer skilled in rasa, greedy for kirtana —
how many merry companions are with Him!
In the sidelong glances of His eyes
hundreds of thousands of Lakshmis play.[^08-33]

**10.3.** Beyond purusha and prakriti, enchanting Manmatha Himself,
He is the very limit of the joy of beauty.
Gaura is an ocean of rasa, deep, an elusive thief:
the pride of the town's women could not stand.[^08-34]

**10.4.** His neck held high, beautiful as Manmatha,
His body rejoices, thrilling with ecstasy;
perfume and sandal anoint His body —
in such prema Vasu Ghosha is drowning.[^08-35]

[^08-32]: Signature: "Vasu Ghosha." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 222 (printed p. 211), 17th pallava, no. 20 (mark "॥২০॥২০৭৮॥");
raga tori; MS P-R-Sa no. 2187. GPT1 — p. 252, no. 13 (raga tori); GPT2 — sect. 4.2, no. 13 (the catalogue knew it only
from GPT). Majumdar counts PK 2078 among Vasu's padas on the Lord's bhava.
[^08-33]: The sense is not fully clear. Lakshmi is the goddess of beauty and fortune: in the Lord's glances are countless
Lakshmis, i.e. all the beauty and good of the world. "In the sidelong glances" follows MSS "ka," "kha," "gha," "ca,"
P-R-Sa and GPT1 (apāṅge); PK's main text has anaṅge ("in the tremulous Ananga"). MSS "ka," "kha": lakhimi.
[^08-34]: "Beyond purusha and prakriti" — the Lord transcends both the enjoying spirit and material nature. "Enchanting
Manmatha Himself" (the god of love) — cf. Bhag. 10.32.2: Krishna is "the Manmatha of Manmatha himself." "Elusive thief"
(gabhīra caura, the stealer of hearts); MSS "ka," "kha," "ca," P-R-Sa and GPT1: "deep and serene" (gabhīra dhīra). "The pride of
the town's women could not stand" — an image of beauty that captivates every heart; we translate faithfully (see note
14).
[^08-35]: "Perfume" — apparently chuya (cuyā, fragrant oil); the word cuvaka is unclear (GPT1 has the same, by the OCR). MSS
"ka," "kha," "ca," P-R-Sa: "thus" (aiche) instead of "in such"; GPT1: "thus Vasu Ghosha speaks of prema" (bhāṣe).

## 11. Vasu Ghosha — "kām̐cā kāñcana maṇi gorā-rūpa…" (PK 2144)
*Play on the bank of the Ganga: Gaura, lovelier than a jewel of pure gold, wearing a garland of fresh flowers and
leaning on Narahari, strolls with Nityananda and His companions, crying "Hari, Hari!"; He roars like a lion, the hairs
of His body stand on end; Gadadhara holds His left hand, Govinda sings; remembering the rasa of the Vrindavana lilas, the
Lord smiles softly and speaks with longing. Narahari Chakravarti quotes the pada in the *Bhakti-ratnakara*: Srinivasa is
shown the bank of the Ganga where the Lord sported with His companions. In PK it stands in the 18th pallava. Raga
kamoda.*[^08-36]

**11.1.** Lovelier than a jewel of pure gold is Gora's form,
rippling with waves of prema;
on His neck a garland of fresh flowers sways beyond compare,
and He leans upon Narahari.[^08-37]

**11.2.** *(Refrain)* He sports in supreme bliss:
taking Nityananda with Him, on the bank of the Ganga, rejoicing,
He cries with His own people: "Hari, Hari!"[^08-38]

**11.3.** His body is powerless with bhava, His hairs stand on end like kadamba flowers;
He roars like a lion.
His dear Gadadhara holds His left hand;
Govinda sings of His qualities.[^08-39]

**11.4.** With a slight smile on His lips the Lord laughs softly, softly
and speaks with such longing.
He remembers all those games, the rasa of the Vrindavana lilas —
what can Vasudeva Ghosha say?[^08-40]

[^08-36]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 247 (printed pp. 236–237), 18th pallava, no. 36 (mark
"॥৩৬॥২১৪…॥" — the last digit is cut off in the scan; by the sequence of marks — 2144); raga kamoda; MS P-R-Sa no. 2251.
BR, 12th wave: ed. 1913 — p. 962 (raga kamoda), ed. 1960 — vv. 3083–3086; KGC — 28th kshanada (shukla-trayodashi), no.
1, pp. 222–223 (raga kamoda). GPT1 — p. 282, no. 16 (raga kamoda); GPT2 — sect. 4.3, no. 16. The catalogue listed it under
"214?" and separately under GPT; PK 2144 given for another line (VG-008) is an error (that is PK 2143, no. 5 here).
Majumdar names "PK 2140" among Vasu's padas on bhava — PK 2140 belongs to Govinda Dasa; probably PK 2144 is meant.
[^08-37]: Narahari is Narahari Sarakara Thakura of Shrikhanda, the Lord's constant companion in the Navadvipa kirtanas (cf.
parts 02, 03). MSS "kha," "gha": "with waves of prema" (prema); P-R-Sa adds after this stanza: "His face a full moon,
a gentle smile on it, nectar flowing from His eyes; the devotees, like chataka birds, drink and drink without end, day
and night intoxicated with prema." BR, KGC: "He leans upon Narahari" (helana).
[^08-38]: MSS "ka," "kha," "gha" and GPT1: "on the bank of the Yamuna" — the Lord sees the Ganga as the Yamuna (cf. CC Madhya
3); MS "ca": "on the Ganga." BR: "with His beloved ones"; KGC begins the pada with the refrain: "Gauranga sports in
supreme bliss."
[^08-39]: Gadadhara Pandita is the Lord's closest companion, in whom the Gaudiya tradition sees Sri Radha. Govinda is
apparently Govinda Ghosha, Vasu's brother, a kirtana singer. BR, KGC: "dear Gadadhara, holding His left hand" — the same.
[^08-40]: The Lord remembers the Vrindavana lilas in Radha's mood — this is pure prema, not a worldly feeling. BR: "now and
again He smiles from the corners of His reddish eyes and speaks with what longing"; KGC: "now He smiles… now He weeps
from the corners of His reddish eyes." BR, KGC, GPT1: "what can I, Vasudeva Ghosha, say" (ki valiva).

## 12. Vasu Ghosha — "hari hari gorā kene kām̐de…" (PK 764)
*The Lord's bhava: His companions do not understand why Gora weeps; tears fall like pearls from a broken string;
remembering Vrindavana and looking at His own body, He calls "Rai, Rai!" and falls senseless; Gadadhara embraces Him and
says something into His ear — and the Lord laughs aloud. In PK it is the gaura-chandrika to the section on Radha's
prema-vaichittya (the beginning of the 9th pallava). Raga gandhara.*[^08-41]

**12.1.** *(Refrain)* Hari, Hari! Why does Gora weep?
His companions ask the reason,
gazing at the moon of Gora's face.[^08-42]

**12.2.** His reddened eyes, from the fullness of prema, grow twice as red;
the tears of prema stream and stream —
as if from a broken string pearls
were falling one after another.[^08-43]

**12.3.** Remembering Vrindavana, He sighs again and again,
looking at His own body;
pressing both hands to His breast, crying "Rai, Rai!",
He fell to the ground senseless.[^08-44]

**12.4.** Then dear Gadadhara embraced Him
and said something into His ear —
and again He laughs aloud, gladdening the people,
while Vasu Ghosha pines away in tears.[^08-45]

[^08-41]: Signature: "Vasu Ghosha." PK: vol. 2, PDF pp. 115–116 (printed pp. 102–103), 3rd shakha, 9th pallava ("Now
Sri Radha's prema-vaichittya. The Sri Gaurachandra befitting it"), no. 1 (mark "॥১॥৭৬৪॥"); raga gandhara; MS P-R-Sa no.
1264. GPT1 — p. 284, no. 24 (raga gandhara); GPT2 — sect. 4.3, no. 24. Balarama Dasa's pada with the same opening ("hari hari
gorā kena kām̐de / nā jāni ṭhekilā pahum̐ kāra premaphām̐de," GPT1 no. 39) is a different pada; the catalogue wrongly linked it
with PK 764. Majumdar counts PK 764 among Vasu's padas on the Lord's bhava. Prema-vaichittya is Radha's state in which,
though near Krishna, She feels separation from Him out of the excess of love.
[^08-42]: MS P-R-Sa: "not understanding the reason" (nā vujhiye kāraṇa).
[^08-43]: MSS "ka," "ca": gām̐thila, P-R-Sa: gathita (the same, "strung"); P-R-Sa: "pearls" (mukutāphala) and "fall" (khasatahi).
[^08-44]: Looking at His golden body, the Lord remembers Sri Radha, whose complexion and bhava He has accepted (CC Adi 4),
and calls Her — "Rai." MS P-R-Sa has "Govi, Govi" instead of "Rai, Rai" and "falls to the ground" (dharaṇīte paṛe); MS
"kha": "sighs again" (niśvāsai puna).
[^08-45]: MS "ka": "sitting down" (vasiyā) instead of "embraced"; P-R-Sa: "Gaura" (gaura) instead of "again." "Pines away in
tears" (maraye jhuriyā) — lit. "dies weeping": a usual expression of boundless longing.

## 13. Vasu Ghosha — "aruṇa nayane dhārā vahe…" (PK 356)
*The Lord in Radha's mood — vasaka-sajja: with reddened eyes and bowed head, He starts at the sight of a shadow and rolls
on the ground; having spread lotus petals, He sits alone, absorbed in meditation; seeing this, the poet speaks to Him,
clasping His feet. In PK it is the gaura-chandrika to the section on vasaka-sajja (6th pallava). Raga suhai.*[^08-46]

**13.1.** Streams flow from His reddened eyes;
Gora sits with His head bowed.

**13.2.** Seeing a shadow, He starts in His heart
and again and again rolls on the ground.[^08-47]

**13.3.** Having spread out lotus petals,
the Lord sits absorbed in meditation.[^08-48]

**13.4.** Sitting in seclusion, all alone,
He lives the bhava of vasaka-sajja.[^08-49]

**13.5.** Vasudeva Ghosha, seeing this,
says something to Him, clasping His feet.

[^08-46]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha." PK: vol. 1, PDF p. 241 (printed p. 230), 2nd shakha, 6th pallava ("Now the
vasaka-sajja. The Sri Mahaprabhu befitting it"), no. 5 (mark "॥৫॥৩৫৬॥"); raga suhai (MS P-R — kedara); MSS P-R-Sa no.
468, P-R 17.1. Not found in the OCR of GPT1. Majumdar counts PK 356 among Vasu's padas on the Lord's bhava. The
vasaka-sajja is the heroine who adorns herself and the bower and waits for her beloved; in the gaura-chandrika the Lord
lives this bhava of Radha waiting for Krishna — this is pure prema, not a worldly feeling.
[^08-47]: The shadow seems to Him to be Krishna approaching. MSS "ka," "kha": "astonished" (camakita); P-R, instead of "Seeing
a shadow… heart": "what bhava is in His heart!" MSS P-R-Sa, P-R: "again and again" (kṣaṇe kṣaṇe, khane khane) — the same.
[^08-48]: The bed of petals prepared for the Beloved is a detail of the vasaka-sajja bhava. MS P-R: "tender leaves" (komala)
instead of "lotus petals," and "Gora sits absorbed in meditation."
[^08-49]: MS P-R-Sa: ekāmbare, P-R: ekāsare (the same, "alone").

## 14. Vasu Ghosha — "āji kene gorācām̐dera virasa vayāna…" (PK 370)
*The Lord in Radha's mood — khandita: Gorachand's face is cheerless, His eyes full of tears, His lips pale, His body
weary, His steps unsteady; the poet wonders where Gora was and in hope of what rasa He spent the night without sleep. In
PK it is the gaura-chandrika to the section on the khandita (6th pallava). Raga vibhasa or tori.*[^08-50]

**14.1.** Why is Gorachand's face so cheerless today?
What bhava is in His heart — His eyes are full of tears?[^08-51]

**14.2.** Why has the moon of His face withered — for what reason?
Why have His red lips grown pale?

**14.3.** His limbs are powerless with weariness — He cannot hold Himself up;
swaying and swaying, He falls whenever He takes a step.[^08-52]

**14.4.** Says Vasu Ghosha: where was Gora?
In hope of what rasa did He spend this night?[^08-53]

[^08-50]: Signature: "Vasu Ghosha." PK: vol. 1, PDF pp. 250–251 (printed pp. 239–240), 2nd shakha, 6th pallava ("Now the
khandita. The Sri Gaurachandra befitting it"), no. 19 (mark "॥১৯॥৩৭০॥"); raga vibhasa or tori (MS P-R — "southern
shri"); MS P-R 17.1 (according to PK's apparatus). The pada is in the index of GPT1 ("āji kena gorācām̐dera virasa vadana"), but
its text was not found in the OCR. Another pada of Vasu with a similar opening is "āju kena gorācām̐dera virasa vayāna / ke āila ke
āila…" (GPT1 p. 313, section "Separation," no. 1). Majumdar counts PK 370 among Vasu's padas on the Lord's bhava. The
khandita is the heroine who has waited in vain all night for her beloved and is offended; in the gaura-chandrika the
Lord, in Radha's mood, has spent the night without sleep waiting for Krishna — hence the reddened eyes, the pallor and
the weariness. This is pure prema; we translate faithfully.
[^08-51]: MSS "ka," "ga": paṛeche (the same, "has arisen"); P-R: "has risen" (uṭheche).
[^08-52]: MS P-R, instead of couplet 14.2: "How much nectar His moon-face pours forth — why then has that face withered?" P-R:
"body" (gā) instead of "limbs," "bending" (ḍhaliyā) instead of "swaying."
[^08-53]: The poet's question is the bewilderment of a companion who does not know the cause; the answer is given by the
gaura-chandrika itself: the Lord has waited all night (as Radha waits for Krishna). MS "ga": "in hope of what rasa did He
spend this night awake."

## 15. Vasu Ghosha — "varaṇa kāñcana daśavāna…" (PK 476)
*The Lord in Radha's mood — mana: golden, clad in crimson, Gora sits with bowed head, tears streaming from His eyes; now
He puts His palm to His head, now draws on the ground with His nail, weeps and rolls in the dust. In PK it is the
gaura-chandrika to the section on the "unyielding mana" (2nd shakha). Raga suhai.*[^08-54]

**15.1.** His complexion is gold of the highest assay,
He is clad in crimson cloth.

**15.2.** Gora sits with His head bowed;
streams flow from His reddened eyes.

**15.3.** Now He puts His palm to His head,
now He draws on the ground with His nail.[^08-55]

**15.4.** Gora Raya weeps, distraught;
His golden body rolls in the dust.

**15.5.** Vasudeva Ghosha sings of His qualities:
night and day nothing else is dear to him.[^08-56]

[^08-54]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha." PK: vol. 1, PDF pp. 322–323 (printed pp. 311–312), 2nd shakha, "Now the section on
mana; first, mana with a cause: the unyielding mana, when signs of enjoyment [with another] are seen on the hero's body.
The Sri Gaurachandra befitting it," no. 1 (mark "॥১॥৪৭৬॥"); raga suhai; MS P-R-Sa no. 700. GPT1 — p. 311, no. 12 (raga
pathamanjari; section on mana); GPT2 — sect. 4.6, no. 12. Majumdar counts PK 476 among Vasu's padas on the Lord's bhava.
Mana is Radha's jealous pique with Krishna; the Lord lives this bhava of Radha — this is pure prema. "Gold of the highest
assay" (daśavāna) — lit. "of tenfold assay."
[^08-55]: Drawing on the ground with the nail is the usual gesture of the offended heroine in poetry. Instead of couplets
15.2–15.5, MS P-R-Sa has: "His eyes are like lotuses, tears flow down on both sides like strings of pearls falling; His
body rolls on the ground — a golden mountain grey with dust; says Vasudeva Ghosha: without Gora I cannot live." MSS "ka,"
"ga," "ca": śira, "ca": karatale, "ka": "with the palm" instead of "on the ground," "ca": nakha — the same meaning. GPT1: "now He
lays His head on His palm."
[^08-56]: MSS "kha," "gha": "day and night" (divā niśi).

## 16. Vasu Ghosha — "kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa vali gorā kām̐de…" (PK 525)
*The Lord in Radha's mood — mana: Gora weeps, repeating "Krishna, Krishna," tears flow from His eyes like Gangas; He does
not anoint His body with sandal, and, all grey with dust, rolls on the ground; His face is dulled with pique, nothing
pleases Him, neither by day nor by night does He sleep. In PK it is the gaura-chandrika to the section "mana — another
mode" (the beginning of the 18th pallava). Raga suhai.*[^08-57]

**16.1.** Repeating "Krishna, Krishna," Gora weeps again and again;
how many Suradhunis flow from His reddened eyes!

**16.2.** Gora does not anoint His body with fragrant sandal;
grey with dust, He rolls on the ground.[^08-58]

**16.3.** His face is dulled by mana, nothing pleases Him;
night and day Gora passes without sleep.

**16.4.** Again and again His body starts — He cannot be held;
of Gorachand's bhava of mana sings Vasu Ghosha.[^08-59]

[^08-57]: Signature: "Vasu Ghosha." PK: vol. 1, printed p. 353, 2nd shakha, 18th pallava ("Now mana, another mode. The Shri
Gaurachandra befitting it"), no. 1 (mark "॥১॥৫২৫॥"); raga suhai; no manuscript number. In the main scan (IA
in.ernet.dli.2015.337379, PDF p. 364) the page is damaged; the text was read from a second scan of the same edition
(IA in.ernet.dli.2015.513340, PDF p. 372). GPT1 — p. 311, no. 15 (raga suhai; section on mana); GPT2 — sect. 4.6, no.
15. Majumdar counts PK 525 among Vasu's padas on the Lord's bhava. On mana, see note 54.
[^08-58]: MS "gha": bhome (the same, "on the ground").
[^08-59]: MSS "ka," "kha," "ga," "ca": kṣaṇe (the same, "again and again") and dharaṇa; MS "ka": "of the various bhavas" (nānā)
instead of "of the bhava of mana."

# Chapter 9. Vasu Ghosha: the Lord's Bhavas, Separation, Nityananda, Prayers

*Padas of Vasu (Vasudeva) Ghosha known from the *Padakalpataru* (PK), in the order of the lilas: Gaura in the
kirtana of Navadvipa, His form, His rest and the boat play on the Ganga; the Lord in Krishna's mood and in the mood of
Radha pining in separation (gaura-chandrikas to the sections of PK on impending and accomplished separation); the
devotees' longing for Gaura who has gone; praise of Nityananda; stavas and prarthanas — prayers to Gauranga. Majumdar
regards Vasu Ghosha as an eyewitness of the Navadvipa kirtanas and counts these padas among his padas on the Lord's
bhava, on Nityananda and among his stavas. The text follows PK, checked against the scans, with the manuscript
variants from PK's apparatus, the *Gaura-pada-tarangini* (GPT1 — 1st ed., 1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934) and the
*Kshanada-gita-chintamani* (KGC); the Bengali original, variants and word-for-word translation are in the full version of the book.*

## 1. Vasu Ghosha — "navadvīpe udaya karilā dvija-rāja…" (PK 1494)
*Gaura in the kirtana of Navadvipa: the moon risen in the darkness of Kali among the stars, His companions; grey with
dust, He sways on the waves of bhava, sings "Hari, Hari" and stands still in the tribhanga pose; at His left is
Gadadhara; remembering Vrindavana, the Lord weeps and pours a downpour of the holy name upon the world. In PK it is the
gaura-chandrika to the section "the spring rasa." Raga dhanashi or vasanta.*[^09-1]

**1.1.** *(Refrain)* In Navadvipa the king of the twice-born has risen[^09-2] —
dense is the darkness of Kali, but Gorachand shines
amid the stars — His companions.

**1.2.** In kirtana, brimming over with love, grey all over with dust,
He sways on the waves of bhava;
karatalas in His hands, He sings, "Hari, Hari!" —
and again and again stands still, bent in three places.[^09-3]

**1.3.** At His left is dear Gadadhara,
and on his shoulder rests the Lord's graceful arm that reaches to the knees.[^09-4]
Remembering Vrindavana, ceaselessly yearning,
He sheds streams of tears from His reddish eyes.

**1.4.** His eyes pour and pour like a fresh raincloud,
His teeth shine brighter than lightning.
Vasudeva Ghosha sings: to deliver the souls of the age of Kali,
He has rained a downpour of Hari's name.[^09-5]

[^09-1]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha." PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 432 (printed p. 419), 3rd shakha, 27th pallava, section "atha vāsantī
rāsalīlā । taducita-śrīgauracandra" (gaura-chandrika to the spring rasa), no. 70 (mark "॥৭০॥১৪৯৪॥"); raga dhanashi or vasanta;
MS P-R-Sa no. 2044. GPT1 — p. 131, no. 59 (raga dhanashi). Majumdar counts PK 1494 among Vasu's padas on the Lord's
bhava.
[^09-2]: "Dvija-raja," "king of the twice-born," is both the moon and the best of brahmanas: Gaura is a brahmana risen
over Navadvipa like the moon.
[^09-3]: Tribhanga is the pose of Krishna playing the flute (bent at the neck, waist and knee): in kirtana the Lord
spontaneously assumes Krishna's form.
[^09-4]: Gadadhara Pandita, according to the *Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika*, is a manifestation of Radha; he stands at Gaura's
left as Radha stands at Krishna's left. MS "kh": "ājāno"; P-R-Sa: "ajāne" (the same).
[^09-5]: MS "kh": "pours" (varikhata). P-R-Sa: "like" (yena) instead of "brighter than" (jini).

## 2. Vasu Ghosha — "cala dekhi giyā gorā ati manohare…" (PK 973)
*Gaura's form in Nadia: "Come, let us go and see Gora!" — His body brighter than tested gold, His arms reaching to the
knees like golden pillars, a red cloth at His waist, a garland of malati down to His feet; the poet is ready to give
his life for Him. In PK it is the gaura-chandrika to the section "anuraga: setting out to the tryst by night." Raga
suhai.*[^09-6]

**2.1.** Come, let us go and see Gora, beautiful beyond words:
wondrous is Gora's form in the town of Nadia!

**2.2.** His body, tender and radiant, outshines tested gold;
who, seeing the waves of His eyes, can keep his composure?

**2.3.** His arms reach to His knees like golden pillars,
a red cloth is at His waist, broad are His hips.[^09-7]

**2.4.** A garland of malati sways on His neck down to His feet.
Says Vasu: "Come — I will give my life for Him!"[^09-8]

[^09-6]: Signature: "Vasu." PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 200 (printed p. 187), 3rd shakha, 12th pallava, section "tataḥ punaśca
abhisārānurāgaḥ rātrau yathā । śrīgauracandraḥ," no. 1 (mark "॥১॥৯৭৩॥"); raga suhai; MS P-R-Sa no. 1423. The same pada stands in
PK a second time — PK 2176 (vol. 3, PDF pp. 259–260, printed pp. 248–249; 19th pallava, no. 9; MS P-R-Sa no. 2284), in
the section of padas spoken by the women of Nadia, with the ending "Says Vasu: 'I will go and offer [Him] my youth'";
so too in GPT1 (p. 161, no. 15, raga shri), among padas in nagari-bhava. Majumdar counts PK 973 among the padas on the
Lord's form and PK 2176 under nagari-bhava. The PK 973 recension is translated here; the 2176 recension belongs to
nagari-bhava: worship of Gaura in the spirit of "Gaura-nagari" is not accepted by the Gaudiya tradition (Vrindavana
Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta).
[^09-7]: Long arms, a broad chest and broad hips are marks of a great personality (mahapurusha) according to the
samudrika-shastra; so too Vrindavana Dasa and Krishnadasa Kaviraja describe the Lord's form.
[^09-8]: Literally "I will give my life as nichhani" — a rite in which something precious is waved around a beloved
person to ward off misfortune and then given away; here the poet gives his very life.

## 3. Vasu Ghosha — "śutiyāche gorācām̐da śayana-mandire…" (PK 656)
*Gorachand lies in His bedchamber on a wondrous couch, languid; it is as if the Creator had strained lightning from
the clouds and put all rasa into Him; Vasudeva Ghosha looks on in joy. In PK it is the gaura-chandrika to the section
"languor after the play" (rasalasa). Raga vibhasa.*[^09-9]

**3.1.** Gorachand lies in His bedchamber
on a wondrous couch, on a lovely bed.

**3.2.** Languid is the body of Gora, the king of dancers —
how can I tell the beauty of His body? It cannot be told![^09-10]

**3.3.** As if lightning had been carefully strained from the clouds —
so much rasa did the Creator put in, fashioning Him!

**3.4.** A lovely bed, wondrous pillows —
Vasudeva Ghosha looks on with joy in his heart.

[^09-9]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha." PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 51 (printed p. 38), 3rd shakha, section "atha rasālasa । taducita-śrīgauracandra,"
no. 1 (mark "॥১॥৬৫৬॥"); raga vibhasa; MS P-R-Sa no. 1131. GPT1 — pp. 361–362, no. 53 (raga vibhasa). According to PK's
index of first lines (vol. 5), the same pada stands in PK a second time — PK 2474 (vol. 4, the section on the night and
morning plays); in the scan of vol. 4 (IA 354459) the leaf with PK 2474–2478 is missing between PDF pp. 44
and 45, so its variants have not been checked. The catalogue wrongly linked PK 656 to the GPT pada "nācata śacītanaya
gaurasundara…" (VG-057). Majumdar counts PK 656 among Vasu's padas on the Lord's bhava. PK's section "rasalasa" is about the
languor of Radha and Krishna after the night's play; the gaura-chandrika shows the Lord wearied by the night's kirtana
and bhava.
[^09-10]: MSS "gh," "c": "Gaura lies" (śutiyā āchena gaura) instead of "Gorachand lies"; "k," "c": "in absorption" (āveśe),
"gh": "in languor" (alase) instead of "languid" (ālase; GPT1 — "āveśe," with "ālase" in a note); P-R-Sa: "how can I tell the
beauty of His body" (ki kava aṅgera śobhā), "says Vasudeva Ghosha" (kaya) instead of "looks on" (dekhe).

## 4. Vasu Ghosha — "nā jāniye gorācām̐dera kona bhāva mane…" (PK 1409)
*The boat play on the Ganga: Gorachand goes to the bank with His companions, steps into a boat with Gadadhara and
steers it Himself; everyone cries "We are sinking!" and bails out water, and, remembering the former play, floats in
the waters of prema, while the Lord, looking at Gadadhara, gently smiles. In PK it is the gaura-chandrika to the
section "the boat play" (nauka-vilasa). Raga tudi.*[^09-11]

**4.1.** I do not know what bhava is in Gorachand's heart:
He went with His companions to the bank of the Suradhuni.[^09-12]

**4.2.** Taking with Him dear Gadadhara and others,
Gaura stepped into a boat, overwhelmed by prema.

**4.3.** Becoming the helmsman Himself, He steers the boat;
"We are sinking, sinking!" all cry, and bail out the water.

**4.4.** All the companions call out, "Hari, Hari!" —
remembering the former play, some float in the waters of prema.[^09-13]

**4.5.** Looking into Gadadhara's face, He smiles ever so gently —
so says Vasudeva Ghosha, with jubilation in his heart.

[^09-11]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha." PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 388 (printed p. 375), 3rd shakha, 26th pallava, section "atha
naukā-vilāsa । taducita śrīmahāprabhu," no. 1 (mark "॥১॥১৪০৯॥"); raga tudi; MS P-R-Sa no. 1925. GPT1 — p. 333, no. 38 (raga tudi;
among the padas on the dana-lila). Majumdar counts PK 1409 among Vasu's padas on the Lord's bhava. Compare Ramananda's
pada on the same play (PK 1417, chapter 6).
[^09-12]: Suradhuni, "the river of the gods," is the Ganga.
[^09-13]: "The former play" is Krishna's play with Radha and the gopis in a boat on the Yamuna (nauka-lila): the Lord at
the helm is Krishna, Gadadhara is Radha. MSS "k," "c," P-R-Sa: "Himself" — āpani (the same); P-R-Sa: "guides" (vahe) instead
of "steers" (vāya), "with joy" (hariṣe) instead of "with jubilation" (ullāse). GPT1: "smiles to Himself" (mane mane hāse).

## 5. Vasu Ghosha — "āre mora gorā dvijamaṇi…" (PK 54)
*The Lord in the mood of Krishna stricken with purvaraga: "Radha, Radha!" Gora calls, weeps and rolls on the ground,
chants Radha's name with great devotion, rivers of tears flow from His eyes, and again and again He loses
consciousness. In PK it is the gaura-chandrika to the section "Sri Krishna's purvaraga." Raga suhai, tala
jayajayanti.*[^09-14]

**5.1.** O my Gora, jewel of the twice-born!
"Radha, Radha!" He calls, weeps and rolls on the ground.

**5.2.** Gora chants Radha's name with great devotion,
and streams of the Suradhuni flow from His reddish eyes.[^09-15]

**5.3.** Again and again Gora's body rolls on the ground,
again and again, uttering Radha's name, He swoons.

**5.4.** His body is thrilled with gooseflesh, His voice falters.
Says Vasu: "Why is Gora so agitated?"

[^09-14]: Signature: "Vasu." PK: vol. 1, PDF p. 51 (printed p. 40), 1st shakha, section "śrīkṛṣṇasya pūrvvarāgaḥ । taducita-śrīmahāprabhuḥ,"
no. 1 (mark "॥১॥৫৪॥"); "suhai । jayajayantī." GPT1 — p. 297, no. 16 (jayajayanti). Majumdar counts PK 54 among Vasu's padas on
the Lord's bhava. Usually the Lord abides in Radha's mood, but His companions also saw His mood of Krishna longing for
the gopis (cf. CC Adi 17: the Lord chants "Gopi, gopi!").
[^09-15]: Streams of the Suradhuni (the Ganga) are His tears. MS "kh" and GPT1: "how many Suradhunis flow…". Line 5.2 is
repeated by Radhamohana Dasa in his pada on Gaura and Gauridasa (GPT1, p. 290, no. 43).

## 6. Vasu Ghosha — "sakala bhakata meli ānande hulāhuli…" (PK 2041)
*In the morning the devotees come with joyful cries to see Gauranga, but He has not slept all night and His face is
wan; rising, He sits down again on the ground, alone, apart; the devotees are alarmed, not understanding what bhava
has risen in His heart; one washes His face, another tidies His hair. In PK it is the gaura-chandrika "on the next
day" to the section "recollections of the complete union." Raga pahida.*[^09-16]

**6.1.** All the devotees together, with joyful cries,
came to see Gauranga.
Gauranga is lying down, no one is near Him;
He has stayed awake all night, His face is wan.

**6.2.** *(Refrain)* Here is a great wonder:
rising, Gaura Hari sat down again on the ground,
and sits with no one beside Him.[^09-17]

**6.3.** Seeing this, the devotees were alarmed:
why is His face so cheerless?
All say, "Alas, alas! Nothing can be understood —
what bhava has risen in His heart today?"

**6.4.** One gently washes His face with water,
another tidies His hair.
"We know nothing: Gora is bhava embodied" —
and sad is Vasu Ghosha's face.[^09-18]

[^09-16]: Signature: "Vasu Ghosha." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 210 (printed p. 199), 4th shakha, 16th pallava ("samriddhiman
sambhoga: recollections"), section "atha dināntare śrīmadgauracandro yathā," no. 18 (mark "॥১৮॥২০৪১॥"); raga pahida. GPT1 — p. 312,
no. 17 (pahida), just before the section on separation; in GPT2 — in the section on the antya-lila (the catalogue had
it twice: VG-080 and VG-122). The place is not named. Majumdar counts PK 2041 among Vasu's padas on the Lord's bhava.
The PK section shows Radha, on the next day, recalling the night of union with Krishna; the gaura-chandrika shows the
Lord absorbed in such recollections.
[^09-17]: MSS "k," "kh": "Gauranga" instead of "Gaura"; "k," "kh," "c" and GPT1: "having sat" (vasiyā) instead of "sat." In MS "k"
there is a lacuna mark in place of the word "with joyful cries" (hulāhuli).
[^09-18]: "Bhava embodied" (bhāvera mūrati): the Lord, in whom Radha's bhava manifests in its fullness.

## 7. Vasu Ghosha — "āju kene gorācām̐dera virasa vayāna…" (PK 1598)
*The Lord in the mood of Radha foreseeing separation: Gorachand's face is cheerless, He asks, "Who has come?" and
weeps; the devotees around have fainted, not understanding the cause; crying "Hari, Hari," Gora sighs heavily. In PK it
is the gaura-chandrika to the section "impending separation." Raga suhai, tala kandarpa.*[^09-19]

**7.1.** Why is Gorachand's face so cheerless today?
"Who has come? Who has come?" He says, and tears stream down.[^09-20]

**7.2.** All around, the devotees, weeping, have fainted:
why Gauranga is so, they cannot understand.[^09-21]

**7.3.** To look at that face — the heart is wrung:
how many Suradhunis pour from His eyes!

**7.4.** Crying "Hari, Hari," Gora sighs heavily;
Vasu strikes his head with his hand and speaks, faltering with tears.

[^09-19]: Signature: "Vasu." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 18 (printed p. 7), 4th shakha, 2nd pallava, section "atha bhāvī virahaḥ ।
tadbhāvākrāntaḥ śrīmahāprabhuḥ" ("impending separation; Sri Mahaprabhu, overwhelmed by this bhava"), no. 1 (mark "॥১॥১৫৯৮॥");
"suhai । kandarpatāla"; MS P-R-Sa no. 806. GPT1 — p. 313, no. 1 (suhai, kandarpa) — the first pada of the section on
separation. Majumdar counts PK 1598 among Vasu's padas on the Lord's bhava.
[^09-20]: The PK section: Radha learns that Akrura has come for Krishna to take Him to Mathura; the Lord in Radha's mood
asks, "Who has come?" GPT1: "'Who has come? Who has come?' — and tears stream down" (kari instead of vali).
[^09-21]: MS "k": "kena" (the same, "why"); "gh": "they cannot understand His heart" (vujhilu mana) instead of "cannot understand
the cause"; "k": "before Him" (samukha) instead of "that face" (se mukha); MS "kh" lacks the word "jāni" ("is wrung," literally
"I know not how"); P-R-Sa: "weep" (jhure) instead of "pour" (jhare).

## 8. Vasu Ghosha — "roi roi jape gorā kṛṣṇa-nāma-madhu…" (PK 1634)
*The Lord in the mood of Radha separated from Krishna: weeping, Gora chants the honeyed name of Krishna; He whose feet
Shiva and Brahma do not attain sits under a tree, having left all company and all comforts; His golden body is adorned
with the treasures of bhava; seeing Him, all weep. In PK it is the gaura-chandrika to the section "accomplished
separation." Raga suhai.*[^09-22]

**8.1.** Weeping and weeping, Gora chants the honey of Krishna's name —
as if a spotless moon were showering nectar.[^09-23]

**8.2.** He whose feet Shiva and Brahma do not attain by worship
has sat down under a tree, forsaking all company.[^09-24]

**8.3.** Leaving all comforts, He has grown weak;
His golden body is adorned with the treasures of bhava.[^09-25]

**8.4.** Seeing Him, all the people weep ceaselessly;
Vasudeva Ghosha's heart can find no rest.

[^09-22]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 37 (printed p. 26), 4th shakha, 4th pallava, section "atha
bhūta-virahaḥ । nāyikā proṣitabhartṛkā । tadbhāvākrāntaḥ śrīgauracandro yathā" ("accomplished separation; the heroine whose beloved has
gone abroad; Sri Gaurachandra, overwhelmed by this bhava"), no. 1 (mark "॥১॥১৬৩৪॥"); raga suhai (P-R: sindhura); MS P-R-Sa
no. 857, MS P-R no. 40.19. GPT2 — in the section on separation (the catalogue had it as VG-043 and VG-115; one pada).
Not found in GPT1. Majumdar counts PK 1634 among Vasu's padas on the Lord's bhava. Sitting under a tree, having left
all company — the Lord after His sannyasa.
[^09-23]: MSS "k," "kh," "c," P-R-Sa and GPT2: "as if a spotless moon were pouring nectar" (jharaye; "k," "kh," "gh," "c," P-R-Sa and
GPT2 — vimala, "spotless," instead of niramala, the same).
[^09-24]: MSS "k," "c": "whose feet they do not attain by devotion (bhakti)"; P-R: "by seeking" (khuji).
[^09-25]: MS P-R: "He left all comforts, renouncing strength" (chāṛala sava sukha tejiyā śakati); "k," "kh," P-R: "went" (gela) instead of
"has grown weak" (bhela aśakati — literally "became powerless"). The treasures of bhava are the sattvika-bhavas: tears,
trembling, gooseflesh and the other signs of prema. P-R: "the heart finds no rest" (sthira).

## 9. Vasu Ghosha — "virale vasiyā ekeśvare…" (PK 1635)
*The Lord as a sannyasi in separation: alone, in solitude, He ceaselessly chants the name of Hari; His body, once
anointed with sandal, now cares for nothing but dust; He has left the pastimes with Lakshmi and lives under a tree, has
left the flute and taken the sannyasi's staff; He knows neither day nor night. In PK it is the second gaura-chandrika
to the section "accomplished separation." Raga suhai.*[^09-26]

**9.1.** In solitude He sits alone
and ceaselessly chants the name of Hari.

**9.2.** His body was anointed with fragrant sandal —
now nothing pleases Him but dust.[^09-27]

**9.3.** The Lord has left the pastimes with Lakshmi —
now His dwelling is beneath a tree.[^09-28]

**9.4.** Leaving the enchanting flute from His hands,
He has taken the staff and become a sannyasi.

**9.5.** He knows neither day nor night.
Says Vasu: "The heart is breaking!"[^09-29]

[^09-26]: Signature: "Vasu." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 37 (printed p. 26), 4th shakha, 4th pallava, "tathā rāga" (P-R: sindhura), no. 2
(mark "॥২॥১৬৩৫॥"); MS P-R-Sa no. 858, P-R no. 40.41. KGC 12.1 and 23.1 (raga barari; the same pada twice) and GPT2 (no. 11,
barari) — in a fuller recension (see note 29). The catalogue also listed it as BD-040 (by a misreading of the KGC
bhanita as "Balarama"; in KGC the signature is "Vasu"). Majumdar counts PK 1635 among Vasu's padas on the Lord's bhava.
[^09-27]: MS P-R: "alone" (ekāsare) instead of "alone" (ekeśvare); MS "k": "else" (āra) instead of "other" (āna). After 9.2 MS P-R has the
couplet: "The crown of all incarnations, / the wish-fulfilling gem of the destitute" (it is also in KGC and GPT2).
[^09-28]: Lakshmi is the goddess of fortune, the Lord's eternal consort; in Gaura-lila — Lakshmipriya and Vishnupriya. MS
P-R: "He left" (chāṛala) instead of "the Lord has left"; "now" — P-R: "ive" (the same); instead of "leaving the enchanting
flute from His hands" — P-R: "He left the garland of forest flowers" (chāṛala vanamālā).
[^09-29]: MSS "k," "kh," P-R-Sa: "heeds not" (māna) instead of "knows not" (jāna); P-R: "jāne" (the same); "parāṇe" (the same). In KGC
and GPT2 the pada is longer: after 9.1 — "The crown of all incarnations, / the wish-fulfilling gem of the destitute";
after 9.2 — "Ornaments of jewels / He does not touch even in dreams"; instead of 9.3–9.4 — "He left the pastimes with
Lakshmi — / why then does He dwell beneath a tree? / He left the garland and the flute — / now, taking the staff, He has
become a sannyasi" (GPT2: "He left the enchanting flute from His hands"); then — "Spurning laughter and play, / His eyes
are swollen with weeping"; "Making prema His treasure, / He has taken all the destitute with Him"; the ending — "He
bathes in the waters of prema. / Says Vasu: 'The heart is breaking!'"

## 10. Vasu Ghosha — "majhu mane lāgala śela…" (PK 451)
*A lament for Gaura who has turned away from His lover: a spear has pierced the heart, life has become fruitless; if
one is never again to see Gora's face, what joy is there in life? Without Gora life cannot be held. In PK it is the
gaura-chandrika to the section "repentance after a quarrel" (kalahantarita). Raga pathamanjari.*[^09-30]

**10.1.** A spear has pierced my heart:
Gaura has turned away from me.

**10.2.** My life has become fruitless —
a cruel Creator has sent me grief.

**10.3.** To whom shall I tell this grief?
When I begin to speak, my breast is torn apart.[^09-31]

**10.4.** If I am never again to see Gora's face,
what joy is there for me in life?[^09-32]

**10.5.** Vasudeva Ghosha sings this rasa:
without Gora life cannot be held.

[^09-30]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha." PK: vol. 1, PDF p. 307 (printed p. 296), 2nd shakha, section "punaśca kalahāntaritā ।
taducita-śrīgauracandraḥ," no. 1 (mark "॥১॥৪৫১॥"); raga pathamanjari (P-R: suhai); MS P-R-Sa no. 640, P-R no. 22.1. GPT1 — p. 312,
no. 19 (pathamanjari), following a pada of Radhamohana on the Lord in the mood of mana and separation; GPT2 — in the
section of the laments of Shachi and Vishnupriya after the sannyasa (no. 16). Whose words these are, the author does
not say; the PK section shows Radha repenting that in anger She rejected Krishna. We translate it as the lament of a
devoted soul separated from Gaura. Majumdar does not discuss this pada.
[^09-31]: MS P-R in 10.2: "majhu" instead of "mora" (the same, "my"); "k," "g," P-R-Sa: "eha dukha" (the same); P-R: "to whom then shall I
tell this grief" (hāma kāhe kahavahim̐ dukha).
[^09-32]: MSS "k," "g," "c," P-R: "tava"; P-R-Sa: "tavahi" (the same: "then"); P-R: "kivā sukha" (the same).

## 11. Vasu Ghosha — "kata dine herava gorācām̐dera mukha…" (PK 2279)
*The devotees' longing for Gaura after the sannyasa: when shall we see Gorachand's face, when will the Lord embrace
us, when will our ears hear His words? The people of Nadia weep, not seeing Gora. In PK it is the section "the
devotees' longing" in the pallava on Gauranga's sannyasa. Raga suhai.*[^09-33]

**11.1.** When shall I see Gorachand's face?
When will all the sorrow of my heart be stilled?

**11.2.** When will the Lord Gora clasp me in His embrace?
When will fate be kind to me?[^09-34]

**11.3.** When will the auspicious day dawn for my ears —
to hear day and night the words of the Moon-faced One?

**11.4.** Says Vasu Ghosha, remembering Gora's virtues:
the people of Nadia weep, not seeing Gora.[^09-35]

[^09-33]: Signature: "Vasu Ghosha." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 296 (printed p. 285), 4th shakha, 21st pallava ("The sannyasa of Shri
Gauranga, etc."), section "atha bhaktagaṇasya utkaṇṭhā yathā," no. 62 (mark "॥৬২॥২২৭৯॥"); raga suhai; MS P-R-Sa no. 2383, P-R no. 41.11.
GPT1 — p. 387, no. 14 (suhai); GPT2 — sect. 5.4, no. 14. Majumdar counts PK 2279 among Vasu's stavas and prarthanas.
Next in PK (2280) comes Vasu's pada "gorā-guṇe prāṇa kānde…" (chapter 5).
[^09-34]: MS P-R: "shall I see" (dekhiva); instead of "when will all the sorrow of my heart be stilled" — P-R: "at the sight of
Gora's face [sorrow] will cease" (gorāmukha daraśe ṭuṭava); P-R-Sa, P-R: "kore," "more" (the same).
[^09-35]: MSS "k," "kh," "gh," "c," P-R-Sa and GPT1: "śravaṇe haive" (the same); P-R: "sings" (gāya) instead of "says," "the Lord's" (pahum̐) instead of "Gora's"; instead of "the
people of Nadia weep" — MS "kh": "how can life be kept [, not seeing Gora]" (kemane rahive prāṇa); P-R: "weeping, the eyes are
dying" (jhuriyā maraye ām̐khi).

## 12. Vasu Ghosha — "nitāi kevala patita janāra vandhu…" (PK 2314)
*Praise of Nitai: He alone is the friend of the fallen, an ocean of jewels amid the destitute; in separation from Gaura
He looks all around and calls, "Lord Gora Raya!" and falls unconscious; His companions take Him in their arms and weep;
tears of prema flow from His reddish eyes, with a thundering voice He calls, "Brother, brother!" and the earth trembles
under His steps; He gave the world prema through sankirtana — why then has Vasu been left out? In PK it stands in the
pallava "Description of Sri Nityananda's virtues." Raga sindhura.*[^09-36]

**12.1.** *(Refrain)* Nitai alone is the friend of fallen people.
By the fruit of the living beings' age-old pious deeds the Creator has granted them,
amid their poverty, an ocean of jewels.[^09-37]

**12.2.** Looking all around, He goes and calls, "Lord Gora Raya!" —
and falls unconscious to the ground.
His dear companions gather, take Nitai in their arms
and weep, gazing at His moonlike face.

**12.3.** His eyes, red as a fresh lotus, brim with tears of prema —
as if the Mandakini were streaming down Sumeru.[^09-38]
With a voice deep as the thunder of clouds He calls, "Brother, brother!" —
under the weight of His steps the earth trembles.

**12.4.** Merciful Nitai gave the living beings the shelter of prema —
such mercy is known to all the world.
Through the sankirtana of the name so dear to Him He delivered the people of the world —
why then has Vasu been left out?[^09-39]

[^09-36]: Signature: "Vasu." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 308 (printed p. 297), 4th shakha, 22nd pallava ("Description of Shri
Nityananda's virtues"), no. 21 (mark "॥২১॥২৩১৪॥"); raga sindhura; MS P-R-Sa no. 2418. KGC 27.2 (sindhura; "of Shri
Nityananda-chandra"); GPT1 — pp. 423–424, no. 31 (sindhura); GPT2 — sect. 6.1, no. 31. Majumdar counts PK 2314 among
Vasu's padas on Nityananda.
[^09-37]: MS "kh": "to the living beings" (jīve); P-R-Sa: "jīva" (the same). KGC: "the Creator brought and joined [to them]" (vidhi
āni milāola); GPT1: "amid poverty, an ocean of love" (pirītera sindhu).
[^09-38]: The Mandakini is the heavenly Ganga; Sumeru is the golden mountain: the tears flowing down Nitai's golden-hued
body. MSS "k," "kh," "gh," "c," KGC and GPT1: "red as gunja berries" (guñjāruṇa). MS "kh": "meli," P-R-Sa: "mile" (the same:
"gather"); P-R-Sa: "holding" (kare) instead of "take in their arms." KGC and GPT1: "and the Lord [Nitai] weeps, gazing at
the moonlike face," "with thunderous sound again He calls, 'Brother!'"
[^09-39]: "The name so dear to Him" (nija-nāma), literally "His own name": the name of Gaura, whom Nitai regards as His own.
KGC: "He gave the living beings prema unknown even to the Creator; by His own virtues, giving prema, He flooded the three
worlds — / only Vasudeva Ghosha is left out"; so too GPT1.

## 13. Vasu Ghosha — "saṃkīrtane nityānanda nāce…" (PK 2315)
*Nityananda dances in sankirtana with His dear companions near Him, while Govinda and Madhava Ghosha sing; embracing
the fallen, He weeps and says, "I owe you much — take the wares of prema! I will destroy your misfortunes and give you
prema with interest"; Vasu pines in tears, remembering such mercy. In PK it is the next pada of the same pallava. Raga
shri.*[^09-40]

**13.1.** In sankirtana Nityananda dances,
His dear companions near Him.

**13.2.** Hearing the song of Govinda and Madhava Ghosha,
who could keep hold of life?[^09-41]

**13.3.** Embracing the fallen by the neck,
the Lord weeps, full of compassion.

**13.4.** With a faltering voice He speaks to the fallen —
hearing it, stones split apart:[^09-42]

**13.5.** "I owe a great debt to all of you —
take, take the wares of prema!

**13.6.** I will destroy all your misfortunes,
I will give you prema — and with interest besides!"[^09-43]

**13.7.** With love they gaze at His moonlike face,
and He, embracing them by the neck, weeps.

**13.8.** Remembering such mercy,
Vasu Ghosha pines away in tears.

[^09-40]: Signature: "Vasu Ghosha." PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 308–309 (printed pp. 297–298), 4th shakha, 22nd pallava, no. 22 (mark
"॥২২॥২৩১৫॥"); raga shri; MS P-R-Sa no. 2419. Not found in GPT1 or KGC. Majumdar counts PK 2315 among Vasu's padas on
Nityananda.
[^09-41]: Govinda and Madhava Ghosha, Vasu's brothers, were kirtana singers. According to the *Chaitanya-bhagavata*
(Antya 5) the Ghosha brothers were the singers in Nityananda's kirtanas in Gauda; the pada pictures these kirtanas. MS "k": "ghoṣe" (the same).
[^09-42]: MS "gh": "patitere" (the same).
[^09-43]: MS "k": "tā sabhāra" (the same: "to all of you") instead of "to sabhāra" in 13.5 and 13.6. "With interest" — vyāja.

## 14. Vasu Ghosha — "jaya jaya jagannātha śacīra nandana…" (PK 2192)
*Praise of Gaura — Jagannatha, the son of Shachi: in Nilachala He holds the conch, disc, club and lotus, in Nadia the
staff and water pot of a sannyasi; formerly He slew Ravana and manifested the splendour of the pastimes of Goloka, now
in Radha's mood He has come as Gora and preached the name Hare Krishna; He is Gaura, He is Krishna, He is Jagannatha.
In PK it stands in the pallava "Sri Gaurachandra — another mode." Raga tirota.*[^09-44]

**14.1.** Glory, glory to Jagannatha, the son of Shachi,
whose feet the three worlds worship!

**14.2.** In Nilachala He holds the conch, disc, club and lotus,
in the town of Nadia — the staff and water pot in His hands.[^09-45]

**14.3.** Some say that formerly He slew Ravana;
He manifested the splendour of the pastimes of Goloka.[^09-46]

**14.4.** And now, in the mood of Sri Radha, He is the Gora-avatara:
Gaura has preached the name "Hare Krishna."[^09-47]

**14.5.** Vasudeva Ghosha says with folded palms:
He is Gaura, He is Krishna, He is Jagannatha.

[^09-44]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 265 (printed p. 254), 4th shakha, 20th pallava, no. 9 (mark

pada twice: VG-001 (from GPT, wrongly linked to PK 2151) and VG-131 (PK 2192, only the ending). Majumdar counts PK 2192
among Vasu's stavas and prarthanas.
[^09-45]: Nilachala is Puri: Jagannatha is the Lord Himself (Vishnu with four emblems); in Nadia He is a sannyasi with a
staff (danda) and water pot (kamandalu).
[^09-46]: Slaying Ravana is Rama's lila; the pastimes of Goloka are Krishna's lila. MSS "k," "kh," "gh," "c": "puruve" (the
same: "formerly").
[^09-47]: "The name 'Hare Krishna'" is the maha-mantra "Hare Krishna Hare Krishna Krishna Krishna Hare Hare / Hare Rama Hare
Rama Rama Rama Hare Hare." MS "kh": "ei" instead of "sei" in 14.5; GPT1: "He who is Gaura is Krishna, is Jagannatha" (yei
gaura sei kṛṣṇa).

## 15. Vasu Ghosha — "gaurāṅga nahita ki mene haita…" (PK 2345)
*Had there been no Gauranga, who would have revealed to the world the glory of Radha and the summit of the rasa of
prema, the way into the sweetness of Vrindavana and devotion in the mood of the maidens of Vraja? In the ocean of
worldly existence there is none more merciful than He; the poet reproaches himself for his heart of stone. In PK it
stands in the pallava on the form and virtues of Chaitanya and Nityananda.*[^09-48]

**15.1.** Had there been no Gauranga, what would have become of us?
How would we have lived?
The glory of Radha, the summit of the rasa of prema —
who would have made it known to the world?[^09-49]

**15.2.** The very essence of the art of entering
the sweetness of the sweet forest of Vrinda,
devotion in the mood of the young maidens of Vraja —
who would have had the power for it?[^09-50]

**15.3.** Sing then again and again of Gauranga's virtues,
O my mind, becoming simple!
In this ocean of worldly existence one so merciful
is not to be found — not one.

**15.4.** Saying "Gauranga," he has not melted —
how does he still live?
Surely of stone they have fashioned
the heart of Vasu![^09-51]

[^09-48]: Signature: "Vasu." PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 319–320 (printed pp. 308–309), 4th shakha, 23rd pallava ("Description of
the form and virtues of Sri Chaitanya and Nityananda"), no. 14 (mark "॥১৪॥২৩৪৫॥"); "tathā rāga"; MS P-R-Sa no. 2449. Majumdar
counts PK 2345 among Vasu's stavas and prarthanas. In GPT1 (pp. 12–13, no. 30, raga vibhasa) and GPT2 (sect. 1.2, no. 30)
it bears the signature "Narahari" and ends in the first person: "Saying 'Gauranga,' I have not melted — how do I still
live? Surely of stone they have fashioned the heart of Narahari" (in the catalogue — NG-002). The attribution is
disputed: PK (and MS P-R-Sa) give Vasu, GPT gives Narahari.
[^09-49]: "How would we have lived" — literally "how would [we] have kept the body" (kemane dharita de). MSS "k," "gh": "kemane"
instead of "ki mene" ("how would it have been"); "kh": "ki mane" (the same); GPT: "tave ki haita" ("what then would have been").
Cf. CC Adi 3–4: the Lord came to taste Radha's prema and to give the world raganuga-bhakti.
[^09-50]: "The maidens of Vraja" are the gopis. Devotion in their mood (raganuga-bhakti) the Lord gave the world through
Rupa, Sanatana and His other companions.
[^09-51]: MS P-R-Sa: "becoming simple" — haiyā (the same; the main text has hailā).

## 16. Vasu Ghosha — "gaurāṅga tumi more dayā nā chāṛiha…" (PK 3007)
*A prarthana to Gauranga: "Do not withdraw Your mercy from me, keep me at Your reddish feet; for them I have left
everything and bidden farewell to kin on both sides; give me the shade of Your feet." In PK it is the section "prayer
again," on Sri Gaurachandra. Raga shri.*[^09-52]

**16.1.** Gauranga, do not withdraw Your mercy from me;
making me Your own, keep me at Your reddish feet.

**16.2.** For the sake of Your feet I have left everything;
finding Your cool feet, I have taken shelter in them.

**16.3.** To this kin and to that I have bidden farewell forever —
keep me at Your feet, calling me Your own.[^09-53]

**16.4.** Vasudeva Ghosha says, clasping Your feet:
in Your mercy, shelter me in the shade of Your feet.

[^09-52]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha." PK: vol. 4, PDF p. 233 (printed p. 224), 4th shakha, 36th pallava, section "punaḥ
prārthanā । tatra śrīgauracandraḥ," no. 23 (mark "॥২৩॥৩০০৭॥"); raga shri; MS P-R-Sa no. 2516. Not found in GPT1, GPT2 or KGC.
Majumdar counts PK 3007 among Vasu's stavas and prarthanas. MS "k": "You will not withdraw… You will keep" (chāṛive,

## 17. Vasu Ghosha — "āre mora gaurāṅga soṇā…" (PK 3008)
*A prarthana to Gauranga: "O my gold, Gauranga, how much I prayed — and found You; I have no one of my own — keep me at
Your feet; give the nectar of prema and the shade of Your cool feet to one tormented." In PK it is the next pada of
the same section. Raga shri.*[^09-54]

**17.1.** *(Refrain)* O my Gauranga, my gold!
How much I prayed — and I have found You.

**17.2.** I can call no one my own —
keep me beneath Your feet, making me Your own.[^09-55]

**17.3.** Your face — with what can it be compared? Only with the moon.
Give the nectar-rasa of prema, and let it be proclaimed abroad.[^09-56]

**17.4.** Cooler than the lotus are Your feet —
give their shade, then, to Vasu Ghosha, tormented by the heat.
