# Chapter 10. Nayanananda and Balarama Dasa: the Gaura-avatara, the Kirtanas of Navadvipa, Gaura and Gadadhara, Shantipura

*Padas of Nayanananda (Nayana Mishra), the nephew and disciple of Gadadhara Pandita, and padas signed by Balarama Dasa,
in the order of the lilas: praise of the Gaura-avatara; the kirtanas of Navadvipa, where Gaura dances beside
Gadadhara; Gauranga's form; His bhava — the Lord weeps gazing at Gadadhara's face; a spring night on the Ganga and the spring swing; Shantipura after
the sannyasa and the departure for Nilachala; Nityananda in Gauda. Majumdar counts Nayanananda among the Lord's
contemporaries: like his other padas, the pada on Gaura and Gadadhara ("premera gṛhiṇī se paṇḍita gadādhare") is cited
by Narahari Chakravarti in the *Bhakti-ratnakara* as testimony; for Balarama Dasa Majumdar accepts three padas from the
*Bhakti-ratnakara* (many padas of a later Balarama Dasa bear the same signature, so the attribution of the rest is
doubtful). The text follows the *Padakalpataru* (PK), checked against the scans, with the manuscript variants from PK's
apparatus, the *Bhakti-ratnakara* (BR), the *Gaura-pada-tarangini* (GPT1 — 1st ed., 1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934) and the
*Kshanada-gita-chintamani* (KGC); the Bengali original, variants and word-for-word translation are in the full version of the book.*

## 1. Balarama Dasa — "kaliyuga-matta-mataṅgaja-maradane…" (PK 617)
*Praise of the Gaura-avatara: the age of Kali is a mad elephant, Gaura is the king of lions who has appeared in the
mountain cave of Navadvipa; at the roar of sankirtana sins and the mystic perfections flee, and on the wretched He
hangs necklaces of the pearls of the holy name. The gaura-chandrika at the opening of PK's 3rd shakha. Raga kamoda.*[^10-1]

**1.1.** When the mad elephant of the Kali age was crushed,
the she-elephant of evil thinking fled far away;
on the low and the wretched He hung, as much as their necks would hold,
hundred-stranded necklaces of the pearls of the Name.[^10-2]

**1.2.** *(Refrain)* Wondrously shines Gaura:
in the mountain cave of the city of Sri Navadvipa
the king of lions has risen!

**1.3.** Hearing the battle roar of sankirtana,
the leopards — the sins — run away;
the does — anima and the other perfections — are frantic with fear,
abandoning the pride of their merits.[^10-3]

**1.4.** Renunciation, sacrifices, the vows of yama, pilgrimages, fasts —
like hares and jackals they flee as if scorched.
Balarama Dasa says: that is why in the world
only the sound of Hari's name is renowned.[^10-4]

[^10-1]: Signature: "Balarama Dasa." PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 14 (printed p. 1), opening of the 3rd shakha, section "śrīgauracandra"
(gaura-chandrika), no. 1 (label "॥১॥৬১৭॥"); raga kamoda; P-R-Sa MS no. 1091. GPT1 — p. 25, no. 1 (kamoda). The catalogue's link
to the *Bhakti-ratnakara* (BR p. 901) is mistaken: there it is a different pada signed by Narahari — "vali-kali-matta-mataṅgaja-maradana
gaurasiṃha nācata nadīyāya". The pada is in elaborate Vrajabuli; which of the Balarama Dasas wrote it is not established.
[^10-2]: MS "ka": "the elephant (like) Yama"; P-R-Sa: "mataṅgajamavadane" (corrupt). GPT1 in a note: "the elephant's roar." MSS "ka",
"ca": "far" (dūra). MS "ka": "pearl" (motima); so also GPT1. "Hundred-stranded necklaces" — śata-dāma, a necklace of many strands.
[^10-3]: Anima (the power of becoming minute) and the other eight siddhis are the mystic perfections of yoga; before
sankirtana they lose their worth, like does before a lion. The word "puṇavata" (here "merits," from puṇya) is unclear; MS
"ka" has "pumavata," "kha," "gha," "ca" "pumarata," P-R-Sa "patharata." MSS "ka," "kha," "ca," P-R-Sa: "islands" (dvīpagaṇa) instead of
"leopards" (dīpigaṇa); MSS "ka," "gha," "ca": "forest" (vana), "kha": "in the forest" instead of "battle" (raṇa).
[^10-4]: MS "ca": "like" (sama); MS "ka": "moon" (śaśi) instead of "hare." MSS "ka," "ca": "Hari" instead of "sound" (dhani). The
thought: nama-sankirtana is the dharma of the age of Kali (cf. CC Adi 3, 17), and all other means give way before it.

## 2. Balarama Dasa — "vaṛa avatāra bhāi vaṛa avatāra…" (PK 2207 = BR p. 956)
*The great incarnation: Gaura distributes the storehouse of prema to the fallen; women of noble families dance in the
sankirtana; the one whom all drove away as untouchable is now the one whose foot-dust the gods beg for; even yavanas
sing the holy name. Raga shri (BR — dhanashi).*[^10-5]

**2.1.** A great incarnation, brothers, a great incarnation!
To the fallen He has given away the storehouse of prema.

**2.2.** How wondrous are Gorachand's pastimes:
a king — and he carries a Vaishnava's palanquin on his shoulder![^10-6]

**2.3.** No likeness can be found for such an incarnation:
amid the sankirtana the wives of noble families dance.[^10-7]

**2.4.** The one whom everyone shunned, saying, "Do not touch!" —
from him the gods now beg the dust of his feet.

**2.5.** Even yavanas dance, sing and take the name of Hari —
yet in such an incarnation Balarama is left out.[^10-8]

[^10-5]: Signature: "Balarama." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 271 (printed p. 260), 4th shakha, 20th pallava, section "śrīgauracandra —
prakārāntara," no. 24 (label "॥২৪॥২২০৭॥"); raga shri; P-R-Sa MS no. 2315, P-R 9.15. BR, 12th wave (1913 ed., pp. 956–957, "punardhānaśī"):
the pada is sung within the account of Navadvipa. Majumdar cites it among the BR testimonies of Balarama Dasa (the detail of
the noble wives dancing in the sankirtana is new). The catalogue had assigned it to PK 2208, which is a pada of Ananta Dasa.
GPT2 — sec. 1.3, no. 36.
[^10-6]: Who this "king" is, the pada does not say: perhaps the Lord Himself, the King of all, who serves His devotees, or a king
(Prataparudra) humbly serving the Vaishnavas. BR: "a Vaishnava's bag (jholā)" instead of "palanquin (dolā)"; MS P-R: "bears"
(vahe) instead of "holds."
[^10-7]: MS P-R: "in sankirtana people dance, having abandoned all (other) dharmas." BR: "nāpi" (corrupt), "vom̐hāri."
[^10-8]: BR: "all people" (sava loka) instead of "sarvva loka." A yavana is a non-Hindu (a Muslim); cf. the conversion of Chand Kazi
(CB Madhya 23; CC Adi 17).

## 3. Nayanananda — "jaya re jaya re gorā śrīśacī-nandana…" (PK 2)
*Glory to Gora, the son of Shachi, dancing His auspicious dance: Srivasa, Ramananda, Mukunda and Vasu sing; the
mridanga and the mandiras resound; one anoints Gora with sandal paste, another puts on Him a malati garland; some call
Him Rama, others the Kandarpa dear to Radha, but the poet knows only this: He is Gadadhara's life. A mangalacharana —
the second pada of PK. Raga kamoda.*[^10-9]

**3.1.** Glory, glory to Gora, the son of Sri Shachi,
beautiful in His auspicious dance!
In the bliss of kirtana Srivasa and Ramananda,
Mukunda and Vasu sing His virtues.[^10-10]

**3.2.** "Dang drimiki drimi" — the madal sounds,
the mandiras ring sweetly,
conch, karatalas and bells resound,
blending with the rhythm of His feet.[^10-11]

**3.3.** One anoints Gora's body with fragrant sandal paste,
another puts on Him a malati garland;
pierced to the heart by the flower-arrow of love,
the companions are lost in bhava.[^10-12]

**3.4.** Some say Gora is the beloved of Janaki,
others — the Five-arrowed One dear to Radha;
Nayanananda's heart knows nothing else:
He is the life of my Gadadhara.[^10-13]

[^10-9]: Signature: "Nayanananda." PK: vol. 1, PDF p. 13 (printed p. 2), 1st shakha, 1st pallava (mangalacharana), no. 2 (label
"॥২॥"); raga kamoda; P-R-Sa MS no. 1, P-R 1.3 and 38.1 (raga "kamoda-mallara," P-R "mallara"). KGC — 30th kshanada (purnima),
no. 1, gaura-chandrika (kedara); GPT1 — p. 4, no. 4 (kedara or mangala); GPT2 — sec. 1.2, no. 4. The catalogue gave the PK
number as "45" (PK 45 is a pada of Radhamohana on Radha's purvaraga).
[^10-10]: MS P-R: "suṭhāna re," "guṇa-gāna re" (with the refrain particle "re"); KGC lacks "re." Srivasa is the master of the
house where the night kirtanas of Navadvipa were held; Ramananda here is probably Vasu Ramananda; Mukunda is the singer
Mukunda Datta; Vasu is Vasudeva (Vasu) Ghosha.
[^10-11]: The syllables imitate the madal (mridanga): MSS "ka," "kha," "gha," "ca": "dāṃ drimiki drimi drimi"; P-R-Sa: "tā drimi ki
drimi"; P-R 1.3: "drimiki drimiki drimi"; P-R 38.1: "dāṃ drimi drimi," "mandirā"; KGC: "drāṃ drimiki drimi." Mandiras are
small cymbals.
[^10-12]: In the PK scan the epithet of the sandal paste is partly illegible; "fragrant" (sugandhi) follows KGC and GPT1. MS P-R
38.1: "One anoints Gora's body with sandal paste, (one offers) fragrant karabira," "kora re" instead of "bhora re." MSS "kha,"
"gha," "ca," P-R, P-R-Sa: "the (female) companions" (sahacari). The flower-arrow is Kamadeva's weapon; here it is the hearts pierced
by love for the Lord.
[^10-13]: MSS "kha," "gha," P-R, P-R-Sa: "say" (vale); "ka": "says" (kahata), so also KGC. The beloved of Janaki (Sita) is Rama. The
Five-arrowed One is Kamadeva; "the Five-arrowed One dear to Radha" is Krishna as the transcendental Madana (aprakrita-madana,
CC Madhya 8), not the worldly god of desire. Gadadhara Pandita, according to the *Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika*, is a manifestation
of Radha; Nayanananda calls Gaura the life of his Gadadhara. MSS "ka," P-R-Sa: "āmāra"; P-R: "hāmāri."

## 4. Balarama Dasa — "bhāla raṅge nāce mora śacīra dulāla…" (BR p. 837)
*Gaura dances in the kirtana of Navadvipa: sandal paste all over His body, His garland swaying, pearls on His chest,
His ankle bells ringing; the kinnaras learn singing from Him, the gandharvas contemplate His dance; the lotuses shrink
before His eyes. Raga dhanashi.*[^10-14]

**4.1.** How beautifully my darling of Shachi dances!
Sandal paste over all His body, His garland swaying.

**4.2.** On His broad chest is a necklace of "elephant" pearls,
to the rhythm of His feet the ankle bells ring out.[^10-15]

**4.3.** How many bends of the body He knows, in measure and out of measure —
in all the city of Nadia there is no such artist![^10-16]

**4.4.** The kinnaras learn from hearing His soft singing,
the gandharvas, seeing His tandava, sink into meditation.[^10-17]

**4.5.** The lotus shrinks on seeing His eyes,
when He smiles, His teeth shed the radiance of lightning.

**4.6.** His lips are redder than the bandhuli flower — and that smile!
Gazing at this form, Balarama Dasa weeps.[^10-18]

[^10-14]: Signature: "Balarama Dasa." BR, 12th wave: 1913 ed. (Murshidabad), pp. 837–838 ("gīte yathā — dhānaśī"); 1960 ed., vv.
1884–1889. The pada is not in PK or GPT1. In Narahari Chakravarti it is sung in the account of the path by which the Lord went
with kirtana from Srivasa's house to the Ganga and back; Majumdar cites it among the three BR padas of Balarama Dasa.
[^10-15]: Gaja-mukta is the pearl believed to be born in an elephant's head — the finest pearl. 1913 ed.: "jhañcāra," 1960 ed.: "jhaṅkāra"
(ringing).
[^10-16]: Chhanda-bichhanda — dancing in measure and with departures from it (syncopations).
[^10-17]: The kinnaras and gandharvas are celestial singers and musicians. Tandava is the vigorous male dance.
[^10-18]: Bandhuli (vandhuka) is a bright red flower. "oṭakhāni" — "the lips" (oṭha, oṣṭha); 1913 ed.: "…oṭakhāni hāma" (corrupt), 1960 ed.:
"oṭakhāni hāsa."

## 5. Balarama Dasa — "hari hari maṅgala bharala khiti-maṇḍala…" (PK 2065)
*Gaura dances, spreading through the world the storehouse of rasa — the kirtana of His own virtues; His form robs
Manmatha of his senses; the Name that Shiva and Brahma seek in the depths of the heart He strings into a necklace and
gives to the fallen. Raga mangala.*[^10-19]

**5.1.** Hari, Hari! The circle of the earth is filled with blessing —
a shop of the treasures of rasa has opened:
the kirtana of His own virtues, the jewel of prema
He ceaselessly spreads abroad.

**5.2.** *(Refrain)* The skilful dancer, youthful Gaura, dances;
His heart is ceaselessly stirred by bhava,
there is no end to the joy of prema.

**5.3.** That body, shining like pure gold —
it is the Creator who fashioned it![^10-20]
Manmatha has fainted: in every limb there is such
beauty that, seeing it, he has lost his wits.

**5.4.** The Name that Shiva and the Four-faced One worship,
seeking it in the depths of the heart —
of such a Name He carefully strings a necklace
and gives it to the fallen.

**5.5.** Seeing the souls sunk in a dark well,
the Lord appeared in Navadvipa;
the treasure of prema He gave away, filling the world —
only Balarama Dasa is left out.

[^10-19]: Signature: "Balarama Dasa." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 217 (printed p. 206), 4th shakha, 17th pallava "śrīgaurāṅgera nṛtyādi līlā"
(Gauranga's dance and other pastimes), no. 7 (label "॥৭॥২০৬৫॥"); raga mangala; P-R-Sa MS no. 2174. GPT1 — p. 274, no. 86
(mangala); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 86. Majumdar does not discuss the pada; its attribution to one of the Balarama Dasas is not
established. MS "kha": "kara" instead of "karu" (5.4).
[^10-20]: "The Creator fashioned" is a poetic figure of wonder: the Lord's body is eternal and spiritual (sac-cid-ananda), not
created by Brahma.

## 6. Balarama Dasa — "nācata gaura sunāgara-maṇiyā…" (PK 2066)
*Gaura's dance: a golden body, reddish garments, tears like rain, a merciful glance that drowns the world in the ocean
of prema; He embraces the fallen, and at His leaps and roars the hearts of the godless tremble. The raga is not named
("the same raga" — mangala).*[^10-21]

**6.1.** *(Refrain)* Gaura dances, the jewel of refined youths;
His feet, which put the wagtails to shame, delight the eye,
His ankle bells ring with a sweet "ran-ran."[^10-22]

**6.2.** His body has a natural golden lustre —
whoever looks, the whole world is enchanted;
millions of Madanas faint at it;
His garments are like the rays of dawn.

**6.3.** His body sways, He cannot stand steady,
His two eyes pour like clouds unceasingly;
He drowns the world in the ocean of prema,
glancing mercifully from the corners of His eyes.

**6.4.** Absorbed in that rasa, He knows no limit,
He embraces the fallen and fills the world.
Balarama says: seeing His leaps and thunderous roars,
the hearts of the godless tremble.[^10-23]

[^10-21]: Signature: "Balarama." PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 217–218 (printed pp. 206–207), 17th pallava, no. 8 (label "॥৮॥২০৬৬॥"); P-R-Sa
MS no. 2175. GPT1 — p. 250, no. 7 ("yathārāga"); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 7. Its attribution to one of the Balarama Dasas is not
established.
[^10-22]: Sunagara-mani, "the jewel of refined youths," is an epithet of Krishna; the poet sees Krishna Himself in the dancing
Gaura. The wagtail (khañjana) is an image of nimble, light feet or eyes.
[^10-23]: P-R-Sa: "on the earth" (bhūtala) instead of "in the world" (bhuvana). "lakṣa" is a leap (cf. "lakṣe lakṣe" in BR). GPT1: "majāyai,"
"pāoi," "aruṇakiraṇa ambara vaniyā" (without "kiye").

## 7. Balarama Dasa — "govinda mādhava śrīnivāsa rāmānande…" (PK 2067 = BR p. 922)
*Kirtana in Navadvipa: Govinda, Madhava, Srinivasa (Srivasa), Ramananda, Murari and Mukunda sing; hearing of His
former (Vrindavana) pastimes the Lord falls senseless and rolls in the dust; seeing Gadadhara, He weeps; He calls out,
"Shripada!" — and Nityananda, understanding the secret of His heart, weeps too. Raga mallara-kamoda (BR — dhanashi).*[^10-24]

**7.1.** Govinda, Madhava, Srinivasa, Ramananda,
Murari and Mukunda sing together, as their own choir.[^10-25]

**7.2.** Hearing of His former virtues, maddened,
in the bliss of kirtana the Lord falls senseless.

**7.3.** What a wonder — words cannot tell it:
the Lord of Goloka rolls in the dust![^10-26]

**7.4.** His heart is overflowing with bhava — He sees Gadadhara
and weeps in longing, His eyes brimming with tears.

**7.5.** "Shripada!" the Lord calls, falls to the ground and weeps;
understanding the secret of His heart, Nityananda weeps.[^10-27]

**7.6.** Seeing this, people of all three kinds weep, drunk with Gora's rasa,
but of this joy Balarama Dasa has been deprived.

[^10-24]: Signature: "Balarama Dasa." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 218 (printed p. 207), 17th pallava, no. 9 (label "॥৯॥২০৬৭॥"); raga
mallara-kamoda; P-R-Sa MS no. 2176. BR, 12th wave (1913 ed., p. 922, "punardhānaśī"), right after Balarama's pada "…nā darave valarāma
pāṣāṇa-hṛdaya". GPT1 — p. 275, no. 87 (shri-mallara); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 87. Majumdar cites the pada as testimony of Balarama
Dasa: a kirtana with the Ghosha brothers, Srivasa, Vasu Ramananda, Murari and Mukunda.
[^10-25]: Govinda and Madhava are the Ghosha brothers, the singers of Navadvipa; Srinivasa is Srivasa Pandita; Ramananda is
Vasu Ramananda; Murari is Murari Gupta; Mukunda is Mukunda Datta. MS "ka," BR, GPT1: "mili" (together) instead of "meli."
[^10-26]: MSS "ka," "ca," P-R-Sa: "goloka-" (without the case ending); so also GPT1. In BR this couplet is followed by the refrain
mark (dhru).
[^10-27]: Shripada is the Lord's respectful way of addressing Nityananda. MSS "ka," "kha," "gha," "ca": "to the ground" (dharaṇī) instead
of "bhūme"; BR: "prabhu bhūme"; GPT1: "śrīpāda vali pahum̐ dharaṇī paṛi kām̐de." BR: "gadādhare dekhi" (7.4).

## 8. Nayanananda — "maṇḍalī raciyā sahacare…" (PK 2068)
*The companions have formed a circle, and in the middle Gora dances: with Him are Gadadhara and Nityananda; from house to
house He, Shyamasundara Himself, distributes love and devotion and with sankirtana offers everyone the treasure of
prema; men dance in the mood of women, women in the mood of men. The poet and his friends seek shelter at Gadadhara's
feet. Raga kedara.*[^10-28]

**8.1.** *(Refrain)* The companions have formed a circle,
in the middle is Gora, the best of dancers.

**8.2.** Vishvambhara dances, with Him Gadadhara,
Nityananda Raya dances;
recalling their former pastimes, they taste the joy of prema —
each grasps it according to his own nature.[^10-29]

**8.3.** From house to house — Shyamasundara Himself in person —
He gives away love and devotion;
He performs sankirtana and begs all to take the treasure of prema,
together with all His companions.[^10-30]

**8.4.** Men dance in the mood of women,
young women in the mood of men;
each having found his own bhava, his own nature,
people of every caste dance.[^10-31]

**8.5.** Nayanananda says: the bliss of Nadia —
the whole world is drunk with bliss.
We whose life is full of sorrow take shelter
at the feet of Madhava's son.[^10-32]

[^10-28]: Signature: "Nayanananda." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 218 (printed p. 207), 17th pallava, no. 10 (label "॥১০॥২০৬৮॥"); raga kedara;
P-R-Sa MS nos. 2177 and 2213. GPT1 — pp. 250–251, no. 8 (kedara); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 8. PK 2104 (vol. 3, PDF p. 231, no. 46) is
another recension of the same pada (after P-R-Sa no. 2213): "…nāce nityānanda bhāyā। pūrava-kautuka bhuñje prema-sukha sava sahacara laiyā,"
after which Raya refers back to PK 2068.
[^10-29]: "Former pastimes" are the pastimes of Vrindavana. P-R-Sa: "sabhāre" (to all) instead of "svabhāve" (by one's own nature); PK 2104
and GPT1 (in a note): "brother Nityananda" (bhāyā, bhāiyā).
[^10-30]: Shyamasundara, "the dark beauty," is Krishna: the poet sees in Gaura Krishna Himself going from house to house. P-R-Sa:
"merciful to all" (sabhāre sadaya haiyā) instead of "together with all His companions."
[^10-31]: In the ecstasy of kirtana the devotees forget the worldly distinction of sex: each dances in the bhava that has opened
within him. P-R-Sa: "dance" (nācata), "women" (prakṛti) instead of "young women" (yuvatī).
[^10-32]: "Madhava's son" is Gadadhara Pandita, the son of Madhava Mishra; Nayanananda is his nephew and disciple. MSS "ka," "kha,"
P-R-Sa: "duḥkhita"; "gha": "jīvajana" (souls). GPT1: "duḥkhita jīvana, mādhavanandana, caraṇe śaraṇa morā."

## 9. Nayanananda — "duhum̐ duhum̐ piriti ārati nāhi ṭuṭe…" (PK 2069 = BR p. 925)
*Gaura and Gadadhara dance, drunk with each other's love: Gauranga with Gadadhara's rasa, Gadadhara with Gauranga's
pastimes; they are like Sita and Rama, like Radha and Kanu; in Nadia reigns the joy of the kirtana of prema, and the
mistress of the house of prema is Pandita Gadadhara, while Shachi's son is the touchstone of prema. Raga pathamanjari
(BR — kamoda).*[^10-33]

**9.1.** Their love and longing for each other never break off,
at their touch so much supreme joy arises![^10-34]

**9.2.** My Gauranga dances, drunk with Gadadhara's rasa,
and Gadadhara dances, drunk with Gauranga's play.

**9.3.** Prakriti and purusha — are they not Janaki and Sri Rama?
Are they not Radha with Kanu, Rati with the god Kama?[^10-35]

**9.4.** The grace of their limbs surpasses countless Anangas —
how can I find a likeness for the limit of their greatness?

**9.5.** What to say of the moon beside His face — every day it is born and dies;
what is the lotus beside His hands and feet — it falls apart under the weight of frost![^10-36]

**9.6.** The joy of the kirtana of prema is in the city of Nadia;
the mistress of the house of prema is Pandita Gadadhara.[^10-37]

**9.7.** The touchstone of prema is Shachi's son:
He delivered the people of the world by giving them the treasure of prema.

**9.8.** Nayanananda tells of the play of these two:
hearing of it, the heart is captivated — what is there to reason about?[^10-38]

[^10-33]: Signature: "Nayanananda." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 219 (printed p. 208), 17th pallava, no. 11 (label "॥১১॥২০৬৯॥"); raga
pathamanjari; P-R-Sa MS nos. 2178 and 2460. BR, 12th wave (1913 ed., p. 925, "punaḥ kāmodaḥ"): Narahari Chakravarti cites the pada in
the account of Navadvipa as testimony ("ohe śrīnivāsa kichu kahila nā haya। suradhunītīre gorā raṅge vilasaya"). GPT1 — p. 251, no. 9
(pathamanjari); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 9. Majumdar counts the pada among the testimonies of the closeness of Gauranga and Gadadhara
(catalogue: NN-029 = NN-015). In the catalogue the padas NS-005, BD-018 and BD-022 had been wrongly linked to PK 2069. PK 2356 (24th pallava, vol. 3, PDF p. 324) repeats the same pada.
[^10-34]: MS "gha," GPT1: "the heart" (marama) instead of "supreme" (parama); BR: "paraśe parama sukha jāni kata uṭhe."
[^10-35]: Prakriti and purusha are the female and male principles: Gadadhara, the manifestation of Radha (the pleasure energy,
hladini-shakti), and Gaura, Krishna Himself. Rati and Kama (Kamadeva) are the deities of love; the poet's comparisons are
images of beauty and intimacy, not of worldly passion: according to Gaudiya teaching, Krishna is the transcendental Madana
(aprakrita-madana, CC Madhya 8). BR, GPT1: "Radha and Kanu at play (keli)"; BR: "purusha and prakriti."
[^10-36]: The moon wanes and waxes; the lotus withers in the winter frost — but the Lord's face, hands and feet are always
beautiful. MS "ka": "the moon-face" (mukha-cām̐da); "gha": "karapada"; BR: "What likeness is the moon? Every day it is born and dies;
the hands and feet — lotuses? (Lotuses) fall apart from the frost."
[^10-37]: "The mistress of the house of prema" (premera gṛhiṇī) is Gadadhara as the manifestation of Radha. BR: "prema-saṅkīrtana-sukha."
[^10-38]: MSS "kha," "gha," P-R-Sa: "vehāra" (the same). BR: "kahaye nayanānanda ānanda vihāra" ("…the play of bliss"). MS "ka," P-R-Sa:
"prema-parama-maṇi" instead of "prema-paraśa-maṇi" (9.7); BR: "uddhārilā jagajane."

## 10. Nayanananda — "kīrttana mājhe kīrttana-naṭa-rāja…" (PK 2070)
*Amid the kirtana is the king of the kirtana dancers: a garland on His neck with bees humming over it, a moon of sandal
paste on His forehead; this dancing Vishvambhara is Krishna Himself: within Krishna, without the form of Radha,
incomparable gold; He takes on His lap Gadadhara, the Lakshmi of prema. Raga bhatiyari.*[^10-39]

**10.1.** Amid the kirtana is the king of the kirtana dancers,
for the play of kirtana — all the finery of an elegant youth.[^10-40]

**10.2.** On His neck sways a garland, the bees sing over it,
on His forehead is a moon of sandal paste, His brows are flower-arrows.

**10.3.** *(Refrain)* Look, brothers, what a wonder:
this dancing Vishvambhara is Krishna in His own form!

**10.4.** Within — "Krishna, Krishna," the hidden supreme rasa,
without — the form of Radha, incomparable gold.[^10-41]

**10.5.** The joy of prakriti and purusha — rasa with rasa — has become one:
see with your own eyes — here is the incarnation of prema!

**10.6.** Gadadhara, the Lakshmi of prema, He took on His lap;
in the bliss of prema is Nityananda, His own brother, dear as life.[^10-42]

**10.7.** Nayanananda tells of the hidden secret of prema:
He is like a doll of nectar, a form made of nectar.[^10-43]

[^10-39]: Signature: "Nayanananda." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 219 (printed p. 208), 17th pallava, no. 12 (label "॥১২॥২০৭০॥"); raga
bhatiyari; P-R-Sa MS no. 2179. GPT1 — p. 260, no. 41 (bhatiyari); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 41. The linking of pada NS-021 (Narahari) to
PK 2070 is mistaken.
[^10-40]: "Nāgarāli-sāj" — the attire of a nagara, an elegant youth: an epithet of Krishna the dancer, not the language of
nagari-bhava. MSS "ka," "kha": "sways" (dolaye) instead of "dolāra" (10.2).
[^10-41]: Cf. the teaching of Krishnadasa Kaviraja (CC Adi 1.5–6; Adi 4): Sri Chaitanya is Krishna who has accepted the bhava and
the lustre of Radha. MSS "ka," "kha," "gha," "ca": "antara" (within); "ka," "kha," "gha," "ca": "paraśa" instead of "parama"; "gha": "kanā" (a
particle) instead of "koṇā" ("a corner," i.e. something hidden — the reading is unclear).
[^10-42]: The Lakshmi of prema (prema-lakhiminī) is Gadadhara, the manifestation of Radha.
[^10-43]: MS "ka": "nigurṇa," "ca": "niguna," P-R-Sa: "niguni," GPT1: "niguṇa" — slips for "nigūṛha" (hidden); the subject is the secret of
prema, not "qualitylessness" (nirguna) — the Lord has spiritual qualities.

## 11. Nayanananda — "sajanī aparūpa dekha siyā…" (PK 2071)
*Gaura dances in Krishna's mood: He stands still in the tribhanga pose, looks for the flute, ties His hair into a topknot
like Krishna, calls "Krishna, Krishna!", strikes His chest and says, "I am that very Lord"; the Ganga seems to Him the
Yamuna, Navadvipa — Gokula and Mathura. Raga dhanashi.*[^10-44]

**11.1.** *(Refrain)* Friend, come and see what a wonder:
Gaurangachand dances, chanting "Hari-bol"!

**11.2.** The fragrant choicest sandal paste, the scented karabira garland
sway in waves on Gora's body.
What was hidden from sight before — see, here it is before your eyes, what a gain!
He is that very One — this charming Gora.[^10-45]

**11.3.** He stands still, bent in three places, looks for the sweet flute,
ties a topknot of His curly hair;
He calls, "Krishna, Krishna!" — slaps His chest like a wrestler,
and suddenly says, "I am that very Lord!"[^10-46]

**11.4.** The Jahnavi He takes for the Yamuna, the trees on her bank for Vrindavana,
Navadvipa for Gokula and Mathura.
Nayanananda says: the same friends and girlfriends —
and the dark body has now become Gora.[^10-47]

[^10-44]: Signature: "Nayanananda." PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 219–220 (printed pp. 208–209), 17th pallava, no. 13 (label "॥১৩॥২০৭১॥");
raga dhanashi; P-R-Sa MS no. 2180. GPT1 — p. 251, no. 10 (dhanashi); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 10. The address "friend" (sajanī) is a
usual opening of a pada; the speaker is not named. PK 2123 (18th pallava, vol. 3, PDF p. 238; P-R-Sa MS no. 2230) is another recension
of the same pada: "rādhā rādhā vali ḍāke… vale muñi sabhāra ṭhākura" ("He calls, 'Radha, Radha!'… says, 'I am the Lord of all'"), closing
"varaṇakhāni kāra bhāve gorā" ("by whose bhava has the form become golden").
[^10-45]: "Hidden before" — the pastimes of Vraja, formerly beyond sight, are now revealed before the eyes in Gaura.
[^10-46]: Tribhanga is Krishna's pose with the flute; chura is Krishna's topknot. "Mālasāṭ" is a slap of the palm on the arm or
chest, as wrestlers do. In Krishna's mood the Lord speaks of Himself as Krishna — cf. CB Madhya 8–9 (the mahaprakasha).
[^10-47]: The Jahnavi is the Ganga. Gaura's companions are the same as Krishna's companions in Vraja (*Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika*);
"the dark body" is Krishna who has become golden Gaura. MSS "gha," "ca," GPT1: "the trees on the bank" (tīre taru); "ka," "ca,"
GPT1: "in Navadvipa" (navadvīpe).

## 12. Nayanananda — "nāce śacīra nandana dulāliyā…" (PK 2073)
*Shachi's darling son dances — the ocean of all rasas, Gadadhara's dearest friend: a tilaka of musk, a topknot, a face
like a golden moon, a smile that captivates the young women of the town; on His neck a forest garland, on Him yellow
garments. Raga bhatiyari.*[^10-48]

**12.1.** *(Refrain)* Shachi's darling son dances,
the ocean of all rasas, the friend dearer than life to Gadadhara,
ever merry in His play.

**12.2.** Amid a tilaka of musk is a charming topknot,
wondrously framed by curls;
His face is a golden moon, His sweet nectarean smile
captivates the hearts of the young women of the town.[^10-49]

**12.3.** On Gora's neck is a forest garland — a wondrous play —
golden rings and bracelets on His arms;
He wears a pair of yellow garments — the thief of all hearts;
Nayanananda is at His lotus feet.[^10-50]

[^10-48]: Signature: "Nayanananda." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 220 (printed p. 209), 17th pallava, no. 15 (label "॥১৫॥২০৭৩॥"); raga bhatiyari;
P-R-Sa MS no. 2182. GPT1 — p. 153, no. 125 (bhatiyari); GPT2 — sec. 3.1, no. 125. The preceding pada PK 2072 is Uddhava Dasa's
("uddhava dāsa tāra kīṭa").
[^10-49]: The words about young women are the language of nagari-bhava (Gaura as the nagara, the beloved of the town's
women); we translate faithfully to the author. Vrindavana Dasa stresses that in this incarnation the Lord never glanced at
another man's wife; worship of Gaura in the spirit of "Gaura-nagari" is not accepted by the Gaudiya tradition (Vrindavana
Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta). GPT1: "alakā valita vaṛa śobhā" ("…great beauty").
[^10-50]: The forest garland (vanamala) and yellow garments (pitambara) are Krishna's attire. GPT1: "piṅgala" (yellowish) garments;
"maje nayanānanda-padāmbuje" — "…Nayanananda is immersed in (His) lotus feet."

## 13. Nayanananda — "mukhakhāni pūrṇimāra śaśī…" (PK 2102)
*Gora dances, binding the hearts of all souls with prema: His face is the full moon, His lips move all the time as if
chanting a mantra; the moon weeps on seeing the beauty of His face, the sun on seeing the clouds of His eyes; streams of
prema run down His chest. The poet asks: shall I see Gora beside Gadadhara again? Raga dhanashi.*[^10-51]

**13.1.** His face is a full moon: what mantra is He chanting?
Why do His lips, which mock the bimba fruit, always tremble?[^10-52]

**13.2.** *(Refrain)* Gora dances, merry in the dance,
the hearts of all souls He binds with prema.

**13.3.** The moon weeps seeing the beauty of His face,
the sun weeps seeing the clouds of His eyes.[^10-53]

**13.4.** Gora is brighter than fresh, unwrought gold,
streams of the rasa of prema run down His chest.[^10-54]

**13.5.** Nayanananda says in the joy of his heart:
shall I see Gora beside Gadadhara again?[^10-55]

[^10-51]: Signature: "Nayanananda." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 231 (printed p. 220), 17th pallava, no. 44 (label "॥৪৪॥২১০২॥"); raga dhanashi;
P-R-Sa MS no. 2211. GPT1 — p. 154, no. 126 (dhanashri); GPT2 — sec. 3.1, no. 126.
[^10-52]: The bimba is a bright red fruit, the usual comparison for lips. The Lord's lips move — He is ceaselessly chanting the
holy name. MSS "ka," "kha," "gha," "ca," GPT1: "vimba viṛambita adhara."
[^10-53]: The clouds of His eyes are His eyes full of tears. MS "gha": "chāna" instead of "chānda" (beauty, shape), "haiyā" instead of
"heriyā."
[^10-54]: "navāñcala" is unclear; GPT1: "Gora of new rasa" (nava rasera gorā). MSS "ka," "kha," "ca," GPT1: "of touch" (paraśera) instead of "of
rasa" (rasera); "gha": "rasera."
[^10-55]: The poet's question betrays longing: it seems he can no longer see Gaura beside Gadadhara in Navadvipa.

## 14. Nayanananda — "kinā se sukhera sarovare…" (PK 2103)
*Vishvambhara's dance is a lake of joy from which the waves of prema splash over the brim: the earth cannot hold His
feet, His face is a golden moon pouring nectar; His companions are royal swans, bees and chakoras; the treasure of
bhakti has come without effort to all the poor and wretched — Vrindavana has become the town of Nadia. The raga is not
named ("the same raga" — dhanashi).*[^10-56]

**14.1.** What a lake of joy!
The waves of prema surge and splash over the brim.

**14.2.** The Lord Vishvambhara dances;
drunk with prema He steps — and the earth cannot hold His feet.[^10-57]

**14.3.** His face is shaped like a golden moon:
how much nectar it pours — there is no holding it!

**14.4.** His companions are royal swans;
some have become bees, others chakora birds.[^10-58]

**14.5.** Ever new waves of dance —
the Lakshmi of prema dances, the very town of Nadia.[^10-59]

**14.6.** Ever new jewels of bhakti
all the poor and wretched have gained without effort.

**14.7.** Nayanananda tells the essence of joy:
that very Vrindavana has become the town of Nadia.

[^10-56]: Signature: "Nayanananda." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 231 (printed p. 220), 17th pallava, no. 45 (label "॥৪৫॥২১০৩॥"); P-R-Sa MS no.
2212. GPT1 — p. 31, no. 16 (dhanashi); GPT2 gives the pada twice (sec. 1.3, no. 16; sec. 4.2, no. 31).
[^10-57]: MS "gha": "from the weight (of prema)" (bhare) instead of "steps" (dhare). GPT1: "premabhare pada dhare dharaṇī nā dhare."
[^10-58]: The bees cling to the Lord's lotus feet, the chakoras (birds that drink moonlight) to the moon of His face.
[^10-59]: MS "ka": "lachimā." GPT1: "prema lachimā nāce nadīyā-nāgarī" — "…the town-woman of Nadia dances." The PK reading "nadiyā-nagarī" (the
town of Nadia) is adopted.

## 15. Nayanananda — "dekha dekha gorā-naṭa raṅga…" (PK 2106)
*An auspicious kirtana — a circle of the great rasa where the former, Vrindavana days come alive: Nityananda, Advaita,
Srivasa, Mukunda, Murari, Ramananda and Vakreshvara dance; Gora dances with Gadadhara, the mridanga resounds. In the
Lord of Navadvipa are all the incarnations: each sees his own bhava before his eyes. Raga mangala.*[^10-60]

**15.1.** *(Refrain)* Look, look at the dance of Gora the dancer!
An auspicious kirtana — the circle of the great rasa,
in it the former days have come alive.[^10-61]

**15.2.** The Lord Nityananda dances, Thakura Advaitachandra,
Srinivasa, Mukunda, Murari,
Ramananda, Vakreshvara and all the other companions —
an ocean of prema, waves of bliss.

**15.3.** Thakura Pandita sings, Govinda plays in bliss,
Gora dances together with Gadadhara;
"drimiki drimiki thaiyā, tā thaiyā, tā thaiyā thaiyā" —
the enchanting mridanga sounds.[^10-62]

**15.4.** All the incarnations, full of joy, the essence of joy,
are in this Lord of Navadvipa of mine:
whatever bhava one has — see it all before your eyes.
May this abide in Nayanananda's heart![^10-63]

[^10-60]: Signature: "Nayanananda." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 232 (printed p. 221), 17th pallava, no. 48 (label "॥৪৮॥২১০৬॥"); raga mangala;
P-R-Sa MS no. 2215. GPT1 — p. 258, no. 33 (mangala); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 33. The preceding pada PK 2105
("gorā nāce nava nava raṅgiyā") is unsigned in PK, and in MS P-R it has additional stanzas with Lochana's signature; it does not belong
to Nayanananda. The linking of pada NS-016 ("jhulata rasamaya gaurakiśora") to PK 2106 is mistaken.
[^10-61]: The maha-rasa is Krishna's circle dance with the gopis; Gaura's kirtana is like it. "The former days" are the pastimes of
Vrindavana.
[^10-62]: Who is called "Thakura Pandita" is unclear (perhaps Srivasa Pandita). Govinda is probably Govinda Ghosha or a
mridanga player among the companions. MS "gha": "vājāyata" (plays). The syllables imitate the mridanga.
[^10-63]: Gaura is the source of all incarnations (cf. CC Adi 2: Krishna is the avatari, the source of the avatars): each devotee sees
in Him the One he worships. GPT1: "…nayanānandera rahu cite."

## 16. Nayanananda — "nācaye gaurāṅga gadādhara-mukha cāñā…" (PK 2179)
*Gauranga dances gazing at Gadadhara's face: looking at each other, both are lost, they embrace, tremble and shed tears —
body, mind and speech are one in them, one life; the town women of Nadia watch from afar and grasp the secret in their
hearts. Raga varadi.*[^10-64]

**16.1.** Gauranga dances, gazing at Gadadhara's face;
within, the rasa of touch has risen and flooded His heart.

**16.2.** Looking into each other's faces, both are lost:
each has become for the other an ocean of rasa — and a chakora drinking nectar.[^10-65]

**16.3.** Chest to chest, the two have embraced,
they tremble, their hair stands on end, both are flooded with tears.[^10-66]

**16.4.** Body, mind and speech in both are one life;
every limb of theirs is made of the nectar of love.

**16.5.** Gora, the king of dancers, is adorned by the Pandita;
from afar all the town women are watching.[^10-67]

**16.6.** The town women of Nadia have grasped in their hearts
the One by whose grace I obtain the jewel of prema.

**16.7.** Subdued by Gadadhara's love is the rasa-drunk Gaura —
so says Nayanananda, floating in this rasa.

[^10-64]: Signature: "Nayanananda." PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 260–261 (printed pp. 249–250), 4th shakha, 19th pallava "śrīgaurāṅgera rūpa —
nāgarī ukti" (Gauranga's form — the words of the town women), no. 12 (label "॥১২॥২১৭৯॥"); raga varadi; P-R-Sa MS no. 2287. GPT1 —
p. 259, no. 35 (varadi); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 35.
[^10-65]: The chakora is a bird believed to drink moonlight: each of the two is both the moon and the one who drinks its nectar.
[^10-66]: The embrace of Gaura and Gadadhara is an expression of prema: Gadadhara is the manifestation of Radha, and their love
sings of the spiritual prema of Radha and Krishna, not of a worldly feeling. MSS "ka," "kha": "duhum̐"; "gha": "dohe" (16.3, 16.4).
[^10-67]: Raya placed the pada in the section of the nagaris' (town women's) words; here the town women only watch from afar
and grasp the secret of the love of Gaura and Gadadhara. The words about young women are the language of nagari-bhava
(Gaura as the nagara, the beloved of the town's women); we translate faithfully to the author. Vrindavana Dasa stresses that
in this incarnation the Lord never glanced at another man's wife; worship of Gaura in the spirit of "Gaura-nagari" is not
accepted by the Gaudiya tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta). MSS "ka," "kha," P-R-Sa: without
"all" (sava).

## 17. Nayanananda — "o rūpa sundara gaura kiśora…" (PK 2115)
*The beauty of youthful Gaura, at which one cannot gaze enough: He is prema itself made visible, a golden mountain strewn
with flowers; thirsting for the prema of her who is full of rasa, He is beyond the meditation of Shiva, Shuka and Ananta;
the poet is a bee at His lotus feet. Raga suhai.*[^10-68]

**17.1.** How beautiful is the form of youthful Gaura —
however much I gaze, there is no end to the longing to gaze.

**17.2.** Beautiful are His hands and feet, red are His lips;
for the new girl in love — a new love.[^10-69]

**17.3.** His eyes are restless, restlessly His tears flow;
to the heart of her who is full of rasa He has tied Himself with the cord of prema.

**17.4.** Is this prema itself made visible — or King Manmatha?
A golden mountain — or a gathering of flowers?[^10-70]

**17.5.** Thirsting for her prema is Sri Gauranga Raya —
He whom Shiva, Shuka and Ananta do not reach in meditation.[^10-71]

**17.6.** His whole body is ringed with layers of thrilling hair;
in the embrace of her who is full of prema — wave upon wave.

**17.7.** His lotus feet are a flowering mango for the bee:
so says Nayanananda — in them is his heart's delight.[^10-72]

[^10-68]: Signature: "Nayanananda." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 236 (printed p. 225), 4th shakha, 18th pallava "śrīgaurāṅgera rūpa prabhṛti"
(Gauranga's form, etc.), no. 7 (label "॥৭॥২১১৫॥"); raga suhai; P-R-Sa MS no. 2223. GPT1 — twice: p. 136, no. 74 and p. 278, no. 2
(suhai); GPT2 — sec. 3.1, no. 74 and sec. 4.3, no. 2. In GPT1 (p. 136) it is preceded (no. 73) by a pada signed by Narahari, "suradhunītīre gaura
naṭanāgara" (wrongly ascribed to Nayanananda in the catalogue — NN-006).
[^10-69]: "The new girl in love" (nava-anurāgiṇī), "her who is full of rasa" (rasavatī), "her who is full of prema" (premavatī) are
Radha; behind this in the pada stands also Gadadhara, Her manifestation. Gaura is Krishna who longs to taste Radha's prema
and has accepted Her bhava (CC Adi 1.6; Adi 4); this is spiritual prema, not worldly passion.
[^10-70]: Manmatha (Kamadeva) is the god of love; the Lord is the transcendental Madana who surpasses him (CC Madhya 8).
[^10-71]: "Thirsting" (lampaṭa) — of the Lord thirsting for the prema of His devotee. MS P-R-Sa: "achu," "Ananta and others" (anantādi),
"nā" instead of "nāhi."
[^10-72]: Sahakara is the flowering mango tree, beloved of bees. MS P-R-Sa: "valaithe"; "kha," "ca," P-R-Sa: "lahali" (17.6); "ka": "kahala,"
"gha": "kahaye." GPT1: "…kayala nayanānanda citavihāra" — "Nayanananda has made (them) the pleasure-ground of his heart."

## 18. Nayanananda — "āota piriti muratimaya sāgara…" (PK 2116)
*The pastimes in Nadia: the Lord is an ocean of love in person; in Him is all the wealth of Vaikuntha and Vrindavana;
blessed has become the Ganga in which He bathes; in every house and temple, under every grove and in every flowering
garden are His pastimes; Vishvambhara has fulfilled the hopes of all. Raga bala-dhanashi.*[^10-73]

**18.1.** He comes — an ocean, love itself embodied,
the wondrous Lord, the king of the twice-born;
ever new devotees, new devotion, new treasures —
glorious is the circle of dancers.[^10-74]

**18.2.** *(Refrain)* Splendid, splendid are the pastimes in Nadia!
All the wealth of Vaikuntha and Vrindavana,
the essence of the joy of all joys.

**18.3.** Blessed, blessed, thrice blessed now has the Suradhuni become:
in bliss she flows with streams of rasa;
bathing, drinking, immersion, embrace —
how many, many times she meets Him![^10-75]

**18.4.** In every house, in every temple, under every grove,
in every flowering garden are His pastimes.
Nayanananda says: Vishvambhara with prema
has fulfilled the hopes of all.

[^10-73]: Signature: "Nayanananda." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 236 (printed p. 225), 18th pallava, no. 8 (label "॥৮॥২১১৬॥"); raga
bala-dhanashi; P-R-Sa MS no. 2224. GPT1 — p. 32, no. 17 (bala-dhanashi); GPT2 — sec. 1.3, no. 17.
[^10-74]: "The king of the twice-born" is both the moon and the best of brahmanas. The end of the stanza is unclear ("su- / vācata");
GPT1: "nava nava bhakata, nava rasa yāvata, nava tanu ratana samāja" — "ever new devotees, all new rasa, a gathering of new
precious bodies."
[^10-75]: The Suradhuni is the Ganga. The river is blessed because the Lord bathes in her, drinks her water and immerses Himself
in her: her "embrace" and "meeting" with Him are an image of the Ganga's happiness at touching the Lord. GPT1: "…āliṅgana saṅgama,
kata kata vāra."

## 19. Nayanananda — "gadādhara-mukha heri kivā uṭhe mane…" (PK 2114)
*The Lord's bhava: gazing at Gadadhara's face, He remembers the joys of the groves of Vrindavana, pines like a poor man
who has lost a touchstone, weeps, "Hari, Hari!", sways and falls to the ground. The poet asks: from whose love comes such
turmoil? Raga pathamanjari.*[^10-76]

**19.1.** Gazing at Gadadhara's face — what rises in His heart?
He remembers all those joys in the groves of Vrindavana.

**19.2.** Hearing of those virtues, His heart pines ceaselessly —
like a poor man who has lost a touchstone.

**19.3.** "Hari, Hari!" says the Lord, weeping and weeping;
who can tell whose bhava has arisen in His heart?

**19.4.** His golden form sways unsteadily;
reeling and reeling, He falls and rolls on the ground.

**19.5.** Nayanananda says before Gadadhara:
from whose love comes such turmoil?[^10-77]

[^10-76]: Signature: "Nayanananda." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 235 (printed p. 224), 18th pallava, no. 6 (label "॥৬॥২১১৪॥"); raga pathamanjari.
GPT1 — p. 278, no. 1 (pathamanjari; section "bhavavesha and pralapa"). A pada on Radha's bhava in the Lord: Gadadhara awakens
in Him the memory of Vrindavana.
[^10-77]: The answer is implied: it is the love (anuraga) of Radha, whose bhava the Lord has accepted; Gadadhara is Her
manifestation.

## 20. Balarama Dasa — "gaura manohara nāgara-śekhara…" (PK 2113)
*Gaura's form and bhava: at the sight of Him countless Kamas faint, the autumn moon weeps gazing at His face; He
ceaselessly chants His own name, and on looking at Gadadhara's face He cries, "Rai, Rai!" and falls to the ground,
seized by the fever of separation; weeping, He takes the fallen by the hand. Raga todi.*[^10-78]

**20.1.** Gaura, the enchanting crown of elegant youths:
seeing Him, countless Flower-arrowed Ones faint.[^10-79]

**20.2.** His body shines brighter than gold —
gazing at His face, the autumn moon weeps.

**20.3.** His gait is slower than a drunken elephant's;
from the nectar of His lips flows a sweet smile.[^10-80]

**20.4.** Ceaselessly He chants the mantra of His own name,
His body is helpless in bhava, His heart overflowing.[^10-81]

**20.5.** Looking at Gadadhara's face, He is in great anguish:
"Rai, Rai!" He cries and falls to the ground.[^10-82]

**20.6.** The clouds of His eyes pour in torrents,
His heart is filled with the sharp, cruel fever of separation.

**20.7.** Overflowing with rasa, He does not know His own from others:
weeping, He takes by the hand the fallen and the lowest.[^10-83]

**20.8.** Gods and asuras have plunged into this ocean of rasa —
not a drop has touched Balarama Dasa.[^10-84]

no. 2221, P-R 14.76. GPT1 — p. 141 (todi; without the couplet 20.6b–20.7a); GPT2 — sec. 3.1. The pada was not in the catalogue
(new row BD-042); its attribution to one of the Balarama Dasas is not established.
[^10-79]: "Nāgara-śekhara," "the crown of elegant youths," is an epithet of Krishna. The Flower-arrowed One (kusuma-śara) is
Kamadeva.
[^10-80]: MS "gha": "ruciratara"; "ka," "kha," "ca," P-R-Sa: "racita" (20.2). MSS "ka," "kha," "gha," "ca," P-R-Sa, GPT1: "drunken" (matta)
instead of "mada"; "ka," "kha," "gha," "ca," P-R-Sa: "rasa" instead of "sudhārasa."
[^10-81]: Gaura chants the names of Krishna — His own name. MSS P-R-Sa, P-R: "antara" instead of "mantara"; "ka," "ca," P-R-Sa, P-R: "bharama,"
"kha": "marama" instead of "antara" (at the end of the line).
[^10-82]: Rai is Radha: in Krishna's mood the Lord, seeing Gadadhara, calls Radha and pines in separation from Her. The PK scan has
"rāha rāi" (a misprint); GPT1: "rāi rāi."
[^10-83]: MS "gha," P-R: "jarajara" instead of "garagara."
[^10-84]: MS P-R: "of joy" (sukha) instead of "of rasa," "people" (narinara) instead of "gods and asuras."

## 21. Nayanananda — "kāndaye mahāprabhu gadādhara saṅge…" (PK 2181)
*Mahaprabhu weeps together with Gadadhara at the very first mention of their former love; remembering the joys of the
groves, both are filled with prema, they come to greet each other with sandal paste, garlands, tulasi and durva grass,
embrace and float in rasa; the three worlds are maddened by their ecstasy. Raga varadi.*[^10-85]

**21.1.** Mahaprabhu weeps together with Gadadhara —
at the very first mention of their former love.

**21.2.** Remembering all those joys in the forest groves,
both were filled at heart with the bhava of prema.

**21.3.** With fragrant sandal paste, garlands, tulasi and durva
the two came together to greet each other.[^10-86]

**21.4.** Smiling, touching again and again, they embrace;
both float in rasa, finding no shore.[^10-87]

**21.5.** One cannot tell who is man, who woman, who devotee;
by the ecstasy of the two the three worlds are maddened.

**21.6.** Nayanananda tells of the hidden secret:
He is like a doll of nectar, a form made of nectar.[^10-88]

[^10-85]: Signature: "Nayanananda." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 261 (printed p. 250), 19th pallava (section of the nagaris' words), no. 14
(label "॥১৪॥২১৮১॥"); raga varadi ("tathā rāga"); P-R-Sa MS no. 2289. GPT1 — p. 282, no. 17 (section "bhavavesha and pralapa"); GPT2 —
sec. 4.3, no. 17.
[^10-86]: Tulasi and durva grass are articles of worship: Gaura and Gadadhara greet each other like worshippers. MS "ka": "duhum̐"
instead of "dohām̐"; "kha," "gha" lack the word.
[^10-87]: The embrace is an expression of the prema of Radha and Krishna revealed in Gaura and Gadadhara (cf. no. 16), not of a
worldly feeling. MS "ka": "vujhinu," "ca," GPT1: "vujhilum̐" ("…I did not grasp the limit").
[^10-88]: The couplet repeats the close of PK 2070 (no. 10.7).

## 22. Nayanananda — "madhu-ṛtu-yāmini suradhuni-tīra…" (PK 1495)
*A spring night on the bank of the Ganga: the moon shines, the Malaya breeze blows; Gaura, the king of dancers, dances
in kirtana with His companions, with Him Narahari and Gadadhara, khol and karatalas resound, the cuckoos and bees sing.
The gaura-chandrika to PK's section on the spring rasa. Raga suhai.*[^10-89]

**22.1.** A spring night, the bank of the Suradhuni,
the moon shines, the Malaya breeze blows.[^10-90]

**22.2.** With His companions Gaura, the king of dancers,
plays amid the incomparable kirtana.

**22.3.** The sounds of khol and karatalas, waves of dance,
arms raised, again and again they call, "Hari, Hari!"

**22.4.** Narahari and Gadadhara play together with Him,
they dance and sing, bending in every way.

**22.5.** The cuckoos and bees sing on the fifth note —
Nayanananda's Lord is at play.[^10-91]

[^10-89]: Signature: "Nayanananda" ("nayanānanda-pahu," "Nayanananda's Lord"). PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 432 (printed p. 419), 3rd shakha, 27th pallava,
section "atha vāsantī rāsalīlā । taducita-śrīgauracandra" (gaura-chandrika to the spring rasa), no. 71 (label "॥৭১॥১৪৯৫॥"), right after Vasu
Ghosha's PK 1494 (chapter 9, no. 1); raga suhai; P-R-Sa MS no. 2045. Not found by OCR in GPT1; GPT (GPT1 p. 336, no. 48) has a
different pada of Raya Shekhara with the same lines "sahacara saṅge gaura naṭarāja। viharaye nirupama kīrtana mājha" (in the catalogue NS-018,
wrongly linked there to PK 1495). The pada was not in the catalogue (new row NN-030).
[^10-90]: The Suradhuni is the Ganga. The Malaya breeze is the warm southern wind of spring, said by poets to blow from the Malaya
hills.
[^10-91]: Panchama is the fifth note of the scale; the cuckoo sings on the panchama — a sign of spring.

## 23. Nayanananda — "ko kahum̐ ājuka ānanda-ora…" (PK 1449)
*The spring swing festival: in a flowering garden young Gaura swings, with Him Nityananda and Gadadhara, the Lord of
Shantipura sings, the companions shower Gora with red powder; all the people of Nadia come running. The gaura-chandrika
to PK's section on the spring swing and holi. Raga vasanta.*[^10-92]

**23.1.** Who can tell how boundless today's joy is!
In a flowering garden young Gaura swings.

**23.2.** With Him are Nityananda and Gadadhara,
the Lord of Shantipura sings merrily.[^10-93]

**23.3.** The companions shower Gora with phagu;
hearing of it, all the people of Nadia come running.[^10-94]

**23.4.** The sounds of khol and karatalas, "Hari, Hari!" —
Nayanananda is lost in bliss.

[^10-92]: Signature: "Nayanananda." PK: vol. 2, PDF pp. 406–407 (printed pp. 393–394), 3rd shakha, section "atha vāsantī dolā hori-vilāsa ।
tatra śrīgauracandra" (the spring swing and holi; gaura-chandrika), no. 25 (label "॥২৫॥১৪৪৯॥"); raga vasanta; P-R-Sa MS no. 2002.
GPT1 — p. 343, no. 70 (vasanta); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 70. The Dola-yatra is the spring swing festival on the full moon of Phalguna
(the day of the Lord's appearance).
[^10-93]: The Lord of Shantipura is Advaita Acharya. P-R-Sa: "Gadadhara and others" (gadādhara ādi).
[^10-94]: Phagu (phag) is the red powder people throw at each other at the spring festivals. MS "ka": "smear" (lepai), P-R-Sa: "phelaye";
GPT1: "phāgu lepata." GPT1 in 23.4: "nayanānanda dīna ānande vibhola" ("poor Nayanananda…").

## 24. Nayanananda — "ācāryya-mandire bhikṣā kariyā caitanya…" (PK 2234)
*Shantipura after the sannyasa: Chaitanya takes His meal in Advaita's house and dances in the sankirtana in the
reddish robes of a sannyasi; Mukunda and Madhavananda sing; Advaita dances clapping His hands: "After so many days Gora is
in my house!" The poet, standing behind Gadadhara, sighs: what was, what has become, what is yet to be. Raga suhai.*[^10-95]

**24.1.** Having accepted alms in the Acharya's house, Chaitanya
has blessed the fallen, the sinful and the wretched.

**24.2.** His body anointed with sandal paste, His garments reddish —
amid the sankirtana dances Advaita's life.[^10-96]

**24.3.** Mukunda and Madhavananda sing at the top of their voices,
Nitai and Chaitanya dance in Advaita's house.[^10-97]

**24.4.** Acharya Gosani dances, clapping His hands:
"After so many days — Gora-Vanamali in my house!"[^10-98]

**24.5.** Nayanananda says, standing behind Gadadhara:
what was, what has become, and what is yet to be![^10-99]

[^10-95]: Signature: "Nayanananda." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 280 (printed p. 269), 4th shakha, 21st pallava "śrīgaurāṅgera sannyāsa ityādi"
(Gauranga's sannyasa, etc.), no. 17 (label "॥১৭॥২২৩৪॥"); raga suhai; P-R-Sa MS no. 2339. GPT1 — p. 381, no. 48 (suhai); GPT2 — sec.
5.3, no. 48. In the catalogue the one pada is entered twice: NN-021 (the first line, wrongly with no. 2235) and NN-027 (the
second line). PK 2235 ("dhara dhara dhara dhara re nitāi") is a pada signed "Murari," not Nayanananda's. Cf. CC Madhya 3; CB Antya 1.
[^10-96]: Reddish (saffron) robes are a sannyasi's garments. "Advaita's life" is Chaitanya.
[^10-97]: Mukunda is Mukunda Datta; Madhavananda is probably Madhava Ghosha. MS "gha": "advaitera ghare."
[^10-98]: Vanamali, "wearer of the forest garland," is a name of Krishna. MSS "ka," "kha," P-R-Sa: "cira dina."
[^10-99]: "Behind Gadadhara" — as his companion and disciple: the poet places himself among the witnesses. The sigh is for Nimai's
former life in Navadvipa, for the sannyasa and for the coming separation.

## 25. Nayanananda — "sakala bhakata ṭhāñi haiyā vidāya…" (PK 2236)
*The farewell in Shantipura: Gaura Raya takes leave of all the devotees, bows to His mother, receives her permission,
takes leave of Advaita and with "Haribol!" sets out for Nilachala; in the Acharya's house weeping arises. Raga suhai.*[^10-100]

**25.1.** Having taken leave of all the devotees,
Gaura Raya set out to see Nilachala.

**25.2.** Bowing at His mother's feet, receiving her permission,
taking leave of Advaita Acharya,

**25.3.** the Lord Gauranga set out, saying, "Haribol!" —
in the Acharya's house the sound of weeping arose.[^10-101]

**25.4.** "Gauranga, Gauranga!" all weep,
Nayanananda weeps, rolling in the dust.[^10-102]

[^10-100]: Signature: "Nayanananda." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 281 (printed p. 270), 21st pallava, no. 19 (label "॥১৯॥২২৩৬॥"); raga suhai; P-R-Sa
MS no. 2341. GPT1 — p. 381, no. 49 (suhai; the first three couplets, without signature); GPT2 — sec. 5.3, no. 49. Cf. CC Madhya 3;
CB Antya 1.
[^10-101]: GPT1: "the sound of kirtana arose" (kīrtanera rola) instead of "weeping" (krandanera rola).
[^10-102]: According to PK's apparatus, the last couplet with the signature is found only in the P-R-Sa manuscript; the attribution
to Nayanananda is therefore not fully secure.

## 26. Balarama Dasa — "anukṣaṇa aruṇa-nayana ghana ghūrata…" (BR p. 975)
*Nityananda in Gauda (Saptagrama, the house of Uddharana Datta): His reddish eyes roll ceaselessly and pour nectar, He
dances sprinkling the world with prema, now weeps, now laughs, falls senseless with "Hari" on His lips, runs crying
"Gaura, Gaura!" and gives the jewel of prema to the destitute and the lowest. Raga dhanashi.*[^10-103]

**26.1.** Ceaselessly His reddish eyes roll,
His tears stream down and spread;
as if a red cloud drifting over the ocean
were pouring nectar without cease.

**26.2.** *(Refrain)* Nitai dances, the beautiful moon,
sprinkling the people of the world with the nectar-rasa of prema —
wondrous is the beauty of His dance!

**26.3.** On His feet are jewelled anklets,
as He moves His whole body sways;
His body is incomparable, like the peak of Meru,
and the waves of bhava sparkle.[^10-104]

**26.4.** He weeps, laughs, walks slowly,
with "Hari!" on His lips He falls senseless, lost to the world;
again and again He runs crying "Gaura, Gaura!"
and in bliss roars terribly.

**26.5.** The low, the lame, the fallen, the dull, the sick —
there is no end of the wretched, yet He makes no distinction:
the ever unattainable treasure, the jewel of prema,
He Himself offers to the world and gives away freely.

**26.6.** When He gave away the steadfast, rare treasure of prema,
all the world's sufferings went far away;
the desires of all the poor and wretched were fulfilled,
even the women became maddened.[^10-105]

**26.7.** By such a merciful glance
no one was left with dark days —
yet Balarama Dasa was left out:
cruel is his heart, and hard.

[^10-103]: Signature: "Balarama Dasa." BR, 12th wave: 1913 ed. (Murshidabad), pp. 974–975 ("gīte yathā — dhānaśī"); 1960 ed., vv.
3738–3744; 2006 ed., vv. 3738–3744. In Narahari Chakravarti the pada is sung in the account of Saptagrama: Nityananda comes to
Uddharana Datta's house and "is ever immersed in dance and kirtana." By OCR it is not found in GPT1 (on PK see below); GPT2 — sec. 6.1, no. 15
(in the catalogue BD-028, "GPT only"). Majumdar does not discuss the pada. Cf. CB Antya 5 (Nityananda in Gauda, Saptagrama).
Full PK check (chapter 16): the pada is also in PK — **PK 2301** (vol. 3, 22nd pallava, PDF pp. 303–304, label "॥৮॥২৩০১॥", MS P-R-Sa no. 2405; signature "valarāma dāsa kāhe bhela vañcita dāruṇa hṛdaya-kaṭhina").
[^10-104]: 1913 ed.: "padatala tāla-valita maṇi mañjarī"; 1960 ed.: "padatalatale valita muṇimañjarī" (OCR). Meru is the golden mountain.
[^10-105]: 1913 ed.: "avalāu unamata bhela" — "even the women (avalā) became maddened."

# Chapter 11. Balarama Dasa, Yadunandana, Kanu Dasa and Others: Praise of Gaura, His Bhavas in Navadvipa, the Sannyasa, Nityananda in Gauda

*This chapter completes the core — padas of the Lord's contemporaries known from the *Padakalpataru* (PK), the
*Bhakti-ratnakara* (BR) and the *Kshanada-gita-chintamani* (KGC), excluding padas in nagari-bhava. Here are the
remaining padas signed by Balarama Dasa; padas of Yadunandana Chakravarti (a disciple of Gadadhara Dasa) cited by
Narahari Chakravarti in the *Bhakti-ratnakara*; and padas of Kanu Dasa (Kanu Thakura), Raya Ananta, Murari and
Krishnadasa, in the order of the lilas: praise of the Gaura-avatara and of Nitai-Chaitanya; Gaura's form and His bhavas in
the kirtanas of Navadvipa, when, holding Gadadhara's hand, He speaks of Radha and Vrindavana; the lament over the
sannyasa; Shachi in Shantipura; the Lord in Nilachala; Nityananda, sent to Gauda, with Shachi; Gaura's bliss after long separation. Majumdar counts among the
Lord's contemporaries Balarama Dasa (on the strength of three BR padas, translated in chapter 10) and Yadunandana (on the
strength of his BR padas); the signature "Balarama Dasa" in PK covers padas of several poets, so the attribution of the
rest is doubtful. The text follows PK, checked against the scans, with the manuscript variants from PK's apparatus, BR,
the *Gaura-pada-tarangini* (GPT1 — 1st ed., 1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934) and KGC; the Bengali original, variants and
word-for-word translation are in the full version of the book.*

## 1. Balarama Dasa — "varaṇa-āśrama kiñcana akiñcana…" (PK 2212)
*Praise of the Gaura-avatara: making no distinction of varnas and ashramas, of rich and destitute, Gaura gives away the
prema inaccessible to Shiva and Brahma; sinners, beasts and birds weep; kings, yogis and jnanis abandon their own — only
the poet's heart seems made of stone. Raga suhai.*[^11-1]

**1.1.** Making no distinction of varnas and ashramas, of those who have and those who have not,
He takes no account of anyone's faults;
the treasure of prema, inaccessible to Shiva and Brahma,
He distributes to the people of the world, offering it Himself.[^11-2]

**1.2.** An ocean of mercy is the incarnation of Gaura:
I would give my life to turn misfortune away from Him![^11-3]
Who knows what His qualities are, what His sweetness is?
My soul weeps — I cannot forget.

**1.3.** The low, the godless, the poor, the wretched, the weak and the low-born —
hearing of His qualities, the whole world weeps;
even unreasoning beasts and birds weep, tears pour from their eyes:
with what has He bound the hearts of all?[^11-4]

**1.4.** The king abandons royal pleasures, the yogi meditation and yoga,
the jnani weeps, abandoning the taste of knowledge.
Who, then, fashioned Balarama's heart out of stone,
that this rasa has not touched it?

[^11-1]: Signature: "Balarama" ("kevā valarāma-hiyā…"). PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 272–273 (printed pp. 261–262), 20th pallava, no. 29
(label "॥২৯॥২২১২॥"); raga suhai; P-R-Sa MS no. 2320. GPT1 — p. 38, no. 38; GPT2 — sec. 1.3, no. 38. The catalogue (BD-010)
assigns the pada to PK 2214 — a mistake: PK 2214 is a pada of Govinda Dasa, "kundana-kanaya-kalevara-kāti", and PK 2213, which
follows ours (Govinda Dasa, "patita heri kānde…"), repeats its line "varaṇa-āśrama kiñcana akiñcana". Which of the Balarama
Dasas wrote the pada has not been established.
[^11-2]: "Those who have and those who have not" — kiñcana akiñcana. On the prema which the Lord gives away without
distinguishing the worthy and the unworthy, cf. CC Adi 7.
[^11-3]: "nichani laiyā mari" is a set phrase of love: "I would die taking on myself (the beloved's misfortune)"; nichhani is
a rite by which misfortune is turned away from a beloved.
[^11-4]: "The weak" — khīṇa; MS "ka", P-R-Sa: khala ("the wicked"). "The low-born" — jāti ("by birth"); P-R-Sa: mati ("the weak
in understanding").

## 2. Balarama Dasa — "dekha dekha aparūpa gaura-carita…" (PK 2286)
*Gaura's pastimes are like those of Vamana: the Lord of Gokula has appeared again, and Prataparudra, like Bali, gave Him
body, mind and all his possessions, asuras such as Jagai and Madhai bowed to His feet; Advaita is Bhagiratha, who brought
down the Ganga of bhakti, Nityananda is Shiva, who received it; in it all the devotees bathe, and the fallen attain the
supreme abode. Raga kamoda.*[^11-5]

**2.1.** *(Refrain)* Look, look — wondrous are Gaura's deeds!
That very Lord of Gokula has now appeared —
was it not so that Vamana once appeared?[^11-6]

**2.2.** Seeing His majesty, Prataparudra, like Bali,
gave Him body, mind and all he possessed;
Jagai, Madhai and the other asuras
He brought to bow at His feet.[^11-7]

**2.3.** From His feet, with Advaita as Bhagiratha,
flowed the stream of the Ganga of bhakti;
Nityananda is Girisha: He received it
and brought it down into the Himalaya…[^11-8]

**2.4.** Bathing in it, all the devotees
revel in the bliss of prema;
the low and the fallen attained the supreme abode —
only worthless Balarama is left out.[^11-9]

[^11-5]: Signature: "Balarama" ("vañcita valarāma manda"). PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 298 (printed p. 287), 21st pallava "The sannyasa of
Sri Gauranga and so on", no. 69 (label "॥৬৯॥২২৮৬॥"); raga kamoda; P-R-Sa MS no. 2390. GPT1 — p. 46, no. 66; GPT2 — sec.
1.3, no. 66. The catalogue (BD-013) assigns the pada to PK 1245 — wrongly: PK 1245 is Krishna-lila (Govardhana, signed
"Chaitanyadasa"). The pada follows Ananta Acharya's PK 2285 (chapter 3, no. 9).
[^11-6]: Vamana is the Lord's incarnation as a dwarf brahmana who begged three steps of land from Bali, king of the asuras,
and covered the universe with them (Bhag. 8.18–21). The comparison: Gaura, like Vamana, "begs" — and receives everything.
[^11-7]: Prataparudra is the king of Orissa (CC Madhya 11–14); Bali gave himself to Vamana. Jagai and Madhai are the wicked
brothers of Navadvipa delivered by the Lord (CB Madhya 13). "Brought to bow at His feet" — caraṇa pravaṇa nija kela; MS "ka":
prabale, "kha", "gha", "cha": pravaṇe.
[^11-8]: The Ganga flowed from Vamana's foot, Bhagiratha brought it down to earth, and Shiva (Girisha, "lord of the
mountains") received it on his head (Bhag. 9.9). So too Advaita called the Lord down, and Nityananda received and spread
the stream of bhakti. The end of the line is unclear: PK reads "vāma-himācala māha", MSS "cha", P-R-Sa "rāma-himācala"; P-R-Sa
reads "nityānanda gīma" instead of "nityānanda giriśa, dei". MSS "ka", "kha": "path" (patha) instead of "feet" (pada); "kha",
P-R-Sa: "devotee" (bhakata) instead of "bhakti".
[^11-9]: "The supreme abode" — parama pada; MSS "ka", "kha" and GPT1: "the supreme mercy" (parama dayā).

## 3. Raya Ananta — "nitāi caitanya duṭī bhāi dayāra avadhi…" (KGC 28.2)
*Nitai and Chaitanya, two brothers, are the limit of mercy: the prema inaccessible to Shiva and Brahma and sought in vain
by the four Vedas They give away unceasingly; the fallen of the age of Kali, crying "Nitai-Chaitanya", dance and sing.
Raga shri.*[^11-10]

**3.1.** Nitai and Chaitanya, two brothers, are the limit of mercy:
the prema inaccessible to Shiva and Brahma They give away without end.

**3.2.** The prema which the four Vedas search for, to attain it —
such prema the two brothers give away unceasingly.

**3.3.** The fallen, the wretched, as many as are struck down by Kali —
crying "Nitai-Chaitanya!" they dance and sing.[^11-11]

**3.4.** The good of the whole world has come about in the rasa of sankirtana —
Raya Ananta weeps: not a drop of it has come to him.[^11-12]

[^11-10]: Signature: "Raya Ananta" ("rāya ananta"). KGC: 28th kshanada, no. 2 (1925 ed., p. 223; scan PDF p. 257), a
gaura-chandrika to Radha-Krishna lila, raga shri. GPT1 — p. 40, no. 43 (raga mangala); GPT2 — sec. 1.3, no. 43. The pada
was not previously found in PK (see below). According to B. B. Majumdar, the "Raya Ananta" of KGC is Ananta Acharya of Advaita's branch (cf. chapter 4,
no. 9).
Full PK check (chapter 16): the pada is also in PK — **PK 2337** (vol. 3, 23rd pallava, PDF p. 317, label "॥৬॥২৩৩৭॥"; signature "rāya ananta kānde nā pāiyā leśe").
[^11-11]: GPT1, GPT2: "the fallen, the wretched, the sinful, struck down by Kali" (patita durgata pāpī kalihata yārā).
[^11-12]: "Not a drop of it has come to him" follows GPT1 (nā pāiyā leśe, "not obtaining a particle"); KGC reads śeṣe ("at
the end": "weeps, not obtaining [it] at the last").

## 4. Krishnadasa — "soṅaro nava gauracanda…" (PK 1085)
*Remembering the youthful Gaurachandra — the moon of Navadvipa, Krishna Himself: the moon-face, eyes full of prema, locks
dressed with flowers, earrings, the Kaustubha, red garments, sandal; the king of serpents holds an umbrella over Him,
Lakshmi serves His feet, the devotees sing His glory; at the end the poet places his hope in Nitai too, the giver of
prema. Raga bhairavi.*[^11-13]

**4.1.** *(Refrain)* I remember the youthful Gaurachandra —
the graceful Vanamali,
the moon of Navadvipa, the ocean of mercy,
tenderly loving His devotees.[^11-14]

**4.2.** His face is the moon, His lips are red,
waves of prema stream from His eyes;
the beauty of millions of moons, of millions of suns
I offer to Him as a gift to ward off harm.
His locks, dressed with flowers,
the tilaka on His brow, His shining nose,
His teeth are pearls, His smile nectar,
like lightning in a cloud.[^11-15]

**4.3.** Makara earrings flash on His cheeks,
His neck is lit by the Kaustubha gem,
red garments, merciful words —
beauty beyond measure.
His body anointed with sandal, in garlands —
millions of Kamadevas are put to shame;
bracelets on arms and wrists, jewelled anklets,
the sacred thread upon Him.[^11-16]

**4.4.** The king of the bearers of the earth holds an umbrella over Him,
the host of devotees sings His glory;
to the two feet served by Kamala
I offer myself in sacrifice.
Says humble Krishnadasa,
placing his hope in Gaura's feet:
the saviour of the fallen, Nitaichand,
is the giver of prema.[^11-17]

[^11-13]: Signature: "Krishnadasa" ("kahata dāna kṛṣṇadāsa"; GPT1 reads "dīna", "humble"; "dāna" in PK is apparently a misprint).
PK: vol. 2, PDF pp. 251–252 (printed pp. 238–239), 15th pallava, section "rasālasopayuktarūpaṃ" (the form befitting the
languor after the rasa), "śrīgauracandraḥ" — a gaura-chandrika to Radha-Krishna lila, no. 23 (label "॥২৩॥১০৮৫॥"); raga
bhairavi; P-R-Sa MS no. 1494. GPT1 — p. 136, no. 75 (bhairava, ektala). In the catalogue (KR-006) the pada stood without a
first line, marked as probably Krishna-lila: it is a gaura-pada. Which Krishnadasa wrote it has not been established (C).
[^11-14]: "The graceful Vanamali" — nāgara vanayāri: nagara is a graceful youth skilled in love; Banvari (Vanamali, "wearing the
forest garland") is a name of Krishna. Gaura is Krishna Himself (CC Adi 1–4). MSS "ka", "kha", "gha", "cha":
"Gaurasundara" instead of "Gaurachandra"; GPT1: "Remember the youthful Gaurasundara…" (soṅara).
[^11-15]: "I offer to Him as a gift to ward off harm" — nichayāri (from nichhani: everything beautiful is offered up to turn
misfortune away from the beloved). MSS "ka", "kha": "the beauty of His face" (mukhaśobhā). "Like lightning in a cloud" —
dāmini ghanayāri; the sense of the second word is not wholly clear.
[^11-16]: The Kaustubha is the gem on the breast of Vishnu-Krishna. MSS "ka", "kha", "gha", "cha" and GPT1: "sandal" (candana)
instead of "armlets" (aṅgada); MS "kha": tarala instead of ratana.
[^11-17]: "The king of the bearers of the earth" is Ananta-Shesha, the serpent who bears the universes; he serves the Lord as
His umbrella. Kamala is Lakshmi. Instead of the first line GPT1 reads "the devotees run and sing…" (dhārata gāota bhakatavṛnda)
and adds: "majestically He walks, slowly, slowly". MSS "ka", "kha", "gha", "cha": valiyā instead of baliye.

## 5. Balarama Dasa — "kothāya āchila gorā emana sundara…" (PK 2110)
*Gaura's form: where was such a beauty until now? He has charmed the whole town of Nadia: His hair dressed with flowers,
bees hovering above it, pearls on His breast, sandal and kunkuma, the forest garland, a gliding gait, the ringing of
anklets. Raga shri.*[^11-18]

**5.1.** Where was such a beauty — Gora — until now?
With this form He has charmed the town of Nadia.

**5.2.** His glossy hair is dressed with flowers of every kind —
rangana, malati, yuthi, bandhuli, bakula.[^11-19]

**5.3.** Thirsting for honey, how many bees hover over them!
Gazing at this form, life will not stay in the body.

**5.4.** A necklace of gems and pearls glitters on His breast,
on every limb ornaments flash like lightning.

**5.5.** His body is anointed with kunkuma mixed with sandal,
His arms reach to His knees, the forest garland is on His neck.

**5.6.** A gliding gait, swaying now to one side, now to the other —
as if nectar welled up when His neck sways.

**5.7.** As He walks, the anklets on His feet ring sweetly —
Balarama Dasa says: I give myself for Him.[^11-20]

[^11-18]: Signature: "Balarama Dasa." PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 233–234 (printed pp. 222–223), 18th pallava, section "atha
śrīgauracandrasya rūpādivarṇanaṃ" (description of Sri Gaurachandra's form), no. 2 (label "॥২॥২১১০॥"); raga shri; P-R-Sa MS no.
2218. GPT1 — p. 110, no. 2; GPT2 — sec. 3.1, no. 2. The catalogue (BD-014) listed it as "GPT only": the PK number was found
on the scan. The preceding PK 2109 ("gaura-varaṇa maṇi-ābharaṇa nāṭuyā-mohana veśa", with the same signature; BD-017) is in
nagari-bhava (deferred).
[^11-19]: Rangana (ixora), malati and yuthi (kinds of jasmine), bandhuli (pentapetes, a red flower), bakula (mimusops). GPT1:
pārulī (the patali flower) instead of vāndhulī.
[^11-20]: "I give myself for Him" — nichani yāṅa tāya (see note 3).

## 6. Balarama Dasa — "kusume khacita ratane racita…" (PK 2164)
*The form of Gaura the dancer: His hair dressed with flowers and gems, bees above it; a sandal tilaka, locks, earrings;
at His glances the women of Nadia lose their peace; lips, smile, speech are nectar; jasmine garlands, gold and diamonds,
red garments; the gait of an elephant, feet that outshine the lotus, nails that outshine the moon. Raga tori.*[^11-21]

**6.1.** Dressed with flowers, studded with gems —
His glossy tresses;
drunk with honey, greedy for fragrance,
swarms of bees whirl above them.

**6.2.** On the tablet of His brow is a tilaka of sandal,
curling locks adorn it;
skilled in the tandava dance, adorned with earrings —
His rounded cheeks shine.

**6.3.** Seeing this form, the chaste wives of noble families
abandoned their shame before their kin:
dharma, duties, modesty, honour —
as though struck by thunder.[^11-22]

**6.4.** By the hints of sidelong glances, by the play of the brows,
all around is tinged with Ananga;
the longing of Kama has made its abode
in the hearts of the young women of the world.

**6.5.** His lips are bandhuka flowers, sweeter than honey-wine
is His half-smile;
His speech, unhurried, pitcher after pitcher
pours out streams of nectar.

**6.6.** Garlands of jasmine here and there,
rows of lovely flowers;
greedy bees, male and female,
fly down to them, intoxicated.

**6.7.** Gold, diamonds, motionless lightning
adorn His enchanting body;
garments that outshine the red rays of dawn
captivate the young women with their colour.

**6.8.** His bearing and poise astonish Kama —
Gora, like pure gold;
His gait is slow, like a maddened elephant's —
gazing at Him, the world forgets itself.

**6.9.** His lotus feet put the wagtails to shame,
softly His anklets ring;
His nails outshine the moon —
so Balarama Dasa describes Him.[^11-23]

[^11-21]: Signature: "Balarama Dasa" ("vani valarāma dāsa"). PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 254–255 (printed pp. 243–244), 18th pallava, no. 56
(label "॥৫৬॥২১৬৪॥"; the preceding pada of Ramananda, PK 2163, is by a misprint also labelled "২১৬৪"); raga tori; P-R-Sa MS no.
2271. GPT1 — p. 125, no. 42, and p. 140, no. 86 (the same pada twice); GPT2 — sec. 3.1, nos. 42 and 86. The catalogue (BD-016)
gives PK 2165 (a mistake: PK 2165 is Narottama Dasa, "kāñcana darapaṇa varaṇa sugorā re").
[^11-22]: The words about the women of Nadia who, seeing Gaura, lose their shame and peace are an image of the poetics of
describing beauty and the language of nagari-bhava (Gaura as the nagara, the beloved of the town's women); we translate
faithfully to the author. Vrindavana Dasa stresses that in this incarnation the Lord never glanced at another man's wife;
worship of Gaura in the spirit of "Gaura-nagari" is not accepted by the Gaudiya tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa
Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta). MSS "ka", "kha": "with thrills" (pulake) instead of "with earrings" (kuṇḍale); "gha", "cha",
P-R-Sa: bhaṅgita instead of bhaṅgite. The last word of 6.4 is unclear on the scan (sardana?); we read it with GPT1 as sadana
("abode"); MS "gha": sohana instead of hoyala.
[^11-23]: The wagtail (khañjana) is an image of nimble, graceful feet. "Describes" — bani (from varṇana?); MSS "ka", P-R-Sa: bali
("says"). MSS "gha", "cha": lulupa instead of lolupa (6.6); P-R-Sa: kundala instead of kundana (6.8). GPT1 (6.1): kṣubdha
("agitated") instead of khubadha.

## 7. Balarama Dasa — "sahajai kāñcana-kānti kalevara…" (PK 2145)
*Gaura dancing, overwhelmed by Radha's prema: a body the colour of gold, before which millions of Madanas swoon; He
lingers, falls to the ground, trembles, roars, sheds tears and, embracing the fallen, bathes them in His tears. Raga
beloar.*[^11-24]

**7.1.** His body by nature is the colour of gold:
gazing at Him, the people of the world lose their hearts;
before Him how many millions of Madanas swoon!
His garment outshines the red rays of dawn.

**7.2.** Overwhelmed by Rai's prema, He walks slowly, slowly,
His heart brimming over — He falls to the ground;
sweat, trembling, again and again wave upon wave of thrills,
again and again He roars: "Hum! Hum!"[^11-25]

**7.3.** His body sways, He cannot stand firm,
from both cloud-like eyes the rain pours unceasingly;
drunk with that rasa, He finds no end to it,
clasping the fallen to His breast, He bathes them in tears.

**7.4.** Crying "Hari, Hari," how much He weeps and laments! —
only Balarama is left out, day and night.[^11-26]

[^11-24]: Signature: "Balarama" ("vañcita valarāma"). PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 247 (printed p. 236), 18th pallava, no. 37 (label
"॥৩৭॥২১৪৫॥"); raga beloar; P-R-Sa MS no. 2252. The pada follows Vasu Ghosha's PK 2143 and 2144 (chapter 8). GPT1 — p. 116,
no. 16 (beloar); GPT2 — sec. 3.1, no. 16. The catalogue (BD-015) gives PK 788: a mistake (PK 788 is a pada of Govinda Dasa,
"tapata-kāñcana-kānti kalevara").
[^11-25]: "Rai's prema" — rāi-prema: the Lord appeared in Radha's bhava and complexion to taste Her love for Krishna (CC Adi
4). MSS "kha", "gha": "immersed" (magana) instead of "walks" (gamana); "ka", "kha": kara instead of karata.
[^11-26]: Instead of the last couplet GPT1 reads: "Crying 'Hari, Hari,' He weeps and laments, mad with bliss day and night;
hearing the sound 'Hari, Hari,' the world was saved — only lowly Balarama Dasa is left out."

## 8. Balarama Dasa — "vihare āju rasika-rāja…" (PK 2111)
*Gaurachandra, the king of rasikas, sports in Nadia: beauty outshining millions of Kamadevas, a moon-face, smile and speech
of nectar; remembering the groves of Vraja He loses Himself, stumbles, falls into the arms of the fallen, repeats "Rai,
Rai!" — all drink the nectar of prema except the poet. Raga turi.*[^11-27]

**8.1.** Today the king of rasikas,
Gaurachandra, sports in Nadia:
shining like a cluster of nagakeshara flowers,
with the lovely lustre of gold.
The abode of the beauty of millions of Kamadevas,
loveliness that enchants the world —
seeing Him, the young women of the world in turmoil
abandon composure and dharma.[^11-28]

**8.2.** A face whose charm outshines the rays
of the boundless full autumn moon;
a row of lovely teeth
puts the kunda flowers to shame;
on His bimba lips a sweet smile
pouring out so many streams of nectar;
His words, likewise, flow
in torrents of sweet drink.[^11-29]

**8.3.** The sweet groves of the forests of Vraja,
the sweet heaps of love and longing —
remembering, remembering them, He loses Himself more and more,
rapt day and night.
Overcome by bhava, languid, bewildered,
He walks, walks — and slowly stumbles;
enraptured, He falls into the arms of the fallen,
intoxicated with deep bliss.[^11-30]

**8.4.** With reddened eyes He gazes, full of compassion,
unceasingly He repeats: "Rai, Rai!";
He dances, mad with prema, rolls on the ground, wanders —
His breast bursting with what is in His heart.
The high, the middling, the low beings —
all drink the nectar of prema;
Balarama alone is left out,
having offended the sadhus.[^11-31]

[^11-27]: Signature: "Balarama" ("tahim̐ valarāma vañcita ekale"). PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 234 (printed p. 223), 18th pallava, no. 3 (label
"॥৩॥২১১১॥"); raga turi (todi); P-R-Sa MS nos. 1430 and 2219. GPT1 — p. 110, no. 3 (turi). The pada is not in the catalogue
(in chapter 10 it was noted from Ray's footnote to PK 2066 as "outside the catalogue"); new row BD-043.
[^11-28]: Nagakeshara (keśara) is a flower with golden stamens; "cluster" — puñja (the word kuñja at the start of the line is
unclear). The words about young women are the language of nagari-bhava; we translate faithfully to the author (see note
22). MS "gha": murati instead of yubati.
[^11-29]: Bimba is a red fruit; kunda is white jasmine. MS "ka": "a face outshining Madana" (madana badana); P-R-Sa: "badana madana";
instead of chanda ("charm") MS "ka": basana, "kha": sadana, "gha", P-R-Sa: badana. MS "ka": nikare; P-R-Sa: racana (instead of bacana?).
[^11-30]: The idea: Gaura in Krishna's bhava remembers the pastimes in Vraja (cf. CC Madhya 2). P-R-Sa: "the love of the young
(gopis)" (yubati piriti) instead of "love and longing" (piriti-ārati). MSS "ka", "kha", "cha", P-R-Sa: "in ecstasy" (āveśe)
instead of "by bhava"; P-R-Sa: "dances" (naṭata) instead of the second "walks".
[^11-31]: "Rai" is Radha. Cf. chapter 10, no. 20 (PK 2113: "Rai, Rai!" at the sight of Gadadhara). "Having offended the sadhus"
— sādhu ṭhāme aparādhiyā: the poet sees the cause of his being left out in an offence against the devotees. P-R-Sa: "red"
(aruṇa) instead of "full of compassion" (karuṇa).

## 9. Balarama Dasa — "āveśe avaśa aṅga dhīre dhīre cale…" (PK 2081)
*The Lord dances in kirtana: hearing the story of His former pastimes of love, He falls senseless, weeps at the sight of
the fallen, rolls on the ground crying "Hari!"; because of His bhava householders abandon the happiness of home — only the
poet remains indifferent to this rasa. Raga shri.*[^11-32]
