**9.1.** Overcome by ecstasy, He walks slowly, slowly,
brimming with bhava, He does not open His eyes.

**9.2.** *(Refrain)* The Lord dances, the connoisseur of rasa,
by whose qualities wood and stone melt.

**9.3.** All the tales of former deeds, of love —
hearing them, the Lord rolls senseless on the ground.[^11-33]

**9.4.** Seeing the fallen, He weeps, He cannot calm Himself,
in hundreds of streams the tears pour from His eyes.

**9.5.** Covered with thrills, raising both arms,
crying "Hari, Hari," swaying, He falls.

**9.6.** The hearts of chaste wives pine, their eyes pine,
pining, the beasts and birds of the forests weep.[^11-34]

**9.7.** Because of His bhava householders abandon the happiness of home —
Balarama Dasa alone is indifferent to it all.[^11-35]

[^11-32]: Signature: "Balarama Dasa." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 223 (printed p. 212), 17th pallava, no. 23 (label "॥২৩॥২০৮১॥"); raga
shri; P-R-Sa MS no. 1181 (?) and 2190, P-R 4.1. KGC — 3rd kshanada, no. 1 (p. 16; raga varari), a gaura-chandrika. GPT1 —
p. 289, no. 41; GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 16, and 4.3, no. 41. According to B. B. Majumdar, signatures of this type ("everyone —
but I am indifferent") belong to the later Balarama Dasa; attribution C.
[^11-33]: "Former deeds" — puruba-carita: Krishna's pastimes in Vraja sung by the devotees; hearing them, the Lord is plunged into
bhava (cf. CB Madhya 8). MS P-R: "attentive" (avahita) instead of "senseless". In KGC the refrain stands after 9.4.
[^11-34]: The words about "chaste wives" are an image of how every living being pines for Gaura (see note 22). MS P-R: "young
wives" (kulavadhū), "in the heart" (mane); MS "gha": "understanding, understanding, they weep in their hearts" (vujhiyā vujhiyā
mane kānde) instead of "pining, they weep".
[^11-35]: MSS P-R-Sa, P-R: "Balarama Dasa is indifferent to such rasa" (hena rase valarāma dāsa vimukha); KGC: "Balarama Dasa alone among
all is indifferent to this rasa" (valarāma dāsa save e rase vimukha).

## 10. Balarama Dasa — "bhāvabhare gara gara cita…" (BR pp. 921–922)
*The Lord in the kirtana of Navadvipa: brimming with bhava, He now rises, now sits, weeps over His former love — why is
the Lord of Goloka in the midst of sankirtana? — makes no distinction of His own and others, holding Gadadhara's hand
cries out what is in His heart, and falls into the arms of the devotees. Raga suhai.*[^11-36]

**10.1.** His heart brims with bhava:
now He rises, now He sits — He cannot come to His senses.

**10.2.** From the excess of rasa He cannot stand firm,
remembering, remembering, He weeps over His former love.[^11-37]

**10.3.** *(Refrain)* The Lord dances — Gora, the king of dancers:
why is the Lord of Goloka in the midst of sankirtana?[^11-38]

**10.4.** He does not know who is His own and who is another,
the poor, the wretched, the low and the high He does not distinguish.[^11-39]

**10.5.** Holding the hand of His dear Gadadhara,
He tells what is in His heart, crying out again and again.

**10.6.** Swaying in waves of bliss,
He sinks, reeling, into the arms of the devotees.[^11-40]

**10.7.** Through Gora's rasa everything is full of rasa —
only Balarama's stony heart does not melt.[^11-41]

[^11-36]: Signature: "Bala(rama)" ("nā darave vala-pāṣāṇa hṛdaya"). BR, 12th wave: 1913 ed., pp. 921–922 ("punaḥ suhai"), 1960 ed., vv.
3022–3028 — in Narahari Chakravarti's account to Srinivasa of the places of Navadvipa ("here Gaurachandra danced in
sankirtana"); in BR the pada stands before padas of Balarama (PK 2067; chapter 10, no. 7) and Murari (PK 2121; chapter 1, no. 6).
KGC — 17th kshanada, no. 1 (p. 125; raga deshaga), a gaura-chandrika. GPT1 — p. 271, no. 77 (dhanashi). Not previously found in PK (see below). In the
catalogue — BD-041.
Full PK check (chapter 16): the pada is also in PK — **PK 635** (vol. 2, 3rd shakha, gaura-chandrika to "svayaṃ dautya," PDF p. 30, label "॥১॥৬৩৫॥", raga dhanashi, MS P-R-Sa no. 1112; repeated as PK 909); signature "nā darave valarāma pāṣāṇa-hṛdaya."
[^11-37]: "Former love" — the love of Krishna and Radha in Vraja: the Lord in His bhava remembers it.
[^11-38]: Goloka is Krishna's supreme abode. The footnote in BR, and KGC: "the Lord of Gokula" (gokula-pati).
[^11-39]: The couplet is only in BR (KGC and GPT1 lack it). In the 1913 ed. the middle of the line is effaced on the scan; we
read it from the 1960 ed.: "dīnahīna adhama uttama nāhi māne".
[^11-40]: KGC: "into the arms of the Pandita" (paṇḍitera kole), i.e. of Gadadhara Pandita; GPT1: "into the arms of the fallen"
(patitera kola).
[^11-41]: "Balarama" — BR: "Vala-" (vala-pāṣāṇa hṛdaya, "Vala's stony heart"); KGC: "Balarama" (valarāma pāṣāṇa-hṛdaya); GPT1: "Balarama's
hard heart" (valarāma kaṭhina hṛdaya).

## 11. Kanu Dasa — "nija-nāmāmṛte matta anukṣaṇa…" (PK 2117)
*Gauranga's wondrous pastimes: intoxicated with the nectar of His own name, He makes everyone drink it, the lowly above
all; now He says, "I am the Lord," now, "I am the servant"; now He strides like a maddened lion, now stands stunned in
bhava, slaps His arms, roars with laughter, weeps, and sees before Him Shyamasundara, bent in three places. Raga
vibhasa.*[^11-42]

**11.1.** Ever intoxicated with the nectar of His own name,
He makes all drink the Name, the lowly above all.

**11.2.** His eyes reddened, He speaks haltingly,
weeps aloud and embraces whomever He meets.

**11.3.** *(Refrain)* Wondrous are Gauranga's pastimes:
now He says, "I am the Lord," now He says, "I am the servant."[^11-43]

**11.4.** Now He strides like a maddened lion, now stands stunned in bhava,
now embraces the earth, as though He had found an embrace.[^11-44]

**11.5.** Now He slaps His arms like a wrestler and roars with laughter,
now He weeps, now He speaks in a faltering voice.

**11.6.** Now He sees Shyamasundara, bent in three places —
Kanu Dasa says: who can understand this play?[^11-45]

[^11-42]: Signature: "Kanu Dasa" ("kānudāsa kahe"). PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 236 (printed p. 225), 18th pallava, no. 9 (label
"॥৯॥২১১৭॥"); raga vibhasa; P-R-Sa MS no. 2225. GPT1 — p. 278, no. 4 (vibhasa). The preceding PK 2116 is Nayanananda's
(chapter 10, no. 18). In the catalogue — KD-010. Kanu Dasa is Kanu Thakura, son of Purushottama Dasa and grandson of
Sadashiva Kaviraja, of Nityananda's branch (Majumdar).
[^11-43]: The Lord showed now the bhava of His own divinity, now the bhava of a devotee (cf. CB Madhya 9: the mahaprakasha in
Srivasa's house; the Lord, coming to Himself, calls Himself the servant of the devotees). MS "ka": "the Lord is
intoxicated" (pahu matta) instead of "intoxicated" (11.1); "gha", "cha": "speaks" (bola) instead of the second "ādha".
[^11-44]: The sense of the second line is not wholly clear: "kheṇe dharu dharaṇī pāiyā aṅga-saṅga" — apparently in His bhava the Lord
embraces the earth as though embracing the Beloved.
[^11-45]: Slapping one's arms (mālasāṭa) is a wrestler's gesture. Shyamasundara bent in three places (tribhanga) is Krishna with
the flute: in Radha's bhava the Lord sees Krishna before Him. MSS "ka", "kha": "seeing" (dekhi); P-R-Sa: "who would not
understand" (ke nā).

## 12. Yadunandana — "dekha dekha gorācānde…" (BR p. 909)
*Gaura, dancing, speaks of His former love: in the bhava of youth He tells of the banks of the Yamuna and the wanderings
in the forests, Himself tells of Radha, holding Gadadhara's hand, weeps, laughs, rushes like a maddened elephant, and begs
for the treasure of prema: He is the enchanter of Gokula. Raga bhupali.*[^11-46]

**12.1.** *(Refrain)* Look, look at Gorachand:
His colour outshines gold, His dancing
enchants Madana.

**12.2.** He speaks of His former love:
in the bhava of youth
His body is filled with thrills.

**12.3.** Who knows the pain of His heart?
The banks of the Yamuna, the wanderings through the forests —
of all this He speaks.

**12.4.** His lotus eyes are full of tears,
He Himself tells of Radha —
not for a moment can He be still.[^11-47]

**12.5.** Holding Gadadhara's hand,
He speaks words steeped in weeping
and cries: "Hari, Hari, Hari!"

**12.6.** His body is spent with bhava;
He rushes forward with the gait of a maddened elephant,
as though trampling the forest.

**12.7.** Now He laughs, now weeps, now dances;
His lips tremble, He stands still, startled,
now He begs for the treasure of prema.

**12.8.** Yadunandana says:
do you not know? The enchanter of Gokula
is Gauranga, who captivates the world.[^11-48]

[^11-46]: Signature: "Yadunandana" ("e yadunandana kahe"). BR, 12th wave: 1913 ed., p. 909 ("kācicca bhūpāliḥ"), 1960 ed., vv.
2862–2869. GPT1 — p. 294, no. 5 (bhupali). Not found in PK. In BR the pada belongs to a series of padas by Yadunandana
Chakravarti, a disciple of Gadadhara Dasa (BR pp. 904–910), which Narahari Chakravarti puts into the mouths of the women of
Nadia, "full of anuraga", talking about Gaura as He goes to the Ganga; most of these padas are in nagari-bhava (deferred),
but this one is about the Lord's bhava in kirtana.
[^11-47]: The Lord in Krishna's bhava remembers the pastimes in Vraja and Radha (cf. chapter 10, no. 9).
[^11-48]: "You" is the friend whom the poet addresses (the frame of BR). Gokulamohana ("the enchanter of Gokula") is Krishna:
Gaura is Krishna Himself. GPT1: "as though crushing hosts of monkeys" (vānara dalana janu, per OCR) instead of "as though
trampling the forest" (12.6).

## 13. Yadunandana — "chala chala cāru nayana yugala…" (BR pp. 922–923 = PK 2246)
*Gaura, the ocean of mercy: His eyes pour rivers of tears, He roars in a thunderous voice, embraces the fallen, sings
songs of the rasa, calls "Radha, Radha!" and embraces Gadadhara, asks for the flute and the peacock feather, gazing into
Svarupa's face. Raga kamoda.*[^11-49]

**13.1.** His lovely eyes are brimming with tears —
how many rivers flow in streams!
Gora's body is filled with thrills —
the earth cannot hold Him.

**13.2.** *(Refrain)* The Lord — Gora, the ocean of mercy:
in the fullness of bhava
His body sways; as He walks, the world forgets itself.

**13.3.** Again and again how much mercy He shows,
roaring in a thunderous voice;
seeing the lowly, His heart full of turmoil,
He clasps and clasps them and weeps.[^11-50]

**13.4.** His lotus feet are most restless,
unsteady is their gait;
from His lotus mouth, in a faltering voice,
He sings songs of the rasa.[^11-51]

**13.5.** Crying "Aha! Aha!", raising both arms,
He says: "Sing 'Hari, Hari'!";
loudly calling "Radha, Radha!",
He embraces Gadadhara.

**13.6.** Again and again saying, "The flute! The flute!" —
He gazes into Svarupa's face;
saying, "The peacock feather!" — He chokes with sobs:
can Yadu understand this?[^11-52]

[^11-49]: Signature: "Yadu" ("yadu ki vujhite pāre"). BR, 12th wave: 1913 ed., pp. 922–923 ("punaḥ kāmodaḥ"), right after Murari's
PK 2121. PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 285 (printed p. 274), 21st pallava, no. 29 (label "॥২৯॥২২৪৬॥", the second digit damaged on the scan), raga shri, P-R-Sa MS no. 2351 —
without the first stanza and **without a signature** (last line: "who can tell it?"). GPT1 — p. 285, no. 27 (kamoda; signed
Yadu) and p. 46, no. 65 (the PK recension, unsigned). KGC (26th kshanada, no. 1, pp. 207–208, raga varari) joins the first
stanza of Prasada Dasa's pada "keśera veśe bhulila deśe" (PK 2085) to 13.1–13.5 of our pada — without 13.6 and without a
signature. A variant signed "Govinda-dasiya" — GPT1 p. 10, no. 23. The pada was not in the catalogue; RM-005 ("keśera
veśe…", supposedly Ramananda's) is a pada of Prasada Dasa.
[^11-50]: PK: "losing His head" (ākula haiyā) instead of "His heart full of turmoil" (ākula hṛdaya).
[^11-51]: "Songs of the rasa" follows BR (rāsakeli-gīta, songs of the rasa dance); PK and GPT1 (no. 65): "songs full of rasa"
(rasamaya gīta). Instead of "unsteady is their gait" (athira tāhāra rīta) PK reads "like red lotuses" (rātā-utapala-rīta).
[^11-52]: In Krishna's bhava the Lord seeks His flute and peacock feather. Svarupa is Svarupa Damodara, the Lord's closest
companion in Puri (before his sannyasa, Purushottama Acharya, who knew the Lord already in Navadvipa, CC Madhya 10); PK places
the pada among the pastimes after the sannyasa, BR among the places of Navadvipa. PK: "who knows what bhava rises in Him,
who can tell it?" (ki bhāva uṭhaye ke tāhā kahite pāre).

## 14. Yadunandana — "kīrtana-lampaṭa ghana ghana nāṭa…" (BR pp. 923–924)
*Gaura, greedy for kirtana, dances untiringly; seeing nothing for His tears, He walks leaning on the hand of Gadadhara Dasa,
cannot tell water from land, repeats the name of Hari, sings, and, seeing the fallen, clasps them to His breast; Brahma and
Shiva bow at His feet. Raga abhiri.*[^11-53]

**14.1.** Greedy for kirtana, He dances again and again,
He walks — and for His tears cannot see the way.

**14.2.** *(Refrain)* Beautiful youthful Gaura
is rapt in the rasa of former love.

**14.3.** He cannot utter even half a word,
He walks holding the hand of Gadadhara Dasa.[^11-54]

**14.4.** His red soles find no footing:
is it water, is it land, a forest or a house?

**14.5.** He repeats the name "Hari, Hari", sings abhiri —
what gestures His lovely hands display![^11-55]

**14.6.** Why He does what He does — who can fathom it?
Seeing the fallen and wretched, He clasps them to His breast.

**14.7.** Aja, Bhava and the other gods bow at His feet —
Yadu says: without mercy who can fathom His mind?[^11-56]

[^11-53]: Signature: "Yadu" ("yadu kahe"). BR, 12th wave: 1913 ed., pp. 923–924 ("gīte yathā — ābhīrī"), 1960 ed., vv. 3047–3053; in
Narahari Chakravarti's account: "along this path Gorachand slowly walked… in kirtana He danced in many ways". GPT1 — pp.
285–286, no. 28 (abhiri). Not found in PK. The pada was not in the catalogue.
[^11-54]: Gadadhara Dasa is a companion of the Lord (CC Adi 10), the guru of Yadunandana Chakravarti.
[^11-55]: Abhiri is a raga (the pada itself is marked with it); "sings abhiri" — ālāpe ābhīrī (sings the alap in raga abhiri).
[^11-56]: Aja is Brahma, Bhava is Shiva. "Mind" follows the 1960 ed. and GPT1 (mati); the 1913 ed. has "māta". 1913 ed.: "dhāri kare
kora" (14.6).

## 15. Yadunandana — "dāsa-gadādhara-prāṇa gorā…" (BR p. 924)
*Gora, the life of Gadadhara Dasa, is rapt in the memory of His former pastimes: His body is lightning, tears stream from
His eyes, His face is a golden lotus, He trembles, leaps with the cry "Hari!", rolls on the ground like a golden mountain;
the world drowns in prema — only the poet is left out. Raga dhanashi.*[^11-57]

**15.1.** Gora — the life of Gadadhara Dasa —
is rapt in His former pastimes.

**15.2.** His body, the colour of lightning, steals hearts,
from His lotus eyes tears flow.

**15.3.** The radiance of His face is a golden lotus,
when He smiles, gems and pearls tumble out.

**15.4.** With abundant thrills He trembles,
crying "Hari, Hari", He leaps.

**15.5.** Day and night He notices nothing in His rasa,
again and again His hair and garments come loose.[^11-58]

**15.6.** Again and again He rolls on the ground —
a golden mountain rolling on the earth.

**15.7.** The world floats in the rasa of prema —
only Yadu, worthless, has missed it by his own fault.[^11-59]

[^11-57]: Signature: "Yadu" ("yadu eṛāila dīna doṣe"). BR, 12th wave: 1913 ed., p. 924 ("punardhānaśī"), 1960 ed., vv. 3054–3060 —
before Narahari Sarakara's pada "gaurāṅga ṭhekilā pāke" (chapter 3, no. 1). Not found in PK or GPT1. According to Majumdar it is one of
Yadunandana's padas cited in BR as testimony (BR p. 924; in the catalogue YN-007).
[^11-58]: "Hair and garments" — cikura cira (chikura, hair; chira, cloth).
[^11-59]: "Has missed" — eṛāila; "worthless, by his own fault" — dīna doṣe (1913 and 1960 eds.).

## 16. Balarama Dasa — "naṭavara rasika ramaṇi-manomohana…" (PK 2249)
*A lament over the sannyasa: Krishna, the best of dancers, who enchanted the hearts of the gopis, covering His dark form
with a golden one, has appeared to the world — and this Beloved of Radha, who wore garments marked with kunkuma from Her
breast, now lives under a tree as a sannyasi: what siddhi does He seek? Raga sindhura.*[^11-60]

**16.1.** The best of dancers, the knower of rasa, the enchanter of young hearts,
in hundreds of attires and pastimes —
over His dark form clad in a golden body,
He has appeared to the whole world.[^11-61]

**16.2.** *(Refrain)* Look, look — wondrous is the Lord's play:
He who was steeped in the rasa of play with His playful Beloved —
such a One has taken sannyasa![^11-62]

**16.3.** He who gladly wore garments
marked with kunkuma from His Beloved's breast,
who in the depth of His heart, in the frenzy of prema, longed
to touch with His lips Her moon-like face —

**16.4.** who in Her close embrace
thrilled all over with rapture,
who, defeated in the contest of love,
grieved in His heart —[^11-63]

**16.5.** now, abandoning His emerald hue and jewelled ornaments,
lives beneath a tree.
The first of fickle lovers — what siddhi does He seek?
Balarama Dasa does not understand.[^11-64]

[^11-60]: Signature: "Balarama Dasa" ("nā vujhai valarāma dāsa"). PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 286 (printed p. 275), 21st pallava "The sannyasa
of Sri Gauranga and so on", no. 32 (label "॥৩২॥২২৪৯॥"); raga sindhura; P-R-Sa MS no. 2354. GPT1 — p. 19, no. 52; GPT2 — sec.
1.2, no. 52. In the catalogue — BD-006 (number corrected in chapter 7). The next pada, PK 2250 ("gopīgaṇa-kuca-kuṅkume
vañcita…"), is signed "Natavara" (in the P-R-Sa MS "Balarama"); not included in this chapter.
[^11-61]: "Over His dark form a golden body": Krishna appeared covered by Radha's golden radiance (CC Adi 4; "Krishna within,
Gaura without"). MSS "ka", "kha", "cha": vivaraṇa instead of varaṇa; Ray thinks the original reading was "śyāmari varaṇa" and in his
note compares the line with PK 2259 ("antarete śyāma-tanu vāhire gaurāṅga").
[^11-62]: The pada speaks of Krishna's transcendental pastimes with Radha: Their love is pure prema, having nothing in common
with mundane passion (Bhaktisiddhanta: aprakrita-shringara). The poet contrasts Krishna, the Beloved of Vraja, with Krishna
become the sannyasi Gaura.
[^11-63]: "Defeated in the contest of love": Krishna is defeated by Radha's love; to taste it He appeared as Gaura (CC Adi 4).
MSS "ka", "kha", "cha", P-R-Sa: "in union" (saṅgama); MS "ka": "with great joy" (atiśaya sādhe), P-R-Sa: "ati apasādhe"; so too
GPT1: "pulakita atiśaya sādhe"; MS "gha": manabhaba instead of manasija.
[^11-64]: "Emerald hue" — Krishna's dark form. "The first of fickle lovers" — lampaṭa-gurubara (literally "the foremost teacher of
rakes"): a tender reproach in the spirit of the gopis, who call Krishna a deceiver (Bhag. 10.31, 10.47); we translate
faithfully to the author.

## 17. Balarama Dasa — "hari hari e vaṛa vismaya lāge mane…" (PK 2251)
*A lament over the sannyasa: He whose body was darker than a new cloud has become Gauranga; the head that wore a crown with
a peacock feather is shaven; the eyes that charmed Radha are full of tears; He who sported with the gopas and gopis now
does not hear even the name of a woman; the hands that held the flute hold a staff; instead of yellow silk — saffron
garments. Raga shri.*[^11-65]

**17.1.** *(Refrain)* Hari, Hari! Great wonder fills my heart:
He whose body once outshone a new cloud —
why has He now become Gauranga?

**17.2.** He whose crown was lovely, with a peacock feather, wreathed in gunja —
that head I see without hair.
He whose crooked glance captivated Radhika's heart —
His eyes are now full of tears of prema.

**17.3.** He who always sported with the gopas and gopis, delighting in rasa —
now does not hear even the name of a woman.
He who, holding the flute in both hands, drew the women of Vraja —
why does He take a staff in those hands?[^11-66]

**17.4.** He whose hips were adorned with yellow silk —
why does He wear saffron garments?
Finding no bottom to this bhava, Balarama Dasa, bewildered,
ponders a sorrowful thought in his heart.[^11-67]

[^11-65]: Signature: "Balarama Dasa." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 287 (printed p. 276), 21st pallava, no. 34 (label "॥৩৪॥২২৫১॥"); raga
shri; P-R-Sa MS no. 2356. GPT1 — p. 19, no. 51; GPT2 — sec. 1.2, no. 51. The catalogue (BD-005) listed it as "GPT only": the
PK number was found on the scan.
[^11-66]: Gunja are red-and-black berries from which the cowherds of Vraja make necklaces. GPT1: "He who was always with the
gopis, speaking with them in many playful ways…" (sadā gopī saṅge rahe, nānā raṅge kathā kahe). A sannyasi does not listen to
talk of women — thus the Lord strictly kept the rules of sannyasa (CC Antya 2).
[^11-67]: MS P-R-Sa: "grievous" (viṣama) instead of "wonder" (vismaya) in 17.1.

## 18. Balarama Dasa — "rūpa koṭi kāma jini…" (PK 2252)
*A lament over the sannyasa: He whose beauty outshines millions of Kamadevas, who sports in Goloka, the son of the king of
Vraja, the treasure of the gopis' lives — why does He roll on the ground and weep in the midst of sankirtana? He who
sported with Radha, Chandravali and hundreds of young cowherd girls is now a sannyasi with a staff; abandoning His graceful
attire, He goes from land to land seeking out the fallen. Raga sindhura.*[^11-68]

**18.1.** He whose beauty outshines millions of Kamadevas, the crest-jewel of the skilful,
who sports in Goloka full of delight —
the son of the king of Vraja, the treasure of the gopis' lives —
why does He roll on the ground?

**18.2.** *(Refrain)* Hari, Hari! What a spear has lodged in my breast:
why does the king of rasikas weep in the midst of sankirtana?
Not understanding it, I am dying of grief.

**18.3.** He with whom Radha and Chandravali sported,
and hundreds of young girls of Vraja —
now the Lord, breast to breast, does not look at a woman's face:
why is He a sannyasi with a staff?[^11-69]

**18.4.** Abandoning His graceful attire, the Lord goes from land to land,
seeking out the fallen in every house;
by His qualities, like a chintamani, He has saved the people of the world —
only Balarama Dasa remains far away.[^11-70]

[^11-68]: Signature: "Balarama Dasa." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 287 (printed p. 276), 21st pallava, no. 35 (label "॥৩৫॥২২৫২॥"); raga
sindhura; P-R-Sa MS no. 2357. GPT1 — p. 19, no. 50 (a footnote in GPT1 gives a manuscript variant signed by Vasu Ghosha);
GPT2 — sec. 1.2, no. 50. In the catalogue — BD-004.
[^11-69]: Chandravali is a gopi, Radha's rival. The sense of "vuke vuka" ("breast to breast") is unclear: probably the Lord
embraces the devotees in kirtana but does not look at women. GPT1: "nā dekhena nārīmukha". MS P-R-Sa: "many" (vahu) instead of
"the Lord" (pahu) in 18.4.
[^11-70]: The chintamani is the wish-fulfilling touchstone. MS P-R-Sa: "by the gift of the chintamani of the Name"
(nāma-cintāmaṇi-dāne) instead of "by His qualities, like a chintamani" (cintāmaṇi nija-guṇe).

## 19. Murari — "dhara dhara dhara dhara re nitāi…" (PK 2235)
*Shantipura after the sannyasa: Shachi watches her sannyasi son dancing in kirtana in Advaita's house and begs Nitai,
Advaita and Srivasa to support Him when He falls and to stop the kirtana — the night is already far gone. Raga
ramakeli.*[^11-71]

**19.1.** *(Refrain)* "Hold Him, hold Him, hold Him, hold Him, Nitai,
hold my Gauranga!
When He falls, remember that He is Your younger brother,
show mercy just once!"[^11-72]

**19.2.** "Acharya Gosani, take care of Nimai —
the pupil of my eyes!
I do not know at what moment, while He dances in kirtana,
I shall lose my life."[^11-73]

**19.3.** "Listen, Srivasa: He has taken sannyasa —
He rolls on the ground;
golden in colour, a little doll of butter —
may He not be hurt!"

**19.4.** "Listen, devotees, stop the kirtana —
the night is far gone!"
Murari says: listen, Gaurahari,
see what Your mother is going through![^11-74]

[^11-71]: Signature: "Murari" ("kahaye murāri śuna gaurahari"). PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 280 (printed p. 269), 21st pallava, no. 18 (label
"॥১৮॥২২৩৫॥"); raga ramakeli; P-R-Sa MS no. 2340. The preceding PK 2233 (Vallabha Dasa) and PK 2234 (Nayanananda, chapter 10,
no. 24) concern the same stay of the Lord in Advaita's house. GPT1 — p. 380, no. 46 (ramakeli or turi). In chapter 10 the
pada was found to have been wrongly counted as Nayanananda's (NN-021/027 = PK 2234); the Murari section of the catalogue had
no row for it. Whether this Murari is Murari Gupta is not proven (Majumdar doubts other padas signed "Murari" too);
attribution C. Cf. Shachi in Shantipura — CC Madhya 3, CB Antya 1.
[^11-72]: "Your younger brother" — anuja: Shachi sees in Nityananda Nimai's elder brother (a second Vishvarupa, as it were; cf. Shachi's dream of the two
brothers, Krishna and Balarama, CB Madhya 8). MSS "ka", "kha", "cha", P-R-Sa: "hold, hold" (twice); "ka", "kha", "cha": "my Gora"; "gha": "my Gaura".
[^11-73]: MSS "ka", "kha", "cha", P-R-Sa: "take care of Nitai" (nitāi) instead of "Nimai"; P-R-Sa: "of my eyes" (nayana), "some day"
(kakhane) instead of "at what moment".
[^11-74]: "A little doll of butter" — nanīra putalī: so tender, to a mother's feeling, is His body. Shachi's last words and the poet's
signature merge: Murari asks the Lord to have pity on His mother.

## 20. Balarama Dasa — "gaurasundara pahum̐ nadīyā udaya kari…" (PK 2244)
*Gaura rose in Nadia and filled the world with prema, saving the low and fallen with the holy name; He weeps seeing
Gadadhara, holding the hands of Svarupa and Ramananda, rolls in the dust crying "Shripada!", and Nityananda, embracing
Him, weeps; the blind and the deaf go mad with His qualities, high and low become bhagavatas. Raga ramakeli.*[^11-75]

**20.1.** The Lord Gaurasundara, rising in Nadia,
filled the world with the gift of prema;
the low, the godless, the poor, the wretched, the weak and low-born
He saved, giving them the name of Hari.

**20.2.** *(Refrain)* Hearing of the qualities of Thakura Gauranga, my soul weeps.
All the ignorant, seeing Him, their minds made steady,
cry "Haribol!" and give Him their hearts.[^11-76]

**20.3.** Seeing Gadadhara, He weeps, He cannot calm Himself,
holding the hands of Svarupa and Ramananda;
my Lord, crying "Shripada!", rolls in the dust of the earth —
embracing Him, Nityananda weeps.[^11-77]

**20.4.** The blind, the deaf — all are maddened by Gora's qualities,
they know not the quarters of the sky;
brimming with bhava, not knowing His own and others,
He delivers one person after another.

**20.5.** Raising His arms, He cries "Hari", embracing the fallen —
the world floats in Gora's prema;
the high and the low — all have become bhagavatas,
only Balarama Dasa is left out.[^11-78]

[^11-75]: Signature: "Balarama Dasa" ("vañcita valarāma dāse"). PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 283–284 (printed pp. 272–273), 21st pallava, no.
27 (label "॥২৭॥২২৪৪॥"); raga ramakeli; P-R-Sa MS no. 2349. GPT1 — p. 45, no. 63 (ramakeli); GPT2 — sec. 1.3, no. 63. In the
catalogue — BD-011; the same PK 2244 was wrongly given for YN-001, "praphullita kanaka-kamala mukhamaṇḍala" (that is GPT1 p. 118, no. 24,
signed "Vijayananda Dasa", in GPT2 "Yadunandana Dasa"; not in PK). The preceding PK 2243, "jīve emana dayā kothāo nā dekhi", is
signed "Vasudasa".
[^11-76]: GPT1: "seeing Him, their minds unsteady" (athira mana) instead of "their minds made steady" (suthira-mana).
[^11-77]: Gadadhara (Pandita), Svarupa Damodara, Ramananda Raya and Nityananda are the Lord's companions in Puri. Shripada is a
respectful address to a sannyasi: so the Lord called Nityananda. MSS "ka", "kha", "cha": "the Lord" (pahu) instead of "mind"
(mana): "the Lord cannot calm Himself"; "ka": "Ramananda", "Nityananda" (without case endings).
[^11-78]: A bhagavata is a devotee of the Lord. MSS "ka", "kha", "cha", P-R-Sa: "embracing the pandits" (paṇḍita) instead of "the
fallen" (patita).

## 21. Balarama Dasa — "āpanāra guṇa śuni āpanā pāsare…" (PK 2245)
*Hearing of His own qualities, Gaura forgets Himself: His saffron garments slip off, He embraces the fallen, weeping He
begs Nityananda for the dust of His feet, Nitai weeps "my brother!"; Gadadhara, Ramananda, Vasu, Srivasa, Mukunda and
Murari weep; young and old rejoice, beasts and birds weep. Raga varari.*[^11-79]

**21.1.** Hearing of His own qualities, He forgets Himself,
His saffron garment slips — He does not set it right.

**21.2.** For Him there are no quarters of the sky, no own and other:
clasping, clasping them, He weeps over the fallen and the low.[^11-80]

**21.3.** Crying "Shripada!", the Lord weeps aloud,
in hundreds of streams the tears pour from His lotus eyes.

**21.4.** Weeping, weeping, the Lord begs for the dust of His feet;
fallen on the ground, Nitai weeps, saying: "My brother, brother!"[^11-81]

**21.5.** Dear Gadadhara and Raya Ramananda weep,
seeing Gauranga's face, they cannot calm themselves.

**21.6.** Vasu, Srivasa, Mukunda and Murari weep;
in bliss all go along — children, old men, women.[^11-82]

**21.7.** Such an incarnation, brothers, I have seen nowhere:
the world is sunk in happiness, beasts and birds weep.

**21.8.** The blind, the deaf, the dull — all are in bliss,
Balarama Dasa alone of all is left out of this rasa.[^11-83]

[^11-79]: Signature: "Balarama Dasa." PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 284–285 (printed pp. 273–274), 21st pallava, no. 28 (label "॥২৮॥২২৪৫॥");
raga varari; P-R-Sa MS no. 2350. GPT1 — p. 45, no. 64, and p. 289, no. 40; GPT2 — sec. 1.3, no. 64, and 4.3, no. 40. The
catalogue (BD-012) listed it as "GPT only": the PK number was found on the scan.
[^11-80]: MS P-R-Sa: "for Him there are no quarters of the sky" (diga vidiga tāhe nāhi).
[^11-81]: In the humility of a devotee the Lord begs Nityananda for the dust of His feet, and Nityananda calls Him brother (cf.
CB Antya 5–6). GPT1 (p. 289): "fallen on the ground, He weeps: 'Nitai, Nitai, brother!'".
[^11-82]: Vasu is Vasu Ghosha or Vasudeva Datta; Srivasa, Mukunda (Datta) and Murari (Gupta) are companions from Navadvipa who
came to the Lord in Puri. MSS "ka", "kha", "cha", P-R-Sa: "Srinivasa" (śrīnivāsa); "as if" (yena) instead of "all" (yata).
[^11-83]: MS "gha": "such an incarnation I have never seen anywhere" (āra kabhu nāhi dekhi) in 21.7. GPT1: "only Balarama Dasa is left
out of this rasa" (valarāma dāsa mātra e rase vañcita).

## 22. Balarama Dasa — "prabhu kahe nityānanda sava jīva haila andha…" (PK 2261)
*The Lord sends Nityananda to Gauda: all souls have gone blind and have not received the name of Hari — let Nityananda
mercifully give the Name to everyone He sees: sinners, slanderers, disputants, students turned away from bhakti,
children, men and women — and flood Gauda with the prema of sankirtana. Raga varari.*[^11-84]

**22.1.** The Lord says: "Nityananda, all souls have gone blind,
no one has received the name of Hari.
I have one request of You: whomever You see with Your eyes,
mercifully make them repeat the Name.

**22.2.** Hardened sinners, the wicked, slanderers, the godless —
let not one of them be left out;
let souls not fear that Yama will come —
let them joyfully repeat the name of Hari.

**22.3.** Evil-minded disputants, low students,
turned away from bhakti birth after birth —
giving prema for Krishna to children, men and women,
free them all from suffering.

**22.4.** Flood the land of Gauda with the prema and rasa of sankirtana,
fulfil the hope of all."
Whom such an incarnation of mercy did not save —
what can Balarama Dasa do?[^11-85]

[^11-84]: Signature: "Balarama Dasa." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 290 (printed p. 279), 21st pallava, section "tatra nityānandacandrasya
gauṛe preraṇaṃ yathā" (the sending of Nityananda to Gauda), no. 44 (label "॥৪৪॥২২৬১॥"); raga varari; P-R-Sa MS no. 2366. GPT1 —
pp. 403–404, no. 6 (varari); GPT2 — sec. 5.5, no. 6. The catalogue (BD-026) listed it as "GPT only": the PK number was found
on the scan. Cf. CC Madhya 15 (the Lord sends Nityananda to preach in Gauda), CB Antya 5.
[^11-85]: MS "kha": "give" (diha) instead of "make them repeat" (laoyāive) in 22.1; "gha": pāṣaṇḍi; "ka": "flooded" (bhāsāila); "kha":
karā.

## 23. Balarama Dasa — "virale nitāi pāñā…" (PK 2262; fuller in GPT1)
*The Lord alone with Nityananda: "Go to the bank of the Suradhuni and, taking pity on souls, give them the name of Hari; I
have come to give away the Name and prema at Advaita's call, and You are My chief helper; having delivered Nilachala, I
shall go south with Govinda — You hasten to Gauda." Raga varari.*[^11-86]

**23.1.** Finding Nitai alone, taking His hand and seating Him,
the Lord softly speaks sweet words to Him:
"Taking pity on souls, go and make them repeat the name of Hari —
go, Nitai, to the bank of the Suradhuni."

**23.2.** "To give away the Name and prema, at Advaita's thunderous call
I have descended to earth;
to save the souls of the Kali age, to bring them good —
You are My chief helper."[^11-87]

**23.3.** "Having delivered Nilachala, taking Govinda with Me,
I shall go to the southern country;
the charge of Sri Gauda-mandala — preaching the Name —
quickly, Nitai, go there Yourself."[^11-88]

**23.4.** "What I cannot do, You will be able to do:
You are the giver of prema, the most merciful."
Balarama says: Lords, You both are equal —
deliver me: I am but a beggar.[^11-89]

[^11-86]: PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 291 (printed p. 280), 21st pallava, no. 45 (label "॥৪৫॥২২৬২॥"); the same raga (varari); P-R-Sa MS no.
2367. PK has only the first stanza (23.1), **without a signature**; Ray notes that in the P-R-Sa MS the next pada, PK 2263
("caitanya-ādeśa pāiyā…", signed Premadasa), is written as the end of this one, and thinks this right, but in MSS "ka", "kha",
"gha", "cha" they are separate. The full text with Balarama's signature is in GPT1, p. 404, no. 7 (varari); 23.2–23.4 are
translated from GPT1 (scan PDF p. 663). Attribution C. In the catalogue — BD-027.
[^11-87]: Advaita called on the Lord to appear for the deliverance of the world (CC Adi 3; CB Adi 2).
[^11-88]: Govinda is perhaps Kala Krishnadasa or Govinda, the Lord's servant; according to CC (Madhya 7) the Lord went south with
Kala Krishnadasa and sent Nityananda to Gauda later (Madhya 15) — the poet tells the events differently; we translate
faithfully to the author.
[^11-89]: "You both are equal" — dom̐hāra samāna duhum̐: Gaura and Nitai are equally merciful.

## 24. Kanu Dasa — "nadīyā nagare gelā nityānanda rāya…" (PK 2264)
*Nityananda comes to Nadia and falls at Shachi's feet; embracing Him, she weeps; He consoles her with talk of Gauranga:
"Your son is well and happy, He sent me to see you and bowed many times to your feet: Gauranga is bound by your love."
Raga suhai.*[^11-90]

**24.1.** Nityananda Raya came to the town of Nadia,
fell like a rod at the feet of Mother Shachi.

**24.2.** Embracing Him, Shachi weeps piteously,
the tears from her eyes soak her garments.

**24.3.** Crying out, crying out, she weeps with an anguished heart —
with talk of Gauranga He consoles her.

**24.4.** Nityananda says: "Mother, calm your heart:
your son is well and happy.

**24.5.** He sent me to see you,
many times He bowed to your feet."

**24.6.** Kanu Dasa says: "Mother, this I tell you:
Gauranga Gosani is bound by your love."[^11-91]

[^11-90]: Signature: "Kanu Dasa" ("kānudāsa kahe"). PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 291 (printed p. 280), 21st pallava, no. 47 (label
"॥৪৭॥২২৬৪॥"); raga suhai; P-R-Sa MS no. 2368. GPT1 — pp. 404–405, no. 10 (suhai); GPT2 — sec. 5.5, no. 10. In the catalogue —
KD-008. Cf. CB Antya 5–6 (Nityananda in Navadvipa with Shachi).
[^11-91]: Kanu Dasa's words continue Nityananda's speech. GPT1: "pāṭhāiyā dilā", "karilā" (honorific forms) in 24.5.

## 25. Krishnadasa — "ciradine gorācām̐dera ānanda apāra…" (PK 2018)
*After long separation — Gorachand's boundless bliss: He tells the devotees of His former pastimes, His body is covered
with thrills, like a kadamba bud with golden filaments; hearing the words from His lips, the devotees are consoled. In
GPT1 it stands among the padas on the Lord's return to the devotees of Nadia.*[^11-92]

**25.1.** After a long time boundless is Gorachand's bliss:
He tells the devotees of His former pastimes.[^11-93]

**25.2.** From head to foot His body is filled with thrills —
like a kadamba bud with golden filaments.

**25.3.** His heart is full of bhava, His speech falters:
after so much striving Providence has fulfilled the hope.[^11-94]

**25.4.** Gora, the son of Shachi, is our honour, life and wealth:
hearing the words from His moon-like lips, the heart is consoled.

**25.5.** Whoever has come to faith in Gorachand's pastimes —
wretched Krishnadasa is the servant of his servants.

[^11-92]: Signature: "Krishnadasa" ("dukhī kṛṣṇadāsa"). PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 201 (printed p. 190), opening of the 15th pallava,
section "atha samṛddhimat-sambhogasya rasodgāraḥ — tatra śrīgauracandro yathā" (a gaura-chandrika to Radha's account of full union
after separation), no. 1 (label "॥১॥২০১৮॥"); no raga given. GPT1 — p. 413, no. 32 (shri), right after Vasu Ghosha's pada
"āola nadīyāra loka gaurāṅga dekhite" (chapter 1, no. 23). In the catalogue (KR-003) the pada was listed under nagari-bhava (by
the GPT2 section 3.2) without a first line — it is not a nagari pada. Which Krishnadasa wrote it has not been established
(C).
[^11-93]: "Former pastimes" — puraba-vihāra: Krishna's pastimes in Vraja (in PK the pada introduces Radha's account of Her union
with Krishna).
[^11-94]: It can also be understood as the words of the Lord Himself in Radha's bhava: "after so much striving Providence has
fulfilled My hope." MSS "ka", "kha": jine ("outshining") instead of janu ("like") in 25.2.

---

# Chapter 12. Vasu Ghosha: Padas from the *Gaura-pada-tarangini* — Appearance and Childhood, Sannyasa, the Lament of Nadia, Nilachala

*This chapter opens the group of padas known only from the *Gaura-pada-tarangini* (GPT1 — 1st ed. by Jagadbandhu
Bhadra, 1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934), excluding padas in nagari-bhava. Here are padas signed by Vasu (Vasudeva) Ghosha, in
the order of the lilas: praise of the Gaura-avatara; Gauranga's appearance on the night of the lunar eclipse, the
name-giving, His first steps and "the moon from the sky"; the Lord's morning in Navadvipa and the jhulana; Vishnupriya's
forebodings, the sannyasa at Katwa, the lament of Shachi and the devotees, the Lord with Advaita in Shantipura and His
departure for Nilachala; the lament of Shachi and Vishnupriya; the Lord in Nilachala, His bhava of Radha, and the festival
at Shrikhanda. Two padas were found in the *Padakalpataru* (PK) without a signature (nos. 1 and 15) — there the text
follows PK; no. 27 is an abridged recension of a pada by Govinda Dasa (PK 1463). Ten padas (nos. 1, 3–5, 9–12, 14, 17) were
missing from the stage-1 catalogue: they were found in a full check of the signatures of GPT1 (the catalogue section on Vasu
Ghosha has been supplemented). Majumdar considers the GPT unreliable for attributing padas to Vasu Ghosha: Jagadbandhu included spurious
ones as well; the childhood padas he regards as the poet's invention, and the festival at Shrikhanda (no. 29) and the
pada about Svarupa (no. 28) as forgeries. The attribution of all the padas of this chapter is therefore provisional. The
Bengali original, the variants of GPT1/GPT2 and PK, and the word-for-word translation are in the full version of the book.*

## 1. Vasu Ghosha — "avatāra vaṛa avatāra kailā vaṛa…" (PK 2347; GPT1 no. 68)
*Praise of the Gaura-avatara: there was no such mercy in any yuga; in every house there is the weeping of prema, the
name of Hari is proclaimed; Gaura has brought a boat laden with prema to the landing and opened a market; Jagai and
Madhai are saved by the name.*[^12-1]

**1.1.** A great incarnation, a great incarnation You have made!
Such mercy You have shown in no other yuga.

**1.2.** In every house the weeping of prema is heard;
in the age of Kali the name of Hari is proclaimed.[^12-2]

**1.3.** To the landing of the ocean of happiness You have brought a boat full of prema;
a fine market You have opened, Gaura — with wares of prema![^12-3]

**1.4.** Jagai and Madhai — they were two brothers:
by the name of Hari Chaitanya Gosani saved them.[^12-4]

**1.5.** Vasudeva Ghosha says: there will be no other such;
in the age of Kali blessed is the name — the jewel Chaitanya.

[^12-1]: PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 320 (printed p. 309), 4th shakha, last pada of the 23rd pallava (mark "॥১৬॥২৩৪৭॥"), MS P-R-Sa
no. 2451 — **without a signature** (in PK the pada ends at 1.4; it is preceded by PK 2346, signed by Balarama Dasa). GPT1 —
pp. 46–47, no. 68 (raga yatharaga), with the closing couplet 1.5 — the signature of Vasudeva Ghosha; GPT2 — sec. 1.3,
no. 68. Text of 1.1–1.4 follows PK, 1.5 follows GPT. The attribution to Vasu Ghosha is known only from GPT (a new catalogue
entry, VG-154). The first line reads differently in the PK manuscripts and in GPT ("avatāra kailā vaṛa vaṛa" etc.), see the full version of the book.
[^12-2]: "The weeping of prema" (premera kāndanā) — tears of love for God in kirtana, not worldly grief. The name of Hari as the
dharma of the age of Kali — CC Adi 3, 17.
[^12-3]: Images of trade: the boat (bharā — a boat's cargo; in the PK manuscripts bhārā, "load") comes in to the landing, and Gaura
opens a market (hāṭa) whose "wares" are prema, given away freely. Cf. the padas about the "market" of Nityananda and Gaura
(hāṭa-pattana).
[^12-4]: Jagai and Madhai — the villainous brothers of Navadvipa, saved by the Lord and Nityananda (CB Madhya 13; CC Adi 17).

## 2. Vasu Ghosha — "nadīyā-ākāśe āsi udila gaurāṅga-śaśī…" (GPT1 p. 51, no. 3)
*The appearance of Gauranga: in the sky of Nadia the moon Gauranga has risen, and the moon of the sky, out of shame,
has smeared its face with soot — the eclipse; conches and drums sound in every house; Jagannatha Mishra and Shachi are
beside themselves with joy; in the darkness of the eclipse gods mingle with men, celestial women together with the women
of Nadia gaze at the Child; the father gives gifts to the poor. Raga kalyana.*[^12-5]

**2.1.** In the sky of Nadia a moon has risen — Gauranga,
and all are drowned in delight;
and the moon of the sky, out of shame, has smeared its face with soot,
seizing the moment — as if in an eclipse.[^12-6]

**2.2.** The women cry aloud: "Jaya, jaya!" —
in every house bells and conches sound;
kettledrums, drums, gongs, shehnais, horns and flutes,
turi and bheri trumpets and the great victory drum.[^12-7]

**2.3.** Jagannatha Mishra is immersed in great bliss,
Shachi's joy knows no bounds:
seeing Nimai's face, she has forgotten the pains of childbirth
and, unblinking, gazes at her son's face.[^12-8]

**2.4.** In the darkness of the eclipse no one recognizes anyone —
gods have mingled with men;
together with the women of Nadia, celestial women, coming joyfully,
behold the beauty of Gauranga.[^12-9]

**2.5.** Gazing at his son's face, Jagannatha, overjoyed,
gives gifts to all the poor.
The world is full of bliss — the moon Gaura has risen:
this, says Vasu, is the fruit of the good fortune of living beings.

[^12-5]: GPT1 — p. 51, no. 3 (raga kalyana), checked against the scan (PDF pp. 310–311); GPT2 — sec. 2.1, no. 3. The pada is not in
PK, BR, KGC or PS. The preceding pada of GPT (no. 2, "jaya jaya kalarava nadiyā nagare") is PK 1121, translated in chapter 7 (no. 6).
Majumdar regards Vasu's padas on the Lord's birth and childhood as the poet's invention: Vasu was not in Navadvipa at that
time (and the attribution of this pada is moreover known only from GPT). The Lord's appearance on the phalguna purnima
during a lunar eclipse, when everyone was chanting the name of Hari — CC Adi 13; CB Adi 2.
[^12-6]: A play of images: the moon Gauranga has eclipsed the moon of the sky, and it has hidden its face "out of shame" — this is
how the poet explains the eclipse on the night of the Lord's appearance.
[^12-7]: The shehnai (sānāi) is a wind instrument like an oboe; the bheur (bhem̐uṛa) is a horn; the turi and bheri are trumpets.
[^12-8]: The Lord's appearance is not the birth of a conditioned soul: He comes by His own will, in His eternal form, and Mother
Shachi, like Devaki and Yashoda, only in the sweetness of love experiences it as the birth of a son (CC Adi 13; Bhag. 10.3).
The words about "the pains of childbirth" convey her motherly experience in the humanlike lila.
[^12-9]: "The women of Nadia" (nadīyā-nāgarī) here are simply townswomen who came to see the Child, not "nagaris" in the sense of
nagari-bhava. The gods who came in human guise to see the newborn Lord — CB Adi 2.

## 3. Vasu Ghosha — "miśra purandara kichu mane vicāriyā…" (GPT1 p. 62, no. 1)
*The name-giving: Purandara Mishra calls the family priest and gives him gifts, and the priest places the arghya and his
blessing on the Child's head; Shachi asks that her son be given the name "Nimai". Raga suhai.*[^12-10]

**3.1.** Purandara Mishra, having considered something,
called to him the family priest, the best of brahmanas.

**3.2.** Wealth, jewels and ornaments he gave to the brahmana;
the brahmana, pronouncing his blessing, accepted the gift.

**3.3.** The arghya and the blessing the brahmana took in his own hands
and gladly placed them on Gorachand's head.[^12-11]

**3.4.** Shachi Thakurani began to speak:
"Providence has given me this son — He is to me as seven sons.[^12-12]

**3.5.** Give Him the name 'Nimai', O best of brahmanas!" —
so, joining his palms, says Vasudeva Ghosha.

[^12-10]: GPT1 — p. 62, section "Childhood pastimes" (vālyalīlā), no. 1 (raga suhai), checked against the scan (PDF p. 321); GPT2 —
sec. 2.2, no. 1. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS; it was missing from the catalogue (new entry VG-155). On Majumdar's view
of Vasu's padas on the Lord's childhood — note 5. Purandara is another name of Jagannatha Mishra. According to CB (Adi 3–4)
and CC (Adi 13–14), the name "Nimai" was given to the Child by the women (born under a nim tree — as a protection), while
at the name-giving ceremony the brahmanas named Him Vishvambhara; in the poem it is Shachi herself who asks for the name
"Nimai".
[^12-11]: Arghya — a respectful offering (water, rice, durva grass); here it is placed on the child's head as a blessing.
[^12-12]: "sāta putrera ei putra" — lit. "this son is (as) seven sons": an expression of the priceless worth of an only child. It may
also allude to the children Shachi lost before the Lord's appearance (according to CC Adi 13 — eight daughters).

## 4. Vasu Ghosha — "māyera aṅguli dhari śiśu gaurahari…" (GPT1 p. 63, no. 6)
*The first steps: holding His mother's finger, little Gaurahari toddles step by step, pulls her by the hand, stumbles and
falls; Shachi wants to take Him in her arms, but He, being stubborn, rolls on the ground; the mother wipes Him and kisses
Him. Raga beloar (tala dashakoshi).*[^12-13]

**4.1.** Holding His mother's finger, the child Gaurahari
toddles forward step by step.

**4.2.** Pulling His mother by the hand, He suddenly walks faster —
and, before going half a step, stumbles and falls.

**4.3.** Mother Shachi, brushing off the dust, goes to take Him in her arms —
but Gora, throwing a tantrum, rolls on the ground.

**4.4.** Saying "ah, ah", the mother wipes Him with the end of her sari,
takes Him in her arms and kisses the lotus of His face.

**4.5.** Vasu says: this child will roll in the dust —
how long, mother, will you hold Him back out of tenderness?[^12-14]

[^12-13]: GPT1 — p. 63, no. 6 (raga beloar, tala dashakoshi), checked against the scan (PDF p. 322); GPT2 — sec. 2.2, no. 6. The pada
is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS; new catalogue entry VG-156. The neighbouring GPT padas (nos. 2–5) are PK 1141, 1161, 1150, 1151
(translated in chapter 7, nos. 8–11). On Majumdar's view — note 5.
[^12-14]: The Lord's childhood play in the dust — CB Adi 4; Murari 1.6. The sweetness of these pastimes lies in Shachi's motherly
love (vatsalya), which keeps her from seeing her Son's majesty.

## 5. Vasu Ghosha — "pūrṇimā-rajanī cām̐da gagane udaya…" (GPT1 pp. 63–64, no. 7)
*The moon from the sky: on the night of the full moon little Nimai, seeing the moon, cries: "Give me the moon, mother!";
the moon does not come, and in despair He falls in the dust; Shachi gives Him a picture of Radha and Krishna — and He is
happy: in it, says the poet, the Lord sees His own face. Raga beloar (tala dashakoshi).*[^12-15]

**5.1.** On the night of the full moon the moon rose in the sky;
seeing the moon, Gorachand rejoiced in His heart.

**5.2.** "Give me the moon, mother!" — the child cries aloud;
raising her hand, Shachi calls: "Come, moon, come!"

**5.3.** The cruel moon does not come — Nimai is distraught:
weeping, He falls in the dust and tears His hair.

**5.4.** In Mishra's house there was a picture of Radha and Krishna:
to soothe her son, Shachi gave it into His hands.

**5.5.** Getting the picture, Gorachand rejoiced with all His heart;
Vasu says: in the picture, Lord, You behold Your own face.[^12-16]

[^12-15]: GPT1 — pp. 63–64, no. 7 (raga beloar, tala dashakoshi), checked against the scan (PDF pp. 322–323); GPT2 — sec. 2.2, no. 7.
The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS; new catalogue entry VG-157. On Majumdar's view — note 5. The child asking for the moon is
a well-known motif of Krishna's childhood pastimes as well (cf. the story of the moon in a bowl of water).
[^12-16]: The sense of the signature: Gaura is Krishna Himself, who has taken the bhava and complexion of Radha (CC Adi 1.5; 4);
therefore in the picture of Radha and Krishna He sees Himself: in the Child's play the poet reveals the secret of Gaura — Radha and Krishna in one form (cf. the
verse of Svarupa Damodara, CC Adi 1.5).

## 6. Vasu Ghosha — "uṭha uṭha gorācām̐da niśi pohāila…" (GPT1 p. 347, no. 11)
*The awakening of Gaura: the night is over, Nadia has woken, the cuckoo is calling, the dawn has risen, the lotuses have
opened — how long will You sleep, Gora, in the languor of prema? Raga dhanashi.*[^12-17]

**6.1.** Rise, rise, Gorachand — the night is over;
all the people of Nadia have woken and risen.

**6.2.** The cuckoo calls "kuhu" — how charming its voice;
how long will You sleep, O Gora, jewel of virtues?

**6.3.** The dawn has risen, the lotuses have opened;
the moon has left the abode of the night lilies.[^12-18]

**6.4.** Vasudeva Ghosha, with joy in his heart, says:
how long will You sleep, Gora, in the languor of prema?

[^12-17]: GPT1 — p. 347, section "the eight periods of the day" (ashtakaliya), no. 11 (raga dhanashi); GPT2 — sec. 5.2, no. 11. The
pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS. Ashtakaliya songs are a meditation on the Lord's daily pastimes hour by hour; Majumdar
does not discuss such padas.
[^12-18]: The night lilies (kumudini) open under the moon and close at dawn; the lotuses do the opposite.

## 7. Vasu Ghosha — "vāyasa kokilakula ghughu dahiyāla-rava…" (GPT1 p. 351, no. 24)
*Morning and bath: the birds call, the companions call Gora; He rises, rubs His eyes, performs the morning duties, slowly
anoints Himself with fragrant oil and goes with everyone to the Ganga. Raga dhanashi.*[^12-19]

**7.1.** Crows, cuckoos, doves and magpie-robins are calling,
and together with them all the companions call Him.

**7.2.** Casting off drowsiness, Gora rises from His bed,
rubs His eyes with His hands and looks all around.

**7.3.** Having finished the morning duties with His companions,
Gora slowly anoints His body with fragrant oil.

**7.4.** Anointed with oil, they all go toward the Ganga;
Vasu Ghosha joyfully sings the lila of bathing.

[^12-19]: GPT1 — p. 351, section ashtakaliya, no. 24 (raga dhanashi); GPT2 — sec. 5.2, no. 24. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS.
The next GPT pada (no. 25, "jalakeli gorācām̐dera manete paṛila", the water play) is PK 1108, translated in chapter 5 (no. 7). The
dahiyal (dahiyāla) is the magpie-robin (Copsychus saularis), a songbird of Bengal.

## 8. Vasu Ghosha — "jhulata gorācām̐da sundara raṅgiyā…" (GPT1 p. 326, no. 17)
*Jhulana: Gorachand swings on the swing, overflowing with prema; in the bhava of Radha tears stream down His face;
understanding His bhava, Gadadhara swings at His left; "The flute!" Gora exclaims, gazing into his face. Raga
dhanashi.*[^12-20]

**8.1.** Gorachand swings, beautiful and joyous,
overflowing with the fullness of prema.

**8.2.** In the bhava of Radha streams of tears flood His face;
understanding His bhava, Gadadhara swings at His left.[^12-21]

**8.3.** "The flute!" He exclaims, gazing into Gadadhara's face;
Vasu Ghosha sings, remembering Gora's qualities.

[^12-20]: GPT1 — p. 326, section "festivals of the year", no. 17 (raga dhanashi), checked against the scan (PDF p. 585); GPT2 —
sec. 5.1, no. 17. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS. Vasu's other pada on the jhulana (PK 1550, where Gaura sits on the
swing with Gadadhara; according to Majumdar, an eyewitness testimony) is translated in chapter 4 (no. 5). Jhulana is the
swing festival of Radha and Krishna in the month of shravana.
[^12-21]: The bhava of Radha is pure prema, Radha's love for Krishna; in it the Lord tastes the sweetness of His own love (CC Adi 4).
The left side is Radha's place beside Krishna; Gadadhara, the Lord's eternal companion, understands His mood. The cry "The
flute!" is a remembrance of Krishna's flute that has seized the Lord in this bhava.

## 9. Vasu Ghosha — "viṣṇupriyā saṅginīre pāiyā virale…" (GPT1 p. 367, no. 4)
*Vishnupriya's foreboding: alone with a friend, she says that Nadia seems desolate to her today, the right side of her
body twitches, her earring has fallen, on the bank of the Suradhuni the trees have wilted, the current has stopped, the cuckoo
is silent; the poet fears that Gora may leave Navadvipa. Raga dhanashi.*[^12-22]

**9.1.** Vishnupriya, finding her friend alone,
with an anxious heart, faltering, says:

**9.2.** "Why does Nadia seem desolate to me today?
There is no ease in my body, both my eyes weep.

**9.3.** The right side of my body twitches, my right eye;
my earring has slipped and fallen.[^12-23]

**9.4.** On the bank of the Suradhuni the trees and creepers have wilted,
the bees do not drink honey, the leaves have withered.

**9.5.** Why has the current of the Jahnavi stopped?
The cuckoo is not heard — as if it had grown mute."

**9.6.** A great fear has settled in Vasu's heart:
lest Gora, the king of brahmanas, leave Navadvipa!

[^12-22]: GPT1 — p. 367, section "sannyasa", no. 4 (raga dhanashi), checked against the scan (PDF p. 626). In the scan of GPT2 (IA
340178) p. 235 (end of sec. 5.2) is followed by p. 236, which begins with the end of no. 8 of sec. 5.3: padas nos. 1–8
(including this one and the next) are missing from it. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS; new catalogue entry VG-158. The
neighbouring GPT padas are on the same theme (no. 3 — Govinda Ghosha, no. 5 — Madhava).
[^12-23]: According to folk belief, the twitching of the right eye and the right side of the body is an ill omen for a woman.

## 10. Vasu Ghosha — "pāgalinī viṣṇupriyā bhijā vastra cule…" (GPT1 p. 367, no. 6)
*Vishnupriya, as if distraught, runs home in wet clothes and, weeping, tells Shachi of the ill omens: while she was
bathing her nose ring fell into the water, her right eye twitches, she keeps seeing a snake on her right; the poet: today
the lord of your life will leave Navadvipa. Raga dhanashi.*[^12-24]

**10.1.** Vishnupriya, as if distraught, with wet clothes and wet hair,
hurriedly comes home and speaks to her mother-in-law —

**10.2.** but she cannot say anything, breathless with weeping.
Shachi says: "My dear, why are you so distressed?"

**10.3.** Vishnupriya says: "What more can I say, mother?
On all sides there are ill omens — my soul trembles.

**10.4.** As I was bathing, my nose ring fell into the water:
my fortune will break, a thunderbolt will fall on my head.[^12-25]

**10.5.** Again and again my soul weeps, my right eye twitches,
on my right I keep seeing as if a snake."

**10.6.** Weeping, Vasu Ghosha says: "What shall I say, O faithful wife?
Today the lord of your life will leave Navadvipa."

[^12-24]: GPT1 — p. 367, no. 6 (raga dhanashi), checked against the scan (PDF p. 626); missing from the GPT2 scan (note 22). The pada is
not in PK, BR, KGC or PS; new catalogue entry VG-159. The night before the Lord's departure and Vishnupriya's grief — CC Adi 17;
CB Madhya 25–26; in Lochana — Madhya-khanda.
[^12-25]: The nose ring (veśara) is a sign of a married woman; its loss is an ill omen for the husband.

## 11. Vasu Ghosha — "prabhu kahe nijaguṇe deota sannyāsa…" (GPT1 p. 369, no. 11)
*Katwa: the Lord asks Keshava Bharati to give Him sannyasa; the people of Katwa try to dissuade Him, Bharati recalls
that the scriptures allow sannyasa after fifty; the Lord replies: if death comes earlier, when will there be the company
of saints? Bharati agrees, the barber is called; he does not dare touch the Lord's head — the Lord tells him to give up
his trade and promises him a happy life by Krishna's grace. Raga shri.*[^12-26]

**11.1.** The Lord says: "By your grace give Me sannyasa!"
— "Do not become a sannyasi, Nimai, do not shave Your hair!" —

**11.2.** so all the people of Kanchana-nagara try to dissuade Him:
"Do not take sannyasa, dear child, go back home!"[^12-27]

**11.3.** "When one is past fifty and the passions have ceased,
only then do the scriptures allow sannyasa to be given."[^12-28]

**11.4.** Hearing this, the Lord speaks thus:
"What do I know to say before you, O guru?

**11.5.** If death should come before fifty,
when then will there be the company of saints?"

**11.6.** Hearing this, Bharati Gosani says:
"I will give You sannyasa — listen, Nimai!"

**11.7.** Hearing this, the Lord was filled with joy and delight;
then they called the barber to shave His head.

**11.8.** The barber says: "Master, I humbly submit:
there is no such person in the three worlds!

**11.9.** Having touched Your head with my hand, whose feet shall I touch then?
Say what you will, Master — my whole body trembles.

**11.10.** Touching whose feet shall I now shave every day?
I am a barber of low caste — such is my custom."[^12-29]

**11.11.** Hearing this, Vishvambhara Raya speaks,
the Lord says: "Do not follow your trade any longer.

**11.12.** By Krishna's grace you will pass your life in happiness,
and at the end your way will lead to the abode of Vishnu."

**11.13.** The people of Kanchana-nagara are kind-hearted;
Vasu Ghosha, with joined palms, speaks to Bharati…

[^12-26]: GPT1 — p. 369, section "sannyasa", no. 11 (raga shri), checked against the scan (PDF p. 628); GPT2 — p. 236, sec. 5.3, no. 11
(scan PDF p. 525). The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS; new catalogue entry VG-160. The preceding GPT pada (no. 10, "kāñcana nagare
eka vṛkṣa manohara", with the double signature of Krishnadasa and Vasu) is PK 2223 (VG-136), translated in chapter 4 (no. 12). The sannyasa at
Katwa — CB Madhya 28; CC Adi 17, Madhya 3; Lochana, Madhya-khanda; Murari 2.18. Keshava Bharati is the Lord's sannyasa-guru.
[^12-27]: Kanchana-nagara is Katwa (Kantaka-nagara) on the Ganga, where the Lord took sannyasa.
[^12-28]: Apparently the words of Keshava Bharati (GPT1 gives them in quotation marks without naming the speaker): sannyasa was usually
taken in old age, after the stages of grihastha and vanaprastha. The Lord's answer (11.4–11.5) is the word of a man seeking sannyasa: the Lord, who teaches by His own
example, speaks of the brevity of human life, not of Himself — time has no power over Him.
[^12-29]: The barber's trade is shaving and paring nails, touching people's feet; having touched the Lord's head, he can no longer
touch the feet of others (the same motif in Lochana, where the barber is called Haridasa (in the 1983 ed.), and in Govinda's *Karcha*, where he is
Deva).

## 12. Vasu Ghosha — "madhuśīla vale gosāñi nā bhām̐ṛāo more…" (GPT1 p. 369, no. 12)
*Continuation: the barber Madhushil says to the Lord: "Do not deceive me — I know You are God Himself; I shall do Your
will, but first place Your feet on my head"; the Lord places His foot on his head. Raga shri.*[^12-30]

**12.1.** Madhushil says: "Gosani, do not deceive me:
You are Brahma, You are Vishnu — I know it in my heart.[^12-31]

**12.2.** I shall fulfil Your wish — You are all-powerful;
I shall obey Your order without doubt.

**12.3.** You say: by Krishna's grace I shall live happily,
and after death my way will lead to the abode of Vishnu.

**12.4.** The Krishna who will keep me in happiness — that is You;
Your feet are my abode of Vishnu: what else do I know?

**12.5.** I shall shave Your curly hair, I shall touch Your head with my hand —
but first, Lord, place Your holy feet on my head."

**12.6.** At these sweet words the Lord placed His foot on his head —
the foot, says Vasu, before which the post of Brahma is trifling.

[^12-30]: GPT1 — p. 369, no. 12 (raga shri), checked against the scan (PDF p. 628); GPT2 — p. 236, sec. 5.3, no. 12. The pada is not in
PK, BR, KGC or PS; new catalogue entry VG-161. The barber's name is Madhushil (madhuśīla; Shil is a surname of the barber caste).
[^12-31]: "You are Brahma, You are Vishnu" — the simple words of a barber who has recognized God in the Lord; according to Gaudiya
teaching Gaura is Krishna Himself, the Supreme Lord, the source of both Vishnu and Brahma (CC Adi 2) — which the barber himself
says in 12.4: "that Krishna is You".

## 13. Vasu Ghosha — "prabhura muṇḍana dekhi kānde yata paśu pākhī…" (GPT1 p. 370, no. 15)
*After the shaving: beasts, birds and people weep, a cow runs to the Lord with grass in her teeth, all stand silent like
trees; the Lord, in kaupina and with staff, asks the Vaishnavas to bless Him so that His sannyasa may not become a mockery
and He may attain the Lord of Vraja in Vraja, and runs crying "Where is Vrindavana?" through the land of Rarh, with
Nityananda beside Him. Raga pahida.*[^12-32]

**13.1.** Seeing the Lord shaven, all the beasts and birds weep,
all the dwellers of the holy place weep;[^12-33]
the calf does not drink milk, the cow, with grass in her teeth,
runs and gazes at Gauranga's face.

**13.2.** People stand looking at Gauranga's face —
no one can utter a word;
tears flow from both eyes as they gaze at Gauranga's face —
all beings have become still as trees.

**13.3.** Putting on the cord and kaupina, with shaven head,
leaving maya, He has become detached;[^12-34]
He sits, overflowing with prema, taking the staff in His hand,
and says: "I am poor and lowly.

**13.4.** You, the best of Vaishnavas, give Me this blessing,
placing both hands on My head:
I have taken sannyasa — may it not become a mockery;
may I, going to Vraja, attain the Lord of Vraja!"[^12-35]

**13.5.** Saying this, Gora Raya runs in prema with His face upturned
and weeps: "Where is Vrindavana?"
The Lord wanders through the land of Rarh, Nityananda beside Him;
Vasu Ghosha weeps aloud.[^12-36]

[^12-32]: GPT1 — pp. 370–371, section "sannyasa", no. 15 (raga pahida), checked against the scan (PDF p. 629); GPT2 — sec. 5.3, no. 15.
The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS. The couplet about the blessing (13.4) coincides almost word for word with Vasu's pada PK 2225
(VG-059; chapter 4, no. 13), which Majumdar considers part of the historical cycle "Nimai-sannyasa": this is a "double" of that
pada, known only from GPT.
[^12-33]: śrīnivāsī — lit. "dwellers of Shri (the holy place)"; the sense of the word is unclear (perhaps the people of Katwa or of
Nadia).
[^12-34]: "Leaving maya" — here "maya" in the everyday sense: family, home, worldly attachments that the Lord leaves on taking
sannyasa; the Lord Himself is never under the power of maya. The word "ḍuri" after "shaven head" is unclear (omitted in the
translation).
[^12-35]: The Lord, taking the role of a devotee, prays for a blessing — to attain Krishna; cf. CC Madhya 3 (the verse of the Avanti
brahmana, which the Lord recites on taking sannyasa).
[^12-36]: After the sannyasa the Lord wandered for three days in a trance through the land of Rarh, seeking Vrindavana, and Nityananda
led Him to the Ganga and to Shantipura — CC Madhya 3; CB Antya 1.

## 14. Vasu Ghosha — "gaurāṅge sannyāsa diyā bhāratī kām̐dilā…" (GPT1 p. 371, no. 18)
*Having given Gauranga sannyasa and the name Sri Krishna Chaitanya, Keshava Bharati weeps; the Lord asks him for the
blessing of love for Krishna, and Bharati replies: "You are my guru, I see Krishna in You; only for the sake of worldly
custom do You call me guru." Raga dhanashi.*[^12-37]

**14.1.** Having given Gauranga sannyasa, Bharati wept;
the name "Sri Krishna Chaitanya" he gave to Nimai.

**14.2.** The Lord says: "My guru, fulfil the desire of My heart:
bless Me, that My mind may be in Krishna."

**14.3.** Bharati, weeping, says: "You are my guru;
what blessing shall I give? I see Krishna.

**14.4.** You bewilder the whole world, You are the master of every play;
only to keep up worldly custom do You call me guru.[^12-38]

**14.5.** My sannyasa has today borne fruit!"
Vasu says: "I have seen the lotus feet."

[^12-37]: GPT1 — p. 371, no. 18 (raga dhanashi); GPT2 — sec. 5.3, no. 18. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS; new catalogue entry
VG-162. The name "Sri Krishna Chaitanya" — CC Madhya 3, CB Madhya 28; cf. Govinda's *Karcha*, where Bharati inwardly recognizes the Lord as God.
[^12-38]: "You bewilder the world" (bhuvana bhulāo) — of the lila of the Lord, who hides His majesty in the role of a devotee and a disciple;
"the master of every play" (nāṭera guru) — He Himself arranges His lila. This is not "maya" over the Lord: by His own will He shows
the form of a sannyasi in order to teach the world.

## 15. Vasu Ghosha — "svapane giyāchilum̐ kṣīroda-sāyare…" (PK 2269; GPT1 no. 25)
*Shachi's lament: in a dream she went to the ocean of milk, but even there did not find the treasure of virtues; she set up
a market, but fate did not let her trade; where did Keshava Bharati in sannyasi garb come from? She raised her son to be a
pandit — who has taken Him away to a distant land? Shachi calls: "Nimai, come!" Raga pahida.*[^12-39]

**15.1.** "In a dream I went to the ocean of milk —
and even there I did not find the treasure of virtues;
I set up a market — but I was not let to trade:
Providence has turned against me.[^12-40]

**15.2.** From where did this Keshava Bharati come
in the garb of a sannyasi?
I taught Him, instructed Him, raised Him a pandit —
who, then, has taken Him away to a distant land?"

**15.3.** *(Refrain)* Mother Shachi calls: "Nimai, come!"

**15.4.** "My treasure, (come back) to the empty house!"
Vasu Ghosha says: "That Gorachand is the mother's life."[^12-41]

[^12-39]: PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 293 (printed p. 282), 21st pallava "The sannyasa of Sri Gauranga etc.", no. 52 (mark "॥৫২॥২২৬৯॥"), MS P-R-Sa
no. 2373 — **without a signature**, with the refrain "śacī māya ḍāke nimāi āya re"; in MS P-R-Sa the refrain is longer: "…what has he
plotted with Bharati — he goes away, killing his mother." GPT1 — p. 374, no. 25 (raga pahida), checked against the scan (PDF
p. 633); GPT2 — sec. 5.3, no. 25: with a closing line and Vasu's signature (15.4). Text of 15.1–15.3 follows PK, 15.4 follows GPT.
The attribution to Vasu is known only from GPT.
[^12-40]: The ocean of milk (Kshiroda) is the abode of Vishnu; Shachi seeks her son where the Lord dwells. The "market" is an image of a
settled life, of family (cf. no. 1: the market of Gaura's prema).
[^12-41]: Shachi's lament in the spirit of vatsalya: motherly love, in which there is no room for thoughts of the Son's majesty, is
lofty prema (CC Adi 4).

## 16. Vasu Ghosha — "nadīyā chāṛiyā gela gaurāṅga sundare…" (GPT1 p. 374, no. 27)
*Gauranga has left Nadia, and the devotees sink in an ocean of grief: Advaita, Srivasa, Gadadhara, Vasudeva Datta, Murari,
Vakreshvara, Vasudeva and Narahari weep, Raghunandana rolls in the dust, Haridasa weeps with closed eyes, Nityananda —
looking at Shachi; the poet remembers the blissful kirtanas of Nadia. Raga suhai (tala somtal).*[^12-42]

**16.1.** Beautiful Gauranga has left Nadia —
all the devotees have sunk in an ocean of grief.

**16.2.** Advaita Acharya, Srivasa and Gadadhara weep;
Vasudeva Datta, Murari and Vakreshvara weep.

**16.3.** Vasudeva and Narahari weep aloud;
Sri Raghunandana, weeping, rolls in the dust.[^12-43]

**16.4.** Haridasa weeps, closing both eyes;
Nityananda weeps, looking at Shachi's face.

**16.5.** Blissful kirtanas He used to hold in Nadia —
remembering all that, Vasu's heart breaks.

[^12-42]: GPT1 — p. 374, no. 27 (raga suhai, tala somtal), checked against the scan (PDF p. 633); GPT2 — sec. 5.3, no. 27. The pada is not
in PK, BR, KGC or PS. The lament of Navadvipa after the Lord's departure — CB Antya 1; CC Madhya 3. The poet gathers all the companions
into one picture of grief, without regard to where each was (Nityananda, for instance, was with the Lord at Katwa).
[^12-43]: "Vasudeva" is apparently the poet himself (Vasudeva Ghosha), beside Narahari Sarakara of Shrikhanda; Raghunandana is Narahari's
nephew, then still a child.

## 17. Vasu Ghosha — "śuniyā māyera vāṇī kahe prabhu guṇamaṇi…" (GPT1 pp. 379–380, no. 44)
*Shantipura: hearing His mother's lament, the Lord consoles her: birth after birth she is His mother and He her child; so it
was with Dhruva's mother, with Kaushalya, and with Yashoda when Krishna went to Mathura; let her worship Krishna; when she
weeps and calls, He will come. Shachi is silent in tears; the poet begs the Lord to return to Nadia. Raga pahida.*[^12-44]

**17.1.** Hearing His mother's words, the Lord, the jewel of virtues, says:
"Listen, mother, to My words:
birth after birth you are My mother and I am your child;
all this is written by Providence.

**17.2.** There was Dhruva's mother — she gave her son detachment,
and therefore he worships the Lord who holds the disc;
Raghunatha, leaving all pleasures, wanders from forest to forest —
and mother Kaushalya, they say, ever weeps.[^12-45]

**17.3.** And then, in Dvapara, Krishna went to Mathura,
and Nanda's queen and father Nanda remained at home.
So it is with everyone, it is not otherwise:
in vain you grieve, Mother Shachi.

**17.4.** Who will undo what the Creator has ordained?
Knowing this, steady your heart.
Worship Krishna, make this the essence of life —
and there is no more samsara: you will attain the treasure of the supreme abode.

**17.5.** When you weep and call Me — I shall come:
this body was nurtured by you.
Bless Me — I am going to Nilachala;
keep Me near in your heart."[^12-46]

**17.6.** The Lord speaks words of comfort, and Shachi remains silent,
and tears flow from her eyes.
Vasu says: "Gaurahari, thus I pray:
go back to Nadia again!"

[^12-44]: GPT1 — pp. 379–380, section "sannyasa", no. 44 (raga pahida), checked against the scan (PDF pp. 638–639); GPT2 — sec. 5.3,
no. 44 (only the first line is recognized in the OCR). The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS; new catalogue entry VG-163. The pada
answers Shachi's lament in the preceding GPT pada (no. 43, "nitāi kariyā āge…") — this is PK 2233 with the signature of Vallabha
Dasa (in GPT — Vasu; according to Jagadbandhu's note, other collections have a different signature). The meeting with Shachi in
Shantipura and the Lord's answer, "I shall always come when you call" — CC Madhya 3; CB Antya 1. "Birth after birth you are My mother" — of the eternal relationship: Shachi is the Lord's eternal mother (in Krishna's lila — Yashoda; CC Adi 13).
[^12-45]: Suniti, Dhruva's mother, instructed her son to seek refuge in the Lord (Bhag. 4.8); Kaushalya is the mother of Rama
(Raghunatha), who went into exile in the forest.
[^12-46]: According to CC Madhya 3, Shachi herself asks her son to live in Puri so that she may have news of Him; the Lord promises to come
at her call (and, according to CC, comes to eat her offerings).

## 18. Vasu Ghosha — "nānāna prakāre prabhu māyere sāntvāya…" (GPT1 p. 380, no. 45)
*Shantipura: the Lord consoles His mother, Sita, Advaita's wife, reasons with Shachi; in Advaita's courtyard there is kirtana,
Gaura dances embracing Nitai, Advaita follows with outstretched arms lest the Lord fall; Shantipura has become like Navadvipa;
Shachi is outwardly sad, but in her heart she is blissful; for ten days the Lord stays with Advaita. Raga dhanashi.*[^12-47]

**18.1.** In many ways the Lord consoles His mother;
Sita, Advaita's wife, reasons with Shachi.

**18.2.** Shachi and all the people of Nadia
the Lord comforted with His gracious glance.

**18.3.** Over Shantipura rose the cry of "Hari!" —
in Advaita's courtyard the jewel Gaura dances.

**18.4.** He reels in prema, His heart knows no rest;
embracing Nitai, Nimai Pandita weeps.

**18.5.** Advaita, with outstretched arms, follows behind Him,
lest Gora crash down to the ground.

**18.6.** On all sides the devotees cry "Hari, Hari!" —
Shantipura has become like the city of Navadvipa.

**18.7.** About the Lord there seems the radiance of millions of moons;
in this cord and kaupina prema is manifest.

**18.8.** Seeing such a form, such ecstasy of prema, Mother Shachi
is outwardly sorrowful, but in her heart is bliss.

**18.9.** The Avadhuta calms Shachi's heart;
ending the sankirtana, He seats the Lord.[^12-48]

**18.10.** Thus for ten days in Advaita's house
the Lord, blissful at heart, enjoys the meals.

**18.11.** Vasudeva Ghosha says, clasping His feet:
"This hope of Advaita I will not let go!"[^12-49]

[^12-47]: GPT1 — p. 380, no. 45 (raga dhanashi), checked against the scan (PDF p. 639); GPT2 — sec. 5.3, no. 45 (in the OCR the number is
"৩৫"). The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS. The Lord in Shantipura for ten days, Shachi cooking for Him, kirtanas in Advaita's
house — CC Madhya 3; CB Antya 1.
[^12-48]: The Avadhuta is Nityananda.
[^12-49]: The sense is unclear: probably the poet, clasping the Lord's feet, does not want to let go of Advaita's hope of keeping Him
there (or: the hope he himself places in Advaita).

## 19. Vasu Ghosha — "prabhu karuṇa-svare bhakata pravodha kare…" (GPT1 pp. 380–381, no. 47)
*The farewell in Shantipura: the Lord, weeping, with joined palms, begs the devotees not to withdraw their mercy from Him: He has

Nilachala and Nadia will bring news of Him; embracing Advaita and taking the dust of Shachi's feet, He departs, and Shantipura is
filled with weeping. Raga shri-gandhara.*[^12-50]

**19.1.** The Lord in a plaintive voice consoles the devotees,
speaking as He weeps and weeps;
joining His palms, Gaurahari entreats:
"Do not withdraw your mercy from Me in your hearts!

**19.2.** Leaving My life in Navadvipa, I have put on saffron cloth,

in My heart is one hope — to live in Nilachala
with the consent of you all.

took hold of Advaita and embraced Him.[^12-51]

**19.4.** Consoling Shachi, taking the dust of her feet,
the Lord set out on His way without looking back.
Vasudeva Ghosha says: Gora goes to Nilachala —
Shantipura was filled with weeping.

not in PK, BR, KGC or PS. The farewell in Shantipura and the departure for Puri — CC Madhya 3; CB Antya 1–2.

## 20. Vasu Ghosha — "advaita-vilāpe prabhu hailā vikala…" (GPT1 p. 382, no. 53)
*Advaita's lament: moved by His weeping, the Lord in tears says to Him: "Why such bewilderment? You Yourself determined the course of
My lila; if I do not go to Nilachala, the lila will be spoiled and all You wished for will be in vain: how then will the name of
Hari be preached? Do not grieve like an ordinary man: I am always with You." Advaita is comforted. Raga dhanashi.*[^12-52]

**20.1.** At Advaita's lament the Lord was overwhelmed:
like the downpour of shravana, tears pour from His eyes.

**20.2.** He says to Advaita Acharya: "Why such bewilderment?
You Yourself have determined the course of My lila.[^12-53]

**20.3.** If I do not go to Nilachala, the lila will be spoiled,
all that You wished for will be in vain.

**20.4.** How then will the name of Hari be preached?
How will the people of the world find deliverance?

**20.5.** Why do You grieve like ordinary people?
I am always with You — believe this."

**20.6.** At the Lord's words Advaita was comforted.
"Glory, glory to Gauranga!" says Vasu Ghosha.

KGC or PS.

therefore the Lord says that Advaita "determined the course of His lila". The line "kahena advaitācāryya" is understood as "(the
Lord) says to Advaita Acharya" — from the sense of the following verses (20.6: "at the Lord's words").

## 21. Vasu Ghosha — "āmāra nimāi gela re kemana kare prāṇa…" (GPT1 p. 383, no. 1)
*Shachi's lament: my Nimai is gone — with tulasi beads, together with Bharati, and to everyone He meets He gives the name of

With tulasi beads in His hand Nimai goes with Bharati,
and to everyone He sees Nimai gives the name of Hari.

**21.2.** The daughter-in-law Vishnupriya weeps, flinging herself in the dust:
how will her heart endure, not seeing His face?

**21.3.** This is the word of Vasudeva Ghosha: listen, Shachi Thakurani —
to deliver living beings, Bhagavan has become a sannyasi.[^12-55]

GPT2 — sec. 5.4, no. 1. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS.
[^12-55]: The signature consoles Shachi with the truth about the Lord's sannyasa: He took it for the deliverance of all (CC Adi 17:

*Shachi, embracing her son by the neck and kissing Him, implores: she, unfortunate, has no one else; He has abandoned His

**22.1.** "O moon of Nadia, my child Nimai!
Your unfortunate mother has no one else."

**22.2.** Saying this, Shachi embraced Gauranga by the neck
and, in the fullness of affection, kisses the lotus of His face.

and the daughter-in-law Vishnupriya You have hung upon my neck.
