come home, my child — let the grief go far away.

**22.5.** Srinivasa, Haridasa and all the devotees —
with all of them, my child, perform kirtana.

**22.6.** Murari, Mukunda, Vasu and Haridasa —
why, leaving them all, did You take sannyasa?

**22.7.** What You did, You did — come back!
I shall call the brahmanas, and You will be given the sacred thread again."[^12-57]

**22.8.** Vasudeva Ghosha says: "Listen to my word:
go back again to Nadia, Gaura, jewel of virtues!"

[^12-56]: GPT1 — p. 383, no. 2 (raga suhai), checked against the scan (PDF p. 642); GPT2 — sec. 5.4, no. 2. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or
PS. Shachi holds her son in her arms — apparently at the meeting in Shantipura (CC Madhya 3); "Srinivasa" (śrīnivāsa) here is
Srivasa.
[^12-57]: A sannyasi removes the sacred thread (upavita); Shachi wants to give her son back the life of a brahmana householder. Her plea is
motherly love (vatsalya), unaware of the Son's majesty.

## 23. Vasu Ghosha — "kām̐de devī viṣṇupriyā nija aṅga āchāṛiyā…" (GPT1 pp. 387–388, no. 17)
*Vishnupriya's lament: rolling on the ground, she says: "My lord, You have cast me adrift in boundless waters; at whose word did
You take sannyasa? Even Raghunatha went to the forest together with Janaki; even Krishna, going to Mathura, sent Uddhava to the
gopis and so preserved their lives. I shall give this body to the Ganga." Raga pahida.*[^12-58]

**23.1.** Devi Vishnupriya weeps, flinging herself down,
rolling and rolling on the ground.
"O my lord, what have You done? You have cast me adrift in boundless waters and gone!" —
so she says, sobbing.

**23.2.** "Leaving this house and Your mother, making me helpless,
at whose word did You take sannyasa?
Even in the Vedas I hear: Raghunatha
went to the forest only taking Janaki with Him.[^12-59]

**23.3.** And formerly the son of Nanda, when He went to Mathura,
leaving all the gopis,
sent Uddhava to them, gave them news of Himself —
and so preserved their lives.[^12-60]

**23.4.** No more shall I see the moon-face, no more serve Your feet,
there will be no more that happy life;
this body I shall give to the Ganga, I shall take Your refuge."
Vasu has no hope of life.[^12-61]

[^12-58]: GPT1 — pp. 387–388, no. 17 (raga pahida), checked against the scan (PDF pp. 646–647); GPT2 — sec. 5.4, no. 17. The pada is not in
PK, BR, KGC or PS. Below the text Jagadbandhu gives three variants (without naming the source): "mui", "eṛi", "rāmāyaṇe" (see
bn/12.md).
[^12-59]: Variant (GPT1 note): "in the Ramayana" instead of "in the Vedas". Rama took Sita (Janaki) with Him into His forest exile.
[^12-60]: Uddhava, sent by Krishna from Mathura to Vraja with a message for the gopis (Bhag. 10.46–47). Vishnupriya reproaches the Lord: He
has not left her even a message. Her lament is the lament of a wife in separation; Vishnupriya herself, according to tradition,
afterwards lived under a strict vow, chanting the holy name.
[^12-61]: "I shall give my body to the Ganga" is an image of the utmost despair of separation, not the description of an event.

## 24. Vasu Ghosha — "hede re parāṇa nilajiyā…" (GPT1 p. 388, no. 21)
*Vishnupriya reproaches her "shameless" life for not leaving the body: Gauranga has left her, He has become a sannyasi and gone —
the happiness of this life is over. Raga bhupali.*[^12-62]

**24.1.** "O my shameless life,
you have still not left the body!

**24.2.** Gauranga has left me —
what honour do you still have?

**24.3.** Will you ever find Gaurangachand again?
In vain you will live in hope of love.

**24.4.** Becoming a sannyasi, my lord has gone —
the happiness of this life is over."

**24.5.** So, weeping, Vishnupriya speaks.
Vasu says: life will not remain.

[^12-62]: GPT1 — p. 388, no. 21 (raga bhupali), checked against the scan (PDF p. 647); GPT2 — sec. 5.4, no. 21. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC
or PS.

## 25. Vasu Ghosha — "dhika yāu e chāra jīvane…" (GPT1 p. 389, no. 22)
*Lament in separation: fie on this worthless life — where has Gora, the life of my life, gone? I shall not see the moon-face nor
hear His words; gone is the happiness He gave — a spear has remained in my heart; day and night I think only of the pauper's
treasure — His reddish feet; fate has turned away. Raga vibhasa.*[^12-63]

**25.1.** Fie on this worthless life!
Where has Gora gone, the life of my life?

**25.2.** Without Gora my soul is distraught and overwhelmed,
ceaselessly tears brim over in my eyes.

**25.3.** I shall not see the moon-face, I shall not hear His words —
I think: without Gora I shall enter the earth.

**25.4.** Gone is the happiness and all the wealth my lord bestowed —
like a spear (the separation) has remained in my heart.

**25.5.** Apart from Gora, night and day nothing else is in my mind:
ceaselessly I think of the pauper's treasure.[^12-64]

**25.6.** The reddish soles of His feet are exceedingly beautiful —
for them my heart intensely longs.

**25.7.** Fate was favourable — now it has turned away.
Says Vasudeva Ghosha: life will not remain.

[^12-63]: GPT1 — p. 389, no. 22 (raga vibhasa), checked against the scan (PDF p. 648); GPT2 — sec. 5.4, no. 22. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC
or PS. Below the text in GPT1 there are five variants (without naming the source; see the full version of the book). The speaker, judging from the place
in the section, is Vishnupriya (or Shachi); she is not named in the text.
[^12-64]: "The pauper's treasure" — the Lord, the only wealth of one who has nothing.

## 26. Vasu Ghosha — "śuniyā bhakata-dukha vidariyā yāya vuka…" (GPT1 pp. 409–410, no. 23)
*Hearing of the devotees' sorrow, the Lord comes with His companions to Nadia in the twinkling of an eye; Gadadhara lies
senseless, Narahari beside him; the Lord, rolling on the ground, cries out: "What have I done! May lightning strike the
sannyasa — I will not go to Nilachala, I shall stay with the devotees!" — and loses consciousness; the companions lay Him in
Gadadhara's lap, and both float in bliss. Raga dhanashi.*[^12-65]

**26.1.** Hearing of the devotees' sorrow, His heart breaking,
Gora goes with His companions;
He whose going is swift crosses a yojana in a moment —
and here is the meeting with the devotees in Nadia.[^12-66]

**26.2.** Gadadhara lies senseless, Narahari is beside him,
no one else can speak.
Seeing the devotees' state, the sannyasi sage, rolling on the ground,
speaks to Gadadhara:[^12-67]

**26.3.** "Alas, what have I done! May lightning strike the sannyasa:
My heart is like stone!
I will not go to Nilachala — I shall stay with the devotees."
Saying this, He lost consciousness.

**26.4.** The companions who were with Him ran up, lifted Gauranga
and laid Him in Gadadhara's lap;
feeling each other's touch, both speak softly, softly
and float in an ocean of bliss.

**26.5.** The eyes were cooled, seeing the face of Sri Gauranga,
by the touch the heart was soothed:
"I shall not let Him go again — I shall keep Him in my heart!" —
and Vasu Ghosha's bliss increased.

[^12-65]: GPT1 — pp. 409–410, section "antya-lila" (the final pastimes), no. 23 (raga dhanashi), checked against the scan (PDF pp. 668–669);
GPT2 — sec. 5.5, no. 23. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS. In GPT the pada stands before Vasu's pada on the coming of the people of
Nadia to the Lord (no. 24 = PK 2041, chapter 9, no. 6), i.e. it concerns the Lord's coming to Navadvipa on His way to Vrindavana
(1514/15; CC Madhya 16; CB Antya 3). The poet depicts this meeting in his own way: with him Gadadhara is in Nadia (according to CC
Madhya 16 Gadadhara accompanied the Lord from Puri to Cuttack) and the Lord resolves to stay.
[^12-66]: "Crosses a yojana in a moment" — hearing the devotees' call, the Lord comes to them, however long the way; the power of His love
for His devotees.
[^12-67]: The reading "gadādhara-bhāṣā" (lit. "Gadadhara's speech") is found in both editions of GPT; possibly a corruption of "gadagada bhāṣā" ("in a
choked voice").

## 27. Vasu Ghosha — "āju re kanakācala nīlācale gorā…" (GPT1 p. 341, no. 64)
*Phagu in Nilachala: Gora, like a golden mountain, is lost in the play of colours together with Govinda; on His neck sways a garland of
bakula, red with colour; the devotees, red with colour, sing sweetly; bhavas spread over His body, His eyes are half-closed in waves of
prema; looking at Gadadhara, He smiles softly. Raga todi.*[^12-68]

**27.1.** Today Gora, a golden mountain, in Nilachala
together with Govinda is lost in the play of colours.[^12-69]

**27.2.** On His neck sways a garland of bakula, red with colour;
the devotees, red with colour, sing sweetly.

**27.3.** So many bhavas arise — they have spread over all His body;
His eyes are half-closed in waves of prema.

**27.4.** Looking at Gadadhara, He smiles softly, softly —
that smile Vasudeva Ghosha did not understand.

[^12-68]: GPT1 — p. 341, section "festivals of the year", no. 64 (raga todi), checked against the scan (PDF p. 600); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 64. The
pada repeats almost word for word — shorter and with the signature of Vasudeva Ghosha — the pada of **Govinda Dasa** PK 1463
("nīlācale kanakācala gorā…", vol. 2; = GPT1 p. 341, no. 66; also in PS), which Jagadbandhu placed right here, one pada later. Probably this is
a recension of Govinda Dasa's pada which, by mistake or by singers' custom, received Vasu's signature; the attribution to Vasu Ghosha is
highly doubtful. Another pada on the phagu in Nilachala is by Madhavi Dasa (PK 2290; chapter 6).
[^12-69]: Govinda is Krishna; in Puri, at the festival of Dola-yatra, His festival Deity (Dola-Govinda) is sprinkled with coloured powder.
Perhaps the poet means the Lord's play with the Deity at this festival.

## 28. Vasu Ghosha — "svarūpera kare dhari vale kām̐di gaurahari…" (GPT1 pp. 306–307, no. 25)
*The Lord in the bhava of Radha disappointed in Her waiting (vipralabdha): holding Svarupa's hand, He weeps — the night has passed in
vain, the moon has set, Shyama has not come; the bed of flowers has wilted, the garland has withered; "Come, Svarupa, to the Suradhuni, let us
set all this afloat; let honour and family be lost — I shall throw Myself into the water"; the poet: where can the pain of this heart be
eased? Raga kamoda.*[^12-70]

**28.1.** Holding Svarupa's hand, weeping, Gaurahari says:
"My Shyama is not with Me!
In vain have I spent the night — the moon has set;
My heart is breaking.

**28.2.** *(Refrain)* Where is My beloved Shyama?
The bed of flowers has wilted, the garland has withered —
I have not tasted the honey of Shyama's love.

**28.3.** Come, Svarupa, let us go to the waters of the Suradhuni —
let us set all this afloat.
Let honour and family be lost — I shall live no more:
I shall leap into the water and give up My life.[^12-71]

**28.4.** That dark moon of Mine — in whose bower does He spend the night?
Why has He turned away from Me?"
Says Vasudeva Ghosha: in this sorrow the heart burns —
where can the pain of this heart be eased?[^12-72]

[^12-70]: GPT1 — pp. 306–307, section on the vipralabdha, no. 25 (raga kamoda), checked against the scan (PDF pp. 565–566); GPT2 — sec. 4.5,
no. 25. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS. Majumdar considers that the pada does not belong to Vasu: Svarupa Damodara was not the Lord's
companion in Navadvipa (at that time he was called Purushottama Acharya), while the Suradhuni (the Ganga) here points to Navadvipa. Cf. another GPT pada
with the same signature and the same opening, "svarūpera kare dhari gorārāya" (chapter 3, no. 14). Such bhavas of the Lord in Puri, in the
company of Svarupa — CC Antya 14–19.
[^12-71]: Radha's words in separation: "let honour and family be lost" is a sign of prema that gives up for Krishna everything the world
values; this is not worldly passion but the highest, pure love (CC Adi 4). The Lord in the bhava of Radha speaks Her words (Svarupa in
this lila is Radha's friend Lalita). "I shall leap into the water" is the utmost expression of separation
(vipralambha), in which prema reaches its peak.
[^12-72]: "The dark moon" (kālaśaśī) is Krishna; the kunja is a bower-grove in Vrindavana.

## 29. Vasu Ghosha — "ki ānanda khaṇḍapure ṭhākura naraharira ghare…" (GPT1 p. 353, no. 30)
*The festival at Shrikhanda: in the house of Narahari Thakura all the mahantas gather, the twelve gopalas, the sixty-four mahantas and the
six Gosvamis; Srinivasa seats everyone according to rank, in the middle — Gaurahari between the two Prabhus, Nityananda and Advaita;
Raghunandana serves the food, Mahaprabhu puts a mouthful into Nitai's mouth, Narahari and Gadadhara feed each other; after the meal
Srinivasa gives out garlands and sandal. Raga dhanashi.*[^12-73]

**29.1.** What bliss in Shrikhanda, in the house of Narahari Thakura!
Who can describe the joy of this festival?
All the mahantas have come and, floating in the rasa of the bliss of prema,
gaze at the moon of Gaura's face.

**29.2.** The twelve gopalas and with them the sixty-four mahantas,
and then the six Gosvamis;
all the branches and sub-branches — all the devotees have come,
joyfully singing Gaura's qualities.[^12-74]

**29.3.** Srinivasa seated each one in his place —
the mahantas sat in rows;
according to each one's standing he seated them all,
and between the two Prabhus — Gaurahari.

**29.4.** On the right — Nityananda, on the left — Advaitachandra,
and to His left — Gadadhara Acharya.
All sat down to the meal; then Raghunandana came
and began to serve the food.

**29.5.** Mahaprabhu in joyful delight, taking a mouthful in His hand,
puts it into Nitai's mouth;
so also Narahari and Gadadhara feed
each other in the happiness of prema.

**29.6.** After the meal — the cry: "Glory to Gaura, jewel of brahmanas!" —
and all together rinsed their mouths.
Srinivasa in joyful delight, taking mouth-fresheners,
gave everyone garlands and sandal.

**29.7.** Blessed is Narahari Thakura, in whose house Sri Chaitanya
is present Himself — together with Nityananda!
Seeing this, the Vaishnavas cry "Hari!" again and again —
Vasu begs for His two feet.[^12-75]

[^12-73]: GPT1 — p. 353, section ashtakaliya, no. 30 (raga dhanashi), checked against the scan (PDF p. 612); GPT2 — sec. 5.2, no. 30. The pada is
not in PK, BR, KGC or PS. Majumdar cites it as an example of forgery in GPT: the participation of the six Gosvamis is impossible — they
never left Vrindavana together; moreover, the festival is arranged by Srinivasa Acharya, who came to Shrikhanda only after the Lord's
departure (*Bhakti-ratnakara*, *Prema-vilasa*). The attribution to Vasu Ghosha is unreliable (D).
[^12-74]: The twelve gopalas are companions of Nityananda (in the bhava of the cowherd boys of Vraja); the sixty-four mahantas are
devotee-preachers in Bengal (a later tradition); the six Gosvamis are Rupa, Sanatana, Jiva, Gopala Bhatta, Raghunatha Bhatta and
Raghunatha Dasa. "Branches and sub-branches" — the image of the tree of Chaitanya (CC Adi 10–12).
[^12-75]: The presence of Chaitanya and Nityananda "Themselves" at a festival arranged by Srinivasa is understood in the tradition as Their
appearance (avirbhava) in the devotees' kirtana: thus, according to the *Bhakti-ratnakara* and the *Narottama-vilasa*, the Lord with His
companions appeared at the festival in Kheturi. The poet, however, describes the festival as if the Lord were present in person, together
with Gadadhara, Advaita and Narahari.

# Chapter 13. Balarama Dasa, Murari, Yadunatha, Ananta, Ramachandra: Padas from the *Gaura-pada-tarangini* — from Krishna's Resolve to the Prayers

*This chapter continues the group of padas known from the *Gaura-pada-tarangini* (GPT1 — 1st ed. by Jagadbandhu Bhadra,
1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934), excluding padas in nagari-bhava. Here are padas signed by Balarama Dasa, Yadunatha Dasa, Murari,
Ananta (Raya Ananta) and Ramachandra, in the order of the GPT sections (that is, of the lilas): the nandi prologue (Krishna's
resolve to appear as Gaura), praise of the Gaura-avatara and wonder at the sannyasa, Gaura and Gadadhara, childhood plays,
the kirtanas of Navadvipa, the bhava of Radha, the Lord's morning, the people of Nadia in Shantipura, the waiting for His
return, praise of Nityananda and Advaita, the books of Jiva Gosvami, and prayers. Checking against the *Padakalpataru* (PK)
showed that nine padas listed as "GPT only" or missing from the catalogue altogether are in PK (nos. 4–7, 9, 15, 19–21) —
there the text follows PK with the GPT variants; no. 4 is signed by Vasu Ghosha in PK, no. 5 by "Natavara," no. 8 is
Balarama's pada PK 2201 (formerly misidentified with Lochana's pada PK 2203; corrected in the full PK check of chapter 16). Seven padas (nos. 4, 5, 8, 9, 19, 20, 25) were missing from
the stage-1 catalogue: they were found in a full check of the signatures of GPT1. Majumdar considers the GPT unreliable for
attribution; padas of several poets are known under the signature "Balarama Dasa"; the "Ramachandra" of nos. 24–25 is, by his
own words, a grandson of Vamshivadana who lived after the Lord's departure. The attribution of the padas of this chapter is
therefore provisional. The full PK check (chapter 16) found nos. 16 (PK 2512) and 18 (PK 1976) in PK as well;
their variants have been added. The Bengali original, the variants of GPT1/GPT2, PK and KGC, and the word-for-word translation are in the full version of the book.*

## 1. Balarama Dasa — "śunaite rāi vacana adharāmṛta…" (GPT1 p. 2, no. 2)
*Prologue (nandi) of the *Gaura-pada-tarangini*: having heard Radha tell of Her dream in which She saw a golden youth,
Krishna reveals to Her that He Himself will take that form: three desires — to know what Her prema is like, what its
sweetness is, and what happiness She tastes — were not fulfilled in Vraja; taking Her bhava and lustre, making Her prema
His guru, He will rise in Nadia.*[^13-1]

**1.1.** Hearing the nectar of Rai's words, the clever Kanu, full of rasa,
received, know it, the fair one's consent — to reveal Her bhava in His own self.[^13-2]

**1.2.** "Beautiful one, the form of Gaura you have spoken of
no one knows: only by your prema will you make Me such."

**1.3.** "What your prema is like, what its sweetness, in what happiness you are absorbed —
these three longed-for treasures were not fulfilled in Vraja; what can I say — I have found no end to them.[^13-3]

**1.4.** Having pondered, I have understood: except in your very form this joy can never be tasted.
Taking your bhava and lustre, making your prema My guru, I shall rise in Nadia.

**1.5.** I shall fulfil My heart's longing, remove My heart's obstacle, distribute to the world the treasure of prema."
Balarama Dasa says: my Lord is all-merciful — and I, lowest of men, have not served Him.

[^13-1]: GPT1 — printed p. 2, section "Nandi, or Prelude" (nāndī vā pūrvābhāsa), no. 2, no raga given; checked against the IA scan
in.ernet.dli.2015.477854 (PDF p. 261); GPT2 — sec. 1.1, no. 2. The pada is not in the *Padakalpataru* (PK), the
*Bhakti-ratnakara* (BR), the *Kshanada-gita-chintamani* (KGC) or the *Padamrita-samudra* (PS). Padas nos. 2–4 are a dialogue
of Krishna and Radha continuing no. 1 (Radha's dream of a golden youth, signed by Jagadananda) and concluded by no. 5
(Vaishnava Dasa). Majumdar considers the GPT unreliable for attribution; padas of several poets are known under the
signature "Balarama Dasa," and this pada on the purpose of the Gaura-avatara contains nothing pointing to an eyewitness —
the attribution is provisional (C).
[^13-2]: Kanu (Kan) is Krishna. "To reveal Her bhava in Himself" is what Krishnadasa Kaviraja names as the cause of the
Gaura-avatara: Krishna, taking Radha's bhava and lustre, tastes His own sweetness (CC Adi 1.5–6; 4).
[^13-3]: The three desires — CC Adi 1.6 and 4: to know the greatness of Radha's love, the sweetness of Himself which Radha
tastes, and the happiness She feels. The poet puts this theological motif into Krishna's mouth almost word for word.

## 2. Balarama Dasa — "vām̐dhu he śunaite kām̐pai dehā…" (GPT1 p. 2, no. 3)
*Radha's reply: at this news Her body trembles — He is the life of Vraja; like a fish without water or a serpent
without its jewel, Vraja cannot live a moment without Him; will He, leaving Her, reveal prema with His brother and friends
on the bank of another river?*[^13-4]

**2.1.** "Beloved, hearing this my whole body trembles.
You are the life of Vraja: without You how will Vraja keep its footing?

**2.2.** As a fish without water, as a serpent without its jewel gives up its life,
so Vraja without the sight of You for even half a moment — You know what its state will be.

**2.3.** Having finished everything, what perfection will You attain, what happiness will You find?
Will others know Your heart? For this my breast is torn.

**2.4.** You dwell in the groves and bowers of Vrindavana, You, Kanu, best of lovers;
day and night, without the sight of You, all will pine and give up their lives.

**2.5.** With Your elder brother, with Your friends You will sport on the river bank —
and forgetting me You will reveal prema?" Balarama Dasa does not understand.[^13-5]

[^13-4]: GPT1 — p. 2, no. 3, no raga (scan PDF p. 261); GPT2 — sec. 1.1, no. 3. In 2.5 GPT1 reads "pāsaravi mujhe" (you will forget
me), GPT2 "parihari mujhe" (abandoning me). Radha's anguish is not worldly sorrow but the highest prema (mahabhava) by which
Vraja lives; the fear of separation is inseparable from it (CC Madhya 2).
[^13-5]: "Elder brother" — Balarama, who appeared in the Gaura-lila as Nityananda; "friends" — the cowherd boys who became
the Lord's associates. The "river bank" (yamunātaṭa) is in the poem the bank of the Yamuna; in the Gaura-lila its place is
taken by the Ganga of Navadvipa. Radha's fear is answered by Krishna in the next pada: He will not leave Vraja (3.4) — in
Bhaktisiddhanta's teaching Navadvipa and Vraja are non-different, and Gaura is Radha and Krishna in one form (CC Adi
4.55–56).

## 3. Balarama Dasa — "śunaha sundari majhu abhilāṣa…" (GPT1 p. 2, no. 4)
*Krishna's reply: He will reveal the prema of Vraja; with all the cowherd men and boys He will sport in Nadia; the two
bodies will merge into one, and He will ceaselessly repeat Her name; He will never leave Vraja — without Vraja prema is
not attained.*[^13-6]

**3.1.** "Hear, beautiful one, My desire:
the prema of Vraja I shall reveal to the world.

**3.2.** Gathering all the cowherd men and boys,
in the town of Nadia I shall begin My play.

**3.3.** Our bodies, joined, will become one,
and My lips will ceaselessly repeat your name.

**3.4.** Leaving Vraja, I shall never go away:
without Vraja prema is not attained.

**3.5.** With the bhava of Vraja I shall fulfil My heart's desire" —
this Balarama Dasa has known by realization.[^13-7]

[^13-6]: GPT1 — p. 2, no. 4, no raga (scan PDF p. 261; the last line is smudged in the scan, the reading "anubhavi jānala" is
confirmed by GPT2); GPT2 — sec. 1.1, no. 4.
[^13-7]: "Two bodies will become one" — Gaura is Radha and Krishna united in one form (CC Adi 1.5; 4.55); "repeat Her name" —
the Lord in Navadvipa and Puri cries "Radha, Radha!" "The heart's desire" (mana-kāma) is the thirst to taste Radha's love,
not worldly lust.

## 4. Vasu Ghosha (in GPT1 — Balarama Dasa) — "purave vāndhila cūṛā eve keśa-hīna…" (PK 2255; GPT1 p. 18, no. 47)
*The Lord's sannyasa as Krishna's transformation: formerly He tied His hair in a top-knot — now His head is shaven;
instead of the milk-pail in His left hand — the sannyasi's water-pot; in the Treta-yuga He held the bow, in the
Dvapara the flute, in the Kali-yuga He took the staff; Balarama has become an avadhuta, Kanai a sannyasi. Raga
gandhara.*[^13-8]

**4.1.** Formerly He tied His hair in a top-knot — now He is without hair;
leaving the dress of the best of dancers, He has put on the kaupina.

**4.2.** A pail for milking the cows was in His left hand —
after that very pattern Gora has taken the sannyasi's water-pot.[^13-9]

**4.3.** In the Treta-yuga He held the bow, in the Dvapara the flute;
in the Kali-yuga, taking the staff, He has become a sannyasi.

**4.4.** Vasu Ghosha says: listen, people of Nadia:
Balarama is an avadhuta, Kanai a sannyasi![^13-10]

[^13-8]: PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 288 (printed p. 277), 21st pallava "The sannyasa of Sri Gauranga, etc.," label "॥৩৮॥২২৫৫॥", raga
gandhara, MS P-R-Sa no. 2310 — signed by **Vasu Ghosha** (4.4: "vāsughoṣa kahe…"). GPT1 — p. 18, section "Mangalacharana,"
no. 47 (gandhara), checked against the scan (PDF p. 277): the same pada, but in 4.4 "valarāma kahe śuna nadīyānivāsī," i.e. signed by
Balarama; the compiler of GPT1 himself noted that a manuscript and PK ascribe it to Vasu Ghosha. GPT2 — sec. 1.2, no. 47.
The pada was missing from the stage-1 catalogue (new row); the attribution to Vasu Ghosha (per PK) is preferable: the
signature "Balaram" in GPT1 probably arose from the second half of 4.4, where Balarama's name refers to Nityananda.
[^13-9]: Kaupina — the loincloth of the renunciant; karanga (karaṅga) — the sannyasi's water-pot (kamandalu). The poet sets the
marks of Krishna the cowherd beside those of Gaura the sannyasi: the milk-pail in His left hand has "become" the water-pot.
[^13-10]: Avadhuta — a renunciant above outward rules; so Nityananda was called, who is Balarama (CC Adi 5; CB Adi 9). Kanai
(Kanu) is Krishna, appearing as Gauranga. The Lord's sannyasa is not the renunciation of a conditioned soul but a lila
for the deliverance of the people of Kali-yuga (CC Adi 17; CB Madhya 26).

## 5. Balarama Dasa (in PK — "Natavara") — "gopīgaṇa-kuca-kuṅkume vañcita…" (PK 2250; GPT1 p. 18, no. 48)
*Wonder at the Lord's sannyasa: He whom the maidens of Vraja embraced, whose body was coloured with their kunkuma, is
now in saffron cloth, covered with thrills, with streams of tears of prema; the dark-bodied Dancer of Vrindavana has
become a pauper begging prema from house to house. Raga dhanashi (in GPT1 — kedara).*[^13-11]

**5.1.** Bereft of the kunkuma from the gopis' breasts, He has a ruddy cloth shining on His body;
His body, whose lustre puts gold to shame, is from the joy of Rai's touch.[^13-12]

**5.2.** Look, look — the wondrous play of Gaura!
He who was the teacher of love to hundreds of thousands of young maidens has now taken sannyasa.[^13-13]

**5.3.** He whom the maidens of Vraja ceaselessly held in their firm embrace
is now all thrilling with goosebumps, and tears of prema stream from His eyes.

**5.4.** That best of dancers, with a body dark as a rain-cloud, who roamed the forest of Vrinda —
says Natavara — now, a pauper, begs prema from house to house.[^13-14]

[^13-11]: PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 286 (printed p. 275), 21st pallava, label "॥৩৩॥২২৫০॥", raga dhanashi, MSS P-R-Sa no. 2355 and P-R no. 12 —
signature "kahaye naṭavara" (according to Ray's apparatus, P-R-Sa reads "valarāma"). GPT1 — pp. 18–19, no. 48 (kedara), checked
against the scan (PDF p. 277): "kahaye valarāma naṭavara so ava…" — signed by Balarama. GPT2 — sec. 1.2, no. 48. In PK the pada follows
PK 2249 of Balarama (chapter 11, no. 16), where it was noted that PK 2250 is signed "Natavara" and had not been
translated; it was missing from the catalogue (new row). Attribution to Balarama — per P-R-Sa and GPT1 (C).
[^13-12]: The first half-line in PK reads "kuṅkume vañcita" ("bereft of the kunkuma"): formerly Krishna's body was ruddy with the
gopis' kunkuma, now the sannyasi's cloth is ruddy; GPT1 reads "kuṅkume rañjita" ("coloured with kunkuma"). Gaura's golden
lustre comes from Radha's touch: He has taken Her complexion (CC Adi 4).
[^13-13]: "Guru-lampata" (guru lampaṭa) — literally "the foremost of lovers": the language of madhurya-rasa. The gopis' love for
Krishna is not worldly passion but the purest prema, only called "kama" (CC Madhya 8; Adi 4.165–171); the contrast in the
pada stresses that the same Krishna, the Lord of Vraja, has become a renunciant.
[^13-14]: "Natavara" — in PK apparently the poet's name (or an epithet of Krishna taken by a scribe for a signature); in P-R-Sa
and GPT1 — "Balarama." "A beggar of prema" — the Lord, who Himself distributes prema, in the mood of a devotee begs it of
everyone (CC Adi 7).

## 6. Yadunatha Dasa — "gaura-varaṇa tanu sundara sukhamaya…" (PK 2180; GPT1 p. 36, no. 28)
*Gaura and Gadadhara in Navadvipa: a golden body full of bliss, a heart full of compassion; at Gaura's left is the
beloved Gadadhara, and the hidden rasa is revealed, as if the circle of the rasa; in Nadia there are so many moons that the
darkness has gone far away; Gaura and Gadadhara are a lake of prema that has overflowed the earth. Raga the same as that of
the preceding PK pada (in GPT1 — kamoda).*[^13-15]

**6.1.** A golden-hued body — beautiful, full of bliss; a compassionate heart — an abode of rasa;
a garland of jasmine and oleander, woven row upon row, sways — a forest garland.

**6.2.** At Gaura's left is the best one, the beloved Gadadhara: the hidden rasa is revealed;
as if the circle of the rasa had shone forth — and their speech falters with prema.[^13-16]

**6.3.** In the town of Nadia so many moons — the darkness has gone far away;
however many spotless lamps are lit — beside them they cannot even be discerned.

**6.4.** Gaura and Gadadhara are a lake of prema: overflowing, it has filled the earth;
Dasa Yadunatha, cheated by fate, not getting even a touch of it, weeps.[^13-17]

[^13-15]: PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 261 (printed p. 250), label "॥১৩॥২১৮০॥", raga "tathā" (the same as PK 2179), MS P-R-Sa no. 2288. GPT1 — p. 36,
no. 28 (kamoda), checked against the scan (PDF p. 295); GPT2 — sec. 3.1 (OCR, line 25224). In the catalogue (YD-006) the pada was
listed as "GPT only"; it is found in PK — **core**. In PK it stands among Nayanananda's padas on Gaura and Gadadhara. On Yadunatha
Dasa (Kavichandra), a fellow villager of Jagannatha Mishra, see the catalogue (CB Madhya 1; CC Adi 11); other padas signed
"Yadunatha Dasa" in PK are PK 2125, 2126, 2191 (chapter 6).
[^13-16]: Gadadhara Pandita is the Lord's eternal associate, in whom Vaishnavas see a manifestation of Radha (GGD 147–153); the
"hidden rasa" is their prema, not worldly intimacy. The "circle of the rasa" is the image of Krishna's rasa-lila showing
through the kirtana of Gaura and Gadadhara.
[^13-17]: "Cheated by fate" is the usual formula of humility in a poet's signature.

## 7. Balarama Dasa — "yata yata avatāra-sāra…" (PK 2346; GPT1 p. 38, no. 37)
*Praise of the Gaura-avatara: among all incarnations the incarnation of Gora is renowned; prema for Krishna, inaccessible
even to Brahma, the Lord distributed down to the chandalas; the flood of prema has drowned foreigners and unbelievers, beasts
and birds sing and weep in kirtana — only Balarama has been left out. Raga bhatiyari.*[^13-18]

**7.1.** Of all and all the incarnations the essence —
renowned has remained my incarnation of Gora!

**7.2.** Prema for Krishna and the treasure of the Name, hard for even Brahma to obtain,
the Lord gave down to the chandalas and filled the world with them.

**7.3.** In the flood of prema foreigners, unbelievers and the rest —
all people, immersed, laugh, dance and sing.

**7.4.** Beasts and birds, tigers, deer, the creatures of the waters
laugh, weep, dance, sing and perform kirtana.

**7.5.** Heaven, earth and the netherworlds have drowned in prema for Gora —
left out has been only Dasa Balarama.

[^13-18]: PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 320 (printed p. 309), 23rd pallava, label "॥১৫॥২৩৪৬॥", raga bhatiyari, MS P-R-Sa no. 2450; it is followed in PK by
PK 2347 (chapter 12, no. 1). GPT1 — p. 38, no. 37 (bhatiyari), checked against the scan (PDF p. 297); GPT2 — sec. 1.3, no. 37. In the
catalogue (BD-009) the pada was listed as "GPT only"; it is found in PK — **core** (C). A chandala is an outcaste beyond the
varnas; the gift of prema to all without distinction — CC Adi 7; CB Madhya 13.

## 8. Balarama Dasa — "sava avatāra sāra gorā avatāra…" (PK 2201; GPT1 p. 38, no. 39)
*Praise of the Gaura-avatara: such mercy there has never been; the Lord, entreating, gave prema to the humble and fallen;
whoever does not serve such a treasure of mercy drinks poison with his own hands and will not be saved even in millions of
kalpas. Raga shri.*[^13-19]

**8.1.** The essence of all incarnations is the incarnation of Gora:
such mercy is seen nowhere else.

**8.2.** To the humble, the destitute, the low, the fallen — to each one
the Lord, entreating and entreating, gave the treasure of prema.

**8.3.** Whoever does not serve such a treasure of mercy
has lifted poison with his own hand and drunk it.

**8.4.** Whoever has been left out at such an incarnation
will find no deliverance even in millions of kalpas.

**8.5.** And I, low as I am, have not served such a Lord —
says Balarama: now I am burning and perishing.[^13-20]

[^13-19]: GPT1 — p. 38, no. 39 (shri), checked against the scan (PDF p. 297); GPT2 — sec. 1.3, no. 39. **The pada is in PK — PK 2201**
(vol. 3, 20th pallava "Śrī-Gauracandra — prakārāntara," PDF p. 269, printed p. 258, label "॥১৮॥২২০১॥", raga "tathā", MS P-R-Sa no. 2309) —
with the same signature of Balarama ("…kahe valarāma eve marinu puṛiyā" — "now I am burning"). The earlier statement that 8.1–8.4 are
the beginning of Lochana Dasa's pada PK 2203 was mistaken: PK 2203 begins "ke yāve ke yāve bhāi bhava-sindhu pāra" (MS P-R-Sa
no. 2311) and merely stands near this pada (corrected in the full PK check, chapter 16). Balarama's signature is attested both in PK and
in GPT — C. The pada was missing from the stage-1 catalogue (row BD-045).
[^13-20]: "Burning and perishing" (PK: marinu puṛiyā; GPT: paṛiyā — "fallen and perishing") is a formula of penitence in the signature (cf. 7.5); the poet speaks of himself, not of the Lord.

## 9. Balarama Dasa — "navadvīpa-gagane uyala dina rāti…" (PK 2196; GPT1 p. 39, no. 40)
*Gaura as a rain-cloud: in the sky of Navadvipa a cloud stands day and night, watering all that lives; a downpour of the
nectar of prema; foul weather has covered the world; the peacock-devotees dance, the frog-non-devotees croak in the water;
the creeper of bhakti has overspread the three worlds; the lightning of kirtana has burnt the forest of yoga, the thunder
has split knowledge; the serpent of karma is driven out, the chataka is satisfied; the earth has drowned — only Balarama
is left on the mountain of samsara. Raga kamoda.*[^13-21]

**9.1.** In the sky of Navadvipa a cloud has risen and stays day and night:
with a downpour of rasa it has watered all that lives — the unmoving and the moving.

**9.2.** Look, look: Gaura is the incarnation of a cloud,
ceaselessly raining the nectar of prema!

**9.3.** Since then the whole world is wrapped in foul weather;
with the rasa of Hari the people of the world, intoxicated, have forgotten themselves.

**9.4.** In frenzy the peacock-devotees dance;
the non-devotees — the frogs — croak, sunk in the water.[^13-22]

**9.5.** The creeper of bhakti has overspread the three worlds:
the fruit of prema the high and the low have received.

**9.6.** With the thunderbolt of kirtana the forest of yoga is burnt,
and knowledge too the cloud's thunder splits apart.

**9.7.** From the hole of the heart the serpent of karma is driven out;
the waves of Kali's burning intoxication have subsided.

**9.8.** The scorched chataka has drunk its fill;
in all ten directions rivers have flowed.

**9.9.** The earth has drowned, for no one is there any dry place —
on the mountain of samsara only Balarama is left.[^13-23]

[^13-21]: PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 266–267 (printed pp. 255–256), 20th pallava, label "॥১৩॥২১৯৬॥", raga kamoda, MS P-R-Sa no. 2304. GPT1 — p. 39,
no. 40 (kamoda), checked against the scan (PDF p. 298); GPT2 — sec. 1.3, no. 40. The pada was missing from the catalogue (new row); **core** (PK, C).
**core** (PK, C).
[^13-22]: Images of the rainy season: peacocks dance at the sight of clouds, frogs croak in the water; so the Bhagavata describes the
rains in Vraja (Bhag. 10.20), and the poet transfers the images to Gaura's kirtana. "Croak" (royata) — literally "weep, wail."
[^13-23]: The chataka is a bird that drinks only rainwater — an image of the soul thirsting only for prema. "Rivers" (nadiyā) puns on
the name Nadia. "The mountain of samsara" — the poet is left "high and dry," not washed by the flood of prema (cf. 7.5).

## 10. Ananta (Raya Ananta?) — "gaura navaghana premadhārā variṣila…" (GPT1 p. 40, no. 44)
*Gaura's mercy as husbandry: the young cloud Gaura has rained down prema; the hard soil of evil thoughts is broken by the
ploughing of bhakti, and prema has sprouted in hearts; Nitai waters the shoot with the water of bhakti, and the tree of prema
grows day by day, bearing fruit for all. Raga suhai.*[^13-24]

**10.1.** Gaura, a young rain-cloud, has poured down streams of prema:
thirsty, scorched souls have drunk their fill.

**10.2.** The hard soil of evil thoughts is broken by the tillage of bhakti —
in the hearts of living beings a shoot of prema has sprung up.

**10.3.** That shoot Nitai watered with the water of bhakti,
and day by day the tree of prema grew higher.

**10.4.** It has borne the fruits of prema for all living beings —
Ananta has been left out by the turns of his own karma.

[^13-24]: GPT1 — p. 40, no. 44 (suhai), checked against the scan (PDF p. 299); GPT2 — sec. 1.3, no. 44 (last word "kammaphere"). The pada is not
in PK, BR, KGC or PS (catalogue: AN-010; the signature given in the catalogue as "…karmadoṣe" reads "karmaphere" in the scan). In GPT it
follows the pada of Raya Ananta from KGC (no. 43, chapter 11, no. 3), and the signature "Ananta" here is probably the same poet's —
Ananta of Advaita's branch (per M-1961); attribution only by GPT (C). The image of Nityananda watering the shoot of devotion — cf.
the "tree of prema," CC Adi 9.

## 11. Murari — "śacīra āṅginā mājhe bhuvanamohana sāje…" (GPT1 p. 77, no. 47)
*Childhood: in the middle of Shachi's courtyard, enchanting the world, little Gorachand crawls on all fours; holding His
mother's finger He toddles and falls; a tiger-claw swings at His neck, His chest is wet with dribble, on His moon-face is the
lightning of a smile; Shachi takes the dusty child to her breast, but He, crying, climbs down and rolls on the ground again;
Murari, laughing, says: this is no child for the lap — Gaurahari will become a sannyasi. Raga pahira.*[^13-25]

**11.1.** In the middle of Shachi's courtyard, in an attire that enchants the world, Gorachand crawls on all fours;
holding His mother's finger, now He toddles along — and, tripping, falls down.

**11.2.** A tiger-claw swings at His neck, His chest is wet with dribble, on His moon-face is the lightning of a smile;
covered all over with dust — can a mother bear it? — she lifts Him to her breast.

**11.3.** Crying, displeased at this, Gora climbs down from her lap and rolls on the ground again;
Murari, laughing, says: "This is no child for the lap — Gaurahari will become a sannyasi."[^13-26]

[^13-25]: GPT1 — p. 77, section "Childhood plays," no. 47 (pahira), checked against the scan (PDF p. 336); GPT2 — sec. 2.2, no. 47. The pada
is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS. Catalogue: MU-001; the row MU-006 ("…hāsiyā murāri vole e nahe kolera chele," after Majumdar's reference to
GPT1 p. 77) is the same pada (a duplicate). Majumdar considers this pada doubtful: the signature merely names Murari, and he
ascribes the padas on the Lord's infancy to later imagination. The attribution to Murari Gupta is unproven (C). A tiger-claw
(vāghanakha) is an amulet on a child's neck.
[^13-26]: The first syllable of line 11.3 is cut off in the GPT1 scan ("[kām̐]diyā"), restored by sense and metre. Murari's words foretell
the sannyasa; in CB (Adi 4–5) the child's future greatness is spoken of by an astrologer and neighbours, while Murari is Nimai's
senior fellow student (CB, Adi-khanda).

## 12. Murari — "śacīra dulāla manoraṅge…" (GPT1 pp. 77–78, no. 48)
*Children's kirtana: Shachi's darling son plays with boys of His age; Gora is in the middle, the children around Him; holding
hands they whirl in time and clap; Gora cries "Hari, Hari!", the children echo, and Kali trembles; Murari is full of joy — the
reign of sin is over. Raga kamoda.*[^13-27]

**12.1.** Shachi's darling son, with a joyful heart,
plays with children of His own age.

**12.2.** Gora is in the middle, the children all around;
He dances and smiles ever so gently.

**12.3.** Holding one another by the hand,
they whirl in time and dance.

**12.4.** Now they clap their hands together,
now someone cries: "Well done, well done!"

**12.5.** When Gora calls out "Hari, Hari!" —
the children call out "Hari!" along with Him.

**12.6.** Hearing "Hari bol!" again and again,
Kali trembles, sensing disaster.

**12.7.** Murari is filled with joy:
the reign of sin is over.[^13-28]

[^13-27]: GPT1 — pp. 77–78, no. 48 (kamoda), checked against the scan (PDF pp. 336–337); GPT2 — sec. 2.2, no. 48. The pada is not in PK, BR,
KGC or PS. Catalogue: MU-007 (the first line given in the catalogue, "gorā sabe bale hari hari," after Majumdar's reference, is 12.5).
Majumdar allows that it may be an interpolation; the attribution to Murari Gupta is unproven (C).
[^13-28]: Murari's name in the last couplet is the poet's signature (or a mention of Murari Gupta as a witness). Little Nimai's games,
repeating the name of Hari with the children — CB Adi 4; CC Adi 14.

## 13. Yadunatha (?) — "nityānanda saṅge nāce prabhu gauracandra…" (GPT1 p. 271, no. 76)
*The kirtana of Gaura and Nityananda: the Lord dances with Nityananda, His associates after Him; the earth floats in tears; He
embraces the fallen and weeps, calls His devotees, embraces Gadai; He calls Govinda, Madhava and Vasu. Raga suhai.*[^13-29]

**13.1.** With Nityananda dances the Lord Gaurachandra,
and after Him dance His associates — the host of devotees.

**13.2.** The earth floats away on the tears of their eyes;
raising both arms, all cry: "Hari, Hari!"

**13.3.** His body quivers with bhava — how many streams flow!
Embracing the fallen by the neck, He sobs.

**13.4.** His own devotees He Himself calls together,
and, embracing Gadai by the neck, He weeps again and again.

**13.5.** "Govinda, Madhava, Vasu — come here!" He calls;
Yadu says: the darling of the Lord's life weeps.[^13-30]

[^13-29]: GPT1 — p. 271, no. 76 (suhai), checked against the scan (PDF p. 530); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 76. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS.
It is entered twice in the catalogue: YD-007 and YN-013 (a duplicate; the signature "yadu kahe" — Yadunatha or Yadunandana, not
established); C. Govinda, Madhava and Vasu are the Ghosha brothers, the Lord's kirtana singers (CC Adi 10; Madhya 11).
[^13-30]: "The darling of the Lord's life" (prabhura parāṇa-putalī, literally "the doll of the Lord's life") — probably Gadadhara (Gadai), named in 13.4.

## 14. Raya Ananta — "nadīyā-ākāśe saṃkīrtana-megha sāje…" (GPT1 p. 271, no. 79)
*Sankirtana as a thunderstorm: in the sky of Nadia the cloud of kirtana has gathered, khol and karatalas thunder, the roars
of "hum" are like thunderclaps; the two Lords rain down the name; the associates dance, and the lightning of bhava flashes;
Nadia and Shantipura are flooded with the rain of prema. Raga suhai.*[^13-31]

**14.1.** In the sky of Nadia the cloud of sankirtana has gathered:
khol and karatalas are its deep thunder.

**14.2.** Roars of "hum-hum" — thunderclaps — sound again and again;
the two Lords, the clouds, pour down a rain of the Name.

**14.3.** The associates dance and sing, pausing now and then,
and in them the lightning of bhava flashes again and again.

**14.4.** By the rain of prema Nadia and Shantipura are flooded —
only the heart of Raya Ananta has not dissolved in this rasa.[^13-32]

[^13-31]: GPT1 — pp. 271–272, no. 79 (suhai), checked against the scan (PDF p. 531); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 79. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC
or PS (catalogue: AN-009, GPT only; C). The signature "Raya Ananta" is as in KGC 11.2 and 28.2 (chapters 4, 11): per M-1961 this is
Ananta of Advaita's branch.
[^13-32]: "The two Lords" — Gaura and Nityananda; "Shantipura" — Advaita's town: the kirtana has swept both places. Literally: "the heart
of Raya Ananta did not lose itself in the rasa."

## 15. Balarama Dasa — "hari hari gorā kene kānde…" (PK 2254; GPT1 p. 289, no. 39)
*Why does Gora weep? Having left the bank of the Kalindi and the plays by the kadamba, what does He seek on the shore of the
ocean? He who danced the rasa with millions of gopis now, having taken sannyasa, weeps; the eyes at whose glance Kamadeva
swooned pour out streams of tears; the head whose top-knot charmed the world is shaven; instead of yellow garments,
saffron; instead of the dark form, golden. The poet does not know the reason — the reason is she whose colour it is. Raga
suhai (in GPT1 — gandhara).*[^13-33]

**15.1.** Hari, Hari! Why does Gora weep?
I do not know in whose snare of love He has been caught.

**15.2.** Leaving the bank of the Kalindi and the plays by the kadamba,
what does He now desire on the shore of the ocean?

**15.3.** He who danced the rasa with millions of gopis —
now, having taken sannyasa, why does He weep?

**15.4.** Those eyes, at whose play Ananga himself swooned,
now pour out hundreds of streams.

**15.5.** That head whose enchanting top-knot captivated the world —
now without hair: everything turned upside down!

**15.6.** Why has He changed yellow garments for saffron cloth,
why has He changed the dark form for a golden hue?

**15.7.** Balarama Dasa says: I do not know the reason —
the reason for it is she whose colour it is.[^13-34]

[^13-33]: PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 288 (printed p. 277), 21st pallava, label "॥৩৭॥২২৫৪॥", raga suhai, MS P-R-Sa no. 2309. GPT1 — p. 289, no. 39
(gandhara), checked against the scan (PDF p. 548); GPT2 — sec. 4.3, no. 39. In the catalogue (BD-024) the pada was listed as "GPT only"
(in chapter 8 the erroneous link to PK 764 — a pada of Vasu Ghosha with the same opening, translated in chapter 8 — was
corrected); it is found in PK — **core** (C). Kalindi is the Yamuna; the kadamba is the tree of Krishna's plays; the ocean shore is
Puri.
[^13-34]: The poet's answer: Gaura is Krishna who has taken Radha's colour and bhava, and He weeps from Her prema (CC Adi 4). Ananga
(Kamadeva) is the god of love; "swooned" — an image of Krishna's beauty, which captivates Cupid himself (Madana-mohana). The
Lord's sannyasa and tears are not the sorrow of a conditioned soul but prema.

## 16. Yadunatha Dasa — "prabhāte jāgila gorācām̐da…" (GPT1 p. 349, no. 18)
*The Lord's morning in Navadvipa: Gorachand has awoken, and all see Him quite different; His eyes, red with sleep, are
half-closed, He stretches like the golden bow of the god of love; the devotees come at dawn; having washed, Gaurahari sits
in the circle of His own. Raga suhai.*[^13-35]

**16.1.** At dawn Gorachand awoke,
and all see Him quite different.

**16.2.** His eyes, reddened with sleep, keep closing,
the lids half-shut with languor.

**16.3.** Interlacing His fingers, He stretches His whole body —
like the golden bow of Ananga.[^13-36]

**16.4.** The devotees came to see Him
and gathered joyfully in the morning.

**16.5.** Having washed His face, Gaurahari
sits down — and His own surround Him on all sides.

**16.6.** Such are the plays in the town of Nadia;
Yadunatha sees them always, being close by.[^13-37]

[^13-35]: GPT1 — p. 349, section "Ashtakaliya" (morning), no. 18 (suhai), checked against the scan (PDF p. 608); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 18. The
pada is not in BR, KGC or PS; **it is in PK — PK 2512** (vol. 4, 30th pallava "Aṣṭakālīya nitya-līlā," "atha divāyāṃ yathā," raga
bibhasa, PDF p. 56, label "॥৩৯॥২৫১২॥"; found in the full PK check of chapter 16 — M-1961's reference is correct; catalogue: YD-003). PK
reads "herai sakale vayana chānda" ("all look upon the form of His face") and "yadunātha dekhe gadāi pāśa" ("Yadunatha sees it beside
Gadai," that is, Gadadhara); the main text is kept after GPT1, the PK readings are in the full version of the book. The preceding GPT pada (no. 17) is by Ghanashyama, the following (no. 19) by Narahari.
[^13-36]: Ananga is the god of love; the comparison with his bow is a traditional image of a slender, curving body.
[^13-37]: The signature seems to speak of the poet as an eyewitness of the Navadvipa plays; on this ground M-1961 considers Yadunatha
a contemporary of the Lord (Yadunatha Kavichandra is mentioned among the Lord's associates in CB). GPT only — C.

## 17. Murari — "calila nadīyāra loka gaurāṅga dekhite…" (GPT1 pp. 378–379, no. 42)
*After the sannyasa: at Nityananda's word the people of Nadia go to Shantipura to see Gauranga — Shachi in front, everyone
after her; on every lip is "Ha Gauranga!"; without Gauranga they were living dead and seem to have revived at Nitai's words;
Nadia is emptied, and behind them all goes Murari. Raga dhanashi.*[^13-38]

**17.1.** The people of Nadia set out to see Gauranga:
Shachi in front, and all the rest behind.

**17.2.** "Ha Gauranga, ha Gauranga!" is on every lip;
streams pour from their eyes, the heart bursts with grief.

**17.3.** Without Gauranga they had been living dead —
and at Nitai's words they seemed to come back to life.

**17.4.** In the heart one desire: to see Gauranga's face;
all hurry to Shantipura, breathless with running.

**17.5.** The town of Nadia was emptied of its men;
behind them all, following, went Murari.[^13-39]

[^13-38]: GPT1 — pp. 378–379, section on the sannyasa, no. 42 (dhanashi), checked against the scan (PDF pp. 637–638); GPT2 — sec. 5.3, no. 42.
The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS (catalogue: MU-008). It continues no. 40 (PK 2231, "prabhure rākhiyā śāntipure," signed by Murari;
chapter 6, no. 20), where Nityananda comes to Nadia to call everyone to Shantipura. Majumdar considers Murari Gupta's authorship
unproven (C).
[^13-39]: Nityananda brought Shachi and the people of Navadvipa to Shantipura, to Advaita, where the Lord was after His sannyasa — CC
Madhya 3; CB Antya 1. "Behind them all went Murari" — Murari Gupta as a witness (or the poet's signature).

## 18. Yadunatha Dasa — "āsive āmāra gaurāṅgasundara…" (GPT1 p. 412, no. 29)
*Waiting: my Gaurangasundara will come to Nadia! Seeing Him from afar I shall perform the auspicious rites — set out water-pots
with mango twigs, plant banana saplings, hang garlands; the women of Nadia will run to see, in every house "Hari, Hari!" will
resound; His mother will rush to Him, embrace Him, bathe Him in tears and take Him home; Yadunatha, looking on, will fall
down and take His lotus feet. Raga turi.*[^13-40]

**18.1.** My Gaurangasundara will come to the town of Nadia!
Seeing Him from afar, thrilled, I shall perform the auspicious rites.

**18.2.** I shall fill water-pots, set mango twigs in them, and arrange them in rows;
I shall bring banana saplings, plant them, and hang garlands on them.

**18.3.** Hearing that He has come, the women of Nadia will come running to see;
cries of "Hari, Hari!" and "Jaya, jaya!" will rise in every house.

**18.4.** Hearing it, His mother will at once rush to Him and take Him in her arms;
bathing His body in her tears, she will quickly lead Him home.

**18.5.** All the devotees, seeing Him, will rejoice in the bliss of prema;
Yadunatha, looking on, will fall prostrate and take His lotus feet.[^13-41]

[^13-40]: GPT1 — p. 412, no. 29 (turi), checked against the scan (PDF p. 671); GPT2 — no. 29 (OCR, line 44957). The pada is not in
BR, KGC or PS; **it is in PK — PK 1976** (vol. 3, 12th pallava "Bhāvollāsa," raga turi, PDF pp. 182–183, printed pp. 171–172, label
"॥৮॥১৯৭৬॥"; found in the full PK check of chapter 16; catalogue: YD-004; M-1961 mentions this pada under Yadunatha's name). The PK
signature reads "yadunātha yāñā paṛi loṭāiyā" ("Yadunatha, coming, will fall…"; GPT "cāñā," "looking"); the other PK readings are in
bn/13.md. C. Water-pots with mango twigs
(pūrṇakumbha) and banana saplings at the entrance are Bengali rites of welcome.
[^13-41]: The pada is a dream of the Lord's return (cf. CC Madhya 16: the Lord comes to Gauda and meets His mother at Kuliya). The speaker
is a devotee of Nadia (perhaps the poet himself); the "women of Nadia" here are townswomen, not "nagaris" in the sense of
nagari-bhava.

## 19. Balarama Dasa — "rūpe guṇe anupamā lakṣmī-koṭi-manoramā…" (PK 2299; GPT1 pp. 426–427, no. 43; KGC 23.2)
*On Nityananda: He with whom countless maidens of Vraja sported in the rasa-lila — why has He become an avadhuta? The teacher
of all lovers, the wish-fulfilling tree of rasa — why does He wander in renunciation? Balarama, from whose chapters come
Sankarshana and Shesha, who dwells eternally in Goloka — why is He in the midst of sankirtana? Nityananda has plunged everyone
into the rasa of Gaura — only the poet is left aside. Raga kalyani (in KGC and GPT1 — gandhara).*[^13-42]

**19.1.** Peerless in beauty and virtue, more charming than millions of Lakshmis — the maidens of Vraja, tens of thousands —
He with whom they sported in the joy of the rasa-lila — why has that Lord become an avadhuta?[^13-43]

**19.2.** Hari, Hari! To whom shall I tell this sorrow?
The teacher of all lovers, the wish-fulfilling tree of rasa — why does He wander in renunciation?

**19.3.** Sankarshana and Shesha are incarnations of His chapters and parts; He dwells eternally in Goloka —
Krishna's elder brother, Mahaprabhu Balarama — why is Nitai in the midst of sankirtana?

**19.4.** Beyond the reach of Shiva and Brahma, beyond the agamas and nigamas — in the Kali age, Sri Nityananda:
He has plunged every single person into the rasa of Gaura — aside has remained only Balarama, the unworthy.[^13-44]

[^13-42]: PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 303 (printed p. 292), 23rd pallava, label "॥৬॥২২৯৯॥", raga kalyani. KGC — 23rd kshanada, no. 2 (p. 180, gandhara;
tesseract kgc.txt, line 6326). GPT1 — pp. 426–427, section on Nityananda, no. 43 (pahira or gandhara); GPT2 — sec. 6.1, no. 43. In KGC
and GPT stanzas 19.3 and 19.4 are rearranged by half-lines (the second halves of 19.3 and 19.4 change places). The pada was missing
from the catalogue (new row); core (PK, KGC), C.
[^13-43]: Nityananda is Balarama; Balarama's rasa-lila with the maidens of Vraja — Bhag. 10.65 (Balarama, coming from Dvaraka to Vraja, spent
two spring months in the rasa-lila with the gopis). The question "why has He become an avadhuta" is poetic wonder, not doubt.
[^13-44]: According to CC (Adi 5) Nityananda-Balarama is the source of Sankarshana, Maha-Vishnu and Shesha. "Balarama, the unworthy" (valarāma manda)
is the poet himself; a play on names: Balarama-Nityananda has saved everyone, while the poet Balarama is left aside.

## 20. Balarama Dasa — "gajendra-gamane yāya sakaruṇa-diṭhe cāya…" (PK 2298; GPT1 p. 427, no. 44)
*The Avadhuta comes, an ocean of mercy: with the gait of a king of elephants, with compassion in His glance, shaking the earth; His
roar frightens the unbelievers, He floats in prema with the host of the immortals; this is Balarama, the son of Rohini, from whose
chapters come Sheshashayi and Sankarshana; now in the dress of a pauper He goes from land to land, saving the three worlds. If you
wish to attain the lilas of Vraja, serve His feet. Raga mangala.*[^13-45]

**20.1.** He walks with the gait of a king of elephants, He looks with compassion — at His steps the earth sways;
surpassing a maddened lion, He makes the earth tremble — the unbelievers, hearing it, lose their strength.

**20.2.** Here comes the Avadhuta — an ocean of mercy!
His mind overflowing with prema, He performs Hari-sankirtana — Purifier of the fallen, Friend of the destitute.

**20.3.** He walks roaring — the unmoving and the moving shake, the host of the immortals floats in prema;
with His companions, in the joy of many games, He unseen accomplishes every task.[^13-46]

**20.4.** Sheshashayi, Sankarshana, Narayana — the source of incarnations — are counted as chapters of His chapters;
ocean of mercy, Giver of bhakti, Benefactor of the world — this is Rama, the son of Rohini.

**20.5.** Whose lilas are an abode of beauty, sung by the agamas and nigamas, whose form enchants Madana himself —
now in the dress of one who owns nothing the Lord goes from land to land and saves the three worlds.

**20.6.** If in your heart there is the wish to attain the lilas of Vraja, the essence of all refinement,
says Balarama Dasa, the wish will be fulfilled: serve, serve the feet of Shripada.[^13-47]

[^13-45]: PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 302–303 (printed pp. 291–292), 23rd pallava, label "॥৫॥২২৯৮॥", raga mangala, MS P-R-Sa no. 2402. GPT1 — p. 427,
no. 44 (mangala); GPT2 — sec. 6.1, no. 44. The signature is garbled in the GPT1 OCR; by PK — "valarāma dāse kaya". The pada was missing from the
catalogue (new row); core (PK), C.
[^13-46]: "Unseen accomplishes every task" — Nityananda, playing with His companions, secretly fulfils the Lord's plan (the preaching of the
Name in Gauda).
[^13-47]: Shripada is a respectful name for Nityananda. According to CC (Adi 5–6) Nityananda's mercy is the way to the service of Radha and
Krishna in Vraja.

## 21. Balarama Dasa — "vandiva advaita śire ye ānilā dhīre dhīre…" (PK 2348; GPT1 p. 449, no. 35)
*Praise of Advaita: I bow to Advaita, who brought Mahaprabhu to the earth — the son of Nanda become the son of Shachi; He saved the
high and the low by the gift of bhakti; the flood of prema is from Nitai, Advaita its wave, the wind of Chaitanya has raised it to the
sky: the worlds of the nagas, men and gods have drowned, the flood of prema has filled Goloka — only Balarama has been left out. Raga
"tatha" (in GPT1 — mangala).*[^13-48]

**21.1.** I bow my head to Advaita, who slowly, gradually brought Mahaprabhu to the earth —
Him who is the son of Nanda and also the son of Shachi, whose friend is Nityananda Raya.[^13-49]

**21.2.** My Lord is Advaita Gosani!
The high and the low He saved by the gift of bhakti — there is no other giver so merciful.

**21.3.** He brought the high and the low together in embrace — and all the blind and the deaf;
the lame set off running and, making all call "Hari, Hari!", dance with both arms raised.

**21.4.** The flood of prema is from Nitai, Advaita is a wave in it, the wind of Chaitanya raises it high;
the waves touch the sky, in heaven no one can escape — they have pierced the seven netherworlds.

**21.5.** The worlds of the nagas, of men and of gods have drowned, the flood of prema has filled Goloka;
some dance, some sing, some laugh, some run — and the earth is especially blessed.

**21.6.** He who performs such plays is Advaita Acharya, an endless, boundless abode of rasa;
by such a flood of prema all the unmoving and the moving are blessed — Balarama alone has been left out.

[^13-48]: PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 320–321 (printed pp. 309–310), beginning of the 24th pallava "Description of the qualities of Sri Advaita," label
"॥১॥২৩৪৮॥", raga "tathā", MSS P-R-Sa no. 2452 and P-R no. 18. GPT1 — pp. 449–450, section on the associates, no. 35 (mangala), checked against the
scan (PDF pp. 708–709); GPT2 — sec. 6.3, no. 35. In the catalogue (BD-029) it was listed as "GPT only"; it is found in PK — **core** (C).
[^13-49]: Advaita by His prayers (with Ganga water and tulasi leaves) called the Lord to the earth — CC Adi 3; CB Adi 2. "Slowly" (dhīre dhīre) — by
long worship.

## 22. Balarama Dasa — "bhāvera āveśe vahu sītāpati mora pahum̐…" (GPT1 p. 450, no. 36)
*Advaita announces the advent: absorbed in bhava, the husband of Sita sat in a yogic posture — and suddenly with a thunderous roar He
sprang up: "I have brought Him, brought Him to the earth! He who will save the world has risen in Nadia!" — and He dances; at His dance
the earth trembles, men and women dance with the Lord of Shantipura; Advaita's roar has pierced the seven heavens and resounded in the
Paravyoma — the three worlds have learned of Mahaprabhu's coming. Raga suhai.*[^13-50]

**22.1.** Absorbed in bhava, the husband of Sita, my Lord, sat in a yogic posture;
suddenly — what bhava in His heart? — with a thunderous roar of "hum-hum" He abruptly sprang up.

**22.2.** "I have brought Him, brought Him to the circle of the earth!
He who will save the world has risen in Nadia!" — saying this He dances with arms upraised.

**22.3.** At His violent dance the mortal world quaked, the earth cannot bear the weight;
with the Lord of Shantipura men and women dance merrily — as if a market of bliss had opened.

**22.4.** At Advaita's roar the seven heavens are pierced, a ringing has reached the Paravyoma;
the three worlds have learned of Mahaprabhu's coming — boundless is Balarama's joy.[^13-51]

[^13-50]: GPT1 — p. 450, no. 36 (suhai), checked against the scan (PDF p. 709); GPT2 — sec. 6.3, no. 36. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS
(catalogue: BD-030); C. Before it in GPT (no. 34) is a short unsigned pada on the joy of Advaita and Sita on the night of the Lord's
appearance.
[^13-51]: Paravyoma is the spiritual sky, Vaikuntha. Advaita, learning of the Lord's appearance, dances in Shantipura — CB Adi 2; CC Adi 13 (on
the night of the appearance Advaita and Haridasa dance in Shantipura).

## 23. Balarama Dasa — "rūpa sanātana saṅge śrījīva gosāñi…" (GPT1 p. 466, no. 39)
*The books of Sri Jiva: together with Rupa and Sanatana, Sri Jiva Gosani wrote countless books on bhakti; for his purification the
poet names some: *Gopala-virudavali*, *Krishna-pada-chihna*, *Sri Madhava-mahotsava*, *Radha-pada-chihna*, *Gopala-champu*,
*Rasamrita-shesha*, *Kripambudhi-stava*, *Sapta-sandarbha*, *Sutramalika*, *Dhatu-sangraha*, *Krishnarchana*, *Sankalpa-kalpavriksha*,
*Harinamamrita-vyakarana*: he opened the gates of bhakti. Raga velaor.*[^13-52]

**23.1.** Together with Rupa and Sanatana, Sri Jiva Gosani
wrote so many books on bhakti that they cannot be counted.

**23.2.** Wishing in my heart to be purified,
I shall glorify the names of a few books.

**23.3.** *Gopala-virudavali*, *Krishna-pada-chihna*,
*Sri Madhava-mahotsava*, *Radha-pada-chihna*;

**23.4.** *Sri Gopala-champu*, and *Rasamrita-shesha*,
*Kripambudhi-stava*, and especially the *Sapta-sandarbha*;

**23.5.** *Sutramala*, *Dhatu-sangraha*, *Krishnarchana*,
*Sankalpa-kalpavriksha*, *Harinama-vyakarana*.

**23.6.** All these books he wrote — how many names shall I tell?
He opened the gates of bhakti, says Balarama.[^13-53]

[^13-52]: GPT1 — p. 466, section on the associates and followers, no. 39 (velaor), checked against the scan (PDF p. 725); GPT2 — sec. 6.3, no. 39.
The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS (catalogue: BD-031). A pada on the writings of Jiva Gosvami (after the Lord's departure) is not
Gaura-lila in the narrow sense; a poet who lists Jiva's books lived no earlier than the end of the 16th century (C).
[^13-53]: Titles: *Gopala-virudavali*, *Madhava-mahotsava*, *Gopala-champu*, *Sankalpa-kalpavriksha*, *Hari-namamrita-vyakarana*,
*Sutramalika*, *Dhatu-sangraha* are well-known works of Jiva; *Rasamrita-shesha* is his supplement to the *Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu*;
*Krishnarchana-dipika* is a manual of worship; *Krishna-* and *Radha-pada-chihna* describe the marks on the feet; the *Sapta-sandarbha* is
probably the *Shat-sandarbha* (six sandarbhas) together with the *Krama-sandarbha*; the *Kripambudhi-stava* is perhaps one of Jiva's hymns.
Cf. CC Adi 10.85; Madhya 1.

## 24. Ramachandra — "hāhā mora ki chāra adṛṣṭa…" (GPT1 p. 492, no. 25)
*A prayer: alas, how wretched my lot — when Gaura appeared, I was not born; I did not see Gaurachandra, nor Nityananda, nor
Advaita, nor Thakura Sarakara, nor Srivasa and Gadai; the essence of all incarnations, the Sri Gauranga-avatara, I did not
see; I am the grandson of Vamshivadana, the Lord's dear associate — so why is Ramachandra so base? Raga dhanashi.*[^13-54]

**24.1.** Alas, alas, how wretched is my lot!
When Gaura appeared, I was not born — therefore I am low and sinful.

**24.2.** I did not see Gaurachandra, did not see Nityananda, did not see Advaita Gosani;
the feet of Thakura Sarakara I did not see, did not see Srivasa and Gadai.

**24.3.** What fate has karma written for me — none of them did I see; why was I born alone?
The essence of all incarnations, the incarnation of Sri Gauranga, I did not see — why did I not die?

**24.4.** The Lord's dear associate is Thakura Vamshivadana: I am his son's son.
O Gaura, O Nityananda! Why then is Ramachandra so dull of mind, so wicked?[^13-55]

[^13-54]: GPT1 — p. 492, section of prayers (prārthanā), no. 25 (dhanashi), checked against the scan (PDF p. 751); GPT2 — sec. 7, no. 25. The pada
is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS (catalogue: RC-003). The poet says plainly that he was born after the Lord's departure and that he is the
grandson of Vamshivadana (Vamshi Dasa) — this is **Ramachandra Gosvami** (Ramai), Vamshivadana's grandson and Jahnava's adopted son
(16th–17th c.), not a contemporary of the Lord; cf. the padas signed "Ramachandra" PK 2064, 2186 (chapters 1, 7), which sound like
eyewitness accounts — apparently another poet. Attribution by GPT (C).
[^13-55]: "Thakura Sarakara" is Narahari Sarakara of Shrikhanda. Vamshivadana Thakura is the Lord's associate, guardian of Shachi and Vishnupriya
after the sannyasa (according to tradition). "Dull of mind," "wicked" are the poet's formulas of humility about himself.

## 25. Ramachandra — "prabhura lāgiyā yāva kon deśe…" (GPT1 pp. 492–493, no. 26)
*A prayer of longing: to what land shall I go for the Lord, who will show me the way? Will I have the fortune to see Gauranga's
feet? Gora is my master, Gora my refuge, Gora my whole wealth; if I do not see Him, I shall give up this wretched life; let my soul,
becoming a bird, fly to where He is and serve Him; let my body mingle with the dust of His feet. Raga dhanashi.*[^13-56]

**25.1.** For the Lord, to what land shall I go, who will show me the way?
Shall I see Gauranga's feet — will I have such fortune?

**25.2.** Gora is my master, Gora my refuge, Gora my whole wealth;
and if I cannot see Him, I shall give up this wretched life.

**25.3.** My soul, becoming a bird, will fly to the land where the Lord dwells,
and will always be near the Lord, having become His servant.

**25.4.** With the dust of Gauranga's feet this wretched body of mine will mingle;
says Ramachandra: tasting the honey of His lotus feet, I shall lose myself.[^13-57]

[^13-56]: GPT1 — pp. 492–493, no. 26 (dhanashi), checked against the scan (PDF pp. 751–752); GPT2 — sec. 7, no. 26. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or
PS; it was missing from the catalogue (new row RC-007). Its position next to no. 25 suggests the same Ramachandra (Vamshivadana's grandson);
attribution by GPT (C).
[^13-57]: "Master" (pati) — here "lord, refuge" in the spirit of dasya, not in the sense of nagari-bhava. "To what land shall I go for the Lord" —
the longing of a poet who lived after the Lord's departure; cf. Narottama Dasa's prayers to Gaura.

## 26. Balarama Dasa — "bhāi re sādhusaṅga kara sādhu haiyā…" (GPT1 pp. 515–516, no. 59)
*A prayer-instruction: brothers, keep the company of saints, becoming saints yourselves — you will cross the ocean of existence,
singing of Nitai and Chaitanya; having obtained, after eight million four hundred thousand births, the rare human body, do not waste
it; I wear beads and marks, but there is no trace of devotion in me — like the makal fruit: handsome outside, worthless within; sandal
makes all the trees around it like itself — but Balarama, without the company of saints, has remained in the well of existence. Raga
kamoda.*[^13-58]

**26.1.** Brothers, keep the company of saints, becoming saints yourselves:
you will cross the ocean of existence and find great bliss, singing the glories of Nitai and Chaitanya.

**26.2.** Weary of wandering through eight million four hundred thousand births, you have at last obtained the rare body;
laying all upon the great and not walking the path of bhakti, you let your life pass in vain.[^13-59]

**26.3.** Wearing beads and marks, but having not a trace of devotion, I go about showing myself to people —
like the makal fruit: red, handsome and fine to look at, but break it open — fit only to be thrown away.

**26.4.** The trees and creepers growing near the sandal tree it makes like itself by its breeze;
but this essence — the company of saints — wretched Balarama has not: he has remained in the well of existence.[^13-60]

[^13-58]: GPT1 — pp. 515–516, section of prayers, no. 59 (kamoda), checked against the scan (PDF pp. 774–775); GPT2 — sec. 7, no. 59. The pada is not in
PK, BR, KGC or PS (catalogue: BD-033). A prayer of general content; its refrain (the names of Nitai and Chaitanya) links it to Gaura, and so it
is translated; other prayers signed by Balarama without Gaura content are not translated (see the catalogue). C.
[^13-59]: 8,400,000 species of life — Padma Purana; CC Madhya 19. "Laying all upon the great" (mahatera dāya diyā) — the sense is not quite clear:
probably "relying on the mercy of the great but making no effort of one's own."
[^13-60]: The makal is a fruit handsome outside and inedible within — an image of feigned piety. The sandal tree that makes the neighbouring trees
fragrant is an image of the company of saints (sadhu-sanga), CC Madhya 22.
