# Chapter 14. Vamshidasa, Nayanananda, Shivananda, Yadu, Govinda and Vasu Ghosha, Krishnadasa, Kanu Dasa and Others: Padas from the *Gaura-pada-tarangini* — Completing the "GPT Only" Group

*This chapter completes the group of padas by poets other than Narahari that are known from the *Gaura-pada-tarangini*
(GPT1 — 1st ed. by Jagadbandhu Bhadra, 1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934), excluding padas in nagari-bhava. The padas follow the
order of the lilas: mangalacharana and praise of the Gaura-avatara, Gaura's form, the abhisheka in Srivasa's house and the
adhivasa of the kirtana of the "seven groups," Gaura with Gauridasa in the bhava of Krishna and of Radha, the goshtha-bhava and the
festival of colours, the decision to take sannyasa and the lament after it, the Ratha-yatra in Puri, Nityananda (His marriage — in
a pada that Majumdar considers a forgery — His dance and His mercy), Ramananda Raya. Seven padas are signed "Yadu" (nos. 4, 5,
20–23, 26); five of them are also in the *Padakalpataru* (PK 2459, 2460, 1546, 1547, 2300; and PK 1548 without signature, no. 23) —
there the text follows PK with the GPT variants; who this "Yadu" is — Yadunatha Kavichandra, a contemporary of the Lord, or the
later Yadunandana — is not established. Checking against the text of GPT1 showed that the stage-1 catalogue had ascribed to Vamshi,
Gauridasa, Paramananda and Narahari a good many padas of other poets: of the seven padas of "Vamshi," six belong to others
(Vaishnava Dasa, Premadasa, Rajavallabha, Govinda Dasa, Vasu Ghosha, or are unsigned); instead, a goshtha-pada of Vamshidasa
(no. 15) is translated, and the pada "āhā mari kothā gela gorā kām̐cā sonā" (no. 19 — "Vamshi" in the catalogue) is signed by Vasu
Ghosha; the padas of "Gauridasa" are signed by Jagannatha Dasa and Chaitanyadasa, those of "Paramananda" by Vrindavana Dasa and
Gopala Dasa. Four padas (nos. 9, 17, 23, 26) were missing from the catalogue.
Majumdar considers the GPT unreliable for attribution; the attribution of all the padas of this chapter is therefore provisional
(C; D only where authenticity itself is in doubt: an added signature, a forgery). The Bengali original, the variants of GPT1/GPT2 and PK,
and the word-for-word translation are in
bn/14.md.*

## 1. Vamshidasa — "jaya re jaya re mora gaurāṅga rāya…" (GPT1 p. 5, no. 8)
*Mangalacharana: glory to Gauranga, to Nityananda and to Gaura's devotees; the poet asks Sitanatha — Advaita Acharya — to
give him the shade of His feet and to keep his wicked mind there: he has no other hope. Raga kamoda.*[^14-1]

**1.1.** Glory, glory to my Gauranga Raya!
Glory to Nityananda the moon, glory to Gaura's devotees! Sitanatha, give me the shade of Your feet!

**1.2.** Glory, glory to my Acharya Thakura! I am helpless, utterly fallen:
be merciful — keep this sinful mind of mine at Your feet.[^14-2]

**1.3.** In Your feet alone I trust — I see no other way;
keep my wicked mind at Your holy feet — this I beg at Your feet.

**1.4.** Whatever I long for at all times — all of it You know.
Says Vamshidasa: fulfil all my hopes — what more shall I say?

[^14-1]: GPT1 — p. 5, section of mangalacharana, no. 8 (kamoda), checked against the scan IA in.ernet.dli.2015.477854 (PDF p. 264);
GPT2 — sec. 1.2, no. 8. The pada is not in PK, the *Bhakti-ratnakara* (BR), the *Kshanada-gita-chintamani* (KGC) or the
*Padamrita-samudra* (PS) (catalogue: VV-001). Under the signature "Vamshi, Vamshidasa" there are padas of Vamshivadana Thakura, the
Lord's associate, and of a later Vamshidasa (by Majumdar, PK 2851 is his; see chapter 6, no. 16); this pada is a prayer with no
sign of an eyewitness; attribution by GPT (C).
[^14-2]: "Acharya Thakura" — by the refrain (Sitanatha, the husband of Sita) this is Advaita Acharya. After the Lord's sannyasa
Vamshivadana lived with Shachi and Vishnupriya in Navadvipa (according to tradition); a prayer to Advaita is possible from him, but the pada
may also belong to a disciple of Advaita's line.

## 2. Nayanananda — "gorā mora guṇera sāgara…" (GPT1 p. 31, no. 15)
*Praise of Gaura in images: He is an ocean of virtues where waves of prema rise; a spotless moon pouring the nectar of the
holy name; the Himalayan peak from which the Ganga of prema flows; a wish-fulfilling tree; a new cloud that cools everyone; a
mine of bliss. Raga dhanashi.*[^14-3]

**2.1.** My Gora is an ocean of virtues:
in it waves of prema rise without cease.

**2.2.** My Gora is a spotless moon:
day and night the nectar of Hari's name drips from it.

**2.3.** My Gora is the peak of the Himalayas:
from it the Ganga of prema flows without cease.

**2.4.** My Gora is a wish-fulfilling tree that gives prema:
in the shade of His feet living beings dwell happily.

**2.5.** My Gora is a new rain-cloud:
pouring rain, He cools men and women.

**2.6.** My Gora is a mine of bliss:
Nayanananda's life is given for Him as a ransom.[^14-4]

[^14-3]: GPT1 — p. 31, section of praise of the Gaura-avatara, no. 15 (dhanashi), checked against the scan (PDF p. 290); GPT2 — sec. 1.3,
no. 15. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS (catalogue: NN-003). Nayanananda Mishra is the nephew and disciple of Gadadhara
Pandita; his padas on Gaura in PK were translated in chapters 4 and 10. This pada is known only from the GPT (C).
[^14-4]: "Given as a ransom" (nichani) — a rite in which something dear is waved around the beloved and given away to avert harm from
him: the poet gives his life for Gaura. In 2.1 GPT1 has "guṇera nāgara" (a misprint or misreading), GPT2 "guṇera sāgara": the image of an
ocean with waves requires "sagara."

## 3. Shivananda — "akhila bhuvana bhari hari-rasa-vādara…" (GPT1 p. 35, no. 25)
*The cloud of Chaitanya: a downpour of Hari's rasa has filled the universe, and the devotees, like chataka birds, drink and ask
for more; the cloud was born on the full moon of Phalguna and flooded high and low with prema; the holy name became the
maha-mantra, prema was given out by handfuls, the fallen became bhagavatas, Jagai and Madhai were saved; the poet laments
that he has remained in forgetfulness. Raga mangala.*[^14-5]

**3.1.** Filling the universe, a downpour of Hari's rasa pours from the cloud of Chaitanya;
the devotees, like chataka birds, drink and drink without end, every moment begging for the water of prema.

**3.2.** The full moon of Phalguna is the cloud's birthday; that cloud poured the downpour:
high and low — it flooded all with the water of prema: Gora is a great ocean of mercy.

**3.3.** Making living beings His yantra and Hari's name the maha-mantra, He gave prema by handfuls from hand to hand;
all the low and wretched became bhagavatas — so Gauranga's glory grew.[^14-6]

**3.4.** There were Jagai and Madhai — them too He saved with prema: such mercy He showed to living beings.
Says Shivananda-dasa: why have I remained in the forgetfulness of maya? Lord, give me the shade of Your feet![^14-7]

[^14-5]: GPT1 — p. 35, no. 25 (mangala), checked against the scan (PDF p. 294); GPT2 — sec. 1.3, no. 25. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or
PS. In the catalogue (SS-001) the first line was wrong: "iha kaliyuga dhana nityānanda caitanya" is the preceding GPT pada (no. 24), signed by
Haridasa; the pada signed "dāsa śivānanda" is no. 25. Whether this is Shivananda Sena, the father of Kavi Karnapura, is unclear (C);
Majumdar considers Shivananda Sena the author of padas on the Lord composed in His lifetime.
[^14-6]: The full moon of Phalguna is the day of the Lord's appearance (1486). "Yantra" and "mantra" — an image from ritual: as a sacred
diagram and a mantra serve worship, so living beings became the Lord's vessel and Hari's name the great mantra. The sense of the
line is not quite clear. A footnote in GPT1 gives "durgata" (distressed) for "duḥkhita" (wretched). "Glory" (ṭhākurāli) — the Lord's
majesty, lordship.
[^14-7]: Jagai and Madhai — CB Madhya 13; CC Adi 17. "The forgetfulness of maya" (māyā-bhole) — the poet of himself: "maya" here in the
everyday sense — forgetting God and attachment to the world; it has nothing to do with the Lord.

## 4. Yadu — "eke se kanayā-kaṣila tanu…" (PK 2459; GPT1 p. 120, no. 27)
*Gauranga's form: His body like gold tested on the touchstone, outshining the moon; curls tied in a knot, garments of red silk;
raising His arms He stretches — and lightning seems to flash; the gaze slips over His body, over which waves run; all pride is
broken. Raga "the same" (in GPT1, "yatharaga").*[^14-8]

**4.1.** First of all, His body, like gold tested on the touchstone:
as if it subdues even the spotless moon.

**4.2.** And then — the curly locks tied in a knot:
even a trace of that beauty intoxicates the playful fair ones.[^14-9]

**4.3.** How wondrous is Gauranga's beauty —
coveted by the fair women of the three worlds!

**4.4.** In the guise of His red silk garment
the red passion of young hearts seems to overflow.

**4.5.** Raising His arms, He stretches His whole body —
and in its radiance lightning seems to flash.

**4.6.** The gaze cast upon His body slips off:
over all His body waves run in play.

**4.7.** A lovely garland of keshara flowers —
says Yadu: all pride is broken.[^14-10]

[^14-8]: PK — vol. 4 (pt. 2), 4th shakha, 29th pallava, mark "॥২॥২৪৫৯॥," raga "tatha," checked against the scan IA 354459 (PDF p. 35,
printed p. 26); in PK the pada stands among the gaura-chandrikas to the description of beauty (before it, Premadasa's PK 2458;
after it, PK 2460 and the description of Radha's beauty, "atha śrīrādhāyāṃ yathā"). GPT1 — p. 120, section on Gaura's form, no. 27
("yatharaga"), scan PDF p. 379; GPT2 — sec. 3.1, no. 27. The pada is not in BR, KGC or PS (catalogue: YD-008). The signature "yadu" (Yadu)
may belong to Yadunatha Kavichandra, a contemporary of the Lord (M-1961 ascribes to him padas on Gaura's bhavas), or to the later
poet Yadunandana Dasa (17th c.); PK 2459–2460 show no sign of an eyewitness; C.
[^14-9]: "Playful fair ones" (raṅgiṇī), "young hearts" (4.4), "pride" (4.7) — the motif of the townswomen captivated by Gaura's beauty:
the language of nagari-bhava (Gaura as nagara); we translate faithfully to the author. Vrindavana Dasa stresses that in this
incarnation the Lord never looked at another man's wife; worship of Gaura in the spirit of "gaura-nagari" is not accepted by the
Gaudiya tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta). In PK the pada is a gaura-chandrika: it sets the tone
for the description of the beauty of Radha and Krishna, and the attraction here is an image of prema for Krishna, not of a worldly
feeling. "Knot" (loṭana) — hair gathered in a knot; "cām̐cara keśa" — curly locks.
[^14-10]: "Red silk… red passion" — a play on words: "raga" means both "red colour" and "attraction, love." Keshara — the nagakeshara flower
(or kadamba). "Pride is broken" (bhāṅgala māna) — "mana," the beloved's offended pride, melts before Gaura's beauty. PK manuscripts:
"ka" — "chāla," "uchāla," "araṅga" for "chale," "uchale," "taraṅga"; "kha, gha, cha" — "madana" for "damana" (4.1: "subdues Madana").

## 5. Yadu — "vikaca kanayā-kamala-kām̐ti…" (PK 2460; GPT1 p. 120, no. 28)
*Gauranga's form and bhava: the lustre of a full-blown golden lotus, a face like the full moon, teeth like pomegranate seeds,
lips redder than the bandhuli; He walks intoxicated with an unknown rasa, with the gait of a king of elephants; tears flow from
His reddish eyes; remembering His former love He weeps, thundering like a new cloud, and calls: "Where is Gadadhara?" Raga
"the same."*[^14-11]

**5.1.** A lustre like that of a full-blown golden lotus,
a face shining like the full moon.

**5.2.** Teeth in an even row, like pomegranate seeds,
lips red — redder than the bandhuli flower.[^14-12]

**5.3.** Sweet, sweet is Gauranga's beauty —
coveted by the eyes of the three worlds.

**5.4.** Who knows with what rasa He is ever intoxicated? —
His gait is slow, like a king of elephants'.

**5.5.** From His reddish eyes tears stream —
is it a pair of chakoras pouring out nectar?[^14-13]

**5.6.** Remembering His former love, He weeps —
as a new cloud thunders.

**5.7.** "Where is Gadadhara?" He calls.
Says Yadu: the Lord is caught in a whirlpool.[^14-14]

[^14-11]: PK — vol. 4 (pt. 2), 29th pallava, mark "॥৩॥২৪৬০॥," raga "tatha," checked against the scan (PDF pp. 35–36); GPT1 — p. 120, no. 28
("tatharaga"); GPT2 — sec. 3.1, no. 28. The pada is not in BR, KGC or PS (catalogue: YD-009); attribution as for the preceding (C).
[^14-12]: "Shikhara" (śikhara) — in poetics, a ruby the colour of a ripe pomegranate seed; PK manuscripts "ka, kha" and the GPT: "daśana sikara nikara"
(a row of drops), "cha": "śikara." Bandhuli — a red flower (Pentapetes phoenicea), a common image for lips. "Redder" (āti = ati; "ka, kha": "ati").
[^14-13]: Chakoras — birds that drink moonlight; Gaura's eyes are a pair of chakoras on the moon of His face. GPT: "āsiyā vase ki cakora jorā" —
"has a pair of chakoras come and settled?"
[^14-14]: "Former love" — the love of Vrindavana: remembering His lila as Krishna, the Lord calls Gadadhara — the associate in whom the
tradition sees a manifestation of Radha (*Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika* 147–153). His tears and "thunder" are manifestations of prema,
not of worldly grief. "Caught in a whirlpool" (ṭhekilā pāke) — in the power of prema, unable to come out of it. PK MSS "ka, kha, cha": "lorā,"
"jorā"; "gha": "kānde ki."

## 6. Govinda Ghosha — "snāna kari śrīgaurāṅga vasilena divyāsane…" (GPT1 p. 240, no. 9)
*The abhisheka in Srivasa's house: after the bath Gauranga sits on a splendid seat with Nitai and Gadai to His right and left;
Advaita offers sweets and payasa, Srivasa runs to bring the dishes; Gora eats with Nitai and Gadai, Advaita gives Him tambula,
Narahari fans Him with a chamara, gazing at the three forms; Advaita places tulasi at His feet, saying "Krishnaya namah." Raga
mangala.*[^14-15]

**6.1.** Having bathed, Sri Gauranga sat on a splendid seat, with Nitai and Gadai to His right and left;
Advaita, seated before Him, holds sweets and payasa in His hands, Srivasa runs to and fro serving.

**6.2.** Ah, ah, what bliss of the abhisheka!
With Nitai and Gadai Gora sat down to eat — the devotees watch in bliss.

**6.3.** Having finished His meal, Gora rinsed His mouth, Advaita placed tambula in His mouth;
Narahari, standing beside, gazes at the three forms and joyfully fans Him with a chamara.[^14-16]

**6.4.** Placing tulasi leaves with sandal at Gora's feet, the Acharya says: "Krishnaya namah!"
Says Govinda Ghosha: and all, rejoicing, began to call out "Hari!" again and again.[^14-17]

[^14-15]: GPT1 — p. 240, section of the abhisheka, no. 9 (mangala), checked against the scan (PDF p. 499); GPT2 — sec. 4.1, no. 9. The pada is not
in PK, BR, KGC or PS (catalogue: GG-008). The preceding GPT pada (no. 8) is PK 1538 with the signature of the three Ghosha brothers
(chapter 1, no. 4), on the same scene: Gauranga on the throne after the abhisheka, the meal with Nityananda, tulasi from Advaita; this
pada is its continuation with the signature of Govinda Ghosha alone. Govinda Ghosha is the Lord's associate, an eyewitness according to
Majumdar; but the pada is known only from the GPT (C).
[^14-16]: Gadai — Gadadhara Pandita. "The three forms" — Gaura, Nitai and Gadai; Narahari Sarakara, the Lord's associate from Shrikhanda,
served Him with the chamara (CB Madhya 9 names Narahari among those present; cf. chapter 1, nos. 3–4). The abhisheka and the "great
revelation" (mahaprakasha) in Srivasa's house — CB Madhya 9; Murari 2.12; CC Adi 17.
[^14-17]: "Krishnaya namah" — "obeisance to Krishna": Advaita worships Gaura as Krishna Himself. The Acharya — Advaita Acharya.

## 7. Vasu Ghosha — "jaya jaya dhvani uṭhe nadīyā-nagare…" (GPT1 p. 240, no. 10)
*The abhisheka: cries of "Jaya!" throughout Nadia; Advaita roars: "I have brought Him!" — and dances, Haridasa after Him;
Srivasa and his brothers dance; devotees come running from all sides. Raga dhanashi.*[^14-18]

**7.1.** Cries of "Jaya, jaya!" have risen in the town of Nadia:
today is Gora's abhisheka in the Pandita's house.

**7.2.** "I have brought Him, brought Him!" cries Advaita Gosani;
He lets out a great roar, oblivious of everything around.[^14-19]

**7.3.** Arms raised, "Nara" dances — "ta-theiya, ta-theiya!";
behind Him Haridasa goes round, dancing.

**7.4.** Srivasa, Shripati, Shrinidhi and Shrirama
dance in delight — a joy to the eyes.

**7.5.** "Glory to Gauranga, glory to Advaita and Nitai!" —
crying so, the devotees come running.

**7.6.** Some dance and sing in prema, some laugh in prema;
the lila of Gora's abhisheka is sung by Vasu Ghosha.

[^14-18]: GPT1 — p. 240, no. 10 (dhanashi), checked against the scan (PDF p. 499); GPT2 — sec. 4.1, no. 10. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS
(catalogue: VG-165). The colloquial form "enechi, enechi" ("I have brought") is modern Bengali, unusual for the 16th century; by it the pada is
probably late or reworked; Majumdar warns that the GPT contains forgeries under Vasu's name; but this pada shows no sign of forgery. C.
[^14-19]: By His worship and His call Advaita "brought" the Lord to earth (CC Adi 3; CB Adi 2); for this the Lord called Him "Nara" (nāṛā, 7.3)
(CB, Madhya-khanda). "The Pandita" — Srivasa Pandita; Shripati, Shrinidhi and Shrirama are his brothers (CC Adi 10).

## 8. Vasu Ghosha — "gorā-abhiṣeka kathā adbhuta kathana…" (GPT1 p. 240, no. 11)
*The abhisheka: hearing the wonderful news, the devotees run to the Pandita's house and dance, crying "Glory to Gorachand!";
with them the whole universe dances — moon, sun, stars, Brahma, Indra, the gods, the nagas, the guardians of the quarters.
Raga dhanashi.*[^14-20]

**8.1.** Wonderful is the news — of Gora's abhisheka:
hearing it, the devotees run to the Pandita's house.

**8.2.** Running together, they dance joyfully;
raising both arms, they cry: "Glory to Gorachand!"

**8.3.** The moon dances, the sun dances, the stars dance;
Brahma dances, Vayu dances, the Thousand-eyed dances.

**8.4.** Aruna and Varuna dance, all the gods;
in the underworld Vasuki dances, the nagas dance.

**8.5.** Heaven dances, earth dances, the underworld dances;
in supreme bliss the guardians of the ten quarters dance.

**8.6.** In bliss the devotees roar out —
boundless is the joy in Vasu Ghosha's heart.[^14-21]

[^14-20]: GPT1 — p. 240, no. 11 (dhanashi), checked against the scan (PDF p. 499); GPT2 — sec. 4.1, no. 11. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS.
In the catalogue (VG-031) it was listed under section 3.2, "nagari-bhava" — wrongly: it is the abhisheka, section 4.1, with no nagari
motif; it had not been translated. GPT only (C).
[^14-21]: The Thousand-eyed — Indra; Aruna — the charioteer of the Sun; Varuna — lord of the waters; Vasuki — king of the naga serpents. The
rejoicing of the whole universe at the Lord's revelation — cf. CB Madhya 9 (the gods come to see the mahaprakasha).

## 9. Krishnadasa — "abhiṣeke gauracām̐dera ānanda apāra…" (GPT1 p. 241, no. 13)
*The abhisheka: Gaurachand in boundless bliss tells the devotees of His former plays; His body thrills, His speech falters;
listening to Him, the devotees' hearts are comforted. Raga suhai.*[^14-22]

**9.1.** At the abhisheka boundless is Gaurachand's bliss:
He tells the devotees of His former plays.[^14-23]

**9.2.** From head to foot His body thrilled:
the golden hairs stood like a kadamba bud.

**9.3.** The heart melts in bhava, the speech falters with emotion:
with great effort fate has fulfilled our hope.

**9.4.** Shachi's son Gora is the treasure of the life of all:
hearing the words of His moonlike mouth, the heart was comforted.

**9.5.** Whoever has come to believe in Gorachand's lila —
wretched Krishnadasa is the servant of his servants.

[^14-22]: GPT1 — p. 241, no. 13 (suhai), checked against the scan (PDF p. 500); GPT2 — sec. 4.1, no. 13. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS; it was
missing from the catalogue (new row KR-020). The preceding GPT pada (no. 12, "dekha dui bhāi gaura nitāi") is Krishnadasa's PK 1576 (chapter 7).
The signature "Krishnadasa" in GPT and PK covers padas of several poets; attribution by GPT (C).
[^14-23]: "Former plays" — Krishna's lilas in Vraja and the deeds of earlier avataras: during the mahaprakasha the Lord revealed to each devotee
his past and His own former lilas (CB Madhya 9–10). In 9.4 "jāti-prāṇadhana" (lit. "the life-treasure of the kin/of all") — the sense is not
quite clear.

## 10. Vasu Ghosha — "aguru candana lepiyā gorā-gāya…" (GPT1 p. 243, no. 19)
*The abhisheka: Gora's body is anointed with aguru and sandal, the associates fan Him with chamaras and pour water over Him; they wipe
His face, put on Him a garland of malati, dress Him in red garments and ornaments; Vasudeva gazes at that form. Raga
dhanashi.*[^14-24]

**10.1.** Having anointed Gora's body with aguru and sandal,
the dear associates fan Him with chamaras.

**10.2.** Someone, bringing water and holding it in his own hands,
pours it over Gauranga as his heart desires.

**10.3.** The face that outshines the moon they wipe to make it shine still more;
on Gora's body is a garland of malati flowers.

**10.4.** Red garments and various ornaments shine on Him —
Vasudeva gazes at that form.

[^14-24]: GPT1 — p. 243, no. 19 (dhanashi), checked against the scan (PDF p. 502); GPT2 — sec. 4.1, no. 19. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS
(catalogue: VG-164). GPT only (C). The bathing, anointing and dressing of the Lord at the abhisheka — cf. Vasu Ghosha's PK 1536–1537
(chapter 1, nos. 2–3) and CB Madhya 9.

## 11. Parameshvari Dasa — "prabhura ādeśa pāñā bhakata sakala…" (GPT1 p. 246, no. 27)
*The adhivasa of the kirtana: at the Lord's command the devotees form seven groups, led by Nityananda, Mukunda, Advaita, Gadadhara,
Vasu Ghosha, Murari and Narahari; fourteen madals and fourteen pairs of kartals resound; in the courtyard pots of curd mixed with
turmeric are broken, and with it they mark one another's foreheads. Raga dhanashi.*[^14-25]

**11.1.** Having received the Lord's command, all the devotees
divided into seven parts and formed seven groups.

**11.2.** At the head of the first group was Nityananda;
the lead singer of the second was Mukunda.

**11.3.** The head of the third was Sitapati Himself;
Gadadhara became the leader of the fourth.

**11.4.** Of the fifth — Vasu Ghosha, of the sixth — Murari;
the leader of the seventh group was Narahari.

**11.5.** All at once fourteen madals thundered;
from fourteen pairs of kartals rose a great clamour.

**11.6.** Setting curd with amrasara in pots,
in the courtyard they broke them, mixing it with turmeric.[^14-26]

**11.7.** The curd mixed with turmeric all took up,
and in the bliss of prema they mark one another's foreheads.

**11.8.** Thus was the adhivasa — the blessing of the kirtana — performed;
in the bliss of prema sings Parameshvari Dasa.

[^14-25]: GPT1 — p. 246, no. 27 (dhanashi), checked against the scan (PDF p. 505; the catalogue had "p. 247"); GPT2 — sec. 4.1, no. 27. The pada
is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS (catalogue: PD-003). The signature "parameśvarīdāsa" is the same as that of the preceding GPT pada (no. 26 = PK 23,
the kirtana festival at Advaita's house, chapter 5, no. 4), which this pada continues. Parameshvari (Parameshvara) Dasa is an associate of
Nityananda, one of the twelve gopalas (CC Adi 11). By the user's decision it is translated though known only from the GPT (C).
[^14-26]: Madal (mridanga, khol) — a clay drum; kartals — hand cymbals. "Seven groups" (sāta dala, sampradayas) — as at the Ratha-yatra in Puri
(CC Madhya 13), where there were also seven groups and fourteen mridangas; here the poet carries that arrangement over to a kirtana in
Navadvipa. "Amrasara" (āmrasāra) — the sense is unclear (perhaps mango juice or treacle). Marking with turmeric and curd is a festive ritual
game (cf. the "dadhi-haridra" of the Nanda-utsava).

## 12. Vasu Ghosha — "gaurīdāsa saṅge kṛṣṇa-kathā-raṅge…" (GPT1 p. 291, no. 49)
*Gaura with Gauridasa: in a joyful talk about Krishna They embrace, intoxicated with bhava; Gauridasa puts a garland of champaka on
the Lord — and, looking at its golden colour, the Lord remembers Radha: "Gauridasa, Radha has come to My mind!" — and longs to see
Her. Raga dhanashi, tala dashakushi.*[^14-27]

**12.1.** With Gauridasa, joyfully talking of Krishna, Gaurahari sat;
the heart absorbed in bhava, again and again They embrace, arms round each other's necks.

**12.2.** Restraining the bhava and seating the Lord, Gauridasa
at once brought from the house a garland of champaka and suddenly put it round His neck.

**12.3.** At the champaka garland my Gaura Raya looks and looks:
He remembered Radha's colour — a stream of prema flows over His body.

**12.4.** The Lord says: "Listen, Gauridasa, Radha has come to My mind!"
Says Vasu Ghosha: a longing to see Rai, full of rasa, seized Him.[^14-28]

[^14-27]: GPT1 — p. 291, section on the Lord's bhava, no. 49 ("dhānaśrī daśakuśī"), checked against the scan (PDF p. 550); GPT2 — the same section, no. 49 (also in the
GPT2 index of first lines: "gaurīdāsa saṅge kṛṣṇakathāraṅge — vāsu ghoṣa"). The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS (catalogue: VG-166; the first line in
the catalogue, "kata kathā raṅge," is corrected from the scan to "kṛṣṇa kathā raṅge"). GPT only (C). Before it in the GPT stand padas of Radhamohana
Dasa (nos. 43–44) on the same theme: Gaura with Gauridasa, whom He calls Subala.
[^14-28]: Gauridasa Pandita in Krishna's lila is the cowherd Subala, Krishna's intimate friend and helper in His meetings with Radha
(*Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika* 128). The golden champaka garland reminds the Lord of golden Radha; here Gaura is in the bhava of Krishna
longing for Radha — this is the prema of Vraja, not a worldly feeling. "Listen" — the text has "prabhu kahe vāsa, śuna gaurīdāsa": the word "vāsa"
is unclear (by the rhyme, a form of address; possibly a corruption).

## 13. Vasu Ghosha — "gaurīdāsa kari saṅge ānandita tanu raṅge…" (GPT1 p. 292, no. 50)
*Gaura with Gauridasa on the bank of the Suradhuni: in bhava the Lord trembles, tears stream from His eyes, He looks into Gauridasa's face —
and suddenly falls senseless; Gauridasa lifts Him up: "What is Your sorrow?" — "It cannot be told: My heart is breaking." In the bhava
of Radha Gaurahari cannot restrain His heart. Raga bhatiyari, tala dashakushi.*[^14-29]

**13.1.** Taking Gauridasa with Him, joyful, thrilled in body, goes Gora, the treasure of virtues;
from bhava His body trembles, tears stream from both eyes — He looks into Gauridasa's face.

**13.2.** Suddenly losing consciousness in the ecstasy of prema, Sri Chaitanya fell on the bank of the Suradhuni;
Gauridasa gently lifted Him into his arms: "Tell me, what is Your sorrow?"

**13.3.** "It is not a thing to be told — how shall I tell it? My heart is breaking — I am dying."
Says Vasu: ah! — in the bhava of Radha Gaurahari cannot hold His heart.[^14-30]

[^14-29]: GPT1 — p. 292, no. 50 ("bhāṭiyāri daśakuśī"), checked against the scan (PDF p. 551); GPT2 — the same section, no. 50. The pada is not in PK, BR,
KGC or PS (catalogue: VG-167). GPT only (C).
[^14-30]: The bhava of Radha is pure prema, the torment of separation from Krishna (vipralambha); "I am dying" is the Lord's speech in that
bhava, an expression of the utmost intensity of prema, not of worldly grief (cf. CC Antya 14–20). Gauridasa is Subala (see above), the
confidant of the secrets of Radha and Krishna; therefore it is to him that the Lord almost discloses His torment.

## 14. Vasu Ghosha — "vṛndāvanera bhāve gorā phirāya pām̐cani…" (GPT1 p. 330, no. 28)
*Goshtha-bhava in Navadvipa: in the bhava of Vrindavana Gora twirls a herding stick and calls the cows, "Ava, ava!"; Shachi is called to
come and see Gora going to the forest to tend the cows; Srivasa's wife runs, and the poet after her. Raga dhanashi.*[^14-31]

**14.1.** In the bhava of Vrindavana Gora twirls the herding stick;
"Ava, ava!" calls Gora, the jewel of virtues.

**14.2.** Gorachand is absorbed in that bhava:
the bhava of Vrindavana has taken hold of Gora.

**14.3.** They say to Shachi: "Come, let us see —
Gora is going to the forest to tend the cows!"

**14.4.** Srivasa's wife set off running;
says Vasudeva Ghosha: I had to go too.[^14-32]

[^14-31]: GPT1 — p. 330, section of the year's festivals (goshtha-yatra), no. 28 (dhanashi), checked against the scan (PDF p. 589); GPT2 — sec. 5.1,
no. 28. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS (catalogue: VG-170). GPT only (C). Gaura's goshtha-lila in Navadvipa is also described by Vasu
Ghosha in BR (p. 935) and PK 1186, 1353 (chapter 1).
[^14-32]: "Herding stick" (pām̐cani) — the stick for driving cows; "ava, ava" — the cowherds' call. Srivasa's wife is Malini, the Lord's nurse.

## 15. Vamshidasa — "śrīnandanandana śacīra dulāla cale goṭhe pāya pāya…" (GPT1 pp. 330–331, no. 30)
*Goshtha-lila in Navadvipa: Nanda's son, become Shachi's darling, goes to the pasture, Nityananda, Rohini's son, running ahead; Abhirama —
Shridama — drives the cows, Gauridasa — Subala — joins the band; Navadvipa has become Gokula, all the associates are dressed as cowherd
boys; the poet goes with them. Raga lalita.*[^14-33]

**15.1.** Sri Nandanandana, Shachi's darling, goes to the pasture step by step;
Rohini's son, Nityananda Raya, runs ahead of His Brother.

**15.2.** Shridama the friend — Abhirama Svami — drives the cows and calves;
Subala — Gauridasa Pandita — came and quickly joined the band.[^14-34]

**15.3.** Navadvipa today has become Gokula, as at the end of the Dvapara-yuga;
all the associates took up herding sticks, putting on the dress of cowherd boys.

**15.4.** Cries of "Ava, ava!" filled the sky — the gods look and laugh;
together with them all to the pasture went this wretched Vamshidasa.

[^14-33]: GPT1 — pp. 330–331, no. 30 (lalita), checked against the scan (PDF pp. 589–590); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 30. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or
PS. In the catalogue (VV-007) the preceding GPT pada (no. 29, "abhirāma ḍāke dvārete…") was listed under Vamshi, but it is unsigned (it ends with
the words "vāsu yāya niyā chātā" — "Vasu carries the umbrella"), does not belong to Vamshi and is not translated; the pada signed "vaṃśīdāsa" is
no. 30. Attribution by GPT (C). Cf. Vamshivadana's goshtha-pada PK 2564 (chapter 1, no. 12).
[^14-34]: According to the *Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika*, Abhirama Thakura is Shridama and Gauridasa Pandita is Subala, Krishna's cowherd friends;
Nityananda is Balarama, Rohini's son. Vamshivadana himself, according to the GGD, is Krishna's flute.

## 16. Krishnadasa — "khelata phāgu gorā dvijarāja…" (GPT1 p. 339, no. 59)
*The festival of colours: Gora, king of the twice-born, plays with red powder (phagu) with Gadadhara and Narahari, with Nitai and Advaita;
Ramananda Raya plays with Sarvabhauma, Murari and Mukunda with Srivasa and Svarupa; in pairs they shower each other with phagu to cries
of "Hori, hori!"; some dance, some sing. Raga basanta, tala ekatali.*[^14-35]

**16.1.** Gora, king of the twice-born, plays phagu
with the whole circle of Gadadhara and Narahari.

**16.2.** With Nitai and Advaita He plays with relish:
now playful abuse, now sport — all drunk with prema.[^14-36]

**16.3.** With Sarvabhauma plays Ramananda Raya,
with Srivasa and Svarupa — Murari and Mukunda.

**16.4.** In pairs they play phagu to cries of "Hori, hori!";
with Gadadhara plays Gora, the jewel of the twice-born.

**16.5.** Some dance, some sing, clapping their hands;
says humble Krishnadasa, floating in bliss.

[^14-35]: GPT1 — pp. 339–340, section of the year's festivals (dola, phagu), no. 59 (basanta, ekatali), checked against the scan (PDF pp. 598–599);
GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 59. The pada is not in BR, KGC or PS (catalogue: KR-004); on PK see below. Signature "dīna kṛṣṇadāsa" — attribution by GPT (C). The next
GPT pada (no. 60) is also signed by Krishnadasa (no. 17); no. 61 is Shivananda's (BR, chapter 5).
Full PK check (chapter 16): the pada is also in PK — **PK 1464** (vol. 2, PDF p. 413, label "॥৪০॥১৪৬৪॥", raga vasanta, MS P-R-Sa no. 2017; PK: "khelata phāgu gorā dvija-rāja / gadādhara narahari dom̐hāra samāja… dīna kṛṣṇadāse kahe ānande bhāsiyā").
[^14-36]: Playful abuse (gāli) is a custom of the Holi festival. The poet brings together associates of Navadvipa and of Puri (Sarvabhauma,
Ramananda and Svarupa were with the Lord only in Nilachala); historically this is not a single scene but a song-image of the Lord's
festival with His associates.

## 17. Krishnadasa — "phāgu khelata gorā gadādhara saṅge…" (GPT1 p. 340, no. 60)
*The festival of colours: Gora plays with Gadadhara, the two showering each other with kunkuma and squirting from syringes; both are red
from head to foot with phagu — as if in Vraja Kanu and His beloved were playing; the devotees supply phagu, dance and sing; the poet
grieves that he was not born in that happy time. Raga basanta, tala ekatali.*[^14-37]

**17.1.** Gora plays phagu with Gadadhara:
the two shower each other with kunkuma.

**17.2.** They squirt from syringes, throw balls of gulal —
from the phagu both are red from head to foot.

**17.3.** They play as if in Vraja Kanu and His beloved;
on the lips of both, again and again: "Hori, hori!"[^14-38]

**17.4.** From all sides the devotees supply phagu:
some dance, some sing in bliss.

**17.5.** In Krishnadasa's heart a thorn has remained:
in such a happy time he was not born.

[^14-37]: GPT1 — p. 340, no. 60 (basanta, ekatali), checked against the scan (PDF p. 599); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 60. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or
PS; it was missing from the catalogue (new row KR-021). The poet says plainly that he was born after the Lord's departure — so this is not a
contemporary but a later poet with the same signature (C).
[^14-38]: Phagu (phāgu), gulal — the red powder of the Holi festival (dola-yatra); kunkuma — red powder. Gadadhara is, by tradition, a
manifestation of Radha (GGD 147–153); Gaura's play with Gadadhara reflects the plays of Radha and Krishna in Vraja; this is the prema of
Vraja, not a worldly amusement. "Hori" — the festival cry.

## 18. Govinda Ghosha — "prāṇera mukunda he tomarā ki sudhāo āmāya…" (GPT1 p. 366, no. 2)
*The Lord discloses to Mukunda His decision to take sannyasa: He left Goloka seeing the sufferings of living beings, but the panditas and
students do not accept His teaching; to save them He will shave His head and take sannyasa — then even the blasphemers will go mad with
the holy name and prema. Mukunda falls senseless; the poet begs the Lord not to end the lila in Nadia. Raga pahira.*[^14-39]

**18.1.** "Mukunda, My life, what are you asking Me?
The pain I carry in My heart I have no one to tell," — saying this, Gora Raya weeps.

**18.2.** "Seeing the sufferings of living beings, I left the bliss of Goloka and took a human birth;
as much hardship as I have suffered, so much you too have suffered — and all the labour has gone for nothing.

**18.3.** The panditas and students do not accept Me, they do not take My teaching;
thinking of this I lose My reason: how will they be saved, how will they be rid of the fear of hell?

**18.4.** After long thought I have made firm My heart: soon I shall leave the life of the home;
shaving My head, putting on the cord and the kaupina, without delay I shall take sannyasa.

**18.5.** Then all the blasphemers, hearing the cries of 'Hari, Hari!', will go mad with the holy name and prema;
all will go to the eternal abode, My desire will be fulfilled, and My whole descent will bear fruit."[^14-40]

**18.6.** When the Lord spoke thus, Mukunda lost consciousness and only after a while came to himself;
says Sri Govinda Ghosha: "It is not fitting for You to end the lila in Nadia."

[^14-39]: GPT1 — p. 366, section "Presage of the sannyasa, the sannyasa, and the journey to Shantipura," no. 2 (pahira), checked against the scan
(PDF p. 625); GPT2 — sec. 5.3, no. 2 (nos. 1–8 of this section are missing from the GPT2 scan). The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS (catalogue: GG-009). It continues GPT pada no. 1 = PK 1606 of Govinda
Ghosha (Gadadhara brings the news to Mukunda, chapter 1, no. 15). Govinda Ghosha is the Lord's associate, an eyewitness according to Majumdar;
this pada is known only from the GPT (C).
[^14-40]: The reason for the sannyasa is the same as in CC Adi 17 (the Lord sees that the students and panditas of Navadvipa offend Him and do not
accept the holy name, and resolves to take sannyasa so that, honouring a sannyasi, they may be saved) and CB Madhya 26. "Blasphemers"
(pāṣaṇḍī) — those who reject bhakti. "Goloka" — Krishna's eternal abode; the Lord's descent is by His own will, not by the law of karma.

## 19. Vasu Ghosha — "āhā mari kothā gela gorā kām̐cā sonā…" (GPT1 p. 385, no. 6)
*A lament after the sannyasa: where has Gora — pure gold — gone? Life did not go out with the words; what use are eyes when their pupil is
gone; His face will be seen no more, His words heard no more; the poet laments that he did not die before. Raga dhanashi.*[^14-41]

**19.1.** Ah! Where has Gora gone — pure gold?
As I speak, my soul weeps; I forget myself.

**19.2.** While I spoke these words, life did not go out with them:
for the sake of what happiness has the soul not left the body?

**19.3.** If the pupil of the eye is gone, what use are the eyes?
No more shall I see Gora's moonlike face.

**19.4.** No more shall I hear from smiling lips words steeped in nectar;
where shall I find Gauranga, the treasury of virtues?

**19.5.** Says Vasu Ghosha, remembering Gora's virtues:
why did I not die before everyone?[^14-42]

[^14-41]: GPT1 — p. 385, section of the lament after the sannyasa, no. 6 (dhanashi), checked against the scan (PDF p. 644); GPT2 — sec. 5.4, no. 6. The
pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS. In the catalogue it was listed under Vamshi (VV-008): in the GPT2 OCR (because of the two-column layout) the last
line of another pada — "…śāśuṛī vadhūra rodana śuniyā, vaṃśī gaṛāgaṛi yāya" (the end of Vamshi's PK 1855, GPT1 pp. 385–386, no. 9; chapter 1) — landed
next to it. The pada itself is signed by **Vasu Ghosha** (new row VG-173). GPT only (C).
[^14-42]: "Gone" — the Lord has left Navadvipa, having taken sannyasa (1510); there is no question of death. "Why did I not die" is the usual formula
of laments, for a devotee to whom separation from the Lord is harder than death.

## 20. Yadu — "aparūpa ratha-āge…" (PK 1546; GPT1 p. 321, no. 2)
*The Ratha-yatra: before the chariot Gora Raya dances, and all the blessed ones sing with Him; in bhava He knows neither day nor night and,
gazing at Jagannatha's face, dances overflowing with bliss; khols and kartals resound, cries of "Jaya!" from gods, men and sages rise to the
sky; the people of Nilachala and pilgrims from many lands swim in the ocean of prema. Raga imana.*[^14-43]

**20.1.** Wondrous — before the chariot
Gora Raya dances, and all the blessed ones, as many as there are, sing together.

**20.2.** Overcome by bhava, He knows not whether it is night or day — in ecstasy He is aware of nothing;
gazing at Jagannatha's face, in great bliss He dances, His heart overflowing.

**20.3.** Khols and kartals, a sweet kirtana, ceaseless "Haribol!";
cries of "Jaya, jaya!" from gods, men and sages rise to the heavens.[^14-44]

**20.4.** The hearts of the people of Nilachala and of folk from many lands overflow;
all swim in the ocean of prema — but wretched Yadu is luckless.

[^14-43]: PK — vol. 2, 3rd shakha, 29th pallava (the Ratha-yatra: "śrīgauracandrasya rathāgre nartanaṃ yathā"), mark "॥৩॥১৫৪৬॥," raga imana (MS P-R-Sa no. 2091 —
"imana kalyāṇa"), checked against the scan IA 336618 (PDF pp. 454–455; the end of the first stanza is effaced in the scan — given from GPT1). GPT1 —
p. 321, section of the Ratha-yatra, no. 2 (imana), scan PDF p. 580; GPT2 — sec. 5.1 (Ratha-yatra), no. 2. Before it in PK stand a pada of Vaishnava
Dasa (PK 1544) and an excerpt from CC Madhya 13 (PK 1545). In the catalogue — YD-010. Signature "dukhī yadu abhāgiyā"; who this Yadu is — Yadunatha
Kavichandra or the later Yadunandana — is not established; the pada, like the following ones, is close to the account of CC Madhya 13 and is probably
late (C).
[^14-44]: Khol — the mridanga; kartals — hand cymbals. "Haribol" — "Utter Hari's name!"

## 21. Yadu — "caudike mahānta meli karaye kīrtana keli…" (PK 1547; GPT1 p. 322, no. 3)
*The Ratha-yatra: on all sides seven kirtana groups, fourteen khols resound, Jagannatha rejoices; in the middle, among Nityananda, Advaita, Srivasa
and Haridasa, Gaurahari dances, the earth shakes under His steps, on His body the eight sattvika-bhavas; in ecstasy He dances, and Jagannatha moves
slowly after Him; grief and sorrow are gone, prema has flooded all that lives. Raga mangala, tala kandarpa.*[^14-45]

**21.1.** On all sides great souls have gathered and give themselves to the sport of kirtana — seven groups sing songs;
fourteen khols resound, the roar has pierced the sky — seeing it, Jagannatha rejoices.

**21.2.** Maddened Nityananda, Acharya Advaitachandra, Pandita Srivasa, Haridasa —
taking them all with Him, Gaurahari dances in the middle, and around Him the circle of devotees.

**21.3.** They cry "Hari, Hari!" — under the steps the earth sways, from the eyes flow streams of tears;
waves of prema play on His body, surpassing Mount Sumeru — on it all eight sattvika-bhavas.[^14-46]

**21.4.** In ecstasy Gora Raya goes dancing — slowly, slowly moves Jagannatha;
amazed and joyful, He watches the sankirtana of prema of His own circle of associates.[^14-47]

**21.5.** Gone are grief and sorrow, prema has flooded the people — the unmoving and the moving, beasts and birds;
says Yadu: incomparable is this abode of the plays of prema — whoever saw it became its companion.

[^14-45]: PK — vol. 2, 29th pallava, mark "॥৪॥১৫৪৭॥," raga mangala, tala kandarpa (MS P-R-Sa no. 2092), checked against the scan (PDF p. 455); GPT1 — p. 322,
no. 3 ("maṅgala-kandarpatāla"), scan PDF p. 581; GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 3. In the catalogue — YD-011. The pada retells CC Madhya 13 (seven groups,
fourteen mridangas, eight sattvika-bhavas); attribution as for the preceding (C).
[^14-46]: The eight sattvika-bhavas — stupefaction, perspiration, horripilation, faltering of the voice, trembling, change of colour, tears, fainting
(CC Madhya 13). Sumeru — the golden mountain: an image of the Lord's golden body.
[^14-47]: The second line of this stanza ("ānanda vismaya mana…") is not in PK — the stanza is incomplete there; it is given from GPT1. "Amazed and joyful" —
according to CC Madhya 13, Jagannatha, seeing the Lord's dance, rejoices and slows the chariot; here it apparently refers to Jagannatha watching
the kirtana.

## 22. Yadu — "līlākārī jagannātha…" (GPT1 pp. 322–323, no. 5)
*The Ratha-yatra: halfway along, Jagannatha's chariot suddenly stops; gods, asuras and men pull it, the temple servants curse, at the king's order
hundreds of elephants are harnessed — it does not move a step; then Gora Raya goes behind and pushes the chariot with His head — and it races
off with the speed of the wind; the pilgrims rejoice, the poet is amazed at the power of the Two. Raga imana.*[^14-48]

**22.1.** Jagannatha is playing:
midway along the road, as it goes, the chariot suddenly stops.

**22.2.** Gods, asuras and men pulled the chariot — and still it does not move;
the parichha and the pujaris, canes in hand, curse in every way.[^14-49]

**22.3.** At the king's order hundreds of mighty elephants are harnessed on both sides;
they pull the chariot with all their strength — yet the best of chariots does not move a single step.

**22.4.** Then Gora Raya goes behind the chariot and pushes it with His head —
and with the speed of the wind, in a moment, it sped a hundred yojanas.

**22.5.** "Glory to Gaura!" — raising both arms, the pilgrims cry;
grasping the power of the Two, Yadu was filled with wonder.[^14-50]

[^14-48]: GPT1 — pp. 322–323, no. 5 (imana), checked against the scan (PDF pp. 581–582); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 5. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS (catalogue: YD-013).
It retells CC Madhya 14 (the chariot stops, the king orders elephants to be harnessed, the Lord pushes it with His head). Signature "yadu"; a late pada
after the CC (C).
[^14-49]: "Is playing" (līlākārī) — the stopping of the chariot is the play of Jagannatha Himself. Parichha — the temple superintendent; pujaris — the
priest-servants.
[^14-50]: "A hundred yojanas" — poetic hyperbole (in the CC the chariot "rolled on, rumbling"). "The Two" — Jagannatha and Gaura.

## 23. Yadunatha Dasa — "caitanya nitāi āre dona bhāi nāce re…" (PK 1548 unsigned; GPT1 p. 323, no. 6)
*The Ratha-yatra: the two brothers, Chaitanya and Nitai, dance, khols and kartals sound; the golden lotus sways in the ocean of the nectar of
prema, and its wave touches all — high, middling and low; the seven groups sing aloud, and to each it seems that Gora Raya is dancing everywhere at
once; the poet begs a particle of mercy. Raga ramakeli, tala trayar.*[^14-51]

**23.1.** Chaitanya and Nitai — the two brothers — dance!
Khols and kartals, the sweet fifth note — "ta-theiya, ta-theiya" it sounds.

**23.2.** The golden lotus sways in the ocean of the nectar of prema;
high, middling, wretched and low — that wave touches all.[^14-52]

**23.3.** The seven groups sing to Jagannatha at the top of their voices;
all can see: Gora Raya is dancing everywhere at once.[^14-53]

**23.4.** Unprecedented majesty, unprecedented sweetness are revealed in this lila;
Yadunatha Dasa floats in the bliss of prema and begs from the Lord a particle of mercy.

[^14-51]: PK — vol. 2, 29th pallava, mark "॥৫॥১৫৪৮॥," ramakeli, tala trayar (MS P-R-Sa no. 2093; "tālatrayaṃ" is absent in MSS ka, kha, cha and P-R-Sa), checked
against the scan (PDF p. 455); PK has only 23.1–23.2, **without a signature**. GPT1 — p. 323, no. 6 (ramakeli), scan PDF p. 582 — with two more stanzas
(23.3–23.4) and the signature "yadunātha dāsa"; GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 6. It was missing from the catalogue (new row YD-015). GPT1 also attached the
signature "yadunātha dāsa" to verses of the CC (no. 4 = PK 1545; YD-012, excluded), so the signature and the additional stanzas of GPT1 are not beyond
doubt (D).
[^14-52]: The golden lotus is Gaura. "The fifth note" (pañcama) — the fifth degree of the scale, the voice of the kokila. MSS ka, kha, cha and P-R-Sa: "uttama adhama" for
"uttama madhyama"; P-R-Sa in 23.1: "caitanya nitāi re dona bhāi saṅge pariṣada nāce re" ("with the brothers the associates dance").
[^14-53]: According to CC Madhya 13 the Lord, dancing among the seven groups, appeared in all of them at once, and each group thought He was with it.

## 24. "Ramananda" — "ohe nitāi nīlācala nā chāṛiva āra…" (GPT1 p. 405, no. 13)
*The Lord tells Nityananda that He will not leave Nilachala again: Haridasa has wound up his lila, Advaita, Srinivasa, Puri, Damodara,
Vishvarupa and Krishnadasa are gone; He bids Nitai live as a householder — go to the Pandita, who will give Him two daughters — and be merciful
to the fallen; Gauda is His own abode. Holding Nitai's hand, the Lord weeps, repeating "Hari, Hari." Raga dhanashi.*[^14-54]

**24.1.** "Nitai, I shall not leave Nilachala any more.
There was Haridasa, dear to Me as life — he has wound up his lila; with whom shall I now play?

**24.2.** Advaita, Sri Srinivasa, Puri, Damodara Dasa — they have gone, leaving this joy;
who will share rasa with Me, with whom shall I wander? They have gone, laying a stone upon My breast.[^14-55]

**24.3.** Vishvarupa, My brother — there is no news of him: he went away, taking renunciation;
Krishnadasa, a mine of rasa — I shall hear his songs no more: he too has gone, driving a spear into My heart.

**24.4.** Nitai, live as a householder — go to the Pandita: seeing You, he will be happy;
with care he will give You two daughters in marriage — show him Your own form.[^14-56]

**24.5.** The fallen, the low, the ignorant — do not grieve them, be merciful to all;
call them Your own, have pity on living beings — Your mercy will be proclaimed in the three worlds.

**24.6.** And that land is My own abode; keep My glory, Balarama," — saying this mercifully, the Lord weeps.
Holding Nitaichand's hand, the Lord says "Hari, Hari!" — Ramananda's heart finds no rest.[^14-57]

[^14-54]: GPT1 — p. 405, section on Nityananda in Gauda, no. 13 (dhanashi), checked against the scan (PDF pp. 664–665); GPT2 — sec. 5.5, no. 13 (GPT1
p. 405 — as cited by Majumdar). The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS (catalogue: RM-015). Signature "rāmānanda." **Majumdar considers the pada a
forgery composed to justify Nityananda's marriage**; it also departs from tradition: Advaita outlived the Lord, and the Lord sent Nityananda to
preach in Gauda long before Haridasa's departure (CC Madhya 15; Antya 11). We translate it as a text of the GPT without accepting it as
authentic (D).
[^14-55]: If "gone" is understood as departure from the world, this contradicts the CC and CB: Advaita and Svarupa Damodara were with the Lord to
the end of His lila; perhaps their leaving Puri is meant. "Puri" — probably Paramananda Puri; "Damodara Dasa" — Svarupa Damodara or Damodara
Pandita; "Krishnadasa, a mine of rasa" — it is unclear who is meant.
[^14-56]: "The Pandita" — Suryadasa Pandita (Sarakhel), father of Vasudha and Jahnava, whom Nityananda married (CC Adi 11; *Bhakti-ratnakara* 12).
"Show him Your own form" — Nityananda as Balarama. Nityananda's marriage and His householder life in Gauda are His own will, manifested at the
Lord's command for the sake of preaching; Nityananda, Balarama, is not subject to worldly attachments.
[^14-57]: "That land" (seha) — apparently Gauda, the land of Nityananda's preaching. "Balarama" — an address to Nityananda (He is Balarama). The signature
"Ramananda": according to Majumdar, neither Ramananda Raya nor Ramananda Vasu is the author of this pada.

## 25. Vasu Ghosha — "aruṇa-vasane vividha bhūṣaṇe śirete pāga laṭapaṭiyā…" (GPT1 p. 423, no. 30)
*Nityananda's dance: in red garments and ornaments, His turban slipping askew, He whirls, arms raised, crying "Hari, Hari!"; His gait is that of a
maddened elephant, His ankle-bells ring; in bhava, heedless of the quarters, He roars: "Gaura!"; the devotees roll on the ground, gazing at His
moonlike face. Raga bala-suhai.*[^14-58]

**25.1.** In red garments, in various ornaments, the turban on His head slipping askew,
He whirls round and round, both arms raised — He dances, crying "Hari, Hari!"

**25.2.** Merry Nitai dances!
In the reddish eyes, in the moonlike face — how much sweetness!

**25.3.** Lovely is His gait — like a maddened elephant's, His ankle-bells ringing;
overcome by bhava, heedless of the quarters, He roars: "Gaura!"

**25.4.** All the devotees roll on the ground, gazing at that moonlike face;
Vasudeva Ghosha, wretched, deprived, begs the Giver for the rasa of prema.[^14-59]

[^14-58]: GPT1 — p. 423, section on Nityananda, no. 30 ("vālā suhai"), checked against the scan (PDF p. 682); GPT2 — sec. 6.1, no. 30. The pada is not in PK,
BR, KGC or PS (catalogue: VG-171). GPT only (C). The GPT1 footnotes give variants from an unnamed source: "vidita bhuvane" ("known to the world") for
"vividha bhūṣaṇe," "sundara" for "raṅgiyā," and a different last line — "vasu rāmānande, kām̐de nirānande, nitāi caraṇa dhariyā" ("Vasu Ramananda weeps in sorrow,
clasping Nitai's feet"): there the pada is signed by Vasu Ramananda.
[^14-59]: "The Giver" (dāniyā) — Nityananda, the giver of prema. The turban (pāga) and red garments are the appearance of Nityananda the avadhuta in
Gauda (CB Antya 5).

## 26. Yadu — "nitāicām̐da dayāmaya…" (PK 2300; GPT1 p. 429, no. 51)
*Nityananda's mercy: never was there one so merciful to the people of Kali; His body now darkens, now brightens, now turns yellow; He laughs, He
weeps, unaware of Himself; He tries to say "Gora" and cannot; His eyes, red with love for Gaura, swim in tears; drowning Himself, He has flooded the
earth — only Yadu has remained on the mountain of worldly existence. Raga pathamanjari.*[^14-60]

**26.1.** Nitaichand is merciful, Nitaichand is merciful!
Such mercy to the living beings of Kali there never was.

**26.2.** Now He is dark, now fair, now His body turns yellow;
now He laughs, now He weeps — He is unaware of Himself.

**26.3.** Now He stammers "Go… go…" — He cannot say "Gora";
His eyes, red with love for Gora, swim in tears.

**26.4.** Drowning Himself in those waters, He has flooded the earth —
only Yadu has remained on the mountain of worldly existence.[^14-61]

[^14-60]: PK — vol. 3, 4th shakha, 22nd pallava ("Description of the virtues of Sri Nityananda"), mark "॥৭॥২৩০০॥," pathamanjari, MS P-R-Sa no. 2404,
checked against the scan (PDF p. 303); GPT1 — p. 429, no. 51 (pathamanjari), scan PDF p. 688; GPT2 — sec. 6.1, no. 51. It was missing from the
catalogue (new row YD-016). Signature "yadu": Yadunatha Kavichandra or the later Yadunandana — not established (C).
[^14-61]: Changes of colour (vaivarnya), laughter and tears are the sattvika-bhavas of prema. "The mountain of worldly existence" (bhava-acala) — existence,
immovable like a mountain: the poet of himself, unmoved by the flood of prema. PK MSS "ka, kha, cha": "śīta" ("cold") for "pīta"; "gha": "galita."

## 27. Kanu Dasa — "preme mātoyārā nitāi nāgara…" (GPT1 p. 432, no. 60)
*Praise of Nityananda: lovely Nitai is intoxicated with prema, an ocean of incomparable prema and mercy; making no distinction between His own
and others, He gives prema beyond the injunctions of the Vedas, saves sinners, weeps for the fallen, gives prema generously as from an
inexhaustible treasury; the poet asks for a place at His feet. Raga dhanashi.*[^14-62]

**27.1.** Lovely Nitai is intoxicated with prema:
incomparable prema — an ocean of mercy.

**27.2.** His heart is brimming with prema:
the Lord does not distinguish who is His own and who is not.

**27.3.** Where on earth is such mercy?
He gives prema beyond the reach of the Vedic injunctions.[^14-63]

**27.4.** Delivering sinners is His ceaseless work;
for the sufferings of the fallen tears stream from His eyes.

**27.5.** Offering prema of His own accord, He gives it to all without stint —
like a lovely inexhaustible treasury.

**27.6.** Says Kanu Dasa with joined palms:
give this wretched servant a place at Your feet.

[^14-62]: GPT1 — p. 432, section on Nityananda, no. 60 (dhanashi), checked against the scan (PDF p. 691); GPT2 — sec. 6.1, no. 60. The pada is not in PK, BR,
KGC or PS (catalogue: KD-004). Signature "kānu dāsa" — Kanu Thakura (Kanurama Dasa), son of Purushottama Dasa, associate of Jahnava (cf. PK 2327,
chapter 5); attribution by GPT (C).
[^14-63]: "Nagara" (nitāi nāgara) — here an epithet, "lovely, elegant," usual in praise of Nitai, not the motif of nagari-bhava. "Beyond the reach of the Vedic
injunctions" (vedavidhi-agocara) — the prema of Vraja is above the rules of Vedic dharma (CC Adi 4).

## 28. Kanu Dasa — "vidyānagarādhipa apāra sampadaśālī…" (GPT1 pp. 454–455, no. 9)
*Praise of Ramananda Raya: the ruler of Vidyanagara, owner of boundless wealth, received Gauranga in his house and gave Him the bee of his mind;
glory to Ramananda, with whom the Lord tasted boundless bliss; in a dialogue of questions and answers they established the goal and the path of the
living being; his padas of rasa are like a full-blown red lotus, the life of the rasikas; the poet begs for Ramananda's feet. Raga kamoda.*[^14-64]

**28.1.** The ruler of Vidyanagara, owner of boundless wealth, Rama Raya, first among men,
receiving Sri Gauranga in his house, gave His feet the bee of his own mind.

**28.2.** Glory, glory to Raya Ramananda!
With him my Lord Sri Gauranga tasted boundless bliss.

**28.3.** The two, in the form of questions and answers, examined the sacred teaching — and learned what the path of sadhana is for living beings;
his padas of rasa are like a full-blown red lotus: the life of those who know rasa.[^14-65]

**28.4.** Always place the dust of Ramananda's feet on your head — and serve: this is the essence of the essence of service, the treasure.
Kanu Dasa, poor in wit, poor in madhura-rasa: Rama Raya, give me your holy feet!

[^14-64]: GPT1 — pp. 454–455, section on the associates, no. 9 (kamoda), checked against the scan (PDF pp. 713–714); GPT2 — sec. 6.3, no. 9 (in the GPT2 index:
"vidyānagarādhipa — kānudāsa"). The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS (catalogue: KD-005). Signature "kānudāsa"; attribution by GPT (C).
[^14-65]: The Lord's conversation with Ramananda Raya on the Godavari — CC Madhya 8 (the Lord's questions and Ramananda's answers on sadhya and sadhana — the
goal and the path). The GPT1 print has "svādhyāya nirṇaya" ("established [the meaning of] the study of scripture"); by sense one would expect "sādhyera
nirṇaya" ("established the goal"). Ramananda's padas are his verses on rasa (including the drama *Jagannatha-vallabha*, whose songs the Lord heard in
Puri, CC Madhya 2, Antya 5).

# Chapter 15. Krishnadasa, Kanu Dasa, Vasu Ghosha, Yadunandana, Nayanananda, Yadu, Ramananda, Chaitanyadasa: the rest of the "GPT only" group and finds of a full check of signatures

*This chapter completes the group of padas by the other poets (apart from Narahari) that are known from the "Gaura-pada-tarangini"
(GPT1 — 1st ed. by Jagadbandhu Bhadra, 1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934), without the padas in nagari-bhava. It contains padas missed by
earlier checks (in the OCR text of GPT1 some headings "N pada" lack the danda, and such padas merged with their neighbours) and finds
of a full manual re-check of the signatures of all contemporary poets throughout GPT1. Four of the finds turned out not to be "GPT
only": they are in the "Padakalpataru" (PK 2099 — Yadunandana, PK 2101 — Yadu, also in the "Bhakti-ratnakara", PK 2083 — unsigned,
PK 1867 — Chaitanyadasa); there the text is given from PK with the readings of GPT. The padas follow the order of the lilas: praise of
the Gaura-avatara, Advaita's call and the Lord's appearance, goshtha-bhava and the kirtanas of Navadvipa, Shachi's lament after the
sannyasa, the Lord's bhavas in Puri, Nityananda. The language of some padas (nos. 1, 3–5, 14) has New Bengali forms — by these they
are probably late; Majumdar in general considers GPT unreliable for attribution. Hence the attribution of padas known only from GPT is
conditional (C, the late ones included: late language alone does not indicate a forgery). The Bengali original, variant readings and word-for-word translation are in the full version of the book.*

## 1. Krishnadasa — "āre re ninduka bhāi…" (GPT1 p. 14, no. 35)
*Rebuke of a blasphemer: Gauranga is the essence of all avataras; when drunkenness, killing of the unborn and debauchery under the
guise of tantric religion had overrun Bharata and people had begun to worship yakshas, rakshasas and Vishahari, Sri Chaitanya
appeared in Navadvipa, gave everyone the name of Hari, saved Jagai and Madhai, united brahmanas with yavanas; whoever does not
believe this has no deliverance. Raga dhanashi.*[^15-1]

**1.1.** "Hey, brother blasphemer, have you no understanding at all? In vain you bear a pair of eyes!
The essence of all avataras is the avatara of Sri Gauranga — and you pass Him by with disregard.

**1.2.** Drunkenness, violence, killing of the unborn, debauchery — under the guise of tantric religion they overran Bharata;
yakshas, rakshasas and Vishahari people began to worship with all kinds of offerings.[^15-2]

**1.3.** Seeing the misery of the living beings, my Lord Sri Chaitanya appeared in Navadvipa:
the saving name of Hari — the taraka-brahma — He Himself offered and gave to all, and removed the decline of dharma.[^15-3]

**1.4.** Jagai, Madhai and others who did evil without end He saved by the name of Hari;
He united brahmanas and yavanas — made them embrace: see it with your own eyes but once!

**1.5.** He made atheists into devotees, gave the lame the power to walk, granted the blind their sight."
Says lowly Krishnadasa: if you do not believe this, there is no more deliverance for you.[^15-4]

[^15-1]: GPT1 — p. 14, section of mangalacharana, no. 35 (dhanashi), checked against the scan IA in.ernet.dli.2015.477854 (PDF p. 273);
GPT2 — sec. 1.2, no. 35. The pada is not in PK, the "Bhakti-ratnakara" (BR), the "Kshanada-gita-chintamani" (KGC) or the
"Padamrita-samudra" (PS); it was missing from the catalogue (new row KR-022). Under the signature "Krishnadasa" PK has 22 padas by
different poets. The denunciation of "tantric religion" and words like "killing of the unborn" (bhrūṇahatyā) point to a late origin
(18th–19th c.); C.
[^15-2]: Cf. Vrindavana Dasa's description of Navadvipa before the Lord's appearance: people worship yakshas with wine and meat and honour
Vishahari (CB Adi 2). Vishahari is Manasa, the goddess of snakes. "Tantric religion" here means the rites with wine and the like that
the poet denounces.
[^15-3]: "Taraka-brahma" — the name that carries one across the ocean of birth and death: the maha-mantra "Hare Krishna," which the
"Kali-santarana Upanishad" calls the destroyer of the taint of Kali. "Decline of dharma" echoes Bhagavad-gita 4.7–8.
[^15-4]: Jagai and Madhai — CB Madhya 13; CC Adi 17. "Brahmanas and yavanas embraced": the Lord accepted all without distinction of caste —
thus Haridasa Thakura, born in a Muslim family, was one of His closest associates (CB Adi 16); the Kazi became His devotee (CC Adi 17).

## 2. Krishnadasa — "śāntipurera vuṛāmālī…" (GPT1 pp. 14–15, no. 36)
*An allegory of the tree of Chaitanya: the old gardener of Shantipur (Advaita) brought a seedling from the garden of Vaikuntha and gave
it to the gardener Nitai; in Nadia grew the tree of Chaitanya and bore two fruits — the Name and prema; Nitai gives them out to all,
down to chandalas and yavanas, whether they wish it or not; the poet laments that he did not see that tree and did not know the
merciful gardener. Raga suhai.*[^15-5]

**2.1.** The old gardener of Shantipur, emptying the garden of Vaikuntha, brought a single seedling;
finding the gardener Nitai, He put the seedling into His hands — "Plant it with care," said Nara.[^15-6]

**2.2.** Nadia is the finest place: laying out a garden there, the gardener planted the tree of Chaitanya;
the tree grows day by day, its branches and leaves past counting: watering it with care, He brought it up.

**2.3.** Receiving the water of bhakti, the beautiful tree bore two fruits — the Name and prema;
in hope of these two fruits the birds — the living beings — come every day and chatter without cease.

**2.4.** The joyful gardener Nitai, a basket on His head, gives out the two fruits to all;
there is no distinction of caste — everyone's sorrow is gone: each one gets the taste of the fruit.

**2.5.** "Hold it, take it, take it!" — crying out, the joyful gardener Nitai gave out the fruits down to the chandalas;
whoever asks receives, whoever does not ask receives too: even the yavanas tasted the fruit.[^15-7]

**2.6.** What a turn of my karma: I did not see that tree, I did not know that merciful gardener!
Krishnadasa, full of bad desires, holding a straw between his teeth, says: shame, shame on my wretched fate!

[^15-5]: GPT1 — pp. 14–15, section of mangalacharana, no. 36 (suhai), scan PDF pp. 273–274; GPT2 — sec. 1.2, no. 36. The pada is not in PK,
BR, KGC or PS; it was missing from the catalogue (new row KR-023). Date of composition not established; attribution by GPT (C).
[^15-6]: Nara (nāṛā) is Advaita Acharya: so the Lord called Him (CB). In Krishnadasa Kaviraja the tree of bhakti is the Lord Himself, who
is also the gardener; the first sprout is Madhavendra Puri (CC Adi 9); here the allegory is different: the seedling is brought by
Advaita, who called the Lord down, and the gardener is Nityananda, who gives out the fruits.
[^15-7]: "Whoever does not ask receives too": Nityananda gave prema even to those who did not seek it (CC Adi 5; CB Antya 5). "Holding a straw
between the teeth" is a sign of complete humility.

## 3. Kanu Dasa — "ekadina kamalākṣa kana haridāse…" (GPT1 p. 448, no. 32)
*Advaita (Kamalaksha) says to Haridasa: many years have passed, and the hope with which He came to earth is not fulfilled; the Lord of
Vaikuntha Himself told Him that He would descend to earth for the sake of the suffering living beings and bade Him come before Him; can
the Lord's promise be in vain? The poet: the Lord never speaks untruth — He will surely appear. Raga dhanashi.*[^15-8]

**3.1.** One day Kamalaksha says to Haridasa:
"The wish with which I came to earth —

**3.2.** many years have passed, and the hope is unfulfilled:
my austerity is fruitless, I am in despair.

**3.3.** The Lord of Vaikuntha with His own lips told me:
'The earth is burdened with sins, the living beings weep in sorrow;

**3.4.** to destroy the sorrow of the living beings I shall descend to earth;
You Yourself set foot there before Me.'

**3.5.** Can that promise of the Lord have proved vain?
Will the sorrow of the living beings not be removed through me?"[^15-9]

**3.6.** Says Kanu: the Lord never speaks untruth —
by the good fortune of the living beings He will surely appear.

[^15-8]: GPT1 — p. 448, section on Advaita, no. 32 (dhanashi), scan PDF pp. 707–708; GPT2 — sec. 6.2, no. 32. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC
or PS; it was missing from the catalogue (new row KD-012). Signature "Kanu" (kānu); Kanu Thakura, the son of Purushottama, is a poet of
the next generation, and the language of the pada (sādhanā viphala, pāpabhārākrānta) is New Bengali: the pada is probably late; C.
Kamalaksha is Advaita's childhood name.
[^15-9]: Advaita Acharya is Maha-Vishnu Himself; He appeared before the Lord in order to call Him down (CC Adi 3, 6; CB Adi 2). His "despair"
is not ignorance but compassion for the living beings and longing for the Lord's appearance, expressed in lila. The conversation of
the Lord with Advaita in Vaikuntha that is spoken of here is not described in CC or CB; CC (Adi 3) speaks of Advaita's resolve to call
Krishna by worship with Ganga water and tulasi. Haridasa Thakura came to Advaita in Shantipur (CB Adi 16).

## 4. Kanu Dasa — "cauddaśata sāta śāke…" (GPT1 p. 449, no. 33)
*The Lord's appearance: in the year 1407 of the Shaka era, on the full moon of Phalguna, during a lunar eclipse, Advaita Acharya was
offering tulasi leaves to the Ganga; suddenly He leapt up with a thundering cry and broke into a dance: "I have brought, I have brought
Gaura to Nadia!" — and Haridasa understood that Gauranga had been born. Raga dhanashi.*[^15-10]

**4.1.** In the year fourteen hundred and seven of the Shaka era, on the day of the full moon,
at the time of the lunar eclipse, in the month of Phalguna,

**4.2.** Advaita Acharya Prabhu, with a heart full of devotion,
was offering tulasi leaves to the Ganga.

**4.3.** Suddenly Nara leapt up with a thundering cry;
Haridasa was astonished, seeing His manner.

**4.4.** "I have brought, I have brought Gaura, I have brought Him to Nadia!" —
crying so, He dances, intoxicated with bliss.[^15-11]

**4.5.** Haridasa understood: Gauranga was born.
Grasping the hidden meaning, Kanu is beside himself with joy.

## 5. Vasu Ghosha — "abhirāma ḍāke dvārete…" (GPT1 p. 330, no. 29)
*Goshtha-bhava in Navadvipa: Abhirama calls Gaura at the door to come and play — the game of Vraja was grazing the cows, the game of
Nadia is sankirtana; the time for going to the pasture is passing, but Gaura, offended, sits on Mother Shachi's lap; Shachi asks
where they will go; Gorachand sets out for the pasture, and Vasu carries an umbrella for Him. Raga lalita.*[^15-12]

**5.1.** Abhirama calls at the door: "Hey, Gaura, will You come and play?
You are giving Yourself airs — sitting on Mother Shachi's lap!

**5.2.** The game of Vraja is grazing the cows, the game of Nadia is sankirtana — the boys are mad for it;
'Ha-re-re!' — we shall see there; let us go to the bank of the Suradhuni.

**5.3.** The hour is past — the time for going to the pasture has gone: Gaura, tell us, will You come or not?
You have taken offence — sitting on Mother Shachi's lap!"

**5.4.** Hearing Abhirama's words, Mother Shachi says: "And where will you all go?"
Gorachand will go to the pasture — Vasu goes carrying the umbrella.[^15-13]

## 6. Yadunandana — "gaurāṅga-sundara naṭa-purandara…" (PK 2099; GPT1 p. 138, no. 80)
*Gauranga's dance: He is the lord of dancers, the manifest body of prema, like a new cloud or a golden Madana moulded of nectar; for
the sweetness of His face and smile one gives the autumn moon as a ransom; His eyes defeat the wagtail; the poet longs for His red
feet. Raga mayura.*[^15-14]

**6.1.** Gauranga the Beautiful, lord of dancers — the manifest body of prema:
is He a new cloud, is He a golden Madana? — as if moulded of nectar.[^15-15]

**6.2.** *(Refrain)* Wondrously dances Gauranga — an ocean of bliss!
For the sweetness of His face, for the cunning of His smile one gives the autumn moon as a ransom.

**6.3.** What eyes — they defeat the wagtail! How lovely the curve of His brows!
His two red feet — this Yadunandana longs for them.

[^15-10]: GPT1 — p. 449, section on Advaita, no. 33 (dhanashi), scan PDF p. 708; GPT2 — sec. 6.2, no. 33. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or
PS; it was missing from the catalogue (new row KD-013). Signature "Kanu"; the language is New Bengali (akasmāt, sacakita) — the pada
is probably late; C.
[^15-11]: The time of the Lord's appearance — Shaka 1407 (1486 AD), the full moon of Phalguna, a lunar eclipse — CC Adi 13; there it is also
said that at the hour of His birth Advaita Acharya in Shantipur and Haridasa Thakura danced in bliss. Advaita's worship with Ganga water
and tulasi, by which He called Krishna down, — CC Adi 3. "I have brought" — Advaita called the Lord to earth; cf. the same words in the
pada on the abhisheka (chapter 14, no. 7). Nara (nāṛā) is Advaita.
[^15-12]: GPT1 — p. 330, section on goshtha-bhava, no. 29 (lalita), checked against the scan (PDF p. 589); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 29. The pada is not
in PK, BR, KGC or PS. In the catalogue (VV-007) the pada was listed as "unsigned," but the last line names Vasu (vāsu yāya niyā chātā) —
thus the poet often brings himself into the lila as a participant; new row VG-174. The colloquial language (halo, yeye, śune) points to a
late origin; C. Cf. other padas on Gaura's goshtha-bhava in Navadvipa: chapter 1, nos. 11–12; chapter 14, nos. 14–15.
[^15-13]: Abhirama Thakura (Ramadasa) is an associate of Nityananda, one of the twelve gopalas; the tradition sees in him Shridama, Krishna's
friend (Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika). In the pasture the cowherd friends hold an umbrella over Krishna; naming himself, the poet becomes
one of them.
[^15-14]: PK — vol. 3, 17th pallava ("śrīgaurāṅgera nṛtyādi līlā"), mark "॥৪১॥২০৯৯॥," raga "tathā" (mayura, as for PK 2097), MS P-R-Sa no. 2208,
checked against the scan (PDF p. 230, printed p. 219); GPT1 — p. 138, section on Gaura's beauty, no. 80 (mayura), scan PDF p. 397; GPT2 —
sec. 3.1, no. 80. The pada was missing from the catalogue (new row YN-014). Signature "yadunandana": Yadunandana Chakravarti, a disciple
of Gadadhara Dasa (by Majumdar a contemporary of the Lord; his padas are in BR, chapter 11), or the later Yadunandana Dasa (17th c.) —
not established; C.
[^15-15]: "A new cloud" is the form of Krishna, "a golden Madana" the form of Gaura: within the golden Gaura the dark Krishna is hidden.
Madana (Kamadeva) is an image of beauty; Krishna is Madana-mohana, "He who enchants Madana himself": the point is a beauty before which
the god of love is powerless, not worldly attraction. GPT1 has "sudhāya garala janu" ("as if poison in nectar") — apparently a misprint for
"gaṛala" ("moulded"). "Gives as a ransom" (nichiye) — a rite that averts misfortune from the beloved (cf. chapter 14, no. 2).

## 7. Nayanananda (?) — "nāce re bhāli gaurakiśora vara-raṅgiyā…" (PK 2083 unsigned; GPT1 p. 284, no. 23)
*A dance in Radha's bhava: young Gaura dances, His golden body quivering with prema; remembering Vrindavana, Govardhana and the bank of
the Yamuna, He falls and cries: "The flute!"; in Radha's bhava He takes on Radha's colour and repeats "Radha, Radha!" — and Gadadhara,
understanding the hint, smilingly takes his place at His left. Raga turi.*[^15-16]

**7.1.** He dances — ah, young Gaura, finest of merry ones!
The beautiful body of Gaura, shining like gold, quivers under the weight of prema.

**7.2.** Remembering Vrindavana, Govardhana, the bank and the groves of the Yamuna, He sways and falls;
"The flute! the flute!" He cries again and again, and stands still, as if gazing at the flute at His lips.

**7.3.** In the bhava of Sri Radha, Gora took on the colour of Radha; from His lips — "Radha, Radha!";
understanding the hint, His dear Gadadhara playfully took his place at the left.[^15-17]

## 8. Yadu — "gorā mora vaṛai raṅgiyā…" (PK 2101; BR pp. 925–926; GPT1 p. 257, no. 30)
*Kirtana on the bank of the Suradhuni: Gaura dances in the midst of His associates — Gadadhara and Narahari on either side, and Srivasa,
Haridasa, Mukunda, Murari, Vasu, Ramai, Damodara and Jagadisha singing; "Hari! Hari!" is heard on all sides; seeing the moon of His
face, one forgets all torments. Raga suhini.*[^15-18]

**8.1.** *(Refrain)* My Gora is a great merry-maker:
on the bank of the Suradhuni — with new merry companions.

**8.2.** The associates sing, enchanting hearts;
in their midst dances Gaura — the jewel among brahmanas.

**8.3.** Gadadhara and Narahari — on the right and the left;
Srivasa and Haridasa sing the name of Hari.

**8.4.** With Him are Mukunda, Murari, Vasu, Ramai;
Damodara and wise Jagadisha sing.[^15-19]

**8.5.** On all sides is heard: "Hari! Hari!" —
the ocean of prema has risen in waves of nectar.

**8.6.** Seeing the moon of His face, one is freed of all torments.
Says Yadu: who could forget such beauty?

## 9. Ramananda — "drāṃ drimiki drimi mādala vājata…" (GPT1 p. 335, no. 45)
*The Lord's dance in kirtana: the madala thunders, Srivasa and all the associates sing; His arms reach to His knees, His body is as of
gold, in red garments He shines like the morning sun; now He trembles, now His hair stands on end, now, raising His arms, He cries
"Hari! Hari!", cherishing His former prema; with Him are Nityananda, Advaita and the associates; at this play even a diamond softens.
Raga gandhara.*[^15-20]

**9.1.** "Drang-drimiki-drimi" thunders the madala: how many talas, how many well-matched rhythms!
He dances the dance of the whole universe — Srivasa and all the others sing.[^15-21]

**9.2.** His arms reach to His knees, His body is as of pure gold;
in red garments — the whole world trembles: like the morning sun.

**9.3.** Now He trembles, now His hair stands on end, now He waves His arms;
now, raising them high, He cries: "Hari! Hari!" — cherishing His former prema.

**9.4.** The avadhuta moon, Thakura Advaita, and with them all the associates.
Says Ramananda: at this play a diamond softens and wood melts.

the pada is unsigned. GPT1 — p. 284, section on bhavavesha, no. 23 (turi), scan PDF p. 543: the second half of the last line is replaced by
the signature "kahe nayanānanda dāsa"; GPT2 — sec. 4.3, no. 23. The pada is not in BR, KGC or PS; it was missing from the catalogue (new row
NN-031). Nayanananda, the nephew of Gadadhara Pandita, is a contemporary poet (chapters 4, 10, 14); but his signature is found only in
GPT — the attribution is conditional (C).

dipika 147–153); the left side is Radha's place beside Krishna. "As if gazing at the flute at His lips" (muralī-mukha heriyā) may also mean

Pandita; Jagadisha — Jagadisha Pandita. The night kirtanas of Navadvipa — CB Madhya 8; CC Adi 17.
