prema of Vrindavana, of Krishna's lila. The avadhuta moon is Nityananda. "A diamond (vajra) softens, wood melts" — even the hardest
hearts melt. "Like the morning sun": GPT1 has "pātara" (= prātara, "morning").

## 10. Vasu Ghosha — "paṛiyā dharaṇītale śoke śacī…" (GPT1 p. 372, no. 21)
*Shachi's lament after the Lord's departure: fallen on the ground, she complains of cruel fate — her priceless treasure has been
stolen; Gorachand's bracelets, necklace and bed lie abandoned, Nadia is plunged in darkness; she is ready to become a yogini and go in
search of Him, to sell herself as a maid to whoever will give her back Gauranga; the poet: do not weep, Shachi — for the sake of the
living beings Nimai has become a sannyasi. Raga karuna.*[^15-22]

**10.1.** Fallen on the ground, Shachi weeps in grief and says: "Cruel fate has become my enemy!
I had a priceless treasure — what fate has stolen Gorachand, the darling doll of my soul?

**10.2.** The bracelets from His arms, Gorachand's necklace, the bed, the silk, the gold-woven rug —
all lie abandoned: Gaura has left me, and I go on living in vain.

**10.3.** Gauranga has gone — Nadia is plunged in darkness, my heart tosses about.
I shall become a yogini, I shall go where I can find Gauranga — I shall weep, my arms around His neck.

**10.4.** Whoever gives me back Gauranga — to him I shall sell myself without price, I shall be the maid of his servant."
Says Vasudeva Ghosha: why do you weep, Shachi? For the sake of the living beings Nimai has become a sannyasi.[^15-23]

## 11. Vasu Ghosha — "svarūpera mukhe śuni mānalīlā…" (GPT1 p. 290, no. 42)
*The Lord in Radha's bhava: hearing from Svarupa of the mana-lila, He is plunged into the bhava of the Loving One (Radha), dances crying
"Radha-kunda!", slowly walks to the bank of the "Yamuna," sits by the water and, His face bowed, is lost in thought; the poet: only one
who has realized rasa in the heart knows its essence. Raga dhanashi, tala dashakushi.*[^15-24]

**11.1.** *(Refrain)* Young Gaura is in bhavavesha:
hearing from Svarupa's lips of the mana-lila, the jewel of brahmanas was lost in the bhava of the Loving One.[^15-25]

**11.2.** "Radha-kunda! Radha-kunda!" — crying out, He dances with arms flung up; streams of prema flow from both His eyes.
One cannot understand where His bhava is drawing Him: slowly, slowly He walks, His gait surpassing the king of elephants.

**11.3.** Coming to the bank of the Yamuna, sitting right by the water, He is lost in thought;
seeing the waves of that bhava, I can understand nothing: He sits with His holy face bowed.

**11.4.** Says Vasudeva Ghosha: one who has realization in his heart — he, the connoisseur of rasa, knows the essence of rasa;
one who has no realization — to him it is unknowable: his life has been in vain.

## 12. Vasu Ghosha — "svarūpera kāche gaurahari…" (GPT1 p. 306, no. 24)
*The Lord in the bhava of Radha disappointed in waiting (vipralabdha): weeping before Svarupa, He says that in vain He set the snares
of love — Kala-chand did not come to the kunja, the dew is falling, the night has passed for nothing; having said this, He rolls on the
ground. Raga suhai.*[^15-26]

**12.1.** Before Svarupa Gaurahari,
weeping, speaks, sobbing aloud:

**12.2.** "In vain I laid the snares of love —
Kala-chand did not come to the kunja.

**12.3.** Drip, drip — the dew is falling;
the night has grown very deep.

**12.4.** In vain I watched the road of hope,
in vain I spent this night."[^15-27]

**12.5.** Having said this, He rolls on the ground;
Vasu Ghosha moans: "Alas, alas!"

[^15-22]: GPT1 — p. 372, section on the sannyasa, no. 21 (karuna), checked against the scan (PDF p. 631); GPT2 — sec. 5.3, no. 21. The pada is not in
PK (including Vasu's sannyasa cycle PK 2221–2229, chapter 4), BR, KGC or PS; it was missing from the catalogue (new row VG-175). The
preceding pada of GPT (no. 20) is Vasu's PK 2221 (chapter 4, no. 10). GPT only; C.
[^15-23]: "I shall become a yogini" — I shall go as a wandering ascetic to find my son: so speaks a mother's love (vatsalya). "For the sake of the
living beings": the Lord took sannyasa so that even the proud, seeing a sannyasi, would bow before Him and receive prema (CC Adi 17;
CB Madhya 26). Shachi's grief after the sannyasa — CC Madhya 3; CB Antya 1.
[^15-24]: GPT1 — p. 290, section on bhavavesha, no. 42 (dhanashi, dashakushi), checked against the scan (PDF p. 549); GPT2 — sec. 4.3, no. 42. The
pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS; it was missing from the catalogue (new row VG-176). Svarupa Damodara was with the Lord in Puri and sang
Him songs in keeping with His bhava (CC Madhya 10; Antya 14–19); the "Yamuna" is apparently the sea or a river in Puri which the Lord in
His bhava takes for the Yamuna (cf. CC Antya 18). Majumdar doubts that GPT padas in which Svarupa is with the Lord belong to Vasu (see
chapter 12, no. 28); GPT only; C.

is Radha. Radha's bhava is pure prema, not a worldly feeling; the Lord tastes it in order to know Radha's love (CC Adi 4). Radha-kunda is
Radha's pond near Govardhana.

no. 24. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS; it was missing from the catalogue (new row VG-177). The next pada of GPT (no. 25, "svarūpera kare
dhari…") was translated in chapter 12 (no. 28). GPT only; C.
[^15-27]: The Lord in Radha's bhava speaks Her words (Svarupa in this lila is
Radha's friend Lalita). Kala-chand, "the dark moon," is Krishna; a kunja is a bower in Vrindavana. The Lord's bhavas in Puri in Svarupa's
company — CC Antya 14–19.

## 13. Chaitanyadasa — "ki valiva vidhātāre e dukha sahāya…" (PK 1867; GPT1 p. 281, no. 12)
*The divine madness of prema (divyonmada): the poet does not know what to say to the Creator — seeing Gora's face, how can one still
live? The Lord sits with faded face, tears pour like the heavenly Ganga onto the peak of Sumeru; now He rubs His face and head, now He
leaps up and runs, now He falls senseless; His breath stops — all weep. Raga suhini.*[^15-28]

**13.1.** What shall I say to the Creator, who makes us bear this pain?
Seeing Gora's face, why does life not leave me?

**13.2.** He sits with a faded face, tears pour from both His eyes —
like a stream of the heavenly Ganga onto the peak of Sumeru.

**13.3.** Now He rubs His face and head, now He leaps up and runs;
utterly spent, He falls to the ground senseless.

**13.4.** There is no breath in His nostrils — seeing this, all weep;
the heart of Chaitanyadasa cannot be calm.[^15-29]

## 14. Vasu Ghosha — "nitāi āmāra parama dayāla…" (GPT1 p. 424, no. 32)
*Nityananda's flood of prema: Nitai brought a flood of prema into the world, and it filled the rivers and canals; the wave carried away
sinners and sufferers alike, the devotees sport in it, some swim; Nadia and Shantipur went under — and started a boat race; Nitai
laughs, and the poet flounders in the waves. Raga sindhura.*[^15-30]

**14.1.** *(Refrain)* My Nitai is supremely merciful:
bringing a flood of prema, He blessed the world — filled the rivers and canals with prema.

**14.2.** The wave of prema struck — no one was left aside: sinners and sufferers were carried off by the current;
all the devotees together sport in that prema, and some go swimming.

**14.3.** Nadia went under, Shantipur is sinking in prema — the two together have started a boat race;
seeing this, Nitai laughs; all float in prema, and Vasu Ghosha flounders, gulping water.[^15-31]

## 15. Kanu Dasa — "āota nityānanda adabhuta cām̐da…" (GPT1 pp. 431–432, no. 59)
*Praise of Nityananda: Nityananda comes — a wondrous moon with the enchanting gait of a dancer; His face and eyes are lotuses, His lips
brighter than the dawn, His teeth pearls; with the nectar of His words He sprinkles those scorched by worldly existence, with the rays of
the name "Hare Krishna" He dispels the darkness of bad desires; around Him are His companions like stars. Raga kalyana.*[^15-32]

**15.1.** *(Refrain)* Nityananda comes — a wondrous moon:
natural is His gait, beautiful His dancing step — a form that enchants the people of the three worlds.

**15.2.** His face and eyes are pure, beautiful lotuses, and over them, like bees, the pair of brows;
the lustre of His red lips is brighter than the dawn, His teeth a string of pearls.[^15-33]

**15.3.** Those scorched by the heat of worldly existence He mercifully sprinkles with streams of the nectar of His words;
with the rays of the name "Hare Krishna" He destroys all the darkness of bad desires.

**15.4.** Around Him are His merry companions, like a host of stars: night and day this moon shines.
Hoping for the feet, tender as young shoots, of Sri Jahnava-vallabha, speaks Sri Kanu Dasa.[^15-34]

missing from the catalogue (new row CD-008). Chaitanyadasa, according to Majumdar, is probably a contemporary of the branch of Gadadhara
(chapters 4–7); B.

the walls of the Gambhira (CC Antya 19); in the deepest swoon of prema His breath stops (cf. CC Antya 14, 17). "Why does life not leave me"
is the sorrow of a devotee who sees the Lord's suffering in separation. The heavenly Ganga (Mandakini) flowing down the golden mountain
Sumeru is an image of the tears streaming down Gaura's golden body. PK MSS: "uṭhe" — kha; "duravale" — cha; "bhome" — cha.

gulping water") point to a late origin; C. Nityananda's preaching in Gauda — CB Antya 5–6.
[^15-31]: The flood of prema that inundated the world is an image from CC Adi 7: Advaita called the Lord down, Nityananda spread prema all over
Gauda. Nadia (Navadvipa) is the Lord's place, Shantipur Advaita's. "Flounders" — the poet's humility: he cannot swim in this flood.

the signature "Sri Jahnava-vallabha" (Jahnava's husband, Nityananda) fits him; but the pada is known only from GPT; C.

eyes" is the usual image of brows. "A string of pearls": GPT1 "motikala," GPT2 "motiphala" ("pearl").

at the Lord's command, gave to everyone (CB Madhya 13).

# Chapter 16. Yadu: Two Gaura-padas from the *Padakalpataru* Found in the Full Check of PK

*This chapter is the result of a full check of all four volumes of the *Padakalpataru* (PK) by the signatures of the poets
contemporary with Mahaprabhu on Majumdar's list. Only three
gaura-padas turned out to be unknown to the catalogue and to translations 01–15, all signed "Yadu" (Yadunatha): two are translated
here, the third (PK 703) is in nagari-bhava and is deferred to the section of nagari-padas. The other results of the check are PK
numbers for padas previously known only from the *Gaura-pada-tarangini* (GPT), the *Bhakti-ratnakara* or the
*Kshanada-gita-chintamani* and already translated (YD-003 = PK 2512, YD-004 = PK 1976, AN-007 = PK 2328, AN-008 = PK 2337, BD-028 =
PK 2301, BD-041 = PK 635, KR-004 = PK 1464, VG-151 = PK 2668), and a correction: Balarama's pada "sava avatāra sāra…" (chapter 13,
no. 8) is PK 2201, bearing his signature in PK itself, not Lochana Dasa's pada PK 2203; the notes of those chapters have been
supplemented. Both padas of this chapter stand in the 20th pallava of PK ("Sri Gaurachandra — other descriptions") and are also in
GPT1 (p. 37, nos. 33–34): praise of the Gaura-avatara, before whom all living beings weep, and the love of Gaura and Gadadhara. The
text follows PK with the GPT variants; the Bengali original and the word-for-word translation are in the full version of the book.*

## 1. Yadu — "jalera jīva kānde dekhiyā prativimba…" (PK 2209; GPT1 p. 37, no. 34)
*Praise of the Gaura-avatara: at the sight of Gorachand all living beings weep — the creatures of the water seeing His reflection,
the beasts and birds in the forests; trees thrill, stones melt, the blind weep aloud hearing of Him, the wives of noble families
weep, the deaf and the helpless, infants leaving the breast; there will be no such incarnation again — He saved all, only the poet
is left out. Raga mangala.*[^16-1]

**1.1.** The creatures of the water weep, seeing His reflection; in the forests the beasts and birds weep;
the trees thrill, the stones melt, the blind, hearing of Him, weep and cry aloud.

**1.2.** *(Refrain)* Wondrous is the body of Gorachand!
Boundless is what one feels: how can one tell it with a single mouth? What is in the heart does not come to the lips.

**1.3.** The wives of noble families — even they weep aloud; the deaf and the helpless weep in bewilderment;
the infant, leaving its mother's breast, weeps — no one knows why.[^16-2]

**1.4.** There will be no such incarnation again: He is an ocean of nothing but mercy.
The fallen, the foolish, the inanimate and the animate — He saved them all; only Yadu was left out.[^16-3]

## 2. Yadu — "gaura gadādhara duhum̐ tanu sundara…" (PK 2182; GPT1 p. 37, no. 33)
*Gaura and Gadadhara: both are beautiful and wondrously spread prema; when, rejoicing, they touch each other, nectar flows; hand in
hand, eye to eye — a sweetness beyond understanding; who, plunging into these feelings, will reach the bottom? Seeing them, people
forget body and mind. Raga kedara.*[^16-4]

**2.1.** Gaura and Gadadhara — both are beautiful, wondrously spreading prema;
when, rejoicing, they touch each other in their play, nectar pours without end.[^16-5]

**2.2.** *(Refrain)* Behold, behold: wondrous is the love of these two!
Who, plunging into these feelings, into this art full of prema, will reach the bottom?

**2.3.** Hand in hand, eye to eye — the sweetness that is between them, how could I understand it?
Seeing their wondrous beauty, the body thrills: there is none like it in all the worlds.

**2.4.** Are they dolls of nectar, or embodiments of rasa, or is it prema itself that has taken two forms?
Seeing them, the people of the world forget body and mind — will Yadu find a limit to it?[^16-6]

[^16-1]: PK — vol. 3, 20th pallava ("Śrī-Gauracandra — prakārāntara"), label "॥২৬॥২২০৯॥", raga mangala, MS P-R-Sa no. 2317 (MS P-R — 9.21),
checked against the scan (PDF p. 272, printed p. 261); GPT1 — p. 37, section of praise of the Gaura-avatara, no. 34 (mangala), checked
against the scan (PDF p. 296); GPT2 — sec. 1.3, no. 34 (p. 26). The pada is not in the *Bhakti-ratnakara* (BR), the
*Kshanada-gita-chintamani* (KGC) or the *Padamrita-samudra* (PS). It was missing from the catalogue (new row YD-019): it was found in
the full check of PK (the log of chapter 8 mentions it in passing — "PK 2209 — Yadu" — but it never entered the catalogue; the earlier
checks of GPT1 signatures missed it because the signature "yadu" is garbled in the OCR). The signature "yadu": Yadunatha Dasa
(Kavichandra), whose padas stand nearby in the same pallava (PK 2180, 2191; chapters 6 and 13), or Yadunandana — not established; C.
[^16-2]: They weep not from grief but from the prema that the sight of the Lord awakens — so the stones melt and the trees thrill (cf. CC
Madhya 17: in the forests of Jharikhanda beasts and birds danced and chanted the name together with the Lord). The wives of noble
families here are among all living beings: this is not the motif of townswomen captivated by Gaura's beauty (nagari-bhava) but a
picture of universal prema; cf. the wives of noble families dancing in sankirtana in Balarama's pada (PK 2207, chapter 10, no. 2).
"The helpless" (jaṛa) — the dull, unable to move or understand; MS P-R: "the dumb and the deaf" (mūka vadhira).
[^16-3]: "The inanimate and the animate" (jaṛa ajaṛa) — the unmoving (the trees and stones of 1.1) and the moving: the Lord's mercy embraces all
that exists. "Only Yadu was left out" is the usual formula of humility in signatures (cf. Balarama in PK 2201 and 2207, chapters 13 and
10): the poet speaks of himself. MS P-R-Sa: "the fallen, the foolish people" (jana for jaṛa) and "the Deliverer" (uddhāraṇa for uddhārila).
[^16-4]: PK — vol. 3, 20th pallava, label "॥১৫॥২১৮২॥", raga kedara, MS P-R-Sa no. 2290, checked against the scan (PDF pp. 261–262, printed
pp. 250–251); GPT1 — p. 37, section of praise of the Gaura-avatara, no. 33 (kedara), checked against the scan (PDF p. 296); GPT2 — sec.
1.3, no. 33 (pp. 25–26). The pada is not in BR, KGC or PS; it was missing from the catalogue (new row YD-018) — found in the full check of
PK. In PK it immediately follows Nayanananda's pada on Gaura and Gadadhara (PK 2181) and stands one after Yadunatha's pada
"gaura-varaṇa tanu…" (PK 2180, chapter 13, no. 6), with which it shares theme and phrasing. The signature "yadu" is the same poet as in
no. 1 (see note 1); C.
[^16-5]: Gadadhara Pandita, according to Kavi Karnapura's *Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika* (vv. 147–153), is Sri Radha appearing in the Lord's
lila; his whole life is service to Gaura. The intimacy of Gaura and Gadadhara is the Lord's lila with the embodiment of His internal
energy: it is pure prema with nothing mundane in it, and therefore the poet sees in them "prema itself that has taken two forms" (2.4).
The worship of Gaura together with Gadadhara (Gaura-Gadadhara) is accepted in Gadadhara's line; the pada has nothing to do with
"gaura-nagari" (Gaura as the nagara among the women of Nadia).
[^16-6]: GPT1 and GPT2 read in the refrain (2.2) "who, immersed [in it], will obtain it" (majiyā pāova seha) instead of "will reach the bottom"
(nimajiyā pāova theha PK). "Find a limit" (pāova pāra) — "reach the shore": admiration, not complaint; cf. the humble signature of the same poet in
no. 1.

# Part II. Appendix: Padas Signed "Narahari" from the Gaura-pada-tarangini

---

# Chapter 17. Appendix. Padas signed "Narahari" from the Gaura-pada-tarangini — I: mangalacharana, Gaura's form, abhisheka, kirtana and dance, bhavavesha

## Introductory note to the appendix

*In the Gaura-pada-tarangini (GPT1 — 1st ed. by Jagadbandhu Bhadra, 1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934) more than three hundred padas
are signed with the name "Narahari" (narahari, "narahari dāsa", "dāsa narahari", "narahari-pahu"). Those also found in the
Padakalpataru (PK) were translated in the main part (chapters 1–6): they are padas of Narahari Sarakara, which Majumdar
examines as songs of an eyewitness. Here, as a separate appendix, are gathered the padas with the same signature known only
from the GPT (and from the Bhakti-ratnakara) — by decision, all are to be translated, with a caveat about attribution.*

*Narahari is the name of two poets. **Narahari Sarakara Thakura** of Shrikhanda was an associate of Mahaprabhu, the teacher
of Lochana Dasa, a singer of the Lord's bhavas in Navadvipa and Puri; according to the Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika (177), he is Madhumati, an intimate friend of
Radha in Vrindavana. **Narahari Chakravarti** (also called Ghanashyama Dasa), who lived in Vrindavana in the first half of the 18th
century, is the author of the Bhakti-ratnakara (BR), Narottama-vilasa, Gita-chandrodaya and other books; in the BR he inserted
many of his own songs signed "Narahari" or "Ghanashyama", mostly in Vrajabuli, and often put them in the mouths of the people
of Navadvipa while describing the holy places.*

*The signature alone does not tell whose a pada is. The index of poets in GPT2 divides the "Narahari" padas into three groups:
≈30 of Sarakara (taken from the journal Gauranga-madhuri, published in Shrikhanda), ≈171 of Chakravarti (those found in the
BR) and 112 of "Narahari Dasa", undistinguished. Majumdar accepts as Sarakara's only the padas preserved in PK and regards
padas known only from the GPT as unreliable; of the "Narahari" padas in the BR, by his analysis, only one belongs to Sarakara
(BR p. 924 = PK 2122, chapter 3, no. 1). Sarakara's marks, according to Majumdar, are a simple Bengali without Vrajabuli,
without heaped comparisons and alliterations, a correct metre, brevity; ornate Vrajabuli with chains of assonance is
Chakravarti's manner. But even the index groups are not beyond doubt: thus pada no. 128 of the section on Gaura's form stands
in the index on a page assigned to Sarakara, while in the BR it is put in the mouth of a woman of Nadia (below, no. 8).*

*Therefore each pada is marked in its heading: **"probably Sarakara"** — simple Bengali, absent from the BR, assigned by the
GPT2 index to Sarakara; **"probably Chakravarti"** — the pada is in the BR (usually the language too is Vrajabuli with
alliterations); **"not established"** — the arguments conflict or are lacking. In the lila database the padas "probably
Chakravarti" have authority B (the author is a recognized acharya, the author of the Bhakti-ratnakara; his authorship is established by his
works), the padas "probably Sarakara" and "not established" have authority C; no pada of the appendix has authority D (doubtful
authenticity). Chakravarti's padas are a late (18th-century) poetic elaboration of the lilas by a recognized acharya: not the testimony of an
eyewitness, but not a forgery either; they often follow the Chaitanya-bhagavata and the Chaitanya-charitamrita. Padas in nagari-bhava
(speech of townswomen in love with Gaura) are deferred to the
section of nagari padas; padas in which "Narahari" is merely mentioned among the associates while the signature is
another's are excluded.*

*Chapter 17 is the first chapter of the appendix: three padas of mangalacharana (by the GPT2 index — Sarakara's), Gaura's form,
the abhisheka in Srivasa's house and arati, kirtana and dance in Navadvipa (a large cycle, almost all of it known also from
the BR), bhavavesha — the Lord in the mood of Shiva and in the mood of Krishna. The padas follow the order of the lilas. The
base text is GPT1 (tesseract recognition, doubtful places by the IA scan in.ernet.dli.2015.477854) collated with GPT2 and
the BR (eds. 1912 and 1960); variants are in the full version of the book. All the padas were also checked against Narahari Chakravarti's Gita-chandrodaya — none of them is there. The notes of the GPT editors are not reproduced.*

## 1. Narahari — "gaura-līlā daraśane icchā vaṛa haya mane…" (GPT1 p. 11, no. 27)
*Mangalacharana: the poet, seeing Gaura-lila, wishes to write it down in his own tongue but does not know how; the one who will
write a book of it is not yet born; the lila of Gaura and Gadadhara, which melts stone, cannot be described even by Sarasvati
and Shiva — may at least the poet's few songs help someone to reveal the Lord's lila. Raga pahida. **Attribution: probably
Sarakara** — the GPT2 index assigns the pada to Sarakara; it is not in the BR; simple Bengali tripadi; the poet speaks as an
eyewitness, before books on Gaura had appeared.*[^17-1]

**1.1.** Seeing Gaura's lila, I greatly long in my heart to write it all down in our own tongue;
but I am most lowly, I do not know how to write in due order — how then shall I write it?[^17-2]

**1.2.** He who will write this book is not yet born — long yet is the delay before his birth;
when it is composed in our own tongue, all people will understand — when will the Lord fulfil my wish?[^17-3]

**1.3.** The lila of Gaura and Gadadhara softens stone — who has the power to describe it?
Even if Sharada were to write ceaselessly, without end, and five-faced Sadashiva with her…[^17-4]

**1.4.** If, seeing the few songs I write, someone reveals to the world the Lord's lila —
Narahari will find happiness, the grief of his heart will go: at the singing of that book stones will melt.

## 2. Narahari Dasa — "vraja-bhūma kari śūnya nadīyāya avatīrṇa…" (GPT1 pp. 11–12, no. 28)
*Mangalacharana: an address to Gaura, recognized as the Krishna of Vraja: having emptied Vraja, He has descended in Nadia; there
is no peacock feather, no yellow cloth, no flute, no curving pose — yet, since He has let Himself be seen, the mind will not be
deceived: this is that very Kanai of Vraja. Raga pahida. **Attribution: probably Sarakara** — GPT2 index (Sarakara); not in
the BR; simple Bengali tripadi.*[^17-5]

**2.1.** Having emptied the land of Vraja, You descended in Nadia — such is Your cunning!
Giving ceaseless pain, having changed colour and bhava, You again multiply the snares of separation.[^17-6]

**2.2.** There is no crown of peacock feather, none of that yellow cloth, in Your hand none of that enchanting flute —
that flute with whose song You stole the very life of the gopis: where is that flute, Gaurahari?

**2.3.** None of those slanting eyes — now I see lovely eyes; none of that curve, none of that bending.
But since You have let Yourself be seen, the mind is not deceived by this form: You are that very Kanai of Vraja.[^17-7]

**2.4.** Says Narahari Dasa: whoever has no faith, let him come and see with his own eyes.
To speak of what happened that day at the meeting of the two is a pain in the heart.[^17-8]

## 3. Narahari — "rase tanu ḍharaḍhara gaura-kiśora-vara…" (GPT1 p. 12, no. 29)
*Mangalacharana: the Shyama of Dvapara is called Sri Krishna Chaitanya in Kali; within He is Shyama, without golden: to play with
Rai in the groves, out of love He became golden; the poet fears to speak of the hidden and cannot keep silent. Raga pahida.
**Attribution: probably Sarakara** — GPT2 index (Sarakara); not in the BR; simple Bengali tripadi.*[^17-9]

**3.1.** His body brimming with rasa, the best of youths, Gaura-kishora — now His name is Sri Krishna Chaitanya.
To speak of these hidden things is a pain in the heart: without bhakti no one else will know them.

**3.2.** In the Dvapara age Shyama, in Kali the name Chaitanya — so are Garga's words written in the Bhagavata.
I ponder in my heart: Shyama has become Gauranga — the body of Radha and Krishna is its witness.[^17-10]

**3.3.** Within, the dark body; without, the golden body — wondrous is Gauranga's lila!
To play with Rai, to enjoy the groves, out of love He took the golden body.[^17-11]

**3.4.** This is not a thing to be told — who knows what may come of telling it; yet not to tell is great pain in the heart.
Pondering in his mind, holding Gauranga in his heart, Narahari laments.

[^17-1]: GPT1 — p. 11, mangalacharana section, no. 27 (pahida), checked against the scan (PDF pp. 270–271); GPT2 — sec. 1.2, no. 27
(catalogue: NG-001). Not in PK, the BR, the Kshanada-gita-chintamani (KGC) or the Padamrita-samudra (PS). The index of poets of GPT2
assigns p. 8 (padas nos. 27–29) to Narahari Sarakara (from the journal Gauranga-madhuri); the language is simple Bengali tripadi
without Vrajabuli, which fits Majumdar's marks of Sarakara. But the pada is known only from the GPT; C.
[^17-2]: "In our own tongue" (bhāṣāya) — in Bengali, not in Sanskrit: the first books on the Lord (Murari Gupta, Kavi Karnapura) were
written in Sanskrit.
[^17-3]: If the pada is genuine, it was written in the Lord's lifetime or soon after, when there were as yet no Bengali books about
Gaura. Whom the poet awaits he does not say; Bengali poems on the Lord were written by Vrindavana Dasa (Chaitanya-bhagavata) and by
Lochana Dasa, a disciple of Narahari Sarakara, who calls him his Thakura (Chaitanya-mangala, Sutra-khanda, ch. 1, vv. 9, 61).
[^17-4]: Sharada — Sarasvati, goddess of speech; Sadashiva — Shiva, the five-faced (pañcānana). Gadadhara — Gadadhara Pandita, the
inseparable associate of the Lord (in Krishna-lila — Radha): "the lila of Gaura and Gadadhara" is a favourite theme of Narahari
Sarakara (cf. chapter 3, no. 1).
[^17-5]: GPT1 — pp. 11–12, no. 28 (pahida), checked against the scan (PDF p. 271); GPT2 — sec. 1.2, no. 28. The pada was not in the
catalogue (new row NG-236): the stage-1 catalogue missed it. Not in PK, BR, KGC, PS. GPT2 index — Sarakara (p. 8). C.
[^17-6]: "Having changed colour and bhava" (varṇa kari bhāvāntara) — Krishna, who is dark, became golden, accepting the bhava of Radha
(CC Adi 1.5; ch. 4). The speaker is a resident of Vraja who has recognized Krishna in Gaura: "the snares of separation" are his
separation from Krishna, who has left Vraja for Nadia.
[^17-7]: "Curve" — tribhanga, the threefold bend of Krishna's body with the flute; "slanting eyes" — Krishna's sidelong glance. Kanai —
an endearing name of Krishna in Vraja. Cf. CC Madhya 8 (Ramananda Raya sees Krishna in the Lord).
[^17-8]: Who "the two" are the poet does not say; it is only clear that he speaks of a meeting in which the Lord revealed Himself as
Krishna to an associate who recognized Him.
[^17-9]: GPT1 — p. 12, no. 29 (pahida), checked against the scan (PDF p. 271); GPT2 — sec. 1.2, no. 29. The pada was not in the catalogue
(new row NG-237). Not in PK, BR, KGC, PS. GPT2 index — Sarakara (p. 8). C.
[^17-10]: Garga's words — Bhag. 10.8.13: in former ages Krishna had white, red and yellow colours, now He has become dark. The words "in
Kali the name Chaitanya" are not in Garga: this is the poet's interpretation; CC Adi 3.36–40 sees in the "yellow" (pīta) colour an
indication of the golden avatara of the Kali age. "The body of Radha and Krishna" — Gaura, Radha and Krishna united in one form
(CC Adi 1.5; 4.55–56).
[^17-11]: "Krishna within, Gaura without" — cf. Tattva-sandarbha, mangalacharana 2 (CC Adi 3.81). "Out of love" (anurāge) — Krishna,
wishing to taste Radha's love, took Her bhava and golden lustre (CC Adi 1.6; ch. 4); the golden colour is Her colour, not a
worldly passion.

## 4. Narahari — "nācata bhuvana-mano-mohana…" (GPT1 p. 135, no. 70; BR)
*Gaura's form in the dance: His colour brighter than champaka, gold and lotus, His body in sandal paste and Chinese silk, His face
gentler than moons, His brows a row of bees, necklace and earrings swaying, curls scattering, His tendril-like hands playing,
His feet keeping the rhythm. Raga karnata. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli
with chains of comparisons.*[^17-12]

**4.1.** He dances, the Enchanter of the minds of all the worlds — His colour surpassing champaka, gold and lotus;
His shapely, tender body anointed with sandal, He wears garments of Chinese silk, densely shining.

**4.2.** His sweet face puts to shame hosts of moons; sweetly He smiles — as if nectar were flowing;
His brows a row of bees; His eyes gleam and sway, robbing the dawn's rays of their power.[^17-13]

**4.3.** The jewelled necklace sways, stealing all composure; the earrings tremble, flashing at His ears;
His curling locks, under their own weight, scatter and sway like strands of darkness in the wind.

**4.4.** In graceful play of His tendril-like hands, stepping on the earth, He keeps hundreds of rhythms;
Narahari, in great delight, sings His glory: who can describe this boundless beauty?

## 5. Narahari — "nadīyāra mājhāre nācaye gorācām̐da…" (GPT1 p. 135, no. 72; BR)
*Gaura's form, from face to feet: Gorachand dancing in the midst of Nadia is a snare for every heart; seeing Him, the young
wives lose their senses; His face is the autumn moon, His speech nectar, His eyes the abode of love, His brows shame Kama's bow,
His curls are twined with malati, on His brow a drop of sandal; garland, long arms, slender waist, feet before whose nails Kama
swoons — this is the Nagara of Gokula, the ocean of rasa. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the
BR (12th wave, among the songs of the people of Nadia).*[^17-14]

**5.1.** In the midst of Nadia dances Gorachand —
a snare to capture the hearts of all people.

**5.2.** His body like golden filaments, His radiance beyond compare;
seeing Him, crowds of young wives lose their senses.[^17-15]

**5.3.** How sweet His face — the autumn moon!
His speech a stream of nectar, cooling the afflicted.

**5.4.** Slightly mingled with a smile, His lips shine;
the pearl-row of His teeth flashes.

**5.5.** His eyes are the abode of love;
with a glance He steals the life of the whole world.

**5.6.** Who carved these brows — so full of play —
to break the pride of Kama's bow?

**5.7.** The knot of His curling hair, flashing, is bent aside;
around the malati twined in it, swarms of bees are circling.

**5.8.** Who can keep composure, seeing that lovely brow?
The drop of sandal on it is death to the moon's pride.

**5.9.** On His breast sways the garland that has conquered the world;
whoever has seen it once keeps his eyes on it and remembers it ever.

**5.10.** How graceful the curve of His long arms!
How many movements in them — crushing the steadfastness of the chaste.

**5.11.** His slender waist — it would hide within a fist;
without price He buys hearts and refreshes the eyes.

**5.12.** The soles of His lotus feet are beyond compare;
before the radiance of His nails many a Kama swoons.[^17-16]

**5.13.** Says Narahari: what play does He not know! —
the Nagara of Gokula, that ocean of rasa.[^17-17]

## 6. Narahari — "suradhunī-tīre gaura naṭa-nāgara…" (GPT1 p. 136, no. 73; BR)
*Gaura's dance on the bank of the Suradhuni: Gaura, the graceful dancer, sports with His associates, captivating the eyes of the world;
His body outshines a golden mountain, His arms put to shame an elephant's trunk, again and again He cries "Hari, Hari!"; seeing
Gadadhara, He sheds tears like a cloud of the month of Shravana, and the earth trembles beneath His feet. Raga somaraga.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli.*[^17-18]

**6.1.** On the bank of the Suradhuni, Gaura, the graceful dancer, sports together with His associates;
the peerless, many-sided dance, ever-new sweetness — steals the eyes of all the people of the world.

**6.2.** His body, robbing a golden mountain of its pride, shines with abundant thrills;
the curve of His arms, which surpass an elephant's trunk, puts to shame hundreds of Kamas.[^17-19]

**6.3.** His teeth flash, lovely — the lustre of kunda flowers — in a soft smile on His sweet lips;
His face sways, His lips cry ceaselessly "Hari, Hari!" — who, hearing it, can keep composure?

**6.4.** His heart overflows when He sees Gadadhara: His eyes pour tears like a cloud in the month of Shravana;
says Narahari: the earth trembles under the weight of His lovely, light feet.[^17-20]

## 7. Narahari — "viharata surasarita-tīra…" (GPT1 pp. 151–152, no. 119; BR)
*Gaura's form on the bank of the Ganga, from face to feet: youthful, He sports by the river; His colour outshines lightning, gold
and kunkuma, His face is a snare for the eyes of young wives, His curls dark clouds, His brows serpents; broad chest, slender
waist, lotus feet about which bee-devotees hover; a cloud of mercy, He ever showers the nectar of prema — only foolish Narahari it
does not touch. Raga nataraga. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli with strings of
comparisons.*[^17-21]

**7.1.** By the bank of the heavenly river strolls Gaura — young, in unchanging youth: the lustre of His body crushes the pride of
lightning, gold and kunkuma; His moon-face torments Madana, a snare for the eyes of all young wives; in His smile His teeth gleam —
a row of kunda flowers.

**7.2.** The colour of dense collyrium, His curling locks steal composure; peerless shine His pure attire and scattered tresses;
the tilaka on His brow flashes brightly, His brows are gracefully gliding serpents; the corners of His restless eyes, tinged with
rasa, are an abode of beauty.[^17-22]

**7.3.** Earrings touch His cheeks, on His neck the forest garland; long arms, bracelets, tender palms — I give my life for them!
His broad, peerless chest destroys the steadfastness of many a noble wife; His graceful, slender waist humbles the pride of the
lion.

**7.4.** His arms sway, His knees are youthful; His feet are rays of the red dawn; to the sweet fragrance of these lotuses cling the
bee-devotees, intoxicated; a cloud of mercy, famed in the world, He ever showers the nectar of prema — only foolish Narahari is not
touched by a single drop.[^17-23]

## 8. Narahari — "ki jāni ki bhāve bhāvita antara…" (GPT1 p. 154, no. 128; BR)
*Gaura's form with Gadadhara: absorbed in an unknown bhava, His eyes reddened, He holds Gadadhara's hand and says something — as
if honeyed; His lips a bandhuli flower, His teeth lightning, His smile pours nectar; He dances in the guise of a nagara, the thief
of the hearts of the women of Nadia — this is Gora, the Enchanter of Gokula. Raga vallari. **Attribution: not established
(more likely Chakravarti)** — the GPT2 index assigns the page to Sarakara, but the pada is in the BR, where it is sung by a woman
of Nadia.*[^17-24]

**8.1.** Who knows by what bhava His heart is seized — both eyes are reddened;
holding Gadadhara's hand, what He says I do not know — as if steeped in honey.[^17-25]

**8.2.** His lips a tender bandhuli flower, His teeth a flash of lightning;
mingled with His smile pours a sea of nectar — the splendour of His moon-face.

**8.3.** In the guise of a nagara dances the Thief of the hearts of Nadia's women;
says Narahari: do you not know? Gora is the Enchanter of Gokula.[^17-26]

pada "nācata gaura puruva rase bhora" (below, no. 13). Not in PK, KGC, PS. The GPT2 index assigns p. 92 to Chakravarti. B.

vv. 2830–2842), among the songs which Narahari Chakravarti puts in the mouths of the people of Nadia remembering the Lord. Not in PK,
KGC, PS. B.

the motif of the townswomen captivated by Gaura's beauty: the language of nagari-bhava (Gaura as nagara); in the BR the pada is in
fact put in the mouth of a woman of Nadia. We translate faithfully to the author. Vrindavana Dasa stresses that in this incarnation
the Lord never looked at another man's wife; worship of Gaura in the spirit of "gaura-nagari" is not accepted by the Gaudiya
tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta). The attraction here is an image of the all-attractiveness of
Bhagavan, not of a worldly feeling.
[^17-16]: Description "from face to feet" (nakha-shikha) is the usual genre for describing Krishna's form; "many a Kama" — Gaura is more
beautiful than countless gods of love (cf. Bhag. 10.32.2: Krishna is "the enchanter of Manmatha himself").
[^17-17]: "The Nagara of Gokula" — Krishna, the beloved of the gopis of Gokula: the poet recognizes Krishna in Gaura. "What play does
He not know" — the Lord is expert in every lila.
[^17-18]: GPT1 — p. 136, no. 73 (somaraga); GPT2 — sec. 3.1, no. 73. In the catalogue it stood as a pada of Nayanananda (NN-006; chapter

Ishana shows Srinivasa the place on the bank of the Ganga where the Lord danced, and this song is cited. Not in PK, KGC, PS. B.
[^17-19]: "Natanagara" (naṭanāgara) — "skilled, graceful dancer": an epithet, not a motif of nagari-bhava. Kama (Kusumashara — "He whose
arrows are flowers") — the god of love: the Lord's beauty is above Kama's.
[^17-20]: Gadadhara Pandita is Radha in Krishna-lila (Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika 147–153): at the sight of him Krishna's love for Radha awakens
in the Lord. Shravana — a month of the rainy season (July–August).

kahe"); the first line is corrected. BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 890; ed. 1960, vv. 2630–2633). The GPT2 index assigns p. 103 to
Chakravarti. Not in PK, KGC, PS. B.
[^17-22]: "Brows — serpents" (bhāṅa-bhujaga) — the thin, curving brows are likened to gliding snakes; "abode of beauty" (chavidhāma).
[^17-23]: "Destroys the steadfastness of many a noble wife" (7.3) — the same motif of the townswomen as in no. 5 (see note 15). The last
words differ among the witnesses (GPT1 "mati mandakababha", GPT2 "mati manda karaha", BR "mati mandaka bahu"); the sense is "only foolish
Narahari is not touched (by the nectar) at all": the poet's usual self-abasement.

2858–2861): Chakravarti cites it as the song of a certain woman of Nadia ("kācit — vallarī") and opens it with an address to a friend:
"Friend! What a wondrous form! The body thrilled, peerless — like a new king Madana." The two attributions conflict; by the BR,
Chakravarti is more likely. Not in PK, KGC, PS. C. The neighbouring no. 129 (address to women friends, the wish "to keep Him in the
heart") is nagari-bhava and is deferred.
[^17-25]: Gadadhara — see note 20. Cf. PK 2122 of Narahari Sarakara (chapter 3, no. 1): the Lord in the mood of Krishna embraces Gadadhara.
[^17-26]: "Nagara, the thief of the hearts of Nadia's women" — the motif of the townswomen (see note 15). The address "do you not know"
is to the listeners; in the BR, to the speaker's friend.

## 9. Narahari — "āju abhiṣeka sukhera avadhi…" (GPT1 pp. 241–242, no. 14; BR)
*The abhisheka in Srivasa's house: Gaura, the treasury of virtues, sits on the throne; His curls stream down His back like the
Yamuna down a golden mountain; Nityananda and Advaita recite the abhisheka mantras, Srivasa and others pour fragrant water from
pitchers on the Lord's head; Jagadisha, Vasudeva, Narayana, Mukunda, Madhava sing, Govinda and Govindananda play the mridanga,
Vakreshvara dances; the invisible gods shower flowers, the devoted wives cry "Jaya!". Raga suhai or mayura. **Attribution:
probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave, account of the abhisheka).*[^17-27]

**9.1.** Today is the abhisheka — the very limit of happiness: on the throne sits Gora, the treasury of virtues;
peerless is the beauty of His bearing — no one on earth can keep composure.

**9.2.** Smooth curling locks adorn His head and stream down His back — their lustre charms the mind,
as if on the peak of a golden mountain the stream of the Yamuna were flowing.[^17-28]

**9.3.** His pure body shines, robbing hundreds of Kamas of their pride;
who would not lose himself, glancing but once at His moon-face steeped in smiles?

**9.4.** Again and again reciting the abhisheka mantras, Nityananda and Advaita rejoice at heart;
Srivasa and the others, pitchers in hand, pour fragrant water on the Lord's head.

**9.5.** Jagadisha, Vasudeva, Narayana, Mukunda, Madhava — skilled in singing —
in various strains, by shruti, jati and svara, sing the song of the abhisheka, like nectar.[^17-29]

**9.6.** Govinda and Govindananda play the khol: "dha-dha, dhik-dhik, dheka, na-na" it sounds;
Vakreshvara dances in a sweet rhythm; from the eyes of some flow streams of bliss.[^17-30]

**9.7.** The gods with their retinues, unseen, enchanted by the joy of the abhisheka,
shower flowers layer upon layer, cry "Jaya, jaya!", their bodies thrilling.

**9.8.** The wives devoted to their husbands again and again cry "Jaya!" — how delightful!
What ever-new auspicious rites! Seeing them, Narahari feels his heart surge with joy.[^17-31]

## 10. Narahari — "ki ānanda śrīvāsa-bhavane…" (GPT1 p. 242, no. 15; BR)
*The abhisheka in Srivasa's house: the Lord is seated on a golden throne, mantras are recited and water is poured on His head from
pitchers; the women raise the auspicious cry "ulu-ulu", instruments resound, all sing songs of the abhisheka; the gods, beholding the
abhisheka, dance; the poet offers himself to the Lord, before whose face Madana swoons. Raga dhanashi. **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave, right after the preceding one).*[^17-32]

**10.1.** What bliss in Srivasa's house!
The beloved associates perform the Lord's abhisheka.

**10.2.** Seating Him on a golden throne,
they bring fragrant water, rejoicing.

**10.3.** Having recited the abhisheka mantras,
they pour water on the Lord's head from brimming pitchers.

**10.4.** The women raise the cry "ulu-ulu",
various instruments resound, piercing the sky.[^17-33]

**10.5.** All sing songs of the abhisheka;
their eyes ceaselessly shed streams of bliss.

**10.6.** The gods, crying "Jaya, jaya!",
dance with what delight, beholding the abhisheka!

**10.7.** Enchanting is the beauty of the abhisheka:
His tender body shines.

**10.8.** Narahari offers himself to Him;
before His nectarean face Madana swoons.[^17-34]

## 11. Narahari — "śrī-śacī māyere āge kari…" (GPT1 p. 242, no. 16)
*The abhisheka: the women of Nadia, row upon row, follow Shachi to Srivasa's house to see Gora's abhisheka; the devotees pour Suradhuni
water on His head, wipe Him, dress Him in dry silk; Shachi puts sandal, gorochana and perfume on His forehead; the women raise the cry
"ulu-ulu", the khol, the kartals and the ramshinga horn resound. Raga suhai. **Attribution: not established** — the pada is not in
the BR; simple Bengali tripadi; the GPT2 index assigns the page to Chakravarti (because of the neighbouring pada).*[^17-35]

**11.1.** Letting Mother Shachi go before them, all the women of Nadia walk in rows upon rows;
they come to the house of Srivasa Pandita to see Gora's abhisheka.

**11.2.** Gora's abhisheka is a wondrous lila: no one has ever seen the like with his own eyes;
filling pitchers with Suradhuni water, all the devotees pour it on Gora's head.

**11.3.** Wiping His body with the edge of a silk cloth, they gave Him dry silk garments to wear;
on His brow Mother Shachi lovingly placed sandal, gorochana and the perfume chua.[^17-36]

**11.4.** The women raise the cry "ulu-ulu", on all sides sounds "Glory to Gauranga!";
khol, kartals and ramshinga resound — Narahari looks on, rejoicing at heart.

## 12. Narahari — "jaya jaya ārati gaura-kiśora…" (GPT1 p. 244, no. 21; BR)
*Gaura's arati: young Gaura shines on the throne like a golden mountain; Advaita, seized by prema, performs arati gazing at His Lord;
on the right Nityananda, on the left Gadadhara, someone holds a parasol over the Lord, Srivasa throws flowers, Narahari tirelessly
waves the chamara, Shuklambara anoints Him with sandal, Murari cries "Jaya!", Madhava, Vasu Ghosha, Purushottama, Vijaya, Mukunda
sing, instruments resound, Vakreshvara dances; the gods in the sky, Shiva and Brahma weep with love. Raga gauri. **Attribution:
probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli; signature "narahari-pahu".*[^17-37]

**12.1.** *(Refrain)* Glory, glory to the arati of Gaura-kishora!
He shines on the throne like a golden mountain — the swaying Thief of the hearts of the young women of the world.[^17-38]

**12.2.** Sri Advaita, seized by prema, performs arati, gazing at His own Lord;
on a golden tray studded with gems the lamps flash, destroying the darkness of sins.[^17-39]

**12.3.** On the right, a wondrous beauty: Nityananda, absorbed in rasa;
on the left, Gadadhara in a graceful pose; someone holds a shining new parasol.

**12.4.** The best Srinivasa throws handfuls of flowers, Narahari tirelessly waves the chamara;
the best Shuklambara anoints Him with sandal, Murari Gupta cries "Jaya!".[^17-40]

**12.5.** Madhava, Vasu Ghosha, Purushottama, Vijaya, Mukunda and other masters of the art
sing sweetly, with peerless distinctions of ragas, shrutis, murchhanas, gramas and the seven svaras.

**12.6.** Muraja, mridanga, changadaka, vina, nishana, bamboo flutes sound without end;
again and again bells ring, jhanjharis clash, cymbals thunder deeply.[^17-41]

**12.7.** Vakreshvara dances in great joy — with graceful, skilful movements of a dancer;
he calls out "dhikat, dhikat, dhidhi kat, tak thai thai" — in various ways.

**12.8.** In the bhava of the former lila, the rasika Gadadhara is beside himself; Shridhara, Gauridasa, Haridasa —
who can describe them all? — the devotees are beyond themselves, seeing the sweet smile on Gaura's face.[^17-42]

**12.9.** In the sky the gods with their retinues are immersed in bliss; the lord of the gods with effort keeps himself hidden;
the Lord of Parvati and the Four-faced thrill, streams of tears pour from their eyes.[^17-43]

**12.10.** Ananta-Shesha in the three worlds joyfully recounts His glory, the munis praise Him, uttering new names;
the poet Narahari's Lord — the ornament of Vraja, full of rasa, bestower of supreme bliss on Nadia.[^17-44]

[^17-27]: GPT1 — pp. 241–242, section on abhisheka and adhivasa (4.1), no. 14 ("suhai or mayura"); GPT2 — sec. 4.1, no. 14. The pada was
not in the catalogue (new row NG-240). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 893; ed. 1960, vv. 2662–2665): Narahari Chakravarti tells of the
abhisheka in Srivasa's house and cites first the pada of Vasu Ghosha PK 1536 (chapter 1, no. 2), then this one and the next. GPT2
index — Chakravarti (p. 152, no. 14). Not in PK, KGC, PS. B. The abhisheka in Srivasa's house — CB Madhya 9 (mahaprakasha).
[^17-28]: The Yamuna, a dark river, down a golden mountain — the dark curls down the Lord's golden back.
[^17-29]: Jagadisha (Pandita), Vasudeva (Ghosha or Datta), Narayana, Mukunda (Datta), Madhava (Ghosha) — kirtana singers of Navadvipa.
Shruti, jati, svara — terms of musical theory: microtones, classes of melodies, notes.
[^17-30]: Govinda (Ghosha) and Govindananda — kirtana singers; "dha-dha, dhik-dhik…" — rhythm syllables of the mridanga (khol).
[^17-31]: "The wives devoted to their husbands" (pativratā nārīgaṇa) — the women present at the abhisheka, as in the pada of Vasu Ghosha PK
1537 (chapter 1, no. 3); "jaya" and the cry "ulu" are auspicious acclamations.
[^17-32]: GPT1 — p. 242, no. 15 (dhanashi); GPT2 — sec. 4.1, no. 15 (in the catalogue NG-136, wrongly in the "nagari-bhava" section: it is
the abhisheka, sec. 4.1). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 894; ed. 1960, vv. 2666–2673), right after the preceding; then Ishana tells
Srinivasa about Srivasa's maidservant Duhkhi, whom the Lord named Sukhi (CB Madhya 9). Not in PK, KGC, PS. B.
[^17-33]: "Ulu-ulu" (ulululu) — the auspicious cry of Bengali women at rites.
[^17-34]: "Offers himself" (āpanā nichaye) — Bengali nichhani: the rite of waving something around the beloved and offering oneself for his
welfare; a sign of selfless love. Madana (Kama) swoons before the Lord's beauty.
[^17-35]: GPT1 — p. 242, no. 16 (suhai); GPT2 — sec. 4.1, no. 16 (in the catalogue NG-137, wrongly in the "nagari-bhava" section). Not in
BR, PK, KGC, PS. The GPT2 index assigns p. 153 to Chakravarti — probably because of pada no. 15 on that page (no. 10). C.
[^17-36]: Gorochana — a yellow pigment for tilaka; chua (cuyā) — a fragrant resin, perfume. Shachi herself adorns her Son after the
bathing — cf. CB Madhya 9.
[^17-37]: GPT1 — p. 244, no. 21 (gauri); GPT2 — sec. 4.1, no. 21 (in the catalogue PA-005, wrongly as a pada of Paramananda; excluded in
chapter 11). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 846–847; ed. 1960, vv. 2018–2027): Ishana shows Srinivasa the place in Navadvipa where
Gadadhara adorned the Lord with flowers and the associates performed arati to Him. GPT2 index — Chakravarti. Not in PK, KGC, PS. B.
[^17-38]: "Thief of the hearts of the young women of the world" — an epithet of Krishna applied to Gaura: the same motif as in no. 5 (note
15).
[^17-39]: "His own Lord" (nija nātha) — Advaita worships Gaura as the Lord whom He called down by His prayers (CC Adi 3).
[^17-40]: Srinivasa — Srivasa Pandita; Narahari with the chamara — Narahari Sarakara, the Lord's associate already in Navadvipa (cf. PK 2128, chapter 4, no. 4);
Shuklambara — Shuklambara Brahmachari; Murari Gupta.
[^17-41]: Muraja, mridanga, changadaka — drums; nishana — kettledrum or horn; jhanjhari — small cymbals.
[^17-42]: "In the bhava of the former lila" (pūrava rase) — Gadadhara, in Krishna-lila Radha (Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika 147–153). Shridhara —
the seller of plantain leaves (CB Madhya 9); Gauridasa — Gauridasa Pandita; Haridasa — Haridasa Thakura.
[^17-43]: The lord of the gods (surapati) — Indra; the Lord of Parvati — Shiva; the Four-faced — Brahma. "With effort keeps himself hidden" (yatane karata
parihāra) — the gods are present invisibly.
[^17-44]: "The poet Narahari's Lord" (narahari-pahu, lit. "Narahari-Lord") — the Lord whom Narahari serves (cf. "nayanānanda-pahu" — "the Lord of
Nayanananda", chapter 10): Chakravarti's usual form of signature. "Bestower of supreme bliss on Nadia" (nadīyāpura-paramānanda-kārī) — in
the catalogue the word "paramānanda" was taken for the signature of the poet Paramananda.

## 13. Narahari — "nācata gaura purava-rase bhora…" (GPT1 p. 261, no. 44; BR)
*Kirtana in Navadvipa: Gaura dances, absorbed in the rasa of the former lila; His smile dispels the darkness of sin, the earth trembles
at His step; He roars like a lion, and the Kali age flees in fear; the associates sing, khol and kartals resound, the whole world is
intoxicated. Raga somaraga. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli. With this pada begins
the large cycle "Gaura's dance" of the GPT (sec. 4.2), almost all of which is known also from the BR.*[^17-45]

**13.1.** *(Refrain)* Gaura dances, absorbed in the rasa of the former lila;
His body flashes, crushing the pride of a golden mountain — it steals the heart even of bodiless Kama.[^17-46]

**13.2.** Softly He smiles — the beauty of His moon-face destroys the dense darkness of sin;
keeping the rhythm, His light lotus feet step — and the earth trembles, unable to bear their weight.

**13.3.** His two eyes are the young dawn, swaying; He is adorned with constant, abundant thrills;
again and again He roars with a might surpassing a lion's — and the mighty Kali age flees in great fear.[^17-47]

**13.4.** The song of the dear associates pierces the sky, khol and graceful kartals play;
the whole world is intoxicated, says Narahari — His pure, boundless fame has filled the universe.

## 14. Narahari — "nṛtyata gauracandra janarañjana…" (GPT1 p. 262, no. 45; BR)
*The dance of Gaura and Nityananda: both are golden mountains, Their glance steals Kama's pride, Their speech flows with nectar; the
associates sing, the mardala sounds, the gods on the paths of the sky shower flowers, the world is full of the cry "Jaya!". Raga
deshapala. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli.*[^17-48]

**14.1.** Gaurachandra, the delight of the people, and Nityananda, the destroyer of the fear of calamity, dance: Their lotus eyes surpass
ever-new khanjana birds, Their glance steals Kama's pride; both bodies flash — golden mountains; in the dance Their feet strike the
earth; Their faces, mingled with smiles, shine like moons; when They speak, it is as if nectar were flowing.[^17-49]

**14.2.** Peerless is this beauty — it cannot be told; surrounding Them, the associates sing Their virtues; sweetly, sweetly, softly the
mardala plays: "dha-dha, dhigi-dhigi, dhikat, dhilanga"; the gods with their retinues on the paths of the sky again and again shower
choice flowers; the cry "Jaya, jaya, jaya" fills the world — what can Narahari say of the waves of prema?

## 15. Narahari — "āju ki ānanda saṅkīrtane…" (GPT1 p. 262, no. 46; BR)
*The sankirtana of Gaura and Nityananda: all are beside themselves with prema, from everyone's eyes rivers of tears flow, some fall on
one another, others roar, tremble, embrace one another and cannot let go, take the dust of one another's feet and roll on the ground;
Lord and servants are all alike in this. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); simple
Bengali tripadi.*[^17-50]

**15.1.** *(Refrain)* What bliss today in the sankirtana!
Gaura and Nityananda dance — the root of supreme bliss — together with Their dear associates.

**15.2.** Dancing, they cry: "Well done, well done!"; khol and kartals resound — all are beside themselves with prema;
from everyone's eyes pour streams like the current of a river; some fall upon one another.

**15.3.** Someone, thrilling, roars and shouts aloud; someone trembles, unable to stand steady;
someone, looking at another, opens his arms, embraces him — and cannot let him go.

**15.4.** Someone seizes another's feet and puts the dust of his feet on his head; someone, falling to the ground, rolls in the dust;
Lord and servants are in one state: seeing this, Narahari in great bliss sings the virtues of the Lord.[^17-51]

## 16. Narahari — "nācata gaurāṅga-cām̐da vibhora bhāvete…" (GPT1 p. 262, no. 47)
*Gauranga dances, seized by bhava; in the same bhava, on His left, Gadadhara dances; Nitai follows behind so that His golden body may
not fall to the ground; the Lord embraces the fallen. Raga pathamanjari. **Attribution: not established** — the pada is not in the BR
(the GPT2 index, however, assigns its page to Chakravarti); simple Bengali payar.*[^17-52]

**16.1.** Gaurangachand dances, seized by bhava;
in the same bhava on His left dances Gadadhara.

**16.2.** Lest His body of pure gold should fall to the ground,
Nitaichand keeps following close behind Him.[^17-53]

**16.3.** My Gauranga dances, swaying, rocking;
khol and kartals sound: "ta-dhiya, ta-dhiya".

**16.4.** He seizes and embraces the fallen who have gone astray —
only sinful Narahari is not immersed in this rasa.

## 17. Narahari — "nācata gauracandra guṇadhāma…" (GPT1 p. 263, no. 49; BR)
*Gaura's dance: the radiance of His body outshines a golden mountain and lightning; His smile steals composure, earrings tremble, curls
are decked with flowers, a garland on His chest, His arms in new play, His feet keeping the rhythm; the associates sing, khol and khamak
resound. Raga bangala. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli.*[^17-54]

**17.1.** *(Refrain)* Gaurachandra dances, the abode of virtues;
the radiance of His body flashes, charming the heart — it casts far away both golden Meru and garlands of lightning.

**17.2.** His lovely face crushes Madana's pride; His sweet smile steals the composure of young wives;
at His ears tremble jewelled earrings surpassing the young dawn; both His eyes sway — how beautiful they are![^17-55]

**17.3.** His smooth curling locks are decked with flowers; on His restless, lovely chest — a garland;
in the peerless, ever-new play of His arms His feet keep a graceful rhythm.

**17.4.** The Lord moves, beside Him shine the dear associates, singing sweet ragas, intoxicated with rasa;
the whole world rejoices, says Narahari; khol and khamak sound in every manner.

## 18. Narahari — "nācata gauracandra naṭabhūpa…" (GPT1 p. 263, no. 50; BR)
*The dance of Gaura, king of dancers: a form crushing the pride of a hundred thousand Kamas; He roars in bhava, spreads His arms,
smiles, His face is the autumn moon; the devotees sing, outdoing the kinnaras, the ocean of prema has flooded the earth — only
Narahari it does not touch. Raga belavali. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli.*[^17-56]

**18.1.** *(Refrain)* Gaurachandra dances, the king of dancers:
a form crushing the pride of a hundred thousand Kamas — the delight of the people of all the worlds.

**18.2.** Ceaselessly seized by peerless bhava, He roars — wondrously, beautifully;
He sets His auspicious feet on the earth, moves with both arms outspread.

**18.3.** Sweetly He smiles, His lips soft and lovely, the play of His face surpasses the autumn moon;
His eyes, petals of a red lotus, sway: who can tell how much rasa He reveals?

**18.4.** Sweetly the devotees sing ever-new songs, crushing the pride of the host of kinnaras;
the ocean of prema has surged and flooded the earth — only foolish Narahari it has not touched.[^17-57]

## 19. Narahari — "nācata dvija-kula-candra gaurahari…" (GPT1 p. 264, no. 52; BR)
*The dance of Gaurahari, moon of the brahmana line: auspicious feet, absorption in the bhava of the former lila, body thrilling, curls
like a cloud on a golden mountain, a garland of malati, His face a snare of Kama; the associates sing, the world sinks in an ocean of
happiness. Raga nata. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli.*[^17-58]

**19.1.** *(Refrain)* Gaurahari dances, the moon of the twice-born line;
His auspicious, fear-removing feet He sets on the earth, assuming wondrous poses.

**19.2.** Ceaselessly seized by the bhava of the former lila, His body is covered with thrills, as if with kadamba flowers;
His smooth, glossy curling locks — like a cloud on the peak of a golden mountain.[^17-59]

**19.3.** A garland of malati flowers, wondrously arrayed, sways, hanging on His restless, lovely chest;
His face is Kama's snare, the delight of the heart; His eyes sway — a pair of red lotuses.

**19.4.** Seeing the peerless dance, the dear associates sing sweetly, showering rasa;
the whole world sinks in an ocean of happiness — only foolish Narahari stays far off, untouched.

## 20. Narahari — "nācata gaura nikhila-naṭa-paṇḍita…" (GPT1 p. 264, no. 53; BR)
*The dance of Gaura, most skilled of dancers: the radiance of His body, outshining the sun, lights up all directions; He roars like a
lion, and the elephant Kali trembles; leaps and stamping feet shake the earth; the associates sing, the sound of the khol reaches the
sky; the wicked, trembling, seek refuge at His feet. Raga ghantarava. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR
(12th wave); Vrajabuli.*[^17-60]

**20.1.** Gaura dances, the most skilled of all dancers; with peerless movements He takes away Madana's pride;
crushing the pride of the blazing sun, with the radiance of His body He lights up all the quarters.

**20.2.** Intoxicated, He roars beyond compare, stronger than a lion — hearing it, the mighty elephant Kali trembles;
again and again leaps, a graceful, restless gait — at the strokes of His feet the earth shakes.[^17-61]

**20.3.** The associates crush the pride of the kinnaras, singing in jubilation — a nectarean sound flows;
many khols and khamaks play, the sound touches the sky — who can keep composure?

**20.4.** Before His peerless might the wicked tremble, seek refuge, fall at His feet;
the fame of the poet Narahari's Lord fills the world: ceaselessly He gives away the highest, rarest treasure.[^17-62]

## 21. Narahari — "suradhunī-tīra parama niramala thala…" (GPT1 p. 265, no. 54; BR)
*Gaura's dance on the bank of the Suradhuni: at a pure place by the river the generous devotees rejoice, sing nectarean songs, play
instruments; Gaura-kishora dances anointed with sandal, His face outshines autumn moons, His necklace flashes, His anklets tinkle.
Raga biragupta. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli.*[^17-63]

**21.1.** The bank of the Suradhuni is a most pure place; there all the generous devotees rejoice,
sing many nectarean songs, play instruments of every kind.

**21.2.** *(Refrain)* Gaura-kishora dances, the jewel of virtues;
His lovely body is anointed with sandal — a wondrous form, stealing the hearts of women.[^17-64]

**21.3.** His eyes, petals of a pure lotus, sway; the play of His brows, the new charm of His locks;
His face shames hosts of autumn moons, His smile crushes the pride of millions of Madanas.

**21.4.** On His restless, lovely, broad chest flashes a jewelled necklace, outshining lightning;
when the poet Narahari's Lord keeps the rhythm with His feet — how sweetly the anklets tinkle!

## 22. Narahari — "āju ki ānanda nadīyā-nagare…" (GPT1 p. 265, no. 55; BR)
*After the deliverance of Jagai and Madhai: the men and women of Nadia run to see the brothers and talk among themselves: they shine
like the sun — where has their sinful body gone? The brothers, in bhava, weep, tremble, roll in the dust, cannot take their eyes off
Gora's face, bathe Nitai's feet with tears, take the dust of the feet of Advaita, Gadadhara, Srivasa, and, holding straw between
their teeth, with arms raised, beg the Lord and His associates for mercy. Raga gurjari. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the
pada is in the BR (12th wave, the account of Jagai and Madhai).*[^17-65]

**22.1.** What bliss today in the town of Nadia! To see Jagai and Madhai, women and men run from every side and talk with one
another.
Someone says, standing apart: "Look, look at the two of them! Now they shine like the sun — where has that sinful body gone?"

**22.2.** Someone says: "Ah, ah! Seized by bhava, they keep sitting down, bursting into tears — streams rush from their eyes, they
cannot check them, they are beside themselves."
Someone says: "Look, an unheard-of thing: their bodies thrill and constantly tremble; grey with dust, they fall to the ground and
roll, remembering nothing."[^17-66]

**22.3.** Someone says: "How they gaze at Gora's moon-face — as though floating in some great happiness! Drunk with the nectar of His
smile, they fall and roll at His feet."
Someone says: "Look, gazing at Nitaichand, how bitterly they repent in their hearts: touching His two feet, they bathe them —
perform abhisheka — with their tears."[^17-67]

**22.4.** Others say: "Look, they sit beside the ascetic Advaita, beside Gadadhara, Srivasa and the others, they wander about, full of
peerless joy, and take the dust of everyone's feet."
Others: "There the two, with broken hearts, stand aside with straw between their teeth and, raising their arms, say to the poet
Narahari's Lord and His associates: 'Have mercy!'"[^17-68]

## 23. Narahari — "nācata gaura naṭana-paṇḍita-vara…" (GPT1 pp. 265–266, no. 56; BR)
*The dance of Gaura, best of skilled dancers: His body outshines kunkuma and lightning, His smile pours nectar, His glance crushes the
pride of Madanas; raising His arms He cries "Hari, Hari!"; the associates sing, instruments resound; He gives the world the treasure of
prema — only Narahari is left out. Raga meghamallara. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave);
Vrajabuli.*[^17-69]

**23.1.** *(Refrain)* Gaura dances, the best of skilled dancers;
His body, shaming kunkuma and garlands of lightning, is adorned with peerless, abundant thrills.

**23.2.** Red lips, the tender moon-face shining, teeth like kunda flowers, a light smile pouring nectar;
His lotus eyes, the delight of the people, are full of rasa; His glance crushes the pride of hundreds of Madanas.

**23.3.** Raising His arms, which put to shame golden lotus stalks, He cries "Hari, Hari!" — His heart overflowing;
His auspicious, tender, graceful feet He sets on the earth in manifold movements.

**23.4.** Small cymbals, khamaks, many khols sound; the associates sing sweetly, sweetly;
He gives away throughout the world the treasure, the jewel of prema — only foolish, sinful Narahari is left out.

## 24. Narahari — "vali-kali-matta-mataṅgaja-maradana…" (GPT1 p. 266, no. 57; BR)
*The lion Gaura, crusher of the mad elephant Kali, dances in Nadia; the world is full of the cry "Jaya!", people run from all sides, the
associates sing, drums thunder, the earth trembles; giving prema, the Lord embraces the sinners. Raga devakiri. **Attribution:
probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli.*[^17-70]

**24.1.** The crusher of the mighty mad elephant Kali, the lion Gaura, dances in Nadia;
the cry "Jaya, jaya!" fills the whole world, from everywhere people gather and come running.

**24.2.** The dear associates sing mightily and beautifully — waves of rhythms beyond even the kinnaras;
muraja and mridanga thunder: "drimiki drimi drimi, drimikat, dhikat, dhilanga".[^17-71]

**24.3.** The earth trembles as He sets down His lotus feet; peerless are the swaying movements of His body;
His eyes surpass the young dawn in beauty; at His lovely glance many a Kama starts.

**24.4.** The sweetness of His face shames hosts of moons; He smiles gently, pouring out nectar;
giving prema, the poet Narahari's Lord, spreading His arms, embraces the sinners.

## 25. Narahari — "nācata gaura naṭana-janarañjana…" (GPT1 p. 266, no. 58; BR)
*Gaura's dance: hearing of the former love, He thrills and trembles; His eyes are full of tears, like pearls; seeing Gadadhara, He
embraces him again and speaks of the secret of His heart, unable to restrain Himself; the ocean of prema surges, the sinners float in
happiness — only Narahari it does not touch. Raga bhupali. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave);
Vrajabuli.*[^17-72]

**25.1.** Gaura dances, delighting the people by His dance; His body crushes the pride of all the Madanas;
He thrills, gracefully trembling, again and again beside Himself, hearing the story of the former love.[^17-73]

**25.2.** His eyes, petals of a red lotus, are brimming with tears; the moisture flashes like strings of pearls;
when He laughs, His teeth flash like lightning — peerless are His soft, sweet lips.

**25.3.** Spreading His lovely long arms, which take away the pride of an elephant's trunk,
He sees Gadadhara, embraces him again, speaks of what lies in His heart — and cannot restrain Himself.[^17-74]

**25.4.** The peerless ocean of prema surges, raising mighty, playful waves;
the sinful, the fallen, the afflicted float in happiness — only sinful Narahari it does not touch.

## 26. Narahari — "nācata gaura parama-sukha-sadanā…" (GPT1 pp. 266–267, no. 59; BR)
*The dance of Gaura, abode of supreme happiness: His thrilling body crushes Madana's pride, His glance is full of compassion, His
smile steals the heart, His gait is like a royal elephant's; with faltering voice He cries "Hari, Hari!", gives away the treasure of
prema, fulfilling the desires of all — only the poet is left out. Raga natanarayana. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada
is in the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli.*[^17-75]

**26.1.** *(Refrain)* Gaura dances, the abode of supreme happiness;
shining with constant, abundant thrills, His graceful body torments Madana, crushing his pride.

**26.2.** His eyes, petals of a pure lotus, sway; His glance, full of compassion, is lovely with the beauty of dawn;
His face, spurning the autumn moon, shines with a smile; His gleaming teeth instantly steal the heart.

**26.3.** His gait, ever new, takes away the pride of a royal elephant; as He steps, the earth rejoices;
His heart overflowing, His voice faltering, He ceaselessly cries "Hari, Hari!" — a peerless wealth of bhava has risen in Him.

**26.4.** Intoxicated, giving away the peerless treasure, He has removed misfortunes; His fame has filled this world;
He has fulfilled the desires of all — only Narahari is left out: vain is his birth, shame on his life![^17-76]

## 27. Narahari — "nācata śacī-tanaya gaura…" (GPT1 p. 267, no. 60; BR)
*The dance of Gaura, the son of Shachi: His sweetness charms the mind, His body thrills, His smile pours nectar, His anklets ring in
rhythm, Kama is ashamed before His movements; the world sings His virtues and sinks in happiness — only Narahari burns in the forest
fire of worldly existence. Raga nata. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli.*[^17-77]

**27.1.** Gaura, the son of Shachi, dances — His sweetness charms the mind;
on His body, which crushes a golden mountain, rows of thrills are shining.

**27.2.** His moon-face gleams, pouring nectar in a gentle smile;
with the corners of His restless eyes He reveals so much rasa!

**27.3.** With His feet He keeps the rhythm, the anklets ring out resoundingly;
seeing His many new movements, Kama dies of shame.

**27.4.** The people of the world sing His virtues, sinking in a stream of happiness;
only deprived, lowly Narahari burns in the forest fire of worldly existence.[^17-78]

[^17-73]: "The story of the former love" (pūruva-pīriti-parasaṅga) — the account of the love of Radha and Krishna in Vraja: hearing it, the
Lord enters into bhava.
[^17-74]: Gadadhara is Radha in Krishna-lila (note 20). The Lord's feelings for Gadadhara are the prema of Krishna-lila, not a worldly
attachment.

## 28. Narahari — "āju śaṅkara-carita śuni…" (GPT1 pp. 283–284, no. 22; BR)
*The Lord in the mood of Shiva: hearing a song of Shankara's deeds, the son of Shachi became Shankara — a radiance brighter than the
silver mountain, a body smeared with ashes, a horn in His hand, the damaru sounding, three eyes, serpents for ornaments and clothes,
matted locks on His head. Raga malavashri. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave, the account of the
singer of Shiva); Vrajabuli.*[^17-79]

**28.1.** Today, hearing of Shankara's deeds, the son of Shachi became Shankara;
His radiance sways, surpassing the silver mountain — He has stolen the composure of the world.[^17-80]

**28.2.** His body, adorned with ashes, is graceful — it takes away Ananga's pride;
in His lovely hand He holds a horn and blows it; charmingly the damaru sounds.

**28.3.** Restless and lovely are the corners of His three eyes, His moon-face shines;
pure and tender are His cheeks, on His brow the eyebrows curve.

**28.4.** Huge serpents are His ornaments and garments, the hide shines brightly;
on His head lovely, tangled, heavy matted locks — seeing this, Narahari is beside himself.[^17-81]

## 29. Narahari Dasa — "ki bhāve gaurāṅga mora bhāvita thāke…" (GPT1 p. 292, no. 52)
*The Lord in the mood of Krishna: seized by bhava, He calls "Radha!", the Ganga reminds Him of the Yamuna, a flower garden — of
Vrindavana; with His companions He plays, standing in the threefold bend and asking for the flute; taking Gadadhara for Radha, He
says something unknown to him and does not take His eyes off his face; Gadadhara, understanding the bhava, stands at His left. Raga
mallara. **Attribution: probably Sarakara** — the GPT2 index assigns the page to Sarakara; not in the BR; simple Bengali payar; the
content is close to Sarakara's pada PK 2122.*[^17-82]

**29.1.** By what bhava is my Gauranga seized?
Again and again, in bhava, He calls: "Radha!"

**29.2.** Seeing the Bhagirathi, He remembers the Yamuna;
a flowering garden He takes in His heart for Vrindavana.[^17-83]

**29.3.** With His companions the Lord begins so many games;
standing in the threefold bend, He says: "The flute, the flute!"[^17-84]

**29.4.** Taking Gadadhara for Radha, who knows what He says to him;
without blinking He gazes at the Pandita's face.

**29.5.** Understanding the bhava, Gadadhara stands at His left;
this rasa Narahari Dasa does not comprehend.[^17-85]

[^17-79]: GPT1 — pp. 283–284, section on bhavavesha (4.3), no. 22 (malavashri); GPT2 — sec. 4.3, no. 22 (catalogue: NG-153). BR — 12th
wave (ed. 1912, p. 834; ed. 1960, vv. 1841–1844): Ishana tells Srinivasa that here a singer of Shiva sang and danced, playing the
damaru, and the Lord, in the mood of Maheshvara, crying "I am Mahesha!", climbed onto his shoulders (a retelling of CB Madhya 8). GPT2
index — Chakravarti. Not in PK, KGC, PS. B. Before it in the GPT (no. 21) stands a pada signed Narahari about the Lord in the mood of
Balarama (for the next chapter).
[^17-80]: The mood of Shiva is one of the moods the Lord displayed in Navadvipa (CB Madhya 8; cf. the moods of Varaha, Nrisimha, Balarama):
the Lord is the source of all His manifestations, and Shiva is His partial manifestation and the greatest of Vaishnavas (Bhag.
12.13.16; Brahma-samhita 5.45). This is not God turning into a demigod: hearing of His devotee, the Lord takes on his form and mood.
The silver mountain — Kailasa.
[^17-81]: Shiva's attributes: ashes, the horn (shringa) and the small drum damaru, the third eye, serpents, a hide (of tiger or elephant),
matted hair (jata).
[^17-82]: GPT1 — p. 292, no. 52 (mallara; the recognition is incomplete, text from GPT1 and GPT2); GPT2 — sec. 4.3, no. 52. The pada was
not in the catalogue (new row NG-247). Not in BR, PK, KGC, PS. The GPT2 index assigns pp. 187–188 to Sarakara (here stand no. 51 = PK
853, a pada of Sarakara, and this one). The content repeats the motifs of Sarakara's pada PK 2122 (chapter 3, no. 1; Majumdar places
it in the Navadvipa lila): the Ganga seems the Yamuna, a garden Vrindavana, the Lord is in the mood of Krishna with Gadadhara as Radha. C.
[^17-83]: Bhagirathi — the Ganga. Cf. Rupa Gosvami, Chaitanyashtaka (Stava-mala) 1.6 and CC Antya 14–15 — in Puri the sea seems to the Lord
the Yamuna, and the groves Vrindavana.
[^17-84]: The threefold bend (tribhaṅga) — Krishna's pose with the flute. Here the Lord is in the mood of Krishna, not of Radha.
[^17-85]: Gadadhara is Radha in Krishna-lila (note 20): understanding the Lord's bhava, he stands at the left, where Radha stands beside
Krishna. This is the prema of Vraja, not a worldly feeling. "Does not comprehend" — the poet's humility.

# Chapter 18. Appendix. Padas signed "Narahari" from the Gaura-pada-tarangini — II: kirtana and dance (conclusion), bhavavesha, the festivals of the year, prarthanas

*Continuation of the appendix (the introductory note on the two Naraharis, on the arguments for attribution and on the marks in the
headings is in ch. 17). Chapter 18: the end of the cycle of kirtana and dance in Navadvipa (GPT, section 4.2), two padas on the
Lord's bhavas (the bhava of Balarama; the Lord in the bhava of Radha waiting for Krishna), the festivals of the year — the "twelve-month
lila" (GPT, section 5.1: the swing-jhulana, Janmashtami and Nanda-utsava, Radhashtami, the remembrance of the rasa-lila, spring and
Holi) and two prarthanas. Before translation the "Narahari" signatures in these sections were checked throughout in GPT1 (tesseract
recognition): the catalogue had missed several more padas. The base text is GPT1 (doubtful places from the scan), collated with GPT2 and
with the Bhakti-ratnakara (eds. 1912 and 1960; almost all padas of the chapter are in its 12th wave); PK, KGC, PS and the
Gita-chandrodaya have been checked. Padas signed "Ghanashyama" (the same Narahari Chakravarti) are not included in the appendix. The
notes of the GPT editors are not reproduced.*

## 1. Narahari — "kivā khola karatāla vāje…" (GPT1 p. 267, no. 61; BR)
*Kirtana: the khol and karatalas sound, the associates stand around; they sing the sweet lila at which wood and stone melt; Gaura
dances, and no one knows by what bhava He is seized; His body thrills, streams of tears flow from His eyes; He embraces the fallen and
gives the treasure of prema to everyone — only the poet is left out. Raga nata. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is
in the BR (12th wave); short payar with Vrajabuli forms.*[^18-1]

**1.1.** How the khol and karatalas resound!
All around stand the adorned associates.

**1.2.** Today they sing the sweet lila —
hearing it, wood and stone melt.

**1.3.** *(Refrain)* Joyfully the beautiful Gora dances —
who knows by what bhava He is seized?

**1.4.** His body is covered with fresh thrills —
as if a golden jackfruit were shining.[^18-2]

**1.5.** Like the current of the celestial river,
streams flow from both His eyes.[^18-3]

**1.6.** Again and again raising both arms,
He thunders: "Hari, Hari!"

**1.7.** Seeing the most fallen and sinful,
again and again He clasps them in His embrace.

**1.8.** To each and every one He gives the treasure of prema,
passing over only one wretched Narahari.[^18-4]

[^18-1]: GPT1 — p. 267, no. 61 (nata); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 61 (catalogue: NG-249). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 903; ed. 1960,
vv. 2783–2790): Ishana, showing Srinivasa Navadvipa, quotes it at the house of Sanjaya, "dear to the Lord", where Vishvambhara
danced, right after the pada "nācata śacītanaya gaura" (chapter 17, no. 27). The GPT2 index assigns the page to Chakravarti. Not in
PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. The Lord's dancing in kirtana in Navadvipa — CB Madhya 8, 23; CC Adi 17.
[^18-2]: Thrills (pulaka) are one of the sattvika-bhavas, signs of prema: the hairs stand up like the spikes on the rind of a jackfruit
(panasa).
[^18-3]: "The celestial river" (surasarit) is the Ganga.
[^18-4]: Self-reproach is the usual ending of the padas of this cycle (cf. chapter 17, nos. 13–27): the poet regards himself as the only
one passed over by the mercy given to all.

## 2. Narahari — "bhuvanamohana gorācām̐da…" (GPT1 p. 268, no. 63; BR)
*Dancing in prema: Gorachand, enchanter of the world, dances weeping, cries "Hari!", embraces the fallen, floods everyone with His
rasa, throws Himself on the ground and rolls in the dust; seeing this, all living beings weep. Raga varadi or dhanashi. **Attribution:
probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave), though its language is a simple Bengali payar.*[^18-5]

**2.1.** Gorachand, the enchanter of the world —
a net that snares the hearts of all people.[^18-6]

**2.2.** The Lord dances, seized by prema;
His reddened eyes swim in tears.

**2.3.** Raising His arms, He cries: "Hari, Hari!" —
and, seizing the fallen, clasps them to His breast.

**2.4.** With His own rasa He floods everyone;
all around His associates sing.

**2.5.** Flinging His most tender body to the ground,
He falls and rolls in the dust.

**2.6.** Seeing this, all living beings weep;
Narahari's heart finds no rest.

[^18-5]: GPT1 — p. 268, no. 63 (varadi or dhanashi); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 63 (catalogue: NG-149). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 904; ed.
