1960, vv. 2795–2800), at the same place, the house of Sanjaya; after the pada — "under this tree the Lord stayed a while and went on
by the road to the Ganga". Not in PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^18-6]: Marginal variants of GPT1: "purifier of the world" instead of "enchanter of the world", "of all living beings" instead of "of
all people". These are the readings of the second occurrence of the same pada in the BR: Narahari Chakravarti quotes it twice — at the
house of Sanjaya (vv. 2795–2800) and at the house of Srivasa (ed. 1960, v. 3397 ff., "bhuvanapāvana gorācām̐da | akhila jīvera mana-phām̐da").

## 3. Narahari — "nācata gaurakiśora. suradhunītīre ujora…" (GPT1 p. 268, no. 65; BR)
*Dancing on the bank of the Suradhuni: young Gaura with hundreds of associates, making no distinction between His own and others, gives
away the treasure of prema, weeps in a peerless bhava and, speaking in a faltering voice, takes Gadadhara by the hand. Raga dhanashi.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); short payar with Vrajabuli forms.*[^18-7]

**3.1.** Young Gaura dances,
illumining the bank of the Suradhuni.

**3.2.** With Him are hundreds of associates;
in the kirtana His movements are peerless.[^18-8]

**3.3.** Making no distinction between His own and others,
He gives away the treasure of prema.

**3.4.** Immersed in a peerless bhava,
He sheds tears from His reddened eyes.

**3.5.** Uttering so many words in a faltering voice,
He takes Gadadhara by the hand.[^18-9]

**3.6.** Again and again His body trembles —
what can Narahari grasp of this play?

[^18-7]: GPT1 — p. 268, no. 65 (dhanashi); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 65 (catalogue: NG-250). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 912; ed. 1960,
vv. 2889–2894): Ishana shows the bank of the Ganga where the Lord danced with His associates and quotes several padas in a row
(including the next one, no. 4); after them — "having spread the good fortune of the Ganga, the Lord went home this way with His
associates". Not in PK, KGC, PS. The Gita-chandrodaya (ed. 1948, no. 30) has a pada with the same opening ("heranu gaurakiśora |
suradhanītīre ujora"), but it is a different song — signed by Kavishekhara Raya and with a different text after the first couplet; the
common opening is probably a current formula. B.
[^18-8]: The BR reads: "in the kirtana — peerless play" (raṅga instead of aṅga).
[^18-9]: Gadadhara Pandita is Radha in Krishna-lila (cf. chapter 17, note 20): in the dance the Lord turns to him in the bhava of
Krishna-lila. This is the prema of Vraja, not worldly attachment.

## 4. Narahari Dasa — "gaura suradhunītīre nācata…" (GPT1 p. 268, no. 66; BR)
*Dancing on the bank of the Suradhuni: Gaura's body takes away the pride of a golden mountain, His locks are adorned with flowers, at the
sight of His arms and breast Kama loses his peace; He walks with the gait of a king of elephants, from His lotus eyes flow as it were
two Gangas, the earth rejoices at the rhythm of His feet. Raga gauri. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR
(12th wave); Vrajabuli with chains of assonance.*[^18-10]

**4.1.** Gaura dances on the bank of the Suradhuni with His skilful associates;
His body, full of supreme sweetness, takes away the pride of a golden mountain.

**4.2.** His peerless locks are adorned with ketaki, kunda jasmine and bright flowers;
seeing the curve of His arms and His broad chest, Ananga loses his peace.[^18-11]

**4.3.** Seized by bhava, He steps, putting to shame the king of elephants, and thunders unceasingly;
tears roll from His lotus eyes — as if two Gangas had appeared.

**4.4.** When His unsteady feet keep the rhythm, the earth rejoices beyond measure;
Narahari Dasa cries: "Glory, glory!" — what can be said of this play?

[^18-10]: GPT1 — p. 268, no. 66 (gauri, gauraṛī); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 66 (catalogue: NG-251). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 912; ed. 1960,
vv. 2895–2898), right after the preceding pada, at the Ganga. The GPT1 recognition of this pada is faulty; the readings are restored
from GPT2 and the BR (see the full version of the book). Not in PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^18-11]: Ananga ("the Bodiless") is Kama, the god of love: the Lord's beauty surpasses Kama's (a usual image of the gaura-padas). Ketaki
and kunda are flowers.

## 5. Narahari Dasa — "vali-kalidamana śamanabhayabhañjana…" (GPT1 p. 269, no. 67; BR)
*The son of Shachi dancing in the midst of the kirtana: subduer of Kali and of the fear of death, skilful giver of prema, more
beautiful than a golden mountain; at the rhythm of His feet the earth sways, He spreads His arms, smiles, and seeing Gadadhara's face
loses His composure; His eyes reveal the former play of Vraja. Raga belavali. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in
the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli.*[^18-12]

**5.1.** Subduer of mighty Kali, dispeller of the fear of Yama, giver of joy to the people of all the worlds,
skilled in giving away the rare treasure of prema, taking away the pride of all the wish-fulfilling trees —[^18-13]

**5.2.** *(Refrain)* the son of Shachi dances in the midst of the kirtana;
His body, lovelier than a golden mountain, shines like a new king Manmatha.

**5.3.** At the rhythm of His feet the earth sways; gracefully bending, He spreads His arms;
smiling gently, His lips tremble — and seeing Gadadhara's face, He loses His composure.

**5.4.** His lotus eyes sway, turning again and again, revealing the peerless former play;
the skilful associates rejoice — only Narahari Dasa is deprived of this rasa.[^18-14]

[^18-12]: GPT1 — p. 269, no. 67 (belavali); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 67 (catalogue: NG-150). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 921; ed. 1960,
vv. 3018–3021): "here Gaurachandra, with joy in His heart, danced in sankirtana in a wondrous bhava". Not in PK, KGC, PS or the
Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^18-13]: "Subduer of mighty Kali" — the Lord who conquers the age of Kali by sankirtana; "the fear of Yama" — the fear of death and its
consequences. The wish-fulfilling tree (sura-taru, kalpa-vriksha) grants only what is asked for, but the Lord gives prema beyond asking.
[^18-14]: "The former play" (pūrava raṅga) is Krishna's lila in Vraja, which the Lord remembers in the dance. Gadadhara is Radha in
Krishna-lila (note 9).

## 6. Narahari — "āju gorā nagarakīrtane…" (GPT1 p. 269, no. 68; BR)
*The night-time city kirtana: adorned Gora walks with His associates, dances, pours down a rain of prema; gods disguised as men shower
flowers, the townspeople run and sing, fools hearing the lion's roar expect disaster; hundreds of thousands of lamps are burning, the
whole world is intoxicated. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave, the account of the
night kirtana); Bengali payar.*[^18-15]

**6.1.** Today Gora is in the city kirtana:
having dressed Himself, He goes with His dear associates.

**6.2.** Beautifully shines the attire on His body;
He dances in every manner, charming the hearts of the world.

**6.3.** Ceaselessly He pours down a rain of prema;
in the midst of Nadia flows a river of bliss.

**6.4.** The gods, mingling with men,
shower flowers with joy in their hearts.[^18-16]

**6.5.** All the townspeople run;
in the depths of their hearts they sing the virtues of Gorachand.

**6.6.** Fools, hearing the lion's roar,
grow sullen and expect disaster.[^18-17]

**6.7.** Hundreds of thousands of lamps are burning —
what comparison is there? Earth and sky are lit up.

**6.8.** What does Narahari know how to tell?
The world is intoxicated — no one can keep his composure.

[^18-15]: GPT1 — p. 269, no. 68 (kamoda); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 68 (catalogue: NG-151). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 927; ed. 1960,
vv. 3104–3111): Ishana tells of the night kirtana, when the Lord went through the streets of Navadvipa by the light of hundreds of
thousands of lamps, while "the foolish pashandis took it for a calamity" (v. 3103). Not in PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. The
night procession with kirtana through Navadvipa (to the Kazi's house) — CB Madhya 23; CC Adi 17.
[^18-16]: According to the CB (Madhya 23), gods who had taken human form were also in the procession.
[^18-17]: "The lion's roar" (siṃhanāda) is the loud singing of Hari's names. "Fools" are the opponents of kirtana (pashandis), who expected
the noise to bring down the ruler's wrath.

## 7. Narahari — "śacīra dulāla gorā nāce…" (GPT1 pp. 269–270, no. 69; BR)
*The dance of the son of Shachi: Gora offers to anyone the treasure unattainable for the gods; seeing the fallen, He cannot restrain
Himself, waves of bhava rise in Him; His face and breast are bathed in tears; devotees intoxicated with prema circle around, no one can
keep his composure. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Bengali payar.*[^18-18]

**7.1.** *(Refrain)* Gora, the darling son of Shachi, dances:
the treasure unattainable for the gods He offers to whoever comes.

**7.2.** Seeing the fallen, He cannot restrain Himself;
again and again waves of bhava rise in Him.

**7.3.** A radiance surpassing gold flashes;
how beautiful He is, covered with abundant thrills!

**7.4.** His holy face and breast are bathed in tears;
raising both arms, He cries again and again: "Hari!"

**7.5.** All around move devotees intoxicated with prema;
cries of "Glory, glory!" fill earth and sky.

**7.6.** Looking at the Lord, no one can keep his composure;
Narahari, fallen at His reddish feet, weeps.

[^18-18]: GPT1 — pp. 269–270, no. 69 (kamoda); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 69 (catalogue: NG-152). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 948; ed. 1960,
vv. 3381–3386): at the house of Srivasa — "how Gaura plays in Navadvipa even Brahma cannot fathom; the fortunate will see the
dances, kirtana, bhavas and mercy of this place" (vv. 3379–3380). Not in PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.

## 8. Narahari — "nāce gorā guṇamaṇi…" (GPT1 p. 270, no. 70; BR)
*The dance of Gora, mine of prema, among His associates — like a golden moon among the stars; His body more tender than a shirisha
flower, a smile on His red lips; seeing the fallen, He weeps, and as it were the Suradhuni flows from His eyes; the khol and karatalas
sound, all are intoxicated — only the poet is left out. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR
(12th wave); Bengali tripadi.*[^18-19]

**8.1.** Gora dances, the jewel of virtues, a very mine of prema, His dear associates around Him;
a wondrous beauty — as if a golden moon had risen among the stars.

**8.2.** His body, more tender than a shirisha flower, is lovely, covered with thrills;
the full-blown lotus is left far behind, Madana weeps before His face; a smile is on His red lips.[^18-20]

**8.3.** Striking so many poses, He raises His arms and cries "Hari!" — ceaselessly He rains nectar;
His heart is full of compassion: seeing the fallen He weeps, and from His eyes flows a stream like the Suradhuni.

**8.4.** The khol and karatalas sound, lovely is His gait — who, seeing this, would not be enchanted?
No grief or sorrow remains, all the people are intoxicated — only Narahari is deprived of this joy.

[^18-19]: GPT1 — p. 270, no. 70 (kamoda); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 70 (catalogue: NG-252). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 949; ed. 1960,
vv. 3387–3390), right after the preceding pada, at the house of Srivasa. Not in PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^18-20]: The shirisha is a tree with very delicate flowers (an image of tenderness). Madana (Kama) "weeps" seeing that the Lord's face is
more beautiful than his own.

## 9. Narahari — "nācata naṭavara gaurakiśora…" (GPT1 p. 270, no. 72; BR)
*Young Gaura, the best of dancers, enchants the world with new movements: the radiance of His body is peerless, a garland of forest
flowers sways on His neck, His moon-face pours nectar which the chakora-devotees drink; He sings the names of Hari, and all weep — only
the poet's heart does not melt. Raga suhai. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli.*[^18-21]

**9.1.** Young Gaura dances, the best of dancers;
with new movements He sends the world into rapture.

**9.2.** The peerless radiance of His body flashes;
seeing it, countless Kamas swoon.

**9.3.** His large eyes sway;
on His neck swings a garland of forest flowers.

**9.4.** His radiant moon-face pours down nectar —
the chakora-devotees drink it to the full with their eyes.[^18-22]

**9.5.** Again and again He utters the sweet name of Hari —
who, hearing it, does not weep without end?

**9.6.** The sinful and the fallen are intoxicated with the rasa of prema —
only Narahari's hard breast does not melt.

[^18-21]: GPT1 — p. 270, no. 72 (suhai); GPT2 — sec. 4.2, no. 72. The pada was not in the catalogue — **new row NG-254** (the signature
sweep had matched it to another pada). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 952; ed. 1960, vv. 3430–3435), right after a pada of Vasu
Ramananda (GPT1 no. 73), before the account of Advaita's dance in the house of Srivasa. The GPT2 index assigns the pages of this
place to Chakravarti. Not in PK (PK 2065 "nācata naṭavara gaura kiśora" is a different pada, by Balarama Dasa), KGC, PS or the
Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^18-22]: The chakora is a bird which, by poetic tradition, feeds on moonlight: the devotees "drink with their eyes" the beauty of the
Lord's face.

## 10. Narahari — "prabhu viśvambhara priya parikara…" (GPT1 p. 283, no. 21; BR)
*The Lord's dream of Balarama: Vishvambhara tells His associates that at night He saw a beautiful chariot with a palm-tree banner arrive
here; a tall man with an earring in one ear, a pitcher in His hand, dressed in blue and with a blue cloth on His head, swaying, looked
around and asked for Him by name again and again — Haladhara must have come; having said this, the Lord was absorbed in the bhava of
Balarama. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave) and is set in the account of
Nityananda's arrival in Navadvipa; Bengali tripadi.*[^18-23]

**10.1.** Lord Vishvambhara says to His dear associates: "Listen to what I saw in a dream.
What a wondrously made, beautifully adorned chariot with a palm-tree banner has come here!

**10.2.** I saw a handsome man of tall stature — what can He be compared with?
In one ear an earring, and what a neck! His moon-face enchants the world.

**10.3.** A dark pitcher in His hand, a blue cloth on His head, and He was fittingly dressed in blue;
He looked about on all sides and walked swaying — who, seeing that gait, could keep his composure?

**10.4.** Calling My name, He asked for Me again and again — Haladhara must have come."
Having said this, Narahari's Lord was absorbed in the bhava of Balarama.[^18-24]

[^18-23]: GPT1 — p. 283, sec. 4.3 (bhavavesha), no. 21 (kamoda); GPT2 — sec. 4.3, no. 21 (catalogue: NG-253). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912,
p. 826; ed. 1960, vv. 1731–1734): Nityananda came to Navadvipa and stayed with Nandana Acharya; the Lord, knowing this, in the temple of
Vishnu where He worshipped Vishnu and where the Vaishnavas gathered, "told here the dream of that night"; after the pada Srivasa and
others, seeing the Lord in this bhava, offer prayers, and Haridasa and Srivasa are sent to search for Nityananda (vv. 1735–1738). The
GPT2 index assigns this page to Chakravarti. Not in PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. The dream and the bhava of Balarama — CB
Madhya 3; cf. Murari 2.14 (the bhava of Balarama).
[^18-24]: The palm-tree banner (tala-dhvaja), blue garments, an earring in one ear are marks of Balarama (Haladhara, "Bearer of the
plough"); the one who has come is Nityananda, the Balarama of Gaura-lila, whom the Lord recognises before meeting Him. "Narahari's Lord"
(narahari-prabhu) is the Lord whom the poet serves (cf. chapter 17, note 44). The bhava of Balarama is one of the bhavas the Lord revealed
in Navadvipa: a manifestation of His own fullness, not a transformation into another.

## 11. Narahari — "pālaṅka upare gaurāṅga sundara…" (GPT1 p. 306, no. 23)
*The Lord in the bhava of Radha waiting for Krishna (vasaka-sajja): beautiful Gauranga sits sadly on the couch; He has decked the bed
with flowers because Shyama promised to come, but the night is almost over — where is the dark moon? Kala has not come — how much longer
to bear the burning of love? "I will break off love with cruel Shyama!" Raga dhanashi. **Attribution: not established** — the pada is
not in the BR; the GPT2 index assigns the page to "Narahari Dasa" (undistinguished); simple Bengali tripadi, like the neighbouring pada
of Sarakara PK 307 (GPT1 no. 22), which it follows in content.*[^18-25]

**11.1.** On the couch beautiful Gauranga sits in sadness:
His heart is seized by the bhava of Radha — He shows the state of vasaka-sajja.[^18-26]

**11.2.** He says: "My dark friend said He would come — and I decked the bed with flowers;
the night is almost gone — where is He, the dark moon? The night has passed in vain.

**11.3.** Kala has not come — how much longer will the heart bear the burning of love?"
Narahari conveys: "I will break off love with that cruel Shyama!"[^18-27]

[^18-25]: GPT1 — p. 306, sec. 4.5 (abhisara, rasodgara, utkanthita), no. 23 (dhanashi); GPT2 — sec. 4.5, no. 23 (the catalogue did not know
this pada — **new row NG-255**; the signature sweep had matched it to another pada). Before it (no. 22) stands Narahari Sarakara's pada
"kī lāgiyā mora gaurasundara vasiyā gṛhera mājhe" (PK 307, chapter 3, no. 3) on the same theme. Not in BR, PK, KGC, PS or the
Gita-chandrodaya. C.
[^18-26]: Vasaka-sajja is the heroine who has adorned herself and the bed and waits for her beloved (one of the eight states of the heroine
in alankara-shastra; Rupa Gosvami, Ujjvala-nilamani). The Lord, Krishna Himself, appeared in order to taste Radha's love for Him (CC Adi
4), and lives through Her waiting and separation. This is pure prema, not worldly passion: Radha's bhava is the highest manifestation of
the hladini-shakti.
[^18-27]: Anger at Krishna (mana) is one of the expressions of Radha's prema, in which love only grows stronger; the words "I will break off
love" are not a cooling but the voice of wounded love. PK 307 has a similar ending (chapter 3, no. 3). The pronoun "I" is the Lord's
speech in Radha's bhava, which the poet conveys.

## 12. Narahari — "jhulata rasamaya gaurakiśora…" (GPT1 p. 324, no. 10; BR)
*Jhulana: on the bank of the Suradhuni, under a lofty tree, a peerless swing has been made; the skilful associates gently swing young
Gaura, sing and play; the people of Nadia leave their homes and run to see His smiling face, the gods shower flowers, and Narahari
cannot count the virtues of the Lord of his life. Raga mallara or imana. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR
(12th wave, the beginning of the account of jhulana); Vrajabuli.*[^18-28]

**12.1.** *(Refrain)* Young Gaura, full of rasa, is swinging;
on the bank of the Suradhuni, under a lofty tree, a peerless, charming swing has been made.

**12.2.** The skilful associates gently swing Him and sing, rapt in the rasa of the melodies;
they utter a sweet "dhik-dhik-dhini" and play on so many sweet-sounding instruments.[^18-29]

**12.3.** Crowds of the men and women of Nadia leave their homes and come, unable to restrain themselves;
their eyes, unblinking, gaze at His moon-face lit with a smile.

**12.4.** The gods in the sky, immersed in bliss, with their companions shower flowers and cry "Glory!";
Narahari, intoxicated by the virtues of the Lord of his life, speaks of them without end — and cannot count them.[^18-30]

[^18-28]: GPT1 — p. 324, sec. 5.1 (the "twelve-month lila"), no. 10 (mallara or imana; in the recognition the number is distorted —
"১৪"); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 10. In the catalogue — row NS-016 (with a wrong reference to PK 2106, a pada of Nayanananda); a Narahari
pada, known only from the GPT and the BR, now assigned to the appendix (new row NG-256). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 938; ed. 1960,
vv. 3263–3266): "by Gaurachandra's will the six seasons are always embodied in Nadia; to delight the rainy season, here the Lord swings
on a swing" (vv. 3261–3262). The GPT2 index assigns these pages to Chakravarti. Not in PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
Jhulana-yatra is the swing festival in the month of Shravana (July–August).
[^18-29]: "Dhik-dhik-dhini" are rhythmic syllables (bol) chanted to the drum.
[^18-30]: "The Lord of Narahari's life" (narahari-prāṇanātha) is Lord Gaura (cf. note 24).

## 13. Narahari — "āju suradhunītīre gorārāya…" (GPT1 p. 324, no. 11; BR)
*Jhulana: Gora Raya swings on the bank of the Suradhuni, looking at Gadadhara's face, and in His joy cannot sit still; all sing of the
former swinging, and everyone runs to see. Raga mallara. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); short
Bengali payar.*[^18-31]

**13.1.** Today on the bank of the Suradhuni Gora Raya
swings on the swing — in how many ways!

**13.2.** Looking at the face of dear Gadadhara,
in His joy He cannot sit still.[^18-32]

**13.3.** All sing of the former lila of the swing;
who does not run to see this beauty?

**13.4.** Fixing their eyes on the Lord of Narahari's life,
some, returning home, tell how happy they are.[^18-33]

[^18-31]: GPT1 — p. 324, no. 11 (mallara); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 11 (catalogue: NG-158). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 939; ed. 1960, vv.
3267–3270), right after the preceding one. Not in PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^18-32]: "The former lila of the swing" is the jhulana of Radha and Krishna in Vraja; the Lord remembers it with Gadadhara, who in
Krishna-lila is Radha (note 9).
[^18-33]: So in GPT2 ("kata sukhī"); the GPT1 recognition has "kata sakhī" ("tells her friend"); in the BR the line is damaged. The next pada of
the GPT (no. 12, "jhulata jhulata sundara rasamaya gorā…", also signed by Narahari and also in the BR) is the speech of a townswoman who
has resolved to forget her shame before her family for Gaura's sake — nagari-bhava; it is assigned to the section of nagari padas (new
catalogue row NG-257).

## 14. Narahari — "āju gorā suradhunītīre. jhule kivā lalita hindore…" (GPT1 p. 325, no. 13; BR)
*Jhulana in the rainy season: Gora swings on a charming swing by the Suradhuni, His form flashes like lightning in the dark clouds, the
thunder of the mridanga is like a storm, the peahens dance, Nadia rejoices, creepers and trees thrill; Narahari, looking at the Lord's
face, gently rocks the swing. Raga mallara. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); short Bengali
payar.*[^18-34]

**14.1.** Today Gora on the bank of the Suradhuni
swings on a charming swing.

**14.2.** And what a rainy season it is!
Darkness from the gathered clouds.

**14.3.** Gora's form flashes like lightning,
stealing the life of the world.

**14.4.** Sweetly the associates sing —
as if pouring down so much nectar.

**14.5.** The mridanga resounds like thunder —
the peahens dance.[^18-35]

**14.6.** The town of Nadia rejoices,
creepers and trees are covered with thrills.

**14.7.** All run to see,
and each has so many desires.

**14.8.** Narahari, looking at the Lord's face,
gently, gently rocks the swing.[^18-36]

[^18-34]: GPT1 — p. 325, no. 13 (mallara); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 13 (catalogue: NG-159). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 940; ed. 1960, vv.
3275–3282), after pada no. 12 (nagari). Not in PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^18-35]: Images of the rainy season: Gaura is the lightning, the thunder of the drum the storm; peacocks (here peahens) dance on hearing
thunder.
[^18-36]: Narahari Sarakara is an associate of the Lord who served Him in Navadvipa (in the pada on the arati he waves the chamara —
chapter 17, no. 12); Chakravarti, describing the Navadvipa lila, often speaks in the person of Narahari the associate.

## 15. Narahari — "gorā pahu dole hindolete…" (GPT1 p. 325, no. 14; BR)
*After the jhulana: the Lord swings, looking at Gadadhara's face, His golden body thrills; the rejoicing associates take Him down from
the swing and seat Him under a kadamba tree; Nityananda weeps with prema, Advaita roars; Srivasa and others lovingly bring delicacies;
Gora Raya feeds everyone, and Narahari partakes of the remnants. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the
BR (12th wave); short Bengali payar.*[^18-37]

**15.1.** Lord Gora swings on the swing —
how much happiness in the bhava He remembers!

**15.2.** He looks at Gadadhara's face,
thrills fill His golden body.

**15.3.** The associates, rejoicing at heart,
take Him down from the swing,

**15.4.** to seat Him at the roots of a kadamba;
Nitai swims in tears of prema.

**15.5.** Advaita gives a thunderous roar —
a boundless ocean of happiness swells.

**15.6.** Srivasa and the others with care
bring and set out all kinds of delicacies.

**15.7.** Gora Raya is the life of all; will He eat Himself? —
He feeds everyone.

**15.8.** Can this joy be described?
Narahari partakes of the remnants.[^18-38]

[^18-37]: GPT1 — p. 325, no. 14 (kamoda); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 14 (catalogue: NG-160). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 940; ed. 1960, vv.
3283–3290), the last pada of the account of jhulana. Not in PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. The next GPT pada signed Narahari
(no. 16, "āju racita nava ratana-hindora") is PK 1559 (catalogue: NG-161 = NS-032), already translated (chapter 4).
[^18-38]: The last couplet is restored from GPT2 and the BR ("avaśeṣa bhuñje narahari"; distorted in the GPT1 recognition). The remnants of the
Lord's food (mahaprasada) are the highest mercy for a servant (cf. CC Antya 16).

## 16. Narahari — "gorā mora gokulera śaśī…" (GPT1 p. 327, no. 20; BR)
*Janmashtami and Nanda-utsava in the house of Srivasa: Gora, smiling, announces "Today is Krishna's birth!" and dances in a cowherd's
dress; Nitai with a staff, Gauridasa, Ramai and Sundara with carrying-poles, Srivasa and Advaita scatter turmeric and yoghurt, Mukunda and
Madhava sing, the women perform auspicious rites — the house of Srivasa has become the house of Nanda. Raga kamoda. **Attribution:
probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave, the account of the festival of Krishna's birth); Bengali payar.*[^18-39]

**16.1.** My Gora is the moon of Gokula;
smiling, He says: "Today is Krishna's birth!"

**16.2.** Seized by bhava, He cannot remain still:
putting on a cowherd's dress, He dances with joy in His heart.

**16.3.** Nitai, dressed as a cowherd,
with a staff in His hand dances, bending in every way.

**16.4.** Gauridasa, Ramai and Sundara
dance in cowherd dress, with lovely carrying-poles on their shoulders.[^18-40]

**16.5.** Srivasa and Advaita in cowherd dress
scatter turmeric and yoghurt with joy in their hearts.

**16.6.** Some play on various instruments;
Mukunda and Madhava sing of the lila of the birth.

**16.7.** The women perform auspicious rites;
the house of Srivasa is like the house of Nanda.[^18-41]

**16.8.** Again and again cries of "Glory!" ring out;
people run, and no one can keep his composure.

**16.9.** With what longing they gaze, filling their eyes!
This beauty makes the world forget everything, says Narahari.

[^18-39]: GPT1 — p. 327, sec. 5.1 (subsection "janma-līlā"), no. 20 (kamoda); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 20 (catalogue: NG-162). BR — 12th wave
(ed. 1912, pp. 930–931; ed. 1960, vv. 3160–3168). According to the BR account (vv. 3148–3159), one day in the house of Srivasa the Lord
said, laughing: "Tomorrow is Krishna's birthday"; Srivasa and the others prepared everything, at night they performed Krishna's
abhisheka and spent the night in sankirtana; in the morning the Lord and His associates put on cowherd dress (Nityananda was the most
skilful at it), with pots of yoghurt and butter on carrying-poles they entered Srivasa's courtyard, Srivasa and Advaita scattered
yoghurt and turmeric — "the house of Srivasa became like the house of Nanda". Not in PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
Nanda-utsava is the festival on the day after Janmashtami (Krishna's birth, Bhadra krishna-ashtami): the cowherds of Vraja in their joy
drenched one another with milk, yoghurt and butter (Bhag. 10.5). Cf. CC Madhya 15 — Nanda-utsava in Puri, where the Lord also
appears in cowherd dress.
[^18-40]: Ramai is probably Abhirama (Ramadasa), Sundara is Sundarananda: both among the twelve "cowherd boys" (gopalas) of Nityananda;
Gauridasa Pandita is Subala in Krishna-lila. In this lila they reveal their eternal bhava of cowherd friends.
[^18-41]: Auspicious rites (maṅgala) — the "ulu-ulu" cry, lamps and so on, with which women greet the birth of a child; Nanda is Krishna's
foster-father in Vraja.

## 17. Narahari — "gokulera śaśī gorā guṇarāśi…" (GPT1 pp. 327–328, no. 21; BR)
*Nanda-utsava: on the day of His former birth Gora dances in cowherd dress; Nitai dances with Ramai and Sundara, Advaita pours a pot of
yoghurt on His head, Srivasa and others sprinkle turmeric on Advaita, Shankara and Murari dance with carrying-poles, Mukunda and others
sing. Raga dhanashi. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Bengali tripadi.*[^18-42]

**17.1.** The moon of Gokula, Gora, a treasury of virtues — on the day of His former birth
with what joy He dances in cowherd dress, His heart seized by that bhava!

**17.2.** Nitai in bliss dances in cowherd fashion together with Ramai and Sundara;
Advaita, running up with a pot of yoghurt, pours it on Nitai's head.

**17.3.** Srivasa and the others playfully sprinkle turmeric on Advaita and laugh;
Shankara and Murari, carrying-poles on their shoulders, dance in cowherd dress.

**17.4.** Mukunda and the others sing and play various instruments, gazing at the moon of Gora's face;
Narahari sings well: moment by moment the ocean of bliss swells.

[^18-42]: GPT1 — pp. 327–328, no. 21 (dhanashi); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 21 (catalogue: NG-163). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 931; ed. 1960,
vv. 3169–3172), right after the preceding one. Not in PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. Shankara is Shankara Pandita, brother of
Damodara Pandita; Murari is Murari Gupta.

## 18. Narahari Dasa — "gauraguṇamaṇi varajaśaśadhara…" (GPT1 p. 328, no. 22; BR)
*Nanda-utsava: on the day of Krishna's birth, the eighth of Bhadra, Gaura is with His associates in the house of Srivasa; like the
cowherds of Vraja all put on turbans, flowers, bracelets; with carrying-poles and staffs they dance in a courtyard covered with mud of
turmeric, yoghurt and butter, crying "hi-hi!"; Nitai sprinkles turmeric on the Lord, Advaita smears Nitai's face with butter, they roll
in the mud; the gods shower flowers, people run from all sides. Raga mayura. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the
BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli with long chains of assonance.*[^18-43]

**18.1.** Gaura, the jewel of virtues, the moon of Vraja — on the eighth day of Bhadra, when He appeared before — lovingly abides with
His associates in the house of Srivasa;
tying soft, jaunty turbans, adorning their heads with flowers and leaves, putting on bracelets and new waistcloths, all dress like
the cowherds of Vraja.

**18.2.** Some carry on their shoulders painted poles with pots of yoghurt, others have staffs in their hands; stepping gracefully,
they shine in the courtyard, where there is a mud of turmeric, yoghurt and butter;
crying "hi-hi!" without end, covered with thrills, stirred in body and mind, they dance with peerless grace, enchanting the whole
world.[^18-44]

**18.3.** Laughing with joy, Nitai says so many things and sprinkles turmeric and yoghurt on the Lord's body; at once Advaita smears
fresh butter on Nitai's face;
mighty Nitai playfully seizes Him, and they roll with delight in the thick mud; all smeared, Advaita dances there at once, flinging
His arms to the sky.

**18.4.** Vasudeva, Mukunda, Madhava and others sing of the festival of the birth; the musicians play many instruments: "dha-dhi-
dhiki-taka-dhini-ni-ni";
the gods shower flowers, Narahari Dasa gazes at his Lord; no one can keep his composure — men and women run from all sides.

[^18-43]: GPT1 — p. 328, no. 22 (mayura); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 22. The pada was not in the catalogue — **new row NG-258**. BR — 12th wave
(ed. 1912, pp. 931–932; ed. 1960, vv. 3173–3176), right after the preceding one. Not in PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. The
eighth day of the dark half of Bhadra (August–September) is Janmashtami; "before" — in Krishna-lila.
[^18-44]: "Hi-hi!" is the cowherds' cry. The playful romp of Nityananda and Advaita in the mud of yoghurt and turmeric is a game of the
Nanda-utsava, in which the Lord's associates reveal the bhava of the cowherd boys of Vraja (cf. CC Madhya 15).

## 19. Narahari — "āju gorācām̐da gaṇasaha gopaveśe…" (GPT1 p. 328, no. 23; BR)
*Radhashtami in the house of Pundarika Vidyanidhi: Gorachand with His associates in cowherd dress, smiling, looks at Gadadhara and
weeps with bliss; Mukunda, Madhava and Vasu sing of Radhika's birth, the Lord dances, the earth sways; Gauridasa with a carrying-pole,
Vidyanidhi scatters butter, turmeric, milk and yoghurt; men and women run to see; Narahari dances crying "Glory!". Raga kamoda.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave, the account of Radhashtami); Bengali payar.*[^18-45]

**19.1.** Today Gorachand with His associates in cowherd dress
moment by moment sinks deeper into that rasa.

**19.2.** Gently smiling, He looks at Gadadhara;
streams of tears of bliss flow from both His eyes.[^18-46]

**19.3.** Mukunda, Madhava and Vasu, with joy in their hearts —
all sing of the birth of Radhika.

**19.4.** The khol and karatalas sound, auspicious for the world;
the Lord dances — the earth sways.

**19.5.** Gauridasa and others dance with carrying-poles on their shoulders;
seeing this cowherd dress, who can stay calm?

**19.6.** With what fervour Pundarika Vidyanidhi dances,
scattering butter, turmeric, milk and yoghurt!

**19.7.** Nitai, Advaita, Srivasa and the others, seeing this play,
float in an ocean of happiness and cannot take their eyes away.

**19.8.** Men and women run to see this play;
standing in the courtyard, they look in all directions.

**19.9.** Seeing the peerless sweetness of Gora's form,
some say: "Is it not a golden Kama dancing?"[^18-47]

**19.10.** The gods dance, showering flowers;
joyfully Narahari dances with cries of "Glory, glory!"

[^18-45]: GPT1 — p. 328, no. 23 (kamoda); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 23 (catalogue: NG-234, formerly NS-017; there and in the sweep the
signature is "nāce narahari"). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 932–933; ed. 1960, vv. 3183–3192): one day the Lord, laughing, said to Pundarika
Vidyanidhi: "Tomorrow at your house is the festival of the birth of Sri Radhika"; Vidyanidhi prepared everything, and the next day the
Lord came to him with His associates, and an abhisheka in honour of Radhika's birth was performed there (vv. 3177–3182). Not in PK, KGC,
PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. Radhashtami is the eighth day of the bright half of Bhadra, the day of Sri Radha's appearance. Pundarika
Vidyanidhi is an associate of the Lord, in Krishna-lila Vrishabhanu, Radha's father (Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika 54), hence the festival
is held at his house.
[^18-46]: Gadadhara is the Radha of Krishna-lila (note 9): on Radha's birthday the Lord looks at him with bliss.
[^18-47]: "A golden Kama" is an image of the Lord's beauty (cf. note 11); among the onlookers are both men and women — this is not the
nagari motif.

## 20. Narahari Dasa — "rādhikā-janama-utsave mātiche…" (GPT1 p. 329, no. 25)
*Radhashtami: Gora rejoices at the festival of Radhika's birth, and with Him in cowherd dress dance His associates skilled in dancing;
the madal, khol, cymbals, karatalas, khamaka, ramashinga, gopi-yantra and khanjari resound; Mukunda and others sing, the boys take up the
melody; the sound of conches and the cowherds' call mingle with it — and the poet sings together with all. Raga dhanashi. **Attribution:
not established** — the pada is not in the BR; the language is late Bengali (present continuous forms: mātiche, vājiche, miśiche, gāiche)
with heaped-up onomatopoeia; probably a comparatively late pada.*[^18-48]

**20.1.** At the festival of Radhika's birth Gora, Shachi's darling, full of joy, is rapt;
putting on cowherd dress, His associates skilled in dancing dance with Him.

**20.2.** The madal booms: "tadrim, tadrim", to the beat "dhika-dhinna" the khol sounds;
"jhanana-jhanan" — the clash of cymbals, the karatalas sound with a loud din.[^18-49]

**20.3.** "Gab-gab-gab" — the khamaka resounds, "bheu-bheu, bhon-bhon" — the ramashinga blares;
"dim-dim-dim" — the gopi-yantra sounds, "takrita-tadhin" — the khanjari tambourine.

**20.4.** Mukunda and all the others sing on the low notes, the boys take the melody on the fifth;
again and again in three registers the seven notes rise with all the murchhanas.[^18-50]

**20.5.** With this mingles the boom of conches and gongs, mingles the cowherds' call "ava-ava";
together with all sings Narahari Dasa: "I offer myself in sacrifice for Gora!"[^18-51]

[^18-48]: GPT1 — p. 329, no. 25 (dhanashi; text checked against the scan, PDF p. 588); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 25 (catalogue: NG-164). Before
it (no. 24) stands a pada on the same festival signed "Ghanashyama" (it is also in the BR; not included in the appendix). This pada is
not in BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. C.
[^18-49]: The madal is a large drum; the khol is the clay drum of kirtana; cymbals (jhām̐jhari) and karatalas are small brass cymbals.
[^18-50]: The khamaka is a one-stringed plucked instrument; the ramashinga a curved horn; the gopi-yantra a one-stringed instrument of
wandering singers; the khanjari a tambourine. The low notes are shadja (kharaja); the fifth is panchama; three registers (gramas), seven
notes (svaras), murchhanas — concepts of Indian music theory.
[^18-51]: "Ava-ava" (āvāvā) is the cry of cowherds calling the cows (cf. the padas on taking out the cows: "āvā āvā rabe"). "I offer myself
in sacrifice" (valihāri yāi… nichani) is an expression of utmost devotion.

## 21. Narahari — "sarasa suradhunī-pulina-vana…" (GPT1 p. 334, no. 43; BR)
*Remembrance of the rasa-lila: seeing the grove on the sandy bank of the Suradhuni, young Gaura remembers the former play of the rasa and is
absorbed in bliss; His face eclipses the moon, He dances in the threefold bend to the sweet thunder of the mridanga, the associates sing of
the rasa of the rasa dance, and Narahari's heart overflows. Raga shri. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th
wave, the account of the rasa-lila in Navadvipa); Vrajabuli.*[^18-52]

**21.1.** Seeing the grove on the lovely sandy bank of the Suradhuni, young Gaura
remembered the former play of the rasa — and was absorbed in joy.[^18-53]

**21.2.** His body, which takes away Madana's pride, flashes like a garland of lightning;
the sweetness of His moon-face, which eclipses the moon, pours down nectar without end.

**21.3.** Today, performing a peerless dance, He stands in a charming threefold bend;
"drimiki-drimi-drimi-drim" — sweetly, sweetly the mridanga sounds.

**21.4.** The skilful associates sing, rapt in the joy of the rasa of the rasa dance;
at this wondrous play, rare even for the gods, Narahari's breast overflows.

[^18-52]: GPT1 — p. 334, sec. 5.1 (subsection "rasa and maharasa"), no. 43 (shri); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 43. The pada was not in the
catalogue — **new row NG-259**. BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 941; ed. 1960, vv. 3297–3300): "here Gaurachandra revealed great bliss,
remembering the former rasa of the rasa dance" (v. 3291), after a pada of Vasu Ghosha on the same subject. The GPT2 index assigns these
pages to Chakravarti. Not in PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. The next GPT pada (no. 44, "kī madhura madhuniśā" — the rasa of
Balarama revealed by Nityananda; in the catalogue wrongly VG-048, Vasu Ghosha) is also signed Narahari and also in the BR; as a pada about
Nityananda it is translated in chapter 24, no. 13 (new row NG-260).
[^18-53]: The rasa-lila is Krishna's circle dance with the gopis on an autumn night in Vrindavana (Bhag. 10.29–33), the summit of the lila
of love. The Lord, remembering it on the bank of the Ganga, experiences it as Krishna Himself; this is the pure prema of Vraja, not
worldly passion (Bhag. 10.33.39: one who hears of the rasa is freed from lust).

## 22. Narahari — "vasanta samaya suśobhita…" (GPT1 p. 338, no. 55; BR)
*Spring in Nadia: the trees and creepers blossom, the cuckoos call, the bees hum, the southern breeze blows; Gora, the Nagara of Gokula,
plays with His associates on the bank of the Suradhuni: Mukunda and Madhava sing, all throw flower-pollen phagu at one another, Nitai,
Advaita, Gadadhara and Srivasa play phagu; the gods cannot keep their composure. Raga basanta. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** —
the pada is in the BR (12th wave, the account of the spring games); Bengali payar.*[^18-54]

**22.1.** Beautiful is the springtime:
how the trees and creepers of Nadia blossom!

**22.2.** Ceaselessly the cuckoos call,
swarms of bees roam about and hum.

**22.3.** A gentle southern breeze blows;
the heart overflows — no one can remain still.

**22.4.** Gora, the Nagara of Gokula, joyfully
plays with His associates on the bank of the Suradhuni.[^18-55]

**22.5.** Mukunda, Madhava and others sing,
all play the mridanga, the mandira and many instruments.

**22.6.** Taking flower-pollen for phagu,
someone, softly laughing, throws it on Gora's body.[^18-56]

**22.7.** Some dance in various ways;
Gorachand throws phagu over everyone.

**22.8.** Nitai, Advaita, Gadadhara,
Srivasa and others play phagu with one another.

**22.9.** Seeing this wondrous play,
the gods cannot keep their composure.

**22.10.** Who does not cry "Glory!"?
Narahari says: the earth is filled with happiness.

[^18-54]: GPT1 — p. 338, no. 55 (vasanta); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 55 (catalogue: NG-166). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 941–942; ed. 1960, vv.
3303–3312): "Gaurachandra plays in spring with His associates; here the wondrous phagu games began" (vv. 3301–3302). Not in PK, KGC, PS
or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^18-55]: "The Nagara of Gokula" (gokulanāgara) is an epithet of Krishna, the "skilful lover" of Vraja; here it indicates that Gaura is Krishna
Himself, not the nagari motif (cf. chapter 17, note 15).
[^18-56]: Phagu (phāgu) is the red powder (abir) people throw on one another at the spring festival of Holi (Dola-yatra, phalguna-purnima);
here flower-pollen is used instead.

## 23. Narahari — "phāgu khelata gaurakiśora…" (GPT1 p. 338, no. 56; BR)
*The phagu game: young Gaura in special attire, the radiance of His body eclipses lightning; with a golden syringe in hand He squirts
saffron water, the associates toss abir, and sky and earth turn red; the associates dance fearlessly, sing of the lilas of Vraja, and
cry "Ho-ho, Hari!" Raga basanta. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli.*[^18-57]

**23.1.** Young Gaura plays phagu,
in special, radiant attire.

**23.2.** The radiance of His body surpasses a garland of lightning —
at the sight of it hundreds of Kamas swoon.

**23.3.** Taking a golden syringe in His hand,
He squirts saffron water.

**23.4.** Without end they toss abir and gulal —
both the sky and the earth turn red.[^18-58]

**23.5.** Seeing the moon of the Lord's face,
the associates dance without fear.

**23.6.** Together they sing of the lilas of Vraja;
no one can keep his composure.

**23.7.** They play on many sweet-sounding instruments,
beating the rhythm "dhiki-dhiki-taka".

**23.8.** Crying "Ho-ho, Hari!", all are beside themselves;
what can Narahari, whose mind is so small, say?

[^18-57]: GPT1 — p. 338, no. 56 (vasanta); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 56 (catalogue: NG-167, its first line not recognised in the catalogue). BR —
12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 942; ed. 1960, vv. 3313–3320), right after the preceding one. Not in PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. The
next GPT pada (no. 57, "phāguyā khelata gaurakiśora") is signed "Ghanashyama" and is not included in the appendix.
[^18-58]: Abir and gulal are the red and pink powders of the spring festival; saffron water (keshara-vari) is coloured water with which people
drench one another.

## 24. Narahari — "gaura gokula-nāha naṭavara…" (GPT1 p. 339, no. 58; BR)
*A spring game on the bank of the Suradhuni: Gaura, the Lord of Gokula, best of dancers, with His associates dressed in every possible way;
His body eclipses a golden mountain, His face the moon; syringe in hand He tosses phagu; the associates cry "Hori!"; a cloud of gulal hides
the sun, the sky glows red; musk and saffron are poured on Nitai's head, Advaita frowns and claps His hands; the mridangas thunder. Raga
basanta. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli with long chains of assonance.*[^18-59]

**24.1.** Gaura, the Lord of Gokula, best of dancers, with His associates dressed in every way, plays on the bank of the Suradhuni,
increasing the joy of spring;
the radiance of His body humbles a golden mountain, lovely as Kama incarnate; a gentle smile pouring nectar flashes, His face crushes the
pride of the moon.

**24.2.** His pair of lotus eyes is charming, His sidelong glance restless and peerless; gracefully taking the syringe, He tosses phagu
by handfuls;
around Him shine the skilful associates, adorned, immersed in bliss, and crying "Hori!" they look at the Lord's face — whose eyes would
not be soothed?[^18-60]

**24.3.** Intoxicated by touch they play, filling the path of the sky with gulal; hiding the rays of the sun, the sky glows red;
crushed paste of musk and saffron they joyfully pour on Nitai's head, while Advaita, knitting His brows and clapping His hands, charms
people's hearts.[^18-61]

**24.4.** Skilful dancers dance, the drummers beat the mridanga and muraja: "thungut-theta-taka-taka-thodi-drimikat-da-drimiki-
drimi";
Narahari says: most sweetly the singers sing, keeping the shrutis and svaras — and all the gods, men and women, forgetting their
composure, run to see.

[^18-59]: GPT1 — p. 339, no. 58 (vasanta); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 58 (catalogue: NG-168). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 944; ed. 1960, vv.
3339–3342). Not in PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^18-60]: "Hori" (hori) is the cry of the Holi festival.
[^18-61]: Advaita's frowning is play: the elder associate "gets angry" to make everyone laugh (cf. no. 18).

## 25. Narahari — "suradhunītīre taruṇa taru-vallarī…" (GPT1 pp. 340–341, no. 63; BR)
*A spring dance: on the bank of the Suradhuni young trees and creepers in new leaves and flowers, the bees hum, intoxicated by the scent,
cuckoos and parrots flit around; there young Gaura dances, anointed with saffron, musk and sandal, red with phagu; the associates sing,
the gods cry "Glory!", Narahari plays the mridanga. Raga dhanashi or basanta. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the
BR (12th wave, in the cycle of the dance); Vrajabuli.*[^18-62]

**25.1.** On the bank of the Suradhuni are young trees and creepers — ever new leaves, flowers opening;
intoxicated by the fragrance, swarms of bees hum, cuckoos and parrots flit all around.

**25.2.** *(Refrain)* There young Gaura, the best of dancers, dances;
anointed with saffron, musk and sandal, His body, red with phagu, shines all the more.

**25.3.** Peerless attire, garments, jewelled ornaments; His garland of forest flowers sways charmingly;
with new movements that charm the hearts of the world, again and again He beats the rhythm with His feet.

**25.4.** Most sweetly the associates sing, gazing at the moon of His face, rejoicing without end;
the gods in the sky, immersed in bliss, cry "Glory, glory!", Narahari plays the sweet-sounding mridanga.

[^18-62]: GPT1 — pp. 340–341, no. 63 (dhanashi or basanta); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 63 (catalogue: NG-169; in the GPT2 recognition the number is
"৬৬"). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 891–892; ed. 1960, vv. 2638–2641): in the BR this and the next pada stand in the cycle of the dance on
the bank of the Ganga, right after the pada "suradhunītīra parama niramala thala" (chapter 17, no. 21); after them — "having played on the
bank of the Ganga, the Lord went home this way" (v. 2650). Not in PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.

## 26. Narahari — "āju suradhunītīre sundara gaura nṛtye vibhora…" (GPT1 p. 342, no. 67; BR)
*A spring dance, a description of His form: beautiful Gaura, absorbed in dance on the bank of the Suradhuni, sprinkled with drops of phagu and
sandal; tilaka, locks, earrings, lotus eyes, smile, arms, broad chest, a garland of malati, a belt with bells, anklets; the associates sing
raga basanta, the people of Nadia run to see; "blessed is the age of Kali: in it the Lord of Gokula plays". Raga basanta. **Attribution:
probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli.*[^18-63]

**26.1.** Today on the bank of the Suradhuni beautiful Gaura is absorbed in dance;
His body, sprinkled with drops of phagu and fragrant sandal, shines.

**26.2.** On His forehead a peerless tilaka flashes, lovely is the weight of His locks;
the earrings in His ears adorn His cheeks, the arch of His brows is boundless.

**26.3.** His restless eyes are lovely lotuses, the radiance of His face conquers the moon;
His red lips with a gentle, gentle smile, His teeth put pearls to shame.

**26.4.** His arms are golden lotus stalks, His broad chest crushes Manmatha;
on His neck a lovely, skilfully woven, swaying garland of malati.

**26.5.** On His slender waist a belt with bells, He wears beautiful garments;
peerlessly His anklets jingle — all His attire intoxicates.

**26.6.** Seeing the wondrous beauty, the associates are immersed in His virtues, which have no end;
cymbals, muraja and mridanga play, they sing raga basanta.

**26.7.** Hearing it, the gods in the heavens cannot keep their composure;
from all sides run the men and women of the young town of Nadia.

**26.8.** Throughout the world cries of "Glory!" resound, a stream of prema overflows;
Narahari says: blessed is the age of Kali — in it the Lord of Gokula plays.[^18-64]

[^18-63]: GPT1 — p. 342, no. 67 (vasanta); GPT2 — sec. 5.1, no. 67 (catalogue: NG-170); the GPT2 index assigns this pada (p. 220, no. 67) to
Chakravarti. BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 892; ed. 1960, vv. 2642–2649), right after the preceding one. Not in PK, KGC, PS or the
Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^18-64]: "Blessed is the age of Kali" — because in it the Lord appeared, giving prema through sankirtana (cf. Bhag. 11.5.36: "the wise
value the age of Kali, in which everything is attained by sankirtana").

## 27. Narahari Dasa — "gaurāṅgacām̐da hera nayanera koṇe…" (GPT1 p. 488, no. 3; PK 116)
*Prarthana: the poet has taken refuge at the cool feet of Gauranga, he has no one but the Lord; he begs Nityananda for mercy: before,
They saved sinners and gave away prema — let Them now show the world the deliverance of the most sinful; with a straw between his teeth
he asks Gauranga and Nitai not to leave him without hope. Raga kedara. **Attribution: not established** — the pada is in PK, but without
a signature (the last couplet with Narahari's name is not there); the GPT2 index assigns the page to "Narahari Dasa" (undistinguished);
not in the BR; simple Bengali payar.*[^18-65]

**27.1.** Gaurangachand, look at me at least from the corner of Your eye:
I have taken refuge at Your cool feet.

**27.2.** I have laid my burden on You — I have no one;
if You show no mercy, to whom shall I go?

**27.3.** Lord Nityananda, show compassion:
in distress a lowly, wretched man calls You.

**27.4.** Before, You saved sinners — and now You do not save?
Show the world now the deliverance of the most sinful!

**27.5.** Not having received Your mercy, I wander weeping;
yet before You gave away prema, Yourself offering it to the world.[^18-66]

**27.6.** Reveal that mercy and deliver me:
I have heard that You are the merciful Lord — let the world see it.

**27.7.** Gauranga, Nitai, do not leave me without hope! —
with a straw between his teeth says Narahari Dasa.[^18-67]

[^18-65]: GPT1 — p. 488, sec. "the devotee's dainya and prarthana", no. 3 (kedara); GPT2 — sec. 7, no. 3 (catalogue: NG-235, formerly
NS-023). The pada is in PK: vol. 1, PK 116 (the concluding "prayer" of the 5th pallava, "anya prārthanā") — without a signature and
without the last couplet; the readings of the PK manuscripts are in the full version of the book. Who added the couplet with Narahari's name is unknown.
Not in BR, KGC, PS, the Gaura-charita-chintamani or the Gita-chandrodaya. C.
[^18-66]: Cf. CC Adi 7: the Lord and Nityananda give away prema indiscriminately, "without asking who is worthy".
[^18-67]: "A straw between the teeth" is a sign of humility and supplication (cf. chapter 17, note 68).

## 28. Narahari — "mari mari ogo nadīyā mājhe…" (GPT1 p. 494, no. 30)
*Golden Navadvipa: a wondrous beauty in the midst of Nadia — the house of Shachi captivates the world, around it are rows of golden
palaces, in the golden courtyards golden men and women; trees, creepers, beasts and birds have become golden, the Ganga flows as a golden
stream, the sky and the whole world have become golden — so great is the power of the beauty of the poet's Lord. Raga "as one likes"
(yatharaga). **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in Narahari Chakravarti's Gaura-charita-chintamani (where it is put in the
mouth of a woman of Nadia); not in the BR; Bengali payar with repetitions.*[^18-68]

**28.1.** Ah, ah, people! What a wondrous beauty in the midst of Nadia!
I do not know who built the house of Shachi, which captivates the world.

**28.2.** All around shine rows of new golden palaces;
in the golden courtyards play so many golden men and women.

**28.3.** And another wonder — look: the whole town of Nadia has become golden;
golden kadamba trees are adorned with golden creepers.

**28.4.** All the beasts and birds, all the insects and moths are like gold;
who has stolen the whiteness? The Jahnavi has become a golden stream.[^18-69]

**28.5.** The sky has become golden — what is this? Look: the whole world is like gold —
so great, it seems, is the power of the beauty of the poet Narahari's Lord.[^18-70]

[^18-68]: GPT1 — p. 494, sec. "the devotee's dainya and prarthana", no. 30 (yatharaga; checked against the scan, PDF p. 753); GPT2 — sec. 7,
no. 30. The pada was not in the catalogue — **new row NG-261** (the catalogue made from the GPT2 recognition had missed it). The pada is
in Narahari Chakravarti's Gaura-charita-chintamani (ed. Haridasa Dasa, 1947; recognition in
the OCR text) with the heading "kācicca" ("a certain [woman sings]"), right after a pada about
the townswomen of Nadia. Not in BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. Chakravarti's framing is the speech of a woman of Nadia (the
motif of the townswomen, cf. chapter 17, note 15); the pada itself speaks only of the Lord's beauty transforming His abode — we translate
faithfully to the author.
[^18-69]: The Jahnavi is the Ganga. The white waters of the Ganga have become golden from Gaura's radiance.
[^18-70]: "The poet Narahari's Lord" (narahari-pahu) — see note 24. Navadvipa is a spiritual abode (dhama), non-different from Vrindavana (cf. the
next GPT pada, no. 31: "where Krishna is, there is Vraja"); the gold is an image of Gaura's radiance, which it reflects.

---

# Chapter 19. Appendix. Padas signed "Narahari" from the Gaura-pada-tarangini — III: the childhood pastimes of Nimai

*Continuation of the appendix (the introductory note on the two Naraharis, on the arguments for attribution and on the marks in the
headings is in ch. 17). Chapter 19: padas on the Lord's childhood from the "Balya-lila" section of the GPT (2.2). First come three
padas which Narahari Chakravarti quotes in the Bhakti-ratnakara while showing the house of Jagannatha Mishra (the first feeding with
rice, Nimai in His father's arms, the first steps); then a large cycle in which the old men and elderly women of Navadvipa, coming at
dawn to the house of Shachi, gaze at Gaura, bless Him and recall His childhood pranks. Almost the whole of this cycle is found in the
Gaura-charita-chintamani of Narahari Chakravarti (chapters 5 and 6 of the "morning pastimes": the love of the old men and the love of the
women in vatsalya) — a strong argument for Chakravarti; two padas (nos. 24 and 27) have not been found in any witness. The index of poets of GPT2
assigns the padas of the section to Chakravarti (those found in the BR) or to an undistinguished "Narahari Dasa" (the GCC padas); none to Sarakara. According to
Majumdar, the padas on the birth and childhood of Nimai are late: Narahari Sarakara, who lived in Shrikhanda, did not see the Lord's
childhood, and the "Narahari" padas known only from the GPT are unreliable for attribution. Before translation the "Narahari" signatures
in sections 2.1–2.2 were checked throughout in GPT1 (tesseract recognition): the catalogue had missed 14 padas of this section (13 of
them in this chapter). The base text is GPT1 (doubtful places from the scan), collated with GPT2, the BR (eds. 1912 and 1960) and the
Gaura-charita-chintamani (ed. 1947); PK, KGC, PS and the Gita-chandrodaya have been checked. The childhood games of the Lord are the lila
of Bhagavan, not an ordinary childhood (note 2). The notes of the GPT editors are not reproduced.*

## 1. Narahari — "nadīyāra nārī puruṣa…" (GPT1 p. 65, no. 10; BR)
*The first feeding with rice: the men and women of Nadia gather with gifts; the Child sits on Nilambara's lap in new ornaments;
tasting grains of sweet rice, He smiles; all praise Shachi and Jagannatha. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the
pada is in the BR (12th wave); tripadi with chains of chiming sounds.*[^19-1]

**1.1.** The men and women of Nadia, counting it the reward of their pious deeds, in great joy
gather for Nimai's first feeding with rice — each bringing various gifts.[^19-2]

**1.2.** They gaze their fill at the beauty of Shachi's son on the lap of fortunate Nilambara:[^19-3]
all in ever-new ornaments, a silk cloth about His hips, the hem of His garment swaying.

**1.3.** His body surpasses a golden lotus, and His face — what can compare? — the splendour of the moon;
how wondrously, tasting grains of sweet rice, He flashes a gentle smile!

**1.4.** At such a festival who can keep his composure? The joy cannot be put into words.
All praise Shachi and Jagannatha — Narahari's heart overflows with happiness.

[^19-1]: GPT1 — p. 65, section 2.2 ("Balya-lila"), no. 10 (kamoda; checked against the scan, PDF p. 324); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 10. The
catalogue did not know it (new row NG-262). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 768; ed. 1960, vv. 956–959): Ishana, showing Srinivasa the
house of Jagannatha Mishra, says that here at six months the Lord was given His first rice and named, and quotes the pada. Not in PK,
KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. The first feeding with rice (annaprashana) — CB Adi 4; CC Adi 14;
Murari 1.6.
[^19-2]: The childhood games of the Lord are not an ordinary childhood but the lila of Bhagavan (balya-lila): by His own will He appears
as an infant and a child for the sake of His eternal associates who love Him in vatsalya (parental love). Shachi and Jagannatha Mishra
are His eternal parents (in Krishna-lila, Yashoda and Nanda, CC Adi 13); their love, like the love of the people of Navadvipa, is pure
prema, not worldly attachment. So the whole Gaudiya tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati)
understands Gaura's childhood games, and so they are to be understood in all the padas of this chapter.
[^19-3]: Nilambara Chakravarti — the Lord's maternal grandfather (CC Adi 13).

## 2. Narahari — "jagannātha miśra mahāsukhe…" (GPT1 p. 65, no. 11; BR)
*Jagannatha Mishra fondles his son; Nimai climbs down from his lap and crawls about the courtyard, looking back; Shachi calls Him into
her arms — "dust will stick to You"; He climbs up to her, smiling. Raga tudi. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in
the BR (12th wave).*[^19-4]

**2.1.** Jagannatha Mishra in great happiness
takes his son on his lap and kisses the moonlike face.

**2.2.** The father adorns the hair on His little head —
running his fingers through it, his heart overflows with love.

**2.3.** From His father's lap Nimai
gracefully gets down to roam about the courtyard.

**2.4.** On all fours He crawls about the courtyard;
golden nupuras ring on His lovely feet.[^19-5]

**2.5.** As He crawls, He looks back;
Mishra stands watching the sweetness of His movements.

**2.6.** His mother comes before Him and says:
"Come up into my arms, darling — dust is sticking to Your body."

**2.7.** Putting His little hand in His mother's hand,
He climbs onto her lap, smiling and smiling.

**2.8.** His little teeth shine like drops of milk;
when they show in His smile — who can keep his composure?

**2.9.** Whomever He looks at with both eyes,
him He immerses for ever in an ocean of happiness.

**2.10.** Beautifully He shines on His mother's lap;
Narahari offers himself to the Enchanter of the world's heart.[^19-6]

[^19-4]: GPT1 — p. 65, no. 11 (tudi; scan, PDF p. 324); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 11 (catalogue: NG-006). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 769;
ed. 1960, vv. 970–979): Ishana shows the courtyard where the Lord crawled on His knees (jānu-caṃkramaṇa), quotes the pada of Vasu Ghosha
"ek mukhe ki kahiba" (GPT no. 2, chapter 12) and after it this one. Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the
Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. Cf. Murari 1.6; CC Adi 14.
[^19-5]: Nupuras — ankle bells.
[^19-6]: "Offers himself" (nichani) — Bengali nichhani: the rite of waving something around the beloved and offering oneself for his welfare
(cf. chapter 17, note 34). The signature of this cycle is usually "Narahari offers himself…" or "Narahari's life is Nimai".

## 3. Narahari — "śacī ṭhākurāṇī cāru chām̐de…" (GPT1 p. 65, no. 12; BR)
*The first steps: Shachi teaches Gora to walk, holding out her finger; He stands up, takes two or four steps, lets go of the finger
and falls; His mother takes Him in her arms and nurses Him. Raga tudi. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR
(12th wave).*[^19-7]

**3.1.** Shachi Thakurani tenderly
teaches Gorachand to walk.

**3.2.** Very gently she says, smiling:
"Come, take hold of my finger."

**3.3.** Hearing this, the Moon of Nadia joyfully
takes hold of His mother's finger with a smile.

**3.4.** Slowly, slowly He rises and stands up,
and takes two or four steps.

**3.5.** Letting go of the finger, He falls to the ground;
Shachi takes Him in her arms and kisses His little face.

**3.6.** Climbing onto her lap, He swings His little feet,
and the nupuras ring on His reddish soles.

**3.7.** Fingering with His little hand, He drinks at the breast —
there is no comparison for it.

**3.8.** He looks about on all sides with charming gestures —
Narahari offers himself for this.

[^19-7]: GPT1 — p. 65, no. 12 (tudi; scan, PDF p. 324); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 12. The catalogue did not know it (new row NG-263). BR — 12th
wave (ed. 1912, pp. 770–771; ed. 1960, vv. 990–997, "todi"): Ishana says that here in the courtyard the Lord took His first steps,
quotes a verse from Murari's Shri-Krishna-Chaitanya-carita (part 1: "walking with His reddish feet, He took from the earth the fever
of separation") and the pada. Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. The first steps — Murari 1.6;
CB Adi 4; cf. the pada of Vasu Ghosha "māyera aṅguli dhari" (chapter 12).

## 4. Narahari — "gaura-vadana sukha-sadana sudhāmaya…" (GPT1 p. 66, no. 15; GCC)
*The old men of Navadvipa gaze at Gaura's face: each offers himself for Him; trembling, in tears, leaning on one another, they say:
who created Mishra's son, who has stolen our hearing, mind and eyes? A moment without Him is like a kalpa; people tease us as madmen, we
have forgotten all order in eating and sleeping, home has grown hateful, we have no love for our own sons. Yatharaga. **Attribution:
probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in his Gaura-charita-chintamani; Vrajabuli with chains of chiming sounds.*[^19-8]

**4.1.** Again and again the old men gaze at the face of Gaura — the abode of happiness, full of nectar;
counting many of their births crowned with fruit, each again and again offers his whole self for Him.

**4.2.** They totter, their eyes brimming with tears, their bodies covered with abundant thrills;
leaning on another's hand, someone speaks soft, sweet words:

**4.3.** "Tell me, who fashioned Mishra's son, who has stolen my hearing, my mind and my eyes?
A moment when I do not see Him is like a kalpa; I am thrown into turmoil, and not a drop of steadiness remains.[^19-9]

**4.4.** It is boundless happiness to follow Him everywhere; for this everyone laughs at us, calling us madmen;
but as soon as those words reach our ears, the heart rejoices all the more.

**4.5.** Eating, walking, sleeping, speaking — all order is forgotten, everything goes topsy-turvy;
the household routine is nothing but a burden, and we have no love for our own sons."[^19-10]

**4.6.** Having spoken thus, they fall silent, absorbed within, and again cherish desires in their hearts.
How can I, Narahari Dasa, the crest-jewel of fools, describe their overflowing supreme love?

[^19-8]: GPT1 — pp. 66–67, no. 15 (yatharaga; scan, PDF pp. 325–326); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 15 (catalogue: NG-007). Gaura-charita-chintamani
(GCC) — chapter 5 ("morning pastimes": the love of the old men), pada 8, the last song of the chapter. In the GCC this whole cycle is
framed by Gaura's morning in Navadvipa: at dawn He sits in the courtyard of Shachi's house among His associates, and the people of the
town gather to gaze at Him; therefore many padas of the cycle speak of Gaura no longer as an infant, and the childhood pranks in them are
recollections. Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. Cf. the love of the people of Navadvipa for Nimai — CB Adi 6–7.
[^19-9]: A kalpa is a day of Brahma, an immeasurably long time; cf. the gopis' complaint about the blinking of the eyelids that hinders
them from seeing Krishna (Bhag. 10.31.15).
[^19-10]: Cf. Parikshit's question why the people of Vraja loved Krishna more than their own sons (Bhag. 10.14.49–57) — Krishna is the Soul
of all souls. Chakravarti transfers this to the people of Navadvipa.

## 5. Narahari — "rajanī prabhāta teji nija gṛha…" (GPT1 p. 67, no. 16; GCC)
*At dawn the old men, leaning on their sticks, come to Shachi's courtyard and cannot take their eyes off Gaura; each prays for Him: to
the Creator for long life, to Vishnu for grace and universal love, to Shiva for fame and freedom from misfortune, to Sarasvati for
invincible learning, to Bhagavati that they may always see Nimai. Raga vibhasa. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in
the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^19-11]

**5.1.** At the end of the night, leaving their homes, the venerable old men
all come to the lovely courtyard of Shachi, and in their hearts joy upon joy arises.

**5.2.** They stand leaning on their sticks and again and again gaze at Gaura's body,
as if after long days, with great toil, they had found a jewel for their hearts.

**5.3.** One, overcome by love, says to the Creator: "Fulfil all His wishes;
may He live longer than I, may He, the beautiful one, always live in this town of Nadia."[^19-12]

**5.4.** Another, with joined palms, says to Vishnu: "Cast a gracious glance on the son of Mishra;
may He be a stranger to no one, may all love Him and ceaselessly sing His virtues."

**5.5.** Another says to the Lord of Kailasa: "Increase the radiance of each of His limbs;
may His fame fill the world, may there be plenty; ward off the hosts of invincible misfortunes."

**5.6.** Another says to Sarasvati: "Make Him a pandit, invincible, so that He may never know defeat";
another says to Bhagavati: "May we always see Nimai — the life of Narahari."

[^19-11]: GPT1 — p. 67, no. 16 (vibhasa; scan, PDF p. 326); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 16 (catalogue: NG-008). GCC — chapter 5, pada 6; in the
GCC it is followed by a short stanza (rasika-chandas) with the same signature — "thus all the old men ceaselessly bless Him…" — which is
not in the GPT. Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^19-12]: The old men pray to Brahma (the Creator), Vishnu, Shiva (the Lord of Kailasa), Sarasvati and Bhagavati (the goddess Durga) for
Gaura's welfare — this is how vatsalya, parental love, shows itself: in it the devotee forgets the Lord's majesty and, seeing Him as in
need of protection, entreats all the gods on His behalf (cf. the cowherds of Vraja and Yashoda entrusting Krishna to the protection of
the gods, Bhag. 10.6, 10.7). The sweetness (madhurya) of this love, by the will of yogamaya, hides from them the majesty (aishvarya) of
the Lord; this is not independent worship of the demigods, and the Lord, of course, needs no one's protection. Bhagavati here is an
epithet of the goddess, not of Bhagavan.

## 6. Narahari — "gaura-sneha-bhare gara gara gāta…" (GPT1 p. 67, no. 17; GCC)
*At the end of the night the old men, overflowing with love for Gaura, tell their households about Him; unable to live without His
darshan, they gather all their strength, rise from their beds and, trembling, sticks in hand, go to Him. Raga dhanashi. **Attribution:
probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^19-13]

**6.1.** Their bodies overflowing with love for Gaura,
the old men rejoice at the end of the night.

**6.2.** Each told his household everything in detail;
hearing it all, they rejoice without end.

**6.3.** Unable to stay without the darshan of Gaura,
they left their beds, gathering all their strength.

**6.4.** Sticks in hand, bodies trembling —
Narahari watches this matchless spectacle.

[^19-13]: GPT1 — p. 67, no. 17 (dhanashi; scan, PDF p. 326); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 17 (catalogue: NG-009). GCC — chapter 5, pada 5
(yatharaga). GPT1 has "tejala śeṣe" ("left… at last"), the GCC "tejala śeja" ("left their beds"); the GCC reading is adopted. Not in the BR,
PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.

## 7. Narahari — "śuna mora vāṇī nā jāni ki have…" (GPT1 p. 67, no. 18; GCC)
*An old man says to his household: "I have grown utterly decrepit, and Nimai is our life and all our wealth; I always want to see Him,
but have no strength to walk. Worship the gods, give gifts to brahmanas, send Him presents that please Him; go with Narahari to Shachi,
teach her auspicious rites and make Nimai swear to give up His obstinacy." Raga suhai. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada
is in the GCC.*[^19-14]

**7.1.** "Listen to what I say: I do not know what will be — I have grown utterly decrepit.
Our treasure of life, all our wealth, is Nimai, the solace of the soul.

**7.2.** *(Refrain)* Ah, I always long to see Him!
But I have no strength to walk — that is my grief: Providence has turned against me.

**7.3.** Worship the gods, give gifts to the brahmanas, always think of His welfare;
carefully send Him various presents — whatever pleases Him.

**7.4.** Go with Narahari and teach Shachi auspicious rites;
let Nimai swear to give up His dreadful obstinacy."[^19-15]

[^19-14]: GPT1 — p. 67, no. 18 (suhai; scan, PDF p. 326); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 18. The catalogue did not know it (new row NG-264). GCC —
chapter 5, pada 4 (yatharaga). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^19-15]: The poet introduces himself into the lila as one of the people of Navadvipa ("go with Narahari") — a frequent device of
Chakravarti in the GCC. "Obstinacy" (ām̐khuṭi) — Nimai's childish whims, of which the following padas tell (cf. CB Adi 6: the neighbours'
complaints to Jagannatha Mishra).

## 8. Narahari — "niśi parabhāta samaye yerūpa ānanda śacīra ghare…" (GPT1 p. 68, no. 19; GCC)
*The joy in Shachi's house at dawn cannot be told even by a thousand mouths through hundreds of yugas: Gaurachand, who gives happiness
to His own, has spread in the courtyard a net that enchants the world; people leave their beds, come running, drown in the ocean of His
beauty and cannot go home. Raga vibhasa. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^19-16]

**8.1.** What joy there is in Shachi's house at the end of the night —
not even in hundreds of yugas could a thousand mouths describe a fraction of it![^19-17]

**8.2.** How many games Gaurachand knows to give happiness to His own!
It seems that in the middle of the courtyard He has spread a net that enchants the world.

**8.3.** Leaving their beds, running and running, everyone gathers, rejoicing;
drowned in the ocean of that beauty, they can no longer return home.

**8.4.** A wondrous love ceaselessly arises in everyone's heart;
they give body and mind to those reddish feet, says Narahari Dasa.

[^19-16]: GPT1 — p. 68, no. 19 (vibhasa; scan, PDF p. 327); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 19. The catalogue did not know it (new row NG-265). GCC —
the first pada of chapter 7, which is devoted to the townswomen of Navadvipa (nāgarī) seized by love for Gaura; the pada itself speaks
only of the joy of all who come at dawn to Shachi's house, without the nagari motif, and in the GPT it stands in the section on
childhood — therefore it is translated here. In Chakravarti's frame it belongs to the motif of the townswomen (cf. chapter 17, note 15):
worship of Gaura in the spirit of "gaura-nagari" is not accepted by the Gaudiya tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja,
Bhaktisiddhanta). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^19-17]: "A thousand mouths" — an allusion to the thousand-headed Ananta-Shesha, who eternally sings of the Lord and finds no end to His
qualities.

## 9. Narahari — "āhā mari mari gaurāṅgacām̐dera carite…" (GPT1 p. 68, no. 20; GCC)
*The people of Nadia cannot live through the night without Gaura: in sleep they see only Him and at dawn they wake with His name;
matchless are their old men and women; Gora, overflowing with tenderness, speaks sweet words with these old kinsfolk. Raga vibhasa.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^19-18]

**9.1.** Ah, who does not pine for the deeds of Gaurangachand!
The people of Nadia cannot live through the night without seeing Him.

**9.2.** Lying down, in their dreams they know nothing else: Gora is all their wealth;
at dawn they wake crying "Gora, Gora!", absorbed in that rasa.

**9.3.** There is no one to equal all these old men and women;
who with such care created their beautiful nature and conduct?

**9.4.** Narahari offers himself to his Lord: among all these old kinsfolk
Gora, overflowing with tenderness, says something to them in sweet words.

[^19-18]: GPT1 — p. 68, no. 20 (vibhasa; scan, PDF p. 327); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 20 (catalogue: NG-010, wrongly as no. 10). GCC — chapter
5, pada 1; the chapter opens with the heading "Again in the morning — the excellence of the old men's love". Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or
the Gita-chandrodaya. B.

## 10. Narahari — "śuna he sumati ati nirajane…" (GPT1 p. 68, no. 21; GCC)
*One old man tells another in secret: "It seems the Son of the Lord of Vraja has appeared here: there is no one in Nadia who does not
pine for His qualities; Srivasa, Murari and the others do not live without His darshan; the ascetic Advaita of Shantipur is constantly
here and tells everyone of His sweet qualities. Make Gorachand the necklace of your throat." Raga vibhasa. **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^19-19]

**10.1.** "Listen, wise one, in great secrecy I tell you a hidden thing:
it seems that the Son of the Lord of Vraja, who was in Vraja, has appeared here.[^19-20]

**10.2.** There is no one in the town of Nadia who does not pine for His qualities;
Srivasa, Murari and all the others do not live without His darshan.

**10.3.** The resident of Shantipur, the ascetic Advaita, is constantly here,
and with what zeal He tells of His sweet qualities to whomever He meets!

**10.4.** Ah, will there ever be another such wondrous youth?
Make Gorachand, Narahari's all, the necklace of your throat."

[^19-19]: GPT1 — p. 68, no. 21 (vibhasa; scan, PDF p. 327); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 21 (catalogue: NG-011). GCC — chapter 5, pada 2, marked
"someone says" (kopyāha); the address there is "listen, O worthy one, O wise one" (śuna ohe sati he sumati), that is, apparently to his
wife. Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. Srivasa, Murari and Advaita, "who do not live without His darshan", are a
sign of the GCC frame (Gaura's morning among His associates in Navadvipa after His return from Gaya); the "youth" here is the young
Gaura.
[^19-20]: The old man guesses the truth: Sri Gauranga is Krishna Himself, the Son of Nanda, the Lord of Vraja (CC Adi 1–4); "secret" — because in this incarnation
the Lord hides His divinity (the "concealed" avatara of the Kali-yuga, Bhag. 7.9.38).

## 11. Narahari — "śuna ohe sati nadīyā vasati…" (GPT1 p. 68, no. 22; GCC)
*Another old man says to his wife: "Not in vain have I lived in Nadia — in my old age Providence has been merciful: I have gazed my fill
at Nimai; a moment without Him, and my soul weeps. Worship the gods, make vows for His welfare, reward the astrologers; go with Narahari
to Shachi's house and perform auspicious rites." Raga vibhasa. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^19-21]

**11.1.** "Listen, good wife: my life in Nadia has been crowned with fruit;
in my old age Providence has been merciful — there is no end to my happiness.

**11.2.** With these two eyes I have gazed my fill at Nimaichand, the son of Shachi;
not seeing Him for half a moment, my soul always weeps bitterly.

**11.3.** May I die taking His misfortunes upon myself: I have never seen or heard of anyone like Him;[^19-22]
worship the gods with various rites and make vows for His welfare.

**11.4.** Generously reward the astrologers so as to propitiate the planets;
go with Narahari to Shachi's house and perform auspicious rites there."

[^19-21]: GPT1 — pp. 68–69, no. 22 (vibhasa; scan, PDF pp. 327–328); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 22. The catalogue did not know it (new row
NG-266). GCC — chapter 5, pada 3, marked "and another [says]" (kopi ca). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. On the
prayers to the gods for the Lord see note 12.
[^19-22]: "To die taking His misfortunes upon oneself" (vālāi laiyā mari) — a Bengali expression of tender love: "may all His troubles fall
on me".

## 12. Narahari — "āju śubhakṣaṇe pohāila niśi…" (GPT1 p. 69, no. 23; GCC)
*An auspicious dawn: the people of Nadia run to Shachi's house to see Gaurangachand; Gora sits in the middle of the courtyard,
surrounded by His associates like the moon by the stars; all have forgotten themselves and cannot take their eyes off His face. Raga
vibhasa. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^19-23]

**12.1.** Today at an auspicious hour the night has ended;
the people of Nadia are immersed in bliss.

**12.2.** To see Gaurangachand with love,
all come running to Shachi's house.

**12.3.** In the middle of the courtyard Gora is shining,
the stealer of the hearts and eyes of all the world.

**12.4.** On all sides His associates shine —
He among them like the moon among the stars; but what is that comparison!

**12.5.** No one remembers anything —
everyone's eyes are fixed on that face.

**12.6.** What can Narahari tell with only one mouth?
Each rejoices in his own rasa.

[^19-23]: GPT1 — p. 69, no. 23 (vibhasa; scan, PDF p. 328); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 23 (catalogue: NG-012, wrongly as no. 13). GCC — the first
