pada of chapter 6, devoted to the love of the women in vatsalya ("morning pastimes": the love of the elderly women). Not in the BR, PK,
KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.

## 13. Narahari — "advaita-gharaṇī sītā ṭhākurāṇī…" (GPT1 p. 69, no. 24; GCC)
*Sita Thakurani, Advaita's wife, gazes unblinking at Gaura's smile; remembering His new deeds, she becomes as she was before, weeps,
carefully instructs Shachi, blesses and praises. Yatharaga. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^19-24]

**13.1.** Advaita's wife, Sita Thakurani — the very embodiment of rasa —
with unblinking eyes gazes at the beautiful smile on Gaura's face.

**13.2.** Thinking and thinking of His new deeds, she became just as she was before;[^19-25]
unable to restrain herself — streams of tears flow from both her eyes.

**13.3.** So many words arise in her heart, her mind is faint with tenderness;
and with care she gives Shachi instructions on what to do.

**13.4.** Blessing without end, she praises [Him] — there is no limit to her happiness.
Narahari says: who has the power to understand all these deeds?

[^19-24]: GPT1 — p. 69, no. 24 (yatharaga; scan, PDF p. 328); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 24. The catalogue did not know it (new row NG-267). GCC — chapter 6, pada 2. Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the
Gita-chandrodaya. B. Sita Thakurani — the wife of Advaita Acharya; according to CC Adi 13, she came with gifts to bless the newborn
Lord.
[^19-25]: "As before" (pūrava pārā) — apparently as in the days of His appearance, when she first came to the Child (CC Adi 13); another
reading is possible — as in the former (Krishna-)lila.

## 14. Narahari — "śrīvāsa-vanitā ati sucaritā…" (GPT1 p. 69, no. 25; GCC)
*Srivasa's wife, tenderness incarnate, chaste and modest, her face covered with the hem of her cloth, stands beside Sita and gazes at
Gaura, who sits in the middle of the courtyard among His dear associates; Malini floats in the ocean of His beauty. Raga vibhasa.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^19-26]

**14.1.** Srivasa's wife, virtuous, like tenderness itself in bodily form,
always modest, chaste, devoted to her husband — there is none like her in the world.

**14.2.** Her whole matchless body has blossomed with joy; half covering her face with the hem of her cloth,
she stands beside Sita and cannot take her eyes off [Him], rejoicing at heart.

**14.3.** In the middle of the courtyard, surrounded by His dear associates, sits Gora;
His beautiful moonlike face flashes, and His body is like gold.

**14.4.** What can I say of all these ever-new [wonders]? Malini floats in the ocean of that beauty.[^19-27]
May Narahari Dasa die warding off misfortune from this wondrous love!

[^19-26]: GPT1 — pp. 69–70, no. 25 (vibhasa; scan, PDF pp. 328–329); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 25 (catalogue: NG-013, wrongly as no. 15). GCC —
chapter 6, pada 3 (the editor of the GCC marked the name "mālyānī" with a question mark). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the
Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^19-27]: Malini (mālyāni = mālinī) — the wife of Srivasa Pandita, in Krishna-lila the nurse Ambika (Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika); in Navadvipa she
cared for the Lord with motherly love.

## 15. Narahari — "rajanī-prabhāte śacīdevī cite…" (GPT1 p. 70, no. 26; GCC)
*At dawn Shachi, weeping with joy, clasps Sita's feet and begs: "Be gracious to Nimai, bless Him with a long life; this child is the
apple of my eye; let Him stay at home and give up His restlessness; after Vishvarupa He is my life — let there be no separation."
Yatharaga. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^19-28]

**15.1.** At dawn there is no end to the joy in the heart of Shachi-devi;
gazing at that face, she cannot restrain herself — tears flow from her eyes.

**15.2.** Clasping Sita's feet, she earnestly speaks sweet words:
"All my hope is in you, O revered one: I do not know what is good and what is bad.

**15.3.** Regarding Nimaichand as your own, be always gracious to Him;
give such a blessing that He may live long and happily.

**15.4.** I have no one — what more shall I ask? — this child is the apple of my eye;
make it so that He always stays at home, giving up His restless ways.

**15.5.** And I say more: [Vishvarupa is gone] — now this Nimai is my life and soul;
give me this boon: that there be not half a moment of separation."[^19-29]

**15.6.** Having said much more like this, she quickly performs auspicious rites.
What can Narahari tell with one mouth of the incomparable love of the mother?

[^19-28]: GPT1 — p. 70, no. 26 (yatharaga; scan, PDF p. 329); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 26. The catalogue did not know it (new row NG-268). GCC —
chapter 6, pada 4 (GCC scan, p. 60). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. Shachi's fear that her younger son too will
leave home like Vishvarupa — CB Adi 7.
[^19-29]: Vishvarupa, the Lord's elder brother, took sannyasa and left home (CB Adi 7; CC Adi 15). In the GCC the line reads differently:
"…Vishvarupa — this is my Nitai, my life and soul" (nitāi instead of nimāi) — Shachi sees her elder son in Nityananda (cf. Shachi's
dream of her two sons, Krishna and Balarama — CB Madhya 8; cf. GPT no. 40, where Nitai loves Nimai as Balarama loved Krishna).
Translated according to the GPT.

## 16. Narahari — "śacīra ālaya ālo haiyāche…" (GPT1 p. 70, no. 27; GCC)
*The elderly women of Navadvipa stand in Shachi's courtyard and gaze at Nimai; each prays for Him: one gives Him all her merit, others
will worship Shiva, the Ganga, Chandi, Lakshmi — that He may live long, not leave Nadia, never go abroad to earn money, and be rich;
their love for Him is stronger than for their own sons; "may we see this boy in Nadia birth after birth". Yatharaga. **Attribution:
probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^19-30]

**16.1.** Shachi's house is full of light — what can I say of such happiness!
The elderly women stand there and gaze, rejoicing at heart.

**16.2.** One says: "Ah, the lamp of the family, Nimai, the treasury of virtues,
has come and appeared to make our eyes fruitful."

**16.3.** Another says: "Ah, may Shachi's son always be well!
I have given Him all my merit — may He escape many thorns."

**16.4.** Another says: "Ah, for His sake I shall worship the Lord of Kailasa,
that He may live long and stay like this in Nadia."

**16.5.** Another says: "Ah, every day I shall worship the Ganga and ask for a boon:
may Shachi's darling live joyfully in His own home with His own people."[^19-31]

**16.6.** Another says: "Worshipping Chandi, I shall ask for what is in my heart:
may He never go abroad to earn money."

**16.7.** Another says: "Ah, I worship Lakshmi, and there is a reason for it:
may He become very rich without effort and never know want."

**16.8.** Another says: "Ah, and listen to this too — I do not understand what goes on in my heart:
a love arises for Him a hundred times stronger than for my own son."

**16.9.** Another says: "Ah, I leave my house and come here for His sake —
and I do not know how my soul endures it when I must leave even for a moment."

**16.10.** Another says: "Ah, fortunate Shachi performed many pious deeds —
that is why she obtained this Moon of Nadia, the treasure of life for all."

**16.11.** Another says: "Ah, say what you will, I ask only this of the Creator:
that birth after birth I may see this boy in Nadia."

**16.12.** Thus, seized by love, they speak without end.
Narahari says: have I the power to tell of the love of them all?

[^19-30]: GPT1 — pp. 70–71, no. 27 (yatharaga; scan, PDF pp. 329–330); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 27. The catalogue did not know it (new row
NG-269). GCC — chapter 6, pada 5. Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. On the prayers to the gods for the Lord — note 12:
this is vatsalya, not independent worship of the demigods; Chandi is the goddess Durga. Lakshmi, to whom the woman prays, is in
Gaura-lila His eternal consort Herself (Lakshmipriya).
[^19-31]: An unwitting sadness which the poet puts into these wishes: the Lord would later go "abroad" — to East Bengal (CB Adi 14; CC Adi 16) — and
would take sannyasa, leaving home (CB Madhya 26–28).

## 17. Narahari — "āju ki ānanda śrīśacī-bhavane…" (GPT1 p. 71, no. 28; GCC)
*Dawn in Shachi's house: Vishvambhara sits among His dear associates and gives happiness to each in his own bhava; the old men and women,
faint with tenderness, weep as they gaze at His face and tell one another of His deeds. Yatharaga. **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^19-32]

**17.1.** What joy there is today in the house of Sri Shachi at the end of the night!
Among His dear associates Vishvambhara shines in a charming pose.

**17.2.** Whatever one's bhava, in that bhava He responds, and He makes everyone happy;[^19-33]
never have I seen such an artist, a jewel of qualities, enchanting the world.

**17.3.** All the old men and women are faint under the weight of tenderness;
gazing and gazing at that moonlike face, no one can keep his composure.

**17.4.** Tears flow unceasingly from their eyes, bliss is in the depths of their hearts;
and again they tell one another the deeds of Gauranga, the life of Narahari.

[^19-32]: GPT1 — p. 71, no. 28 (yatharaga; scan, PDF p. 330); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 28 (catalogue: NG-014). GCC — chapter 6, pada 6 ("vṛddha
naranārī"). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^19-33]: Cf. Bhagavad-gita 4.11: "As they surrender to Me, so I reciprocate with them" — the Lord responds to each in his own rasa.

## 18. Narahari — "nadīyāra ati puṇyavatī pativratā-gaṇera…" (GPT1 p. 71, no. 29; BR)
*The pious married women of Nadia think more of Shachi's son than of their own sons: as soon as the night ends, they go to Him with trays
of gifts, see Him playing on His mother's lap, take Him in their arms and forget themselves. Raga vibhasa. **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave).*[^19-34]

**18.1.** What a disposition of heart the pious women of Nadia, devoted to their husbands, have!
Their thoughts are not on their own sons — ceaselessly they speak of the deeds and ways of Shachi's son.

**18.2.** Seeing that the night is ending, they disregard their beds — they cannot hold back even for half a moment;
filling trays with various delicacies, in rows they carry them to the Moon of Nadia.

**18.3.** As soon as they enter Shachi's house, an ocean of joy surges in their hearts;
they all see: on His mother's lap sits Gora, the Moon of Gokula, playing.

**18.4.** Their eyes are soothed, and the women's souls — taking Him in their arms, they forget their bodies.
Narahari says: ah, ah, how beautifully this love was fashioned!

[^19-34]: GPT1 — p. 71, no. 29 (vibhasa; scan, PDF p. 330); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 29. The catalogue did not know it (new row NG-270). BR —
12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 771; ed. 1960, vv. 1000–1003): Ishana says that the women of Navadvipa used to come here at dawn to see
Gaurachandra, and quotes the pada (immediately after no. 3). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the GCC. B. This is love in
vatsalya (the women are mothers, the Lord an infant in Shachi's arms), not the nagari motif.

## 19. Narahari — "śuna śuna prāṇasakhi tomāre valiye go…" (GPT1 p. 72, no. 30; GCC)
*A woman of Navadvipa says to her friend: "Blessed is life in Nadia: in Treta there was Kaushalya, in Dvapara Yashoda, in Kali fortunate
Shachi; blessed is Jagannatha Mishra; Shachi is like the Mother of the world: who else could have borne so many childish pranks? Some god
has shown mercy — now Nimai has become good, but He was a dreadful scamp." Yatharaga. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada
is in the GCC.*[^19-35]

**19.1.** "Listen, listen, dear friend, I tell you: blessed is life in this Nadia!
In the Treta-yuga there was queen Kaushalya, in the Dvapara Yashoda, and in the Kali-yuga fortunate Shachi.[^19-36]

**19.2.** Blessed is Jagannatha Mishra, known to all the world — there is no limit to his holy merit;
and his wife, devoted to her husband and full of tenderness — she who has such a son, Nimai.

**19.3.** Truly I would call her the Mother of the world: who else has such a nature?
Who could bear so many childish pranks? There is none like her in the world.

**19.4.** I do not know what god has shown mercy — that is why all is well now;
otherwise, you know, Nimai, the life of Narahari, was a dreadful scamp."

[^19-35]: GPT1 — p. 72, no. 30 (yatharaga; scan, PDF p. 331); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 30. The catalogue did not know it (new row NG-271; the
first line in catalogue row NG-015 had mixed it with no. 31). GCC — chapter 6, pada 7, marked "a certain [woman] says" (kācidāha). Not in
the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. The words "now all is well, but He was a scamp" show the GCC frame: the women recall the
childhood of Gaura, who is already a youth (cf. note 8).
[^19-36]: Kaushalya — the mother of Rama; Yashoda — the mother of Krishna in Vraja; Shachi — the mother of Gaura in the Kali-yuga.
Chakravarti places her in the line of the Lord's eternal mothers.

## 20. Narahari — "nimāicām̐dera kathā tomāre valiye go…" (GPT1 p. 72, no. 31; GCC)
*Another recalls: "Nimai is the chief of scamps: born on the full moon of Phalguna during an eclipse, He cried wildly and would not take
the breast; only the great ascetic of Shantipur, who knows the nature of this child, by some trick got Him to suck. I do not fear what
people say: from His very birth He has been a great scamp." Yatharaga. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the
GCC.*[^19-37]

**20.1.** "I'll tell you about Nimaichand: Nimai is the chief of scamps;
such obstinacy I have never seen anywhere else — truly blessed are His father and mother!

**20.2.** On the full moon of Phalguna, at the time of the eclipse, having been born, He cried wildly;[^19-38]
however they tried, the child would not take the breast; seeing this, everyone was frightened.

**20.3.** The resident of Shantipur, the great ascetic Gosani, who knows the nature of this child —
I do not know by what trick He got Him to suck the breast — and everyone calmed down.[^19-39]

**20.4.** Let them say what they like — I am not afraid, I have judged it so in my heart:
the treasure of Narahari's life will be a great scamp — it began from His very birth."

[^19-37]: GPT1 — p. 72, no. 31 (yatharaga; scan, PDF p. 331); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 31 (catalogue: NG-015). GCC — chapter 6, pada 8, marked
"and another [says]" (anyā ca). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^19-38]: "Having been born" — the author's word; the Lord is not born as conditioned souls are: by His own will He appears from the womb of
Shachi, as Krishna from the womb of Devaki (Bhag. 10.3; CC Adi 13). His appearance on the full moon of the month of Phalguna during a
lunar eclipse, when everyone was chanting the name of Hari — CC Adi 13; CB Adi 3.
[^19-39]: "The great ascetic of Shantipur" — Advaita Acharya. According to the Advaita-prakasha, the newborn would not take the breast until
He heard the holy name; in Chakravarti, Advaita calms the Child "by some means". The Infant's crying stilled by the name of Hari — CC Adi
13, 14; CB Adi 4.

## 21. Narahari — "parāṇa nimāi mora khepā vaṛa vaṭe go…" (GPT1 p. 72, no. 32; GCC)
*A woman recalls: little Nimai, all covered in dust, was crawling about the courtyard, called His mother, climbed into her arms and
suddenly burst into inconsolable sobs, struggled, and no one could calm Him; one woman in despair clapped her hands and said "Hari" — and
at once He fell silent, laughed and hugged her neck; all sang "Hari, Hari", and He, not yet able to stand, danced holding His mother's
hand. Yatharaga. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^19-40]

**21.1.** "Nimai, my life, is a great scamp, it's true: one day I saw with my own eyes:
His wondrous little body all grey with dust, He was crawling on all fours about the courtyard.

**21.2.** With a smile on His beautiful moonlike face He called: 'Mama!' — and at once Shachi came running;
having climbed into her arms, He suddenly burst into inconsolable sobs — seeing it, one's heart broke.

**21.3.** However she tried, He would not be soothed — again and again He threw Himself about;
'What has happened, what has happened?' — the pious lady wept; no one could stay calm.

**21.4.** Just then a woman in despair clapped her hands and said: 'Hari!'
Hearing this, the restless child stopped crying and, laughing, hugged her neck.

**21.5.** All rejoiced and sang: 'Hari, Hari!' — and Nimai climbed down from her arms;
He could not yet stand, but, holding His mother's hand, He danced merrily.

**21.6.** Why He had cried, no one understood — everyone just wondered to themselves.
That is how Nimai, the life of Narahari, knows how to play His pranks."[^19-41]

[^19-40]: GPT1 — pp. 72–73, no. 32 (yatharaga; scan, PDF pp. 331–332); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 32 (catalogue: NG-016). GCC — chapter 6, pada 9.
Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. The same pada is printed in the GPT a second time — p. 76, no. 42, raga vibhasa
(catalogue: NG-023), in a shortened and altered form: without the episode of the name of Hari (lines 21.3b–21.4a are merged into one:
"however she tried, He would not be soothed — laughing, He hugged her neck"), with an added line "all the townspeople were enchanted,
seeing that wondrous form" and the ending "…knows how to play"; the variants are in the VAR, and it is not translated separately. The
Infant's crying stilled by the name of Hari — CC Adi 14; CB Adi 4 (the Lord cries, and the women, clapping their hands, sing "Hari").
[^19-41]: "Play His pranks" (khepāmi) — on the lips of those who love Him this is an affectionate word; the meaning of the lila, according to
the CB and CC: the Lord cries so that everyone will sing the name of Hari.

## 22. Narahari — "nimāi cañcala khepā kichui nā māne go…" (GPT1 p. 73, no. 33; GCC)
*A woman recalls: holding the hem of His mother's cloth, the little one was walking about the courtyard, saw His shadow and began to play
with it, and there lay a snake — He lay down on its terrible hood; all ran up in horror, the snake tried to slip away, and He caught it
again; Shachi carried Him off in her arms; then a bird flew by — "Catch it for Me!" — and He wept bitterly until He Himself forgot it.
Yatharaga. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^19-42]

**22.1.** "Nimai is restless and a scamp, He heeds nothing; listen to what happened one day:
holding the hem of His mother's cloth, He was walking about the courtyard — and saw His own shadow there.

**22.2.** Letting go of the hem, He began to play with His shadow, and there was a snake;
lying down on its terrible hood — what bliss! — He feared nothing at all.[^19-43]

**22.3.** Crying 'Alas, alas!' all came running; the snake tried to slip away, and He caught it again;
everyone trembled, and Shachi in distress carefully took Him up in her arms.

**22.4.** Just then a bird flew past — how charmingly He looked at it!
'Catch it for Me!' He said again and again, and wept, His arms around His mother's neck.

**22.5.** From His eyes, two streams like a necklace of sapphires: the kohl was washed away;
that moonlike little face grew dim — can one bear to look at it?

**22.6.** Whatever anyone said — He would not yield to anyone's words; one's heart broke hearing His crying;
and then the child, the life of Narahari, forgot it Himself, and His heart grew calm."

[^19-42]: GPT1 — p. 73, no. 33 (yatharaga; scan, PDF p. 332); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 33. The catalogue did not know it (new row NG-272). GCC —
chapter 6, pada 10. Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^19-43]: The snake in the courtyard of Mishra's house, on whose coils the crawling Infant lay down — CB Adi 4; BR 12 (ed. 1960, vv. 982–983):
"that is why Ananta-deva passed along this road". It is Ananta-Shesha, the Lord's couch, come to serve Him; that is why the Child knows no
fear.

## 23. Narahari — "soṇāra nimāi mora parāṇa-putali go…" (GPT1 p. 73, no. 34; GCC)
*A woman recalls: if Nimai is not given what He wants — there is trouble; once, holding His mother's hem, He cried and begged for butter
and rolled in the dust; Shachi brought butter from somewhere, He ate it and said: "I am a cowherd's son, nothing but this pleases Me";
when they laughingly asked Him: "Which cowherd's, then?" — He ran away, and Shachi said in embarrassment: "Well, well." Yatharaga.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^19-44]

**23.1.** "Golden Nimai, the doll of my soul — are there such games anywhere in the world!
Whatever He wants — if it is not given, there is trouble: no one can soothe Him.

**23.2.** One day Nimai, holding the hem of His mother's cloth, was crying: 'Give Me butter!'
The more they tried to soothe Him, the more He rolled in the dust — He could not calm down for a moment.

**23.3.** I do not know where His mother brought butter from, but she put it in Nimai's hands;
having eaten the butter, He says: 'I am a cowherd's son; nothing but this pleases Me.'[^19-45]

**23.4.** Looking into His face, we laughed and asked: 'Which cowherd's little son are You, then?'
Hearing this, the child — the life of Narahari — ran away, and Shachi said in embarrassment: 'Well, well!'"

[^19-44]: GPT1 — p. 73, no. 34 (yatharaga; scan, PDF p. 332); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 34 (catalogue: NG-017). GCC — chapter 6, pada 11. Not in
the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^19-45]: The Lord lets slip the truth about Himself: He is Krishna, the son of the cowherd Nanda, who loves butter (cf. no. 10 and note 20).
Shachi is embarrassed: a brahmana's son calls himself the son of a cowherd; by the will of yogamaya her motherly love does not let her
reflect on these words.

## 24. Narahari — "ekadina nirjane nimāi ghare vule go…" (GPT1 p. 73, no. 35)
*Three wonders of childhood: Shachi sees in the house footprints with the marks of a flag, a vajra and a goad — Mishra says these are the
footprints of their household Deity Gopala; another day Shachi hears the sound of a flute and the name "Radha" pouring from Nimai's
mouth; a third time two thieves carry Nimai off for His ornaments, but, deluded, return to Shachi's house, leave Him and flee. Yatharaga.
**Attribution: not established** — the pada is neither in the GCC (although it stands in the middle of its cycle) nor in the BR or other
witnesses; the metre is uneven, the refrain "go" is placed carelessly — perhaps a later imitation of the cycle.*[^19-46]

**24.1.** One day, when Nimai was wandering alone about the house, Shachi saw wondrous footprints;
very secretly, calling Mishra Purandara into the house, she shows him these footprints.

**24.2.** Mishra sees in the footprints a flag, a vajra, a goad and other marks; the best of the Mishras ponders within himself
and secretly says to Shachi: "These are the footprints of our household Deity Gopala."[^19-47]

**24.3.** Another day Shachi hears: from Nimai's mouth pours the sound of a flute,
and in it the words "Radha, Radha"; seeing such play, Shachi fell silent from fear.[^19-48]

**24.4.** Another day two thieves, coveting His ornaments, carried Nimai off;
"Nimai, Nimai!" Shachi calls aloud and weeps; they search for Him everywhere.

**24.5.** Meanwhile the two thieves, bewildered by some illusion, taking Shachi's house for their own, came back there,
set the child down from their shoulders onto the ground and hastily ran away.[^19-49]

**24.6.** Having regained their lost treasure, all rejoiced, but could understand nothing;
seeing the plight of the thieves, Narahari began to smile slyly.

[^19-46]: GPT1 — pp. 73–74, no. 35 (yatharaga; scan, PDF pp. 332–333); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 35. The catalogue did not know it (new row
NG-273). It is not in the GCC: in chapter 6 the pada "soṇāra nimāi" (no. 23) is followed immediately by "śunaye nimāira kathā" (no. 25). Not in
the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. C. The pada retells all three episodes closely following the Chaitanya-bhagavata (Adi 4–5).
[^19-47]: Footprints with the marks of a flag (dhvaja), a vajra (thunderbolt) and a goad (ankusha) — the marks on the soles of Bhagavan. In CB
Adi 4, Jagannatha Mishra and Shachi, seeing these footprints, decided that their household Bala-Gopala had walked about the house, and
worshipped Him.
[^19-48]: The sound of the flute and the name of Radha in the child's mouth are signs that Gaura is Krishna Himself and His heart is full of
Radha; Shachi, out of motherly love, is frightened, without reflecting on her son's majesty. This episode is not in the CB.
[^19-49]: "Bewildered by an illusion" (ki bhule bhuli) — according to CB Adi 4, the thieves were confused by the Lord's power (vishnu-maya)
and, wandering, came back to the house of Jagannatha Mishra. The Lord Himself is not subject to it: it is His energy, which He directs for
the sake of His lila.

## 25. Narahari — "śunaye nimāira kathā ekadina sukhe go…" (GPT1 p. 74, no. 36; GCC)
*Shachi, so that Nimai may become calmer, worships a god with offerings; Nimai runs up from somewhere, eats the offering and laughingly
says: "I am the God of gods, why do you not worship Me?" Shachi chases Him in fear, afraid that something may happen to her son, and He,
sitting on His father's lap, complains: "Mother won't give Me anything to eat"; the father rejoices. Yatharaga. **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^19-50]

**25.1.** Listen to this about Nimai: one day Shachi-ma joyfully, with various offerings,
so that restless Nimai might become good, was diligently worshipping a deity.

**25.2.** Just then He, running in from somewhere — no one even noticed — ate the offering
and, laughing, says: "I am the God of gods; why do you not worship Me?"[^19-51]

**25.3.** Crying "Alas, alas!" Shachi chases Him, a great fear in her heart;
in distress she thinks: "What if something happens to Nimai!"

**25.4.** And meanwhile the child, sitting on Mishra's lap, says: "Mother won't give Me anything to eat."
Hearing the words of Nimai, the life of Narahari, the father feels great joy in his heart.

[^19-50]: GPT1 — p. 74, no. 36 (yatharaga; scan, PDF p. 333); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 36 (catalogue: NG-018). GCC — chapter 6, pada 12. Not in
the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^19-51]: Cf. Lochana Dasa: Nimai eats the offering to the goddess Shashthi and tells His mother that worship of Him, like watering the root,
satisfies all the gods (Chaitanya-mangala, Adi-khanda; Bhag. 4.31.14). The Lord is the God of gods, and all the demigods are His
servants; here He reveals this in jest, and Shachi out of love fears only for Him.

## 26. Narahari — "e mora nimāicām̐da khāite cāhile go…" (GPT1 p. 74, no. 37; GCC)
*A woman tells: let Nimai ask for food and you delay a moment — in anger He smashes the house and spoils everything; scold Him — it gets
twice as bad; He fears neither father nor mother, the neighbours cannot restrain Him, He fears only Vishvarupa; He roams Nadia alone,
gets into other people's houses and everywhere makes the children cry. Yatharaga. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in
the GCC.*[^19-52]

**26.1.** "This Nimaichand of mine — if He asks for food and you delay even a moment,
in great anger He smashes the house and the doors, spoils and scatters everything.

**26.2.** Say anything to Him — He plays up twice as much; He fears neither father nor mother;
none of the neighbours can restrain Him — He fears only Vishvarupa.[^19-53]

**26.3.** I have never seen such a boy anywhere: He wanders alone through Nadia,
slips unnoticed into anybody's house and playfully gets up to all sorts of things.

**26.4.** Wherever He goes, He makes the children cry — what can their mothers say?
At the doings of Vishvambhara, the life of Narahari, who in Nadia does not tremble?"

[^19-52]: GPT1 — p. 74, no. 37 (yatharaga; scan, PDF p. 333); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 37 (catalogue: NG-019). GCC — chapter 6, pada 13. Not in
the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. Nimai's childhood pranks in Navadvipa and the neighbours' complaints — CB Adi 6; CC Adi 14.
[^19-53]: His elder brother Vishvarupa (see note 29); according to CB Adi 7, Nimai loved and obeyed him.

## 27. Narahari — "ekadina nimāi praveśi gṛhamājhe go…" (GPT1 p. 74, no. 38)
*Nimai mixed together in the house rice, dal, salt, oil, yogurt, milk, butter and ghee; His mother ran after Him with a stick, and He sat
down on a heap of discarded pots; "Fie, get down, it is impure!" — "How can a pot in which bhoga was cooked for Vishnu be impure? The
impurity is in your mind"; the astonished mother bathed Him and took Him in her arms: "This child is not a child, but Hari of
Vaikuntha." Yatharaga. **Attribution: not established** — the pada is neither in the GCC (although it stands in the middle of its
cycle) nor in the BR or other witnesses; the metre is uneven, the refrain "go" drops out — perhaps a later imitation.*[^19-54]

**27.1.** One day Nimai got into the house and made a great deal of mischief:
He mixed together rice, dal, salt, oil, yogurt, milk, butter and ghee.

**27.2.** Unable to bear His wildness, His mother, a stick in one hand,
ran after Nimai, and the child raced ahead of her.

**27.3.** Where a heap of discarded pots lay, there Nimai sat down on top;
Shachi says: "Fie, fie, my son, leave that impurity, come here — I'll bathe You and take You home."[^19-55]

**27.4.** The child replies: "A pot in which bhoga was cooked for Vishnu — how can it be impure?
The impurity is in your mind; I see everything as pure; tell Me, Mother, what in the world is impure?"[^19-56]

**27.5.** Hearing words of truth from the child's mouth, the mother was amazed, bathed Him and took Him in her arms.
"This child is no child: your son is Hari who dwells in Vaikuntha," says Narahari.

[^19-54]: GPT1 — pp. 74–75, no. 38 (yatharaga; scan, PDF pp. 333–334); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 38 (catalogue: NG-020). It is not in the GCC:
there the pada "e mora nimāicām̐da" (no. 26) is followed immediately by "nimāicām̐dera e carita" (no. 28). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the
Gita-chandrodaya. C.
[^19-55]: Earthen pots in which food had once been cooked were thrown away as ritually impure; cf. CB Adi 6, CC Adi 14.
[^19-56]: Cf. CC Adi 14 (the Lord, sitting on the discarded pots, answers His mother; Krishnadasa Kaviraja explains that in these words He
playfully speaks like Dattatreya) and CB Adi 6; Murari 1.6. The meaning is not that the distinction between pure and impure is altogether
illusory: the Lord is Vishnu Himself, everything connected with service to Him is pure, and He Himself is defiled by nothing.

## 28. Narahari — "nimāicām̐dera e carita kata kava go…" (GPT1 p. 75, no. 39; GCC)
*At bathing time on the bank of the Suradhuni Nimai gives neither men nor women any peace and quarrels with those carrying offerings to the
gods; but when they complain of Him to Shachi and Mishra, He is virtue itself; all marvel: as Kanu was in the house of Nanda, so is He in
the house of Shachi — it must be He. Yatharaga. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^19-57]

**28.1.** "How much can I tell of such doings of Nimaichand! At bathing time on the bank of the Suradhuni
neither women nor men can find any peace — such havoc He wreaks there.

**28.2.** Whoever goes with offerings, carefully carrying them to worship a deity —
with all of them He quarrels without number: what does He not do in Nadia!

**28.3.** But if someone complains to Shachi and Mishra — then what good manners He has!
Everyone's merriment grows: seeing Him, one loses one's wits.[^19-58]

**28.4.** Such as were the pranks of Kanu in the house of Nanda, such I see in the house of Shachi;
Nimai, the life of Narahari — it must be He Himself: otherwise who would act like this?"[^19-59]

[^19-57]: GPT1 — p. 75, no. 39 (yatharaga; scan, PDF p. 334); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 39. The catalogue did not know it (new row NG-274). GCC —
chapter 6, pada 14. Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. Nimai's pranks on the ghats of the Ganga, the complaints of the
brahmanas and the girls to Jagannatha Mishra, and Nimai's instant "good manners" — CB Adi 6.
[^19-58]: According to CB Adi 6, when Mishra angrily went after his son to the Ganga, Nimai was already waiting at home — clean, without a
trace of water or sand — and the accusers did not know what to say.
[^19-59]: Kanu is Krishna; the poet sees in Nimai's childhood pranks the pranks of Krishna in Vraja: Gaura is Krishna Himself (cf. note 20).

# Chapter 20. Appendix. Padas signed "Narahari" from the Gaura-pada-tarangini — IV: the appearance of Gaura, the end of childhood, the samskaras and the betrothal

*Continuation of the appendix (the introductory note on the two Naraharis, on the arguments for attribution and on the marks in the
headings is in ch. 17). Chapter 20: a pada surveying Gaura's lila from the section "aishvarya and madhurya" (GPT 1.3); padas on the
appearance of the Lord (section 2.1); the last padas of the section "Balya-lila" (2.2); the beginning of the section "Karnavedha and the
wedding" (2.3) — the first tonsure and ear-piercing, the upanayana, the first meeting with Lakshmipriya by the Ganga, the news of the
wedding and the adhivasa (the wedding day follows in the next chapter). Almost all the padas of the chapter are quoted by Narahari
Chakravarti in the 12th wave of the Bhakti-ratnakara, where Ishana shows Srinivasa the house of Jagannatha Mishra and tells what happened
there (two are in Chakravarti's Gaura-charita-chintamani); one pada (no. 12) has not been found in any witness. According to Majumdar, the
padas on the birth and childhood of Nimai known under the name "Narahari" are late: Narahari Sarakara did not see the Lord's childhood.
Before translation the "Narahari" signatures in sections 1.3 and 2.1–2.3 were checked throughout in GPT1: the catalogue had missed five more
padas of section 2.3 (here nos. 13 and 15, new rows NG-280, 281; NG-282…284 follow in the next chapter). The base text is GPT1 (doubtful places from the scan), collated with GPT2, the
BR (eds. 1912 and 1960) and the Gaura-charita-chintamani (ed. 1947); PK, KGC, PS and the Gita-chandrodaya have been checked. On the "birth" of
the Lord see note 4; on the childhood games as lila, note 2 of chapter 19; on the samskaras, note 26. The notes of the GPT editors are not
reproduced.*

## 1. Narahari — "śacīsuta gaurahari…" (GPT1 p. 26, section 1.3, no. 2; BR)
*A survey of the lila: the son of Shachi appeared in Navadvipa and revealed sankirtana; He took sannyasa, remained in Nilachala and,
intoxicated with Radhika's love, intoxicated the world with it; His associates are beside themselves with prema; the treasure unattainable
even for the gods He gave to the world. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave).*[^20-1]

**1.1.** The son of Shachi, Gaurahari, having descended in Navadvipa, displayed manifold pastimes:
together with His dear associates He revealed sankirtana and increased the joy of all.

**1.2.** And then, in the dress of a sannyasi, the Lord wandered from land to land and, coming to Nilachala, remained there;
intoxicated with Radhika's love, knowing neither day nor night, He intoxicated the whole world with that love.[^20-2]

**1.3.** Nityananda who is Balarama, Advaita the abode of virtues, Gadadhara, Srivasa and all the rest,
seeing this wondrous way, cannot keep their composure — ceaselessly overwhelmed with prema.

**1.4.** The treasure unattainable even for the gods He has, with effort, bestowed [on us] — may I die warding off all ill from such mercy!
The Lord Krishna-Chaitanya has blessed the age of Kali — Narahari Dasa sings His glory.

[^20-1]: GPT1 — p. 26, section 1.3 ("aishvarya and madhurya of the Gaura-avatara"), no. 2 (kamoda; scan, PDF p. 285); GPT2 — section 1.3, no. 2
(catalogue: NG-003). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 914; ed. 1960, vv. 3605–3608): Ishana, having told Srinivasa of the Lord's departure from
Navadvipa to Puri, quotes this pada as a brief survey of His whole lila. Variant: the BR has "vilāilā" — "distributed", the GPT "milāilā" —
"procured, bestowed". Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
[^20-2]: In Puri the Lord is absorbed in the bhava of Radha longing for Krishna: it was to taste Her love that He appeared (CC Adi 4; Antya 14–20).
Nityananda is Balarama Himself (1.3; CC Adi 5).

## 2. Narahari — "phālguna-pūrṇimā śubhakṣaṇe…" (GPT1 p. 59, section 2.1, no. 19; BR)
*In the auspicious hour of the full moon of Phalguna Shachi, having given birth to a son, cannot gaze at Him enough; Jagannatha Mishra,
hearing the news, floats in an ocean of happiness and performs the rites; the Ganga and the Earth forget their sorrows; with the rising
of Gaurachandra the darkness of sin departs. Raga vasanta. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave).*[^20-3]

**2.1.** In the auspicious hour of the full moon of Phalguna Shachi, having given birth to a son, cannot take her eyes from Him.[^20-4]

**2.2.** How many feelings rise in her heart at every moment! As if He were golden fresh butter, she dares not touch Him.

**2.3.** With what care she takes Him on her lap and sends word of the son's birth to the best of the Mishras.

**2.4.** Jagannatha, the crown of brahmanas, hearing of the birth of his son, floats in an ocean of happiness.

**2.5.** With what joy he hastens [to the son] — and, seeing the moonlike face, cannot contain himself.

**2.6.** Gathering his dear ones, he performs auspicious rites for the welfare of the son.

**2.7.** On all sides sounds "jaya, jaya"; all say: "Blessed, blessed are the father and the mother!"

**2.8.** Happiness grows in everyone's heart; the Suradhuni and the Earth forget all their sorrows.[^20-5]

**2.9.** All ten directions have become bright; beasts, birds, trees and creepers — all have blossomed.

**2.10.** What more can Narahari say? With the rising of Gaurachandra the darkness of sin has gone.

[^20-3]: GPT1 — p. 59, section 2.1 ("the appearance"), no. 19 (vasanta; scan, PDF p. 318); GPT2 — section 2.1, no. 19. The catalogue did not know it
(new row NG-276). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 764; ed. 1960, vv. 907–916): Ishana, showing Srinivasa the place of the Lord's appearance in
the house of Jagannatha Mishra, quotes padas of Vasu Ghosha and Vrindavana Dasa on the birth and then — in a row — this one and the next four
(nos. 3–5; between them a pada signed by Ghanashyama, GPT 2.1 no. 23, outside the appendix) and no. 6. Variant in the last line: the BR has
"the darkness of suffering" (tāpa), the GPT "the darkness of sin" (pāpa). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
The GPT1 footnotes to lines 2.8–2.9 (editor's notes) are not reproduced.
[^20-4]: The poet speaks in the language of the lila: "gave birth to a son", "birth". But the Lord is not born as a conditioned soul is, by karma and
in a material body: He appears (avirbhava) by His own will in His eternal form — as Krishna appeared before Devaki (Bhag. 10.3; Gita 4.6, 4.9;
CC Adi 13–14). So the appearance of the Lord is understood by Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja and Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati; so too are all the
padas on the "birth" in this chapter to be understood.
[^20-5]: The Suradhuni ("the river of the gods") is the Ganga. The poet says that with the appearance of the Lord both the Ganga and the Earth,
burdened with the sins of the age of Kali, forgot their sorrows: on the banks of the Ganga He will perform His pastimes, and the sins of the world
will depart.

## 3. Narahari — "phālguna-pūrṇimā maṅgalera sīmā…" (GPT1 pp. 59–60, no. 20; BR)
*The full moon of Phalguna: the Moon of Gokula has appeared, in every house of Nadia there is an ocean of joy; Shachi with her son on her lap
in the birth-chamber; in the darkness of the eclipse crowds run to see the Child and forget themselves. Raga not stated (in the BR —
dhanashi). **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^20-6]

**3.1.** The full moon of Phalguna — the summit of all blessings: the Moon of Gokula has appeared!
In the town of Nadia, in every house, an ocean of joy surges.

**3.2.** What merriment among them all!
Shachi-devi, taking her son on her lap, shines in the birth-chamber.

**3.3.** To see the Child they run from all sides — no one can restrain himself;
in the darkness of the eclipse who can tell who is who? There is no counting the people coming.[^20-7]

**3.4.** Gazing their fill at the sweetness of the Child, they forget their own bodies.
Narahari says: the son of Shachi reveals some new love!

[^20-6]: GPT1 — pp. 59–60, no. 20 (no raga; scan, PDF pp. 318–319); GPT2 — section 2.1, no. 20. The catalogue did not know it (new row NG-277). BR —
12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 764–765; ed. 1960, vv. 917–920, "punardhānaśī"). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
Line 3.2 is the refrain (dhru).
[^20-7]: The Lord appeared in the evening of the full moon of Phalguna, during a lunar eclipse, when by custom everyone was bathing in the Ganga and
repeating the name of Hari (CC Adi 13; CB Adi 2–3; Murari 1.5). "The Moon of Gokula" is Krishna: Gaura is Krishna Himself, the Lord of Gokula.

## 4. Narahari — "parama śubha śacīgarbhe…" (GPT1 p. 60, no. 21; BR)
*Gaura, the Lord of Gokula, in the womb of Shachi; the gods praise Him; on the night of the full moon, when Rahu had swallowed the moon, the
Lord appeared, having first revealed His name; those entering Mishra's house, seeing the Child, lose their senses; the pride of Kali is
crushed. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR; Vrajabuli.*[^20-8]

**4.1.** In the womb of Shachi, in the supremely auspicious hour, abides Gaura — the Lord of Gokula;
again and again the gods offer praises and bow down; the house brims with jubilation.

**4.2.** On the auspicious night of the Phalguna full moon, when Rahu had swallowed the rising moon —
at such an hour the Lord appeared, having first revealed His name.[^20-9]

**4.3.** "Jaya, jaya" resounds through the whole world, no one can restrain himself;
those entering Mishra's house, beholding the Child, go mad with happiness.

**4.4.** They perform various auspicious rites, ever new; all desires are fulfilled.
Narahari says: the pride of mighty Kali is crushed.

[^20-8]: GPT1 — p. 60, no. 21 (kamoda; scan, PDF p. 319); GPT2 — section 2.1, no. 21. The catalogue did not know it (new row NG-278). BR — 12th wave
(ed. 1912, p. 765; ed. 1960, vv. 921–924). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. "In the womb of Shachi" —
on the appearance of the Lord see note 4.
[^20-9]: During the eclipse all the people of Nadia, bathing, were repeating "Hari, Hari" — thus the Lord, before appearing, made the whole world sing
His name (CC Adi 13). Rahu — according to the Puranas, the demon who swallows the moon at an eclipse.

## 5. Narahari — "jaya jaya jaya maṅgalarava…" (GPT1 pp. 60–61, no. 22; BR)
*The night of the Phalguna full moon: from the womb of Shachi Gaura, the delight of Vraja, has appeared; His body flashes like steady
lightning; the gods shower flowers, the kinnaras sing, the heavenly dancers dance; it is spring, the Malaya breeze blows, the waters of the
Ganga surge; the poet is beside himself with the festivity in Mishra's house. Raga vasanta. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada
is in the BR; ornate Vrajabuli with rhythmic syllables.*[^20-10]

**5.1.** "Jaya, jaya, jaya!" — auspicious cries; the night of the Phalguna full moon shines anew:
from the womb of Shachi Gaura has appeared — the delight of Vraja.
The lovely body of the Child flashes — like steady lightning the colour of kunkuma;
His moonlike face gleams, sweetly shattering all composure.

**5.2.** Seeing the Lord's appearance, the gods with hosts of clouds shower from the sky
garlands of flowers; their bodies are filled with great thrills.
How many longings in their hearts! Excitedly they sing of His lovely deeds;
through the tears that flood their eyes, how many images they behold, in what rapture!

**5.3.** The kinnaras sing to a sweet sound, the mridanga softly plays:
"dhā-dhiki dhikitā dhik dhik dhikkaṭak dhinnānā";
the heavenly dancers dance, enacting performances of every kind:
"uṭṭata kathai thai thai ti ai ai atennānā".[^20-11]

**5.4.** Pure and bright are all ten directions, gently blows the breeze from the Malaya hills,
the flocks of cuckoos sound "kuhu" — spring, the king of seasons, is full of sweetness.
The waters of the river of the gods surge, joy spreads over the land of Nadia;
at the festivity in Mishra's house Narahari's heart is beside itself.

[^20-10]: GPT1 — pp. 60–61, no. 22 (vasanta; scan, PDF pp. 319–320); GPT2 — section 2.1, no. 22. The catalogue did not know it (new row NG-279). BR —
12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 765–766; ed. 1960, vv. 925–928). Line 5.3: GPT1 has "nṛtyasura", the BR "nṛtyata sura" ("the heavenly ones dance") — translated
after the BR; 5.4: GPT1 and GPT2 have "miśrabhuvana", the BR "miśrabhavana" ("Mishra's house") — translated after the BR. Not in PK, KGC, PS, the
Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
[^20-11]: Kinnaras — heavenly singers. The syllables "dhā-dhiki…", "thai thai…" imitate the strokes of the mridanga and the dancers' counting (as in the
dance padas, chapters 17–18).

## 6. Narahari — "bhuvanamanocorā gokulapati gorā…" (GPT1 pp. 61–62, no. 24; BR)
*The birth festival: the women of Nadia come with trays of gifts, and with them, mingling with the humans, the wives of the gods; Sita-devi and
Malini perform auspicious rites; the cowherd men and women, after their former nature, scatter curd in the courtyard and dance; the gods in
the guise of cowherds dance with them; in Mishra's house is the custom of Nanda's house. Raga vasanta or tori. **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^20-12]

**6.1.** The Stealer of the world's hearts, the Lord of Gokula, Gorachand — in what an auspicious hour was He born!
How much happiness Shachi had when she saw her son's face — who else could tell it?

**6.2.** The women of the town of Nadia come in rows, bringing trays full of all kinds of gifts;
and, richly adorned, the wives of the gods, mingling with the humans, cannot gaze at the Child enough.

**6.3.** Sri Sita-devi came and, entering the birth-chamber, rejoices at heart seeing the Child;
together with Malini and others, floating in merriment, she performs many auspicious rites.[^20-13]

**6.4.** How many cowherd women, hundreds of cowherd men come in lovely attire, bringing curd;
all, their hearts overwhelmed, after their former nature scatter curd in the middle of the courtyard.

**6.5.** Clapping their hands, laughing, they dance splendidly; seeing this, the gods, taking the guise of cowherds,
dance in the courtyard — who does not dance there? — again and again crying "jaya, jaya".[^20-14]

**6.6.** So the instruments sound, such festivity is nowhere else: in Mishra's house is the custom of Nanda's house.
What can Narahari say? At the festival of the Lord's birth, for jubilation no one remembers anything.

[^20-12]: GPT1 — pp. 61–62, no. 24 (vasanta or tori; scan, PDF pp. 320–321); GPT2 — section 2.1, no. 24 (catalogue: NG-004). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912,
pp. ≈765–766; ed. 1960, vv. 937–942, "punarvvasanta—toṛī"), immediately after a pada of Ghanashyama (GPT 2.1 no. 23). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the
Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. Signature "narahari ki kaba" (6.6).
[^20-13]: Sita Thakurani, Advaita's wife, came to bless the newborn and brought gifts (CC Adi 13); Malini is Srivasa's wife (note 27 of chapter 19).
[^20-14]: As at the festival of Krishna's birth in Nanda's house the cowherds scattered curd, milk and butter and danced (Bhag. 10.5), so here: the
cowherds of Navadvipa act "after their former nature" (pūrvva svabhāvete), that is, as the cowherds of Vraja. Cf. CB Adi 3 (the gods in human
guise come to see the Child).

## 7. Narahari — "nimāicām̐dera kathā ati aparūpa go…" (GPT1 p. 75, section 2.2, no. 40; GCC)
*One of the elderly women of Navadvipa about Nimai: where have His pranks gone — now He is grave, the pandits respect Him, the Vaishnavas are
inseparable from Him; Nitai loves Him as Balai loved Krishna; Shachi is the very Queen of Vraja, Nimai and Nitai are the two stars of her eyes.
Yatharaga. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^20-15]

**7.1.** "Wondrous are the ways of Nimaichand: now He is like a gracious deity of our family!
Where have all those pranks gone? Who else is as grave as He?

**7.2.** All the pandits living in Nadia — which of them does not respect Him?
Srivasa, Murari and all the Vaishnavas — none can bear to part from Him.

**7.3.** And my Nitai loves Him like His own life — as Balai loved Krishna;
it seems that very thing has appeared here again: nowhere have I seen the like.[^20-16]

**7.4.** Blessed in this world is virtuous Shachi — it seems she is that very Queen of Vraja;
Nimai and Nitai are the two stars of her eyes." Narahari offers himself to this love.

[^20-15]: GPT1 — p. 75, section 2.2, no. 40 (yatharaga; scan, PDF p. 334); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 40 (catalogue: NG-021; in the GPT2 recognition the
number was read as "70"). GCC — chapter 6, pada 15 (ed. 1947, printed pp. 65–66). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. The pada
continues the GCC cycle in which the people of Navadvipa come at dawn to Shachi's house and gaze at Gaura, returned from Gaya (chapter 19,
nos. 4–28): "now" (eve) is the time after Gaya, when Nityananda is already in Navadvipa and Srivasa and Murari are inseparable from the Lord. In
line 7.3 the GCC has "kṛṣṇe yena karila valāi" ("as Balai [loved] Krishna"); the GPT "kṛṣṇa yena…", with the same sense.
[^20-16]: Nityananda is Balarama, Krishna's elder brother in Vraja; Shachi is Yashoda (CC Adi 13; Adi 5). Shachi loved Nityananda as a son; cf. her
dream in which Nimai and Nitai appear as Krishna and Balarama (CB, Madhya-khanda). "My Nitai" — the affectionate words of an elderly woman.

## 8. Narahari — "nadīyāra yata vṛddhanārīgaṇe…" (GPT1 pp. 75–76, no. 41; GCC)
*The elderly women of Nadia speak thus to one another, gaze at Gauranga's face, count themselves fortunate and bless Him. Yatharaga.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC (the last pada of its 6th chapter).*[^20-17]

**8.1.** Thus all the elderly women of Nadia speak to one another.

**8.2.** How wondrous is the way of them all! With what to compare it? They are full of tenderness.

**8.3.** Again and again gazing at the moonlike face of Gaurangachand, they count themselves fortunate.

**8.4.** How many times they bless Him, again and again! Narahari, hearing this, swims in happiness.

[^20-17]: GPT1 — pp. 75–76, no. 41 (yatharaga; scan, PDF pp. 334–335); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 41 (catalogue: NG-022). GCC — chapter 6, pada 16
(printed p. 66): with it Chakravarti closes the chapter on the love of the women of Navadvipa in vatsalya. Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the
Gita-chandrodaya. B. The next one in GPT1, no. 42, is an abridged doublet of no. 21 of chapter 19 (NG-023) and is not translated.

## 9. Narahari — "nāco āre vāpa viśvambhara…" (GPT1 p. 76, no. 43; BR)
*The virtuous women, clapping their hands and saying "Hari-bol", coax little Vishvambhara to dance, promising butter and cream; He, looking at
His mother, dances crying "Hari-bol"; the courtyard shines with His golden body. Raga tudi. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is
in the BR.*[^20-18]

**9.1.** "Dance, dear Vishvambhara! We will give You handfuls of butter, thickened milk and cream!"

**9.2.** The virtuous wives around say this tenderly to Nimaichand.

**9.3.** Saying "Hari, Hari-bol", all together clap their hands again and again.

**9.4.** Gora, looking at His mother, dances in various ways crying "Hari-bol".[^20-19]

**9.5.** What a gentle smile on the moonlike face! It enchants the world, pouring out nectar in streams.

**9.6.** Lovely is the glance of His eyes; seeing the curves of His arms, who can stay calm?

**9.7.** What a sweet, sweet radiance! The courtyard gleams with the rays of His golden body.

**9.8.** Sweetly the belt of bells and the anklets jingle; Narahari offers himself to the rhythm of His feet.

[^20-18]: GPT1 — p. 76, no. 43 (tudi; scan, PDF p. 335); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 43 (catalogue: NG-024). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 772; ed. 1960,
vv. 1005–1012): "here is Nimai's wondrous dance: the women, clapping their hands, make Him dance" (v. 1004). In GPT1 the first word is "nāce"
(a misprint?), in the BR "nāco" ("dance!"); translated after the BR. In 9.7 GPT1 has "hena aṅgera", the BR "hema-aṅgera" ("golden body") — after the
BR. Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
[^20-19]: Cf. CB Adi 4: when the Child cried, the women clapped their hands and sang "Hari", and He, quieted, danced — thus from infancy the Lord made
everyone sing the holy name (cf. no. 21 of chapter 19).

## 10. Narahari — "āre mora soṇāra nimāi…" (GPT1 pp. 76–77, no. 44; BR)
*Shachi begs Nimai to play at home and not to roam about other people's courtyards: let the children come to Him, she will give Him
whatever He wants; when He goes off with a band of rascals, her heart is not at rest. Raga dhanashi. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** —
the pada is in the BR.*[^20-20]

**10.1.** "Ah, my golden Nimai!
Do not leave Your own house for other people's courtyards — sit and play here.

**10.2.** The children will come to play with You — keep them all right here.
Whatever You want, I will bring You: what is lacking in my house?

**10.3.** If anyone calls You — say You are afraid: Your father forbids it.
When You go out of the house with a band of rascals — can a mother keep hold of her heart?

**10.4.** If You are out of my sight for a moment, my life will not stay in my body; Narahari knows my pain.
Heed Your mother, play at home — so that I may always see Your moonlike face."[^20-21]

[^20-20]: GPT1 — pp. 76–77, no. 44 (dhanashi; scan, PDF pp. 335–336); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 44 (catalogue: NG-025). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 772;
ed. 1960, vv. 1014–1017): "here the mother, beside herself with tenderness, spoke to Nimai, looking at His face" (v. 1013). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the
Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. Line 10.1 is the refrain (dhru) with the first line of the stanza.
[^20-21]: The mother's fear for the Child is vatsalya, the pure love of the Lord's eternal mother (note 2 of chapter 19), like Yashoda's anxiety for
Krishna.

## 11. Narahari — "raṅge nācaye śacīra vālā…" (GPT1 p. 77, no. 45; BR)
*Shachi's child dances merrily in the courtyard, grey with dust, clapping His hands and saying "Hari"; His mother gives Him cream; He whirls
round, the hem of His dhoti trails on the ground, the bells and anklets jingle. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada
is in the BR.*[^20-22]

**11.1.** Merrily dances Shachi's child, lighting up the world with His beauty.

**11.2.** His body surpasses a golden lotus; grey with dust — as if with flower pollen.

**11.3.** Lovely shine His dress and ornaments; saying "Hari", He claps His hands.

**11.4.** He smiles gently, sweetly and gracefully — who can keep his composure then?

**11.5.** How merrily He looks around on all sides! His mother gives Him handfuls of cream.

**11.6.** Striking poses, He whirls round again and again; the hem of His dhoti trails on the ground.

**11.7.** Lovely flashes the belt of bells; from it a ringing "jhini-ni".

**11.8.** On His feet the anklets jingle "jhunu-nu"; Narahari offers himself to them.

[^20-22]: GPT1 — p. 77, no. 45 (kamoda; scan, PDF p. 336); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 45 (catalogue: NG-026). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 775; ed. 1960,
vv. 1049–1056), immediately after Vasu Ghosha's padas on Nimai's dance in the courtyard (PK 1151, 1161 — chapter 7). Not in PK (under Narahari's
signature), KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. "Whirls" (ghume) — Vrajabuli, cf. Hindi "ghūmnā".

## 12. Narahari — "āji āṅginā para nadīyā vālaka saṅge…" (GPT1 p. 77, no. 46)
*Shachi's child plays in the courtyard with the boys of Nadia — like the moon among the stars; Shachi, beside herself with joy, kisses Him,
wipes His sweat and fans Him; beside them stands the poet with a chamara. Raga mangala. **Attribution: not established** — the pada is in
neither the BR nor the GCC nor any other witness; Vrajabuli; in the signature the poet himself serves in the lila (note 24).*[^20-23]

**12.1.** Today in the courtyard, with the boys of Nadia, Shachi's child plays merrily —
as if amid a host of stars a single moon shines, lighting up all directions.

**12.2.** Taking various toys, all together they play various games;
smiles blossom on every face — as if a multitude of lotuses had opened at once.

**12.3.** Watching this play, Shachi, her heart overflowing, is beside herself with joy;
a hundred times in a moment, taking Vishvambhara in her arms, she kisses His moonlike face.

**12.4.** With the hem of her garment she wipes away His sweat and fans His holy body;
and beside them, chamara in hand, stands the wretched Narahari Dasa.[^20-24]

[^20-23]: GPT1 — p. 77, no. 46 (mangala; scan, PDF p. 336); GPT2 — section 2.2, no. 46 (catalogue: NG-275). Not in the BR, GCC, PK, KGC, PS or the
Gita-chandrodaya. C. The following padas of the section in GPT1 — nos. 47–48 signed "Murari" (Majumdar considers them doubtful), no. 49 without
Narahari's signature, no. 50 by Lochana Dasa — are not part of the appendix.
[^20-24]: The poet places himself in the lila as a servant fanning the Lord with a chamara (a yak-tail whisk) — an image of inner service (manasi-seva)
in meditation on the lila, usual for later Vaishnava poets; it is not a claim to have witnessed the Lord's childhood.

## 13. Narahari — "āju ki ānandamaya…" (GPT1 p. 79, section 2.3, no. 1; BR)
*Nimai's chudakarana (first tonsure): Shachi's house is full of people; Mishra, having adorned his son, performs the rites according to the
Vedas and custom; the barber, having done his work, ties a yellow thread at the ears; the women rejoice, the brahmanas recite the Vedas, the
bards compose praises. Raga dhanashi. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^20-25]

**13.1.** How joyful today! People throng to the shining house of Shachi:
a delight for all — in what a wondrous, auspicious hour Nimaichand's chudakarana is performed!

**13.2.** Having dressed Vishvambhara in divine clothes and ornaments and seated Him on a divine seat,
Mishra carefully performs all that the Vedas enjoin and custom requires.[^20-26]

**13.3.** The worthy barber came and, having done his work, tied a yellow thread at the root of the ears;
the women raise jubilant cries — who does not cry "jaya"? Auspiciousness spread over the earth.[^20-27]

**13.4.** The brahmanas recite the Vedas, the bards compose verses of praise, the musicians play various instruments;
all the dancers dance, the singers sing His pure glory — how much can Narahari tell?

[^20-25]: GPT1 — p. 79, section 2.3 ("Karnavedha and the wedding"), no. 1 (dhanashi; scan, PDF p. 338); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 1. The catalogue did not
know it (new row NG-280). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 781; ed. 1960, vv. 1156–1159): "here Mishra Purandara said to Shachi: Vishvambhara has
reached the age for the chudakarana — and both, as the Vedas enjoin, performed the chudakarana of their son" (vv. 1154–1155). Line 13.1: GPT1 has
"nimāicām̐dera cūṛā, karmma ki apūrvva śubhakṣaṇe", the BR "cūṛā-karmmādi apūrvva śubhakṣaṇe" — in sense the same: chuda-karma. Not in PK, KGC, PS, the
Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
[^20-26]: The samskaras are the purificatory rites of a brahmana's life (chudakarana, karnavedha, upanayana and others). The Lord, Himself the goal of
the Vedas, needs no purification: He accepts the samskaras following His lila in the form of a brahmana's son and setting an example for people.
So Chakravarti too understands it: right after this pada the BR says that the Lord, full of consciousness and bliss, performs His lila like a human
being — and the barber, before piercing His ears, saw that the holes were already there, but by the Lord's will told no one (vv. 1160–1161).
[^20-27]: The yellow thread at the root of the ears is the mark for the ear-piercing (karnavedha), which was performed together with the chudakarana;
hence the title of the GPT section "Karnavedha and the wedding". The women's jubilant cries (jayakāra, ulu) are an auspicious custom at Bengali
family festivals.

## 14. Narahari — "āju nirupama gauracandra-cūṛā…" (GPT1 p. 79, no. 2; BR)
*The same chudakarana: the wives of Navadvipa cry "ulu-lu" in jubilation, the brahmanas chant the Vedas, the sutas, magadhas and bandins
compose tales, the musicians and dancers beat the rhythm; Mishra gives gifts to the supplicants, the gods in the sky cry "jaya". Raga
belavali. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR; ornate Vrajabuli with rhythmic syllables.*[^20-28]

**14.1.** Today is the incomparable chudakarana of Gaurachandra as the Vedas enjoin: an auspicious celebration, the house is full of people;
the wives of Sri Navadvipa, by an incomparable custom, cry "ulu-lu-lu-lu-lu-lu" — what a joy for the ear!

**14.2.** The assembly of brahmanas shines; in many modes the Vedas resound, sweetly filling hearts with delight;
the sutas, magadhas and bandins compose new tales of His deeds — reaching the ear, they steal the heart of the world.[^20-29]

**14.3.** The musicians on mridangas and other instruments play in many modes: "dhā-dhā dhilaṅga dhikitaka dhinninā";
skilled singers sing in well-measured metres, the dancers dance beating out: "tattathai thai ti ai tinninā".

**14.4.** Thrilling all over, the jubilant Mishra, distributing many gifts, satisfies all the supplicants.
What can Narahari say? The gods, gazing at this great splendour, beside themselves, loudly cry "jaya, jaya" in the sky.

[^20-28]: GPT1 — p. 79, no. 2 (belavali; scan, PDF p. 338); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 2 (catalogue: NG-027). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 782; ed. 1960,
vv. 1163–1166), immediately after the account of the pierced ears (note 26). Variants: 14.1 GPT1 "de’", BR "deta"; 14.2 GPT1 "śravaṇa pakṣagata", BR
"śravaṇapatha-gata" ("reaching the ear") — translated after the BR; 14.3 GPT1 "prabheda bhavi", BR "prabheda bhaṇi". Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the
Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. In the GPT1 signature the first letter of the name is cut off by the edge of the page ("…rahari").
[^20-29]: Sutas, magadhas and bandins — court bards, singers of genealogies and panegyrists.

## 15. Narahari — "ki ānanda nadīyānagare…" (GPT1 pp. 79–80, no. 3; BR)
*The upanayana: all over Nadia the news that Shachi's son will receive the sacred thread; everyone hastens with gifts; Mishra gives his son the
thread; Gaura in red cloth, with staff and bag, begs alms, and the heavenly women, mingling with the humans, and His associates give Him alms.
Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^20-30]

**15.1.** What joy in the town of Nadia!
"The son of Sri Shachi-devi will receive the sacred thread!" — this news is in every house.

**15.2.** Who, beside himself with tenderness, does not hasten to Mishra's house with various gifts?
Mishra's incomparable house is full of people — whom will this splendour not enchant?

**15.3.** Mishra, in great joy, performs the rites according to the Vedas and gives Gorachand the sacred thread;
lovely is the golden form: He wears a red cloth, in His hand a divine staff, on His shoulder a bag.[^20-31]

**15.4.** The Lord merrily begs alms; seeing this, the heavenly women, mingling with the humans, give to Him;
and the Lord's dear associates — with what merriment they put alms into His bag!

**15.5.** Who can recount all the auspicious rites, all the jubilant cries of the women?
The brahmanas chant the Vedas — who, hearing them, can keep his composure? The bards recite verses of praise.

**15.6.** Cries of "jaya, jaya" spread in all directions; dancing, singing, music of every kind.
Narahari Dasa says: the supplicants, having received fitting gifts, intoxicated with happiness, sing His glory.

[^20-30]: GPT1 — pp. 79–80, no. 3 (kamoda; scan, PDF pp. 338–339); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 3. The catalogue did not know it (new row NG-281; formerly its
first line was confused with the wedding pada no. 11 "ki ānanda nadīyā-nagare | nimāira vivāhakathā…", NG-030). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 783;
ed. 1960, vv. 1173–1178): "here Jagannatha Mishra resolved to give his son the sacred thread, fixed the day, called the relatives" (vv. 1170–1172).
The next pada of GPT1, no. 4 (the upanayana: the Lord in the form of Vamana begs alms), is signed by Ghanashyama (outside the appendix); it is also
in the BR (vv. 1179–1192). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
[^20-31]: The red cloth, the staff and the alms-bag are the dress of a brahmachari at the upanayana; he begs his first alms from his relatives. The Lord,
Bhagavan Himself, accepts the sacred thread not out of need but following the lila (note 26). According to CB Adi 8, when He put on the thread, He
was seen as Vamana-deva (cf. Ghanashyama's pada no. 4, note 30). The heavenly women mingling with the humans are the same image as in no. 6.

## 16. Narahari — "gaurasundara parama śubhakṣaṇe…" (GPT1 p. 80, no. 5; BR)
*Gaurasundara in an auspicious hour receives the sacred thread; Shachi and Mishra perform the rites; the women rejoice, the bards praise, the
singers sing, the dancers dance; the gods are beside themselves at this lila. Raga suhai. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is
in the BR; Vrajabuli.*[^20-32]

**16.1.** In the supremely auspicious hour Gaurasundara has received the sacred thread;
Shachi and Mishra, skilled in the rites the Vedas enjoin, perform them in incomparable order.

**16.2.** Various auspicious rites are performed; the noble wives cry "ulu-lu-lu-lu-lu-lu";
the bards proclaim His auspicious glory and drink in this beauty with their eyes.

**16.3.** Skilled singers sing in new metres, merrily sound the murajas and other drums;
the dancers dance, often beating out: "dhā-dhi dhikadha dhilaṅga".

**16.4.** The hearts of the gods are wholly immersed in bliss at the sight of this charming lila;
"jaya, jaya" resounds through the whole world — Narahari Dasa offers himself [to Him].

[^20-32]: GPT1 — p. 80, no. 5 (suhai; scan, PDF pp. 339–340); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 5 (catalogue: NG-028). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 784; ed. 1960,
vv. 1193–1196), immediately after Ghanashyama's pada; then the BR tells how Mishra took his son to study with Gangadasa Pandita (vv. 1197–1200). The
following padas of the section in GPT1 — nos. 6–8 signed by Lochana, no. 9 by "Trilochana" (wedding padas, partly in nagari-bhava) — are not part of the appendix. Not in
PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.

## 17. Narahari — "vallabhaduhitā lakṣmī sucaritā…" (GPT1 p. 83, no. 10; BR)
*The first meeting by the Ganga: Lakshmi, Vallabha's daughter, goes with her friends to bathe and, seeing Gaurangachand, cannot restrain
her hidden love; Gora, recognising His beloved, looks at her; their glances secretly meet, and He goes home smiling. Raga kamoda.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^20-33]

**17.1.** Vallabha's daughter, virtuous Lakshmi, surrounded by her friends,
goes to the bank of the Ganga to bathe, timidly glancing around.

**17.2.** Seeing Gaurangachand a little way off, she feels a hidden love surge up;
drinking the nectar of the sweetness of that form, she cannot keep her composure.

**17.3.** Gora, the jewel of virtues, recognising His beloved, looks at Lakshmi;
her form, surpassing pure gold, seems to enter His very heart.[^20-34]

**17.4.** The glances of the two meet secretly from the corners of their eyes — so that no one else notices;
Narahari's Lord, smiling softly, went home in joy.

[^20-33]: GPT1 — p. 83, no. 10 (kamoda; scan, PDF p. 342); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 10 (catalogue: NG-029). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 787; ed. 1960,
vv. 1232–1235): "one day Shachi thought of her son's marriage; His boyhood was ending, His youth beginning… to increase His mother's joy, the Lord
wished to marry; He went along this road to the Ganga, and Lakshmi-devi, the Lord's beloved, came to bathe; their meeting is described by the wise"
(vv. 1226–1231). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. The meeting by the Ganga — CB Adi 10; Murari 1.9.
[^20-34]: Lakshmipriya is the eternal consort of the Lord, Lakshmi Herself (CB Adi 10; CC Adi 14–15); that is why He "recognises His beloved". Their
love is not a worldly attraction but the eternal relation of the Lord and His energy. "Narahari's Lord" (narahari pahum̐) is a habitual turn of
Chakravarti's signature (note 44 of chapter 17).

## 18. Narahari — "ki ānanda nadīyā-nagare nimāira vivāhakathā…" (GPT1 p. 83, no. 11; BR)
*In every house of Nadia they talk of Nimai's wedding; all long to see it; the bards, dancers and musicians, astrologers, gardeners with
garlands, hundreds of poor supplicants come running; the poet longs to see the wedding with his own eyes. Raga dhanashi. **Attribution:
probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^20-35]

**18.1.** What joy in the town of Nadia! In every house there is talk of Nimai's wedding.

**18.2.** The men and women of Nadia — the hearts of all are eager to see the wedding.

**18.3.** The bards come running, reckoning they will get much wealth.

**18.4.** The dancers, the musicians and the rest — all hasten, vying with one another, with what hopes!

**18.5.** The astrologers hasten: "We shall fix an incomparable auspicious hour for the wedding!"

**18.6.** Joyfully the gardeners go with various garlands of flowers to the house of Sri Shachi.

**18.7.** Who with one mouth can tell how many they are? The poor supplicants come by the hundred.

**18.8.** In Narahari's heart is one hope: to see the wedding festivity to the full with both eyes.

[^20-35]: GPT1 — p. 83, no. 11 (dhanashi; scan, PDF p. 342); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 11 (catalogue: the wedding part of row NG-030; see note 30). BR —
12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 788; ed. 1960, vv. ≈1245–1252): after the account of Vanamali Acharya's matchmaking and of the wedding day (vv. 1237–1240).
Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. The matchmaking and the marriage with Lakshmipriya — CB Adi 10; CC Adi 15;
Murari 1.9.

## 19. Narahari — "nadīyāra navavadhū sava viralete kahe…" (GPT1 p. 83, no. 12; BR)
*The young wives of Nadia, apart by themselves, rejoice at the coming wedding: fortunate are Vallabha Acharya and his wife, who gain such a
son-in-law; fortunate is Lakshmi, who gains a husband more beautiful than Kama; Vanamali has made a good match; today is the adhivasa — time to
dress up. Raga dhanashi. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^20-36]

**19.1.** The young wives of Nadia, apart by themselves, speak with sweet smiles:
"How fortunate we are that we shall see such a wedding, floating in an ocean of bliss!"

**19.2.** One says: "The worthy Vallabha Acharya and his wife, devoted to her husband and virtuous —
I think it is for their former pious deeds that they gain so rare a son-in-law."

**19.3.** Another says: "Blessed is Vallabha's daughter, the beautiful Lakshmi — like Lakshmi herself;
who else is so fortunate? She will gain a husband who surpasses Madana!"

**19.4.** Yet another says: "Vanamali has made a fine match — how much joy he has had!
Today is the adhivasa — come, let us dress up: Narahari came and told us."[^20-37]

[^20-36]: GPT1 — p. 83, no. 12 (dhanashi; scan, PDF p. 342); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 12 (catalogue: NG-031). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 788; ed. 1960,
vv. 1253–1256; the 1960 editor's heading: "the adhivasa of Nimai's wedding"). Line 19.1: GPT1 has "dhanya mora mena", the BR "dhanya morā yena" — translated
after the BR. Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
[^20-37]: Vanamali Acharya is the matchmaker who arranged the Lord's first marriage (CB Adi 10). The adhivasa is the pre-wedding rite on the eve of the
wedding (scents, garlands, blessings). The young wives' talk is joy at the wedding, not nagari-bhava; "surpassing Madana" is the usual praise of
a bridegroom's beauty. Here too the poet places himself in the lila — as the messenger calling the women to the adhivasa (cf. note 24).

## 20. Narahari — "śrīśacī-ālaya ati śobhāmaya…" (GPT1 pp. 83–84, no. 13; BR)
*The women of noble families, telling themselves that today is Gora's adhivasa, dress up and go in rows, lighting up the streets of Nadia, to
Shachi, bow to her and, seeing the Lord in the courtyard, comfort their hearts. Raga dhanashi. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the
pada is in the BR.*[^20-38]

**20.1.** "The house of Sri Shachi is all aglow, in it an ocean of joy surges:
today is the adhivasa — adorned, the blissful Gora, the Moon of Gokula, will shine."

**20.2.** Saying this to themselves, unable to keep still, glancing around on all sides, the maidens of noble families —
with what to compare it? — as if lovely garlands of moons had come out of the houses.

**20.3.** Their many-coloured clothes and ornaments shine, every limb is adorned;
striking various poses, they go in rows, lighting up the streets of Nadia.

**20.4.** With what longing they come to Ai, with what reverence they bow to her!
And finding Narahari's Lord in the courtyard, they comfort their hearts gazing at that face.[^20-39]

[^20-38]: GPT1 — pp. 83–84, no. 13 (dhanashi; scan, PDF pp. 342–343); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 13 (catalogue: NG-032). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 789;
ed. 1960, vv. 1257–1260). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. The pada continues the previous one: the young
wives go to the adhivasa.
[^20-39]: Ai ("mother") is Shachi. The women who "comfort their hearts gazing at the face" of the Lord are an image of the all-attractiveness of
Bhagavan at His festival: they have come to bow to the mother and bless the bridegroom; this is not nagari-bhava. Worship of Gaura in the spirit
of "gaura-nagari" is not accepted by the Gaudiya tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta) (cf. note 15 of chapter 17).

## 21. Narahari — "śobhāmaya śacīra aṅgane…" (GPT1 p. 84, no. 14; BR)
*Nimai's adhivasa: the brahmanas chant the Vedas, the relatives offer scents and garlands, Gora in the assembly surpasses myriads of Kamas;
Vallabha Acharya, having performed the rite, goes home; Shachi with the married women performs the auspicious rites; humans and gods together.
Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^20-40]

**21.1.** In Shachi's shining courtyard on all sides the brahmanas chant the Vedas.

**21.2.** What joy has appeared today! In an auspicious hour — the adhivasa of Nimaichand.

**21.3.** The relatives offer scents and garlands; the radiance of Gora's body lights up all directions.

**21.4.** In the midst of the assembly Gora, the jewel of brahmanas, shines, surpassing myriads of Kamas.

**21.5.** Whoever looks even once at Gora loses his composure and forgets himself.

**21.6.** All who have come to the adhivasa are given scents, sandal paste and the like.

**21.7.** Having performed the adhivasa according to the rules, Vallabha Acharya went to his own home.[^20-41]

**21.8.** There is no end to the happiness, it cannot be told: with the married women Ai performs the auspicious rites.

**21.9.** The women raise jubilant cries, the bards recite auspicious verses of praise.

**21.10.** Dancing, singing, music of every kind — no one has the power to find a comparison for it.

**21.11.** Who does not say there: "Good, good!"? Through the whole world — sweet cries of "jaya, jaya".

**21.12.** The gods, mingling with the humans, watch the merriment of the adhivasa — says Narahari.

[^20-40]: GPT1 — p. 84, no. 14 (kamoda; scan, PDF p. 343); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 14 (catalogue: NG-033). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 789–790; ed. 1960,
vv. 1261–1272). Variants: 21.3 GPT1 "ambagaṇe", BR "āptagaṇe" ("the relatives") — after the BR; 21.8 in GPT1 the end of the line is cut off ("kare a…"),
BR "kare āi" — after the BR. Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. Line 21.2 is the refrain (dhru).
[^20-41]: Vallabha Acharya, the bride's father, came to perform the bridegroom's adhivasa (by custom — with scents and garlands), and then at his own home
performs the bride's adhivasa (next pada). "The married women" (āiho śuiho) are wives whose husbands are living: only they perform the auspicious
wedding rites.

## 22. Narahari — "āju snehete vihvala haiyā…" (GPT1 p. 84, no. 15; BR)
*The bride's adhivasa: Vallabha Acharya with his relatives performs the rite; the mother adorns Lakshmi and seats her on a throne; Lakshmi,
receiving scents and a garland, rejoices, while around her, invisible, throng the heavenly women; music and the women's cries. Raga dhanashi.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^20-42]

**22.1.** Today, beside himself with tenderness,
Vallabha Acharya with his brahmana kinsmen performs the rite of adhivasa.

**22.2.** With what love the mother, having dressed her daughter Lakshmi in lovely clothes and ornaments,
seats her on a divine throne in the middle of the beautiful courtyard — and her friends float in happiness.

**22.3.** When in the auspicious hour scents and a garland are offered to her, her heart rejoices and her form shines brighter;
hearts know no rest: around, invisible, throng hosts of heavenly women, gazing.[^20-43]

**22.4.** Conches, bells and various instruments, dancing, singing; the bards proclaim auspicious words;
at the women's jubilant cries Narahari cannot keep his composure — and offers himself.
