---

# Chapter 21. Appendix. Padas signed "Narahari" from the Gaura-pada-tarangini — V: the wedding with Lakshmipriya and the beginning of the second wedding

*Continuation of the appendix (the introductory note on the two Naraharis, on the arguments for attribution and on the marks in the
headings is in ch. 17). Chapter 21: the end of GPT section 2.3 "Karnavedha and the wedding" — the wedding day with Lakshmipriya (the
morning after the adhivasa, the water rite, the bath and dressing of the bridegroom, the procession, the wedding in the house of Vallabha
Acharya, the bridal chamber, the return home) and life with Lakshmipriya; the beginning of section 2.4 "The second marriage" — the news of
the wedding with Vishnupriya, the women of Nadia with Shachi, the adhivasa of bridegroom and bride, the morning of the wedding day (the bath
and dressing of the bridegroom; the procession and the wedding itself follow in the next chapter). Narahari Chakravarti quotes almost all
the padas of the chapter one after another in the 12th wave of the Bhakti-ratnakara, where Ishana shows Srinivasa the house of Jagannatha
Mishra (two padas of section 2.4 are also in Chakravarti's Gaura-charita-chintamani); one (no. 13) has not been found in any witness. Before
translation the "Narahari" signatures in sections 2.3–2.4 (GPT1 pp. 84–100) were checked throughout, in the OCR and on the scan: the
catalogue had missed two padas of section 2.4 (nos. 18 and 23, new rows NG-285, 286). From section 2.4, up to the adhivasa and the morning
of the wedding, the following are not translated: nos. 4 and 11 — signed Ghanashyama (outside the appendix); nos. 2, 3 and 7 — padas in
nagari-bhava (a young wife's dream in which Gaura invites her to the wedding and embraces her; the "anuraga" of the women for Gaura; women
who give Him "life and youth") — assigned to the section of nagari padas. The base text is GPT1 (doubtful places from the scan), collated
with GPT2, the BR (eds. 1912 and 1960) and the Gaura-charita-chintamani (ed. 1947); PK, KGC, PS and the Gita-chandrodaya have been checked. On
Lakshmipriya and Vishnupriya as the eternal energies of the Lord and on the wedding rites as lila see notes 2 and 30; on the motif of the
women of Nadia, note 5. The notes of the GPT editors are not reproduced.*

## 1. Narahari — "adhivāsa niśi pohāile…" (GPT1 p. 85, section 2.3, no. 16; BR)
*The wedding day: the night of the adhivasa is over; Nimai, surrounded by brahmanas, performs the Vedic rites; crowds, music, songs, the
praises of the bhatas, the women's cries of joy; everyone rejoices at the women's rites. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR (12th wave).*[^21-1]

**1.1.** When the night of the adhivasa had passed, everyone set about the wedding tasks.

**1.2.** Surrounded by brahmanas, Nimai performs the rites enjoined by the Vedas.[^21-2]

**1.3.** The crowds cannot be described: the clamour of "take! give!" is immense.

**1.4.** Instruments of every kind play without pause; the singers sing song after song.

**1.5.** The bhatas recite verses of praise; the women raise sweet cries of joy.

**1.6.** All rejoice at the women's rites; Narahari floats in that ocean of happiness.[^21-3]

[^21-1]: GPT1 — p. 85, section 2.3 ("karnavedha and the wedding"), no. 16 (kamoda; scan, PDF p. 344); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 16 (catalogue: NG-282).
BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 790–791; ed. 1960, vv. 1277–1282), straight after the adhivasa of the bride (no. 22 of chapter 20); then the BR gives
the padas nos. 2–12 of this chapter in sequence. Variants: 1.4 GPT1 "pūrvvāpara" ("one after another"), BR "manohara" ("enchantingly"); 1.6 GPT1
"sāyare", BR "pāthāre" (both "in the ocean"). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. The wedding with
Lakshmipriya — CB Adi 10; CC Adi 15; Murari 1.9–1.10.
[^21-2]: Lakshmipriya is the eternal consort of the Lord, Lakshmi Herself (CB Adi 10; CC Adi 14–15); the Lord's wedding is not a worldly event but His
lila with His own energy. The Lord, the goal of all the Vedas, is bound by nothing enjoined; He accepts the wedding rites in keeping with the
lila and for the joy of His mother and His associates — as Krishna did in Dvaraka. So are all the padas of this chapter on the Lord's
"marriage" to be understood.
[^21-3]: The women's rites (strī-ācāra) are the wedding customs performed by married women in addition to the Vedic rites (the cries of "ulu-lu", the
water rite, the anointing of the bridegroom, etc.). Here too the poet places himself in the lila as a witness and participant (cf. note 24 of
chapter 20).

## 2. Narahari — "kulavadhūgaṇa ulasita mana…" (GPT1 p. 85, no. 17; BR)
*The wives of noble families dress to go for the water of the wedding bath; looking at Gora's face, they cry "ulu-lu"; they go, talking among
themselves; anklets ring, music plays; having performed the water rite, they enter the house. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^21-4]

**2.1.** The wives of noble families, their hearts rejoicing, gaily dress to go for the water;
gazing again and again at Gora's moonlike face, they smile and cry "ulu-lu", and a thrill runs through their bodies.

**2.2.** They come out of their houses — how many feelings rise in their hearts! — intoxicated by the fragrance of the body of the Gaura-moon;
their hearts know no rest, brimming with feeling; from the corners of their eyes — how many different glances!

**2.3.** How much they say to one another of what cannot be told! Which of them, playful, does not offer herself for Him?
With their dress, ornaments and attire they shatter all composure — who could find a likeness for that beauty?

**2.4.** Anklets, girdles of bells, the sounds of many instruments — how sweet, words cannot tell!
Having completed the water rite, they enter the house — and Narahari's heart overflows with joy.[^21-5]

[^21-4]: GPT1 — p. 85, no. 17 (kamoda; scan, PDF p. 344); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 17 (catalogue: NG-035). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 791; ed. 1960,
vv. 1283–1286). Variant: 2.1 GPT1 "pāni-sahivāre", BR "pāni sāivāre" — "to perform the water rite" (translated by the sense of both readings).
Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. "Pani-sai" (jala sādhā) is a wedding custom: married women go with music
to the Ganga and draw water for the bath of the bridegroom (or bride).
[^21-5]: The poet describes the delight of the women of Nadia at the Lord's wedding in words close to the motif of the townswomen (nagaris) enamoured
of Gaura. We translate faithfully to the author; but the Gaudiya tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati)
does not accept the worship of Gaura in the mood of "Gaura-nagari": Gaura is Krishna Himself in the mood and lustre of Radha; He came to taste Her
love, not to enjoy as a nagara. The Lord's attractiveness for the people of Navadvipa is the quality of Bhagavan, who attracts all; it is not
worldly passion. The same holds for the other padas of the chapter about the women of Nadia (cf. note 39 of chapter 20).

## 3. Narahari — "kivā śrīśacī-bhavana mājhe…" (GPT1 p. 85, no. 18; BR)
*The wedding bath of the bridegroom: amid auspicious cries the women loosen His locks and braid them again, oiling them, rub Him with
turmeric and perfumes; He is bathed with Ganga water, and the poet playfully dries Him with a towel. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^21-6]

**3.1.** What [bustle] in the house of Sri Shachi! Amid manifold auspicious cries all are busy with the wedding tasks.

**3.2.** For Gora is the Moon of Gokula: at the bath enjoined before the wedding the ocean of joy surges beyond measure.

**3.3.** The wives of noble families, sweetly and gracefully, saying, "Let us oil His lovely locks," loosen and braid them again and again.

**3.4.** One rubs His body with turmeric; seeing the turmeric grow dim, all laugh and give their lives for Him.[^21-7]

**3.5.** One anoints His body with perfumes — but the fragrance of that body robs the perfumes of their pride: with what to compare it?

**3.6.** They bathed Him with Ganga water; Narahari, taking a towel, dries His body as if in play.

[^21-6]: GPT1 — p. 85, no. 18 (kamoda; scan, PDF p. 344); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 18 (catalogue: NG-036). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 791; ed. 1960,
vv. 1287–1292). Variants: 3.2 GPT1 "sthāne" ("in the place"), BR "snāne" ("at the bath") — following the BR; 3.5 GPT1 "upamā diva ki saṅge", BR-1912
"ke dive upamā aṅge". Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. Line 3.1 is the refrain (dhru).
[^21-7]: Grown dim beside the golden radiance of the Lord's body. "Give their lives" (parāṇa nichaye) refers to the rite of nimchhani: out of love one
waves something (in poetry — one's very life) around the beloved to ward off misfortune. The playful care of the women who perform the wedding
rites (anointing the bridegroom with turmeric and oil) is festive merriment, not nagari-bhava.

## 4. Narahari — "āju kata nā ānanda mane…" (GPT1 p. 86, no. 19; BR)
*His friends dress the bridegroom: they anoint Him with sandal, draw the tilaka, adorn His curls with a garland of malati, put on earrings,
necklace, bracelets and rings and a golden chain on His waist; the poet, having clothed Him in a red-bordered cloth, beholds His beauty.
Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^21-8]

**4.1.** How much joy in the heart today! Seating Vishvambhara on a seat, His friends dress Him.

**4.2.** They anoint His body with fragrant sandal paste and draw a lovely tilaka on His forehead — whom would it not enchant?

**4.3.** Gathering the curling locks above His brow, in gladness of heart, sweetly and gracefully they wind them with a garland of malati.

**4.4.** They put earrings in His ears — they flash beside His cheeks, and His cheeks rob mirrors of their pride.

**4.5.** They put a necklace of jewels on His neck; it sways charmingly on His broad chest — who can find a likeness for it?

**4.6.** On His arms armlets and bracelets, on His fingers they put rings — and, looking at His face, they cannot keep their composure.

**4.7.** His waist is slender, slenderer than a lion's; as they adorn it with a golden chain, their eyes cease to blink.

**4.8.** An array that tempts the world! Having clothed Him in a red-bordered cloth, Narahari beholds His beauty.[^21-9]

[^21-8]: GPT1 — p. 86, no. 19 (kamoda; scan, PDF p. 345); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 19 (catalogue: NG-037). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 791–792; ed. 1960,
vv. 1293–1300). Variant: 4.6 GPT1 "cāhilā dhairaja dhare" ("having looked, they kept composure"?), BR "cāhi nā dhairaya dhare" — translated following the BR. Not
in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. Line 4.1 is the refrain (dhru).
[^21-9]: Vishvambhara ("He who sustains the universe") is the name given to the Lord at His naming (CB Adi 4). The red-bordered cloth is the
bridegroom's wedding garment. Here too the poet takes part in the lila, clothing the Lord (cf. 3.6).

## 5. Narahari — "veśa vanāiyā sahacare…" (GPT1 pp. 86–87, no. 20; BR)
*His friends, having dressed Nimai, give Him a golden mirror; even the gods cannot take their eyes off Him; Shachi and her friends perform
auspicious rites; the young wives look on from afar; bowing to His mother, Gaura sets out for the wedding amid Vedic chanting and music.
Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^21-10]

**5.1.** Having dressed [Him], His friends put into His hand a golden mirror like the moon.

**5.2.** Seeing the attire of Nimaichand — what to speak of others? — even the gods cannot turn their eyes away.

**5.3.** Mother Shachi with her friends performs many auspicious rites, gazing at her son's face.

**5.4.** The young wives, standing at a distance, cannot keep their composure as they look at Gorachand.

**5.5.** The women cry "ulu-lu"; the news of the joyful wedding has filled the world.

**5.6.** Bowing at His mother's feet, Gaura Raya sets out to be married.[^21-11]

**5.7.** The brahmanas chant the Vedas; instruments of many kinds resound — the sound pierces the sky.

**5.8.** Who can tell of this merriment? Narahari swims in that ocean of happiness.

[^21-10]: GPT1 — pp. 86–87, no. 20 (kamoda; scan, PDF pp. 345–346); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 20. The catalogue did not know it (new row NG-283, chapter 20).
BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 792; ed. 1960, vv. 1301–1308; the 1960 editor's heading before the next pada: "the wedding of Sri Nimai"). Variant: 5.6 BR
"gaurarāya" — the same. Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. Line 5.1 is the refrain (dhru).
[^21-11]: The Lord bows to His mother, setting an example of respect for one's parents. On the young wives (5.4) see note 5.

## 6. Narahari — "āju godhūli samaya śubhakṣaṇa…" (GPT1 p. 87, no. 21; BR)
*The wedding procession: at the auspicious hour of dusk Gaura in wedding attire mounts the palanquin and, surrounded by brahmanas, moves
slowly to Vallabha's house; praises, dances, songs, a sea of music; the gods gaze unblinking from the sky and descend unseen to earth;
crowds, hundreds of lamps, moonlight; the Earth, the Ganga, beasts and birds rejoice. Raga bhupali. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** —
the pada is in the BR; ornate Vrajabuli.*[^21-12]

**6.1.** Today, at the auspicious hour of dusk, Gaura — the jewel of virtues, enchanter of the world — is in the attire enjoined for a wedding,
and the beauty of His tender body seems to brim over;
crushing the pride of millions of Kamas, lotus-eyed, delighting people's hearts, glancing in all four directions with a soft smile, He mounts
the palanquin, shining.[^21-13]

**6.2.** Surrounded by brahmanas He moves towards Vallabha's house — His gait very slow and sweet; the bards proclaim abundant blessings, the
world is filled with cries of "jaya, jaya";
dancers dance, beating out "thai-tata", how many singers are absorbed in song to "thonga-thongina"; composing lovely [songs on His] deeds,
tuning the mode, the artists rain down sweet rasa.

**6.3.** How many instruments play in every manner, the rhythmic syllables sound without a break; skilled musicians, as if churning the ocean of
music, swim in it;
in the sky the gods are utterly absorbed — they gaze steadily with unblinking eyes; thrilling all over they descend unseen to earth — what
delight in their hearts!

**6.4.** Countless men and women run; the broad road is incomparably beautiful; hundreds upon hundreds of lamps blaze, the moon, lord of the
night, sheds its light;
the Earth has blossomed in great joy, the waters of the Jahnavi surge; what can the servant Narahari say? — beasts and birds all float in
happiness.

[^21-12]: GPT1 — p. 87, no. 21 (bhupali; scan, PDF p. 346); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 21 (catalogue: NG-038). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 792–793; ed. 1960,
vv. 1309–1312). Variants: 6.1 GPT1 "chalakāya", "jhalakāya", BR "chalakaye", "jhalakaye"; 6.2 GPT1 "vandīgaṇa, bhuri maṅgalabhaṇa", BR "vandigaṇa bhaṇa bhuri maṅgala"; 6.3 GPT1
"janu", BR "yanu" (both "as if"). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. The syllables "thai-tata",
"thonga-thongina" imitate the dancers' counting and the strokes of the drums (cf. note 11 of chapter 20).
[^21-13]: Dusk (godhūli, "the hour of cow-dust", when the herds return home) is an auspicious hour for a wedding. The palanquin (caudola) is the litter
on which the bridegroom is carried to the bride's house. The wedding with Lakshmipriya takes place in the house of her father, Vallabha
Acharya (CB Adi 10).

## 7. Narahari — "gorācām̐dera vivāha dekhivāre…" (GPT1 pp. 87–88, no. 22; BR)
*The young wives of Nadia, in fine dress and ornaments, their bells ringing, hurry to see Gorachand's wedding; they talk among themselves,
smiling under their veils; their glances dart in all directions; seeing the poet's Lord enter Vallabha's house, they are beside themselves
with joy. Raga bhupali. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^21-14]

**7.1.** To see Gorachand's wedding, with what longing the young wives of Nadia run — not one can keep her composure!

**7.2.** Incomparable attire and garments, bodies adorned with ornaments — their charm glitters and shines;
as they walk, the bells of their girdles and the anklets on their feet ring; with their sweet gait they light up the road.

**7.3.** Absorbed in that feeling, how much they say to one another — how charmingly! — the rings at their nostrils sway;
on their lovely faces hidden by veils, a soft, soft smile; whom would the radiance of that smile not enchant?

**7.4.** Darkened with collyrium, delighting the heart, surpassing the khanjana bird, their lovely glances [dart] on every side;
and, seeing Narahari's Lord of life entering Vallabha's house, they are beside themselves with joy.[^21-15]

[^21-14]: GPT1 — pp. 87–88, no. 22 (bhupali; scan, PDF pp. 346–347); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 22 (catalogue: NG-039). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 793; ed.
1960, vv. 1313–1316). Variants: 7.4 GPT1 "uthalaye", BR-1960 "ulaye" (OCR?); 7.3 GPT1 "veśara", BR "vesara" (the same word, "nose-ring"). Not in PK, KGC, PS,
the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. Line 7.1 is the refrain (dhru).
[^21-15]: The khanjana is the wagtail, in Indian poetry an image of lively, restless eyes. "Narahari's Lord of life" (narahari parāṇanātha) is the poet's Lord, a
turn of the signature (like "Narahari's Lord", note 34 of chapter 20); the young wives' joy is festive delight at the wedding (see note 5).

## 8. Narahari — "vallabha-bhavane gorā rāya…" (GPT1 pp. 88–89, no. 23; BR)
*The wedding in Vallabha's house: Vishvambhara stands on a little board under the wedding canopy; the bride's mother with the married women
welcomes the bridegroom, circling Him seven times with seven lamps; Vallabha Acharya brings his daughter, seats her on a throne and by the
rite gives Lakshmi to the son of Shachi; Vedic chanting, cries of joy, music; from their celestial chariots the gods invisibly shower the
wedding with flowers. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^21-16]

**8.1.** Gora Raya in Vallabha's house increases the great joy of Vallabha Mishra.

**8.2.** Vallabha, rejoicing, has the auspicious rites enjoined for a wedding performed.

**8.3.** Vishvambhara, His heart glad, stood on the little board under the wedding canopy.[^21-17]

**8.4.** The movements of His body steal one's life; the radiance of His form lights up the ten directions.

**8.5.** To what shall His moonlike face be compared? With a slight smile it destroys the pride of nectar.

**8.6.** The glance of His eyes is lovely: whomever He looks at cannot hold his composure.

**8.7.** At the roots of His ears, makara-shaped earrings; whom would the arrangement of His curling hair not enchant?

**8.8.** Armlets and bracelets sit beautifully; seeing that beauty, how many Madanas die of shame!

**8.9.** To welcome such a bridegroom, the bride's mother comes out with the married women.

**8.10.** Who can describe that beauty? With seven lamps in her hands she circles Him seven times.

**8.11.** Wondrous are the women's rites! Having welcomed the bridegroom, all go into the house.

**8.12.** Fortunate Vallabha Acharya had his daughter brought to perform the kanya-dana — the giving of the daughter.

**8.13.** They seated her on a divine throne — and it shone with the radiance of her body.

**8.14.** Her body is so tender, her smiling face surpasses the full moon.

**8.15.** She wears many-coloured garments; ornaments of many jewels glitter.

**8.16.** Such a daughter, with every prescribed rite, Mishra gave to the son of Shachi.[^21-18]

**8.17.** The brahmanas chant the Vedas; all the women of noble families cry "ulu-lu".

**8.18.** Instruments of every kind resound, dancers dance, the bhatas recite verses of praise.

**8.19.** The gods, mounting their celestial chariots, invisibly shower flowers, crying "jaya!".

**8.20.** Great happiness has spread through the world — how can Narahari tell of it with one mouth?

[^21-16]: GPT1 — pp. 88–89, no. 23 (kamoda; scan, PDF pp. 347–348); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 23 (catalogue: NG-040). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 794–795; ed.
1960, vv. 1317–1336). Variants: 8.3 GPT1 "sarasa hiyāya" ("with a heart full of rasa"), BR "haraṣa hiyāya" ("with a glad heart"); 8.9 GPT1 "āyogaṇa sāte", BR
"āigaṇa sāthe" (the same: married women); 8.17 GPT1 "kulera kāminī", BR "kulera ramaṇī"; 8.18 BR "rāyavāra". The GPT1 editor's notes on 8.3 and 8.9 are not
reproduced. Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
[^21-17]: The piri (piṛi) is a low wooden board on which the bridegroom stands or sits during the rite; choṛalā is the place of the wedding rite under the
canopy.
[^21-18]: Kanya-dana is the central rite of a Hindu wedding: the father gives his daughter to the bridegroom. The Lord's wedding with Lakshmipriya —
CB Adi 10; CC Adi 15. Lakshmipriya is Lakshmi Herself, the eternal energy of the Lord; the marriage is His lila (note 2).

## 9. Narahari — "gorā guṇamaṇi prāṇapriyā saha…" (GPT1 p. 89, no. 24; BR)
*The bridal chamber: Gora is in the chamber with His beloved; the women keep coming in and going out, joke, give Him betel to put into
Lakshmi's mouth, themselves offer Him betel, braid and loosen His hair, seat Lakshmi on His lap. Raga bhupali. **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^21-19]

**9.1.** Gora, the jewel of virtues, with His beloved, dear as life, passes the time in the bridal chamber;
the wives of noble families keep coming in and going out, full of merriment.

**9.2.** Some, inventing various pretexts, tease and laugh, laugh for the joy of their hearts;
another, placing betel in Gora's lotus hand, says, "Put it into Lakshmi's mouth!"

**9.3.** One offers betel to Gora's moonlike mouth — and her affection grows and grows;
another, longing to touch Him, braids His hair — and, loosening it, cannot contain herself.

**9.4.** Yet another, seating Lakshmi on Vishvambhara's lap, looks at them with a charming smile;
says Narahari: the rasa that surges in the bridal chamber has no comparison.[^21-20]

[^21-19]: GPT1 — p. 89, no. 24 (bhupali; scan, PDF p. 348); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 24 (catalogue: NG-041). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 795; ed. 1960, vv.
1337–1340). Variant: 9.1 GPT1 "śoja" (misprint), BR "se ye" — following the BR. Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
[^21-20]: Vasara (vāsara) is the first night after the wedding, which the couple spend in the chamber while the women of the bride's house keep them awake
joking with the bridegroom — a custom of the Bengali wedding. The women's jokes at the wedding are ritual merriment, not nagari-bhava;
Lakshmipriya is the eternal energy of the Lord (note 2), and the whole scene is the Lord's lila with His energy, not worldly love.

## 10. Narahari — "gorācām̐dera vivāha paradine…" (GPT1 p. 89, no. 25; BR)
*At dawn after the wedding the women run together to admire bride and bridegroom; Vallabha's fortunate wife rejoices; generous Vallabha
Mishra does everything for his son-in-law; Gaurahari, having performed the wedding rites, is glad; the gods praise Vallabha. Raga todi.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^21-21]

**10.1.** The day after Gorachand's wedding, at daybreak — how much joy surges up!

**10.2.** The wives of noble families run together from every side; seeing the beauty of bride and bridegroom, all delight their eyes.

**10.3.** How fortunate is Vallabha's wife! Having gained a jewel of a son-in-law, she does not know where she is.

**10.4.** Mishra Vallabha is generous beyond measure: what does he not do for the good of his son-in-law!

**10.5.** And Vallabha's son-in-law, Gaurahari, having performed the wedding rites, is filled with joy.

**10.6.** All has been completed as is proper; says Narahari: the gods praise Vallabha.

[^21-21]: GPT1 — p. 89, no. 25 (todi; scan, PDF p. 348); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 25 (catalogue: NG-042). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 795–796; ed. 1960, vv.
1341–1346; the catalogue and the chapter plan took it for "GPT only" — the search by witnesses missed it because of garbled OCR; it was found by
reading the BR straight through). Variant: 10.3 GPT1 "jāmātāratna", BR "jāmātā-ratana" (the same). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or
the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.

## 11. Narahari — "gaura gokulacandra calu nija gehe…" (GPT1 p. 89, no. 26; BR)
*At dawn Gaura sets out for His home; Vallabha in private speaks lovingly to Him of Lakshmi; the women on the road weep, Lakshmi's friends
know that her Lord is departing; conches, kettledrums, dancing, songs, Vedic chanting, praises — the world is full of cries of "jaya". Raga
todi. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR; Vrajabuli.*[^21-22]

**11.1.** When the night gave way to dawn, Gaura, the Moon of Gokula, set out for His own home;
in private Vallabha tenderly said much to Him — he spoke of Lakshmi.

**11.2.** Looking at the road, all the women cannot restrain themselves — tears stream from their eyes:
Lakshmi's friends know that Lakshmi's Lord is departing.[^21-23]

**11.3.** Conches, kettledrums and great drums sound, instruments of every kind;
troupes of dancers dance, skilled singers sing songs without end.

**11.4.** The brahmanas chant the Vedas, the bards proclaim His virtues;
the whole world is full of cries of "jaya, jaya" — what a pastime of Narahari's Lord [returning] home!

[^21-22]: GPT1 — p. 89, no. 26 (todi; scan, PDF p. 348); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 26 (catalogue: NG-043). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 796; ed. 1960, vv.
1347–1350). Variants: 11.1 GPT1 "kahala lakhimī ki vāta", BR "kahala lakhimika vāta" ("spoke of Lakshmi") — following the BR; 11.2 GPT1 "karava payāna" ("will depart"),
BR "kayala payāna" ("departed"). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
[^21-23]: By custom the bride leaves her father's house after the wedding for her husband's house; the father entrusts his daughter to his son-in-law,
and her friends lament the parting.

## 12. Narahari — "vivāha kariyā viśvambhara…" (GPT1 p. 90, no. 27; BR)
*Vishvambhara returns home with His young wife; the married women perform auspicious rites; Shachi, taking her daughter-in-law on her lap,
blesses her with paddy and durva grass and gazes again and again at the faces of her son and daughter-in-law; the Lord gladdens everyone
with sweet words and fulfils the wishes of the bhatas, dancers and musicians. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada
is in the BR.*[^21-24]

**12.1.** Having married, Vishvambhara returned from His father-in-law's house to His own home.

**12.2.** That joy I cannot describe: the women devoted to their husbands perform all the auspicious rites.

**12.3.** Shachi, taking her daughter-in-law on her lap, blessed her, [showering her] abundantly with paddy and durva grass.[^21-25]

**12.4.** There is no limit to Sri Shachi's happiness: how many times she looks at her son's face and her daughter-in-law's face!

**12.5.** Seeing the beauty of Lakshmi and Vishvambhara, no one can turn away their unblinking eyes.

**12.6.** Gora Raya, enchanter of the world, gladdens everyone with sweet words.

**12.7.** For the bhatas, dancers, musicians and all the rest He fulfilled every wish.

**12.8.** Narahari cries aloud: "Oh, that I might see such merriment in Nadia!"

[^21-24]: GPT1 — p. 90, no. 27 (kamoda; scan, PDF p. 349); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 27 (catalogue: NG-044). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 796; ed. 1960, vv.
1351–1358). Variant: 12.4 GPT1 "śrīśacī sukhera nāhi pāra… dekhe kata vāra", BR "śrīśacī-snehera nāi pāra… cumbe kata vāra" ("there is no limit to Shachi's
tenderness… how many times she kisses"). In the BR, straight after the pada, Ishana tells Srinivasa: "I saw this wedding merriment with my own eyes"
(v. 1359) — whereas the signature of the pada voices the poet's wish to see such merriment (12.8): so might speak a poet who had not seen the
wedding — one more argument for Chakravarti. Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
[^21-25]: Paddy and durva grass (dhānya dūrvvā) are auspicious gifts with which a newly married couple is blessed.

## 13. Narahari — "lakṣmī prāya lakṣmī ṭhākurāṇī…" (GPT1 p. 90, no. 28)
*Life with Lakshmipriya: Lakshmi serves her mother-in-law and her husband day and night; Nimai Pandita teaches countless students who come
from every side — as if Brihaspati were teaching in Nadia; a pupil of Gangadasa, He poses such tricky questions that no one can answer; in
the evening He enjoys learning with His students by the Ganga; His fame spreads in every direction. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: not
established** — GPT only; by its place in the cycle and its closeness to the BR narrative, rather Chakravarti.*[^21-26]

**13.1.** Lakshmi Thakurani, like Lakshmi Herself, serves her mother-in-law day and night.

**13.2.** To her husband — unwavering devotion: she serves her husband day and night.

**13.3.** Nimai Pandita gives lessons; countless students come from every side.

**13.4.** Such learning is to be found nowhere — as if Brihaspati were giving lessons in Nadia.

**13.5.** Vishvambhara, pupil of Gangadasa, versed in every science, is an ocean of learning.

**13.6.** Nimai poses such tricky questions that no one is able to answer them.[^21-27]

**13.7.** In the evening, taking His students, He goes to the bank of the Ganga and delights in learning.

**13.8.** In every direction — the fame of Nimai; Narahari is beside himself with bliss.

[^21-26]: GPT1 — p. 90, no. 28 (kamoda; scan, PDF p. 349; in the OCR the signature is garbled — "narahabri"); GPT2 — section 2.3, no. 28. The catalogue made
from the OCR of GPT2 did not know it (new row NG-284, chapter 20). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani;
but in the BR, straight after the cycle of wedding padas (no. 12), Ishana says the same in prose: Lakshmi serves Ai, her Lord is absorbed with
His students in the rasa of learning, all the scholars of Nadia honour Vishvambhara (ed. 1960, vv. 1360–1364). C. Line 13.2 is metrically
incomplete in GPT1. Nimai Pandita teaches — CC Adi 16. After it GPT1 (nos. 29–35) gives the Lord's
learning, the journey to East Bengal and Lakshmipriya's departure — padas of Vrindavana Dasa, Lochana and Govinda Ghosha (no Narahari
signatures; the pada of Govinda Ghosha is PK 1597, chapter 1, no. 1).
[^21-27]: "Like Lakshmi" is a turn of praise; according to the CB and CC Lakshmipriya is Lakshmi Herself (note 2). Brihaspati is the preceptor of
the gods. Tricky questions (phām̐ki) are knotty problems of grammar and logic with which students and pandits in the schools of Navadvipa tested
one another.

## 14. Narahari — "nadīyā-nagare haila dhvani…" (GPT1 p. 93, section 2.4, no. 1; BR)
*Section "The second marriage". The news spreads through Nadia: Gora is marrying again — Sanatana Mishra is giving Him his daughter Vishnupriya,
peerless in beauty and virtue; tomorrow is the adhivasa; the women cannot wait for morning to go to Shachi's for the water rite. Raga kamoda.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^21-28][^21-29]

**14.1.** Through the town of Nadia the news rang out: "Gora, the jewel of virtues, is marrying again!

**14.2.** Fortunate Sanatana Mishra will give his daughter to Nimaichand.

**14.3.** The maiden's name is Vishnupriya — in beauty and virtue she has no equal in the world.[^21-30]

**14.4.** Tomorrow will be the auspicious adhivasa — we shall see the wedding festivities to our eyes' content.

**14.5.** How soon will the night be over? Let us go to Sri Shachi's house for the water rite!"

**14.6.** Narahari says: "I think it was your eagerness that brought the night to an end."

[^21-28]: Before section 2.4, a brief note on the lila. While the Lord was travelling in East Bengal, Lakshmipriya left this world: according to the
CB and CC, the "snake of separation" from the Lord bit her, and she departed with her mind fixed on His feet; on His return the Lord consoled His
mother with instruction on the transience of everything worldly (CB Adi 14; CC Adi 16; Murari 1.11–1.12). Lakshmipriya is the eternal energy of
the Lord; her departure, too, is lila. In GPT1 the departure of Lakshmipriya is the subject of padas by Lochana and Govinda Ghosha (2.3, nos.
32–35; no Narahari signatures). Then Shachi, wishing to marry her son again, through the matchmaker Kashinatha arranges His marriage with
Vishnupriya, the daughter of Sanatana Mishra (CB Adi 15; Murari 1.13–1.14). In the BR this account is in the 12th wave (ed. 1960, vv. 1372–1396):
according to Chakravarti, Shachi herself noticed Vishnupriya at a ghat of the Ganga, the match was arranged by Kashinatha Pandita, and the
expenses of a wedding "like a prince's" were taken on by Buddhimanta Khan and Mukunda Sanjaya.
[^21-29]: GPT1 — p. 93, section 2.4 ("the second marriage"), no. 1 (kamoda; scan, PDF p. 352); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 1 (catalogue: NG-045). BR — 12th wave
(ed. 1912, p. 799; ed. 1960, vv. ≈1397–1402: the first line falls on a part lost in the OCR), straight after the account of the match; then the BR
gives in sequence the padas of section 2.4 nos. 2–16 (nos. 15–24 of this chapter and nos. 2–4, 7, 11, not translated here). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the
Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
[^21-30]: Vishnupriya is the eternal consort of the Lord, His own Bhu-shakti (the energy of the Earth); like Lakshmipriya (note 2), she is not a worldly
wife but His own energy, and the wedding with her is the Lord's lila.

## 15. Narahari — "yuvatī-yūtha mati gati ati adabhuta…" (GPT1 p. 94, no. 5; BR; GCC)
*The morning of the adhivasa: lines of young women who have come to Shachi's house bow down at her feet like young golden creepers weighed
down with flowers; they stretch out their hands to take the dust of her feet and, covering their faces with the ends of their veils, smile
softly. Raga belavali. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR and in the Gaura-charita-chintamani; Vrajabuli.*[^21-31]

**15.1.** Lines of young women — wondrous their thoughts and their gait — bow down charmingly;
slender, they bend like young golden creepers under the weight of clusters of flowers.

**15.2.** At the edge of [Shachi's] lovely feet they lay their heads — their dark, lustrous hair loosened;
they look like a rain-cloud fallen to the earth with a swarm of motionless lightnings.

**15.3.** Gently, gently they stretch out their palms, tender as shoots, longing to take the rare dust [of her feet];
their nails flash — as if jewels had come in reverence to pay homage with peerless zeal.

**15.4.** Covering their lotus faces with the ends of their veils, they smile softly, softly, and radiance spreads around —
as if, carefully straining fresh nectar, they sprinkle it abundantly, says Narahari Dasa.[^21-32]

[^21-31]: GPT1 — p. 94, no. 5 (belavali; scan, PDF p. 353); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 5 (catalogue: NG-048). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 800–801; ed. 1960, vv.
1415–1418). GCC — ch. 9 ("the desires of the nagaris of Navadvipa", morning), pada 19: there it stands among padas on the townswomen-nagaris, while
in the BR and GPT it is among the wedding padas. Variants: 15.2 GPT1 and BR "śithila saroruha" ("a loosened lotus"), GCC "śithila śiroruha" ("loosened hair") —
translated following the GCC; GPT1 "kira caratachu", BR "thira-cara tachu" — following the BR; 15.4 GPT1 "siñcita ghanabhaṇa", BR and GCC "siñcata ghana bhaṇa". Not in PK, KGC,
PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. The preceding GPT pada (no. 4, signed Ghanashyama; outside the appendix) describes how these women come to Ai
(Shachi) and strew her feet with champaka buds; the next (no. 16) how Shachi blesses them.
[^21-32]: Subtle Vrajabuli similes: the women bowing in dark garments with loosened hair are a cloud, their golden bodies the lightnings; their nails
are jewels come to bow at her feet; their smile is strained nectar. On the motif of the women of Nadia see note 5.

## 16. Narahari — "śacī jagata-jananī jana-nītavida…" (GPT1 p. 95, no. 6; BR; GCC)
*Shachi, mother of the world, lovingly receives the young wives, asks each about her welfare and blesses her, placing a hand on her head; they
answer with a smile: "Having seen these auspicious feet, how could misfortune remain with us?" — and stand with joined palms; Shachi's eyes
fill with tears of tenderness. Raga todi. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR and in the Gaura-charita-chintamani.*[^21-33]

**16.1.** Shachi — mother of the world, who knows how to treat people, renowned for her lovely ways —
regarding all as her daughters-in-law, dearer than her own life, shows them all the greatest love.

**16.2.** Asking each one about her welfare, she places a hand on her head and blesses her abundantly:
"May your fortune ever grow; may your husbands and all your kin live long and prosper!"

**16.3.** Hearing this, the young wives smile inwardly and, floating in happiness, speak sweet words:
"Oh, tell us — having seen these auspicious feet, why should any misfortune stay here?"

**16.4.** Having shyly said a little, they stand on with joined palms;
the mother of Narahari's Lord of life, seeing this, is overcome with tenderness — her eyes brim with tears.[^21-34]

[^21-33]: GPT1 — p. 95, no. 6 (todi; scan, PDF p. 354); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 6 (catalogue: NG-049). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 801; ed. 1960, vv. 1419–1422).
GCC — ch. 9, pada 21 (there "jananī-tattvavida", "kara yuṛi nikaṭe dām̐ṛāyā rahe" — "they stand near with joined palms"). Variant: 16.3 GPT1 "āgā", BR and GCC
"ogo" — following the BR. Not in PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^21-34]: Shachi is the Lord's mother, His eternal associate in vatsalya-rasa; blessing the wives of Nadia, she wishes them worldly welfare, as befits a
mother in the lila — and they reply that after the darshan of her feet no misfortune can remain: that is the highest good.

## 17. Narahari — "gorā-rase bhāsi hāsi hāsi lahu lahu…" (GPT1 pp. 95–96, no. 8; BR)
*The water rite on the day of the adhivasa: at Shachi's bidding the women of noble families, young and mature, dress and go in lines for the
water with auspicious articles, lotuses and trays; girdles and anklets ring, musicians go in front; celestial women invisibly mingle with them;
returning, they distribute oil and turmeric and perform the women's rites. Raga not specified ("yatha-raga"). **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^21-35]

**17.1.** Floating in Gora's rasa, smiling softly, softly, the women of noble families rejoice.

**17.2.** At the bidding of Shachi-devi they dress for the water rite — what merriment in their hearts!
Beauties in early, middle and full youth, in lines, their gait so sweet;
restless their lovely sidelong glances, manifold their graces — there is no comparison for them.

**17.3.** They wear garments of many kinds, on every limb ornaments of gold and jewels;
veils gleam on their faces, peerlessly lovely braids sway on their backs;
some carry auspicious articles in their hands, some fresh lotuses,
on the heads of others trays shine, beautifully covered with silk.

**17.4.** As they walk, the bells on their girdles ring — "jhani-jhini, jhani-jhinini ni-ni-ni",
the anklets on their feet — "runu-jhunu, runu-jhunu jhu-jhu" — delighting the ear with their sound;
in front the musicians walk joyfully, playing sweet rhythms —
"dha-dha dhing ning ning dho dhiki dhikatadhenna": with many instruments they steal away composure.

**17.5.** Invisible celestial women have merrily mingled with the wives of Nadia;
having performed the water rite, all enter the house — who does not say "Blessed, blessed, blessed!"?
They distribute oil, turmeric and the rest — who can tell all the women's rites?
Who does not swim in that ocean of happiness? Narahari gives himself to the Lord in this [joy].[^21-36]

[^21-35]: GPT1 — pp. 95–96, no. 8 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF pp. 354–355); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 8 (catalogue: NG-051). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 802; ed. 1960, vv.
1429–1432). Variants: 17.4 GPT1 "vālaka" ("boys"), BR "vādaka" ("musicians") — following the BR; the bells in the BR "rini jhini rini jhinini"; 17.5 GPT1 "bhuvane"
("into the world"), BR "bhavane" ("into the house") — following the BR; GPT1 "narahari pahum̐ nichani tāhe", BR "narahari vahu nichani tāhe" ("Narahari again and again gives
himself for that"). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. Line 17.1 is the opening couplet. The chapter plan had
provisionally assigned this pada to the nagari section ("floating in Gora's rasa"); in substance it describes the wedding water rite (cf. no. 2), and
it is translated here — with the caveat of note 5.
[^21-36]: "Floating in Gora's rasa" — in joy over the Lord whose wedding is being celebrated; on the motif of the women of Nadia see note 5. The celestial
women come invisibly to take part in the Lord's wedding (cf. no. 21).

## 18. Narahari — "śacīdevī ulasita haiñā…" (GPT1 p. 96, no. 9; BR)
*Shachi with the married women goes to the Ganga and worships her with flowers and sandal — and the Suradhuni surges, holding in her heart the feet
of Shachi's son; then she worships Shashthi — and Shashthi, rejoicing, praises her own good fortune; the women return home; at home Shachi
performs the auspicious rites. Raga not specified. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^21-37]

**18.1.** Shachi-devi, rejoicing, goes to the bank of the Ganga to worship the Ganga, taking the married women with her.

**18.2.** With various flowers, perfumes and sandal paste she carefully worships the Jahnavi;
and the Suradhuni surges unceasingly, holding in her heart the feet of Shachi's son.[^21-38]

**18.3.** Instruments play beautifully; she goes to the place of Shashthi and worships Shashthi with many offerings;
Shashthi, floating in happiness, praises her own good fortune — her heart overflows with the virtues of Gorachand.

**18.4.** With what longing the wives go home — how great the rejoicing in all their hearts!
Returning home, [Shachi] performs the auspicious rites — Narahari cannot find a comparison.

[^21-37]: GPT1 — p. 96, no. 9 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF p. 355; in the OCR the number is garbled — "“ma pada"); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 9. **The catalogue did not
know it** (new row NG-285). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 803; ed. 1960, vv. 1433–1436). Variants: 18.1 GPT1 "āyo suyogaṇa", BR "āiha-suihagaṇa" (the same:
married women); 18.4 GPT1 "vadhūgaṇa", BR "vandhugaṇa" ("kinsfolk"). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. Line 18.1 is the
refrain (dhru).
[^21-38]: The Ganga flows from the feet of the Lord (Bhag. 5.17), so, says the poet, she "holds in her heart" Gaura's feet. Shashthi is the goddess who
protects children; the worship of the Ganga and of Shashthi before a son's wedding is a custom of Bengali mothers, and Shachi follows it in the
lila. The Gaudiya tradition does not worship the demigods for separate ends; and the poet shows that the Ganga and Shashthi themselves rejoice as
servants of the Lord.

## 19. Narahari — "gorā-vidhu adhivāsa-sukhe…" (GPT1 p. 96, no. 10; BR)
*The bridegroom's adhivasa: everyone hurries into the house; Gora's dear ones skilfully perform the rites and distribute garlands and sandal; in
the midst of the assembly the son of Shachi shines like Indra among the gods; Sanatana Mishra with his people brings gifts, touches Him with
perfume and cannot take his eyes from His face; Vedic chanting, cries of joy, praises, music. Raga not specified. **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^21-39]

**19.1.** Who, in the joy of the Gora-moon's adhivasa, would not enter the house and sit down?
Gora's dear ones show ever new skill in the rites of the adhivasa.

**19.2.** To each they give garlands, sandal paste and the rest — who can tell of that great merriment?
In the midst of the assembly the son of Shachi shines — like Purandara surrounded by the gods.

**19.3.** Mishra Sanatana with his people came at the auspicious moment with various gifts;
touching [Him] with perfume, he gazes with unblinking eyes at Gora's face.[^21-40]

**19.4.** The brahmanas chant the Vedas, the women raise cries of joy, the bhatas recite lovely praises;
Narahari sings the rasa of the adhivasa, the musicians play on many instruments.

[^21-39]: GPT1 — p. 96, no. 10 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF p. 355); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 10 (catalogue: NG-052). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 803–804; ed. 1960, vv.
1437–1440). Variants: 19.1 GPT1 "bhūvana mājhe" ("into the world"), BR "bhavana-mājhe" ("into the house") — following the BR; GPT1 "gorā priyāgaṇa" ("Gora's
beloveds"), BR "gorā-priyagaṇa" ("Gora's dear ones") — following the BR; 19.2 GPT1 "ke kata kare", BR "ke kata kabe" ("who can tell") — following the BR. Not in PK,
KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
[^21-40]: Purandara is Indra, king of the gods. Sanatana Mishra is Vishnupriya's father, the "Raja-pandita" of Navadvipa (CB Adi 15); by custom the
bride's father comes to the bridegroom's house and performs his adhivasa, touching him with perfume (cf. no. 21 of chapter 20).

## 20. Narahari — "miśra sanātana harṣa mane…" (GPT1 pp. 97–98, no. 12; BR)
*The bride's adhivasa in the house of Sanatana Mishra: brahmanas bring from Ai's house all that is needed for the rite, the noble brahmanas of
Nadia gather in the house of the Raja-pandita; Mishra's wife and her friends perform auspicious rites; Vishnupriya, glancing shyly around,
comes out and sits on a throne in the midst of the assembly — her beauty eclipses the moon; all touch her with perfume and bless her. Raga not
specified. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^21-41]

**20.1.** Mishra Sanatana, his heart glad, at the auspicious moment performs his daughter's adhivasa.

**20.2.** Brahmanas from Ai's house came in haste, bringing everything needed for the adhivasa.

**20.3.** The brahmanas and worthy people of Nadia — all go to the house of the Raja-pandita.

**20.4.** Mishra with great respect seats everyone, presenting garlands, sandal and the rest.

**20.5.** What wondrous beauty in the courtyard! All sit arranged in a lovely circle.

**20.6.** Mishra's wife with her friends performs so many auspicious rites that I cannot tell them.

**20.7.** Glancing shyly on every side, Vishnupriya came out of the house.

**20.8.** In the midst of the assembly she sits on a throne — everyone gazes at her beauty with unblinking eyes.

**20.9.** Her garments and ornaments become her well; with the radiance of every limb she lights up the world.

**20.10.** To what shall she be compared — to gold, to lightning? The sweetness of her face steals the moon's pride.

**20.11.** Who can describe all that beauty? Touching her with perfume, all bless her.

**20.12.** The women raise cries of joy, the brahmanas chant the Vedas without pause.

**20.13.** The bhatas praise auspicious deeds, many instruments sound, skilled singers sing songs.

**20.14.** How much merriment in Mishra's house! Narahari floats in that ocean of happiness.[^21-42]

[^21-41]: GPT1 — pp. 97–98, no. 12 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF pp. 356–357); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 12 (catalogue: NG-053). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 805; ed. 1960, vv.
1445–1458). Variants: 20.13 GPT1 "sucarita", "guṇījane", BR "svacarita", "guṇigaṇe" — minor. Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
Before it in the GPT (no. 11) stands an ornate pada on the bridegroom's adhivasa signed Ghanashyama ("ghanaśyāma hiyā"; = BR vv. 1441–1444) — outside the
appendix.
[^21-42]: The Raja-pandita is Sanatana Mishra, the court scholar (CB Adi 15; note 40). Vishnupriya is the eternal energy of the Lord (note 30); as at
Lakshmipriya's adhivasa (no. 22 of chapter 20), all the people of Nadia come to bless her.

## 21. Narahari — "adhivāsa divasera pare…" (GPT1 p. 98, no. 13; BR)
*The wedding day: through Nadia rings "today is Nimai's wedding"; to see it there come invisibly Shiva with Parvati, Ananta with his
associates, the residents of Vaikuntha, Brahma with his consort, Indra with Shachi, the gods, the celestial women, gandharvas and kinnaras,
the heavenly dancers, the divine sages; the Yamuna and the Ganga surge; the brahmanas of Nadia gather in Nimai's house; Gaurahari, having
performed the wedding rites, sits in joy. Raga not specified. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^21-43]

**21.1.** On the day after the adhivasa, joy grows in the new town of Nadia.

**21.2.** Everywhere people run about, saying: "Today is Nimai's wedding!"

**21.3.** The world is full of cries of "jaya, jaya" — who would not long to see the wedding?

**21.4.** Shiva in joy, with Parvati, leaving Kailasa, comes to see the wedding.

**21.5.** Ananta with his own associates remains here unseen to behold the wedding.

**21.6.** All the residents of Vaikuntha, saying "we shall see the wedding", are restless at heart.

**21.7.** The four-faced [Brahma] with his consort longs every moment to see the wedding.

**21.8.** The lord of the gods, taking Shachi with him, dresses in great joy to see the wedding.[^21-44]

**21.9.** The gods say with zeal: "We shall see the wedding, staying in the Lord's house!"

**21.10.** The celestial women have resolved: "We shall make merry at the wedding together with the wives of Nadia!"

**21.11.** The gandharvas and kinnaras think: "We shall join the artists in song and music at the wedding!"

**21.12.** Indra's dancers say: "We shall dress for the wedding together with the dancers of Nadia!"

**21.13.** The divine sages, rejoicing at heart, long so much to see the wedding!

**21.14.** The Yamuna and the Jahnavi surge; the Earth rejoices in the delight of the wedding festivities.

**21.15.** The brahmanas and worthy people of Nadia — all go to the wedding at Nimai's house.

**21.16.** The son of Shachi, Gaurahari, having performed the rites enjoined for the wedding, sits [among them] in joy.

**21.17.** Gazing at the Lord's moonlike face, how much they say — no one can master his heart.

**21.18.** How much auspiciousness arises here! How can Narahari tell of it with one mouth?

[^21-43]: GPT1 — p. 98, no. 13 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF p. 357); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 13 (catalogue: NG-054). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 806; ed. 1960, vv. 1459–1476;
two lines, 1469–1470, fall on a part lost in the 1960 OCR; the 1960 editor's heading — "the wedding of Sri Nimai"). Variants: 21.13 BR "devṛṣi"; 21.15
BR-1960 "vrāhmaṇī(?)" — OCR. Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
[^21-44]: "The lord of the gods" is Indra; Shachi here is his consort (not the Lord's mother). Ananta is Ananta-Shesha, the thousand-headed servant of the
Lord. All the demigods and the residents of Vaikuntha themselves come to the Lord's wedding as His servants — thus the poet shows that Gaura is the
Supreme Lord Himself.

## 22. Narahari — "gorā rasamaya sukhera ālaya…" (GPT1 p. 98, no. 14; BR)
*The bridegroom's wedding bath (before the second wedding): the women, crying "ulu-lu", gaze at His face; some tremble, others anoint Him with
perfumes and turmeric, rub oil into His curls, bathe Him with Ganga water, dry Him with a towel and clothe Him in a dry red-bordered cloth. Raga
not specified. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^21-45]

**22.1.** Gora, full of rasa, abode of joy, takes the bath enjoined before the wedding;
the wives of noble families, crying "ulu-lu", gaze at His lovely moonlike face.

**22.2.** Some, at the breeze coming from that body, tremble again and again — more than lightning;
others, longing to touch Him, cannot master themselves as they anoint Him with perfumes, turmeric and the rest.

**22.3.** One, rubbing oil into His lovely curls, feels so much merriment rise in her heart;
another bathes Him with Ganga water — manifold her movements, beyond compare.

**22.4.** Yet another, half-smiling, floating in rasa, dries His body, taking a towel in her hands;
they clothe Him in a dry red-bordered cloth — Narahari is in great merriment over it.[^21-46]

[^21-45]: GPT1 — p. 98, no. 14 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF p. 357); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 14 (catalogue: NG-055; the catalogue's first line "(gāra samaya…" is a garbling of
"gorā rasamaya"). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 806–807; ed. 1960, vv. 1477–1480). Variant: 22.4 GPT1 "pidhāya e", BR "pim̐dhā-ae" (the same: "they clothe").
Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. Cf. the bath before the first wedding (no. 3).
[^21-46]: The trembling and the "longing to touch" of the women who perform the bridegroom's bath are an image of the Lord's all-attractive beauty,
conveyed in a lyrical manner; this is a wedding rite and merriment, not nagari-bhava (see note 5).

## 23. Narahari — "ki ānanda śacīra bhavane…" (GPT1 p. 99, no. 15; BR)
*After the bath Gaurahari sits on a wondrous throne; the married women perform auspicious rites; His dear ones come, cannot take their eyes off

**23.1.** What joy in Shachi's house! The married women perform the auspicious rites.

**23.2.** Having taken the bath enjoined before the wedding, Gaurahari sits on a wondrous throne.

**23.3.** The radiance of His form enchants the mind; His curling, glossy hair falls beautifully down His back.

**23.4.** His dear ones come to Gora's side — having looked once, they cannot turn their eyes away.

**23.5.** Intoxicated with great joy, all array Him in various ways in His wedding attire.

**23.6.** What can Narahari say? Let me die taking on myself the misfortunes of this peerless attire![^21-48]

[^21-47]: GPT1 — p. 99, no. 15 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF p. 358); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 15. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-286). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912,

or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
[^21-48]: "Taking on myself the misfortunes" (vālāi laiyā mari) is a homely formula of love: may every misfortune that threatens the beloved fall on me

## 24. Narahari — "nadīyāra śaśī rasika-śekhara…" (GPT1 p. 99, no. 16; BR)
*The bridegroom's wedding attire: the Moon of Nadia in auspicious wedding array — His body anointed, a crescent-shaped sandal tilaka on His
forehead, a crown of flowers on His head, His eyes lined with collyrium, makara earrings in His ears; paddy and durva tied with thread, a golden
mirror in His right hand. Raga not specified. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^21-49]

**24.1.** The Moon of Nadia, crown of the connoisseurs of rasa, shines beautifully in auspicious wedding attire;
His body anointed, on His forehead a lovely sandal tilaka shaped like a half-moon.

**24.2.** On His head a wondrous crown of many flowers: whom would its arrangement not enchant?
The line of collyrium at His eyes does not let the young chaste wives of noble families stay within the bounds of their families.[^21-50]

**24.3.** At the roots of His ears jewelled makara earrings; how the radiance of His cheeks flashes!
To His sweetly smiling face hosts of full moons offer themselves.

**24.4.** Paddy, durva and the rest tied with thread, and a beautiful golden mirror in His right hand;
says Narahari: seeing every limb adorned with ornaments, who can keep his composure?

[^21-49]: GPT1 — p. 99, no. 16 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF p. 358); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 16 (catalogue: NG-056). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 807; ed. 1960, vv. 1487–1490).
Variants: 24.4 GPT1 "dakṣiṇa dakṣiṇa kare" (the word repeated), BR "dakṣiṇa kare" — following the BR; 24.3 GPT1 "purṇima-cām̐dera", BR "pūrṇimā-cāndera". Not in PK, KGC,
PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. Next in GPT1 (no. 17 — signed Ghanashyama; no. 18 onwards — Narahari) and in the BR comes the
wedding procession to the house of Sanatana Mishra and the wedding (chapter 22).
[^21-50]: The praise of the bridegroom's beauty is expressed in a conventional turn of love poetry (a beauty before which women "do not stay within the
bounds of their families" is a familiar formula about Krishna); the poet speaks of the Lord's all-attractive beauty. Translated faithfully to the
author; on the position of the tradition see note 5.

# Chapter 22. Appendix. Padas signed "Narahari" from the Gaura-pada-tarangini — VI: the wedding with Vishnupriya; the beginning of the ashtakaliya

*Continuation of the appendix (the introductory note on the two Naraharis, on the arguments for attribution and on the marks in the
headings is in ch. 17). Chapter 22: the end of GPT section 2.4 "The second marriage" — the wedding procession to the house of Sanatana
Mishra, the reception of the bridegroom, the wedding, the gods and celestial women at the wedding, the bridal chamber (vasara), the morning
after the wedding and the Lord's return home with Vishnupriya (nos. 1–16; GPT 2.4 nos. 18–20, 22–34); the beginning of section 5.2
"Ashtakaliya" — the songs of Gaura's awakening at the end of the night (nos. 17–26; GPT 5.2 nos. 1–10). Narahari Chakravarti quotes all the
wedding padas of the chapter one after another in the 12th wave of the Bhakti-ratnakara (Ishana shows Srinivasa the house of Jagannatha
Mishra), and all the awakening songs in his Gaura-charita-chintamani (kiranas 2–3: the last part of the night and the awakening). Before
translation the signatures in these sections were checked throughout, in the OCR and on the scan; the Bhakti-ratnakara (ed. 1960, vv.
1491–1626) was read continuously. Not translated: 2.4 no. 17 — signed Ghanashyama (outside the appendix); no. 21 — a pada in nagari-bhava
(assigned to the section of nagari padas); nos. 35–38 — without the Narahari signature: an extract from Lochana Dasa's Chaitanya-mangala
(no. 38 is signed "dāsa trilocana"; translated with Lochana, *Chaitanya-mangala*, Adi-khanda, part 14, vv. ≈146–178); nos. 39–40 — Vrindavana Dasa (= CB Adi 15).
The base text is GPT1 (doubtful places from the scan), collated with GPT2, the BR (eds. 1912 and 1960) and the Gaura-charita-chintamani (ed.
1947); PK, KGC, PS and the Gita-chandrodaya have been checked. On Vishnupriya and the wedding rites as lila see note 2; on the motif of the
women of Nadia, note 5; on the ashtakaliya as eternal lila, note 36. The notes of the GPT editors are not reproduced.*

## 1. Narahari — "gaura rasika-śekharavara…" (GPT1 p. 100, section 2.4, no. 18; BR)
*The wedding procession: Gaura, surrounded by brahmanas, sets out for the wedding in a palanquin; instruments of the four kinds sound;
invisible celestial dancers dance together with earthly ones, the gandharvas sing with the singers; Ananta, Brahma, Shiva, Indra, Ganesha,
Parvati float in an ocean of joy; horses, elephants, guards, jesters, hundreds of banners; having gone round Nadia and paused on the bank of
the Suradhuni, the procession approaches Mishra's house. Raga not stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR; ornate
Vrajabuli.*[^22-1]

**1.1.** Gaura, best of the crowns of the connoisseurs of rasa, surrounded by His dear brahmanas — "joyfully I shall celebrate an auspicious
wedding!" — sets out, mounting the palanquin;
strings, metal, drums and winds — splendid instruments of the four kinds — sound in many manners: the sound has filled the vault of the sky.[^22-2]

**1.2.** All the instruments are splendid and new; the boom of the mardala increases the joy: "dho-dho dhigi taga dhilanga, dha-dha ni-ni
nidhiya";
invisible, the celestial dancers together with the [earthly] dancers dance the lasya without pause: "bhana taka-taka thai-thai-thai, ai ati
ni-ni-ni tiya".

**1.3.** Together with the singers, rejoicing, the gandharvas sing sweetly; shrutis, sweet gramas and the rest — in every manner they
display their delight;
the Thousand-mouthed One, Brahma, Mahesha, the lord of the gods with his retinue, Ganesha, Girija and others — how could they keep their
composure? — float in an ocean of joy.[^22-3]

**1.4.** Horses, elephants, many armed men; jesters display their arts; hundreds of banners and the like shine — the crowd blocks the road;
going round the town of Nadia, pausing again and again on the bank of the Suradhuni — near Mishra's house Narahari beholds this
splendour.

[^22-1]: GPT1 — p. 100, section 2.4 ("the second marriage"), no. 18 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF p. 359); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 18 (catalogue: NG-057). BR — 12th wave
(ed. 1912, pp. 809–810; ed. 1960, vv. 1495–1498), immediately after pada no. 17 on the same procession signed by Ghanashyama ("ghana ghanaśyāma hiya umatāaī";
= BR vv. 1491–1494 — outside the appendix); after it the BR gives all the wedding padas of this chapter one after another (vv. 1499–1614), then prose:
Vishnupriya's service to her mother-in-law and the Lord's journey to Gaya (vv. 1615–1625). Variants: 1.1 GPT1 "surata cira" (misprint?), BR "surucira" —
following the BR; 1.3 BR "surapati" — the same. Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. The wedding with Vishnupriya —
CB Adi 15; CC Adi 16; Murari 1.14.
[^22-2]: Vishnupriya is the eternal consort of the Lord, His own Bhu-shakti (the energy of the Earth); she is not a worldly wife but His own
energy, and the wedding with her is the Lord's lila (note 30 of chapter 21). The Lord is bound by nothing that is enjoined; He accepts the
wedding rites following the lila, for the joy of His mother and His associates (note 2 of chapter 21). So are all the padas of the chapter
about the Lord's "marrying" to be understood. The instruments "of the four kinds" (tata ghana ānaddha śuṣira) — strings, metal (cymbals, gongs),
skin-covered (drums) and winds — are the classical division of Indian music.
[^22-3]: As in the pada on the wedding day (no. 21 of chapter 21), the demigods gather at the Lord's wedding: Ananta-Shesha ("the Thousand-mouthed
One"), Brahma, Shiva (Mahesha), Indra ("the lord of the gods"), Ganesha, Parvati (Girija); invisible to men, they come to serve their Lord
and to behold His lila. The gandharvas are the celestial singers; shrutis and gramas are the intervals and scales of Indian music; lasya is
the tender, "feminine" kind of dance.

## 2. Narahari — "gorācām̐dera vivāha dekhivāre…" (GPT1 p. 100, no. 19; BR)
*The wives of noble families, with great longing, adorn themselves to see Gorachand's wedding: collyrium, braids with golden clasps,
sindura and sandal, necklaces, flowers in their ears, silk saris; with stately gait they go to the wedding, and on seeing the poet's Lord
they whisper. Raga not stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^22-4]

**2.1.** To see Gorachand's wedding, with what longing the wives of noble families adorn themselves — not one can keep her composure!

**2.2.** Absorbed in rasa, how charmingly they line their eyes with collyrium — sidelong glances, arched brows;
smooth braids fall down their backs — how lovely the golden clasps!

**2.3.** On the forehead a dot of sindura, how beautifully the sandal shines! Their ornaments glitter;
on their necks sway necklaces of gems and pearls; in their ears they put gandharaja and champaka flowers.

**2.4.** Putting on silk saris, leaving their homes, they walk with a stately gait like that of a royal elephant;
seeing Narahari's Lord — the heart overflows — one whispers something into another's ear.[^22-5]

[^22-4]: GPT1 — p. 100, no. 19 (scan, PDF p. 359); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 19 (catalogue: NG-058). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 810; ed. 1960, vv. 1499–1502).
Variant: in 2.3 the BR has the second half-lines interchanged ("…gandharāja cām̐pā dei kāṇe" in the first line, "…jhalamala kare ābharaṇe" in the second). Not in PK,
KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. Line 2.1 is the refrain (dhru). The first line is the same as that of the pada on the
first wedding (2.3 no. 22, no. 7 of chapter 21), but the text is different.
[^22-5]: The poet describes the delight of the women of Nadia at the Lord's wedding in words close to the motif of the townswomen (nagaris)
enamoured of Gaura. We translate faithfully to the author; but the Gaudiya tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja,
Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati) does not accept the worship of Gaura in the mood of "Gaura-nagari": Gaura is Krishna Himself in the mood and
lustre of Radha; He came to taste Her love, not to enjoy as a nagara. The Lord's attractiveness for the people of Navadvipa is the quality
of Bhagavan, who attracts all; it is not worldly passion. The same holds for the other padas of the chapter about the women of Nadia (nos.
3, 11, 12; cf. note 5 of chapter 21). GPT pada no. 21 ("āhā mari ki madhura rīti": the "nagaris of Nadia" dream of being "with Gora day and night" and of
touching His golden body in the bridal chamber; = BR vv. 1507–1510) is openly in nagari-bhava and is assigned to the section of nagari padas.

## 3. Narahari — "sai ai dekha nadīyāra cām̐de…" (GPT1 p. 101, no. 20; BR)
*A woman says to her friend: look at the Moon of Nadia — hundreds of Kamadevas, offering themselves for His beauty, fall weeping at His
feet; His glance, His face, His smile; who has arranged this wedding attire — the crown, the curls, the yellow thread and durva, the golden
mirror? Raga not stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^22-6]

**3.1.** Friend, look — there is the Moon of Nadia! Offering themselves for His world-enchanting beauty, hundreds upon hundreds of Madanas
fall weeping at His feet.

**3.2.** The glance of His two eyes, drowning in rasa — I think the Creator made it to slay young women;
the beauty of His moon-face takes away the moon's pride; mingled with His smile, nectar pours down in streams.[^22-7]

**3.3.** Ah, I die, I die! With what longing of heart has someone arranged this wedding attire!
On His head a wondrous, dazzlingly bright crown, covered by His smooth, curling, lovely locks.

**3.4.** In His hand the yellow thread and the blades of durva enjoined for the auspicious rite; the incomparable golden mirror shines
beautifully;
His garments and ornaments are sweet; by the grace of every limb [He] enchants Narahari's mind.

[^22-6]: GPT1 — p. 101, no. 20 (scan, PDF p. 360); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 20 (catalogue: NG-059). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 810; ed. 1960, vv. 1503–1506).
The variants are minor (3.1 GPT1 "laiñā", BR "laiyā"; 3.3 GPT1 "enā", BR "e nā"). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
Line 3.1 is the refrain. The next pada in the GPT and the BR (no. 21) is in nagari-bhava (note 5).
[^22-7]: "Made it to slay young women" is a conventional formula of love poetry about Krishna's beauty; here it speaks of the all-attractive
beauty of the Lord (see note 5). Madana is Kamadeva, the god of love; hundreds of Madanas "offer themselves" (nichani — give themselves as a
ransom) for His beauty: it surpasses the beauty of Kamadeva himself.

## 4. Narahari — "sanātana miśrera bhavane…" (GPT1 pp. 101–102, no. 22; BR)
*The reception of the bridegroom in the house of Sanatana Mishra: music sounds; Sanatana with his kin comes out to meet Him; the
bridegroom shines in the palanquin; around Him brahmanas and worthy men, a countless crowd; the blind, holding others' hands, stand
where Gaurachandra is, the lame come out on the road, the infirm totter along with sticks; all sing Gora's glories; children and old men
dance; hundreds of lamps burn; Mishra, embracing his son-in-law, brings Him into the house, seats Him on a wondrous seat, showers Him
with flowers and performs the reception of the bridegroom. Raga not stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^22-8]

**4.1.** What auspicious rites are performed in the house of Sanatana Mishra — who could describe them?

**4.2.** All kinds of splendid instruments sound; an immense joyful clamour surges up.

**4.3.** Sanatana with his kin comes forward to receive his jewel of a son-in-law.

**4.4.** How captivating the son-in-law's attire! He shines in the midst of the wondrous palanquin.

**4.5.** On all sides brahmanas and worthy men; the crowd of countless people cannot be counted.

**4.6.** The blind, holding others' hands, stand on the side where Gaurachandra is.[^22-9]

**4.7.** The lame come out on the main road and gaze to their heart's content at Gora's beauty.

**4.8.** Whoever cannot walk comes slowly along the road, leaning on a stick.

**4.9.** Who does not sing Gora's glories! They do not know how happiness grows in their hearts.

**4.10.** Various instruments sound in various manners; children and old men dance — no one can stand still.

**4.11.** Hundreds of great lamps burn; the light has filled the earth and the vault of the sky.

**4.12.** Someone displays some entertainment — and all that happens there spreads over the whole earth.

**4.13.** Mishra, greatly rejoicing, embracing his son-in-law, enters the house.

**4.14.** Seating [Him] on a wondrous seat, he showers [Him] with flowers, gazing at His moon-face.

**4.15.** Cries of "jaya, jaya" sound without pause; the musicians of both sides play their instruments in rivalry.

**4.16.** Mishra performs the reception of his son-in-law; Narahari, seeing it, refreshes his eyes.

[^22-8]: GPT1 — pp. 101–102, no. 22 (scan, PDF pp. 360–361); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 22 (catalogue: NG-061; the number in the catalogue is garbled — "no. 2").
BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 811–812; ed. 1960, vv. 1511–1526). Variants: 4.12 GPT1 "kula-raṅga", BR "kuna raṅga" ("some entertainment") — following the BR;
others are minor. Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. The reception of the bridegroom in Sanatana's house — CB
Adi 15; in Lochana — *Chaitanya-mangala*, Adi-khanda, part 14, vv. 146–147.
[^22-9]: The blind, the lame, the infirm — an image by which the poet shows that the Lord draws all to Himself without distinction. "The
reception" (varaṇa) is the honouring of the bridegroom by the bride's father: water for washing the feet, arghya, clothes, ornaments, a garland
(in Lochana, vv. 146–147, 153). "Of both sides" (dom̐hāra) — the musicians of the bridegroom and of the bride.

## 5. Narahari — "nadīyāra śaśī vilasaye cāru…" (GPT1 p. 102, no. 23; BR)
*The bridegroom under the wedding canopy: Vishnupriya's mother, under various pretexts, looks at Him again and again, her feet not
touching the ground; with the married women skilled in auspicious rites she places rice and durva on His head, blesses Him, circles Him
seven times with a lamp and, going into the house, looks back at the poet's Lord and cannot take even half a step. Raga not stated.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^22-10]

**5.1.** The Moon of Nadia shines charmingly under the wedding canopy — how sweet His array!
His youthful body surpasses gold and fresh butter — seeing His bearing, who could keep composure?

**5.2.** Again and again Vishnupriya's mother, under various pretexts, gazes [at Him] with unblinking eyes;
with what joy her heart overflows — her feet do not touch the ground!

**5.3.** Finely dressed, she comes with the married women, very skilled in auspicious rites;
on His lovely head she places rice and durva and blesses Him in a matchless way.

**5.4.** Lamp in hand she circles [Him] seven times; having performed the reception of the bridegroom, she goes into the house,
but, looking back at the Lord of Narahari, under the weight of tenderness she cannot take even half a step.[^22-11]

[^22-10]: GPT1 — p. 102, no. 23 (scan, PDF p. 361); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 23 (catalogue: NG-062). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 812; ed. 1960, vv. 1527–1530).
Variant: 5.4 GPT1 "cāhe pālaṭi nā cale pada ādha" ("looks back — cannot take even half a step"), BR "cāhe pālaṭiyā, cale pada ādha" ("looking back, takes half a
step") — following GPT1. The signature is garbled in the GPT1 OCR ("narahabi"), so the signature-checking script misses the pada (chapter 21). Not in PK,
KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
[^22-11]: The wedding canopy (chom̐ṛalā) is the place of the rites in the courtyard of the bride's house. The reception of the bridegroom (vare urathiyā)
is performed by the bride's mother and the married women: rice and durva on the head, a lamp, the sevenfold circling (in Lochana, vv.
149–152). The tenderness of the mother-in-law for the Lord is parental love, which He accepts from His associates.

## 6. Narahari — "sanātana miśrera gharaṇī…" (GPT1 pp. 102–103, no. 24; BR)
*The wedding: Sanatana's wife adorns her daughter; at Mishra's bidding Vishnupriya is brought out and seated on a throne under the canopy;
Vishnupriya first, offering a garland, gives herself to the Lord's feet; Gaura with a smile puts a garland round her neck; They shower each
other with flowers; Sanatana performs the kanya-dana, placing his daughter's hand in Vishvambhara's, and gives the dowry; at the end the
homa is performed. Raga not stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^22-12]

**6.1.** The wife of Sanatana Mishra performs so many customary rites — I cannot even tell them.

**6.2.** She swims in an ocean of happiness, adorning her daughter with many ornaments.

**6.3.** Seeing Vishnupriya's beautiful attire, joy grows boundlessly in everyone's heart.

**6.4.** The venerable Mishra at the auspicious moment told his dear ones to bring his daughter.

**6.5.** Mishra's house is captivating; the spacious courtyard glitters.

**6.6.** There the wedding canopy is beautiful; they brought the daughter and seated her on a throne.

**6.7.** All the rites there are by custom are also performed — and in this is boundless merriment.

**6.8.** First the goddess Vishnupriya, offering a garland, gave herself to the Lord's feet.[^22-13]

**6.9.** Smiling slightly, Gaura Raya put a garland of flowers round Vishnupriya's neck.

**6.10.** The two shower each other with flowers; each knows well what is in the other's heart.

**6.11.** Moment by moment the joy grows: Gaurachandra rejoices together with Vishnupriya.

**6.12.** What new beauty without end! On all sides the women raise cries of "jaya".

**6.13.** Everyone makes a clamour; various instruments sound — the sound pierces the sky.

**6.14.** The blessed Sanatana Mishra joyfully sat down to perform the kanya-dana.

**6.15.** Having performed the rites enjoined by the Vedas and the rest, he gave his daughter, placing her hand in Vishvambhara's.

**6.16.** Floating in happiness, he gave the dowry: splendid cows, wealth, land, a bed, menservants and maidservants.

**6.17.** At the very end the homa is performed: the daughter is seated at Vishvambhara's left.

**6.18.** How wondrous the sweetness of the two of Them! What can one say? Narahari gives himself for Them both.[^22-14]

[^22-12]: GPT1 — pp. 102–103, no. 24 (scan, PDF pp. 361–362); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 24 (catalogue: NG-063). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 812–813; ed. 1960,
vv. 1531–1548). The variants are minor (6.10 GPT1 "kelākeli", BR "phelāpheli" — the same "shower each other"). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya
or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. The wedding — CB Adi 15; in Lochana — vv. 155–160.
[^22-13]: Vishnupriya is the eternal energy of the Lord (note 2); offering the garland, she "gives herself" to the Lord (ātmasamarpaṇa) — not a worldly
bride but His shakti, eternally serving Him. The exchange of garlands and flowers is a wedding custom; "each knows what is in the other's
heart" — the inseparability of the Lord and His energy.
[^22-14]: Kanya-dana is the "gift of the daughter" by her father; the homa is the fire sacrifice; the bride is seated at the bridegroom's left.
The Lord accepts these rites following the lila (note 2). "Gives himself for Them" (nichani) is a formula of love and devotion (cf. note 7).

## 7. Narahari — "dekhi pahum̐ka vivāha mādhurī…" (GPT1 p. 103, no. 25; BR)
*The gods at the wedding: seeing the sweetness of the Lord's wedding, Shesha, Shiva, Brahma, Indra, Ganapati and others thrill; the
chariots of the gods block the path of the sky; invisible, telling one another of His deeds, the gods shower the wedding with flowers and
praise the good fortune of the brahmana Sanatana; the poet longs to be intoxicated with that joy. Raga not stated. **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR; Vrajabuli.*[^22-15]

**7.1.** Seeing the sweetness of the Lord's wedding, no one can stay steady:
Shesha, Shiva, Brahma, Indra, Ganapati and the others — their whole bodies thrill.

**7.2.** The crowd is immense: many chariots of the gods have blocked the path of the sky;
sweet cries of "jaya, jaya" sound — how it was cannot be told.

**7.3.** In great delight, telling one another of [the Lord's] wondrous deeds, full of rasa,
invisible, they pour down a rain of flowers, spreading lovely merriment.

**7.4.** Praising the great good fortune of the brahmana Sanatana, they are utterly enraptured;
the hope of the servant Narahari: will my mind become intoxicated with this joy?[^22-16]

[^22-15]: GPT1 — p. 103, no. 25 (scan, PDF p. 362); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 25 (catalogue: NG-064). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 813; ed. 1960, vv. 1549–1552).
Variants: 7.3 BR "alakṣita" ("invisible") — the same; 7.4 GPT1 "bhāgabhara", BR "bhāga bhara" — the same. Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the
Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
[^22-16]: The demigods are the Lord's servants: invisibly they come to behold His lila and to serve it (note 3). Sanatana Mishra's good fortune
is that the Lord Himself has accepted his daughter. Shesha is Ananta; Ganapati is Ganesha.

## 8. Narahari — "deva-ramaṇīvṛnda viraci veśa…" (GPT1 p. 103, no. 26; BR)
*The celestial women at the wedding: adorned, with flashing bangles, their countless hosts roam the path of the sky and deem their eyes
rewarded at seeing Gaura's wedding; praising Mishra's house, they thrill; with full eyes they drink in the form of the Lord and His beloved
and give their lives for Them. Raga not stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR; Vrajabuli.*[^22-17]

**8.1.** The hosts of celestial women have adorned themselves in various ways;
[their ornaments] ring, the lustre of their conch-shell bangles flashes matchlessly.

**8.2.** Countless hosts roam the path of the sky, eagerness in their hearts;
they deem their eyes rewarded, seeing the wedding of the beautiful Gaura.

**8.3.** Praising the lovely custom of Mishra's house, they thrill all over;
new and ever new desires arise in them — composure cannot be kept.

**8.4.** With full eyes they drink in the form of the incomparable Lord and His beloved;
how much can Narahari say? — all give their lives for Them.[^22-18]

[^22-17]: GPT1 — p. 103, no. 26 (scan, PDF p. 362); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 26 (catalogue: NG-065). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 813–814; ed. 1960, vv. 1553–1556).
Variants: 8.2 GPT1 "mānata diṭhi sakala nirakhi gauravara nivāha", BR "saphala", "vivāha" — following the BR; 8.1 "vājata thara māhi" (BR 1912 "vājata thara, nāhi atula") — the
sense is unclear, the translation conjectural. Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
[^22-18]: The celestial women, like the demigods, come to behold the Lord's lila and to serve Him (cf. no. 21 of chapter 21: "we shall make merry
