at the wedding together with the wives of Nadia"). "His beloved" (preyasī) is Vishnupriya, the eternal energy of the Lord (note 2). "They give
their lives" (prāṇa nichani deta) is a formula of love and devotion (note 7).

## 9. Narahari — "āhā mari mari suranārīgaṇa…" (GPT1 p. 103, no. 27; BR)
*The celestial women, watching the wedding of the Moon of Nadia, talk among themselves: Sanatana Mishra is beside himself with joy at
having given his daughter to Krishna; seating his daughter at his son-in-law's left he performs the homa but cannot take his eyes from His
face; Mishra's wife is as if maddened in the wedding bustle and, gazing at the poet's Lord, does not feel the ground under her feet. Raga
not stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^22-19]

**9.1.** Ah, I die! The celestial women, seeing the wedding of the Moon of Nadia,
all swim in that ocean of beauty and sate their thirsting eyes.

**9.2.** One says to another: "Look — Mishra Sanatana's heart cannot contain his joy!
With what longing he has given his daughter to Krishna — how much he says, how many gifts of every kind he gives!"[^22-20]

**9.3.** Another says: "Seating his daughter at his son-in-law's left, he deems himself blessed;
he performs the homa, but his mind is not on it — he keeps gazing at the moon-face".

**9.4.** Yet another says: "Look — Mishra's wife is as if maddened in the wedding bustle;
under various pretexts she gazes at the Lord of Narahari, and in her delight her feet do not touch the ground".

[^22-19]: GPT1 — p. 103, no. 27 (scan, PDF p. 362); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 27. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-287). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912,
p. 814; ed. 1960, vv. 1557–1560). The variants are minor (9.2 BR 1960 "kaṣe" — an OCR distortion of "kṛṣṇe"). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya
or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
[^22-20]: "Has given his daughter to Krishna" — the celestial women call Gaura Krishna outright: He is Krishna Himself, and Vishnupriya is His
eternal energy (note 2).

## 10. Narahari — "deva devaramaṇī ullāse…" (GPT1 p. 104, no. 28; BR)
*Gods and celestial women talk softly of the wedding: fortunate are the people of Nadia; the brahmanas who have beautiful daughters
lament that they could not give a daughter to such a bridegroom; all praise Sanatana Mishra; he completes the homa; the women raise their
cries; Vishnupriya and Gorachand are led to the bridal chamber. Raga not stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in
the BR.*[^22-21]

**10.1.** The gods and the celestial women, rejoicing, all talk of the wedding in soft voices:

**10.2.** "Fortunate are the people of Nadia! The wedding has taken place — seeing it, all rejoice".

**10.3.** All the brahmanas who have a beautiful daughter at home grieve bitterly at heart:

**10.4.** "We could not give a daughter to such a bridegroom — such happiness is not in our fate!"

**10.5.** So one says one thing, another another; all praise Sanatana Mishra.

**10.6.** The blessed Sanatana Mishra completed the homa and all the rest.

**10.7.** Gazing at his daughter and son-in-law, he feels his happiness grow moment by moment and his heart overflow.

**10.8.** Who could tell of the wedding customs? Again and again the women raise cries of "jaya".

**10.9.** Who can stay calm as the goddess Vishnupriya and Gorachand are led to the bridal chamber?

**10.10.** The Lord of Narahari, Gaura Raya, goes to the bridal chamber with such delight in His heart![^22-22]

[^22-21]: GPT1 — p. 104, no. 28 (scan, PDF p. 363); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 28 (catalogue: NG-066; GPT2 has "dekha deba ramaṇī" — "look: the celestial women…").
BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 814–815; ed. 1960, vv. 1561–1570). Variants: 10.4 GPT1 "nā pārāli", BR "nā pārilum̐" — following the BR. Not in PK, KGC, PS,
the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
[^22-22]: The bridal chamber (vāsara-ghara) is the room where the newly-weds spend the first night; by custom the women of the house gather there,
sing and joke with the bridegroom (nos. 11–12). The brahmanas' lament is praise of the bridegroom: such a son-in-law is not to be found again.

## 11. Narahari — "nadīyā-vinoda gorā…" (GPT1 p. 104, no. 29; BR)
*The bridal chamber: Gora, the delight of Nadia, enters the bridal chamber; the wives of noble families seat Vishvambhara with Vishnupriya
and gaze unblinkingly at His face; one, wishing to touch Him, anoints Him with sandal, another sets a casket of betel before Him, a third
leans towards Him in jest, yet another offers Him a handful of flowers. Raga not stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada
is in the BR.*[^22-23]

**11.1.** Gora, the delight of Nadia, stealer of the lives of ever new young women, enters the bridal chamber.

**11.2.** The wives of noble families, joy in their hearts, taking Vishvambhara and Vishnupriya,
sweetly, by custom, seat [Them] in the bridal chamber and gaze with unblinking eyes at that face.

**11.3.** One, wishing to touch [Him], smilingly anoints His body with fragrant sandal;
another, having prepared rolls of betel, merrily sets the casket before Him.

**11.4.** Yet another, on the pretext of a jest, leans towards Him, her heart thrilling;
and another stands before the Lord of Narahari and gracefully offers a handful of flowers.[^22-24]

[^22-23]: GPT1 — p. 104, no. 29 (scan, PDF p. 363); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 29. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-288). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912,
p. 815; ed. 1960, vv. 1571–1574). The variants are minor (11.2 BR "chande" for "chām̐de"; 11.4 BR "ḍhali’ paṛe gāya"). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya
or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. Line 11.1 is the refrain.
[^22-24]: In the bridal chamber, by custom, the married women of the house joke merrily with the bridegroom, treat Him to betel and anoint Him
with sandal; the poet describes these wedding jests — this is not nagari-bhava, though the words ("stealer of the lives of young women",
"wishing to touch") are close to its language. We translate faithfully to the author; for the position of the tradition see note 5. The
Lord's attractiveness is the quality of Bhagavan, who attracts all; and what the women do here is service to Him: sandal, betel, flowers.

## 12. Narahari — "vāsara gharete gorārāya. rūpe koṭi madana mātāya…" (GPT1 p. 104, no. 30; BR)
*In the bridal chamber: by His beauty Gaura Raya intoxicates millions of Kamadevas; the wives of noble families cannot take their eyes
from His moon-face and whisper with their veils drawn together; one covers the thrill of her body with her cloth, another trembles in the
rapture of rasa, yet another, unable to master her heart, offers her life at His reddish feet; the poet longs to see these pastimes. Raga
not stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^22-25]

**12.1.** In the bridal chamber Gaura Raya by His beauty intoxicates millions of Madanas.

**12.2.** The wives of noble families, joy in their hearts, give their eyes to His moon-face.

**12.3.** One, drawing her veil close to another's, says something, smiling slightly.

**12.4.** All their bodies are full of thrill — they cover it with their cloth.

**12.5.** One, standing beside another, trembles in the rapture of rasa.

**12.6.** Another, her heart without rest, offers her life at His reddish feet.[^22-26]

**12.7.** How much merriment in the bridal chamber — who could tell so much?

**12.8.** A great hope is in Narahari's heart: shall I see all these pastimes?

[^22-25]: GPT1 — p. 104, no. 30 (scan, PDF p. 363); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 30. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-289; the row NG-067 with the
same first line "vāsara gharete gorārāya" is no. 31, no. 13 here). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 815–816; ed. 1960, vv. 1575–1582). Variants: 12.6 "rāṅgā pāya"
in GPT1 and BR 1912 (the BR 1960 OCR has "rādhā pāya", a distortion); 12.8 GPT1 "narahari mane vaṛa āśa", BR "narahari-mane ei āśa". Not in PK, KGC, PS, the
Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
[^22-26]: "Offers her life at His feet" (nichaye jīvana rāṅgā pāya) is an image of devotion to the Lord. The thrill and the "rapture of rasa" of the women
in the bridal chamber are delight in the Lord's all-attractive beauty; we translate faithfully to the author, for the position of the
tradition see note 5.

## 13. Narahari — "vāsara gharete gorārāya. viṣṇupriyā saha…" (GPT1 p. 105, no. 31; BR)
*The morning after the wedding: Gaura Raya spends the night with Vishnupriya in the bridal chamber; Sanatana and his kin are enraptured;
at dawn the Lord performs the kushandika and asks Sanatana to let Him go home; Sanatana, restraining himself, places his daughter's hand in
Vishvambhara's; the Lord bows to the venerable people, and they bless Him with rice and durva; Mishra's wife cannot master herself; amid
Vedic chanting, the women's cries and music all perform the auspicious rites for the journey. Raga not stated. **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^22-27]

**13.1.** In the bridal chamber Gaura Raya happily spends the night with Vishnupriya.

**13.2.** The merriment is endless — it cannot be told; Sanatana with his kin is enraptured with joy.

**13.3.** At dawn Gaurahari, having performed the kushandika and the other rites, was filled with joy.[^22-28]

**13.4.** "I shall go to My home," He says to the venerable Sanatana Mishra.

**13.5.** Sanatana, sending off his jewel of a son-in-law, keeps his composure with difficulty.

**13.6.** How much he consoled his daughter — and gave her, placing her hand in Vishvambhara's.

**13.7.** Gaurahari, setting out, bows in great joy to the venerable people.

**13.8.** What can be said of the longing of them all? With rice and durva on His head they bless [Him].

**13.9.** Mishra's wife, sending off her daughter and son-in-law, cannot keep her composure.

**13.10.** As Gora sets out for home, the brahmanas chant the Vedas on all sides.

**13.11.** The women raise cries of "jaya"; various instruments sound, the bhatas recite praises.

**13.12.** Gazing at the Lord of Narahari, all perform the auspicious rites proper for a departure.

[^22-27]: GPT1 — p. 105, no. 31 (scan, PDF p. 364); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 31 (catalogue: NG-067). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 816; ed. 1960, vv. 1583–1594).
Variants: 13.8 GPT1 "karite ki se bhāra sādha", BR "kahite ki se sabhāra sādha" — following the BR; 13.11 GPT1 "kāyavāra", BR "rāyavāra" (the same — a song of
praise). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. The morning after the wedding and the departure — CB Adi 15; in
Lochana — vv. 166–174.
[^22-28]: The kushandika is the rite at the sacred fire on the day after the wedding, which completes it. The Lord, the Goal of all rites,
performs them following the lila (note 2), and bows to His elders, setting an example of respect.

## 14. Narahari — "varaja-bhūṣaṇa gaura-vidhuvara…" (GPT1 p. 105, no. 32; BR)
*The return home: Gaura, the ornament of Vraja, after the wedding rides home in the palanquin with His beloved; countless men and women
watch and say to one another: "This is Lakshmi and the Lord of Lakshmi!"; the praises of the bhatas, Vedic chanting, music, dancing,
singing such that the does come out of the forest; at the hour of cow-dust, having paused on the bank of the Suradhuni, He comes home. Raga
not stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR; ornate Vrajabuli.*[^22-29]

**14.1.** The ornament of Vraja, the beautiful moon — Gaura, having celebrated the wedding, with playful gait
goes with His beloved to His home — His splendour is wondrous beyond words;
mounted on the palanquin He flashes; the stream of the nectar of His beauty overflows;
His eyes adorned, His array incomparable — He enchants the minds of all people.

**14.2.** Cries of "jaya, jaya" sound without pause; countless men and women watch
and say to one another: "It is as if Lakshmi and the Lord of Lakshmi — the two of Them — were shining!";[^22-30]
the singers of praises in great joy proclaim ever new sweet deeds;
many brahmanas chant the Vedas again and again — and their bodies thrill.

**14.3.** Many instruments — muraja, mardala, trisari, kundali, pataha — sound abundantly:
"ku-ku nu-nu nu-nu"; throngs of musicians play sweetly in various manners;
the dancing girls and lines of dancers dance, beating out "ta-dhika dhikita dhini,
ni-dhi dhenna dhiki taka", keeping time; the movements of their feet — the lustre of their bodies flashes.

**14.4.** Jati, shruti, svaras, gramas, murcchanas, tanas — ever new alapas;
hearing them, the does leave the forest and run to the skilled musicians;
all around the house a great clamour; the heart of the servant Narahari overflowed:
at the hour of cow-dust, having paused on the lovely bank of the Suradhuni, [the Lord] comes home.

[^22-29]: GPT1 — p. 105, no. 32 (scan, PDF p. 364); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 32 (catalogue: NG-068). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 816–817; ed. 1960, vv. 1595–1598).
Variants: 14.2 GPT1 "ucarita nava nava carita madhumaya", BR "ucari nava nava carita rasamaya" — the sense is the same; the onomatopoeic syllables in 14.3 differ among the
witnesses (GPT1 "ku kunu nu nunu sudhā", BR 1912 "kuku nunu nunu, mu dhā"). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. Jati,
shruti, svara, grama, murcchana, tana, alapa are terms of Indian music (modes, intervals, notes, scales, transitions, runs, preludes).
[^22-30]: "Lakshmi and the Lord of Lakshmi" — in the newly-weds the people of Nadia recognise Lakshmi and Narayana: Vishnupriya is the eternal
energy of the Lord (note 2), Gaura is the Lord Himself; "the ornament of Vraja" (varaja-bhūṣaṇa) is Krishna. Cf. CB Adi 15 (= GPT 2.4 no. 39, Vrindavana
Dasa): on the way back some say this is Hara and Gauri, others — Kamala and Sri Hari.

## 15. Narahari — "gorācām̐da vivāha kariyā…" (GPT1 p. 106, no. 33; BR)
*The welcome at home: Gorachand, having married, returns home in joy; the invisible gods strew the way with flowers; someone hurries to
tell Shachi of the wedding; hearing the music, Shachi, beside herself with joy, comes out of the house, circles the newly-weds with
countless offerings and casts them away, kisses her son's moon-face and leads her son and daughter-in-law into the house; Vishvambhara with
Vishnupriya sit on the throne; the women raise cries of "ulu-lu", the bhatas recite praises, the brahmanas chant the Vedas. Raga not
stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^22-31]

**15.1.** Gorachand, having celebrated the wedding, comes home in great joy.

**15.2.** The invisible gods shower flowers along the whole way.

**15.3.** An ocean of happiness in Nadia! Someone tells Mother Shachi of the wedding.

**15.4.** Hearing the clamour of the great music, Shachidevi is beside herself with joy.

**15.5.** Mother Shachi [comes] out of the house; circling [the newly-weds], she casts away countless offerings.[^22-32]

**15.6.** Tenderly kissing the moon-face, she enters the house, leading her son and her daughter-in-law.

**15.7.** Vishvambhara with Vishnupriya sit on the throne; all the associates gaze at Them.

**15.8.** The women raise cries of "ulu-lu"; the whole house became filled with blessing.

**15.9.** The bhatas recite praises; the brahmanas chant the Vedas without pause.

**15.10.** All joyfully play various instruments. How much can Narahari tell with a single mouth?

[^22-31]: GPT1 — p. 106, no. 33 (scan, PDF p. 365); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 33 (catalogue: NG-069). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 817–818; ed. 1960, vv. 1599–1610).
Variants: between 15.4 and 15.5 the BR has two couplets more: "Mother Shachi outside the house waits with the chaste wives, watching the road.
Gora with all comes slowly and at the door descends from the palanquin. Seeing her son and daughter-in-law, mother…" (vv. 1603–1605); in GPT1
these lines are compressed into the single couplet 15.5 — the translation follows GPT1. 15.8 BR "sakala bhuvana" ("the whole world"). Not in PK, KGC,
PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B.
[^22-32]: "Circling, she casts away" (nichiyā phelaye) — the custom of nirmanchhana: the mother circles the newly-weds with offerings and casts them
away, warding off all evil (in Lochana, vv. 175–178). Shachi is the mother of the Lord, eternally abiding in parental love for Him. Shachi
welcomes her son and daughter-in-law — CB Adi 15.

## 16. Narahari — "gorā guṇamaṇi sughaṛa-śekhara…" (GPT1 p. 106, no. 34; BR)
*The Lord gives gifts and sends off the guests: to the bhatas, dancers, singers, musicians, beggars and brahmanas He gives clothes,
ornaments and wealth, fulfilling their desires, and satisfies all with kind words; all go home singing the glories of Gaurahari; Shachi
honours each of the women. Raga not stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR; Vrajabuli.*[^22-33]

**16.1.** Gora, the jewel of virtues, the crown of the skilful, in great joy of heart
sends off [with gifts] the many people who came to the wedding in excitement.

**16.2.** To the bhatas, dancers, connoisseurs of song, musicians, beggars and the many brahmanas
He gives to all many clothes, ornaments and riches, fulfilling their desires.

**16.3.** With most sweet words He skilfully satisfies everyone;
all together go to their homes, singing the glories of Gaurahari.

**16.4.** Sri Shachi showed so much honour to each of the women;
says Narahari: they all went home in happiness.[^22-34]

[^22-33]: GPT1 — p. 106, no. 34 (scan, PDF p. 365); GPT2 — section 2.4, no. 34 (catalogue: NG-070). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 818; ed. 1960, vv. 1611–1614).
Variants: 16.1 GPT1 "vivāhe ātula", BR "vivāhe ākula" — following the BR; 16.2 GPT1 "manorama puri", BR "manoratha pūri" ("fulfilling desires") — following
the BR. Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. Next in the BR comes prose on Vishnupriya's service to her
mother-in-law and on the Lord's journey to Gaya (vv. 1615–1625); in the GPT — nos. 35–38 (an extract from Lochana's Chaitanya-mangala) and nos. 39–40
(Vrindavana Dasa) — outside the appendix (introductory note).
[^22-34]: To send off with gifts (vidāya) all who came to the wedding and served at it is the custom; the Lord is a generous host, Shachi the
mistress of the house. In the chronology of the biographies the Lord's journey to Gaya follows (CB Adi 17; CC Adi 17).

## 17. Narahari — "jāgaha jana-mana-cora caturavara…" (GPT1 p. 343, section 5.2, no. 1; GCC)
*Ashtakaliya, the songs of awakening at the end of the night: "Awake, Stealer of hearts, jewel of Radha's heart! The night is over. You
who, hearing of the deeds of Vraja, find no taste in food or sleep, who hold sankirtana dearer than life — what sleep has overcome You?"
Raga not stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^22-35]

**17.1.** Awake, Stealer of people's hearts, best of the clever, beautiful One who sports in the town of Nadia, —
jewel of the heart of Radha, crown of women, full of rasa — You who shine with Her light![^22-36]

**17.2.** What shall I say? Again and again [I tell You]: the night is over!
What languor is this? I understand nothing — there is much doubt in my heart.

**17.3.** Hearing of the virtues of the lovely deeds of Vraja, You find no taste in food or sleep;
telling of them, You pass days and nights — how then is sleep pleasing to You now?

**17.4.** Every moment You hold dearer than life the incomparable sankirtana, the root of joy;
without it a moment seems to You a kalpa — and so Narahari's heart is perplexed.[^22-37]

[^22-35]: GPT1 — p. 343, section 5.2 "Ashtakaliya" (dvitīya ucchvāsa — aṣṭakālīyalīlā), no. 1 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF p. 602); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 1 (catalogue:
NG-171). GCC — kirana 2 (the last part of the night: "the pastimes on the bed"), pada 23. All the awakening songs GPT 5.2 nos. 1–10 are in the
GCC, but in a different order: in kirana 2 as padas 14 (no. 10) and 16–23 (nos. 6, 7, 8, 9, 4, 5, 2, 1), in kirana 3 ("the awakening") as pada 8
(no. 3); between them the GCC says that these songs were sung by a clever parrot (kīra), raised by the Lord's servant, together with Narahari
(pada 15), and that the sleeping Gaura, absorbed in rasa, heard a little of them (pada 24). The variants are minor (17.1 GCC "jana-mana-cora"). Not
in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. Cf. Gaura's awakening in Vasu Ghosha (GPT 5.2 no. 11; chapter 12, no. 6).
[^22-36]: Ashtakaliya, "the eight parts of the day": songs of the Lord's eternal pastimes in Navadvipa by the hours of day and night, on the
model of the ashtakaliya of Radha and Krishna in Vraja; it is eternal lila, which devotees remember in their service, not the routine of an
ordinary day. The Lord's sleep is not the sleep of a conditioned soul under the sway of maya: in the GCC Gaura's night is "the pastimes on
the bed", absorption in the pastimes of Vraja (cf. 17.3; no. 18: "as before"); His associates wake Him (in the GCC a parrot, as in Vraja
Vrinda's parrots wake Radha and Krishna), and in their joking reproaches to the "sluggard" is their love. "Jewel of Radha's heart… You who
shine with Her light" (tākara hṛdaya-ratana-rucikārī, lit. "who illumines the jewel of Her heart") — Gaura is Krishna Himself, the jewel of Radha's
heart, appearing in Her mood and lustre (CC Adi 1.5).
[^22-37]: Sankirtana is the congregational singing of the holy names, for which the Lord appeared (CC Adi 3); a kalpa is a day of Brahma, an
image of endlessly long time.

## 18. Narahari — "uṭha uṭha āji eki adbhuta ghuma…" (GPT1 pp. 343–344, no. 2; GCC)
*A joking reproach to the sleeping Gaura: "Get up! What strange sleep is this? People laugh at You; were it now as before, You would run
away Yourself for shame; it is well that Your Gadadhara, Narahari and the others are asleep too and the old fears are gone — otherwise
they would have run away, leaving You; sleep with them, but if it gets late, do not blame Narahari afterwards". Raga not stated.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^22-38]

**18.1.** Get up, get up! What wondrous sleep are You sleeping today, O clever One!
Never have I seen such a habit in You — how much longer must I coax You?

**18.2.** What joy is there in such languor at this hour? Others laugh at Your doings.
Were it now as before, You would not need waking: You would run away for shame.[^22-39]

**18.3.** Likewise Your Gadadhara, Narahari and all the others are lying asleep;
those fears are gone too — so it is well; otherwise they would have run away, leaving You.

**18.4.** What shall I say? Lie with Your dear ones — what do You lose by it?
But if it gets very late — do not blame Narahari afterwards.

[^22-38]: GPT1 — pp. 343–344, no. 2 (scan, PDF pp. 602–603); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 2 (catalogue: NG-172). GCC — kirana 2, pada 22. The variants are minor
(18.3 GCC "śuyā", "thuyā"; 18.4 GCC "śuyā thāka"). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^22-39]: "As before" — a hint at the eternal lila of Vraja: at the end of the night Krishna and the gopis hurriedly leave the kunja, afraid of
being seen by the elders. Gadadhara, according to Kavi Karnapura's Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika, is the manifestation of Radha in Gaura's lila;
Narahari Sarakara is Madhumati, Radha's friend. In Navadvipa "those fears are gone" — so the associates sleep beside the Lord. The joking
reproaches are the associates' love, not censure (note 36).

## 19. Narahari — "śuna śuna ohe kichu nā vujhiye…" (GPT1 p. 344, no. 3; GCC)
*At Gaura's bedside: the night is over, yet He, the enchanter of the world, sleeps, absorbed in who knows what rasa; Gadadhara, his eyes on
His face, sits at His feet and smilingly presses them; Narahari floats in an ocean of joy, gazing at Gauranga, and whispers something into
Gadadhara's ear; others, intoxicated with Gaura-rasa, doze; someone insists that the Lord be woken. Raga lalita. **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^22-40]

**19.1.** Listen, listen! I cannot understand — in what rasa is He lost?
The night is over, and still Gora, the enchanter of the world, sleeps.

**19.2.** And look at Gadadhara: his eyes fixed on the face of Gaurangachand,
he sits at His feet and, smiling, joyfully presses His feet.

**19.3.** Narahari floats in an ocean of joy, gazing at Gauranga;
with wondrous grace he whispers something into Gadadhara's ear.

**19.4.** Others, intoxicated with Gaura-rasa, nod in drowsiness, their senses confused;
and someone insists that the Lord of Narahari's life be woken.[^22-41]

[^22-40]: GPT1 — p. 344, no. 3 ("lalita"; scan, PDF p. 603); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 3 (catalogue: NG-173). GCC — kirana 3 ("the awakening"), pada 8 (introduced
there with the words "and someone [says]", kopi ca). Variants: 19.1 "tamu" in both GPT1 and GCC — probably "tavu" ("still"); 19.2 GCC "ām̐khi diyā". Not in
the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^22-41]: Here Narahari is a participant in the lila at the Lord's bedside beside Gadadhara; if the pada belongs to Chakravarti, this is
Narahari Sarakara, the Lord's associate (introductory note in ch. 17; cf. note 39). Gadadhara pressing the Lord's feet is an image of his
eternal service.

## 20. Narahari — "jāga jāga ohe gauraśaśī…" (GPT1 p. 344, no. 4; GCC)
*"Awake, Gaura-moon: the night is over; Your associates, leaving their homes, have gathered in the courtyard like chakoras without the
moon; leave Your bed, show Yourself, sate their thirsting eyes, speak but a word, embrace them and take away their sorrow". Raga not
stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^22-42]

**20.1.** Awake, awake, O Gaura-moon! How long You sleep — the night is over.
Leaving their homes, Your associates have hurried here and filled the courtyard.

**20.2.** I have seen none like them: they are like chakora birds without the moon;
so leave Your bed quickly, show Yourself and sate their thirsting eyes.

**20.3.** What shall I say? The lovely talks of [Your] deeds have fallen silent here — all stand mute;
let them hear but once Your soft words steeped in nectar — take away the pain of their hearts.

**20.4.** They look around on all sides, their hearts restless; I have understood — they are utterly exhausted;
embrace them and drive away the suffering of their bodies, O Lord of Narahari's life![^22-43]

[^22-42]: GPT1 — p. 344, no. 4 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF p. 603); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 4 (catalogue: NG-174). GCC — kirana 2, pada 20. The variants are minor
(20.2 GCC "yena cakora pākhi"; 20.4 GCC "atiśaya khiṇa"). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^22-43]: The chakora is a bird which, according to poetic tradition, feeds only on moonlight; an image of devotees who live by beholding the
Lord. The Lord's embrace is His mercy to His associates.

## 21. Narahari — "pohāila niśi pāila parāṇa…" (GPT1 pp. 344–345, no. 5; GCC)
*"The night is over — all have come back to life; thinking of Your deeds, no one can attend to household work, and all have hurried to You,
yet You do not wake. The brahmanas of Nadia go to the Suradhuni and laugh: 'Look, Nimai Pandita is still asleep!' Get up and perform Your
morning duties, or ill fame will spread about You and Narahari will be ashamed". Raga not stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** —
the pada is in the GCC.*[^22-44]

**21.1.** The night is over — and all the men and women have as it were regained their lives;
thinking of Your many lovely deeds, no one can attend to household work.

**21.2.** In great haste all have come to You, to sate themselves [with seeing You];
yet You do not wake — what a trouble! I do not know what joy there is in this sleep.

**21.3.** All the brahmanas of Nadia, about their business, have hurried to the bank of the Suradhuni;
they laugh among themselves: "Look, Nimai Pandita is still lying asleep!"

**21.4.** So, I say, leave Your bed and perform Your morning duties, O Gora, jewel of virtues,
or else all will spread ill fame about You — and hearing it, Narahari will be ashamed.[^22-45]

[^22-44]: GPT1 — pp. 344–345, no. 5 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF pp. 603–604; the number is garbled in the OCR — "৫ pda", and the signature-checking script misses the
pada); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 5. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-290). GCC — kirana 2, pada 21. Variants: 21.2 GPT1 "nā jānaha tumi" ("You
do not know"), GCC "nā jāgaha tumi" ("You do not wake") — following the GCC; 21.2 GCC "ati tvarātvari". Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^22-45]: "Nimai Pandita" is the Lord's name in the time of His scholarship; the brahmanas go to the Ganga for the morning bath. The joking
threat of "ill fame" is the love of the one who wakes Him (note 36): the eternal lila of Navadvipa includes these pastimes of the Lord in
the guise of a young scholar and householder.

## 22. Narahari — "jāgaha jagajīvana nava nadīyāpuracām̐da he…" (GPT1 p. 345, no. 6; GCC)
*A hymn of awakening in solemn Vrajabuli: "Awake, Life of the world, new Moon of Nadia!" — with a chain of epithets: auspicious king
Kamadeva, form the colour of gorochana, full of rasa, teeth like jasmine, eyes a snare for glances and hearts, crusher of Kama, golden lotus
in the lake of the devotees' hearts, clad in cloud-coloured garments, King of dancers, He whose feet, dispelling the fear of worldly
existence, are worshipped by the gods; "today, seeing Your sleep, I am perplexed". Raga bhairava. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** —
the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^22-46]

**22.1.** Awake, Life of the world, new Moon of the town of Nadia!
Auspicious king Kamadeva, Your form is lovely as gorochana;
full of rasa, overwhelmed by rasa, ornament of the connoisseurs of rasa, root of rasa!

**22.2.** Beautiful One, with teeth like jasmine flowers, with a soft, lovely, joy-giving face,
with lovely, restless eyes — a snare for the eyes and hearts of people!

**22.3.** On Your beautiful chest a sweet garland; You are the delight of trembling women,
stealing their composure, Yourself the abode of steadiness, crusher of Kama!

**22.4.** Beautiful curling hair, an incomparable graceful attire,
a golden lotus that has made its home in the lake of the devotees' hearts!
Neck like a lion's, pure ears, a tilaka of golden sandal,
clad in cloud-coloured garments, King of dancers, delighting His dear ones!

**22.5.** Temple of jewel-like virtues, captivating, with a gait surpassing the elephant's, grateful,
He whose feet, which shatter the burden of the fear of worldly existence, are worshipped by the gods!
Dear One of Narahari, what can I say of what is in my heart? — nothing can be expressed:
today, seeing Your sleep, I am perplexed.[^22-47]

[^22-46]: GPT1 — p. 345, no. 6 ("bhairaba"; scan, PDF p. 604); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 6. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-291). GCC — kirana 2, pada 16
("rāga bhairava"). Variants: 22.1 GCC "nadīyāpuracanda"; 22.3 "kāma-dalata śanda" — the last word is unclear (also in the GCC), translated by the sense; 22.4 GPT1
"bhabhaktahṛdaya" (misprint). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. Lines 22.1 are the refrain (dhru).
[^22-47]: "Worshipped by the gods" (vṛndāraka-vandya), "dispelling the fear of worldly existence" are epithets of the Supreme Lord; "crusher of Kama" —
His beauty surpasses that of the god of love, and remembrance of Him destroys lust. The attraction of women to the Lord (22.3) is the
quality of Bhagavan, who attracts all (note 5). Gorochana is a bright yellow pigment; "King of dancers" (naṭendra) is the Lord dancing in
kirtana.

## 23. Narahari — "tejaha śayana gaura guṇadhāma…" (GPT1 p. 345, no. 7; GCC)
*Dawn: "Leave Your bed, Gaura, abode of virtues: the moon has paled, the watches of the night are gone; the East, forgetting everything, has
put on red out of love; the night-lotus has closed, and the bees fly to the opened day-lotus; the chakravaki rejoices with her mate;
seeing these pastimes, Narahari laughs". Raga not stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^22-48]

**23.1.** Leave Your bed, Gaura, abode of virtues! The moon has paled, the watches of the night are gone.

**23.2.** The East — the [night's] companion — has forgotten everything and out of love has put on red.

**23.3.** The night-lotus where the bees lived has closed — and they fly to the opened day-lotus.

**23.4.** The chakravaki rejoices, united with her mate; Narahari, seeing so much merriment, laughs.[^22-49]

[^22-48]: GPT1 — p. 345, no. 7 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF p. 604); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 7. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-292). GCC — kirana 2, pada 17
("punaryathārāga"). Variants: 23.1 GPT1 "gata yāminī yāma" (the last word is distorted in the GCC); 23.2 GCC "anurāga hi". Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the
Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^22-49]: Images of dawn in Indian poetry: the night-lotus (kumuda) closes, the day-lotus (kamala) opens; the chakravaka birds, separated for
the night according to legend, are united in the morning. "The East, which out of love has put on red" is the dawn; "anuraga" means both
"love" and "redness".

## 24. Narahari — "niśigata śaśī darapa dūre…" (GPT1 p. 345, no. 8; GCC)
*"The night is over — the moon's pride is far away, the chakora is in great sorrow; the stars, ashamed at their husband's humiliation,
have hidden in the forest of the sky; the people of Nadia are awake — so leave Your bed, Gora; if You do not believe me, ask Narahari".
Raga not stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^22-50]

**24.1.** The night is over — the moon's pride is far away; in great sorrow the chakora flutters about.

**24.2.** Ashamed at their husband's humiliation, the stars have hidden in the forest of the sky.

**24.3.** The people of Nadia are already awake — so, I say, leave Your bed, Gora.

**24.4.** If You do not believe me — then ask Narahari.[^22-51]

[^22-50]: GPT1 — p. 345, no. 8 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF p. 604); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 8 (catalogue: NG-175). GCC — kirana 2, pada 18. Variants: 24.2 GPT1 "pati
viṛambita", GCC "gati-viṛambana" ("seeing the [moon's] humiliation"). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^22-51]: The moon is the "husband" of the stars (nakshatras) in Indian legend. "Ask Narahari" — in the GCC these songs are sung by a parrot
(note 35), who appeals to Narahari as a witness; in the GPT the line reads as the poet's signature.

## 25. Narahari — "jāga jāga ohe jīvana gorā…" (GPT1 p. 346, no. 9; GCC)
*"Awake, Gora, my life, stealer of hearts and eyes! You are still asleep at dawn, while the neighbours are awake and chuckling; the people
of Nadia praise You and run to Your house — are You not ashamed? Tell me, what do You do at night? The peacocks, the bees, the chakoras
pine without You; get up, come out into the courtyard — otherwise Narahari's fault will not be washed away". Raga not stated.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^22-52]

**25.1.** Awake, awake, O Gora, my life, stealer of the hearts and eyes of the people of the world!
I do not know in what You are lost, that You are still asleep at dawn;
open Your eyes, look: the night is over, all these neighbours are awake;
casting off sorrow, floating in an ocean of joy, they chuckle in every way.

**25.2.** And I say more: in this town of Nadia all praise [You] in various ways
and run to Your house — are You not ashamed at all?
What strange languor You keep: dawn has come, and You cannot get up!
Tell me, what do You do at night? You are so clever — why then like this?[^22-53]

**25.3.** The peacock and the peahen are apart: neither comes near the other;
dejected, they sit in the trees — not seeing You, they do not dance.
The bee and his mate in the lovely kunja, forgetting all, do not alight on the clusters of flowers;
"For whom should we hum?" — saying so, they do not hum and roam the forest as if distraught.

**25.4.** The chakora, seeing in it the likeness of Your moon-face, was devoted to the moon in the sky;
it has paled — and he, bewildered, weeps in great sorrow: "What will become of me?"
Make him happy, O treasure of joy: get up, come out and stand in the courtyard,
or else, I feel, there will be trouble — then Narahari's fault will not be washed away.

[^22-52]: GPT1 — p. 346, no. 9 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF p. 605); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 9. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-293; by the opening "jāga jāga
ohe" the checking script matched it with NG-174). GCC — kirana 2, pada 19. Variants: 25.1 GPT1 "paṛavāsī", GCC "paṛasa-vāsī" ("neighbours") — following the
GCC; others minor. Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^22-53]: "What do You do at night?" is the joking reproach of one who loves; the Lord's nights pass in kirtana and in absorption in the
pastimes of Vraja (17.3; note 36). The peacocks, bees and chakora are the nature of Navadvipa, which, like the nature of Vraja, lives by
love for the Lord.

## 26. Narahari — "āju rajanīśeṣa samaya sukha-samāja sāje…" (GPT1 pp. 346–347, no. 10; GCC)
*Navadvipa before dawn: at the end of the night a feast of joy gathers — melodies rare even for the kinnaras, the songs of parrots, the fifth
note of the cuckoos; in the blossoming kunjas the bees hum as if instruments were playing; the peacocks dance and the celestial dancers are
ashamed; swans and cranes call, doves coo; the breeze stirs the leaves, dew on the grass is like tears of joy: incomparable is the town of
Nadia on earth. Raga bhairava. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^22-54]

**26.1.** Today, at the end of the night, a feast of joy gathers:
melodies rare even for the race of kinnaras — flocks of parrots sing songs,
the lovely, sweet fifth note of the cuckoos resounds.

**26.2.** New flowering kunjas have opened — there swarms upon swarms of bees
hum so wondrously, as if sweet instruments were playing;
shadja and pairs of gamakas, lovely trills — "dhi-dhi kiti dhilanga";
the peacocks dance — seeing them, the celestial dancers are ashamed.

**26.3.** The swans raise auspicious calls; the cranes, hearing them, lose their composure;
the earth, as if thrilling in the guise of sprouts, bows beneath the creepers;
wondrously drunk with love, hundreds of flocks of doves shine;
"ghu-ghu" is their cooing, rolling sounds resound.

**26.4.** The breeze, as if offering adornment, stirs the leaves in boundless delight;
in the guise of flowers it radiantly bestows coral and pearls;
drops of dew fall on the grass — as if tears of joy were flowing;
says Narahari: incomparable is the town of Nadia on earth.[^22-55]

[^22-54]: GPT1 — pp. 346–347, no. 10 ("bhairaba"; scan, PDF pp. 605–606); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 10. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-294). GCC — kirana 2,
pada 14 ("bhairaba rāga"; in the GCC the first of the awakening songs). Variants: 26.1 GPT1 "sukha samājha sāje", GPT2 "sukha samāja sāje"; the places in 26.3
("aṅkurachala pulaka vallīndra bhūmi namitāye", GCC "… vallīnrara bhūmi nadi tām̐je") and 26.4 ("pavana miśa śiṅgāra hāra", GCC "pavana niśa siṅgāra hara") are unclear in all
witnesses — the translation is conjectural. Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. Further in GPT 5.2: no. 11 — Vasu Ghosha (chapter 12,
no. 6), no. 12 — Jagannatha Dasa, nos. 13–14 — Radhamohana, no. 15 — signed by Uddhava Dasa (the catalogue wrongly listed it under Narahari: NG-176),
no. 16 onwards — Narahari and others (chapter 23).
[^22-55]: The nature of Navadvipa at dawn serves the Lord: the birds sing, the dew is tears of joy; so too in Krishna's ashtakaliya the nature
of Vrindavana awakens together with Him. Navadvipa-dhama is no worldly place; according to Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati it is non-different
from Vrindavana. Shadja is the first note of the scale, gamakas are ornaments of the sound.

---

# Chapter 23. Appendix. Padas signed "Narahari" from the Gaura-pada-tarangini — VII: the ashtakaliya (the last part of the night, morning, day, evening)

*Continuation of the appendix (the introductory note on the two Naraharis, on the arguments for attribution and on the marks in the
headings is in ch. 17). Chapter 23: the continuation of GPT section 5.2 "Ashtakaliya" (GPT1 pp. 348–362, nos. 16–51): the Lord's words
in sleep at the end of the night and His awakening; the morning in Shachi's house among the companions; the pastimes of the day — the Lord
playfully takes away the companions' clothes, the meal on the bank of the Ganga; the walk through Navadvipa — old men, old women, the blind,
the lame, the dandies and the merchants gaze at Him; the companions' longing at night as they wait for the dawn; two "table-of-contents"
padas of the ashtakaliya (the eight parts of Gaura's day and night); the evening kirtanas — the Lord's dance in the guise of Rukmini and the
dance in Srivasa's courtyard. The signatures in the section were checked throughout, in the OCR and on the scan; the Gaura-charita-chintamani
(GCC, kiranas 1–4) and the 12th wave of the Bhakti-ratnakara (BR) were read continuously at the relevant places. Not translated (outside
the appendix): nos. 17, 52, 54 — signed Ghanashyama; no. 18 — Yadunatha Dasa (translated in chapter 13, no. 16); nos. 24, 25, 30, 32, 53 — Vasu
Ghosha (no. 24 — chapter 12, no. 7; no. 25 = PK 1108 — chapter 5; no. 32 — chapter 5; no. 53 = PK 656 — chapter 9; no. 30 — the festival in the
house of Narahari Thakura at Shrikhanda, signed Vasu); nos. 29, 41 — Narottama Dasa; no. 31 — Madhava (= PK 2638); nos. 33, 46 — Radhamohana; no. 44 —
without the Narahari signature (= PK vol. 4); no. 45 — Vaishnava Dasa; no. 39 — a pada in nagari-bhava (assigned to the section of nagari padas).
The padas on Gaura's night sleep (nos. 55–63, 65) go to the next chapter. The base text is GPT1 (doubtful places by the scan), collated with
GPT2, the GCC (ed. 1947) and the BR (eds. 1912 and 1960); the PK, KGC, PS and the Gita-chandrodaya were checked. On the ashtakaliya as eternal
lila and on the Lord's sleep see note 36 of chapter 22; on the motif of the women of Nadia, note 7. The notes of the GPT editors are not
reproduced.*

## 1. Narahari — "alasa avaśa pahum̐ rasika-śiromaṇi…" (GPT1 pp. 348–349, section 5.2, no. 16; GCC)
*The last part of the night: the Lord, in the languor of half-sleep, speaks as in a dream words full of rasa: without the sight of
Radharamana His life is burning; calling by name Gauridasa, Haridasa, Dhananjaya and dozens of companions, He asks them to sing of the deeds
of the people of Vraja to quench the burning of His heart; in humility He says that enemies have subdued Him and He has taken a body in
vain, and prays to be, birth after birth, a servant of the feet of the Lord of the gopis; having said this, He grows still again in sleep.
Raga not stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^23-1]

**1.1.** Languid and overcome, my Lord, the crown of the relishers of rasa, speaks as in a dream words full of rasa:
"Bereft of the rasa of seeing Radharamana, My life is wasting — My life is burning away.[^23-2]

**1.2.** Listen, Gauri[dasa], Haridasa, Dhananjaya, Sanjaya, Vijaya, Mukunda, Murari,
Madhava, Vasudeva, Purushottama, Shridhara, Krishnadasa, giver of joy,

**1.3.** Shrinidhi, Madhusudana, Vakreshvara, Satyaraja, wise Kavichandra,
Shankara, Garuda, Bhagavata, Nandana, Chandrashekhara, deep Saranga,

**1.4.** Shuklambara, Yadunatha, Nakula, Vanamali, Mahesha, Shrinidhi, abode of virtues!
The Creator, most kind, understanding My heart, gave Me all of you as inseparable companions.

**1.5.** So accept My humble request: those lovely deeds of the people of Vraja, full of rasa,
sing in all the beauty of sweet ragas — and quench this cruel burning of My heart.

**1.6.** How much shall I reveal the secret of My heart? These mighty wicked enemies have subdued Me;
in vain I have taken a body — I have understood nothing, I have lost the way in the bewilderment of prema.

**1.7.** Again, with joined palms, I say: all of you, with joy, fulfil the heart's desire of the One who is your own —
that birth after birth, without hindrance, I may be a servant of the lotus feet of the Lord of the gopis."[^23-3]

**1.8.** Having spoken such words, the Lord of the twice-born, sinking for a little into sleep, again fell silent.
Narahari, bewildered, cannot describe this incomparable lovely deed, rare even for the gods.

[^23-1]: GPT1 — pp. 348–349, section 5.2 "Ashtakaliya", no. 16 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF pp. 607–608); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 16 (p. ≈224). **The catalogue did
not know it** (new row NG-295). GCC — kirana 2 ("the pastimes on the bed" in the last part of the night), pada 25: after the awakening songs sung by
the parrot (padas 14–23; chapter 22, nos. 17–26, note 35), the GCC says that Gaura, absorbed in rasa, heard a little of them (pada 24) — and the Lord
speaks these words in His sleep. Variants: 1.1 GCC "rasamaya vāta" ("words full of rasa"; GPT "rasa rasa vāta"); 1.6 GCC "maramaka vāta", "hom̐yalu"; 1.7 GCC "jaga" for
"jani". The name "Shrinidhi" stands twice in the list in all witnesses. Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. On the ashtakaliya and
the Lord's sleep see note 36 of chapter 22.
[^23-2]: Radharamana, "the beloved of Radha", is Krishna: the Lord, Krishna Himself appearing in the mood of Radha, longs for Krishna as Radha longs
for Him. The list names the Lord's companions in Navadvipa, mostly known from the biographies: Gauridasa Pandita (in the GCC "gauri"), Haridasa
Thakura, Dhananjaya, Sanjaya, Vijaya Dasa, Mukunda Datta, Murari Gupta, Shridhara, Vakreshvara Pandita, Satyaraja Khan, Garuda Pandita, Nandana
Acharya, Chandrashekhara Acharya, Shuklambara Brahmachari, Nakula Brahmachari, Vanamali and others.
[^23-3]: The words of 1.6–1.7 are the Lord's humility (dainya) in the mood of a devotee: He, the Supreme Lord, is subject neither to maya nor to the
"enemies" (lust, anger and the rest), but, relishing the mood of a bhakta, speaks of Himself as a fallen soul — cf. His words "there is not a
trace of love for Krishna in Me" (CC Madhya 2.42), the prayer "birth after birth, causeless devotion to You" (Shikshashtaka, CC Antya 20.29) and
the verse "a servant of the servant of the servant of the lotus feet of the Lord of the gopis" (CC Madhya 13.80). The reading "prema bharāti" (GCC
"premabharāti") is unclear; understood as "prema-bhrānti", "the bewilderment of prema".

## 2. Narahari — "śuti rahum̐ sundara gaurakiśora…" (GPT1 pp. 349–350, no. 19; GCC)
*Dawn: the beautiful young Gaura is still asleep; the companions read prose and verse, sing songs about Him to instruments, compose verses,
loudly recite the names, weep in humility; the cows low, calling their calves — and the Lord, hearing them, wakes, stretches, yawns, leaves
the chamber and asks for the hobbling rope, calling Gauridasa and the others by their former names. Raga not stated. **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^23-4]

**2.1.** The beautiful young Gaura still lies [asleep].
The sun is already on its way to the east, people are waking — the night is over.

**2.2.** Someone reads the sweetest prose and verse, wholly absorbed in it — a wondrous thing!
Someone, to the sound of many instruments, beautifully sings songs of the Lord's loving deeds.

**2.3.** Someone composes lovely verses, someone by vow loudly recites the names,
someone, struck down by humility, is drunk with the rasa of bhakti — not even an autumn downpour compares with it.

**2.4.** The cows low, distressed by the weight of their udders — they must give milk to their calves;
hearing their call, the Lord at once woke and sat up on the bed.

**2.5.** Then He stretched, covered both eyes with His lovely palms, yawned a little,
left the chamber and goes with an eager heart, asking again and again for the hobbling rope.[^23-5]

**2.6.** Seeing Gauridasa and the others, He joyfully calls each by his former name.
Narahari says: wondrous is this lovely deed — is it deep sleep, or a play of prema?

[^23-4]: GPT1 — pp. 349–350, no. 19 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF pp. 608–609); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 19, pp. 224–225 (catalogue: NG-177). GCC — kirana 3 ("the
awakening"), pada 10. Variants: 2.2 GCC "kou" for "koi" (and so on); 2.3 GCC "śabda ghaṭāpaṭatara nāhi hoya" for "śarada ghaṭā paṭatara…" — the end of the line is
unclear in both readings, the translation is tentative ("not even the roar of autumn clouds compares with it" by the GCC); 2.4 GPT1 "rata sapiyā ana" —
a misprint, corrected by the GCC "vatasa piyāana" ("to give milk to the calves"); 2.5 GCC "puna tanu moṛi" ("stretched His body"). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS
or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^23-5]: The hobbling rope (chām̐dana-ḍora) is used to tie a cow's hind legs at milking. Woken by the lowing of the cows, the Lord is in the mood of a
cowherd boy of Vraja: He hurries to the cows and calls the companions by their "former names", their names in Krishna's lila (thus Gauridasa
Pandita is Subala, Krishna's friend, according to Kavi Karnapura's Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika). Here too the Lord's sleep is absorption in the
lilas of Vraja (note 36 of chapter 22).

## 3. Narahari — "pekhaha gauracandra aparūpa…" (GPT1 p. 350, no. 20; GCC)
*Morning: Gaurachandra, still drowsy, sits on a jewelled seat; the radiance of His body fills the three worlds and rises in the hearts of His
own; His smile is lovelier than a forest of lotuses, His sleepy eyes are reddish; jasmine flowers fall from His loosened hair like stars to
the earth. Raga not stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^23-6]

**3.1.** Behold the wondrous Gaurachandra!
On a gleaming lovely seat of jewels sits the incomparable king Kamadeva.

**3.2.** His beautiful body crushes the pride of the peaks of the mountain of the gods; His mighty radiance has filled the three worlds;
ceaselessly rising in the hearts of His own, He crushes the pride of millions of suns and moons.

**3.3.** His lovely face with its gentle smile — a forest of blossoming lotuses is no match for it;
His reddish eyes droop in deep drowsiness — and destroy the shame, fear and family honour of young women.[^23-7]

**3.4.** From His loosened hair fall jasmine flowers — as if stars, leaving the sky, were falling to the earth.
What poet will describe this wondrous pose? Narahari again and again offers himself for it.

[^23-6]: GPT1 — p. 350, no. 20 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF p. 609); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 20 (catalogue: NG-178). GCC — kirana 3, pada 12 (before it the GCC has
pada 11 "guṇamaṇi gauracandra dvijarāja", which is not in the GPT: Gaura comes out of the chamber and sits on the seat). Variants: 3.1 GPT1 "vilapita" (a
misprint), GCC "vilasata"; 3.3 GCC "nāśata yuvati-lāja-bhaya-kula". Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. "The mountain of the gods" is
Sumeru, the golden mountain; "king Kamadeva" (manamatha-bhūpa) — an image of beauty surpassing that of the god of love.
[^23-7]: The line repeats a common formula of love poetry about the all-attractive beauty of Krishna. We translate faithfully to the author; but
the Gaudiya tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati) does not accept the worship of Gaura in the mood of
"Gaura-nagari": Gaura is Krishna Himself in the mood and lustre of Radha; He came to taste Her love, not to enjoy as a nagara. The Lord's
attractiveness for the people of Navadvipa is the quality of Bhagavan, who attracts all; it is not worldly passion. The same holds for the other
places of the chapter speaking of the young women of Nadia (no. 22, v. 22.2). GPT pada no. 39 ("nadīyāra śaśī raṅge rājapathe": a young woman "has drowned in
the rasa of Narahari's Lord and given up shame and family"; = BR 12, vv. 2380–2383) is in nagari-bhava and is set aside for the section of nagari
padas. "Offers himself for it" (niramañchana) — the rite of "warding off" (nirmanchhana): the lover waves something around the beloved and gives it
(or himself) away for him, averting misfortune.

## 4. Narahari — "śrīśacībhavane adhika sukha āja…" (GPT1 p. 350, no. 21; GCC)
*Morning in Shachi's house: Gaura sits on a seat, around Him circle upon circle of companions, like gods around Sumeru; someone, leaning on
another's hand, stands still as a painting; someone's cloth is slipping; someone, startled, has run from his bed with sleepy eyes — all
drink, like bees, the honey of His face. Raga lalita. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^23-8]

**4.1.** Great joy today in the house of Sri Shachi:
on an incomparable seat sits the beautiful Gaurachandra, king of the twice-born.

**4.2.** Around the Lord — circle upon circle of dear companions, wondrously beautiful,
like the gods surrounding Mount Sumeru: even Shesha cannot describe this beauty.

**4.3.** Someone, leaning his hand on another's hand, stands still like a painted doll;
someone's cloth is slipping, and he does not set it right — what feeling is he experiencing?

**4.4.** Someone, startled, has left his bed and come — his eyes still drooping in deep drowsiness.
Narahari says: they are like bees drunk on the honey of this lotus-face.

[^23-8]: GPT1 — p. 350, no. 21 ("lalita"; scan, PDF p. 609); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 21. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-296). GCC — kirana 4
("the Lord surrounded by devotees"), pada 2 (pada 1 of kirana 4 is a list of companions signed Ghanashyama). Variants: 4.3 GCC "kaichana bhāva na
anubhaba hoya" ("what feeling — it cannot be grasped"); 4.4 GCC "mukha paṅkaja-madhupāne". Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. Shesha
(Ananta) is the thousand-mouthed serpent who eternally sings the Lord's glories.

## 5. Narahari — "āju ānanda parabhāta śacī-aṅganahi…" (GPT1 p. 350, no. 22; GCC)
*A joyful morning in Shachi's courtyard: the companions come and go, sing, dance, whisper and laugh, embrace and bow to one another, ask
whether the night passed well, call one another blessed; someone recites verses, someone with a sigh takes a blade of grass between his
teeth; the companions are countless — like a surging ocean of joy. Raga not stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in
the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^23-9]

**5.1.** Today a joyful morning in Shachi's courtyard — unending love, new delights of every kind!
Someone comes and goes, someone sings a lovely raga, dances wondrously, wanders drunk with rasa.

**5.2.** Someone, putting his lips to another's ear, softly says many words — and, laughing, collapses, unable to stand;
someone calls another and embraces him; someone bows down at someone's feet.

**5.3.** Someone asks another whether the night passed well; someone says: "Now all is well — from seeing the Lord";
someone says to another: "Blessed are you, blessed! Sorrow will go at the mere touch of the breeze from your body."

**5.4.** Someone recites verses and prose; someone with a sigh takes a blade of grass between his teeth;
the companions are countless — as if an ocean of joy had surged: how can Narahari describe it with one mouth?[^23-10]

[^23-9]: GPT1 — p. 350, no. 22 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF p. 609); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 22 (catalogue: NG-179). GCC — kirana 4, pada 3 (the search through
the witnesses missed it because of the garbled OCR; found by reading the GCC continuously). Variants: 5.1 GCC "bhaṅga hu neha" (OCR unclear); 5.2 GCC
"kahu vacana"; 5.4 GCC "kutakāri" (OCR). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^23-10]: A blade of grass between the teeth is a sign of humility: so one begs for mercy in Bengal. The Lord's companions honour one another
("blessed are you!") — for each of them is His eternal intimate.

## 6. Narahari — "ki kahava ājuka aparūpa raṅga…" (GPT1 p. 351, no. 23; GCC)
*The courtyard of Shachi's house: Gaurahari and the companions are like a host of moons in a clear starless sky, which will dispel the
darkness of the threefold miseries; like an arena of mighty wrestlers, who will overcome the asuras averse to the Lord's feet; like a field
of blossoming wish-fulfilling trees giving priceless fruits — no one will be left without. Raga not stated. **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^23-11]

**6.1.** What shall I say of today's wondrous delight!
In the midst of the spacious courtyard shine Gaurahari and His dear companions, inseparable from Him.

**6.2.** Is it a host of moons shining brightly in the clear starless [sky]?
Surely they will destroy the dreadful, densest darkness of the world's threefold miseries.

**6.3.** Is it an arena that removes the burden of the fear of worldly existence — a lovely assembly of mighty wrestlers?
Having overcome the invincible asuras averse to the Lord's feet, they will surely accomplish their work.

**6.4.** Is it a field free of every obstacle, where wish-fulfilling trees have appeared and blossomed?
They will give away incomparable, priceless fruits; Narahari says: surely no one will be left without.

[^23-11]: GPT1 — p. 351, no. 23 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF p. 610); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 23 (catalogue: NG-180). GCC — kirana 4, pada 4. Variants: 6.2 GCC
"uḍugaṇa-vihīna vimala ākāśa kiye…" (the GPT lacks the word "ākāśa", "sky"; supplied in brackets); 6.4 GCC "phire" for "kiye" (OCR). Not in the BR,
PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. The threefold miseries are those from one's own body and mind, from other beings and from the forces of
nature. "The asuras averse to the Lord's feet" — the godlessness of the age of Kali; the companions are warriors of sankirtana who conquer it with
the holy name; "the wish-fulfilling trees" — the companions who give everyone the fruit of prema (cf. CC Adi 9: the Lord is the gardener and the
tree of prema).

## 7. Narahari — "gorācām̐dera kivā e līlā…" (GPT1 p. 351, no. 26; BR)
*The Lord in the mood of His former lila: as in Vraja He stole the gopis' clothes, so now, glancing at His dear companions, He playfully takes
away their clothes and then, His purpose fulfilled, gives them all back. Raga shri. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the
BR; plain Bengali.*[^23-12]

**7.1.** What a lila of Gorachand!
Once He stole the gopis' clothes — now He is lost in that mood.

**7.2.** Glancing at His dear companions,
He playfully takes away their clothes — who knows the secret of this?[^23-13]

**7.3.** As if everything had become as it was then;
having reached the limit of joy and fulfilled His purpose, He gives everyone back their clothes.

**7.4.** Seeing this, Narahari Dasa says:
who in the world would not go mad singing this lovely deed?

[^23-12]: GPT1 — p. 351, no. 26 ("śrīrāga"; scan, PDF p. 610); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 26 (catalogue: NG-181). BR 12 (ed. 1912, p. 946; ed. 1960, vv. 3358–3361):
Ishana shows Srinivasa the place where "Gaurachandra manifested His former lila — He stole the clothes of the devotees" (v. 3355), and quotes Murari
Gupta's verses about it (in our translation, Murari 2.10.16–17: "at the beginning of the night" the Lord pulled the clothes off His servants, filled
with bhava, and gave them back a moment later). Variants: 7.1 GPT1 "gārācām̐dera" (a misprint), GPT1 and GPT2 "vibhola hailā", BR "vihvala hailā"; 7.3 BR "yena
haila sakali sei". Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^23-13]: The stealing of the clothes (cīra-haraṇa) is Krishna's pastime in Vraja (Bhag. 10.22): by carrying off the clothes of the bathing gopis He
fulfilled their vow and desire and removed the last barrier between them and Himself; it is a play of pure prema, not a worldly prank. Here the
Lord repeats it with the devotees in whom the mood of the gopis has awakened (cf. Murari 2.10.15–17) — this is the "secret" of the lila the poet
has in mind.

## 8. Narahari — "suradhunītīre kata raṅge…" (GPT1 pp. 351–352, no. 27; BR)
*Midday on the bank of the Suradhuni: Srivasa and Murari have food brought; Advaita seats everyone in a circle on palasha leaves; Nitai, forgetting
Himself, feeds Gora sweets, Advaita gives Nitai a drink, Nitai puts sweets into Advaita's mouth; the companions merrily feed one another and
snatch food from one another's leaves, and drink the water of the Suradhuni; Narahari carefully gathers the remnants. Raga saranga. **Attribution:
probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^23-14]

**8.1.** On the bank of the Suradhuni, in many delights,
Gaura wanders with His dear companions.

**8.2.** Two praharas of the day have passed —
who knows what was then in the Lord's mind?

**8.3.** At that hour Srivasa and Murari
had all kinds of food brought on platters.

**8.4.** The Moon of Nadia rejoices,
gazing with a gentle smile at the Lord of Sita.

**8.5.** Advaita, with great joy in His heart,
seated everyone — how lovely! — in a circle.

**8.6.** Spreading palasha leaves there,
He serves everyone all kinds of dishes.

**8.7.** Given leave to eat,
all gaze steadily at Gora's face.

**8.8.** Nitai cannot contain Himself:
love surges in His heart — who can fathom it?

**8.9.** Sweet rice, cream, fresh butter, curd cheese
He puts into Gora's mouth and forgets Himself.

**8.10.** Advaita with His own hand
gives Nitaichand a curd drink.

**8.11.** Lovely Nitai, the mighty,
puts sweet balls into Advaita's mouth.

**8.12.** Their bodies thrilled with rapture —
what merriment arose among the companions!

**8.13.** Someone eats after first putting food into another's mouth,
someone snatches [food] from another's leaf.

**8.14.** There are sweets of many kinds —
eating them, everyone's joy grew boundless.

**8.15.** Handful after brimming handful
all drink the cool water of the Suradhuni.

**8.16.** Whatever was left on the leaves
Narahari Dasa carefully gathered.[^23-15]

[^23-14]: GPT1 — pp. 351–352, no. 27 ("sāraṅga"; scan, PDF pp. 610–611); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 27 (catalogue: NG-182). BR 12 (ed. 1912, pp. 937–938; ed. 1960,
vv. 3241–3256): Ishana shows Srinivasa the bank of the Ganga where "the Lord with His companions holds a vana-bhojana" (a meal in the open, v. 3240).
Variants: 8.3 BR-1960 "pravāsa murāri" (OCR; GPT1 on the scan "śrīvāsa murāri"); 8.8 BR "kivā mehā" for "kivā lehā"; 8.9 BR "kṣīra sara navanīta chenā"; 8.10 BR
"chenā pānā". Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. Two praharas are half the daylight (a prahara is a quarter of the day): in the
ashtakaliya this is midday, the time of Gaura's pastimes on the bank of the Ganga (below, no. 18, v. 18.4).
[^23-15]: The meal of the Lord and His companions is prasada; the remnants from the leaves of the Lord and His eternal companions are mahaprasada,
precious to a devotee: so the poet gathers them "carefully" (cf. CC Antya 16 on the glory of the remnants of the Vaishnavas' meals). Srivasa,
Murari, Advaita ("the Lord of Sita"), Nitai (Nityananda) are the Lord's closest companions in Navadvipa. The curd drink (chānā-pānā) is curd cheese
mashed with water and sugar.

## 9. Narahari — "āju gorā parikara saṅge…" (GPT1 p. 352, no. 28; BR)
*After the meal Gora wanders with His companions along the bank of the Suradhuni; standing in the shade of a tall tree, He says something sweet
and gazes at the Suradhuni, takes Gadai by the hand and gently smiles. Raga saranga. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the
BR.*[^23-16]

**9.1.** Today Gora with His companions,
having finished the merry meal, joyfully wanders along the bank of the Suradhuni.

**9.2.** Standing in the shade of a very tall tree,
saying something sweet, He gazes again and again at the Suradhuni.

**9.3.** Gently taking Gadai by the hand,
He softly smiles — what nectar pours forth! Who could keep his composure?

**9.4.** Ah, how sweet this is!
Narahari says: the desire in my heart — may my mind drown in this rasa.

[^23-16]: GPT1 — p. 352, no. 28 ("sāraṅga"; scan, PDF p. 611); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 28. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-297). BR 12 (ed. 1912,
p. 938; ed. 1960, vv. 3257–3260) — immediately after no. 8. Variants: 9.2 GPT1 "rahi ati uccatara chāya", BR "rahi ati ucca taruchāya" (the BR reading is
adopted); 9.3 BR "dhariyā gadādhara-kare", "dhairaya dhare"; 9.4 BR "manuka cita" (OCR). Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. Gadai is Gadadhara
Pandita (on him see note 39 of chapter 22).

## 10. Narahari — "gaura vidhuvara varajamohana…" (GPT1 p. 354, no. 34; BR)
*The walk through Nadia (the afternoon part of the ashtakaliya): countless old men come out onto the road and gaze at Gaura with joy — "who
created this beautifully formed Ananga? How could we hide Him forever in the casket of the heart?" — and bless Him without end. Raga kamoda.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR; Vrajabuli.*[^23-17]

**10.1.** Gaura, the best of moons, the Enchanter of Vraja, walks through Nadia;
countless old men who have come out onto the road gaze at Him with joy in their hearts.

**10.2.** Someone says: "What is this — a beautifully formed Ananga? Who created Him?
Such a wondrous abundance of beauty has come before our eyes!"

**10.3.** Someone says: "What love is born — it cannot be put into words;
how could we keep Him always in the casket of the heart — tell me, what means is there?"

**10.4.** Someone in every way gives blessings without end;
Narahari Dasa ceaselessly drinks in the Lord's sweetness with his eyes.[^23-18]

[^23-17]: GPT1 — p. 354, no. 34 ("kāmoda"; scan, PDF p. 613); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 34 (catalogue: NG-183, "in the BR"). BR 12 (ed. 1912, p. 868; ed. 1960, vv.
2358–2361): Ishana tells Srinivasa that the Lord, "to dispel the sorrow of the Vaishnavas and to make Himself known", walked through Nadia in beautiful
attire, and men and women, seeing Him, spoke to one another (vv. 2353–2357); then follow in a row nos. 10–14 and GPT pada no. 39 (vv. 2358–2383).
Variants: 10.3 BR "dharava anukṣaṇa" ("I shall keep"; GPT "dharaya"); 10.4 BR "nirata diṭhi bhari leta" (GPT "niyata"). Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC or the
Gita-chandrodaya. B. In the ashtakaliya the walk through the town is the fifth part of the day, in the afternoon (no. 18, v. 18.5; no. 19, v. 19.6).
[^23-18]: Ananga ("the bodiless") is Kamadeva, the god of love: the Lord's beauty surpasses his. "The Enchanter of Vraja" (varajamohana): Gaura is Krishna,
who enchants Vraja. The old men, seeing Gaura, bless Him as the cowherds of Vraja blessed the young Krishna — their love is parental (vatsalya).

## 11. Narahari — "āju ki ānanda nadīyāya…" (GPT1 pp. 354–355, no. 35; BR)
*Old women stand in rows by the road and gaze at Shachi's darling: "He is not human!"; "blessed is Shachi, whom this Moon-faced One calls
mother"; "may He walk through Nadia like this and never leave it"; "may He always be well — let us take His misfortunes on ourselves". Raga
kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^23-19]

**11.1.** What joy today in Nadia!
How many old women, standing in rows by the road, gaze at Shachi's darling!

**11.2.** One says to another: "He is not human — I have understood it, having thought it over;
such a youth I have never seen or heard of since I was born in the land of Bharata."

**11.3.** Another says again and again: "What can I say? Now, after so many days, all sorrows have come to an end."
A third says: "What is in my heart I cannot express; blessed is life in this Nadia!"

**11.4.** One says: "Blessed is Shachi! How many pious deeds she has done — and her love cannot be told:
this Moon-faced One always calls her 'mother' — who else has such fortune?"

**11.5.** One says: "May He go about Nadia like this with all the people";
another says: "I have one thing in my heart — that golden Nimai may never leave Nadia."

**11.6.** One says: "I pray to the Creator for this alone — that He may always live in Nadia in well-being."
Gora is Narahari's life, the very pupil of the eye; may I die taking His misfortunes upon myself![^23-20]

[^23-19]: GPT1 — pp. 354–355, no. 35 ("kāmoda"; scan, PDF pp. 613–614); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 35. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-298). BR 12 (ed.
1912, pp. 868–869; ed. 1960, vv. 2362–2367) — immediately after no. 10. Variants: 11.4 BR "karila kateka puṇya"; 11.5 GPT1 and GPT2 "sakala prakṛti saṅge laiyā"
("with all the people"), BR "sakala sukṛti-saṅge laiyā" ("with all the pious"); 11.6 BR "narahari-prāṇa gorā, kevala ām̐khera tārā, ihāra vālāi laiyā mari". Not in
the PK, KGC, PS, GCC or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^23-20]: "He is not human": the women of Nadia perceive Bhagavan in Gaura. "May I die taking His misfortunes upon myself" (vālāi laiyā mari) is a Bengali
formula of motherly love. The last line apparently continues the women's speech, with the poet's signature inside it ("Gora is Narahari's life").

## 12. Narahari — "gaurāṅga-gamana śuni andhagaṇa…" (GPT1 p. 355, no. 36; BR)
*The blind, hearing that Gauranga is coming, step outside; having gained eyes, they gaze and gaze: "The Creator made us blind to give us great
bliss — so that we should see nothing else; whoever has not seen this beauty is blind though he has eyes; Narahari is witness: I have given
these eyes to golden Nimai." Raga bhupali. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^23-21]

**12.1.** Hearing that Gauranga is coming, the blind step outside;
having gained eyes, they gaze and gaze, and their bodies are full of rapture.

**12.2.** One, taking another by the hand, softly says: "Today [our blindness] has borne fruit:
to give us great bliss the Creator made us blind — He did not let us see anything else.

**12.3.** The heart drinks the nectar of this beauty — what happens to it cannot be known;
whoever has not seen such beauty is blind, though he has eyes.

**12.4.** Again and again [the eyes] run to see Him and know no restraint;
Narahari is witness: I have given these eyes to golden Nimaichand."[^23-22]

[^23-21]: GPT1 — p. 355, no. 36 ("bhūpālī"; scan, PDF p. 614); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 36. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-299). BR 12 (ed. 1912,
p. 869; ed. 1960, vv. 2368–2371). Variants: 12.2 BR "vidhi kaile andha"; 12.3 BR "e rūpa amiyā, piyā e nā hiyā" (understood accordingly: "the heart drinks the
nectar of this beauty"); 12.4 BR "ām̐khi nā dhairya vām̐dhe", "som̐pilu". Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^23-22]: "Having gained eyes" (pāiyā nayana): the blind receive sight at the sight of the Lord, and the only meaning of sight for them is to see Him; the
miracle here is a sign of mercy, and still more an image: truly sighted is only one who sees the Lord (12.3).

## 13. Narahari — "nadīyā bhramaye gorā guṇamaṇi…" (GPT1 p. 355, no. 37; BR)
*The lame, hearing that Gora is walking through Nadia, come out onto the road and cannot take their eyes off His face: "Now I understand,
merciful Creator, why You made me lame: if I were not lame, I would have gone off on business to distant lands and died there without
knowing Him; let me remain lame, so as always to see Narahari's Lord in Nadia." Raga todi. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada
is in the BR.*[^23-23]

**13.1.** Hearing that Gora, the jewel of virtues, is walking through Nadia, the lame went out onto the road;
gazing with unblinking eyes at that face, their hearts overflow with joy.

**13.2.** One says: "Listen, merciful Creator, now I have understood:
the purpose for which You made me lame — that fruit You have brought forth now, after so many days.

**13.3.** If I were not lame, I would have gone to distant lands on household business;
had I died there without knowing [of Him], there would have been no end to my sorrow.

**13.4.** I pray to the Creator: let me remain lame like this —
so as always to see in Nadia Narahari's Lord to my eyes' content."

[^23-23]: GPT1 — p. 355, no. 37 ("tuṛi"; scan, PDF p. 614; the number is garbled in the OCR — "৩| pada"); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 37 (catalogue: NG-184). BR 12 (ed.
1912, pp. 869–870; ed. 1960, vv. 2372–2375). Variants: 13.2 GPT1 "ye lāgiyā paṅgu, karile saphala, phalāle eteka dine", BR "ye lāgiyā paṅgu karile se phala, phalā'le
eteka dine" (the sense is the same; translated by the BR); 13.3 BR "nā jāniye tathā". Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. So in nos. 12–13:
every circumstance of life gains meaning if it leads to the Lord.

## 14. Narahari — "bhuvanamohana gorā guṇamaṇi…" (GPT1 p. 356, no. 38; BR)
*Gora walks along the royal road, and hundreds of Kamadevas swoon at His feet; people run from all sides and give Him body, mind and life;
the young dandies of Nadia, glancing at Him, lose their foppish pride, and the connoisseurs of elegance become like fireflies before the
moon. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^23-24]

**14.1.** Gora, enchanter of the world, the jewel of virtues, walks along the royal road with countless graces;
hundreds upon hundreds of Kamadevas, swooning, roll at His lotus feet.

**14.2.** From all sides people come running, enchanted by His incomparable beauty;
who does not offer [Him] body, mind and life, telling one another of His lovely deeds?

**14.3.** All the young dandies who stroll about the town of Nadia in fashionable dress —
glancing at Gorachand, they lost their foppish pride.

**14.4.** Those who in the world pass for refined and are drunk with the delight of elegance —
says Narahari — have become like fireflies before the moon.[^23-25]

[^23-24]: GPT1 — p. 356, no. 38 ("kāmoda"; scan, PDF p. 615); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 38 (catalogue: NG-185, "in the BR"). BR 12 (ed. 1912, p. 870; ed. 1960, vv.
2376–2379). Variants: 14.4 GPT1 and GPT2 "khadyota yemana, kichu āge haila temana tārā" — "kichu" is clearly an error; the BR reading "vidhu āge" ("before the moon")
is adopted; 14.2 BR "kevā nāhi nichaye". Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. The next GPT pada (no. 39; BR vv. 2380–2383) is in
nagari-bhava (note 7).
[^23-25]: "Dandies" (navīna nāgara) are the fops of the town, men; there is no nagari-bhava here: the Lord's beauty humbles the pride of those who prided
themselves on their beauty and refinement.

## 15. Narahari — "nagarabhramaṇe vāhira haiyā…" (GPT1 p. 356, no. 40)
*Walking through the town, Gora goes into the houses of merchants; they joyfully give Him their goods. "I am a poor brahmana pandita," says
Gauranga, "how shall I pay?" — "Pay when You can, and if You cannot — no matter; since You were born we have lived happily; bless us and give
us the dust of Your feet." Raga dhanashi. **Attribution: not established** — the pada is known only from the GPT; plain Bengali.*[^23-26]

**15.1.** Going out for a walk through the town, Gora goes into the houses of various merchants;
the merchants, beside themselves with joy, bring all kinds of goods and give them to Him.

**15.2.** Gauranga says: "I am a brahmana pandita, friends, and very poor;
where shall I get the price for all these things you are giving?"

**15.3.** The merchants say: "Be kind and accept all this;
when You can, You will pay, and if You cannot, we do not ask for payment.

**15.4.** Since You were born we have lived happily with our wives and sons;
cast an auspicious glance on us, bless us, give us the dust of Your feet for our heads and breasts."

**15.5.** Pleased with their words, the Moon of Nadia went home.
Narahari says: blessed are the merchants, blessed, blessed are all the people of Nadia![^23-27]

[^23-26]: GPT1 — p. 356, no. 40 ("dhānaśī"; scan, PDF p. 615); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 40. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-300). Not in the BR, GCC, PK,
KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya; plain Bengali without Vrajabuli — according to Majumdar, rather a sign of Sarakara, but the pada exists only in the GPT, and
the story is common to the biographies; "not established", C.
[^23-27]: Cf. the account in the Chaitanya-bhagavata (Adi-khanda) of how Nimai Pandita went round the shops of Navadvipa — the weaver, the cowherd, the
sellers of perfumes, flowers and betel — and the merchants joyfully gave Him their goods, saying "You will pay later". The Lord calls Himself "a poor
brahmana" in the lila of a brahmana scholar; the merchants feel that their happiness comes from Him.

## 16. Narahari — "mari mari gauragaṇera carita…" (GPT1 p. 357, no. 42; GCC)
*Night: Gaura's companions know nothing but Him even in sleep; separated from Him for the time of sleep, they look at the sky — is the dawn
near? — and listen for the cries of peacocks and cuckoos. Raga not stated. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the
GCC.*[^23-28]

**16.1.** Ah! Who has the power to understand the ways of Gaura's companions?
In sleep and in dreams they know nothing but Gauranga.

**16.2.** The gentle smile of that moon-face crushes the pride of nectar;
not seeing it even for half a moment, they feel that little while as a kalpa.

**16.3.** What shall I say of them! Separated [from Him] for the time of sleep, they are in great agitation:
"How soon will the night end?" they say, and look at the sky.

**16.4.** They listen for the cries of peacocks, doves, cuckoos;
Narahari says: anxiously they think how to bring the dawn nearer.[^23-29]

[^23-28]: GPT1 — p. 357, no. 42 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF p. 616); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 42 (catalogue: NG-187). GCC — kirana 2 (nishanta, the last part of the night),
pada 2: immediately after pada 1 (= GPT 5.2 no. 63, Navadvipa at night: the companions sleep around the Lord's chamber; that pada goes to the next chapter).
Variants: 16.1 GCC "kichu nā jāne āra"; 16.3 GCC "ki kava se sava śayana vicchede". Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^23-29]: The companions' separation from the Lord for the time of sleep is also a lila of love: cf. the gopis of Vraja, for whom a moment without
Krishna is like a yuga. The cry of the birds is the sign of dawn; in Krishna's ashtakaliya the birds of Vrinda likewise wake Radha and Krishna.

## 17. Narahari — "ko varaṇava parikaragaṇa-leha…" (GPT1 p. 357, no. 43; GCC)
*The end of the night: the companions tremble, dreaming of seeing Gaura rise from His bed, drinking the nectar of His words and touching His
feet to drive away the sorrow of their hearts; their hearts long like the chataka waiting for the cloud. Raga not stated. **Attribution:
probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^23-30]

**17.1.** Who can describe the love of the companions?
Seeing that the end of the night is very near, their bodies thrill unceasingly.

**17.2.** Taking courage, they build up their hopes: "The night is going, now the morning comes;
seeing the new grace of Gaura rising from His lovely bed, we shall satisfy these eyes.

**17.3.** The nectar of words from His gently smiling lips we shall drink our fill with our ears, trembling;
touching His feet with our hands, we shall drive the sorrow of the heart far away."

**17.4.** So many hopes arise in the heart — they sink still deeper, singing His virtues.
Narahari says: the heart, like the chataka [awaiting] the cloud, longs — and does not itself know why.

[^23-30]: GPT1 — p. 357, no. 43 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF p. 616); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 43 (catalogue: NG-188). GCC — kirana 2, pada 3. Variants: 17.1 GCC "nirakhi niśānta
niśānta-sumantara" (OCR); 17.3 GCC "śravaṇa camaka bhari piyaba bhūri"; 17.4 GCC, like the GPT, "utkaṇṭhita (nāhi) samujhata anidāna" — the word "nāhi" is in brackets in both
editions (an editor's supplement?); the sense is tentative. Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. The chataka is a bird that, according to
