tradition, drinks only rainwater from the cloud — an image of the devotee who waits for the Lord alone.

## 18. Narahari — "niśi avaśeṣe lasata nadīyāśaśī…" (GPT1 pp. 358–359, no. 47; BR)
*A "table of contents" of the ashtakaliya in Vrajabuli — the eight parts of Gaura's day and night: at the end of the night, sleep in His
chamber; in the morning, bathing in the Suradhuni, the meal and a short rest; in the forenoon, pastimes in the companions' houses; at midday,
pastimes on the bank of the Suradhuni; in the afternoon, the walk through Nadia; at dusk, the return home to Shachi; at pradosha, the house of
Srivasa; at night, sankirtana and sleep again. Raga not stated (in the BR — shri). **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in
the BR; Vrajabuli.*[^23-31]

**18.1.** At the end of the night the Moon of Nadia rests on the bed in His chamber;
the rays of His body sparkle, delighting people — there is no equal to His grace, which crushes Kamadeva.

**18.2.** In the morning, performing the auspicious rites, He bathes in the Suradhuni with great joy;
having eaten all kinds of food with His companions, He lies down for a moment — all the servants serve Him.

**18.3.** In the forenoon, having gladdened everyone, the Stealer of hearts goes out in new attire;
with His companions He sports in the companions' houses — how to understand what this love is? There is no end to its ways.

**18.4.** Blessed is the time of midday: lakes, groves, the cool bank of the Suradhuni;
what poet will describe the many pastimes there? The gods, watching, lose their composure.

**18.5.** Wondrous is the time of afternoon: He walks with His companions through Nadia;
the beauty conquers the world, a downpour of rasa pours — seeing it, the men and women of the town are in rapture.

**18.6.** At dusk He goes home — Sri Shachidevi rejoices, looking at His face;
a wondrous joy: hundreds of people come again and again to see the Lord.

**18.7.** At the time of pradosha, having gladdened His mother's heart, He comes to the house of dear Srivasa;
there the devotees are in great enthusiasm, and the Lord puts on beautiful attire — the sweetest custom.

**18.8.** At night, in the clear hours, drunk with sankirtana, with a joyful heart, in boisterous delight —
and again with His companions He lies down in His own house, Narahari's Lord, the young Gaura full of rasa.[^23-32]

[^23-31]: GPT1 — pp. 358–359, no. 47 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF pp. 617–618); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 47 (catalogue: NG-189, "in the BR"). BR 12 (ed. 1912, p. 947; ed. 1960,
vv. 3371–3378, "śrīrāga"): Ishana tells Srinivasa that the wise remember Chaitanya's eternal lila by the eight parts of the day, quotes the Sanskrit verses of
"the ancients" (vv. 3366–3370: nishanta — sleep in His house; morning — rising, bathing, the meal; forenoon — the devotees' houses; midday — pastimes on the
bank of the Ganga; afternoon — the walk through Navadvipa; dusk — the return home; pradosha — the house of Srivasa; night — the festival of sankirtana) and
then this pada, which retells them. Variants: 18.1 BR "śayana seje", "manorañjana"; 18.2 BR "avagāhana kara", "gala-chana śayana" (GPT "palachana śayana" — understood as "pala-kṣaṇa", "for a
moment"); 18.3 BR "premaka gati naha ora"; 18.7 BR "pahu rāi suveśa" (OCR). Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^23-32]: Gaura's ashtakaliya follows the model of the ashtakaliya of Radha and Krishna (the eight parts of the day in Vraja); it is eternal lila,
which devotees remember in their service (note 36 of chapter 22). The chapter follows these parts: sleep and awakening (nos. 1–6), midday at the
Ganga (nos. 7–9), the walk through Nadia (nos. 10–15), night (nos. 16–17), kirtana in the houses of Srivasa and Chandrashekhara (nos. 20–22).

## 19. Narahari — "niśiśeṣe gorā ghumera āveśe…" (GPT1 p. 359, no. 48; GCC)
*The same "table of contents" of the ashtakaliya in plain Bengali: sleep at the end of the night; in the morning, Gaura in the courtyard
among His companions; bathing in the Suradhuni, the meal and rest; in the forenoon, in the houses of Shuklambara and other devotees; at midday,
in a flower garden; in the afternoon, the walk through Nadia; in the evening, at home, worship of the Deity to please His mother; at
pradosha, the house of Srivasa; at night, sankirtana and sleep. Raga todi. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the
GCC.*[^23-33]

**19.1.** At the end of the night Gora, absorbed in sleep, lies on the bed;
there is no one who, seeing that beauty even once, could keep hold of his heart.

**19.2.** In the morning, having woken, He sits in the courtyard surrounded by His companions;
playfully stealing the hearts of the people of the world, He enters them and dwells there.

**19.3.** Having cleaned His teeth and so on — the bath in the Suradhuni in joyful rapture;
in His own house — the merry meal with His companions, and then rest.

**19.4.** In the forenoon — in the houses of Shuklambara and other devotees:
overcome by the rapture of prema, He sports in many ways.

**19.5.** At midday — in a most charming flower garden:
with His companions in their finery, drunk with the waves of countless delights.

**19.6.** In the afternoon, putting on attire that enchants the world —
the pleasure-walk through the town of Nadia: there is no end to the beauty.

**19.7.** In the evening — the return home, wondrous in every way:
He diligently worships the Deity and so on — what pleases His mother.

**19.8.** At pradosha — into the house of Srivasa, with great joy in His heart:
there He performs wondrous deeds, as the hearts of His dear companions desire.

**19.9.** At night — sankirtana with all His companions;
and again in His own house blissful rest, says Narahari Dasa.[^23-34]

[^23-33]: GPT1 — p. 359, no. 48 ("tuṛī"; scan, PDF p. 618); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 48 (catalogue: NG-190). GCC — kirana 1 (mangalacarana), pada 61, "rāga toṛī": before it
the GCC says that Narahari arranged the eight parts of the day (dawn, morning, forenoon, midday, afternoon, evening, pradosha, night) following "the view of
the crest-jewel of poets, a devotee of Gaura" (pada 59), and gives it as the "summary" (sūtra) of the ashtakaliya, which it then unfolds kirana by kirana.
Variants: 19.3 GCC "suradhuni sināna"; 19.6 GPT1 and GPT2 "bhramaṇa vivāda" — an error, corrected by the GCC "bhramaṇa-vinoda"; 19.7 GCC "kariye yatane"; 19.9 GCC "parikarasaha sukhe
saṃkīrtana kari", "nijagṛhe". Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^23-34]: "Worships the Deity" (deva-vandanā): the worship of the household Deity of Vishnu in Shachi's house; the Lord, Krishna Himself, in the lila of a
brahmana householder performs the duties of a devotee and pleases His mother. Shuklambara Brahmachari is a companion of the Lord at whose place the
Lord ate the rice he had begged (CB, Madhya-khanda).

## 20. Narahari — "bhuvanamohana gaura naṭavara…" (GPT1 p. 360, no. 49; BR)
*The evening kirtana: Gaura, the best of dancers, today dances in the guise of Rukmini — a description of the attire and beauty from the hair
to the feet: many-coloured silks, a jewelled band, earrings, collyrium, a nose-pendant, a necklace, conch bangles, a golden girdle with
bells, ankle-bells. Raga shankarabharana. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR; Vrajabuli.*[^23-35]

**20.1.** Gaura, enchanter of the world, the best of dancers, the Enchanter of Vraja, crown of the relishers of rasa,
today dances a new dance in the guise of Rukmini — He shines incomparably;
the lustre of His body surpasses a golden mirror — He sparkles, lovely and tender;
His beautiful, wondrously many-coloured dress — He is arrayed in various silks.

**20.2.** The locks of His hair are charmingly arranged; ground musk and patterned sandal paste
shine freshly on His forehead; the jewelled band captivates the mind;
the earrings sway at His tender cheeks; His lovely brows are like bees;
His lotus eyes with charming collyrium are lovelier still.[^23-36]

**20.3.** His lips are like the bimba fruit; His nose is like a parrot's beak, with a pendant;
His face is the moon; His teeth crush the pride of jasmine;
His neck has three lines like a conch, His breast is tender; the jewelled necklace steals Ananga's composure;
on His slender hands are conch bangles, on His fingers rings, a delight [to the eye].

**20.4.** His incomparable shapely belly pours out rasa, [His waist] shames the pride of a young lion;
His slender middle of the sweetest charm — a golden girdle with bells shines;
when He gracefully steps on the earth — the earth becomes very soft;
Narahari offers his life for Him; the ankle-bells ring out jhanana.

[^23-35]: GPT1 — p. 360, no. 49 ("śaṅkarābharaṇa"; scan, PDF p. 619); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 49 (catalogue: NG-191). BR 12 (ed. 1912, pp. 913–914; ed. 1960, vv. 2913–2916,
"rāga śaṅkarābharaṇa"): in the house of Chandrashekhara Acharya, Sadashiva and Buddhimanta Khan prepare costumes; the Lord is to dance in the guise of Lakshmi and
others; Shachi comes with her daughter-in-law to watch; Mukunda begins the kirtana; "the Lord became Rukmini — no one could recognise Him" (vv. 2903–2912);
after the pada the BR says that the Lord is the embodiment of all His energies: He dances now in the guise of Parvati, now in the guise of Lakshmi (vv.
2917–2918). Variants: 20.1 BR "varajabhūṣaṇa" ("ornament of Vraja"), "aṅgaruci jini' kanaka darapaṇa"; 20.2 GPT1 "sarasa lasata lalāṭa taṭa maṇi, vandhanā mana mohaye" — divided by the BR
"lalāṭa-taṭa maṇi-vandhanī"; 20.3 GPT1 "daśana mukunda madabharabhañjana", BR "daśana sukunda madabhara tathanā" (OCR) — understood as "daśana kunda-mada-bhara-bhañjana" ("the teeth crush the pride
of jasmine"); 20.4 BR "bhaṅgi saṅge", "nichai". Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^23-36]: The Lord's dance in the guise of Rukmini (and of Lakshmi, Adya-shakti) in the house of Chandrashekhara is described by Vrindavana Dasa (CB Madhya
18): there the Lord appears in the form of His own energy, and the devotees see in Him the Mother of the universe. The Lord is the source of all
energies; the form of Rukmini, queen of Dvaraka, is a manifestation of His own shakti, not a worldly disguise; the description of beauty "from the hair
to the feet" is the traditional praise (nakha-shikha) of the Lord's form.

## 21. Narahari — "āju śubha ārambha kīrtane…" (GPT1 pp. 360–361, no. 50; BR)
*The night kirtana in Srivasa's courtyard: Gaurasundara in a joyful dance among His companions; His feet keep time, and the earth trembles;
on the left Gadadhara, on the right Nitai, in front the intoxicated Advaita; Vasudeva, Srivasa, Vijaya, Vakreshvara, Mukunda and others sing,
Rama, Govinda and Garuda play the mardala; the world is full of cries of "jaya!". Raga mayura. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada
is in the BR; Vrajabuli.*[^23-37]

**21.1.** Today is the auspicious beginning of the kirtana: Gaurasundara in a joyful dance
shines sweetly among His skilful companions in the courtyard of Srivasa;
the lovely lustre of His body shames the pride of golden filaments [of the lotus] and delights Kamadeva;
His lotus eyes glance restlessly in all directions and captivate people's hearts.

**21.2.** Dancing, with the tenderest feet He keeps time — and the earth trembles;
He makes the hastaka gestures, quivering and graceful — the radiance of His hands like young shoots;
His teeth outshine a string of pearls; His soft smile pours nectar;
the fresh sweetness of His lovely face conquers a host of autumn moons.

**21.3.** His glossy curling hair is bound up, the tilaka and sandal paste are charmingly applied;
a wealth of ornaments sparkles on His body — His graceful bends cannot be described;
on the Lord's left is Gadadhara Pandita, on His right lovely Nitai,
in front the intoxicated Sri Advaita; seeing this, the gods come running.

**21.4.** Vasudeva, Srivasa, Nandana, Vijaya, Vakreshvara, Narayana,
Gopinatha, Mukunda, Madhava — these wondrous masters sing;
Rama, and on the left Govinda, Garuda and others play the mardala: "dhikata tadhika,
dhini-ni-ni-ni-ni-ni," says Narahari; the world is filled with cries of "jaya, jaya!"[^23-38]

[^23-37]: GPT1 — pp. 360–361, no. 50 ("māyūra"; scan, PDF pp. 619–620); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 50 (catalogue: NG-192 — with the wrong number "no. 57"). BR 12 (ed. 1912,
pp. 885–886; ed. 1960, vv. 2568–2571, "punaḥ — māyūra"): in a series of padas on the kirtana in Srivasa's house. Variants: 21.1 GPT1 "mudita nartavane" (a misprint);
21.3 GPT1 "sanathukhe" (a misprint; on the scan "sammukhe"); 21.4 GPT1 "ghāsudeva" (a misprint), BR-1960 "vāsudeva, pravāsa, nakhana…" (OCR garbled), "rāma vāme garuṛa, gobinda ādi
vāye, mardala dhiki tā tā dhik". Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC or the Gita-chandrodaya. B.
[^23-38]: Srivasa's courtyard (Srivasa-angana) is the place of the Lord's night kirtanas in Navadvipa (CB Madhya-khanda; CC Adi 17). The singers and
musicians are the Lord's companions: Vasudeva (Datta or Ghosha), Srivasa, Nandana Acharya, Vijaya Dasa, Vakreshvara Pandita, Narayana, Gopinatha,
Mukunda Datta, Madhava (Ghosha), Rama (Shrirama, Srivasa's brother?), Govinda, Garuda Pandita; "dhikatā tādhika, dhini-ni-ni…" are drum syllables
(bol).

## 22. Narahari — "nācata śacītanaya gaurasundara…" (GPT1 p. 361, no. 51; BR)
*Gaura's dance in the kirtana: the mridangas sound, He sings in a sweet voice; His form from the hair to the feet — flowers in His hair,
earrings, tilaka, brows like bees, a face outshining the moons, His smile, arms like an elephant's trunk, a broad chest with a garland, a slender
waist; His feet shame the morning sun. Raga ashavari. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR; Vrajabuli.*[^23-39]

**22.1.** The son of Shachi dances, beautiful Gaura, enchanter of hearts!
Many mridangas sound, beating out "dhi-dhikat dhilang";
He sings in a sweet voice — the bends of His body are wondrously lovely.

**22.2.** Today an incomparable rasa rejoices: He sports among His dear devotees;
His lovely attire sparkles, robbing young women of their composure;
His beautiful hair is adorned with flowers, earrings in His ears, His cheeks are mirrors,
tilaka on His forehead, His lovely brows are bees above His lotus eyes.

**22.3.** His nostrils are the abode of fragrance; His face shames a host of moons;
His soft smile, His teeth are jasmine, His speech sweet;
His neck steals Madana's pride; His arms surpass an elephant's trunk;
soft armpits, a broad chest — on it sways an incomparable garland.

**22.4.** His navel shines with three folds, the line of hair is like a little snake;
His slender waist with its girdle crushes the pride of a young lion;
He is clad in beautiful garments; even Shesha cannot describe His thighs;
the feet of Narahari's Lord shame the young morning sun.

[^23-39]: GPT1 — p. 361, no. 51 ("āśāvarī"; scan, PDF p. 620); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 51. The catalogue listed it under Vasu Ghosha (VG-057, "5.3 no. 51"), but the
signature is "narahari pahum̐ padatale…": **new row NG-301**, VG-057 corrected. BR 12 (ed. 1912, p. 890; ed. 1960, vv. 2624–2627, "punaḥ — āśāvarī"): in the same series of
kirtana padas (preceded by a pada of Govinda Dasa). Variants: 22.1 BR "bhaṅgi parama śohana"; 22.2 BR "yuvati-dhiraya-mocanā"; 22.3 GPT1 "kakṣa mṛdu vilāsa vakṣa", BR "kakṣa
mṛdu, viśāla vakṣa" (the BR reading is adopted); 22.4 BR "pahire bara vasanaveśa", "taruṇāruṇe gañjanā". Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC or the Gita-chandrodaya. B. "Robbing
young women of their composure" is the same formula as in no. 3 (note 7).

# Chapter 24. Appendix. Padas signed "Narahari" from the Gaura-pada-tarangini — VIII: Gaura's night sleep; Nityananda

*Continuation of the appendix (the introductory note on the two Naraharis, on the arguments for attribution and on the marks in the headings
is in ch. 17). Chapter 24: the end of GPT section 5.2 "Ashtakaliya" — the songs on Gaura's night sleep (GPT1 pp. 362–365, nos. 55–63, 65: the
companions gaze at the sleeping Lord and do not dare to wake Him), then section 6.1 "Nityananda" (GPT1 pp. 414–439) — all padas signed Narahari
(nos. 10, 26, 64–69, 71–78, 80, 81: the advent at Ekachakra, the first meeting with the Lord, the coming to Gauda, Panihati, Khardaha, the wedding,
praises), with the addition of the pada on Balarama's rasa manifested by Nityananda (section 5.1, no. 44). The signatures in both sections were
checked throughout, in the OCR and on the scan; the Gaura-charita-chintamani (GCC, kiranas 2–4) and the 12th wave of the Bhakti-ratnakara (BR) were
read continuously at the relevant places. Not translated (outside the appendix): 5.2 nos. 54, 64 and 6.1 nos. 6, 11, 19, 70, 79 — signed Ghanashyama;
the other padas of section 6.1 are by other poets (Atmarama, Govinda Dasa, Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa, Lochana, Jnanadasa, Vasu Ghosha, Balarama
Dasa, Kanu Dasa, Raya Ananta and others; some were translated earlier). The base text is GPT1 (doubtful places by the scan), collated with GPT2, the
GCC (ed. 1947), the BR (eds. 1912 and 1960) and the Gita-chandrodaya; the PK, KGC and PS were checked. On the ashtakaliya as eternal lila and on the
Lord's sleep see note 36 of chapter 22. The notes of the GPT editors are not reproduced.*

## 1. Narahari — "ko varaṇava vara gaura uttāna śayana…" (GPT1 p. 362, section 5.2, no. 55; GCC)
*The end of the night: Gaura sleeps on His back; the poet describes His form — the shining limbs, the face outshining autumn moons, the
earrings, lips, teeth, the necklaces on His chest, the folded hands: as if even in sleep He were pleading with an offended beloved. Raga not
specified ("yathārāga"). **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^24-1]

**1.1.** Who can describe the delightful beauty of fair Gaura sleeping on His back?
His shapely, graceful limbs shine, robbing hosts of steady lightning of their pride.

**1.2.** The sweet light of His face, which conquers young maidens, defeats hosts of autumn moons;
His ears and clear cheeks are adorned with new earrings, matchless, set with gems and pearls.

**1.3.** His lips, putting to shame the bimba fruit and the rays of dawn, are slightly closed, lovely, full of radiance;
the white, beautiful light of His teeth gleams — the stars and the jasmine stay far behind.

**1.4.** On His broad chest are many necklaces, and on it His hands, joined palm to palm, rest unmoving.
Narahari says: this cannot be grasped — surely He is pleading before an offended beloved.[^24-2]

[^24-1]: GPT1 — p. 362, section 5.2 "Ashtakaliya", no. 55 ("yathārāga"; scan, PDF p. 621); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 55, p. ≈233–234 (catalogue: NG-193,
"5.3" — wrongly). GCC — kirana 2 (the "pastimes on the couch" in the last part of the night), pada 18: before it Gadadhara, waking first, serves the
Lord's feet, and He turns onto His back (padas 15–16); then comes a pada of Ghanashyama (GPT no. 54) and this one. Readings: 1.1 GCC "vara gaura
sarasa uttāna śayana"; "dāminī-puñja" ("of lightning") — GPT1 and GPT2 "yāminī puñja" ("of nights"), a misprint; the GCC reading is adopted; 1.4 GCC
"anubhava na hota" (GPT "anubhava nohata"). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS, Gita-chandrodaya. B. On the ashtakaliya and on the Lord's sleep see note 36
of chapter 22.
[^24-2]: The Lord's sleep is not the sleep of a conditioned soul: He is absorbed in the lilas of Vraja and, in the mood of Krishna, pleads in sleep
with Radha who is in mana (offended pride) — the folded hands betray His inner mood (cf. in the same kirana of the GCC, pada 13: in sleep Gaura calls
upon "the crown of beautiful women" to wake). "Which conquers young maidens" is a stock formula of the lyric on Krishna's all-attractive beauty (cf.
note 7 of chapter 23); here it refers to Gaura as Krishna Himself.

## 2. Narahari — "ki kahava gaura śayana anupāma…" (GPT1 pp. 362–363, no. 56; GCC)
*Gaura's matchless sleep: His limbs shine like Kama embodied; His body is soft as fresh butter — it seems to melt on the couch; His
breathing gently lifts His belly, as the Malaya wind stirs the waves of a river on Sumeru. The poet prays that the Lord may so rest on the
couch of his heart. Raga lalita. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^24-3]

**2.1.** What shall I say of Gaura's matchless sleep!
Each of His shapely limbs shines — as if Kama himself, in visible form, were displaying his play here.

**2.2.** His body is soft as a lump of fresh butter churned from a golden ocean of milk;
and, wonder of wonders, without the sun's heat it seems to melt upon the couch.

**2.3.** Languid, limp, He breathes softly, and His radiant belly rises and falls —
as if the Malaya wind, touching Sumeru, drove the quiet waves of its river.

**2.4.** Words cannot convey it — who could compose it? However long one looks, the eyes are never sated.
Narahari says: when will He so recline on the couch of my heart and give me joy?[^24-4]

[^24-3]: GPT1 — pp. 362–363, no. 56 ("lalita"; scan, PDF pp. 621–622); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 56, p. ≈234 (catalogue: NG-194). GCC — kirana 2, pada 7
("lalita rāga"; preceded by a description of the chamber and the couch). Readings: 2.2 GCC "kṣīrododadhi" ("ocean of milk"; GPT "kṣīroda dadhi"); 2.4 GCC
"viracava" (GPT1 "viracana"). Under line 2.3 GPT1 has an editor's note on the reading "vilāse" (not reproduced). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS. B.
[^24-4]: The comparison with Kama (Manmatha) is a common image of the poetry on Krishna; but Krishna is "the Manmatha of Manmatha himself", who
enchants even the god of love (Bhag. 10.32.2), and Gaura's beauty is not mundane: the poet prays not for anything sensual but that the Lord may
reign in his heart. Sumeru is the golden mountain — an image of Gaura's golden body.

## 3. Narahari — "ki kava analpa talpa jhalakata ati…" (GPT1 p. 363, no. 57; GCC)
*Gaura's couch: spacious, spotless as autumn, fashioned by Kama himself; the white pillows are like blocks of Kailasa and the stilled
waves of the Ganga; heaps of flowers, a painted canopy of moonbeams, a silver frame set with gold and gems. Raga lalita. **Attribution:
probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli (the text is obscure in places).*[^24-5]

**3.1.** What shall I say! The spacious couch shines beyond measure, spotless as the autumn season;
wondrous, beyond even the dreams of the king of the gods, a charming work of mighty Manobhava.

**3.2.** Lovely pillows, full of languor and awakening desire, shine — there is nothing like them in the world:
like blocks of Hara's mountain, whole lumps of fresh curd, the stilled waves of the Ganga.

**3.3.** On it, in heaps — karavira, kunda, ketaki, golden lotuses, jasmine;
and when all their tender flowers are strewn, one can no longer tell that this is Gaurahari's couch.

**3.4.** It is as if the Creator painted pictures on a cloth of moonbeams and with great care brought it into the Lord's chamber;
Narahari will say: this couch rises on a silver frame studded with gold and gems.[^24-6]

[^24-5]: GPT1 — p. 363, no. 57 ("lalita"; scan, PDF p. 622); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 57, p. ≈234 (catalogue: NG-195). GCC — kirana 2, pada 8 ("yathārāga";
right after no. 56). Readings: 3.2 GCC "ālasa-dhara jana lālasa-kara vara vālisa" (GPT "ālasa dhara jala lālasa karavara vālisa"; translated after the
GCC: "… awakening desire in people"); 3.3 GCC "vandhuṇa", "kṛta nayana", "sumanagaṇa" (GPT "vandhure", "kṛtanayanā", "samana gana"); 3.4 GCC "deyala",
"bhaṇava sumati" (the sense of "sumati urathita" is unclear; taken as "rises beautifully"). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS. B.
[^24-6]: Manobhava ("born of the mind") is Kama: the Lord's couch is the matchless furnishing of His eternal chamber; yet even in this sumptuous picture
"Gaura-Hari" is Krishna Himself, not a worldly prince. Hara's mountain is Kailasa, the white abode of Shiva; curd and the waves of the Ganga are
images of whiteness.

## 4. Narahari — "mari mari gaura-mūrati aparūpa…" (GPT1 p. 363, no. 58; GCC)
*One of the companions, looking at the sleeping Lord: wondrous is Gaura's form; alas that I have only two eyes; I keep this treasure in my
heart; every morning I see Him, but I have never seen such sleep — shall I wake Him today? Raga vibhasa. **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^24-7]

**4.1.** Ah, ah! Wondrous is Gaura's form — the enchanter of the world, king Manmatha.

**4.2.** What can I do — I was not given countless eyes! Cruel fate, letting me see Him, gave me grief as well.

**4.3.** I keep this longing, filling my heart with it; like a priceless jewel I reveal it to no one.

**4.4.** Who sculpted His body, this graceful frame? It is all my wealth, matchless in the world.

**4.5.** Every day at the end of the night I see Him, but such sleep I have never seen.

**4.6.** So I understand: a new, unheard-of sleep reigns. Narahari: shall I wake Him now?[^24-8]

[^24-7]: GPT1 — p. 363, no. 58 ("vibhāsa"; scan, PDF p. 622); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 58, p. ≈234 (catalogue: NG-196). GCC — kirana 3 ("the awakening"), pada 4
("ko 'pi ca — vibhāṣa rāgeṇa", "and another [said] in raga vibhasa"): after a pada describing the sleeper (3.3) the GCC puts padas 4–7 into the
mouths of various companions who have come to the Lord's chamber at dawn. The readings differ insignificantly (4.5 GCC "kavahi"). Not in the BR, PK,
KGC, PS. B.
[^24-8]: "King Manmatha" — cf. note 4. Hiding one's love (4.3) is a mark of mature prema: the devotee does not display his feeling. "A new sleep":
the Lord is absorbed in lila more deeply than usual; the companion hesitates to wake Him, not daring to interrupt His bliss.

## 5. Narahari — "dhani dhani āju rajanī dhani lekhi…" (GPT1 p. 363, no. 59; GCC)
*Another companion: blessed is this night! The Lord, greedy for sankirtana, did not close His eyes at night, speaking of Vraja in His former
mood — and now He has sunk into a matchless sleep and speaks nectarean words in it; it is already dawn, and He does not wake. Raga bhairava.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^24-9]

**5.1.** Blessed, blessed — I count this night blessed!
Such sleep of the Lord, greedy for the rasa of sankirtana, I have never seen.

**5.2.** He who, maddened by His own former bhava, ceaselessly speaks of lovely Vraja —
whose eyelids do not close even for a moment, who stays awake all night and so meets the dawn —

**5.3.** He has now sunk into a matchless, deep sleep: will He wake — or is this a still greater play?
Wondrous is the way of His sleep: as if in a dream, He utters words like nectar.

**5.4.** The night has gone, the morning has come — and He who sports in Nadia still does not wake.
How can one grasp this deed of Narahari's Lord? I cannot even say whether this sleep will break.[^24-10]

[^24-9]: GPT1 — p. 363, no. 59 ("bhairava"; scan, PDF p. 622); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 59, p. ≈234 (catalogue: NG-197). GCC — kirana 3, pada 5 ("ko 'pi ca —
bhairava rāga"). Readings: 5.3 GPT1 and GPT2 "adbhuta ghuma karīta" — a wrong word division; the GCC reading "ghumaka rīta" ("the way of sleep") is
adopted; 5.4 GCC "vujhava". Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS. B.
[^24-10]: "Former bhava" is the mood of Vraja: the Lord, Krishna Himself, in the mood of Radha and the gopis, does not sleep at night, speaking of Vraja
and of Krishna (cf. CC Antya 14–19: the Lord's nights in the Gambhira). The word "maddened" (unamata) refers to the madness of prema, not to anything
mundane. His sleep too is lila, "a still greater play": in sleep He utters words full of the rasa of Vraja (cf. no. 1 of chapter 23).

## 6. Narahari — "pekhaha aparūpa pahum̐ka vilāsa…" (GPT1 pp. 363–364, no. 60; GCC)
*Another companion: behold the Lord's wondrous sleep! He whose radiance is not revealed even in the hearts of the gods shines in this
chamber brighter than suns; sages perform sacrifices for ages to imagine Him on the couch of their hearts — and here He is easily
reached; it is not the praises of Brahma and Shiva that please the Lord but the words of the parrot in its cage — the custom of Vraja
returns. Raga lalita. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^24-11]

**6.1.** Behold the wondrous play of the Lord!
His sleep — lovely, boundless, sweet — gives rise to the joy of body, mind and eyes.

**6.2.** He, a glimpse of whose bodily radiance is not revealed in the hearts of the gods, however great their effort —
that mass of radiance, by good fortune, shines in this chamber, outdoing rows of suns.

**6.3.** To imagine Him on the fine couch of their hearts, sages perform sacrifices kalpa after kalpa —
and on this couch He, so hard for them to reach, is easily found: what poet can describe this couch's good fortune?

**6.4.** The words of Brahma and Shiva do not gladden Him now — yet He listens with love to the parrot in its new cage, chattering on.
How long will the poet Narahari's Lord stay hidden? His former custom is plainly showing itself.[^24-12]

[^24-11]: GPT1 — pp. 363–364, no. 60 ("lalita"; scan, PDF pp. 622–623); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 60, p. 235. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-302). GCC —
kirana 3, pada 6 ("ko 'pi ca — rāga lalita"). Readings: 6.2 GPT1 "suruci puñja sukṛti iha mandira mājha" — GCC and GPT2 "so rucipuñja" (adopted); 6.4 GCC
"suprakaṭa". Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS. B.
[^24-12]: Brahma and Shiva glorify the Lord with hymns, but the confidential lila is open not to them but to the companions of Navadvipa. The parrot is the
one who, according to the GCC, was reared by a servant of the Lord and sings the awakening songs at dawn (chapter 22, note 35): in Vraja Vrinda's
parrots wake Radha and Krishna — the "former custom" of Vraja reveals itself in Navadvipa. The sages "imagine" the Lord on the couch of the heart —
an image of meditation: what is not reached by yoga is revealed in love.

## 7. Narahari — "hera cāñā dekha rajanī pāne…" (GPT1 p. 364, no. 61; GCC)
*Another companion: look — who ever knew such sleep? The pose of the hands and feet, the eyes, the moon-face, the smile that seems to drip
nectar; one cannot tell whether He sleeps or wakes; it will be hard to wake Him. Raga vibhasa. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** —
the pada is in the GCC.*[^24-13]

**7.1.** Here, look, see this night: who ever knew such sleep?

**7.2.** How beautifully His hands and feet lie! I never knew that sleep could be like this.

**7.3.** And the eyes — so charmingly closed: how can languor be like this?

**7.4.** The beauty of His moon-face is greater still: as if nectar dripped from His gentle smile.

**7.5.** I cannot tell whether He sleeps or not; what is in my heart I cannot utter.

**7.6.** How much can Narahari say of it? It seems it will be hard to wake Him.[^24-14]

[^24-13]: GPT1 — p. 364, no. 61 ("vibhāsa"; scan, PDF p. 623); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 61, p. 235 (catalogue: NG-198). GCC — kirana 3, pada 7 ("ko 'pi ca — rāga
lalita"; the GCC edition notes that the Agartala manuscript lacks this pada). Readings: 7.1 GCC "hera cāya dekha gaurāṅga pāne" ("look at Gauranga";
GPT "rajanī pāne", "at the night"); 7.2 GCC "kara-pada-bhaṅgimā", "kabhu"; 7.3 GCC "subhagati"; 7.5 GCC "kahite nāri". Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS. B.
[^24-14]: The Lord's sleep cannot be told from waking: it is not the unconsciousness of a conditioned soul but absorption in lila (cf. 5.3: "or is this a
still greater play?").

## 8. Narahari — "gorācām̐dera rajanī śayana…" (GPT1 p. 364, no. 62; GCC)
*The companions gaze at the sleeping Gorachand, and their eyes are refreshed; joyful, they banter with one another and again and again
admire His sleep. Raga vibhasa. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC.*[^24-15]

**8.1.** Gorachand's night sleep: gazing and gazing at it, everyone's eyes find rest.

**8.2.** Each one's heart is full of joy, and playfully they tell one another many things.

**8.3.** Can a poet describe it — the matchless virtues of Gauranga?

**8.4.** Again and again, with full eyes, they gaze at the sweetness of the sleep of the poet Narahari's Lord.[^24-16]

[^24-15]: GPT1 — p. 364, no. 62 ("vibhāsa"; scan, PDF p. 623); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 62, p. 235 (catalogue: NG-199). GCC — kirana 3, pada 9 ("yathārāga"; before it,
pada 8: Gadadhara sits at the Lord's feet and presses them, while Narahari "floats in an ocean of happiness"). Readings: 8.1 GCC "gaurāṅga cāndera rajani-śayana";
8.2 GCC "ati ānanda hṛdaya". The search of the witnesses had missed it (distorted OCR of the GCC); found by reading the GCC continuously. Not in the BR, PK,
KGC, PS. B.
[^24-16]: "Playfully they tell" — the companions' loving talk about the Lord; it too is part of His lila (cf. chapter 23, no. 5: the companions honour one
another).

## 9. Narahari — "kivā se niśira śobhā…" (GPT1 pp. 364–365, no. 63; GCC)
*Night in Nadia: the moon has washed the town, the trees blossom, a cool wind blows, all the inhabitants sleep in bliss; around the Lord's
chamber are His dear companions, some asleep, some awake; others have gone home at His bidding and pine. The poet prays to be near at this
hour. Raga bhairava. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC (it opens the nishanta-lila).*[^24-17]

**9.1.** How lovely is that night — a heap of blessings filling the town of Nadia!
The moon, a washerman, with his own hands has washed all darkness from it.

**9.2.** Wondrous young trees and creepers shine with a sweetness that enchants sages;
over the freshly opened flowers bees roam in hope of honey.

**9.3.** Softly, softly a cool breeze blows, breathing waves of fragrance;
in supreme bliss all the inhabitants of Nadia lie asleep.

**9.4.** The deep house [of the Lord], ever full of happiness — its beauty has no bounds;
in all three worlds I have seen nothing to compare with it.

**9.5.** Around the Lord's chamber all His dear companions have taken their places;
some sleep, some lie awake — who can fathom such love?

**9.6.** And others, at His bidding, lie in their own homes, pining;
Narahari: when will it be so for me — when shall I too be near at that hour?[^24-18]

[^24-17]: GPT1 — pp. 364–365, no. 63 ("bhairava"; scan, PDF pp. 623–624); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 63, p. 235 (catalogue: NG-200). GCC — kirana 2, pada 1 ("rāga bhairava"):
the first pada of the description of the ashtakaliya ("first, nishanta", the end of the night), right after the "table of contents" in kirana 1 (cf. chapter
23, no. 19). Readings: 9.1 GCC has, at the words "purā se", an editor's mark of a reading "vāsa" (sense: "abode"); 9.2 GCC "praphullita nava kusume bhramara
bhramaye madhura āśe" ("bees roam" — the subject missing in the GPT is restored after the GCC); 9.5 GCC "keha śuñā keha jāgiyā rayeche". Not in the BR, PK,
KGC, PS. B.
[^24-18]: The moon as a "washerman" washing away darkness is a familiar image of moonlight. The pining of the companions sent home is a lila of separation
(cf. chapter 23, nos. 16–17). The poet's wish "to be near at that hour" is a prayer for eternal service to the Lord in His nitya-lila.

## 10. Narahari — "ratana mandira madhi śuti gora sundara…" (GPT1 p. 365, no. 65)
*The Lord sleeps in a chamber of jewels, surrounded by His companions, like the moon among the stars; at the end of the night the
companions sing auspicious songs, as court singers wake a prince; the Lord leaves sleep and sits up on the couch to listen. Raga turi.
**Attribution: not established** — only in the GPT; Vrajabuli.*[^24-19]

**10.1.** In the chamber of jewels fair Gora sleeps, enjoying the play of sleep;
the host of dear companions sleeps all around the beloved Lord.

**10.2.** As in the wide sky the moon, encircled by rows of stars —
what poet has the power to describe that wondrous beauty?

**10.3.** Seeing that the night is ending, the companions sing auspicious songs —
as court singers and bards strike up a tune to break a prince's sleep.

**10.4.** Leaving sleep, He who sports in Nadia sat up on the couch to listen;
enchanted Narahari is enchanted beyond measure, beholding that joy.[^24-20]

[^24-19]: GPT1 — p. 365, no. 65 ("tuṛī"; scan, PDF p. 624; the last pada of section 5.2); GPT2 — section 5.2, no. 65, p. ≈235–236. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row
NG-303). Not found in any witness (GCC, BR, PK, KGC, PS, Gita-chandrodaya). The GPT1 OCR is badly distorted ("vatana mandira maṇi śuṇaṭha … bhugcai
śanavilāsa"); the text follows the scan. Before it, no. 64 is a pada of Ghanashyama on the Lord's chamber (= GCC 2.10). "Not established", C.
[^24-20]: Vaitalikas and magadhas are court singers and bards who woke kings with songs and praises. The Lord's awakening by His companions' songs is the
beginning of the morning lila (cf. the awakening songs, chapter 22, nos. 17–26). The companions sleep "around" the Lord, as in 9.5.

## 11. Narahari — "āhā mari āju ki ānanda…" (GPT1 p. 417, section 6.1, no. 10; BR)
*Nityananda's advent at Ekachakra, in the house of Hadai Pandita: the parents' joy; Advaita in Shantipura roars and dances: "I have brought
Balavira!"; the gods shower flowers; the Ojha gives gifts; blessed are the land of Radha and the bright thirteenth night of the month of
Magha. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^24-21]

**11.1.** Ah, what joy today!
In Ekachakrapura, in the house of Hadai Pandita, Nityananda has descended!

**11.2.** His body is most tender, like fresh golden butter; by His beauty the world is enchanted.
Gazing at His moon-face, Padmavati and Hadai Pandita cannot contain their delight.

**11.3.** Sri Advaita in Shantipura roars in a flood of joy and cannot be still for a moment;
He dances with arms raised, slaps His sides and says: "I have brought, I have brought Balavira!"

**11.4.** Brahma and the other gods shower Him with flowers; "Jaya, jaya!" resounds without end;
all the gandharvas and kinnaras play hundreds of instruments and sing His glory — an ocean of happiness.

**11.5.** The Ojha, most fortunate, for his son's welfare gives away gifts beyond counting;
in what merriment the people come running — the house is too crowded to enter!

**11.6.** Blessed is the land of Radha, blessed that nakshatra and that day, blessed the bright thirteenth night of Magha!
Narahari says: well done! Blessed, blessed is the age of Kali — by His appearance He has destroyed the heaps of sorrow.[^24-22]

[^24-21]: GPT1 — p. 417, section 6.1 "Nityananda", no. 10 ("kāmoda"; scan, PDF p. 676); GPT2 — section 6.1, no. 10, p. ≈273 (catalogue: NG-202, "in the BR"). BR 12 (ed. 1912,
pp. 824–825; ed. 1960, vv. 1711–1716): Narahari Chakravarti, showing Srinivasa the places of Navadvipa, tells of Nityananda, His parents and the day of His
advent — the bright thirteenth night of Magha (a Sanskrit verse, v. 1709) — and introduces the pada with the words "this joy the wise have described in many
ways"; then follows a pada of Ghanashyama (GPT no. 11). Readings: 11.2 BR "putramukha nirakhiyā" ("gazing at their son's face"; GPT "candra mukha"), "hāṛāi"
(GPT "hārāi"); 11.5 BR "yautuka laiyā" ("bringing gifts"; GPT "kautuka lañā", "in merriment"). Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC. B.
[^24-22]: Nityananda is Balarama Himself, the first expansion of Krishna (CC Adi 5); therefore Advaita, foreseeing His advent, cries: "I have brought Balavira"
("the hero Bala", Balarama) — just as He called Gaura into the world. Ojha is Hadai Pandita's family title. On Nityananda's childhood at Ekachakra — CB Adi 9.
The land of Radha (Rāṛha) is the region of Bengal west of the Ganga where Ekachakra lies.

## 12. Narahari — "bhāve gara gara nitāi sundara…" (GPT1 p. 422, no. 26; BR)
*The first meeting in Navadvipa: seeing Gorachand's radiance, Nityananda enters ecstasy — roaring, rolling on the ground, sighs, laughter,
leaps, trembling; at last He grows still in Vishvambhara's embrace; the Lord, holding Him in His lap, weeps; Srivasa and the others weep.
Raga mayura. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^24-23]

**12.1.** Overflowing with bhava, beautiful Nitai, seeing Gorachand's radiance —
how much wells up in His heart! He cannot stand still; on every limb new waves of thrill.

**12.2.** What madness! Now a lion's roar, now He rolls on the ground;
now long sighs, now loud laughter; His cloth slips off, He floats in tears.

**12.3.** Now leap after leap, now His whole body trembles; now He runs — no one can hold Him;
now, saying something, He grows still and sinks into Vishvambhara's embrace.

**12.4.** Taking Nityananda in His lap, the Lord floats in tears — such is the way of love!
Narahari says: Srivasa and the others around weep; no one can keep composure.[^24-24]

[^24-23]: GPT1 — p. 422, no. 26 ("māyura"; scan, PDF p. 681); GPT2 — section 6.1, no. 26. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-304; the catalogue row NG-203 had
by mistake given the first line of no. 64). BR 12 (ed. 1912, p. 874; ed. 1960, vv. 2437–2440): Nityananda has come secretly to Nadia; the Lord with the devotees
goes to Him in Nandana Acharya's house; at the Lord's sign Srivasa recites the verse on Krishna entering Vrindavana (Bhag. 10.21.5) — "hearing the verse on
Krishna, Nityananda entered the bhava that everyone sings of". Readings: 12.1 BR "gorā-mukhacāndera chaṭā" ("the radiance of Gora's moon-face"); 12.2 BR
"loṭāyaye dharaṇītale". The Navadvipa-parikrama is the same as the BR. Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC. B.
[^24-24]: The Lord's first meeting with Nityananda in Nandana Acharya's house — CB Madhya 3; CC Adi 17. Nityananda's "madness" (unmāda) is the madness of prema: the
ecstasy of Balarama hearing of His younger brother Krishna — not a worldly derangement. Vishvambhara is the Lord's name in Navadvipa.

## 13. Narahari — "ki madhura madhuniśā…" (GPT1 p. 335, section 5.1, no. 44; BR)
*A moonlit spring night by the Ganga, which is like the Yamuna; remembering His former pastimes, Nityananda trembles; seeing this,
Gaurasundara enters ecstasy; all sing of Balarama's rasa; gods and men dance; through all the world — "Jaya, Nityananda, son of Rohini!"
Raga kedara. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^24-25]

**13.1.** What a sweet spring night! The moon has lit the quarters, a gentle Malaya breeze blows;
the Jahnavi is like the Yamuna, its banks are pure; cuckoos, peacocks and parrots call.

**13.2.** What festivity today in Nadia!
Remembering His former play, Nitai thrills all over and cannot be still for a moment.

**13.3.** Seeing Nitai's ways, Sri Gaurasundara, in great love, is overcome;
no one can keep composure — all sing in many tunes of Balaichand's rasa-lila.

**13.4.** Gods and men dance together with arms raised; many instruments play without end;
Narahari Dasa says: through all the world — "Jaya, jaya Nityananda, son of Rohini!"[^24-26]

[^24-25]: GPT1 — p. 335, section 5.1 ("festivals of the year"), no. 44 ("kedāra"; scan, PDF p. 594); GPT2 — section 5.1, no. 44, p. ≈214. The catalogue had assigned it
to Vasu Ghosha (VG-048); the signature is "dāsa narahari kaya" (NG-260). BR 12 (ed. 1912, p. 945; ed. 1960, vv. 3351–3354): "once here Nityananda-Haladhara,
rejoicing in the rasa of His former rasa-lila…" — among the places of Navadvipa, after a pada on Holi; then follows the account of the stealing of the
companions' clothes (cf. chapter 23, no. 7). Readings: 13.1 BR "kuhure kokila"; 13.2 BR "āju ki kautuka nadīyāte"; 13.3 BR "gāya sabhe nānā chām̐de". Not in the
PK, KGC, PS, GCC. B.
[^24-26]: Balarama's rasa — Bhag. 10.65: coming to Vraja, Balarama spent the moonlit nights of two spring months with the gopis on the bank of the Yamuna
(madhu-madhava); this is His own eternal lila, not a worldly one. Nityananda, Balarama Himself, remembers it by the Ganga, and Gaura, Krishna Himself,
seeing His elder brother's bhava, is Himself overcome. "Sweet night" (madhuniśā) is a night of the month of Madhu (spring).

## 14. Narahari — "gorāpreme gara gara nitāi āmāra…" (GPT1 p. 433, no. 64; BR, Gita-chandrodaya)
*Nityananda comes to Gauda: overflowing with love for Gaura, He weeps, thrills, walks with an elephant's gait, embraces the fallen and makes
them repeat "Hari!". Raga dhanashi. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR and in the Gita-chandrodaya.*[^24-27]

**14.1.** My Nitai, overflowing with love for Gora!
From His crimson eyes flows a stream like the Suradhuni.

**14.2.** Waves of thrill shine on the Lord's body;
with the gait of a lordly elephant He goes, swaying.

**14.3.** Seeing the fallen, He spreads both arms,
embraces them and makes them say again and again: "Hari, Hari!"

**14.4.** Who else will be such an ocean of mercy?
Narahari: He descended to deliver the fallen.[^24-28]

[^24-27]: GPT1 — p. 433, no. 64 ("dhānaśī"; scan, PDF p. 692); GPT2 — section 6.1, no. 64, p. ≈286 (catalogue: NG-203 — with a garbled first line). BR 12 (ed. 1912, p. 967;
ed. 1960, vv. 3632–3635): the Lord sends Nityananda from Puri to Gauda (CB Antya 5 is quoted there); Nityananda, passing through Utkala, comes to Gauda —
"everywhere the word spread: Nityananda Raya has come, intoxicated with prema", — and people run to see Him. Gita-chandrodaya (ed. 1948), section on
Nityananda, pada 2. Readings: 14.2 BR and Gita-chandrodaya "śobhe hema gāya" ("on His golden body"; GPT "śohe pahum̐ gāya"); 14.3 BR "kroṛe kari", "volāya"; 14.4:
see note 28. Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC. B.
[^24-28]: 14.4 in the GPT and BR-1960 reads "narahari adhama tārite avatāra"; BR-1912 has "narahari-adhama" ("to deliver fallen Narahari"), the Gita-chandrodaya
"adhama tāriteo" ("to deliver even fallen Narahari"): the poet counts himself among the fallen. "An elephant's gait", "swaying" — the majestic gait of
Nityananda, intoxicated with prema for Gaura (not with worldly drink).

## 15. Narahari — "prabhu nityānanda rāma…" (GPT1 p. 433, no. 65; BR)
*Nityananda's life in brief: birth from Padmavati, twelve years of play at Ekachakra; leaving home with a sannyasi; twenty years of pilgrimage;
coming to Nadia, where He cast away His staff and water-pot; the journey with the Lord to Puri and the Lord's broken staff; the return to
Gauda by the Lord's order and the giving of prema to all. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^24-29]

**15.1.** Lord Nityananda-Rama, matchless in beauty and virtues, was born from Padmavati's womb;
with His companions He played joyfully for twelve years in Sri Ekachakra.

**15.2.** When Gora had appeared, He left home on the pretext of a sannyasi's company;
He wandered among the holy places and after twenty years joyfully came to Nadia.

**15.3.** Finding Gorachand, His very life, caught in that net of love, He cast His staff and water-pot far away;
ever intoxicated with sankirtana, He went with the Lord to Kshetra and broke the Lord's staff into three pieces.

**15.4.** By the Lord's order He came from Kshetra to Gauda and did the work dear to the Lord's heart;
the refuge of Narahari Dasa, the Husband of Vasudha and Jahnava, gave prema to everyone He met.[^24-30]

[^24-29]: GPT1 — p. 433, no. 65 ("kāmoda"; scan, PDF p. 692); GPT2 — section 6.1, no. 65. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-305). BR 12 (ed. 1912, p. 996; ed. 1960,
vv. 4018–4021): after the account of the wedding and of Nityananda's life in Khardaha — "the poets glorify the virtues of Padmavati's son in many ways"; then
follow the padas on Advaita. Readings: 15.2 BR "tīrtha-paryaṭana ka're"; 15.4 BR "vasu-jāhnavāra pati" (GPT "vasu jāhnavāra pati"). The Navadvipa-parikrama is the
same as the BR. Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC. B.
[^24-30]: Childhood at Ekachakra and the departure with a sannyasi — CB Adi 9; Nityananda broke the Lord's staff on the way to Puri (CC Madhya 5; CB Antya 2); He was
sent by the Lord to preach in Gauda — CB Antya 5. The numbers ("twelve", "twenty" years) follow the poet's account. "Was born from Padmavati's womb" (15.1) is the author's word: Nityananda, Balarama Himself, appears by His own will (cf. 11.1: "has descended"; on the Lord's "birth" see note 4 of chapter 20). On the caveat about Nityananda's marriage —
no. 20.

## 16. Narahari — "kṛṣṇera agraja rāma rohiṇīnandana…" (GPT1 pp. 433–434, no. 66; BR)
*Praise of Nityananda: He is Balarama, Krishna's elder brother, the Lord of Varuni and Revati; now He is Nitai, Chaitanya's elder brother, the
Husband of Vasudha and Jahnava; His form, dance, tears, mercy to the fallen; the poet laments that he did not serve Him. Raga kamoda.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^24-31]

**16.1.** Rama, Krishna's elder brother, the son of Rohini —
the treasure of the lives of His two beloveds, Varuni and Revati —

**16.2.** blessed in the age of Kali is He, beautiful Nitai,
Chaitanya's elder brother, Padmavati's son.

**16.3.** The loving Lord of the lives of Vasudha and Jahnava
by His own goodness became merciful to the living beings.

**16.4.** Intoxicated with love for Gora, He knows neither day nor night;
He sanctified the earth by giving the nectar of prema.

**16.5.** With love for Gora His crimson body
shines, outdoing molten gold.

**16.6.** Earrings sway in His ears, captivating the minds of sages;
His arms reach to His knees — matchless beauty.

**16.7.** Who would not forget himself, seeing His broad chest?
Chaste wives of noble families give up their kin for Him.

**16.8.** From His moon-face never cease the words "Gora, Gora!" —
and tears from His eyes run down His face and chest.

**16.9.** With His dear companions, in that same rapture,
all float in the ocean of the joy of sankirtana.

**16.10.** The treasure of virtues dances so as to enchant the world —
the utmost limit of beauty, unattainable even for the gods.

**16.11.** Who, looking at Nitaichand, can stay steady?
Even a heart of stone melts.

**16.12.** To sinners and the fallen His mercy is boundless —
such a Lord wretched Narahari did not serve![^24-32]

[^24-31]: GPT1 — pp. 433–434, no. 66 ("kāmoda"; scan, PDF pp. 692–693); GPT2 — section 6.1, no. 66, p. ≈286 (catalogue: NG-204, "in the BR"). BR 12 (ed. 1912, pp. 994–995;
ed. 1960, vv. 3997–4008): after the wedding and a quotation from the Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika on Vasudha and Jahnava — "the poets sing the deeds of Nityananda,
the Saviour of the fallen". Readings: 16.2 BR "padmāvatīra kumāra"; 16.7 BR "satī kulavatī tilāñjali dei kule". The Navadvipa-parikrama is the same as the BR. Not in
the PK, KGC, PS, GCC. B.
[^24-32]: Varuni and Revati are Balarama's consorts; Vasudha and Jahnava are their incarnations (Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika, quoted in BR 12, v. 3992). "Give up their
kin" (16.7; lit. "offer their family the water of funeral rites") is the same formula as that used of the gopis who left everything for Krishna: it speaks of the
all-attractive spiritual beauty of Nityananda-Balarama, which frees the soul from worldly bonds, not of a worldly attraction (on Balarama's own rasa with the
gopis — Bhag. 10.65; see no. 13). Nityananda is Balarama Himself, the original spiritual master (CC Adi 5).

## 17. Narahari — "āhā mari ki nitāira śobhā…" (GPT1 p. 434, no. 67; BR)
*Panihati, the house of Raghava Pandita: Nityananda dances in sankirtana with arms raised, calls "Gora!", floats in tears of bliss and gives
the poor the treasure of prema. Raga gandhara. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^24-33]

**17.1.** Ah, what beauty of Nitai!
How wondrously He dances with arms raised — enticing the whole world!

**17.2.** Again and again He calls: "Gora!" —
and His body, a golden mountain, ever floats in tears of bliss.

**17.3.** His heart overflows with compassion:
He makes the poor and lowly rich, giving them the gem of prema.

**17.4.** With what feeling He gently smiles!
Narahari says: [that smile] robs chaste wives of their composure and their rules.[^24-34]

[^24-33]: GPT1 — p. 434, no. 67 ("gāndhāra"; scan, PDF p. 693); GPT2 — section 6.1, no. 67. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-306). BR 12 (ed. 1912, p. 968; ed. 1960,
vv. 3649–3652): "first Nityananda with His companions came to Panihati… who can describe the singing and dancing in the house of Raghava Pandita!" Readings:
17.3 GPT1 "kare mahādhvani" ("raises a great cry") — BR "kare mahādhanī" ("makes [them] rich"; adopted); 17.4 BR "dhairaya-dharama nāśe". The
Navadvipa-parikrama is the same as the BR. Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC. B.
[^24-34]: Panihati and the kirtana in Raghava's house — CB Antya 5. On the formula of 17.4 see note 32: it is an image of Nityananda's all-attractive spiritual
beauty, which frees from worldly bonds, not of worldly temptation.

## 18. Narahari — "kivā nācai nitāicām̐da…" (GPT1 p. 434, no. 68; BR)
*The same place: Nitaichand's dance among His companions; He calls "Gora!", the poor run to Him, feeling the breeze of His mercy; all drown in
prema, Kali's pride retreats. Raga dhanashi. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^24-35]

**18.1.** How Nitaichand dances!
His body shines with matchless beauty — a snare for all eyes.

**18.2.** With what new movements He looks about — who knows in what joy He is!
Raising His arms that reach to His knees, He calls again and again: "Gora!"

**18.3.** He ever floats in the rasa of kirtana with His dear companions;
the poor and lowly run to Him from all sides, feeling the breeze of His mercy.

**18.4.** All are maddened, floating in the waters of prema; Kali's pride has gone far away;
counting the virtues of the poet Narahari's Lord, who in the world would not shed tears?[^24-36]

[^24-35]: GPT1 — p. 434, no. 68 ("dhānaśī"; scan, PDF p. 693); GPT2 — section 6.1, no. 68, p. ≈287 (catalogue: NG-205). BR 12 (ed. 1912, p. 968; ed. 1960, vv. 3653–3656; "punaḥ
dhānaśī", right after no. 67). Readings: 18.1 BR "kivā nācaye nitāicām̐da"; 18.2 BR "nā jāni ki raṅge bhorā". Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC. B.
[^24-36]: "Maddened" (mātila) — with prema. The poet Narahari's Lord here is Nityananda.

## 19. Narahari — "āju ānande nitāicām̐de…" (GPT1 pp. 434–435, no. 69; BR)
*Nityananda's abhisheka at Panihati: He is seated on a throne, Damodara bathes Him with fragrant Ganga water to mantras; the gods,
mingling with men, look on; Narahari brings a dry cloth and anoints Him with sandal. Raga ashavari. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** —
the pada is in the BR.*[^24-37]

**19.1.** Today, in joy, having seated Nitaichand
on a beautiful throne — no one can contain his delight.

**19.2.** Taking fragrant Ganga water
and reciting mantras, Damodara joyfully pours it over His head.

**19.3.** With cries of "Jaya, jaya!"
the gods, mingling with men, gaze at His beauty with full eyes.

**19.4.** Some sing, rejoicing in the abhisheka;
Narahari brings a dry cloth and anoints His body with sandal.[^24-38]

[^24-37]: GPT1 — pp. 434–435, no. 69 ("āśāvarī"; scan, PDF pp. 693–694); GPT2 — section 6.1, no. 69. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-307). BR 12 (ed. 1912, p. 969;
ed. 1960, vv. 3658–3661): "there the abhisheka of Sri Nityananda was performed…"; then prose: Nityananda is seated on a couch and garlanded, Raghava holds
the umbrella; Nityananda asks for a kadamba garland, and kadamba flowers are found on a lemon tree (vv. 3662–3665). Readings: 19.4 GPT "pāiyā śuṣkavāsa narahari,
candana dei se aṅge" — BR "parāiyā śuṣka vāsa narahari, candana dei se raṅge" ("having dressed [Him] in a dry cloth… anoints with sandal in joy"). Not in the PK, KGC,
PS, GCC. B.
[^24-38]: The abhisheka and the kadamba miracle in Raghava's house — CB Antya 5. Who the Damodara performing the bath is cannot be established from this text
alone. "Narahari" in 19.4 is a participant in the event; if the pada belongs to Narahari Chakravarti, this is not a signature but a mention of a companion
(probably Narahari Sarakara), and the pada has no signature. The gods "mingle with men" — they come to the festival unrecognized (cf. no. 20).

## 20. Narahari — "vasudhā jāhnavā devī śobhāvadhi…" (GPT1 p. 435, no. 71; BR)
*The adhivasa of the brides — Vasudha and Jahnava, the daughters of Suryadasa Pandita: the brahmanas bless them, placing rice and durva grass
on their heads; their mother is beside herself with joy; the women friends perform auspicious rites; the heavenly women watch unseen. Raga
bhupali. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^24-39]

**20.1.** Vasudha and Jahnava Devi, the utmost of beauty — their bodies adorned with the ornaments of the adhivasa;
their lovely radiance shines like lightning, kunkuma and ketaki.

**20.2.** Around them the brahmanas count themselves fortunate, looking joyfully at the brides;
reciting the Vedas, they bless them, placing rice and durva grass on the heads of both.

**20.3.** The pandita's wife hardly feels the ground beneath her feet, barely restrains her heart;
the women friends perform every kind of auspicious rite and how eagerly they cry "ulu-lulu"!

**20.4.** Conches, bells and many instruments sound — there is no din to compare with it;
Narahari says: the heavenly women, unseen, watch it with great delight in their hearts.[^24-40]

[^24-39]: GPT1 — p. 435, no. 71 ("bhūpālī"; scan, PDF p. 694); GPT2 — section 6.1, no. 71, p. ≈288. The catalogue (NG-207) had run its first line together with the first line of
no. 73 ("vasudhā jāhnavā devī śobhāvadhi bhuvanapāvana nitāi mora"); no. 73 is the new row NG-309. BR 12 (ed. 1912, pp. 991–992; ed. 1960, vv. 3965–3968): after the
bridegroom's adhivasa at Badagachhi in Krishnadasa's house (vv. 3948–3956; there a pada of Ghanashyama, GPT no. 70), Suryadasa at Saligrama performs the adhivasa
of his daughters — "although he had seen his daughters' glory in a dream, he was still overcome by a father's tenderness". Readings: 20.1 BR "taṛita-kuṅkuma ketakī
yanu"; 20.3 BR "karu sakhīkula". Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC. B.
[^24-40]: Nityananda's wedding is His lila, not a worldly event: Nityananda, Balarama Himself, is not subject to worldly bonds, and Vasudha and Jahnava are
incarnations of His eternal consorts Varuni and Revati (note 32); Jahnava Devi later became one of the foremost teachers of the Gaudiya Vaishnavas. The
adhivasa is the pre-wedding consecration; "ulu-lulu" is the jubilant cry of Bengali women. The pandita's wife is the brides' mother, Suryadasa's wife.

## 21. Narahari — "koṭi manamatha-garavabhara-hara…" (GPT1 pp. 435–436, no. 72; BR)
*The wedding procession: Nitai-Haladhara in wedding attire rides in a new palanquin; brahmanas and bards praise Him, the people run to look;
singers, dancers and musicians; torches turn night into day; the gods unseen shower flowers. Raga deshapala. **Attribution: probably
Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR; Vrajabuli.*[^24-41]

**21.1.** Crusher of the pride of millions of Kamadevas, most handsome Nitai-Haladhara
rides in a new palanquin, His beauty brimming over;
in wedding attire, with ornaments of many kinds on His body,
with lovely lotus-eyes, a charming gentle smile on His shining face.

**21.2.** Intoxicated by drinking His beauty, the brahmanas cry "Jaya, jaya";
the bards rejoice and again and again proclaim His spotless fame;
leaving their homes, men and women run, finding no rest,
and, unblinking, gaze at Him from all sides, floating in the bliss of beholding.

**21.3.** Skilled singers sing, keeping tala, shruti and svara, the sweet ragas with their murchhanas and gramas;
dancers dance, beating out: "kataka thaita thai-thai nini ni na";
musicians play many instruments — their skill has no equal:
"thongka na na na na khunga khungkata dhodhilanga dhiki-dhiki nina".

**21.4.** By the glare of countless torches on the earth the night became bright as day;
amid a great din all the people fill the roads;
seeing from the sky, the gods unseen, thrilled with joy, shower flowers lavishly;
the matchless play of the Lord of Narahari Dasa enchants people's minds.[^24-42]

[^24-41]: GPT1 — pp. 435–436, no. 72 ("deśapāla"; scan, PDF pp. 694–695; the heading is garbled in the OCR — "৭২ parda"); GPT2 — section 6.1, no. 72. **The catalogue did not know it**
(new row NG-308). BR 12 (ed. 1912, p. 993; ed. 1960, vv. 3973–3976): "at dusk the Lord set out from Badagachhi to Saligrama for the wedding; instruments sounded…";
then follows the wedding in Suryadasa's house ("according to the custom of the world and the shastras Suryadasa gave Nityananda his two daughters", v. 3983).
Readings: 21.2 GPT1 (scan) "karata bhūsuravṛnda jaya jaya" (OCR "tṛṣavṛnda"), BR "bhūmsuravṛnda"; 21.4 BR "divasa sama bhela rajanī ujora", "saptalokagati patha
śohaye" (GPT "divasa sava", "sava loka gati-patha"). The onomatopoeic syllables of drums and dance (21.3) differ among the witnesses; given after GPT1. Not in the PK,
KGC, PS, GCC. B.
[^24-42]: Tala is rhythm, shruti and svara are microtones and tones, murchhana and grama are the modes of classical music. Haladhara ("bearer of the plough") is a
name of Balarama. On Nityananda's wedding see note 40.

## 22. Narahari — "bhuvanapāvana nitāi mora…" (GPT1 p. 436, no. 73; BR)
*Nityananda goes to the house of Gadadhara Dasa: He calls "Gora!", walks like an intoxicated elephant, with a malati garland on His chest;
whomever He glances at even once He plunges into the ocean of prema; the poet laments that he did not serve Him. Raga dhanashi.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^24-43]

**22.1.** My Nitai, the purifier of the world —
who knows in what bhava He is, ever absorbed in it!

**22.2.** Calling "Gora, Gora!", He raises both arms
and goes swaying like an intoxicated elephant.

**22.3.** On His neck a malati garland glitters,
playing upon His broad chest.

**22.4.** On His lovely face — a sweet smile,
as if the moon were pouring out heaps of nectar.

**22.5.** His eyes, red as lotuses, brim with tears;
that glance is suffused with lovely compassion.

**22.6.** Whomever He looks at even once with those eyes,
He plunges into the ocean of prema.

**22.7.** The poor, the lowly, the wretched — He rejects no one:
who else gives prema like this?

**22.8.** Narahari did not serve such a Lord —
and stayed drowning in the poison of sense objects.[^24-44]

[^24-43]: GPT1 — p. 436, no. 73 ("dhānaśī"; scan, PDF p. 695); GPT2 — section 6.1, no. 73. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-309; see note 39). BR 12 (ed. 1912, p. 970;
ed. 1960, vv. 3680–3687): "having stayed at Panihati, He set out for Navadvipa to see Ai (Shachi); the Purifier of the world with His companions, absorbed in bhava,
goes to the house of Gadadhara Dasa"; then follows Gadadhara Dasa's mercy to the kazi of that village (v. 3689). Readings: 22.8 GPT1 "viṣayaviśeṣe rahila maji" — BR
"viṣaya-viṣete rahila maji'" ("drowning in the poison of sense objects"; adopted). Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC. B.
[^24-44]: "Like an intoxicated elephant" is an image of the majestic gait of Nityananda, intoxicated with prema for Gaura, not with worldly drink. Gadadhara Dasa
is a companion of Nityananda; on his house and the kazi — CB Antya-khanda.

## 23. Narahari — "nitāi guṇanidhi śobhāra avadhi…" (GPT1 pp. 436–437, no. 74; BR)
*Khardaha: Nityananda's beauty, outshining the morning sun; He walks swaying like an elephant, calling "Gora!", with tears of bliss; gods and
men run to touch His feet, and the age of Kali trembles before His might. Raga dhanashi. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is
in the BR.*[^24-45]

**23.1.** Nitai — treasure of virtues, the utmost of beauty: from what nectar did the Creator so lovingly fashion Him!
The radiance of His body outshines the morning sun — seeing it, who could keep composure?

**23.2.** His arms reach to His knees like serpents; His matchless movements float in joy;
His face — a host of autumn moons — sheds nectar with a slight smile.

**23.3.** Calling "Gora, Gora!", His heart overflowing, He goes swaying like an elephant;
from His trembling eyes, red as lotuses, streams of bliss pour down.

**23.4.** Gods and men run to Him from all sides in the hope of touching those rarest feet;
Narahari Dasa: before the Lord's might the mighty age of Kali trembles with fear.[^24-46]

[^24-45]: GPT1 — pp. 436–437, no. 74 ("dhānaśī"; scan, PDF pp. 695–696); GPT2 — section 6.1, no. 74. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-310). BR 12 (ed. 1912, pp. 971–972;
ed. 1960, vv. 3698–3701): "Lord Nityananda came to Khardaha, surrounded by His companions; in the middle, Nityananda, enchanting Kamadeva"; before it is a pada of
Vrindavana Dasa ("vande prabhu nityānanda", GPT 6.1 no. 5). Readings: 23.1 BR "gaṛhila sādhe", "prabhātera bhānu jini' tanuchaṭā"; 23.3 BR "hili' duli' cale kuñjara-pārā". Not
in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC. B.
[^24-46]: Nityananda in Khardaha — CB Antya 5. The age of Kali "trembles": with Nityananda's coming the power of Kali recedes, and the holy name and prema flood Gauda.

## 24. Narahari — "nitāi karuṇānidhi…" (GPT1 p. 437, no. 75; BR)
*Khardaha: Nityananda dances with His companions, making the poor rich in prema; He knows neither day nor night, weeps calling "Gora!", is
covered with dust; all weep hearing of His virtues — only Narahari is far away. Raga kamoda. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada
is in the BR.*[^24-47]

**24.1.** Nitai — an ocean of mercy: Providence has brought Him to us.

**24.2.** The poor, the lowly and the wretched He made rich, giving them the wealth of prema.

**24.3.** With His dear companions He goes about, joyfully dancing.

**24.4.** Who knows with what prema He is intoxicated: He knows neither day nor night.

**24.5.** Calling "Gora, Gora!", He weeps; not for a moment can He restrain Himself.

**24.6.** His body is grey with dust — seeing this, who can stay steady?

**24.7.** Who does not weep over His virtues? Narahari alone is far away.[^24-48]

[^24-47]: GPT1 — p. 437, no. 75 ("kāmoda"; scan, PDF p. 696); GPT2 — section 6.1, no. 75, p. ≈288 (catalogue: NG-208, "in the BR"). BR 12 (ed. 1912, p. 972; ed. 1960, vv. 3706–3711):
"coming to Khardaha, the Lord with His people — in the temple-house of Purandara Pandita… dances and distributes the rarest treasure". Readings: 24.1 BR "āni'
vilāyala vidhi" ("Providence brought and distributed [Him]"); couplet 24.5 is absent from the BR. Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC. B.
[^24-48]: "Only Narahari is far away" — the poet's humility (cf. 16.12, 22.8). Purandara Pandita is a companion of Nityananda.

## 25. Narahari — "gorāpreme mātiyā nitāi…" (GPT1 p. 437, no. 76; BR)
*The same place: intoxicated with love for Gaura, Nityananda dances, falls into the arms of the fallen, weeps, thrills; Kamadeva swoons at
His beauty; the poet drowns in the beauty of His feet. Raga dhanashi. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the BR.*[^24-49]

**25.1.** Intoxicated with love for Gora, Nitai
intoxicates the world, looking at it with compassionate eyes.

**25.2.** He dances, raising His arms that reach to His knees,
and, swaying, falls into the embrace of the fallen.

**25.3.** How His heart overflows with happiness!
Face and chest are washed by the tears from His eyes.

**25.4.** On every limb — waves of thrill;
Madana swoons, seeing the radiance of His form.

**25.5.** On His lovely moon-face, a gentle smile;
speaking sweet words, He pours out heaps of nectar.

**25.6.** What new grace in His crimson feet!
Narahari's life has, as it were, drowned in it.[^24-50]

[^24-49]: GPT1 — p. 437, no. 76 ("dhānaśī"; scan, PDF p. 696); GPT2 — section 6.1, no. 76. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-311). BR 12 (ed. 1912, p. 972; ed. 1960, vv. 3712–3717;
"punaḥ dhānaśī", right after no. 75). Readings: 25.6 GPT1 (scan) "narahari-parāṇa majila mene tāya" — BR "yena tāya" (adopted). Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC. B.
[^24-50]: "Intoxicated", "intoxicates" — with prema for Gaura; Nityananda gives the world the same intoxication of love for the Lord. Madana is Kamadeva: his beauty
pales before Nityananda's spiritual beauty.

## 26. Narahari — "bhuvane jaya jaya nitāi dayāmaya…" (GPT1 p. 437, no. 77; BR)
*The same place: merciful Nitai removes the fear of the round of births and maddens the fallen with prema; He dances calling "Gaurahari!",
falls in the dust; the whole world, seeing Him, forgets its sorrow. Raga gurjari. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in
the BR.*[^24-51]

**26.1.** Through all the world — "Jaya, jaya!": merciful Nitai by His goodness removes the fear of samsara;
the low and wretched He ceaselessly maddens with the gift of prema.

**26.2.** Calling "Gaurahari!", He dances with arms raised and, swaying, falls to the ground;
His tender body — or a golden mountain? — is covered with dust, and how beautiful it is in it!

**26.3.** His eyes, surpassing lotus petals, brim with tears, and again and again the streams flow;
on His face a gentle smile pours out heaps of nectar — a moon dispelling the darkness of sin.

**26.4.** In what bhava He overflows, trembling all over — how can Narahari Dasa describe this play?
All moving and unmoving beings, seeing the excellent Lord, have forgotten the burden of sorrow and float in happiness.[^24-52]

[^24-51]: GPT1 — p. 437, no. 77 ("gujari"; scan, PDF p. 696); GPT2 — section 6.1, no. 77. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-312). BR 12 (ed. 1912, pp. 972–973; ed. 1960,
vv. 3718–3721; "punaḥ gurjarī"); after it Nityananda leaves Khardaha for Saptagrama, for Uddharana Datta. Readings: 26.2 BR "gaurahari buli'"; 26.3 BR "kaluṣa tama nāśi'
śaśī-pārā". Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC. B.
[^24-52]: "Maddens" (unamata) — with the gift of prema, not with worldly madness. Nityananda removes the fear of samsara: His mercy as the original guru opens the
way to Gaura (cf. no. 28).

## 27. Narahari — "nityānanda haraṣa hiyā māha…" (GPT1 pp. 437–438, no. 78; GCC)
*Morning in Shachi's house, the Lord among the companions: Nityananda, gazing at His younger brother, plunges into the ocean of His beauty
and thinks: "Before, I saw the wondrous dark body — but Gaura's golden body captivates me still more; this secret rasa cannot be fathomed";
He prays never to be separated from Him and longs for a body made all of eyes. Raga velavali. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the
pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^24-53]

**27.1.** Joy in Nityananda's heart:
gazing at His younger brother, forgetting everything, He plunges into that ocean of beauty.

**27.2.** In His mind He reflects: "Before, I saw the wondrous dark body;
but Gaura's body steals my heart still more — how can I fathom this secret rasa?

**27.3.** This is the rarest treasure — now, somehow propitiating [the Creator], I will ask him for a boon:
may there never be separation — may He stay fixed forever before my eyes."

**27.4.** Such hopes arise in His heart — the way of prema is matchless and boundless;
again and again, in longing, the poet Narahari's Lord asks the Creator for a body made all of eyes.[^24-54]

[^24-53]: GPT1 — pp. 437–438, no. 78 ("velāvalī"; scan, PDF pp. 696–697); GPT2 — section 6.1, no. 78. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-313). GCC — kirana 4 ("the Lord among
the devotees", morning in Shachi's courtyard), pada 8 ("velāvalī"); before it (pada 7) is a pada of Ghanashyama on Nityananda gazing at Gaura's face amid the companions.
Readings: 27.1 GCC "nityānanda harṣa hiya māha", "anuja nihāri visāri sakala"; 27.4 GCC "premaka gati". Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS. B.
[^24-54]: Nityananda is Balarama: "before" (in Vraja) He saw dark Krishna, and now Krishna has appeared as golden Gaura — in the mood and radiance of Radha (CC Adi 1.5),
and this "secret rasa" captivates Him even more. The prayer for a "body of eyes" is like the gopis' complaint against the Creator who made eyelids (Bhag. 10.31.15):
Nityananda, the Lord Himself, relishes the mood of a loving servant and brother. The poet Narahari's Lord here is Nityananda.

## 28. Narahari — "aparūpa pahum̐ka prema valihāri…" (GPT1 p. 438, no. 80; GCC)
*The same place: Nityananda, rapt in prema, cannot stand steady; Abhirama hastens up and gives Him his shoulder, and Nityananda, gazing at
Gaura's moon-face, laughs; the poet: whoever hopes to attain Gaura's feet bypassing Nitai is the one fool in all three worlds. Raga veloyara. **Attribution:
probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^24-55]

**28.1.** Wondrous is the Lord's prema — I give myself for it!
His heart overflowing, His movements wavering, His feet unsteady — He cannot restrain Himself.

**28.2.** Seeing [this] from afar, handsome Abhirama came up to Him with swift steps;
[Nitai], utterly beside Himself, not even in control of His cloth, laid His left hand on his shoulder.

**28.3.** Gazing at Gaura's moon-face, He laughs again and again — softly, softly, His lips shining;
not even a little of the beauty of His matchless movements could Shesha or Sharada describe.

**28.4.** Whoever, bypassing Nitai, hopes to attain Gaura's pure lotus feet
is the one fool in all three worlds: all his efforts are in vain, — says Narahari Dasa.[^24-56]

[^24-55]: GPT1 — p. 438, no. 80 ("veloyāra"; scan, PDF p. 697); GPT2 — section 6.1, no. 80. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-314). GCC — kirana 4, pada 10 ("veloyāra"); before
it is a pada of Ghanashyama (GPT no. 79) on Nityananda intoxicated with His brother's bhava. Readings: 28.1 GCC "aparūpa prema valihārī" (without "pahum̐ka"); 28.2 GCC
"avaloki", "āola niyaṛe", "vasana pari tām̐kara kandhe"; 28.3 GCC "gauracandra-mukhacanda", "śobhā śeṣa śārada varaṇa śakata nāhi thora" — "śeṣa" adopted after the GCC (GPT
"śobhā śubha śāradavaraṇa"). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS. B.
[^24-56]: "Handsome Abhirama" (sughaṛa abhirāma) is Abhirama (Ramadasa) Thakura, a companion of Nityananda, one of the twelve gopalas; Nityananda leans on him in
other padas of the section as well (cf. 6.1 no. 2: "calling 'brother Abhirama!'"). It can also be taken as an epithet — "the handsome, charming [Nitai] came up [to
Gaura] and laid His hand on His shoulder"; the first reading is more natural. Shesha is the thousand-headed serpent who sings the Lord's glories with all his mouths; Sharada is Sarasvati, the goddess of speech. 28.4 is the central
thought of the tradition: Nityananda is the original spiritual master (CC Adi 5), and Gaura's mercy is attained only by His mercy; cf. Narottama Dasa's song
"nitāi-pada-kamala" ("without Nitai one cannot attain Radha and Krishna").

## 29. Narahari — "vilase nitāicām̐da rasabhūpa…" (GPT1 pp. 438–439, no. 81; GCC)
*Nityananda's form from head to foot: a body the colour of gold with kunkuma and dawn, softer than shirisha flowers, its fragrance filling
the quarters; the smile, teeth, eyes, brows, tilaka, earrings, arms, chest, navel, slender waist, blue silk garments, crimson feet; the poet
prays that the radiance of Nitai's toenails may dispel the darkness of his heart. Raga veloyara. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** —
the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^24-57]

**29.1.** Nitaichand, king of rasa, shines!
His form, outdoing a heap of kunkuma with the dawn upon a golden mountain, enchants the world.

**29.2.** The radiance of His limbs is wondrous; He is far softer than a shirisha flower;
the fragrance of His body, which shatters chaste maidens' fear for their rules, fills the ten directions.

**29.3.** Sweetness on His lips, a sweet gentle smile — His bright moon-face pours nectar;
the gleam of His teeth humbles strings of pearls, His lips are lovely, His chin steals hearts.

**29.4.** Pure, large eyes like lotus petals glisten in joy, full of countless movements;
His curved fine brows — Ananga's bow — put to shame serpents and rows of bees.

**29.5.** Tilaka on His forehead, earrings swaying in His ears, His nose like Garuda's beak, lovely;
cheeks and proud neck finely sculpted, His mighty arms steal the pride of an elephant's trunk.

**29.6.** His chest, conqueror of the three worlds, broad and fine — hard as a gate: what can compare?
His navel a lake, the line of hair its weed, the three folds — the Triveni: who can keep composure?

**29.7.** Who, keeping patience, created this beauty? His slender waist humbles the lion's pride;
wondrous blue garments of the finest silk entice the minds and eyes of people.

**29.8.** His full shanks are soft and graceful, His mighty thighs and knees give joy;
crimson feet, the lovely radiance of the toenails — may they dispel the darkness of this Narahari's heart![^24-58]

[^24-57]: GPT1 — pp. 438–439, no. 81 ("veloyāra"; scan, PDF pp. 697–698; the last pada of section 6.1); GPT2 — section 6.1, no. 81. **The catalogue did not know it** (new row NG-315).
GCC — kirana 4, pada 11 ("veloyāra"; right after no. 80); next (pada 12) is a pada on Advaita's joy (GPT 6.2 no. 5 — no. 1 of chapter 25). Readings: 29.1 GCC
"aruṇamilita-kanakācala-kuṅkumapuñja gañji jaga-vañcana rūpa" ("upon a golden mountain" — after the GCC; GPT "kala-kāñcana", "pure gold"); 29.2 GCC
"kulavatī-yuvatī-dharama-bhaya-bhañjana"; 29.8 GCC "e narahari hṛdayaka tama karu nāśa". Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS. B.
[^24-58]: A description of the form "from head to foot" (cf. no. 22 of chapter 23) is a devotional contemplation of the Lord. Blue garments are Balarama's
(Nilambara, "clad in blue"). "Shatters chaste maidens' fear for their rules" (29.2) is the same formula as in 16.7 and 17.4 (see note 32): the Lord's spiritual
beauty, which frees from worldly bonds. Ananga is Kamadeva; the Triveni is the confluence of three rivers at Prayaga; the shirisha is a flower that is the
very type of softness. "Enchants the world" — lit. "deceives the world" (jaga-vañcana): under the guise of an avadhuta Balarama Himself is hidden.

---

# Chapter 25. Appendix. Padas signed "Narahari" from the Gaura-pada-tarangini — IX: Advaita

*Continuation of the appendix (the introductory note on the two Naraharis, on the arguments for attribution and on the marks in the headings
is in ch. 17). Chapter 25: GPT section 6.2 "Advaita" (GPT1 pp. 439–449) — all fourteen padas signed Narahari (nos. 5–7, 9–11, 13, 15–18, 20, 21, 24):
Advaita among Gaura's companions in the morning at Navadvipa, His form, His thundering calls and His dancing in the kirtana of Gaura's glories, a
survey of His life, a praise, and His advent at Navagram. The signatures of the section were checked throughout, in the OCR and on the scan; the 12th
wave of the Bhakti-ratnakara (BR) at the relevant places, the Gaura-charita-chintamani (GCC, kirana 4) and the section on Advaita in the
Gita-chandrodaya were read continuously. Not translated (outside the appendix): nos. 8, 12, 14, 19, 22, 23 — signed Ghanashyama; no. 4 — no
signature (it ends "the Lord Sankarshana wanders behind them from door to door"); the other padas of the section are by other poets (Vrindavana Dasa,
Lochana, Shyamadasa, Vaishnava Dasa, Kanu, Trilochana, Gokulananda, Balarama Dasa). The base text is GPT1 (doubtful places by the scan), collated
with GPT2, the GCC (ed. 1947), the BR (eds. 1912 and 1960) and the Gita-chandrodaya; the PK, KGC and PS were checked. Advaita Acharya is Maha-Vishnu
Himself and Sadashiva, non-different from Hari (CC Adi 6; the Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika, 11, 76, also calls Him Sadashiva); as with Gaura and
Nityananda, the pronouns referring to Him are capitalized. The notes of the GPT editors are not reproduced.*

## 1. Narahari — "rajanī prabhāta prabhākara sama…" (GPT1 p. 440, section 6.2, no. 5; GCC)
*Morning among the companions: seeing the rising of Gaura's moon-face, Advaita, shining like the sun, beats His armpits in jubilation, walks to
and fro more intoxicated than the king of elephants; His smile is a rain of jasmine; tears flow from His eyes like strings of pearls. Raga beloyara.
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.*[^25-1]

**1.1.** The night has turned to dawn — and Advaita Mahashaya, like the sun, in supreme delight,
ceaselessly beats His armpits, seeing the rising of Gaura's moon-face.
