# Part III. Nagari Padas

---

# Chapter 27. Nagari Padas — I: Vasu Ghosha (padas from the *Padakalpataru*)

## Introductory Note to the Section of Nagari Padas

*"Nagari" (nāgarī) means a townswoman, a woman of Nadia; "nagara" (nāgara) is a townsman, a gallant, and in the language of
Vaishnava poetry the beloved, the hero of the play of love (Krishna is so called: "Shyama-nagara," "rasika-nagara").
**Nagari-bhava** is the name given to the mood of padas in which the women of Nadia, having seen the young Gaura in the
street, at the bathing ghat on the Ganga, in kirtana, tell their friends of His beauty, lose their peace, forget home,
modesty and family, pine through the nights, see Him in dreams, and after His sannyasa lament the separation. In these
songs Gaura is "Gauranga-nagara," "the nagara of Nadia." The imagery is taken from the padas on Radha and Krishna —
purvaraga, anuraga, longing in expectation, disappointed waiting, telling a friend of the meeting; that is why in the
*Padakalpataru* (PK) such padas stand as gaura-chandrikas (preludes) to the corresponding sections on Radha — marked "the
words of the nagaris" (nāgarī ukti) — or are gathered into a separate pallava, "Gauranga's form: the words of the nagaris
and others."*

*Who sang in this mood. Tradition regards Narahari Sarakara of Shrikhanda and Vasu Ghosha as the first singers of
nagari-bhava (Majumdar remarks that Vasu calls Gaura "nagara" following Narahari); poets of the Shrikhanda school wrote in
the same spirit, among them Narahari's disciple Lochana Dasa; later such padas multiply — Nayanananda, Yadunandana, and many
songs signed "Narahari" in the *Gaura-pada-tarangini* (GPT), mostly by Narahari Chakravarti (18th century). Majumdar counts
about twenty padas of Vasu Ghosha in PK as nagari-bhava; padas known only from GPT he considers unreliable (among them are
even reworkings of padas on Krishna, ascribed to Vasu to give nagari-bhava an air of antiquity).*

*The position of the tradition. The Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition does not accept the worship of Gaura in the spirit of the
nagaris.*
- *Vrindavana Dasa in the *Chaitanya-bhagavata* (Adi-khanda), telling of the young Nimai, says that the Lord, who joked and
  played pranks with everyone, in this incarnation did not look at any woman even from the corner of His eye and would not
  even hear the word "woman"; therefore the wise, though every praise befits Him, do not glorify Him as "Gauranga-nagara,"
  but sing of Him according to His nature.*
- *Krishnadasa Kaviraja in the *Chaitanya-charitamrita* (Adi 1.5–6; Adi 4) reveals the secret of this incarnation: Gaura is
  Krishna Himself, who has taken the bhava and the luster of Radha in order to taste the greatness of Her love, the
  sweetness of Himself that She tastes, and Her happiness. He came to taste Radha's love — as Radha, in the mood of a
  devotee — and not to enjoy the love of women as a hero.*
- *Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati counts "gaura-nagari" among the apasampradayas — currents that have departed from the
  teaching of Mahaprabhu: worshipping Gaura as a nagara-lover transfers to His lila in Navadvipa what belongs to Krishna's
  Vraja-lila and distorts its meaning.*

*Gaura's attractiveness for all who saw Him is a quality of Bhagavan (so Krishna too is Madana-mohana, "the enchanter of the
god of love himself"); the biographers also write that the Lord's beauty robbed the people of Nadia of their peace. But the
Lord Himself in Navadvipa was a brahmana teacher, strict in conduct, then a devotee in Radha's bhava and a sannyasi; His
lilas are not worldly love.*

*Rules of the section. (1) The nagari padas are translated for the completeness of the corpus of padas on Gaura and as a
historical document — a witness to how He was sung of in the 16th–18th centuries; they are no basis for worshipping Gaura as
a nagara. (2) The translation is faithful to the author: the text is neither softened nor heightened; where the original
speaks of a glance and of beauty, it is so translated; where it speaks openly of attraction, it is translated exactly, with
a note. (3) The heading of each pada is marked "nagari-bhava"; the notes give a brief reference to this note instead of the
full caveat. (4) Pronouns referring to Gaura are capitalized; the nagaris' words about themselves are in lower case.*

*Chapter 27 contains the padas of Vasu Ghosha known from PK (the earliest and most reliable layer of nagari padas; Majumdar
includes them in his list of Vasu's padas), in the order of the lila: Gaura's form through the eyes of the townswomen, first
love and longing, a night of vain waiting, dreams and tales told to friends, the lament after the sannyasa. The text
follows PK, checked against the scans, with the manuscript variants from PK's apparatus and the *Gaura-pada-tarangini*
(GPT1 — 1st ed., 1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934); the Bengali original, variants and word-for-word translation are in
bn/27.md.*

## 1. Vasu Ghosha — "sajanī ai dekha śacīra nandana…" (PK 2151)
*Nagari-bhava. Gaura's form: "Friend, look — there is Shachi's son!" Birds, beasts and trees weep hearing of His virtues,
noble wives cannot hold their hearts steady; giving to all the name unattainable even for Brahma, Gora has delivered the
world. In PK it stands in the pallava "Gaura's form." According to Majumdar, a pada of nagari-bhava. Raga varadi.*[^27-1]

**1.1.** *(Refrain)* Friend, look — there is Shachi's son:
whoever sees Him has no peace in his heart.

**1.2.** A treasury of boundless virtues, His glory without end;
in the three worlds there is none who could set a limit to His beauty.

**1.3.** Birds, beasts, trees and creepers weep hearing of His virtues;
by His beauty and virtues noble wives cannot hold their hearts steady.[^27-2]

**1.4.** The name unattainable even for Brahma He has given to everyone —
says Vasudeva — so Gora has carried [all across the ocean of births].[^27-3]

[^27-1]: Signature: "Vasudeva." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 249 (printed p. 238), 4th shakha, 18th pallava, section "atha
śrīgauracandrasya rūpa-varṇanaṃ" (description of Gaura's form), no. 43 (mark "॥৪৩॥২১৫১॥"); raga varadi; MS P-R-Sa no. 2258. GPT1 —
p. 117, no. 20 (raga varadi); GPT2 — sec. 3.1, no. 20 (catalogue: VG-183). Majumdar counts PK 2149–2155 among Vasu's nagari
padas. Here the nagari motif is only "noble wives" (1.3); the rest is praise of Gaura, the giver of the name. On nagari-bhava
see the introductory note to the section.
[^27-2]: "Noble wives" (kulavatī) are married women of worthy families who guard the honour of the family; "cannot hold their
hearts steady" (vuka nāhi vāndhe, lit. "cannot bind the breast") — lose their peace. A common formula for describing
beauty, as in the padas on Krishna; cf. chapter 23, note 7.
[^27-3]: Hari's name, unattainable even for Brahma, Gaura gives to all without distinction — the main theme of the padas on
Him as the yuga-avatara (cf. chapter 9, no. 1). MS "gha" in 1.2: "i" for "e" ("these [three worlds]"), "rūpera" for
"rūpe" (same sense).

## 2. Vasu Ghosha — "sakhi he oi dekha gorā-kalevare…" (PK 2152)
*Nagari-bhava. Gora's form from head to foot: a face more beautiful than many moons, arms like an elephant's trunk, a
glance quicker than a wagtail, a sandal tilaka, garlands to the knees, a neck like a conch, a broad chest with necklaces,
reddish feet, jewel-like nails; "the Creator fashioned this form to be the ruin of young women." Raga kamoda.*[^27-4]

**2.1.** Friend, look — there is Gora's form:
His face more beautiful than many moons, His lips lovely.

**2.2.** His rounded arms surpass the trunk of the best of elephants;
the glance of Gora's eyes surpasses the wagtail.[^27-5]

**2.3.** On His lovely forehead is a tilaka of sandal,
wondrous garlands, ever fresh, hang down to His knees.

**2.4.** His neck is like a conch; on His broad and mighty chest,
anointed with sandal, are many jewelled necklaces.

**2.5.** His thighs are lovelier than plantain stems, His feet are reddish;
His jewel-like nails outshine the full moon and a mirror.

**2.6.** Says Vasu Ghosha: where has Gora come from?
The Creator fashioned this form to be the ruin of young women.[^27-6]

[^27-4]: Signature: "Vasu Ghosha." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 250 (printed p. 239), 18th pallava, no. 44 (mark "॥৪৪॥২১৫২॥"); raga kamoda;
MS P-R-Sa no. 2259. GPT1 — p. 117, no. 21 (raga kamoda); GPT2 — sec. 3.1, no. 21 (catalogue: VG-009). On nagari-bhava see the
introductory note to the section.
[^27-5]: The wagtail (khañjana) is an image of lively, quick eyes. MS "ka": "ai," P-R-Sa: "ai" (the same "there," 2.1).
[^27-6]: Lit. "where was Gora not?" — an exclamation of wonder: such a form had never been anywhere. "The ruin of young women"
is a formula of the poetics of beauty (as in the padas on Krishna, "the enchanter of the god of love himself"), not a
description of the Lord's deeds; cf. chapter 23, note 7. MSS "ka," "kha": "shines" (śobhe) for "adorns" (sāje, 2.3; so also
GPT1); "kha": "body" (aṅga, 2.4).

## 3. Vasu Ghosha — "dekha dekha sakhi gorā vara dvijamaṇiyā…" (PK 2153)
*Nagari-bhava. "Look, friend — Gora, the jewel of brahmanas!" With great patience the Creator made this peerless form: arms
to the knees, a hue brighter than gold — is it ketaki, a golden lotus, champaka or a gem? His speech pours nectar; millions
of moons offer themselves for His face; who, having seen Him, could walk away? Raga kanada.*[^27-7]

**3.1.** *(Refrain)* Look, look, friend — Gora, the finest jewel of the twice-born!
With what patience
the Creator made this peerless form![^27-8]

**3.2.** His two lovely arms reach to the knees,
the hue [of His body] outshines gold.
Is it ketaki, a golden lotus,
or champaka, or a gem?

**3.3.** Is its hue that of gorochana or kunkuma? —
no, the radiant body surpasses them.
With sweet words He pours down nectar,
and the mind of the three worlds is enchanted.[^27-9]

**3.4.** Millions of moons offer themselves for His face
and melt, falling at the moons of His nails.[^27-10]
Says Vasu Ghosha: who, having seen Gauranga's face,
could walk away?

[^27-7]: Signature: "Vasu Ghosha." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 250 (printed p. 239), 18th pallava, no. 45 (mark "॥৪৫॥২১৫৩॥"); raga kanada;
MS P-R-Sa no. 2260 (the word "finest," bara, is absent from it). GPT1 — p. 122, no. 32 (raga kalyani); GPT2 — sec. 3.1,
no. 32 (catalogue: VG-127; row VG-126 has the same PK number). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section.
[^27-8]: "Jewel of the twice-born" (dvijamaṇi) — the best of brahmanas. The words "kemane dhairaja dhariyā" can also be taken as
"how can one keep one's composure?"; following the structure of the sentence ("the Creator made… how, summoning patience")
we translate it as wonder at the Creator's painstaking work.
[^27-9]: Ketaki and champaka are golden flowers; gorochana is a yellow pigment, kunkuma is saffron: all these are customary
comparisons for Gaura's golden body.
[^27-10]: "Offer themselves" (nichani) — a rite in which something precious is waved around the beloved to ward off misfortune
and then given away (glossary): the moons are but a ransom for His face; "the moons of His nails" are His toenails, shining
like moons.

## 4. Vasu Ghosha — "o nā ke vala go sajani…" (PK 2154)
*Nagari-bhava. "Tell me, friend, who is this?" — a face lovelier than moons, a hue of gold and gem; the moon and the red
lotus hide in shame before His nails, palms and feet; at the beauty of His brows Madana throws away his bow; a sidelong
glance mixed with a smile strikes everyone; "beware — He has lit up the whole world." Raga (illegible in PK; in GPT1
varadi).*[^27-11]

**4.1.** *(Refrain)* Tell me, friend, who is this?
His lovely face is lovelier than many moons,
His hue is like gold and gem.

**4.2.** The roundness of His arms surpasses an elephant's trunk,
reaching to His knees — how lovely they are!
The moon and the red lotus, seeing His nails, palms and feet,
have hidden themselves in shame.[^27-12]

**4.3.** The two arches of His brows are so lovely
that Madana throws away his bow;
He casts a sidelong glance, mixing it with a smile —
and strikes everyone.[^27-13]

**4.4.** At His waist is a cloth the colour of dawn,
on His neck sways a garland of forest flowers.
Says Vasu Ghosha: beware —
He has lit up the whole world!

[^27-11]: Signature: "Vasu Ghosha." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 250 (printed p. 239), 18th pallava, no. 46 (mark "॥৪৬॥২১৫৪॥"); MS P-R-Sa
no. 2261; the name of the raga is damaged in the scan. GPT1 — p. 122, no. 33 (raga varadi); GPT2 — sec. 3.1, no. 33
(catalogue: VG-010). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section.
[^27-12]: Nails are compared to the moon, palms and feet to the red lotus (kokanada); here the compared is so beautiful that the
objects of comparison hide in shame. MSS "ka," "gha," "cha," P-R-Sa: "of the best elephant" (karivara); "kha": "the trunk of
the best elephant" (karivara-kara); "kha": "roundness" in the form subalani.
[^27-13]: Madana (Kamadeva) throws away his bow because Gaura's brows are a bow lovelier than his own; "strikes" (hānaye)
continues the same image: the glance is an arrow. Cf. note 6.

## 5. Vasu Ghosha — "dekhaha nāgara nadiyāra…" (PK 2155)
*Nagari-bhava. "Behold the nagara of Nadia!" — His gait is sweeter than the step of a royal elephant; bee-like devotees fly
to the fragrance of His lotus feet, and the whole world, drunk with honey, loses the directions; full of rasa, He smiles
slightly, and at the arrow from the corner of His eye millions of Kamadevas swoon; the world is full of cries of "Glory to
Gora!" Raga kamoda.*[^27-14]

**5.1.** *(Refrain)* Behold the nagara of Nadia![^27-15]
His gait in sweetness has surpassed the step of the best of elephants —
wondrous Gora, king of the twice-born.

**5.2.** His feet are like lotuses, and the devotees, like bees,
fly from all sides to their fragrance;
drunk with honey, the whole circle of the earth
cannot tell the directions apart.

**5.3.** Brimming with rasa, with enchanting lips,
He smiles slightly and glances again and again;
a sign from the corner of His eye, an arrow from the corner of His eyes —
and millions of Kamadevas fall senseless.

**5.4.** His ornaments are many gems, His cloth outshines the dawn,
ankle bells jingle on His reddish feet.
The world is full of cries: "Glory to Gora, the jewel of the twice-born!" —
so sings of His virtues Vasudeva Ghosha.[^27-16]

[^27-14]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 251 (printed p. 240), 18th pallava, no. 47 (mark "॥৪৭॥২১৫৫॥"); raga
kamoda; MS P-R-Sa no. 2262. GPT1 — p. 122, no. 34 (raga kamoda; "nadīyāya" — "in Nadia"); GPT2 — sec. 3.1, no. 34 (catalogue:
VG-011). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section.
[^27-15]: "Nagara" (nāgara) — a townsman, a gallant, in poetry the beloved hero; a word by which Krishna is glorified. Why the
tradition does not so call Gaura — see the introductory note. Here, apart from the name "nagara," the pada is a praise of the
Lord's form; the "bee-like devotees" at His feet and the Kamadevas losing consciousness are images of His divine
attractiveness.
[^27-16]: P-R-Sa: "slow" (sumanthara) for "sweet" (sumādhuri, 5.1). MS "ka" and GPT1: "the world's cry of victory" (jagata
bijaya) for "the world is full of cries" (jaga bhari jaya, 5.4).

## 6. Vasu Ghosha — "āre mora rasamaya gaurakiśora…" (PK 2211)
*Nagari-bhava. Praise of the young Gaura, full of rasa: in the three worlds there is no such nagara; noble wives are
enchanted by His beauty, trees thrill, stones melt, birds and beasts weep, the townswomen lose their peace; He stirs the
minds of gods and sages — Gora, the saviour of the fallen. In PK it stands in the pallava "Gaurachandra — another way."
Raga varadi.*[^27-17]

**6.1.** O my young Gaura, full of rasa!
In all three worlds there is no such nagara.

**6.2.** Chaste wives of noble families, seeing His beauty, are enchanted;
hearing of His virtues, trees and creepers thrill with joy.

**6.3.** Stones and trees melt, birds and beasts weep;
the townswomen cannot keep their hearts at rest.

**6.4.** He stirs the minds of gods, siddhas and sages.
Says Vasu Ghosha: Gora is the saviour of the fallen.[^27-18]

[^27-17]: Signature: "Vasu Ghosha." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 272 (printed p. 261), 20th pallava, no. 28 (mark "॥২৮॥২২১১॥"); raga varadi;
MS P-R-Sa no. 2319. The neighbouring pada of the same pallava is Vasu's PK 2210 (chapter 8, no. 2). GPT1 — p. 44, no. 58
(raga varadi); GPT2 — sec. 1.3 (catalogue: VG-132). Majumdar (1961 ed.) cites this pada as an example of Vasu calling Gaura
"nagara" following Narahari Sarakara. On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section.
[^27-18]: The pada joins nagari motifs (6.1, 6.3) with praise of the Lord before whom stones melt and gods and sages tremble —
Bhagavan, who saves the fallen.

## 7. Vasu Ghosha — "madanamohana gaurāṅga-vadana…" (PK 2149)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman tells her friend: having seen Gauranga's face, which enchants Madana himself, she has lost
herself; this is the former dark Kanu become golden — otherwise how could He have stolen her heart? The young wives of
Nadia drown in love, in every house there is weeping; she will cast the rites of her family into the waters of the
Suradhuni and serve Gora. Raga tudi.*[^27-19]

**7.1.** Gauranga's face enchants Madana himself:
having seen this form, what has not befallen me!
His body is the colour of gold — [yet once] this was dark Kanu;
otherwise would He have stolen [so] my heart?[^27-20]

**7.2.** To one whose life is rasa, what is family?
Such is [He] — in the town of Nadia!
What a bitter, cruel lot: the young chaste wives have drowned,
in every house there is the weeping of love.[^27-21]

**7.3.** [My] lotus eyes are redder than the fresh dawn,
streams [of tears] run down my breast.
Ah, I am dying, dying, friend — to you I open my heart:
I will not live without seeing Gora.

**7.4.** The arrow of love in my heart has wounded all my body,
my soul accepts no consolation.
I will go to the bank of the Suradhuni and cast my family's rites into its waters —
I will serve Gora, the jewel of virtues.[^27-22]

**7.5.** All that I heard before is just so:
[He who was] dark-bodied has now become Gora.
The word of Vasudeva Ghosha: know — He is the rasika-nagara;
otherwise would He be the stealer of the gopis' hearts?[^27-23]

[^27-19]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 249 (printed p. 238), 18th pallava, no. 41 (mark "॥৪১॥২১৪৯॥"); raga tudi;
MS P-R-Sa no. 2256. GPT1 — p. 160, no. 8 (raga tudi); GPT2 — sec. 3.2, no. 8 (catalogue: VG-013). A witness is the *Bhakti-ratnakara*, 12th wave (1913 ed., p. 910, scan PDF
p. 918): in the cycle of the words of the women of Nadia that Narahari Chakravarti cites while describing the places of Navadvipa (chapter 29,
note 1), with Vasudeva Ghosha's signature, raga deshapala, beginning with the words "rūpa heri…"; in 7.2 it reads "rahive" (as MSS "kha," "cha").
On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section.
[^27-20]: Gaura is Krishna (Kanu) Himself, who has taken Radha's golden luster (CC Adi 1.5); the townswoman recognizes in Him the
"stealer of hearts" of Vraja. This affirmation of the identity of Gaura and Krishna is the main theological content of the
pada (cf. 7.5).
[^27-21]: The sense of 7.2: before such a Gaura the bonds of family are powerless. MS "ka": "will say" (kahive), "kha," "cha":
"will remain" (rahive) for "will do" (karive). P-R-Sa: "down face and breast" (mukha buka, 7.3; so also GPT1); "that" (se) for
the particle "go" (7.3).
[^27-22]: "I will cast my family's rites into the waters" — I will abandon the duty and honour of my family: a nagari motif
(introductory note). The words of love and service (bhajiva) are spoken by a townswoman; the translation does not soften
them, nor does it add worldly shades.
[^27-23]: "The stealer of the gopis' hearts" is a name of Krishna; Vasu again bears witness: the golden Gaura is the same
Krishna. "Rasika-nagara" — the connoisseur and enjoyer of rasa; in Krishna-lila this is Krishna with the gopis. The tradition
does not accept the application of this name to Gaura (introductory note).

## 8. Vasu Ghosha — "ki kahava aparūpa gaura kiśora…" (PK 2150)
*Nagari-bhava. "What can I say of the wondrous young Gaura?" — with a sign from the corner of His eye He has stolen her
life; His sidelong glance is a calamity: the ruin of the townswomen has risen in the town; she who sees Him cannot forget,
the noble wife leaves her home; love for Gora is a pain of the heart. Raga suhini.*[^27-24]

**8.1.** What can I say of the wondrous young Gaura?
With a sign from the corner of His eye He has stolen my life.

**8.2.** His sidelong glance is a real calamity:
the ruin of the townswomen has risen in the town.

**8.3.** Whatever woman sees Him cannot forget Him;
the noble wife leaves her family and does not stay at home.

**8.4.** Says Vasudeva Ghosha: listen to my words —
love for Gora is a pain deep in the heart.

[^27-24]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 249 (printed p. 238), 18th pallava, no. 42 (mark "॥৪২॥২১৫০॥"); raga
suhini; MS P-R-Sa no. 2257. GPT1 — p. 160, no. 9 (raga suhini); GPT2 — sec. 3.2, no. 9 (catalogue: VG-014). On nagari-bhava
see the introductory note to the section; "the ruin of the townswomen" is a formula of the power of beauty (cf. note 6).

## 9. Vasu Ghosha — "āra eka dina gaurāṅgasundara…" (PK 2169)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman tells: on another day she saw the beautiful Gauranga bathing at the ghat — a face lovelier than
millions of moons, lotus eyes, brows a bow, glances the arrows of Kama; drops of water on His curls like a string of pearls
in a cloud, on His body like pearls on gold; He wrung out His curls and put on a red cloth — "I cannot stay at home." In PK
it is Vasu's first pada in the pallava "Gauranga's form: the words of the nagaris and others." Raga varadi.*[^27-25]

**9.1.** On another day I saw the beautiful Gauranga —
He was bathing at the ghat.
His face lovelier than millions of moons —
seeing it, the heart breaks.

**9.2.** His body tender and radiant like tested gold,
His eyes pure lotuses;
the glances are arrows, the arches of the brows a bow:
so the archer Kama strikes.[^27-26]

**9.3.** His curling locks, and on them drops of water:
like a string of pearls in a cloud;
the drops on His body are like pearls on gold;
seeing this, Kama swoons.

**9.4.** He wipes His whole body, wrings out His curls,
puts on a red cloth.
Says Vasu Ghosha: so it seems to me —
I cannot stay at home.[^27-27]

[^27-25]: Signature: "Vasu Ghosha." PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 257–258 (printed pp. 246–247), 19th pallava, section "atha śrīgaurāṅgasya
rūpa-varṇanaṃ nāgarīgaṇādyuktiḥ" (description of Gauranga's form: the words of the nagaris and others), no. 2 (mark "॥২॥২১৬৯॥");
raga varadi; MSS P-R-Sa no. 2276 and P-R no. 61. GPT1 — p. 160, no. 10 (raga varadi); GPT2 — sec. 3.2, no. 10 (catalogue:
VG-015). The beginning of 9.2 is illegible in the PK scan — restored from GPT1 ("aṅga ḍhala ḍhala"). On nagari-bhava see the
introductory note to the section.
[^27-26]: The Lord bathed in the Ganga daily — the *Chaitanya-bhagavata* too tells of His baths at the ghats of Navadvipa; here
it is only an occasion to describe His beauty. Kamadeva is "the archer" with flower arrows (cf. note 13).
[^27-27]: MSS "ka," "kha," "gha," "cha," P-R-Sa and GPT1: "she cannot stay at home" (nārive). In MS P-R 9.3 differs: "a cloud
flows over it (the cloud of hair)" (vahe jaladhara), "as if" (yena), "pearls on all His limbs" (sakala aṅge mukutāra phala).

## 10. Vasu Ghosha — "eka dina ghāṭe jale giyāchilāma…" (PK 2171)
*Nagari-bhava. "One day I went to the ghat for water — and what beauty of Gora I saw!" A body like tested gold, the Lord
absorbed in the rasa of prema; a lovely face, signs from the corners of the eyes, a sandal tilaka — like the moon among the
stars; smiling, He speaks half-words; who, seeing such a nagara, can keep composure? Raga dhanashi.*[^27-28]

**10.1.** One day I went to the ghat for water —
what beauty of Gora I saw!
His pure body like tested gold;
the Lord was absorbed in the rasa of prema.

**10.2.** A lovely face, enchanting Madana,
the radiance of signs from the corners of His eyes;
fair cheeks, a sandal tilaka —
like the moon surrounded by stars.[^27-29]

**10.3.** Smiling slightly with sweet lips,
He speaks half-words;
with His smile gems and the finest pearls seem to fall —
seeing this, every living being forgets itself.

**10.4.** Says Vasu Ghosha: who, seeing such a nagara,
can keep composure?
Remarkable is that young woman who, having seen this form,
can still stay at home![^27-30]

[^27-28]: Signature: "Vasu Ghosha." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 258 (printed p. 247), 19th pallava, no. 4 (mark "॥৪॥২১৭১॥"); raga dhanashi;
MS P-R-Sa no. 2279. Between PK 2169 and 2171 stands PK 2170, a pada of Nayanananda (chapter 28). GPT1 — pp. 160–161, no. 11
(raga dhanashi); GPT2 — sec. 3.2, no. 11 (catalogue: VG-016). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section.
[^27-29]: GPT1: "on the fair forehead" (sucāru kapāle) for "fair cheeks" (sucāru kapola). "The Lord was absorbed in the rasa of
prema" (10.1) — Gaura in the mood of a devotee: the townswoman sees Him intoxicated with love of God.
[^27-30]: "Remarkable" (dhanya, lit. "blessed") — with bitter irony: it is impossible, having seen Him, to stay at home.

## 11. Vasu Ghosha — "yakhana dekhilum̐ gorācām̐de…" (PK 2172)
*Nagari-bhava. "As soon as I saw Gorachand — I fell into the snare of love": she gave Him body and soul, bade farewell to
fear for her family; without Gora she cannot live, Gauranga has become the treasure of her life. Raga
pathamanjari.*[^27-31]

**11.1.** As soon as I saw Gorachand —
at once I fell into the snare of love.

**11.2.** Body and soul I gave to Him,
to fear for my family I bade farewell for ever.[^27-32]

**11.3.** Without Gora I cannot live:
Gauranga has become the treasure of my life.

**11.4.** My heart cannot hold its composure;
Vasudeva Ghosha knows this rasa.[^27-33]

[^27-31]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 258 (printed p. 247), 19th pallava, no. 5 (mark "॥৫॥২১৭২॥"); raga
pathamanjari; MSS P-R-Sa no. 2280 and P-R no. 14/24. GPT1 — p. 161, no. 12 (raga pathamanjari); GPT2 — sec. 3.2, no. 12
(catalogue: VG-017). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section.
[^27-32]: Lit. "to fear for my family I gave tilanjali" — the libation of water with sesame offered for the dead: a sign of
final farewell. "I gave body and soul" — the words of a townswoman (a nagari motif; introductory note). MS P-R: "to
propriety" (śīle) for "to fear for my family" (kula-bhaye).
[^27-33]: MS P-R: "Gora is my very own" (gorā mora nija) for "Gauranga has become" (11.3); "without Gora I cannot live"
(jīvana nā rahe gorā vine) for "cannot hold… composure" (11.4).

## 12. Vasu Ghosha — "gorā-rūpa dekhivāre mane kari sādha…" (PK 2173)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman longs to see Gora: love for Gaura is a great calamity; she knows neither day nor night, she
remembers Him ceaselessly; what spell has Gora cast with the arrows of His eyes? Her eyes shed tears without end. The raga
is the same as for the preceding pada (pathamanjari).*[^27-34]

**12.1.** I long in my heart to see Gora's form;
love for Gaura is a great calamity.

**12.2.** Whether it is night or day, I know nothing;
ceaselessly I remember Gora, the jewel of virtues.

**12.3.** Repeating "Gora, Gora," what has become of my heart?
What spell has Gora cast with the arrows of His eyes?

**12.4.** My eyes pour without ceasing and accept no consolation;
"a great calamity is love," sings Vasu Ghosha.

[^27-34]: Signature: "Vasu Ghosha." PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 258–259 (printed pp. 247–248), 19th pallava, no. 6 (mark "॥৬॥২১৭৩॥");
"the same raga" (tathā rāga); MS P-R-Sa no. 2281 (it reads "form" (rūpakhāni) for "the jewel of virtues," 12.2). GPT1 —
p. 161, no. 13 ("yathārāga"); GPT2 — sec. 3.2, no. 13 (catalogue: VG-128 = VG-018). On nagari-bhava see the introductory
note to the section.

## 13. Vasu Ghosha — "gṛha-kāja kari tāhe thira nahe mana…" (PK 2175)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman cannot do her housework — her heart is restless: "Come, let us go and see Gora's moonlike
face!" She has bidden farewell to her family and her hopes, given up food and pastimes; without Gora she cannot live. The
same raga.*[^27-35]

**13.1.** I do my housework — but my heart is restless:
come, let us go and see Gora's moonlike face!

**13.2.** To my family I bade farewell for ever, abandoning all hopes,
I gave up all pleasures — food and pastimes.

**13.3.** Day and night my heart finds no rest.
Says Vasu: without Gora I cannot live.

[^27-35]: Signature: "Vasu." PK: vol. 3, PDF p. 259 (printed p. 248), 19th pallava, no. 8 (mark "॥৮॥২১৭৫॥"); "the same raga";
MS P-R-Sa no. 2283. Before it stands PK 2174 by Lochana Dasa ("āra śunecha ālo sai gorā-bhāvera kathā"; chapter 28). GPT1 —
p. 161, no. 14 (raga shri) — with an extra opening couplet: "āhā mari mari sai āhā mari mari, kikṣaṇe dekhilum̐ gorā
pāśarite nāri" ("Ah, I am dying, dying, friend! In what moment did I see Gora — I cannot forget"); GPT2 — sec. 3.2, no. 14.
In the catalogue the pada was listed twice: VG-019 (from GPT) and VG-129 (from PK). On nagari-bhava see the introductory
note to the section.

## 14. Vasu Ghosha — "cala dekhi giyā gorā ati manohare…" (PK 2176, nagari recension)
*Nagari-bhava. The same pada as PK 973 (chapter 9, no. 2), in PK's second recension — in the pallava of the nagaris'
words: "Come, let us go and see Gora!" — Gaura's form in Nadia; the ending differs: "I will go and give my youth for Him."
The same raga.*[^27-36]

**14.1.** Come, let us go and see Gora, beautiful beyond words:
wondrous is Gora's form in the town of Nadia!

**14.2.** His body, tender and radiant, outshines tested gold;
who, seeing the waves of His eyes, can keep his composure?

**14.3.** His arms reach to His knees like golden pillars,
a red cloth is at His waist, broad are His hips.

**14.4.** A garland of malati sways on His neck down to His feet.
Says Vasu: I will go and give my youth for Him.[^27-37]

[^27-36]: Signature: "Vasu." PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 259–260 (printed pp. 248–249), 19th pallava, no. 9 (mark "॥৯॥২১৭৬॥"); "the same
raga"; MS P-R-Sa no. 2284. GPT1 — p. 161, no. 15 (raga shri); GPT2 — sec. 3.2, no. 15 (catalogue: VG-096). Lines 14.1–14.3 are
identical with PK 973 and are translated as in chapter 9 (no. 2, notes 6–8). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to
the section.
[^27-37]: "I will give… my youth" (diva giyā yauvana nichani) — the rite of nichani (note 10): the speaker gives for Him the
dearest thing she has; in the recension of PK 973 — "I will give my life." The signature is put into the mouth of a
townswoman (as in other padas of the section).

## 15. Vasu Ghosha — "niramala gorā tanu kaṣila kāñcana janu…" (PK 28)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman's first love: seeing Gora's body, pure as tested gold, she lost herself; the serpent of His brow
has bitten her heart; the arrows of His reddish eyes have left her without support — she is as if drowning in the
bottomless Ganga; "if you know a spell or a remedy, help me: for Gora's sake my life is leaving me." In PK it is the
gaura-chandrika to Radha's purvaraga, "the words of a nagari." Raga kamoda.*[^27-38]

**15.1.** Gora's pure body is like tested gold;
gazing at it, I lost myself.
The serpent of His brow has bitten my heart —
everything within me trembles.

**15.2.** *(Refrain)* Friend, ever since I saw Gora,
in my distress I cannot tell the directions apart,
my heart is seized by the longing of Madana.[^27-39]

**15.3.** With sidelong glances of His reddening eyes
He rains down flower arrows with delight.
How shall I live on? — I have found no support:
I have drowned in the bottomless Ganga.[^27-40]

**15.4.** If you know a spell or a mighty remedy,
find a means for me.
Says Vasudeva Ghosha: listen, listen, friend —
for Gora's sake my life is leaving me.[^27-41]

[^27-38]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha." PK: vol. 1, PDF p. 34 (printed p. 23), section "atha śrīrādhāyāḥ pūrvarāgaḥ | taducita
śrīgauracandra | nāgarī ukti" (Radha's purvaraga; the gaura-chandrika befitting it — the words of a nagari), no. 1 (mark
"॥১॥২৮॥"); raga kamoda; MS P-R-Sa no. 258. GPT1 — p. 163, no. 20 (raga kamoda); GPT2 — sec. 3.2 (catalogue: VG-023, "no. 27" —
the number is apparently garbled by the OCR). The earliest nagari pada of PK by number: Satishchandra Raya opens the whole
cycle of purvaraga with it. On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section.
[^27-39]: "My heart is seized by the longing of Madana" (madana-lālase mana bhorā) — the original names the attraction openly
(Madana is the god of love); we translate it exactly. This is the language of Radha's purvaraga, to which the pada serves as
a prelude; in Krishna-lila the "Madana" of such padas is Krishna Himself, Madana-mohana, and their love is not worldly. The
tradition does not accept the application of this language to Gaura (introductory note). P-R-Sa: "the intoxication of
Madana" (madanamadārase); the word "friend" is absent; "I found" (pāyalum̐) for "I cannot tell" (pāiye).
[^27-40]: "I have drowned in the bottomless Ganga" — an image of complete loss of self. MS "ka": "purified" (kaṣita) for
"tested" (15.1); "ka"–"cha": "I fell into oblivion" (paṛi gelum̐). P-R-Sa: "with reddish eyes" (aruṇa nayāne); "He has aimed a
cruel arrow" (vaṛai viṣama śara sāndhi) for "rains down flower arrows"; "I will not hold my composure" (dhairaja nā vāndhava)
for "I have found no support"; "into the bottomless Ganga" (gaṅgā agādhi).
[^27-41]: P-R-Sa: "do you" (so tuhum̐ karaha) for "find for me"; "beauty" (sundari) for "friend" (so also MS "kha"); "without
Gora my body perishes" (gorā vinu mora tanu yāya).

## 16. Vasu Ghosha — "niravadhi mora mane gorā-rūpa lāgiyāche…" (PK 777)
*Nagari-bhava. Gora's form does not leave the townswoman's heart: not seeing His face, her breast is breaking; she fears
neither husband nor elders and is ready to part with life for Gora's sake; she has abandoned all joys and her family —
nothing but Gora pleases her. In PK it is the gaura-chandrika to the section "anuraga: love for the form." Raga
suhai.*[^27-42]

**16.1.** Ceaselessly Gora's form stays in my heart —
tell me, friend, what shall I do?
Not seeing Gora's face, my breast is breaking,
my soul longs to leave my body.

**16.2.** Tell me, friend, what am I to do?
My heart does not fear my husband or my elders:
for Gora's sake I will give up my life.[^27-43]

**16.3.** I have abandoned all joys, bidden my family farewell for ever;
nothing but Gora pleases me.
My eyes pour without end — listen, dear friend of my heart —
what can Vasu Ghosha say to this?

[^27-42]: Signature: "Vasu Ghosha." PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 120 (printed p. 107), 10th pallava, section "atha anurāgaḥ… ādau rūpānurāgo
yathā | tatra śrīmahāprabhuḥ" (anuraga; first, love for the form; here — on Mahaprabhu), no. 1 (mark "॥১॥৭৭৭॥"); raga suhai; MSS P-R-Sa
no. 1267 and P-R no. 14/1 (in P-R the raga is tudi). GPT1 — p. 162, no. 17 (raga suhai); GPT2 — sec. 3.2 (catalogue: VG-095). In GPT1 the same pada stands once more — sect. 3.2, no. 84 (pp. 188–189), with the signature "locana dāsa ki valiva tāya" — Lochana's (found in chapter 34; the signature is erroneous).
On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section.
[^27-43]: "My husband and my elders" (gṛhapati gurujana) — the speaker is married; readiness to disregard husband and elders is
the parakiya motif of the padas on the gopis, transferred to the townswomen of Nadia: precisely this transfer the
tradition rejects (introductory note). P-R: "does not hold" (nāhi laye) for "does not fear." MS P-R: "what shall I do, what
will become of me" (16.1); "ka," "kha," "gha," "cha," P-R-Sa: "form" (rūpa) for "face" (mukha, 16.1); P-R-Sa: "pour without
ceasing" (nijhure jhuraye), "of my heart" (marama) for "dear… of my heart" (16.3).

## 17. Vasu Ghosha — "gorā-rūpa lāgila nayane…" (PK 899)
*Nagari-bhava. Gora's form is imprinted on her eyes — night and day, awake and in dreams; wherever she looks she sees Him,
she wants to turn her gaze away and cannot; He is deep in her heart, and her heart cannot be restrained: "Gora is the
enchanter of women." In PK it is the gaura-chandrika to the section "anuraga — another way." Raga shri.*[^27-44]

**17.1.** Gora's form is imprinted on my eyes —
whether by night or by day, on my bed or in dreams.

**17.2.** Wherever I turn my eyes — there I see [Him];
I wish to look away — my eyes will not turn.

**17.3.** In what moment did I see Gora — what has not befallen me!
Ceaselessly Gora's form is deep in my heart.

**17.4.** I want to restrain my heart — it cannot be restrained.
Says Vasu Ghosha: Gora is the enchanter of women.[^27-45]

[^27-44]: Signature: "Vasu Ghosha." PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 171 (printed p. 158), section "atha anurāgaḥ prakārāntaraṃ yathā | tatra
śrīgauracandraḥ" (anuraga — another way; here — on Gaurachandra), no. 101 (mark "॥১০১॥৮৯৯॥"); raga shri; MSS P-R-Sa nos. 1390 and
1398, P-R no. 14/7. The pada stands in PK a second time — PK 916 (vol. 2, PDF p. 178; with a reference there to 899). GPT1 —
p. 162, no. 18 (raga shri); GPT2 — sec. 3.2, no. 18 (catalogue: VG-021). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the
section.
[^27-45]: "The enchanter of women" (ramaṇī-mohana) — in a townswoman's mouth, praise of His beauty; cf. Madana-mohana, "the
enchanter of the god of love." MS P-R: "my gaze falls" (paṛaye diṭhi) for "I turn my eyes" (17.2); P-R-Sa: "the heart wishes"
(kare mana), P-R: "there is a wish" (kare sādha) for "I wish" (17.2); "ka": "in the eyes" (nayane), P-R: "has entered"
(paśila) for "is deep in my heart" (17.3).

## 18. Vasu Ghosha — "gorā-anurāge mora parāṇa kātare…" (PK 747)
*Nagari-bhava. "My soul languishes with love for Gora": her eyes are full of tears, repeating "Gora, Gora" she is as if
ill; she remembers Him ceaselessly, she does not know where to go; love for Gauranga is no easy thing: "the dharma of the
family will not stand." In PK it is the gaura-chandrika to the section "anuraga with reproaches." Raga suhai.*[^27-46]

**18.1.** With love for Gora my soul languishes;
ceaselessly, brimming over, my eyes shed tears.

**18.2.** Repeating "Gora, Gora," what malady has seized me?
Ceaselessly I remember Gora, the treasury of virtues.

**18.3.** What shall I do, where shall I go from this love for Gora?
At every moment love for Gora awakens in my heart.

**18.4.** Love for Gauranga is no easy thing:
says Vasu — the dharma of the family will not stand.[^27-47]

[^27-46]: Signature: "Vasu." PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 107 (printed p. 94), 8th pallava, section "atha ākṣepānurāgaḥ | śrīgauracandraḥ"
(anuraga with reproaches; gaura-chandrika), no. 1 (mark "॥১॥৭৪৭॥"); raga suhai; MS P-R-Sa no. 1236. GPT1 — p. 386, no. 12 (raga
suhai) — in the section "the lament of Shachi and Vishnupriya" after the sannyasa; GPT2 — sec. 5.4, no. 12 (catalogue:
VG-071). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section.
[^27-47]: "The dharma of the family" (kulera dharama) — the duty and honour of the family; words of a townswoman, not of
Vishnupriya, though GPT places the pada among the laments after the sannyasa. GPT1: "my soul is breaking" (parāṇa bidare,
18.1). P-R-Sa: "weep" (jhure) for "shed" (18.1); MS "ka": "every moment" (anukṣaṇa, 18.3).

## 19. Vasu Ghosha — "e hena sundara veśa kene vanāilum̐…" (PK 360)
*Nagari-bhava. A night of vain waiting: "Why did I adorn myself so? Gora's form I never saw"; the night passes in vain, the
Creator has mocked her; whose body will she now anoint with perfumes and sandal, to whom will she offer camphor and betel?
In PK it is the gaura-chandrika to the section on the utkanthita (the heroine pining in expectation). Raga mallar.*[^27-48]

**19.1.** Why did I adorn myself so beautifully?
Gora's peerless form I never saw.

**19.2.** The night passes in vain — what has become of me?
Now I know for certain: the Creator has mocked me.[^27-49]

**19.3.** Perfumes, aguru, sandal —
without Gora, whose body shall I anoint with them?

**19.4.** Camphor, betel, areca — into whose mouth shall I give them?
Says Vasu Ghosha: the night departs in great sorrow.[^27-50]

[^27-48]: Signature: "Vasu Ghosha." PK: vol. 1, PDF p. 243 (printed p. 232), section "athotkaṇṭhitā | tatra śrīgauracandraḥ"
(utkanthita; gaura-chandrika), no. 9 (mark "॥৯॥৩৬০॥"); raga mallar; MS P-R-Sa no. 479. GPT1 — p. 303, no. 11 (raga mallar) — in
section 4.5 (the bhavas of the night); GPT2 — sec. 4.5, no. 11 (catalogue: VG-180; row VG-088 has the same PK number). On
nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section.
[^27-49]: "The Creator has mocked me" (vidhi viṛambila) — has deceived, thwarted my design. The Creator (vidhi) is Brahma, the
arbiter of fate; not the Lord. MS "gha": "did not obtain" (nā pāilum̐), "cha": (nā pālum̐) for "never saw" (19.1); P-R-Sa:
"today" (āji) for "me" (19.2).
[^27-50]: Camphor, betel and areca are the refreshment offered to a dear guest; the waiting and preparations are the image of
the utkanthita from the padas on Radha, transferred to a townswoman. MS "gha": "agaura" for "agora" (aguru, 19.3); "ka"–"ga":
"Gaura" (gaura) for "Gora" (19.3); P-R-Sa: "guvaka" (the same nut, 19.4).

## 20. Vasu Ghosha — "āju rajani hāma kaiche vañcava re…" (PK 365)
*Nagari-bhava. Disappointed waiting: "How shall I pass this night? The king of dancers has turned away from me"; the hope
of new love has not been fulfilled, half a moment drags on like ages; for Gaura's sake she cast aside respect for her
elders — and the Creator has deprived her of this love; the fruit of prema He has scattered over the whole world, and she
is left without hope. In PK it is the gaura-chandrika to the section on the vipralabdha (the heroine disappointed in her
waiting). Raga kedara.*[^27-51]

**20.1.** How shall I pass this night? —
The king of dancers has turned away from me.
In new love my hope has not been fulfilled,
all my efforts have come to nothing.

**20.2.** *(Refrain)* Friend, why did I adorn myself?
Half a moment drags on like ages;
pining [for Him] I have wasted to the ribs.[^27-52]

**20.3.** Respect for my elders I cast far away
for the sake of the rasa of love for Gaura.
The rare love the Creator has denied me —
he has set fire to my fate.[^27-53]

**20.4.** The jewel-fruit of prema He has scattered over the whole world —
and I am left by it without hope;
deceived by new love, I have gone astray:
Vasu Ghosha's hope has not been fulfilled.[^27-54]

[^27-51]: Signature: "Vasu Ghosha." PK: vol. 1, PDF p. 247 (printed p. 236), section "atha vipralabdhā | tatra śrīgauracandraḥ"
(vipralabdha; gaura-chandrika), no. 14 (mark "॥১৪॥৩৬৫॥"); raga kedara; MSS P-R-Sa no. 493 and P-R no. 18/1. GPT1 — p. 303, no. 12
(raga kedara); GPT2 — sec. 4.5, no. 12 (catalogue: VG-181; row VG-089 has the same PK number). On nagari-bhava see the
introductory note to the section.
[^27-52]: The formula of separation — "half a moment is like many yugas": a moment without Him drags on endlessly (not the
reverse). "I have wasted to the ribs" (lit. "my ribs have come to an end") — I have wasted away with longing. MS P-R:
"looking at the road, I have wasted to the ribs" (patha heri pām̐jara śeṣa).
[^27-53]: "Respect for my elders I cast away" — a nagari motif (cf. note 43). The Creator (vidhi) is the arbiter of fate, not the
Lord. MS P-R: "he has put fire into my honeyed mouth" (deola madhu mukhe āgi); "ka"–"ga," "cha," P-R-Sa: "durlabhi," P-R:
"dulaha" (the same "rare").
[^27-54]: "The fruit of prema He has scattered over the whole world" — Gaura gives love of God to all; the townswoman complains
that she, who awaited Him otherwise, received nothing. In her own words — "the king of dancers has turned away from me"
(20.1) — what Vrindavana Dasa says is unwittingly recorded: the Lord did not turn His gaze to women (introductory note). MS
P-R: "over the world" (jagate) for "over the whole world," "fell" (paṛala) for "am left"; P-R-Sa: "by new love"
(anurāge); "ka"–"ga," "cha," P-R: "tulala" — a slip.
## 21. Vasu Ghosha — "ājuka premaka nāhika ora…" (PK 723)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman's dream: "Today's love has no limit — in a dream I lay in Gaura's embrace"; gazing at the Lord's
face she lost herself, tears flowed and washed down the collyrium, her tilaka grew wet, her adornment was effaced. In PK it
is the gaura-chandrika to the section "telling of the meeting — another way." Raga vibhasa.*[^27-55]

**21.1.** Today's love has no limit:
in a dream I lay in Gaura's embrace.[^27-56]

**21.2.** Gazing at the Lord's face, I lost myself;
tears rolled and rolled from my eyes.

**21.3.** On my high breast — collyrium [with tears], the necklace shines bright;
my tilaka is wet, on my cloth is a golden radiance.[^27-57]

**21.4.** The adornment of my body is effaced, little remains.
Says Vasudeva Ghosha: love brims over.[^27-58]

[^27-55]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha." PK: vol. 2, PDF pp. 96–97 (printed pp. 83–84), section "atha rasodgāraḥ prakārāntaraṃ yathā |
śrīmahāprabhuḥ" (rasodgara — telling a friend of the meeting — another way; here — on Mahaprabhu), no. 60 (mark "॥৬০॥৭২৩॥"); raga
vibhasa; MS P-R-Sa no. 1197. GPT1 — p. 296, no. 13 (raga vibhasa); GPT2 — sec. 4.4, no. 13 (catalogue: VG-039; row VG-093 has
the same PK number). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section.
[^27-56]: The pada describes a meeting in a dream (svapanahi) — this is sambhoga-nagari: a townswoman in Gaura's embrace. The
translation adds nothing beyond the original, but does not soften it either. Majumdar holds that padas on sambhoga with
Gaura known only from GPT were ascribed to Vasu later; this pada, however, stands in PK with his signature. The tradition
rejects such a portrayal of Gaura (introductory note). MSS "ka," "kha," "cha," P-R-Sa: "lay" (śutala) — the same.
[^27-57]: The tears have washed the collyrium (kājara) from her eyes down onto her breast. "A golden radiance" (ruci gora) — we
take it as the reflection of the golden Gaura; GPT1: "ruci mora" — "my attire (its lustre)."
[^27-58]: "Brims over" (āgora) — overflowing, measureless. MSS "ka," "kha," "gha," P-R-Sa: "much" (vahu) for "remains" (rahu);
P-R-Sa: "dark" (ghora) for "little" (thora); "in love" (preme).

## 22. Vasu Ghosha — "ki kahava re sakhi rajanika vāta…" (PK 724)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman tells her friend of the night: she was sleeping beside her elders; at midnight, under the full
moon and the gentle Malaya breeze, love for Gaura overwhelmed her, and weeping she cried out: "Gaura, Gaura!"; the elders
woke and heard Gaura's name — then she raised the cry: "Thief, thief!" Raga dhanashi.*[^27-59]

**22.1.** What shall I say, friend, of last night!
I was sleeping beside my elders.

**22.2.** At midnight, when the moon was full,
very gently the breeze from Malaya was blowing.

**22.3.** Love for Gaura filled my body;
my life in distress could find no support.

**22.4.** Weeping "Gaura, Gaura!" I rose —
the elders woke: "Who is it again?"

**22.5.** Gaura's name they all heard with their own ears;
then the elders began to suspect.

**22.6.** I raised the cry: "Thief, thief!" —
says Vasudeva Ghosha: such is the play![^27-60]

[^27-59]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha." PK: vol. 2, PDF p. 97 (printed p. 84), the same section as PK 723, no. 61 (mark
"॥৬১॥৭২৪॥"); raga dhanashi; MS P-R-Sa no. 1198. GPT1 — p. 204, no. 114 (raga dhanashi); GPT2 — sec. 3.2, no. 114. **Catalogue
correction**: row VG-094 counted PK 724 as "Krishna-lila" and excluded it from translation; in fact the pada is about Gaura
(the name "Gaura" in 22.3–22.5) and stands in GPT among the nagari padas. It is not in Majumdar's list (he gives the
neighbouring PK 723). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section.
[^27-60]: A play on words: "gaura" — "caura" ("thief"): to hide whose name she was calling, the townswoman turns "Gaura" into
"thief." In PK this pada is preceded by a pada of Jnanadasa on Radha (PK 722), where Radha likewise covers an involuntary
"Kanu, Kanu" with the word "Bhanu, Bhanu" (the sun): Vasu transfers a motif of Krishna-lila to the nagaris. MS P-R-Sa:
"canda," "manda" (22.2); "ka," "kha," "cha," P-R-Sa: "śunala" (22.5); "kha," "gha": "I rose" (uṭhalum̐), P-R-Sa: "rose"
(uṭhala) for "I raised the cry" (22.6).

## 23. Vasu Ghosha — "ki kahava re sakhi ājuka bhāva…" (PK 249)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman tells her friend: she was alone, adorning herself and dressing her hair before the mirror — and at
that moment Gora, the king of dancers, appeared; her composure and her modesty gave way; at the sight of Him her body
thrilled, and He took her in His embrace. In PK it follows Radhamohana's gaura-chandrika to the section "telling of the
meeting — another way," under the heading "the words of the nagaris of Navadvipa befitting this rasa." Raga
vibhasa.*[^27-61]

**23.1.** What shall I say, friend, of today!
Without any effort a great fortune has come to me.

**23.2.** I was alone, adorning myself;
looking in the mirror, I was dressing my hair.

**23.3.** At that moment Gora, the king of dancers, appeared:
the composure and modesty of a noble wife gave way.

**23.4.** At the sight [of Him] my body thrilled all over —
says Vasudeva Ghosha: He took [me] in His embrace.[^27-62]

[^27-61]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha." PK: vol. 1, PDF pp. 178–179 (printed pp. 167–168), section "atha punaśca
rasodgāraprakārāntaramāha" — after the gaura-chandrika of Radhamohana Dasa (PK 248) — the subsection "tadrasocita-navadvīpa-nāgarīṇāṃ uktiḥ"
(the words of the nagaris of Navadvipa befitting this rasa), no. 2 (mark "॥২॥২৪৯॥"); raga vibhasa; MS P-R no. 1364. GPT1 —
p. 203, no. 111 (raga vibhasa); GPT2 — sec. 3.2, no. 111 (catalogue: VG-026). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the
section.
[^27-62]: The last line describes an embrace — sambhoga-nagari (cf. note 56); we translate it exactly. An important variant: in
MS P-R the couplet is different — "At the sight my body was filled with thrills; says Vasudeva: Gora is young and fresh"
(daraśe pūrala tanu pulakita mora, vāsudeva kahe gorā naola kiśora), without the embrace. MS P-R: "today with effort He gave
me fortune" (23.1), "I" (āmi), "there I dressed" (tahi vāndhala, 23.2), "fled" (bhāgala, 23.3); "ka," "kha": "dressed"
(vāndhala).

## 24. Vasu Ghosha — "hari hari gorā kothā gela…" (PK 1636)
*Nagari-bhava. A townswoman's lament after Gaura has gone: where has Gora gone? what cruel Creator sent this grief? Her heart
is wounded; she cannot weep aloud, like a thief's wife; she is a daughter of a noble family and does not leave the house, and
even in dreams she cannot see Him; to whom can she tell of His beauty and His pastimes? "Why does not a thunderbolt fall on
my head?" In PK it stands in the section "the lament of the devotees, and also of the nagaris of Navadvipa, in separation
from Gaurachandra." Raga suhai.*[^27-63]

**24.1.** *(Refrain)* Hari, Hari! Where has Gora gone?
What pitiless Creator has sent such grief?

**24.2.** My heart is wounded, my ribs are crumbling;
since life is leaving — what then is left of love?

**24.3.** I cannot weep aloud — I am like a thief's wife;
every moment I remember Gora's face.[^27-64]

**24.4.** I am a daughter of a noble family, I do not leave the house;
even in dreams I cannot see Him — what shall I do?

**24.5.** To whom shall I tell of that sweet beauty and those pastimes?
Without Gora, my Lord, I will enter the fire.[^27-65]

**24.6.** That life holds on without Gora — this is a great shame.
Says Vasu: why does not a thunderbolt fall on my head?

[^27-63]: Signature: "Vasu." PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 37–38 (printed pp. 26–27), 4th shakha, section "atha śrīgauracandra-viraheṇa
bhaktagaṇasya tathā navadvīpa-nāgarīṇāṃ vilāpo yathā" (the lament of the devotees, and also of the nagaris of Navadvipa, in separation from
Gaurachandra), no. 3 (mark "॥৩॥১৬৩৬॥"); raga suhai (P-R: sindhura); MSS P-R-Sa no. 859 and P-R no. 40/111. GPT1 — p. 388,
no. 19 (raga suhai) — in the section "the lament of Shachi and Vishnupriya"; GPT2 — sec. 5.4, no. 19 (catalogue: VG-076, where
this pada is separated from "gela gaura nā gela valiyā," GPT 5.4 no. 18 — GPT only). Separation after the sannyasa. On
nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section.
[^27-64]: A proverb: a thief's wife dare not mourn her husband aloud — her grief is secret. So the townswoman cannot weep openly
for Gaura. MSS "ka," "kha," P-R: "she cannot" (nāre) for "I cannot"; P-R: "form" (gorā-varaṇa) for "face" (24.3); for
"crumbling" P-R has khase ("falling away").
[^27-65]: "I will enter the fire" — a formula of despair in separation, as in the padas on Radha. MS P-R lacks couplets
24.4–24.5; "kha": "vine" (24.6); "ka": "ei," "kha," "gha," P-R-Sa, P-R: "iha" for "eha" (24.6); P-R: "fell" (paṛila, 24.6).

## 25. Vasu Ghosha — "kaha sakhi jivana-upāya…" (PK 1669)
*Nagari-bhava. A lament after Gaura has gone: "Tell me, friend, how shall I live? Gora, the king of dancers, has left [me]";
her body has wasted away, how many days can she live in separation? where can she go to see His face? what has the Creator
written on her forehead? to whom can she tell this grief? In PK it is the gaura-chandrika to the section on Radha's lament
in external consciousness; in GPT it stands among the laments of Shachi and Vishnupriya. Raga suhai.*[^27-66]

**25.1.** Tell me, friend, how shall I live?
Gora, the king of dancers, has left [me].

**25.2.** Pining [for Him], my body has wasted away;
how many days shall I live in separation?

**25.3.** Gauranga's pure face —
where shall I go to see it?

**25.4.** What has the Creator written on my forehead?
I will cut it open and see what is there on my brow![^27-67]

**25.5.** My heart is wounded with love —
to whom shall I tell this grief?

**25.6.** Says Vasu Ghosha at the last:
without Gora life cannot be kept.[^27-68]

[^27-66]: Signature: "Vasu Ghosha." PK: vol. 3, PDF pp. 54–55 (printed pp. 43–44), section "atha kevalaṃ vāhya-daśāyāṃ vilāpo yathā |
tatra śrīgauracandraḥ" (lament in external consciousness; gaura-chandrika), no. 8 (mark "॥৮॥১৬৬৯॥"); raga suhai (P-R: pahida and
gandhara — the pada stands in it twice); MSS P-R-Sa no. 892 and P-R nos. 40/15, 43/12. GPT1 — p. 388, no. 20; GPT2 — sec. 5.4,
no. 20 (catalogue: VG-117). The pada does not name the speaker; GPT assigns it to Vishnupriya's lament, PK to the words of the
townswomen (according to Majumdar, nagari-bhava). Separation after the sannyasa. On nagari-bhava see the introductory note
to the section.
[^27-67]: According to popular belief, the Creator (vidhi) writes a person's fate on his forehead. The Creator is Brahma, not
the Lord.
[^27-68]: Lit. "says Vasu Ghosha the end (nidāna)": the last word, the verdict. GPT1: "kahe vāsu ghoṣa nidāna." MS P-R: "said
Vasu Ghosha" (vāsu ghoṣe kahila), "I will give up [life]" (tejiba) for "cannot be kept" (25.6); "ka," "cha," P-R-Sa:
"jīvana" (25.1); P-R: "goes" (yāya, 25.1), "shedding tears" (jhuri jhuri) for "pining," "became" (haila, 25.2), "in this grief I
will pass" (e duḥkhe vañciva, 25.2), and instead of 25.3: "Shall I see again that pure moonlike face?" (puna ki pāiva
daraśana, niramala o cām̐nda-badana).

## Note to Chapter 27

*Vasu Ghosha in PK — 25 nagari padas (including PK 724, which the catalogue mistakenly regarded as Krishna-lila, and PK 2176 —
the nagari recension of PK 973). Of Majumdar's list, PK 2219 (a pada of Lochana Dasa signed "e dāsa locana gāya") and PK 2228
(already translated, chapter 4, no. 16) are not included. Vasu's nagari padas known only from GPT (VG-020, 022, 024, 025,
027–030, 032, 040, 168, 169, 182 and others), as well as the nagari padas of other poets in the same pallavas of PK
(Nayanananda — PK 2170, 2177; Lochana Dasa — PK 2174; Govinda Dasa — PK 2168 and others), are in chapter 28.*

---

# Chapter 28. Nagari Padas — II: Vasu Ghosha (padas from GPT), Nayanananda, Yadu, Murari, Balarama Dasa, Chandrashekhara, Lochana Dasa

*On what nagari-bhava is, the position of the tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati) and the rules of translation, see the introductory note to the section of nagari padas in chapter 27.*

## 1. Vasu Ghosha — "ki herinu ogo sai vidagadha-rāja…" (KGC 5.1; GPT1 p. 162, no. 16)
*Nagari-bhava (only in the address to a friend). "What have I seen, friend — the king of those versed in rasa!" Gaura is the
wish-fulfilling tree of the devotees in the midst of Navadvipa: its branches are love, its leaves anuraga, its flowers longing,
its fruit pure prema, from which rasa flows without end; the devotees, like birds and bees, taste it, the tree's shade nourishes
all — only the poet is deprived through his own fault. In KGC it is the gaura-chandrika to the 5th kshanada. Raga suhai-deshag.*[^28-1]

**1.1.** What have I seen, friend! — the king of those versed in rasa,
the wish-fulfilling tree of the devotees in the midst of Navadvipa.[^28-2]

**1.2.** Its branches are love, its leaves are anuraga,
its flowers are longing, to enchant the world.

**1.3.** At all times the pure fruit of prema ripens on it;
from a single fruit ever-fresh rasa flows without end.[^28-3]

**1.4.** The devotees — chatakas, cuckoos, parrots, bees, swans —
ceaselessly delight in it, praising its rasa.

**1.5.** The unmoving and the moving, gods and men, are nourished by its shade —
only Vasudeva is deprived through the fault of his own deeds.[^28-4]

[^28-1]: Signature: "Vasudeva." KGC (Vishvanatha Chakravarti, late 17th c.; ed. 1925) — 5th kshanada ("krishna-panchami"), no. 1,
"śrīgauracandrasya" (gaura-chandrika), raga suhai-deshag, p. 34 (scan PDF p. 66). GPT1 — p. 162, no. 16 (raga suhai or desharaga;
scan PDF p. 421); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 16 (catalogue: VG-020). The pada is not in PK. The catalogue listed it as "GPT only";
the KGC witness was found in preparing this chapter (attribution to Vasu by KGC and GPT, A). In GPT the pada stands in the section
of nagari padas (3.2), but the nagari motif in it is only the address "friend": in substance it praises Gaura in the image of the
wish-fulfilling tree. On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^28-2]: "The king of those versed in rasa" (vidagadha-rāja): a vidagdha is a connoisseur, finely sensitive to rasa; so Krishna is
called. "Wish-fulfilling tree" (kalpataru) — an image known from CC (Adi 9: the Lord is both the gardener and the tree of prema itself,
giving its fruits to all). GPT1 notes a variant of the first line: "What shall I say, friend, of a wondrous thing!"
[^28-3]: "Ever-fresh rasa" (nava rasa) can also be understood as "ninefold rasa" (all rasas in one fruit). "Longing" (ārati) is eager
yearning, not the arati rite.
[^28-4]: Self-abasement in the signature is a usual device of Vaishnava poets (cf. "Vasudeva is deprived" in Vasu's padas — chapter 27).
Instead of this couplet GPT1 gives a variant: "the bee-devotees seek the wish-fulfilling tree [of His feet]; says Vasu: wondrous is
this on earth"; instead of 1.4b — "many bhavas arose, but the hope was not fulfilled." KGC: "its shade nourishes" (poṣe), GPT:
"enter its shade" (paise).

## 2. Vasu Ghosha — "āju mui ki dekhilum̐ gorā naṭarāya…" (GPT1 p. 164, no. 23; GCd, no. 12)
*Nagari-bhava. "What have I seen today — Gora, the king of dancers!" The Creator made Him, putting in so much rasa; His body
surpasses gold, His face a hundred moons, His eyes steal the hearts of women; on the bank of the Suradhuni Gorachand shines.
Raga dhanashi.*[^28-5]

**2.1.** What have I seen today — Gora, the king of dancers!
Gora's boundless glory cannot be told.

**2.2.** How did the Creator fashion Him, putting in so much rasa!
Gora's body ripples with radiance, surpassing gold.

**2.3.** His lotus face is lovelier than hundreds of moons;
the pair of His eyes steals the hearts of women.[^28-6]

**2.4.** Says Vasudeva Ghosha, lost in rapture:
on the bank of the Suradhuni Gorachand shines.

[^28-5]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha." GPT1 — p. 164, no. 23 (raga dhanashi; scan PDF p. 423); GPT2 — sect. 3.2 (in the same series,
after VG-025). The catalogue had no row for it (**new row**: VG-184). Witness: the *Gita-chandrodaya* of Narahari Chakravarti (GCd;
ed. 1948, p. 72, gaura-chandrikas to Radha's purvaraga, no. 12, raga suhai) — with the same signature; there it stands among
Vasu's nagari padas known from PK (PK 2169, 28, 2172, 899, 777 — chapter 27, nos. 9, 15, 11, 17, 16). The pada is not in PK or KGC; attribution to
Vasu by GPT and GCd (B). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^28-6]: "Steal the hearts of women" is a formula of the poetics of beauty, as in the padas on Krishna (cf. chapter 27, note 6). GCd:
"how many moons," "ripples" (ḍharaḍhara), in 2.4 — "Gora has lit up the bank of the Suradhuni."

## 3. Vasu Ghosha — "āju mui ki pekhalum̐ gaurāṅga sundara…" (GPT1 p. 164, no. 24)
*Nagari-bhava. "What have I seen today — the beautiful Gauranga: in the three worlds there is no such nagara!" Noble wives are
enchanted by His form, trees thrill hearing of His virtues, stones melt, beasts and birds weep, the townswomen cannot hold their
hearts steady, gods, siddhas and sages are in turmoil: Gora is Madana-mohana. Raga dhanashi.*[^28-7]

**3.1.** What have I seen today — the beautiful Gauranga!
In these three worlds there is no such nagara.[^28-8]

**3.2.** All the noble wives are enchanted, seeing His form;
trees and creepers thrill, hearing of His virtues.

**3.3.** Stones melt and flow, beasts and birds weep;
all the women of the town cannot hold their hearts steady.

**3.4.** The gods, siddhas and sages are in turmoil of heart.
Says Vasudeva: Gora is Madana-mohana.[^28-9]

[^28-7]: Signature: "Vasudeva." GPT1 — p. 164, no. 24 (raga dhanashi; scan PDF p. 423); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 24 (catalogue: VG-182).
The pada is not in PK, KGC or GCd; attribution to Vasu by GPT only (C). It is close to Vasu's PK 2151 (chapter 27, no. 1: "birds,
beasts and trees weep hearing of His virtues; noble wives cannot hold their hearts steady"), but it is a different text. On
nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^28-8]: "Nagara" (nāgara) — townsman, gallant, in poetry the beloved (introductory note); so a townswoman speaks of the young Gaura.
[^28-9]: Madana-mohana — "the enchanter of the god of love himself," a name of Krishna: the Lord's beauty conquers even Kamadeva.
"Cannot hold their hearts steady" (lit. "bind the breast") is a general formula of beauty (chapter 27, note 2). GPT1: "nagarī" — a
misprint for "nāgarī" (GPT2).

## 4. Vasu Ghosha — "sajani lo gorārūpa janu kām̐cā sonā…" (GPT1 pp. 162–163, no. 19)
*Nagari-bhava. "Friend, Gora's form is like pure gold: seeing it, a woman cannot stay at home." His form has fixed itself in
her eyes, wherever she looks there is Gora; He seems familiar, yet she cannot make out who He is. The poet answers: "Townswoman,
that is the stealer of the gopis' hearts!" Raga suhai.*[^28-10]

**4.1.** Friend, Gora's form is like pure gold:
seeing it, a woman cannot stay at home.

**4.2.** Curved brows, slanting eyes — by His glance you know Him;
give your heart to that form, friend, and no family honour remains.[^28-11]

**4.3.** The form has fixed itself in my eyes — I cannot forget it:
wherever I look, I see only that Gora.

**4.4.** He seems familiar, so familiar, yet I cannot make out who He is.
Says Vasu: townswoman, that is the stealer of the gopis' hearts![^28-12]

[^28-10]: Signature: "Vasu." GPT1 — pp. 162–163, no. 19 (raga suhai; scan PDF pp. 421–422); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 19 (catalogue:
VG-022). The pada is not in PK, KGC, PS or GCd; attribution to Vasu by GPT only (C). The language is late and colloquial
("legeche," "cinate," "śudhui"), which, like the absence of early witnesses, tells against Vasu's authorship (cf. Majumdar's argument
on the unreliability of GPT — introductory note to the section). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^28-11]: "No family honour remains" is a nagari motif (a woman ready to disregard her family's honour for Gaura), transferred from the
padas on Radha and Krishna; translated as in the original (introductory note, rule 2).
[^28-12]: The poet's answer reveals what the townswoman cannot grasp: Gora is Krishna Himself, "the stealer of the gopis' hearts," and
that is why He seems familiar to her. This is a tenet of gaura-tattva (Gaura is Krishna who has taken Radha's bhava and luster;
CC Adi 1.5); it does not make Gaura the hero of a love play in Navadvipa (introductory note). GPT2: "e" ("this") instead of "ai".

## 5. Vasu Ghosha — "niravadhi gorārūpa dekhi…" (GPT1 p. 164, no. 25)
*Nagari-bhava. "Ceaselessly I see Gora's form — streams flow from my eyes": night and day the townswoman knows nothing, the jewel
of brahmanas has entered her inmost heart; not seeing Gorachand's face, she cannot hold on to life. Raga dhanashi.*[^28-13]

**5.1.** Ceaselessly I see Gora's form —
from both my eyes it streams like a waterfall.

**5.2.** What shall I say? Where is my remedy?
My life will not stay in me.

**5.3.** Night and day I know nothing:
the jewel of brahmanas has entered my inmost heart.[^28-14]

**5.4.** Not seeing Gorachand's face —
says Vasu — the breast breaks.

Vasu by GPT only (C). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^28-14]: "The jewel of brahmanas" (dvijamaṇi) — the young Gaura, best of brahmanas (cf. chapter 27, note 8).

## 6. Vasu Ghosha — "dekhiyā āyalum̐ gorācām̐de…" (GPT1 p. 164, no. 26)
*Nagari-bhava. "I have seen Gorachand — and since then my soul weeps": not seeing His moon-face, the townswoman finds no rest,
household work falls from her hands; Gauranga's glory has no limit. Raga dhanashi.*[^28-15]

and since then my soul weeps.

**6.2.** My heart is restless, finds no peace,
when I do not see that moon-face.

**6.3.** My mind will not stay on household work
when I do not see Gaura's deeds.

**6.4.** Matchless is Gauranga's glory:
Vasudeva finds no limit to it.[^28-16]

nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^28-16]: The last couplet passes from the townswoman's words to the poet's praise: Gaura's glory has no limit (cf. chapter 27, no. 1:
"in the three worlds there is none who could set a limit to His beauty").

## 7. Vasu Ghosha — "so vahuvallabha gorā jagatera manacorā…" (GPT1 pp. 163–164, no. 22)
*Nagari-bhava. "Gora is beloved of many, He steals the hearts of all the world — why then should I want Him to be mine alone?
Yet whose heart can bear the sharing!" The townswoman gives family, honour, life and youth for the treasure that is Gora; without
Him she will enter the waters of the Suradhuni. Raga vibhasa.*[^28-17]

**7.1.** He is Gora, beloved of many, the stealer of all the world's hearts —
why then do I want Him to be mine alone?
But say, whose heart could give such a treasure to another?
The sharing is unbearable to see.[^28-18]

**7.2.** *(Refrain)* Friend, I will tell you my heart's secret:
not seeing Gauranga's face, I feel my breast breaking —
who has stolen the stealer of hearts?

**7.3.** Take my family, take my honour, take my virtue, take my life,
take my life and my youth —
give me the treasure, Gora, for whom I ceaselessly long:
He is my whole wealth.

**7.4.** Or else I will enter the waters of the Suradhuni and give up my life:
Gora is the life of my life.
Says Vasudeva Ghosha: that treasure is not given away —
every moment, every instant I am bereft of it.[^28-19]

[^28-17]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha." GPT1 — pp. 163–164, no. 22 (raga vibhasa; scan PDF pp. 422–423); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 22
(catalogue: VG-025). The pada is not in PK, KGC or GCd; attribution to Vasu by GPT only (C). On nagari-bhava see the introductory
note to the section (chapter 27).
[^28-18]: "Beloved of many" (vahuvallabha) is an epithet of Krishna, the beloved of all the gopis; the jealousy of a heroine who will not
share her beloved is a motif of the padas on Radha, transferred to a townswoman of Nadia. That Gaura belongs to all (He gave prema to
the whole world) is true; but Gaura's love for the world is mercy, not the love play of a nagara (introductory note). GPT2: "You,
beloved of many, Gora" (to).
[^28-19]: The signature line is ambiguous: "that treasure is not given away" — the poet confirms that Gora cannot be yielded; "every
moment I am bereft" (hai hārā) we take as unceasing separation (cf. chapter 27, note 52); it can also be read "I lose myself."
"I will enter the waters of the Suradhuni," "take my family, honour…" are nagari formulas, translated as in the original.

## 8. Vasu Ghosha — "daṇḍe daṇḍe tile tile gorācām̐da nā dekhile…" (GPT1 p. 296, no. 14)
*Nagari-bhava. "If I do not see Gorachand every moment, I live as one dead": the townswoman wants to keep His golden form always in
her heart; not seeing Him for an instant, she loses her composure; she will set her family's honour adrift on the Suradhuni, burn
her shame and gaze her fill at Gauranga. Raga suhai.*[^28-20]

**8.1.** If every moment, every instant I do not see Gorachand,
I live as though dead at heart.
Ceaselessly I long to keep
His golden-lustred form within my heart.

**8.2.** I do not see Him for a moment — my ribs give way,
I cannot keep my composure.
With the brush of anuraga my heart is painted within and without —
I do not know how much I owe Him.[^28-21]

**8.3.** I will go to the waters of the Suradhuni and set my family adrift,
I will set fire to my shame;
I will place Gauranga before me and gaze my fill —
Vasu wants no other work.[^28-22]

anuraga (4.4); GPT2 — sect. 4.4, no. 14 (catalogue: VG-040). Not in PK, KGC or GCd. According to the catalogue, in the late
collection *Padamrita-madhuri* (vol. 1, pp. 469–470; an edition under copyright, its text is not used) the same pada bears the
signature of Murari Gupta and has an extra couplet: the attribution is disputed (C). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to
the section (chapter 27).
[^28-21]: The line is obscure: "anurāgera tuli diye antara vāhira hiye, nā jāni tāra kata dhāra dhāri" — lit. "with the brush of anuraga —
the inside and outside of the heart; I do not know how much debt I hold to Him." We understand: love has coloured the whole heart,
and the townswoman does not know how to repay this gift. The translation is conjectural.
[^28-22]: "Set my family adrift," "set fire to my shame" are formulas of renouncing family honour for love (from the padas on Radha);
translated as in the original (introductory note, rule 2).

## 9. Vasu Ghosha — "āpana jāni vanāyalum̐ veśa…" (GPT1 p. 305, no. 18)
*Nagari-bhava (vasaka-sajja — "she who has prepared for the meeting"). The townswoman, regarding Gaura as her own, adorns herself
for His coming: she binds her hair, puts on a sandal tilaka, a pearl necklace, draws designs in musk on her breast; love for Gaura
cannot be told. Raga dhanashi.*[^28-23]

**9.1.** Regarding Him as my own, I dressed myself:
carefully I bound my hair in a loose knot.

**9.2.** I put a sandal tilaka on my forehead,
I put a pearl necklace round my neck.

**9.3.** I drew designs in musk on my breast,
I adorned myself all over, limb by limb.[^28-24]

**9.4.** Love for Gaura cannot be told:
Vasudeva Ghosha finds no end to this rasa.[^28-25]

[^28-23]: Signature: "Vasudeva Ghosha." GPT1 — p. 305, no. 18 (raga dhanashi; scan PDF p. 564), in the section of gaura-chandrikas to
abhisara, rasodgara and utkanthita (4.5), next to a pada on vasaka-sajja (no. 19); GPT2 — sect. 4.5, no. 18 (catalogue: VG-168). Not in PK, KGC or GCd; attribution to Vasu by GPT only (C). On
nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^28-24]: The adornment of the vasaka-sajja (the heroine who adorns herself for her beloved's coming) is a canon of the padas on
Radha; designs in musk on the breast (kuca) are part of that canon. Translated exactly, with nothing added. The Vrajabuli forms
"deyala," "caṛhāyala," "kayala" can also be 3rd person ("He put…"); but the pada is framed by "I dressed myself… I adorned myself"
(vanāyalum̐), and it speaks of the heroine's own adornment.
[^28-25]: Lit. "Gaura's love (leha) cannot be told"; we understand it as the townswoman's love for Gaura. Gaura Himself, according to CC,
is in the bhava of Radha, tasting Her love; the tradition does not accept depicting Him as the beloved of the townswomen
(introductory note).

## 10. Vasu Ghosha — "niśi-parabhāte vasi āṅgināte…" (GPT1 p. 163, no. 21)
*Nagari-bhava (khandita — "the deceived"). At daybreak the townswoman sits in the courtyard with a cheerless face: "Friend, who has
done this? Gora, the Creator's finest work — another has got Him!" She had prepared the bed, did not sleep all night, went out of
the door a hundred times; when Gauranga comes she will ask: in whose house did He spend the night? Raga vibhasa-dashakushi.*[^28-26]

**10.1.** At daybreak I sit in the courtyard with a cheerless face:
such conduct from Gaurangachand I never knew.

**10.2.** *(Refrain)* Friend, who has done this?
Gora, the treasury of virtues, the utmost of the Creator's work — she has got Him.[^28-27]

**10.3.** Sprinkling musk and sandal, stringing flower garlands,
I spread the bed on a splendid couch: here Shachi's boy will lie.

**10.4.** Ah, friend, the whole night I sat awake till dawn;
three times an instant, a hundred times a danda I went out of the house.

**10.5.** Says Vasu Ghosha: when Gauranga comes I will ask Him at once:
"You did not come here — where did You spend the night, in whose house were You?"[^28-28]

[^28-26]: Signature: "Vasu Ghosha." GPT1 — p. 163, no. 21 (raga vibhasa-dashakushi; scan PDF p. 422); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 21
(catalogue: VG-024). The pada is not in PK, KGC or GCd; attribution to Vasu by GPT only (C). On nagari-bhava see the introductory
note to the section (chapter 27).
[^28-27]: "The utmost of the Creator's work" (vidhira avadhi) — the most perfect thing the Creator could make (a poetic formula; Gaura is not
created — He is the Lord Himself). "She has got Him" — another woman: the khandita heroine suspects a rival.
[^28-28]: The pada is wholly transferred from the canon of padas on Radha as khandita: Krishna has spent the night with another gopi and
comes at dawn bearing the marks of the meeting. Such a plot is inapplicable to Gaura: Vrindavana Dasa says plainly that in Navadvipa
the Lord did not look at women (CB, Adi-khanda; introductory note) — which is why the townswoman waits for Him all night in vain.
Translated faithfully to the author, but this is a poetic fiction of the late layer of GPT, not a lila; the tradition does not accept
such a depiction of Gaura (introductory note). Cf. the night of vain waiting in Vasu's padas from PK (chapter 27, nos. 19, 20).

## 11. Vasu Ghosha — "kena māna karinu lo sai…" (GPT1 p. 313, no. 20)
*Nagari-bhava (mana — offended pride and repentance). "Why did I take offence, friend? Where has Gora gone?" The townswoman herself
pushed Gaurahari away, and now reproaches her friends for not holding Him back: home and body are empty, Gaura has turned away. The
poet consoles her: the hope will be fulfilled. Raga suhai.*[^28-29]

**11.1.** Why did I take offence, friend?
Where has Gora, the treasury of virtues, gone?

**11.2.** If I have abandoned my beloved,
why then does my life not leave me?

**11.3.** I did abandon Gaurahari —
but why did you not hold Him back?

**11.4.** Now home and body are both empty:
Gaura has turned away.

**11.5.** Why now these vain sighs?
Says Vasu: the hope will be fulfilled.[^28-30]

mana (4.6); GPT2 — sect. 4.6, no. 20 (catalogue: VG-169; the first line according to the scan is "kena māna karinu," not "karisa").
Not in PK, KGC or GCd; attribution to Vasu by GPT only (C). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^28-30]: The motif of the kalahantarita — the heroine who in offended pride (mana) has pushed her beloved away and at once repents — is
taken from the padas on Radha and Krishna. "Beloved" (vam̐dhuyā) is a word of the same padas. "Gaura has turned away" (vaimukha) — as in
Vasu's padas from PK (chapter 27, no. 20: "the king of dancers has turned away from me"), here what is unwittingly reflected is that
the Lord did not respond to such feelings (introductory note).

## 13. Vasu Ghosha (according to Majumdar, not Vasu) — "niśi śeṣe chinu ghumera ghore…" (GPT1 p. 203, no. 112)
*Nagari-bhava (a dream; sambhoga). The townswoman relates: at the end of the night, deep in sleep, "Gaura the nagara" embraced and
kissed her; sleep broke, the nagara went away, and coming to her senses she left the bedchamber in shame. According to Majumdar, a
reworking of a well-known pada on Krishna, ascribed to Vasu. Raga vibhasa.*[^28-33]

**13.1.** At the end of the night I was deep in sleep —
Gaura the nagara embraced me.

**13.2.** He kissed me on the cheek,
with His lips He drank the nectar of my lips.[^28-34]

**13.3.** Sleep broke, the nagara went away;
I had been senseless — and I came to my senses.

**13.4.** Out of shame I left the bedchamber.
Says Vasu: your love is a deceit.[^28-35]

[^28-33]: Signature: "Vasu." GPT1 — p. 203, no. 112 (raga vibhasa; scan PDF p. 462); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 112 (p. 131; catalogue:
VG-027). Not in PK, KGC or GCd. **Majumdar** explicitly names this pada (from GPT2, p. 131) as a reworking of a well-known pada of
Krishna-lila, ascribed to Vasu to lend "antiquity" to sambhoga-nagari-bhava; because of such padas he considers GPT unreliable for
Vasu Ghosha and Narahari Sarakara. Hence the authority is **D** (a forgery according to Majumdar). On nagari-bhava see the
introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^28-34]: Sambhoga (a love meeting) with Gaura, and in such words, is what even Majumdar considers incompatible with the genuine padas
of the contemporaries (in Narahari Sarakara, by his criteria, "there is no sambhoga"), and the tradition rejects it as a distortion
(Vrindavana Dasa: in Navadvipa the Lord did not look at women; Bhaktisiddhanta: "gaura-nagari" is an apasampradaya; introductory
note). Translated exactly, with nothing added, for the completeness of the corpus; this is not a lila of the Lord but a late reworking
of a pada on Krishna.
[^28-35]: "Your love is a deceit" (tuyā kapaṭa leha): a reproach, apparently, to the "nagara" who left at dawn (in the original pada — to
Krishna); it can also be taken as the poet's words to the heroine.

## 14. Vasu Ghosha — "ājuka prema kahane nāhi yāya…" (GPT1 p. 204, no. 115)
*Nagari-bhava (telling of a meeting). "Today's love cannot be told": the townswoman lay on the bed she had spread — and heard the
jingling of anklets: Gauranga, the king of dancers, had come; she hid under her veil, and the skilful nagara searched for her with
His eyes; Gora found great joy. Raga dhanashi.*[^28-36]

**14.1.** Today's love cannot be told:
I lay down, having spread the bed.

**14.2.** Runu-jhunu, runu-jhunu — the anklets jingle on His feet:
I saw Gauranga, the finest king of dancers.

**14.3.** I hid under the end of my sari, covering myself with the veil;
the skilful nagara looks about on all sides.

**14.4.** Great joy did Gora, the king of dancers, find.
Says Vasudeva: the rasa cannot be told.[^28-37]

[^28-36]: Signature: "Vasudeva." GPT1 — p. 204, no. 115 (raga dhanashi; scan PDF p. 463), among the padas on the townswomen's dreams
and meetings (nos. 111–115); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 115 (catalogue: VG-029). Not in PK, KGC or GCd; attribution to Vasu by GPT only (C).
On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).

padas on Radha and Krishna. Majumdar considers the padas of sambhoga with Gaura known only from GPT to be later ascriptions; the
tradition rejects such a depiction of Gaura (introductory note; cf. note 34). Translated exactly, with nothing added. The Lord's
"joy" (sukha) is in truth the joy of prema and kirtana, not worldly love.

## 15. Vasu Ghosha — "gela gaura nā gela valiyā…" (GPT1 p. 388, no. 18)
