## 12. Narahari — "sakhīra samāje rahiyā vāreka…" (GPT1 pp. 226–227, no. 157; GCC 9.16)
*Nagari-bhava; a daydream (reproach). A townswoman dreams: standing among her friends, with a sorrowful face she will say to the nagara with the
corner of her eye: "You do not know the heart of love: You roam every street, I alone am left out; because of You the elders who loved me more than
life regard me as poison, and those I laughed at laugh at me; if You were gracious to me I would count this disgrace as nothing; but You are pitiless
— why this anger?" And He, joining His palms, will answer with a glance: "Perish My nature, I am full of faults — but I know one thing: you are dearer
to Me than life." Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 9, pada 16.*[^32-22]

**12.1.** "Staying among my friends, glancing once at that face, with a sorrowful face I shall say to the nagara with the corner of my eye:

**12.2.** 'Well, well, You: the heart of love You have never known! This quarter and that You can wander — only I am left out.

**12.3.** You, the Crown of connoisseurs of rasa, always stay lost in joy — while to me, unfortunate, what has not befallen me on Your account!

**12.4.** The elders who loved me more than life regard me as poison; those I used to laugh at now laugh when they see me.

**12.5.** If even so You knew me as Your own and were gracious to me, I would count all this disgrace as no more than a straw.

**12.6.** As it is, day and night there is a cruel burning — the body cannot bear it; and on top of that You are pitiless — how can life remain?

**12.7.** So dispel the doubt in my heart: why this anger? Is this Your nature — or have You found some fault in me?'

**12.8.** Understanding this, He, rapt in rasa, looking at me, will unnoticed join His palms and say with the corner of His eye:

**12.9.** 'Perish My nature, I am stained with every fault; but ever in My heart I know one thing: you are dearer to Me than life.'

**12.10.** Understanding this, I shall smile faintly and signal to my friend" — and the heart of Narahari's Beloved will be calmed, seeing [her] great joy.[^32-23]

continues with padas that are not in GPT (9.17–9.23): the townswomen come to Shachi's house and bow to her (9.18 — a Vrajabuli pada signed "Ghanashyama", another name

and all your family live long" (9.21); the kirana ends with the poet's prayer for devotion to the feet of the nagaris of Nadia (9.23). B. Nagari-bhava — see the
introductory note to the section (chapter 27).

and Madhya). 12.5: "as no more than a straw" — by sense (lit. "would count more than a blade of grass"; the grass-blade is the usual image of the worthless).

## 13. Narahari — "śuna śuna ogo prāṇasama tumi…" (GPT1 p. 227, no. 158; GCC 10.10)
*Nagari-bhava (the heavenly women's talk). One says to her friend in her ear: "You judged rightly — the same came to my mind: today something is
strange with Him, I have never seen Him so overcome in the rapture of rasa; who has stolen Gaurangachand's heart? He is indeed a nagara — one can tell
by His doings, but I am ashamed to say it outright." Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 10, pada 10.*[^32-24]

**13.1.** "Listen, listen, you who are dear to me as life — I tell you in your ear: what you have judged has come to my mind too.

**13.2.** Today something is strange — you see it yourself, shrewd one: I have never seen Him so overcome in the rapture of rasa.

**13.3.** And even if I saw it some day, still I could make nothing out. Tell me now: who has stolen Gaurangachand's heart?

**13.4.** Narahari's moon is indeed a nagara — I can tell by His doings; and yet for shame I cannot say it outright to anyone."[^32-25]

## 14. Narahari — "ki valiva ogo anubhavi bhāla…" (GPT1 pp. 227–228, no. 159; GCC 10.12)
*Nagari-bhava (the heavenly women's talk). Another answers: "You judged rightly: I know all His play as a nagara, only I am shy to tell it — it is
laughable to watch how He behaves: He thinks Himself the king of the clever, imagines that everything of His is secret — His descent, His gait, His
dance, His love with the nagaris of Nadia — and covers the sun's rays with His hand. Before one who is cleverer than the clever no cleverness holds —
whom then does He fear?" Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 10, pada 12.*[^32-26]

**14.1.** "What shall I say? You judged rightly: all Gaurangachand's ways as a nagara I know.

**14.2.** Before you all I am shy to tell those tales — and yet, watching Gauranga's conduct, laughter rises within me.

**14.3.** He always thinks of Himself: 'I am the king of the clever: secret is My descent, and secret all My deeds;

**14.4.** secret the gait, secret the speech, secret the poses of the dance; in secret with the nagaris of Nadia — secret the play of love.

**14.5.** I play the nagara in secret — no one can perceive it,' — thinking much like this, He covers the sun's rays with His hand.

**14.6.** Before one who is cleverer than the clever, what cleverness remains? Not understanding this, Narahari's Lord — whom does He fear?"[^32-27]

His hand" (14.5) is a proverb for the vain concealment of the obvious.

## 15. Narahari — "gaurāṅgacām̐dera eirūpa sava…" (GPT1 p. 228, no. 160; GCC 10.13)
*Nagari-bhava (the heavenly women's talk). A third defends secrecy: "Do not grieve: with Gaurangachand all is so; in the open there is sorrow, in
secret greater joy; even people who get a little wealth hide it more carefully than life; love is the supreme jewel and must be hidden, and a
connoisseur of rasa is ashamed if it becomes known; Narahari's Lord is the crown of the adroit, and so He sports in secret." Raga "yatharaga".
**Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 10, pada 13.*[^32-28]

**15.3.** Love is the supreme jewel: it must be kept hidden; if it becomes known, shame arises in the heart of a connoisseur of rasa.

**15.4.** Narahari's Lord is the crown of the adroit: does anyone know His like? Unceasingly He sports in secret, showing His adroitness."

these words are at once answered by other heroines, who describe the Lord's strictness (nos. 19–20 of this chapter).

## 19. Narahari — "ki valiva ogo tomādera prati…" (GPT1 p. 229, no. 164; GCC 10.17)
*An answer: praise of the Lord's strictness (by content — not nagari-bhava). The newcomer says: "I am bewildered: why do you revile the Moon of Nadia?
He is the lamp of Jagannatha Mishra's family, the conqueror of the digvijayi, the pandits of Nadia submit to Him, He is ever on the path of dharma; He does
not listen to talk of women and never, even by mistake, looks at the faces of others' wives; if, while bathing in the Ganga, a woman's cloth touches Him,
He at once performs expiation and still cannot regain His peace. To slander Him wilfully is an aparadha; Narahari is witness: never say such things."
Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 10, pada 17.*[^32-34]

**19.1.** "What shall I say to you? I am quite bewildered: why do you so revile so good a person — the Moon of Nadia?

**19.2.** Who does not know the great scholar Jagannatha Mishra? The world extols Him as the lamp of his pure family.

**19.3.** He conquered the digvijayi, the pandits of Nadia submit to Him; He is ever devoted to the path of dharma and knows nothing but the Vedas and the like.

**19.4.** He never listens to talk of women — it pains Him to hear it; never, even by mistake, does He look at the faces of others' wives.

**19.5.** If ever, while He bathes in the Suradhuni, a woman's cloth touches His body, He at once performs the due expiation and still cannot regain His peace.

## 20. Narahari — "hera āisa ogo o sava sahite…" (GPT1 pp. 229–230, no. 165; GCC 10.19)
*An answer: praise of the Lord's strictness (by content — not nagari-bhava). Another takes her friend by the hand: "Come here — why quarrel with them?
In the city of the gods a false tale has arisen; do not be troubled. Only the guilty revile the faultless. Shachi's son out of modesty does not raise His
face — far from looking at anyone; He does not touch even the shadow of other women — how could there be a touching of bodies? He does not go to the
Ganga ghat where young women throng — He bathes at a secluded pond or at home, trembling for fear of disgrace. Let no one revile Narahari's Lord any more."
Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 10, pada 19.*[^32-36]

**20.1.** "Come over here: why do you quarrel with those? In the city of the gods a false tale has arisen — do not be troubled by it.

**20.2.** All good conduct has gone far away, no one respects anyone; this is a grave thing: what comes of what, of that they know nothing.

**20.3.** To censure one who has faults is forbidden — all say this; and whoever censures the faultless is surely the guilty one in the world.

**20.4.** Shachi's son is the best of men — this is known throughout the world: far from ever looking at anyone, out of modesty He does not raise His face.

**20.5.** He who never touches even the shadow of other women with His foot — I cannot understand at all: how could a touching of bodies and the like be possible for Him?

**20.6.** Knowing that a throng of young women is at the ghat of the Suradhuni, He does not go there: He goes to a pond and bathes where He sees a secluded spot;

**20.7.** or else He performs His bath at home: His heart trembles for fear of disgrace. The great master of the senses, dear to all — who does not praise Him?

**20.8.** Alas, alas! How can one say such words of Him whose peerless fame, like an elixir, has filled the world?

**20.9.** Who will believe such words of Him? I feel ashamed at this. Does a good person know how to revile a good one? It is the work of wicked people.

**20.10.** Still I say, knowing you as neighbours: accept the essence of my words — let no one, even by mistake, revile Narahari's Lord any more."[^32-37]

## 21. Narahari — "bhāla bhāla ogo esava kathāte…" (GPT1 pp. 230–231, no. 166; GCC 10.21)
*Nagari-bhava (a mocking answer). The disputants laugh: "We are not afraid: as virtuous as you are, so is your Gora — ah, He knows nothing, a muni among
sages, He never goes into other people's houses! So many such virtues He has — and how many within He does not show; only young women's glances know them;
but your eyes, like those of some birds, do not see the moon of the night: how should others know that Narahari's Lord is a snare that enchants women?"
Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 10, pada 21.*[^32-38]

**21.2.** Ah, ah! He knows nothing at all — I have never seen such a one! Utterly master of the senses, like the king of sages — His righteousness is renowned!

**21.3.** He does not listen to talk of women — this fame is known in the world; He never leaves His own house to go into anyone's house on any business!

**21.4.** So many such peerless virtues He has — how many of them will you tell? And as many as there are within — those He does not show outwardly.

**21.5.** So I say, listen: others have no power to know those virtues — they appear only in the flash of these young women's glances.

**21.6.** Your eyes, I see, like those of [some] birds, do not see the moon of the night: how should others know that Narahari's Lord is a snare that enchants women?"[^32-39]

## 22. Narahari — "hera āisa prāṇa sajani ihāte…" (GPT1 p. 231, no. 167; GCC 10.22)
*Nagari-bhava (the dispute). The mocker's friend says to her: "Leave it — you hold these secret talks of rasa with her in vain: she is simple and does not
walk this path; one who delights in the formless will not like form. Ask her instead: if He is so master of His senses, why does He take on the guise of
a nagara in the midst of Nadia, why do women lose their shame at the fragrance of His body, why does He, seeing a man's face and mistaking it for a woman's,
fall in a swoon, why does He dance in the assembly of the virtuous taking a woman's name and repeat 'woman' in His mind, why does He gather so many young
women in His house? Let her answer." Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 10, pada 22.*[^32-40]

**22.1.** "Come over here, dear friend: this brings no joy to the heart — in vain you hold these secret talks of rasa with her.

**22.2.** Who but a woman versed in rasa can understand the heart of a rasika? And she is very simple — she never walks this path.

**22.3.** However much you explain, she has no concern with it: one whose delight is in the formless — will form ever please her?

**22.4.** If ever she sincerely keeps your rare company, then she will understand what the play of the Moon of Nadia is.

**22.5.** Let all this be now; ask her just once: being so much master of His senses, how does He sport like this?

**22.6.** He who knows nothing [of this], in whom is no trace of pleasure — why does He take on the guise of a nagara in the midst of the town of Nadia?

**22.7.** Nowhere have I heard of this: is this the deed of a noble person? With the fragrance of His body He breaks the reserve and shame of the women-bees.

**22.8.** He who is so grave — are such deeds His, how do they please His mind? Seeing a man's face and mistaking it for a woman's face, He falls in a swoon.

**22.9.** This is very strange: one who has so much modesty — is such desire His? In the assembly of the virtuous He dances unceasingly, taking a woman's name.

**22.10.** He who never hears talk of women with His own ears — how is it that He constantly repeats "woman" in His mind?

**22.11.** He who in the world is righteous as no one else — for what reason does He gather so many young women in His own house?

**22.12.** Such are the ways of Narahari's Lord: tell her to answer this — how has such faith in such a one arisen in a generous heart?"[^32-41]

## 23. Narahari — "śuna śuna ogo sakala vujhinu…" (GPT1 pp. 231–233, no. 168; GCC 10.24)
*Nagari-bhava (the end of the dispute). Yet another, skilled in speech, says: "She is not at fault — you dispute in vain. Do not be sad, good and fair one:
you say Gora does not look at others' women — how can I believe it, when the nagara's play in Nadia is beyond counting and I have seen it myself? And if
you ask how this is possible in this descent — no one gives up his nature: this son of Shachi is the son of Yashoda; for the gopis' sake He herded cows and
lifted the hill, was subject to them, sought their touch, clasped a friend's feet to end a gopi's mana, carried [a gopi] on His shoulders, and their scolding
was sweeter to Him than the hymns of the Vedas; how would He give up such a nature?" Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC,
kirana 10, pada 24.*[^32-42]

**23.1.** "Listen, listen: I have understood everything — she is not at fault; it is with you all that I am angry, for your disputing.

**23.2.** If someone says something without understanding — should one laugh at that? To explain in the way she can understand — that I would think wise.

**23.3.** She is of good conduct; ah, such a one you do not know how to bring round. Be silent now and listen to what I say.

**23.4.** Come over here, good and fair one, do not be sad: hearing your words, my heart is overjoyed.

**23.5.** You say that Gora does not look at others' women even from the corner of His eye — how can I believe all this?

**23.6.** If I could see even a little of what you praise — then, swearing an oath and saying 'certainly', I would come to believe.

**23.7.** In the town of Nadia the nagara's play is beyond counting; be it as it may with others' words — this I have seen myself.

**23.8.** If you say: how is this possible in this descent? — there is a well-known reason for it; all people speak of it.

**23.9.** Whatever nature one has, no one can ever abandon it: one acts according to one's nature, and no one's prohibition avails.

**23.10.** If you think such a nature of His is seen nowhere — to that I tell you, listen: the world is witness to it.

**23.11.** This son of Shachi is the son of Yashoda: do you not know that? Need I tell you of all the secret pastimes in Vrindavana?

**23.12.** For the gopis' sake — the herding of cows, the lifting of the hill and all else; how much shall I tell of the lilas with the gopis, whatever and wherever they were!

**23.13.** Utterly subject to them all, not seeing them for a moment He feels it an aeon; with so many pretexts He goes about constantly, hoping for the touch of their bodies!

**23.14.** If some [gopi] in mana, being offended, will not turn to look at Kanu, — to end her mana He clasps her friend's feet.

**23.15.** He carries [her] on His shoulders, deeming it His supreme good fortune; hearing their scolding words gives Him more joy than the hymns of the Vedas.

**23.16.** He who for the sake of young women does not mind grave disgrace in the world — tell me now: how would He give up such a nature?

**23.17.** Know this for certain, reflecting in your hearts: by His nature He does all this — you will understand of yourselves.

**23.18.** Narahari's Lord is the Crown of connoisseurs of rasa, who has no equal: who does not know these deeds? What further doubt is there?"[^32-43]

[^32-42]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — pp. 231–233, no. 168 (scan PDF pp. 490–492); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 168 (catalogue: NG-361). GCC — kirana 10, pada 24 (ed. 1947,
pp. 128–129; scan PDF pp. 133–134); it is preceded by the short pada 10.23 (not in GPT): the mockers said much, the defender was abashed, and then another, skilled
in speech, looked at her own group and spoke sweetly. 23.13 "adhīna" ("subject") follows GCC (GPT1 "adhika"). The next GPT pada (no. 169 = GCC 10.25, "vrajapure
rasavilāsa viśeṣa…") is in chapter 33. B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^32-43]: "This son of Shachi is the son of Yashoda" (23.11): that Gaura is Krishna Himself is the foundation of Gaudiya theology (CC, Adi 1–4; CB). But the heroine's
conclusion — "a nature cannot be given up, so in Nadia too He plays the nagara" — the tradition does not accept: according to Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Krishna comes as
Gaura in order to taste Radha's love — in her bhava and complexion, as a devotee, not as an enjoyer (CC, Adi 4); therefore Vrindavana Dasa and Krishnadasa Kaviraja do
not portray Gaura as a nagara, and Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati regards gaura-nagari as a deviation (introductory note, chapter 27). Rendered as in the original.
23.12–23.15 are motifs of Vraja-lila: the lifting of Govardhana, the gopis' mana, the gopi who asked to be carried on His shoulders (*Bhag.* 10.30.37–38); "the beloved's
scolding is sweeter than the hymns of the Vedas" — cf. Krishna's words in CC, Adi 4.26. "Kalpa" (kalapa, 23.13) — an aeon.

## Summary of chapter 32

*The chapter continues the padas signed "Narahari" from section 3.2 of GPT. All 23 padas have been found in Narahari Chakravarti's "Gaura-charita-chintamani" and
checked against its scan ("probably Chakravarti" — B). No. 146 (no. 1) = GCC 9.2 — a mother-in-law, on an astrologer's word, sends her daughters-in-law to
Shachi-devi. Nos. 147–157 (nos. 2–12) = GCC 9.6–9.16 — the "wishes" (manoratha) of the townswomen on the way to Shachi's house, all in the future tense: to steal a
glance at Gaura, feigned mana, a silent conversation of the eyes, reproaches; in GCC no. 150 comes after no. 153 (9.12). Nos. 158–168 (nos. 13–23) = GCC 10.10–10.24 —
according to GCC this is the conversation and dispute of heavenly women (devaramaṇī) looking down on Nadia from the sky: some speak of the "secret play of the nagara",
others (nos. 19–20) answer with a description of the Lord's strictness — He does not look at women, does not listen to talk of them, bathes in a secluded place — and
call slander of Him an aparadha; the dispute ends with mockery and the argument "Shachi's son is Yashoda's son, a nature cannot be given up" (nos. 21–23). Section 3.2 of GPT omits GCC
9.3–9.5, 9.17–9.23, 10.1–10.9, 10.11, 10.18, 10.20, 10.23 (some of them — 9.18–9.19, 9.21–9.22, 10.7–10.9 — stand in other sections of GPT, see the concluding note of chapter 33). Where GCC is more explicit than GPT (no. 9 — "the cloth over the breast" instead of "the cloth over the face";
no. 10 — "wants to embrace" instead of "wants to see your dear face"; no. 2 — "under Madana's weight"), the GPT text is translated and the GCC reading is noted in VAR
and in a note. The motifs of attraction in the townswomen's daydreams and the talk of the "nagara" are rendered exactly, without softening, with notes on the position
of the tradition (notes 5, 25, 27, 30, 41, 43).*

# Chapter 33. Nagari Padas — VII: the "Narahari" padas of GPT (sect. 3.2, nos. 169–180; sects. 2.4, 3.1, 5.1, 5.2): the quarrels of the heavenly women, the townswomen's words at the Lord's wedding; concluding note

*On what nagari-bhava is, the position of the tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati) and the rules of translation, see the introductory note to the section of nagari padas in chapter 27; on the two poets named Narahari (Narahari Sarakara and Narahari Chakravarti) and on the attribution labels ("probably Sarakara", "probably Chakravarti", "not established"), see the introductory note to the "Narahari" appendix in chapter 17.*

## 1. Narahari — "vrajapure rasavilāsa viśeṣa…" (GPT1 p. 233, no. 169; GCC 10.25)
*Nagari-bhava (the heavenly women's talk). The heavenly woman who closed the dispute (chapter 32, no. 23) tells her friend in confidence: who can
tell the special plays of rasa in Vraja? Yet He is the very same, and with all the same dear companions He ever sports in Nadia, absorbed in singing of
His own virtues; first giving His own the nectar of His beauty to drink, He made them as if mad, and the young noble wives, bidding farewell to family
and shame, made Gora their very essence. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 10, pada 25.*[^33-1]

**1.1.** "The special plays of rasa in the city of Vraja — who can tell them all? Keep it secret; attend to what I tell you, counting you as my own.

**1.2.** This is He, and He is this: taking with Him all the same dear companions, He ever sports in the city of Nadia, absorbed in singing of His own virtues.

**1.3.** First giving His own the nectar of the wondrous sweetness of His form to drink, He made their minds and their steps as if mad — and they count nothing else.

**1.4.** Ever new noble wives, giving the last libation to family, to the family's disgrace and to shame, have all made their essence Gora, full of joy, the Beloved of their life — Narahari is witness to it."[^33-2]

[^33-1]: Signature — "Narahari" (narahari sāthī — "Narahari the witness", cf. chapter 31, 13.10). GPT1 — p. 233, no. 169 (scan PDF p. 492); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 169 (catalogue: NG-128).
GCC — kirana 10, pada 25 (ed. 1947, p. 130; scan PDF p. 135), "yathārāga". **Who speaks.** The tenth kirana of GCC is the morning talk of the heavenly women (devaramaṇī)
looking down on Nadia from the sky (chapter 32, note 24); padas 10.25–10.26 (nos. 1–2 of this chapter) close their talk: one tells another "in confidence", and the other asks
to be taught how to come and live in Nadia. GCC readings: "gupate rākhiyā dio cita yāhā kahiye āpana jāniyā tore" ("keeping it secret, attend…"), "nija guṇagaṇe"
("absorbed in His own virtues"). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^33-2]: "This is He, and He is this; with all the same companions" (1.2): that Gaura is Krishna Himself and that Krishna's companions came with Him to Navadvipa is the
teaching of the tradition (CC, Adi 1 and 3–4; Kavi Karnapura's "Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika" names who among Gaura's companions was whom in Vraja). But the gopis in
Gaura-lila are not townswomen of Nadia in love with Gaura: the Lord Himself came in Radha's bhava to taste Her love (CC, Adi 4), and therefore the Gaudiya tradition
does not accept the speaker's conclusion — that "the young wives of Nadia made Gora, as a nagara, their essence" (introductory note, chapter 27). Rendered as in the
original. "Absorbed in singing of His own virtues" — cf. CB, Madhya (the Lord in bhavavesha sings of Himself). "To give the last libation" (tilāñjali) — to abandon for good.

## 2. Narahari — "gaurāṅgacām̐dera sucāru carita…" (GPT1 p. 233, no. 170; GCC 10.26)
*Nagari-bhava (the heavenly women's talk). The listener, hearing of Gaurangachand's lovely deeds, is filled with joy and cannot hold back tears of
love; joining her palms, she asks to be taught how she might once come to live in Nadia and be a companion of its young playful women, keep Narahari's
Beloved in her heart and be rid of the cruel barrier. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 10, pada 26.*[^33-3]

**2.1.** Hearing and hearing of Gaurangachand's lovely deeds, the fair one was filled with joy; she cannot hold her composure — again and again both eyes fill with tears of love.

**2.2.** Joining her palms and bowing, she again speaks soft, sweet words: "Counting me as your own, at last you have, as it were, taken all the pain from my heart.

**2.3.** I pray: how might I once dwell in this city of Nadia? And how might I live as a companion of these ever new playful beauties?

**2.4.** Keeping the Beloved of Narahari's life within my heart, I shall be rid of the cruel barrier. Tell me, tell me: by what means will all these wishes be fulfilled?"

[^33-3]: Signature — "Narahari" (narahari prāṇapiyā — "the Beloved of Narahari's life", glossary). GPT1 — p. 233, no. 170 (scan PDF p. 492); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 170
(catalogue: NG-362). GCC — kirana 10, pada 26 (ed. 1947, p. 130; scan PDF p. 135). 2.4 "be fulfilled" follows GPT2 and GCC "saphala" (GPT1 "sakala", a misprint); "barrier" —
GPT1 and GCC "vādhā" (GPT2 "dhām̐dhā", "bewilderment"). The wish of heavenly beings to be born where the Lord reveals His lila is a commonplace of the hagiographies (CB,
Adi: the gods long to be born in Navadvipa to share in the Lord's sankirtana); the "cruel barrier" is that one living in the city of the gods cannot come to Nadia. The
closing pada of the kirana (GCC 10.27) is not in GPT: the fair one told her friend all she had asked, and the heavenly women, trembling and winking at one another,
gave themselves to merry play, gazing at Narahari's Lord; the colophon: "the description of the play of the heavenly women filled with love for Him". B. Nagari-bhava —
see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).

## 3. Narahari — "surapura mājhe vasati kariyā…" (GPT1 pp. 233–234, no. 171; GCC 11.4)
*An answer: defence of the chastity of the women of Nadia (the heavenly women's talk; by content not nagari-bhava). The opening of the eleventh
kirana of GCC — "the love-quarrels of the heavenly women". A heavenly woman who has just arrived angrily rebukes her friends: living in the city of the
gods, they have grown proud and slander the women of Nadia; what they describe happens only with the young wives of Vraja, while the wives of Nadia are
faithful to their husbands, do not see another man's face even in a dream, revere their elders; whoever sings of others' disgrace is disgraced. Raga
"yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 11, pada 4.*[^33-4]

**3.1.** "Living in the city of the gods, why have you grown so proud? You feel no fear at heart in slandering the women of Nadia!

**3.2.** Alas, alas! Hearing such perverse words, how can I bear it? I do not know what wrong these women of Nadia have done to you all.

**3.3.** You judge others by your own ways and do not know the secret of others' hearts; you understand nothing — what comes of what; so I say: in vain do you bear a body.

**3.4.** What you describe is possible only with the young wives in the city of Vraja; but all the young wives of Nadia are the most faithful of the faithful — the whole world knows it.

**3.5.** They do not see another husband's face even in a dream, never walk an evil road; they know no tricks, no deceit, no guile — all of them always simple of heart.

**3.6.** Steadfast, skilful in their work, of lovely conduct — always on the highest path of dharma; mindful of the matchless shame of family and of fear, never, forgetting themselves, do they sit with a bad man.

**3.7.** They all love their elders as their life; their auspicious virtues cannot be counted. In my heart there is one thing: always to keep them with care in my eyes.

**3.8.** So I tell you: knowing that you are my neighbours, you will surely accept these words — I say nothing else. Whoever sings of another's disgrace is herself disgraced: this Narahari knows."[^33-5]

[^33-4]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — pp. 233–234, no. 171 (scan PDF pp. 492–493); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 171 (catalogue: NG-129). GCC — kirana 11, pada 4 (ed. 1947, pp. 132–133;
scan PDF pp. 137–138), "yathārāga". **Who speaks.** The eleventh kirana of GCC is headed "Again in the morning — the love-quarrels and so on of the heavenly women"; its
opening is not in GPT: from the sky the heavenly women drink the nectar of Gaura's form as He plays in Shachi's courtyard and argue — some say that the nagaris of
Nadia "have gone mad for the Beloved" and will bring disgrace on themselves, others answer that the wives of Vraja did the same (GCC 11.1); a short pada on the heavenly
women's rapture (11.2); praise of the love of Nadia's young wives — and then "a heavenly woman arrived and, waving her hand, said angrily to all" (11.3). GCC readings:
"nā jāniyā" (3.2), "tem̐i vali" (3.3). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27); this pada answers it.
[^33-5]: The defender sets Vraja against Nadia: a love that takes no account of husbands and of talk "is possible only with the young wives of Vraja" (3.4), while the women
of Nadia are faithful wives. Gaudiya theology agrees: the parakiya-rasa of the gopis belongs to Vraja (CC, Adi 4), and in Navadvipa the Lord did not accept the worship
of women as a nagara (CB, Adi). The pada is therefore by content not nagari-bhava (like nos. 19–20 of chapter 32); in the heavenly women's dispute, however, her words
will be mocked (nos. 4–10). "Neighbours" (sahavāsī, 3.8) — those who live with her in the city of the gods.

## 4. Narahari — "bhāla bhāla ihā śikhāte have nā…" (GPT1 p. 234, no. 172; GCC 11.6)
*Nagari-bhava (the heavenly women's quarrel). A mocker answers the defender: they need no teaching — as if they did not know: on earth only the
wives of Nadia are faithful, and in the city of the gods only she; they themselves, forever singing of others' disgrace, will be disgraced, but will not
make her a sharer; how can so clever a woman live among the unchaste? Let her go to Nadia with her dharma and her shame and live among the chaste.
Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 11, pada 6.*[^33-6]

**4.1.** "Well, well! No need to teach us this — as if I did not know it all! On earth only the wives of Nadia are faithful to their husbands, and in the city of the gods only you!

**4.2.** We, ever singing of others' disgrace, shall all be disgraced — do not you worry about that: we shall not make you a sharer in it.

**4.3.** Besides, how will you, the cleverest of women, live alone in the city of the gods? Living with the unchaste, you will easily become unchaste yourself.

**4.4.** So I say: go to this city of Nadia, taking your dharma, your shame and the rest. Narahari is glad of it: be always careful, living among the chaste."

[^33-6]: Signature — "Narahari". GPT1 — p. 234, no. 172 (scan PDF p. 493); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 172 (catalogue: NG-363). GCC — kirana 11, pada 6 (ed. 1947, p. 133; scan PDF p. 138);
before it, the short pada 11.5 (not in GPT): hearing this, a heavenly woman versed in rasa laughed inwardly with her own group, exchanged signs with them and spoke.
4.1 — GPT1 "nā jāni e āmi", GCC "nā jāniye āmi" (GPT2 "jānie āmi", "I know"): the gibe — "as if I did not know"; 4.2 GCC "ihāra bhāgī kakhana nā karite yāva"; 4.4 GCC "tāhe vali".
The tone of the pada is mocking — rendered as in the original. B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).

## 5. Narahari — "hera āisa ogo pativratā saha…" (GPT1 p. 234, no. 173; GCC 11.7)
*Nagari-bhava (the heavenly women's quarrel). Another calls her friend: why talk with a "faithful wife"? Joy is among equals; not all heavenly women
are adroit — as the owl does not see the sun; the secret stories of Nadia's young wives she will not reveal for shame; but our Gora — beautiful, good —
speaks to no one with raised face, is always careful on the path of dharma, knows nothing of such things — and such a Lord of Narahari they bewitched
with signs from the corners of their eyes. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 11, pada 7.*[^33-7]

**5.1.** "Come here, friend: why say all this to a 'faithful wife'? Among equals joy arises; with unequals pain grows.

**5.2.** Being born heavenly women — are all of us then adroit? Never think so: as the owl does not see the sun — so, know, are many.

**5.3.** The young wives of Nadia — the young and the experienced — who equals them in the world? Their secret stories I cannot reveal for shame.

**5.4.** Look, look here: our Gora, the life of our life, beautiful and good, speaks to no one with raised face; wondrous is His way, He is wholly absorbed within.

**5.5.** Always careful on the path of dharma — what shall I say! — He knows nothing of all this. And such a Lord of Narahari they bewitched, signalling from the corners of their eyes."[^33-8]

[^33-7]: Signature — "Narahari" (naraharinātha — "Narahari's Lord"). GPT1 — p. 234, no. 173 (scan PDF p. 493); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 173 (catalogue: NG-130; the catalogue's "paratatratā" is an
OCR error for "pativratā"). GCC — kirana 11, pada 7 (ed. 1947, p. 134; scan PDF p. 139), "anyā ca — yathārāga" ("and another"). 5.1 in GCC "ki lāgi kahicha" — "why are you
saying all this to a faithful wife". "The owl does not see the sun" (5.2) — a proverb for blindness to the obvious. B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the
section (chapter 27).
[^33-8]: The Lord's portrait in 5.4–5.5 is the same as in the hagiographies: He speaks to no one with raised face and is "always careful on the path of dharma" (CB, Adi: in this
incarnation the Lord did not look at women and allowed no jesting with them; cf. nos. 19–20 of chapter 32). The words "they bewitched Him" are the speaker's slander of
the women of Nadia, rendered as in the original; the tradition's answer — introductory note (chapter 27).

## 6. Narahari — "ki valiva ogo nadīyāra nava…" (GPT1 p. 235, no. 174; GCC 11.8)
*Nagari-bhava (the heavenly women's quarrel). Another: the young wives of Nadia do not reveal their secrets, are always gracious outwardly, well-behaved
before mother-in-law and sister-in-law, yet gain their ends so that no one notices, and secretly try to win the Moon of Nadia; she herself saw how they
bewitched Him — and there was no one to restrain the women: Narahari was not with Gauranga. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** —
GCC, kirana 11, pada 8.*[^33-9]

**6.1.** "What shall I say, friend, of the ways of the young wives of Nadia! They do not reveal what is within, but outwardly they are always most gracious.

**6.2.** Before mother-in-law and sister-in-law they always behave well; whatever everyone praises, that they do with great care.

**6.3.** In many ways they gain their ends — no one can ever notice; to win the Moon of Nadia they go about most secretly.

**6.4.** With my own eyes I saw that day how, with so many graceful poses, they bewitched [Him]. Who would restrain the women? Narahari was not with Gauranga."

p. 134; scan PDF p. 139), "anyā ca — yathārāga". "Narahari was not with Gauranga": in GCC the poet usually accompanies the Lord and leads Him away from what is improper
(GCC 11.11, 11.14 — see notes 18 and 19); here the speaker seems to explain why this time "there was no one to restrain the women". As in no. 5, the words about
"bewitching" are the speaker's surmise; in the following padas (nos. 7–8) the mockers themselves describe how the Lord turns away and leaves. B. Nagari-bhava — see the

## 7. Narahari — "nadīyāte kata kata e kautuka…" (GPT1 p. 235, no. 175; GCC 11.9)
*Nagari-bhava (the heavenly women's quarrel). The next one confirms it mockingly: she knows well how "faithful" these young chaste ones are: the other
day, standing under a young kadamba, she saw Gora walking alone in the late afternoon toward Murari Gupta's quarter; the "faithful wives" were coming
along with a fearsome mother-in-law and sister-in-law — and yet, finding Gorachand on a near path, they contrived to stand in His way, signalled to Him
and did not keep the end of the sari over the breast; and Narahari's Lord, lowering His face in shame, stepped aside. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution:
probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 11, pada 9.*[^33-10]

**7.1.** "How many such pranks there are in Nadia — how many will you tell! And how 'faithful to their husbands' all these young chaste ones are — that I know.

**7.2.** That day I saw with my own eyes, standing under a young kadamba: Gora was walking alone in the late afternoon toward Murari Gupta's quarter.

**7.3.** At that hour the 'faithful wives' were coming with a fearsome mother-in-law and sister-in-law — and still, finding Gorachand on a near path, they stood there on a pretext, swaying their bodies.

**7.4.** Signalling to Him again and again, luring Him, not keeping even half the end of the sari over the breast… And Narahari's Lord, lowering His face in shame, stepped aside and stood far off."[^33-11]

scan PDF pp. 139–140), "anyā ca — yathārāga". GCC readings: "jāniye āmi" (7.1), "murārī-guptera" (7.2), "pāyā" (7.3), "lubhāiye" (7.4, "luring"; GPT1 "bhulāiyā", "beguiling"),
"eka bhita hayā". Murari Gupta's quarter (pāṛā) — Murari's house in Navadvipa, which the Lord visited (CB, Madhya; cf. chapter 31, no. 3). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory

"faithful wives" are mockery; the tradition accepts neither this slander nor the worship of Gaura as a nagara (introductory note, chapter 27).

## 8. Narahari — "ki kahiva ogo e sakala kathā…" (GPT1 p. 235, no. 176; GCC 11.10)
*Nagari-bhava (the heavenly women's quarrel). Another: it is shameful even to speak of it — the beautiful Moon of Nadia ever trembles before young women;
once Gora walked alone with an elephant's gait, looking at no one — and the "faithful wives" stood on His path and shot unseen sharp arrows from the
corners of their eyes; one, holding a pomegranate, said: "To whom shall I give this wondrous fruit?", another: "He whose body is like new gold will take
it Himself, unasked"; Narahari's Lord, holding His composure, finished His errand in shame and quickly went home. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution:
probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 11, pada 10.*[^33-12]

**8.1.** "What shall I say, friend: it is most shameful even to speak of these things. Before young women the good and beautiful Moon of Nadia ever trembles.

**8.2.** I do not know on what errand that day Gora went alone with an elephant's gait; He did not look at anyone even once — most gentle, wholly absorbed within.

**8.3.** On that road the 'faithful wives' stood looking at Gauranga — again and again they shot unseen sharp arrows from the restless corners of their eyes.

**8.4.** One, holding a fine pomegranate in her hand, says: 'To whom shall I give this wondrous [fruit]?' Another says: 'He whose body is like new gold will take it Himself, unasked.'

**8.5.** Such words they spoke to one another; who, hearing them, would stay calm? Narahari's Lord, holding His composure, in shame quickly finished His errand and went home."[^33-13]

## 9. Narahari — "ki valiva iha savāre nirakhi…" (GPT1 p. 236, no. 177; GCC 11.15)
*Nagari-bhava (the heavenly women's quarrel). The mocker goes on: the fame of the ways of Nadia's wives has filled the world — mothers-in-law, sisters-in-law,
husbands always scold them and every day fervently pray to Old Shiva, fearing disgrace; they keep them at home, do not let them on the road, let them go to
the Suradhuni only with a sister-in-law; the neighbour-women restrain them unceasingly, no one trusts them in anything; hearing such reproach, Narahari dies of
shame every day. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 11, pada 15.*[^33-14]

**9.1.** "What shall I say! How much she said, looking at them — can one bear it? What the ways of the women of Nadia are — the whole world is full of it:

**9.2.** mother-in-law, sister-in-law, husband and the rest always scold them all; every day they pray with great fervour to Old Shiva — 'there will be disgrace!'

**9.3.** They always keep them carefully at home, do not let them go out on the road; and if one wants to bathe in the Suradhuni — the sister-in-law goes with her.

**9.4.** The neighbour-women restrain them unceasingly; no one trusts them in any matter. What more shall I say? Hearing that reproach, Narahari dies of shame every day."

## 10. Narahari — "surapure kevā nā jāne nadīyā…" (GPT1 p. 236, no. 178; GCC 11.17)
*Nagari-bhava (the heavenly women's quarrel). The defender, frightened, has fallen silent (GCC 11.16); then a playful one, glancing at her own group, says:
in the city of the gods everyone knows the ways of the nagaris of Nadia — why be vainly angry with her? What she said is secret; and taking her hand and
praising her, she goes on gently: the ways of Nadia's young wives are past counting; no one looks at the bracelet on her own hand in a mirror — here is the
jewel in Ai's house: if she came on the astrologer's word, why does she stare unblinking at Gora, playing with her brows, tremble, let her clothes and
ornaments slip, break into gooseflesh and sweat? Narahari's Lord is the husband of them all. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** —
GCC, kirana 11, pada 17.*[^33-15]

**10.1.** "In the city of the gods who does not know what the ways of the nagaris of Nadia are? Why then are you so vainly angry with her?

**10.2.** What shall I say: what she said is most secret; no one knows it. Have patience, all of you, and listen with care to what I say."

**10.3.** So, glancing at her own group, she quickly took her hand, praised her in many words and speaks very softly, full of rasa:

**10.4.** "The ways of the young wives of Nadia — who can tell how many? Many days I have seen many pranks with my own eyes — and I tell no one.

**10.5.** Let that be; no one looks at the bracelet on her own hand in a mirror: look here — the jewel in Ai's house: why has she come running in the morning?

**10.6.** If you say: on the auspicious word of the astrologer she came to Ai on her own business — then why, playing with her brows, does she gaze unblinking at Gora?

**10.7.** And her body trembles again and again, her clothes and ornaments slip, the knot of her hair comes loose; she is all gooseflesh, sweat trickles, her champa-earrings sway again and again.

**10.8.** Who does such things — say, say? Why should anyone not believe it? Narahari's Lord is the husband of them all: have no doubt of this."[^33-16]

and began to sing of His deeds (GCC 11.18); the closing stanza is the poet's prayer: "Lord full of rasa, with Your companions keep me in Nadia" (11.19).

## 11. Narahari — "śuna śuna ei kālikāra kathā…" (GPT1 pp. 236–237, no. 179; GCC 11.14, first part)
*Nagari-bhava (a heavenly woman's story). One, "casting off shame", tells her friend what happened yesterday: many young women joyfully took counsel — one
urges going at once with pitchers for water, for the Moon of Nadia will come to the ghat on the Suradhuni; others advise dressing up, adorning the hair with
flowers, rubbing the face with kunkuma, lining the eyes, putting on necklaces like a snare, ringing anklets and a belled girdle — so that Gora may lose His
composure. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 11, pada 14 (first half).*[^33-17]

**11.1.** "Listen, listen: I shall tell you what happened yesterday, casting off shame. Many young women, with the greatest joy, eagerly took counsel.

**11.2.** One says: 'Oh, do not delay, take your pitcher — let us go for water: the Moon of Nadia will come to the ghat on the Suradhuni — it is time for Him to come.'

**11.3.** Another says: 'Why go like this? Dress yourselves in every way — so that by a spark of that radiance the young Kishora cannot keep His composure even by half a sesame seed.'

**11.4.** Another says: 'Braid your hair, adorn your heads with many flowers — so that by their fragrance even the One who has conquered the senses cannot turn His face away.'

**11.5.** Another says: 'Rub your faces with kunkuma, line your eyes brightly with kajal — so that Gauranga's eyes are enchanted, seeing the charming new graces.'

**11.6.** Another says: 'Put on necklaces of many jewels, like a lovely snare — so that in it the Moon of Nadia, beautiful Gora, may easily be caught.'

**11.7.** Another says: 'Bring and put on ringing anklets and a jewelled, belled girdle — so that the ears of Narahari's Lord are charmed, hearing the sweet sound.'"[^33-18]

## 12. Narahari — "nānā kathā kahi āne āne save…" (GPT1 p. 237, no. 180; GCC 11.14, conclusion)
*Nagari-bhava (a heavenly woman's story, concluded). Dressed up, the women with pitchers on their hips come out of their houses and go to the Suradhuni,
holding hands and talking of rasa; on the way they see Gaura — but He, a great pandita, walks with bowed head, keeping His composure; suspecting something
amiss, He looked back once — and they showered Him with the arrows of their glances; the Jewel of virtues, abashed, thought of disgrace; the nagaris, keeping
His form in their hearts, worshipped Him with love. Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 11, pada 14 (second half; the last
couplet differs in GPT).*[^33-19]

**12.1.** Having said much to one another, all eagerly dressed themselves; each looks at her face in a mirror, hastily chewing betel.

**12.2.** Putting on bright clothes, all very lively, pitchers on their hips — from this house and that they came out, with what joy of heart!

**12.3.** Laughing and laughing, the girls of an age — all that throng of "faithful wives", full of rasa — go, lighting up the bank of the Suradhuni: what wondrous radiance of beauty!

**12.4.** In the rapture of rasa, holding hands, glancing with slight graces, telling tales of rasa in many ways — on the path they caught sight of Gaura.

**12.5.** But Gaura, the best of all, a great pandita, walked with bowed head, keeping His composure; suspecting something most improper, He looked back at them only once.

**12.6.** At that moment they all showered Him thickly with the arrows of glances from the corners of their eyes; and at once, abashed, the Jewel of virtues again thought with fear of disgrace.

**12.7.** All the nagaris, keeping Gauranga's form in their hearts, worshipped Him with love. Narahari says: in the city of Nadia the meeting of the nagaris and the nagara came to pass.[^33-20]

*Nagari-bhava (a dream). The marriage with Vishnupriya, the morning of the adhivasa day. At dawn, in a secluded house, young wives make merry; one, full of

wedding, and then, taking her hand, embraced her again and again; the fragrance of His body is on her still; today is the adhivasa — quickly dress and go to

**13.3.** says very softly: 'At My wedding come in the morning for the water rite.' Saying this, He takes my hand and embraces me again and again — what a jest in that!

**13.4.** All this is from the touch of that body's fragrance; I tell you, casting off shame. Today is the adhivasa — quickly dress and go to meet Narahari's Lord."[^33-22]

## 15. Narahari — "nava nadīyā-nāgarī gori bhori vaya thori…" (GPT1 p. 95, sect. 2.4, no. 7; BR; GCC 9.22)
*Nagari-bhava. In Shachi's house the young nagaris of Nadia secretly gaze at the Beloved and tremble at Madana's arrow: one thinks she has become shameless,
another cannot hold back a smile, a third speaks of love, half covered by her veil; others make signs, wipe their friends' faces, whisper aside; so all the noble
chaste wives were immersed in the ocean of the rasa of prema for Gaura and gave the Lord of their life their life, their soul and their youth. Raga "yatharaga".

**15.1.** The young nagaris of Nadia — fair, enraptured, young in years — who else could understand their ways? Gazing quite unnoticed at the Beloved, their hearts tremble at Madana's arrow.

**15.2.** One, thinking to herself, says: "Today, it seems, I have become shameless before all." Another, signalling to a friend, cannot restrain herself — and at once smiles a little.

**15.3.** One, taking a friend's hand, softly pleads — great joy overflows her heart; another tells a friend of love, half covering herself with her veil.

**15.4.** One makes signs to a friend, hand in hand — how many words arise in the mind! Another, threatening in every way with the lovely corner of her eye, keeps her friend in her senses.

**15.5.** One, to show her own composure, carefully wipes a friend's face with the end of her sari; another, after a whisper in the ear, knowing it improper, stands hidden aside.

**15.6.** So all the noble chaste wives were immersed in the ocean of the rasa of prema for Gaura. What shall Narahari say: to the Lord of their life they gave their life, their soul and their youth.[^33-26]

"sāmā'yā vāsara-ghare" (16.3: "slipping into the bridal chamber" — more outspoken than GPT "rasera ghare"). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
[^33-28]: The townswomen's wishes (16.2–16.3) — "to play with Gora day and night", "to touch the golden body" — are the nagari motif in its plain form; rendered exactly; where BR is more outspoken
than GPT ("the bridal chamber"), GPT is translated. At the Lord's wedding with Vishnupriya, His eternal consort (chapter 21, note 30), Vrindavana Dasa describes the joy of the people of Nadia
without the nagari motif (CB, Adi 15); the tradition does not accept the worship of Gaura as a nagara (introductory note, chapter 27). "Together with Narahari" (16.4) — the poet places himself
among those in the procession.

## 17. Narahari — "dekha dekha ago bhuvanamohana gaurāṅgarūpera chaṭā…" (GPT1 p. 155, sect. 3.1, no. 129; GCC 10.8)
*Nagari-bhava (the heavenly women's talk): praise of His form. One of the heavenly women calls her friends to look at the radiance of Gauranga's form: is it
lightning that has left the cloud and flashed upon the earth? a heap of golden lotus buds, of ground gorochana? fresh kunkuma on the breasts of the young
wives of Vraja, a champaka garland on the necks of the nagaris of Navadvipa? One longs to keep Him always in the heart; the eyes are never sated. Raga
"yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — GCC, kirana 10, pada 8.*[^33-29]

**17.1.** "Look, look, friends: the radiance of the form of Gauranga, who enchants the world! Is it lightning that has left the cloud and flashed above the earth?

**17.2.** Is it a heap of pure, lovely buds of the golden lotus? Is it a heap of finely ground, pure, beautiful gorochana?

**17.3.** Is it fresh kunkuma on the breasts of the young wives of Vraja? Is it a champaka garland on the necks of the nagaris of Navadvipa?

**17.4.** One longs to keep Him always deep within the heart; the eyes are never sated with gazing — Narahari is witness to it."[^33-30]

[^33-29]: Signature — "Narahari" (ithe narahari sāthī — "Narahari is witness to it"). GPT1 — p. 155, sect. 3.1 ("form"), no. 129 (scan PDF p. 414); GPT2 — sect. 3.1, no. 129 (catalogue: NG-248).
**A witness found** (the catalogue had: "not in BR, GPT2 index — Sarakara; nagari, later"): GCC — kirana 10, pada 8 (ed. 1947, p. 121; scan PDF p. 126), "kācicca — yathārāga" ("and a
certain [heavenly woman]"): it is one of the morning speeches of the heavenly women that open the tenth kirana (chapter 32, note 24); after it come GCC 10.9 (no. 18 of this chapter) and
10.10 (GPT no. 158 — chapter 32, no. 13). GPT placed both padas at the end of section 3.1 ("Gaura's form"), before the section of nagari padas. GCC readings: "ogo" (17.1), "dhārādhara"
("cloud"; GPT1 "dharādhara" — "mountain" — rendered "cloud" by sense and after GCC: lightning leaves the cloud), "niramala sundara kanaka kamala-kalikā-rāśi" (17.2), "navayuvatī-kucera"
(17.3). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).

body after embraces — an image of Vraja-lila. Gaura is golden because He took Radha's colour (CC, Adi 4; CC, Adi 1.5); "to keep Him in the heart" is the wish of the speaking heavenly woman;
the tradition does not accept the worship of Gaura as a nagara (introductory note, chapter 27).

## 18. Narahari — "dekha dekha ago gaurāṅgacām̐dera bhuvanamohana veśa…" (GPT1 p. 155, sect. 3.1, no. 130; GCC 10.9)
*Nagari-bhava (the heavenly women's talk): His morning form. Another calls them to look at the world-enchanting form of Gaurangachand: dishevelled curls
wreathed with kunda buds; on His brow a tilaka of kunkuma and sandal — as if the moon had risen in a golden sky; the earrings flash; "He will steal dharma,
modesty and honour"; a garland that enchants young women; "what play this is — I cannot understand". Raga "yatharaga". **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** —
GCC, kirana 10, pada 9.*[^33-31]

**18.1.** "Look, look, friends: the world-enchanting form of Gaurangachand! The lovely curling locks, wreathed with kunda buds, have come loose and fallen.

**18.3.** The earrings flash in His ears — to what shall they be compared? I feel: He will steal everything — dharma, modesty and honour.

**18.4.** On His neck a garland that enchants young women, matchless, falling in curves. I see Narahari's Lord — what a form! I cannot understand what play this is."[^33-32]

steal dharma, modesty and honour" (18.3) — the speaker's words about herself and her friends; rendered exactly; the tradition does not accept gaura-nagari (introductory note, chapter 27).

## 19. Narahari — "jhulata jhulata sundara rasamaya gorā…" (GPT1 pp. 324–325, sect. 5.1, no. 12; BR)

companions, smiling, push the swing and sing; a townswoman says: who, seeing it, could turn her eyes away; I swear — now all family shame will go: I shall go

**19.3.** Some sing sweetly in a lovely tune — who, hearing it, can keep composure? — o! Seeing that beauty, who will turn away her eyes, saying in her mind, "I am lost, I am lost"? — o!

## 20. Narahari — "nadīyāra śaśī raṅge rājapathe…" (GPT1 p. 356, sect. 5.2, no. 39; BR)
*Nagari-bhava; ashtakaliya (a walk through the town). The Moon of Nadia, at play, walks along the royal road, swaying, His heart thrilling; the young women,
unnoticed, restless, long to cast at Him even half a glance; one says to her friend: Gora's form is a heap of nectar — lips bright with betel, a gentle smile, a
garland of rangana, a glance that enchants the world, curls, a sandal tilaka, arms reaching to the knees, a broad chest — "I have drowned in the rasa of Narahari's
Lord and bidden farewell to shame and family". Raga dhanashi. **Attribution: probably Chakravarti** — the pada is in BR (twelfth wave).*[^33-35]

**20.3.** A garland of rangana flowers sways; with the play of His eyes He enchants the world; lovely are the curling locks, on His brow shines a sandal tilaka.

**20.4.** And how the arms reaching to the knees curve! Who would not lose herself at that broad chest? I have drowned in the rasa of Narahari's Lord — I have given the last libation to this shame and family."[^33-36]

## Summary of chapter 33

*The chapter completes the padas signed "Narahari" in nagari-bhava. All 20 padas are "probably Chakravarti" (B). GPT1 3.2 nos. 169–180 (nos. 1–12) = GCC 10.25–10.26 and
the eleventh kirana of the "Gaura-charita-chintamani" ("the love-quarrels of the heavenly women"): 11.4, 11.6–11.10, 11.15, 11.17 and 11.14 — GPT rearranged the padas (no. 177 =
11.15, no. 178 = 11.17) and split 11.14 into two (nos. 179–180). The speakers are heavenly women looking down on Nadia from the sky: one defends the chastity of the women of Nadia
(no. 3 — by content not nagari-bhava), the others mock her, tell of the townswomen's "pranks" and call Narahari's Lord "the husband of them all" (no. 10) — yet they themselves
describe the Lord as strict: He does not raise His face, turns away, hurries home in shame (nos. 5, 7, 8, 12). GPT padas outside section 3.2: 2.4 nos. 2, 3, 7, 21 (nos. 13–16) — the
women of Nadia at the Lord's wedding with Vishnupriya (a dream with an embrace, setting out for Shachi's house, "Madana's arrow", wishes to touch His body; all in the twelfth
wave of the "Bhakti-ratnakara", no. 7 also in GCC 9.22); 3.1 nos. 129–130 (nos. 17–18) — found in GCC (10.8–10.9, the heavenly women's words on Gaura's morning appearance;
no. 130 was not in the catalogue — new line NG-366; for no. 129, NG-248, "Sarakara?, no witnesses" is replaced by B); 5.1 no. 12 (no. 19, jhulana) and 5.2 no. 39 (no. 20, a walk
through the town) — in BR. Where GCC or BR is more outspoken than GPT (no. 8 — an extra couplet in GCC; no. 16 — BR's "bridal chamber"), GPT is translated; the only place
where GPT is more outspoken than GCC is the last couplet of no. 12 ("the meeting of the nagaris and the nagara" instead of GCC's words that Narahari preserved propriety;
note 20). The open motifs of attraction and sambhoga (nos. 7, 10, 13, 15, 16) are rendered exactly, with notes on the tradition's position.*

## Concluding note on the "Narahari" nagari padas (chapters 29–33)

*1. **How many.** In the section of nagari padas, 102 padas signed "Narahari" from the "Gaura-pada-tarangini" have been translated: chapter 29 — 15 (Narahari Chakravarti's
pada NG-079 from the cycle of the twelfth wave of the "Bhakti-ratnakara"; GPT1 3.2 nos. 39, 40, 42–45; nos. 86–93), chapter 30 — 21 (nos. 94–110, 120–123), chapter 31 — 23 (nos. 119,
124–145), chapter 32 — 23 (nos. 146–168), chapter 33 — 20 (nos. 169–180; 2.4 nos. 2, 3, 7, 21; 3.1 nos. 129–130; 5.1 no. 12; 5.2 no. 39). Of the 95 padas signed Narahari in section
3.2 of GPT, 94 are translated here — all except no. 41 (= PK 103 of Narahari Sarakara, translated in the main part, chapter 3); the other 8 are nagari padas from sections 2.4,
3.1, 5.1, 5.2. No. 119 (Gaura in sleep speaks Krishna's words) is by content not nagari-bhava, as are the rebuttals within the heavenly women's dispute (chapter 32, nos. 19–20;
chapter 33, no. 3).*

*2. **Attribution.** "Probably Chakravarti" (B) — 81 padas: 75 are found in Narahari Chakravarti's "Gaura-charita-chintamani" (GCC, ed. 1947) — padas 2.13; 7.2–7.12, 7.14–7.16,
7.29–7.30; 8.2–8.20; 9.1–9.2, 9.6–9.16, 9.22; 10.8–10.10, 10.12–10.17, 10.19, 10.21–10.22, 10.24–10.26; 11.4, 11.6–11.10, 11.14 (two padas in GPT), 11.15, 11.17 — and 6 occur only in the
"Bhakti-ratnakara" (NG-079; 2.4 nos. 2, 3, 21; 5.1 no. 12; 5.2 no. 39). "Not established" or "probably Sarakara" (C) — 21 padas: six short padas GPT1 3.2 nos. 39, 40, 42–45 in plain Bengali
(the GPT2 index assigns them to Sarakara; there are no other witnesses; no. 43 — "not established") and fifteen padas nos. 100–110, 120–123, which stand in GPT in the place of the
lost pages of the only available scan of GCC (pp. 81–88 = GCC 7.17–7.28; apparently also from GCC). Not one "Narahari" nagari pada of GPT is confirmed by PK or by other early
collections as a song of Narahari Sarakara, the Lord's companion; almost all of them are Narahari Chakravarti's poetic elaboration of the nagari motif (first half of the
18th century). The collation confirms Majumdar's argument: the long padas of GPT with this signature do not belong to Sarakara.*

*3. **The composition of GCC 7–11 in GPT.** Kiranas 7–11 of the "Gaura-charita-chintamani" describe morning in Navadvipa: the townswomen of Nadia talk of Gaura and of how,
deceiving their strict elders, they saw Him (kirana 7), tell their dreams (8), go to Shachi's house and dream of meeting Him (9); then the heavenly women look down on Nadia
from the sky — praise its nagaris, argue about Gaura (10) and quarrel among themselves (11). These five kiranas have 121 padas (12 of them on the lost pages of the scan);
the compiler of GPT took at least 78 and distributed them among his sections:
— kirana 7: 7.1 — in sect. 2.2 (GPT1 p. 68, no. 19; chapter 19); 7.2–7.12, 7.14–7.16 = 3.2 nos. 86–99 (no. 97 is only the second half of 7.14); 7.29–7.30 = nos. 124–125; not taken:
7.13 and the closing 7.31; 7.17–7.28 are lost in the scan (in their place — nos. 100–110, 120–123);
— kirana 8: 8.2–8.20 = nos. 126–144; not taken: the opening 8.1 and the closing 8.21;
— kirana 9: 9.1–9.2 = nos. 145–146; 9.6–9.16 = nos. 147–157 (9.12 = no. 150 stands earlier in GPT); 9.18–9.19, 9.21–9.22 — in sect. 2.4 ("the second marriage", nos. 4–7: where they
also stand in BR's wedding narrative); not taken: 9.3–9.5, 9.17, 9.20 and the closing prayer 9.23;
— kirana 10: 10.7 — GPT1 p. 494, no. 30 (chapter 18, no. 28); 10.8–10.9 — in sect. 3.1, "form" (nos. 129–130); 10.10, 10.12–10.17, 10.19, 10.21–10.22, 10.24–10.26 = 3.2 nos. 158–170;
not taken: the opening 10.1–10.6, 10.11, 10.18, 10.20, 10.23 and the closing 10.27;
— kirana 11: 11.4, 11.6–11.10, 11.14, 11.15, 11.17 = nos. 171–180 (in a different order; 11.14 split into nos. 179–180); not taken: the opening 11.1–11.3, the links 11.5, 11.16, the
padas 11.11–11.13 and the close 11.18–11.19. Besides these, GCC 2.13 (Gaura's words in sleep) stands in GPT 3.2 (no. 119).*

*4. **Who speaks.** In GCC the padas of kiranas 7–9 are the words of the townswomen of Nadia (and of a mother-in-law who sends her daughters-in-law to Shachi, 9.2); the padas
of kiranas 10–11 are the words of heavenly women (devaramaṇī), who only watch Nadia from the sky and long to be born there. In GPT the openings, colophons and links of
the kiranas are left out, and all the padas of section 3.2 read as the words of townswomen; but traces remain in the GPT text itself — "you, connoisseurs of rasa in the city of
the gods", "in the city of the gods a rumour has arisen", "living in the city of the gods, why have you grown so proud", "how will you live alone in the city of the gods" (chapter
32, nos. 17, 20; chapter 33, nos. 3, 4, 10). Therefore 25 padas of GPT (3.2 nos. 158–180 and 3.1 nos. 129–130) are translated with the label "the heavenly women's talk".*

*5. **Where GPT softens GCC.** The compiler of GPT did not take the most outspoken padas (10.11 — one heavenly woman's guess at where Gaura spent the night; 11.11–11.13 —
the antics of women at the ghat and on the road), left out single lines (8.15; the couplet in 11.10 about a shadow touching Gora's body) and replaced single words (8.6 "lay
down" → "sat"; 8.11, 8.14, 8.16 — mentions of Madana, e.g. 8.14 "rapt with Madana" → "rapt with joy"; 8.18 — "breast"; 9.6 — "under Madana's weight"; 9.13 "the cloth over
the breast" → "the cloth over the face"; 9.14 "wants to embrace" → "wants to see your dear face"). Throughout, GPT's text is translated and the GCC reading is noted in VAR
and in the notes. The reverse case occurs once: the last couplet of no. 180 (chapter 33, no. 12), where in place of GCC's words that Narahari, being with Gauranga, preserved
propriety stands the formula "in Nadia the meeting of the nagaris and the nagara came to pass"; the compiler's work is also the signature "Narahari" at the end of no. 179,
where GCC has no poet's name.*

*6. **Conclusion.** The "Narahari" nagari padas of GPT are not songs of a contemporary of the Lord but a late (18th-century) poetic elaboration of the nagari motif, carried over
from the "Gaura-charita-chintamani" and the "Bhakti-ratnakara" into an anthology of the early 20th century, abridged and without the author's frame. Within that frame
Narahari Chakravarti himself never shows Gaura responding to the women's attraction: the Lord passes by without raising His face, turns away, hurries home, performs
expiation, and His companion leads Him away (GCC 11.11–11.14; chapter 32, nos. 19–20; chapter 33, nos. 5, 7, 8, 12); the wishes and dreams are the heroines' imagining, and in
kiranas 10–11 it is even a dispute of heavenly women about what they have not seen. Everything is translated faithfully to the author — without worldly vocabulary beyond
the original and without softening — with notes on the tradition's position: Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja and Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati do not accept the
worship of Gaura in the mood of "gaura-nagari"; Gaura is Krishna Himself in Radha's bhava and radiance, tasting Her love as a devotee, not as the enjoyer (introductory note,
chapter 27). What remains of the section is the padas of Lochana Dasa from GPT 3.2 (nos. 61–85, 116; chapter 34) and the concluding note to the whole section of nagari padas.*
